intro.heading: Marking is contract work, not a title
paragraphs: The phrase examiner tutor is used loosely in this market and almost never defined. Here is the definition worth paying for: a tutor who has been recruited by a board to mark a named component of a named subject, trained on it, standardised against a principal examiner's marks, and then released to mark live candidate scripts. That is a specific job with a specific training process. It is not a rank, a title, or anything a board confers permanently on a person. A tutor who marked Paper 2 of one subject for one series has that experience precisely and only, and the honest version of the claim says exactly that.

That definition matters because it is the only version of the claim a family can test. Marking is organised by component: one person marks Paper 2 of one subject for one series, not the Diploma in general. So the useful question is never whether a tutor has examined, but which component, for which board, and what marking that component changed about the way they now teach it. A tutor who can answer in that form has done the job.

This page is built money-first, because that is the order families ask in. Advertised rates in the Kingdom and what moves them come first, then what marking actually teaches a person, then what it does not cover, then how to verify a claim, then value against a group class, then what an online lesson looks like from your sitting room, and finally where an examiner's eye changes a grade and where it does not. That is the order a family spends money in, so it is the order this page runs in.

On delivery, there is no ambiguity to leave standing. Lessons are one-to-one and run over live video on Arabia Standard Time. Nobody is sent to an address in Riyadh, Jeddah or the Eastern Province; in-home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. For a marking specialist that is an advantage rather than a compromise, because the pool of people who have marked one scarce component is spread across several countries and was never going to be within driving distance.

One more framing note. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, from Cambridge, from Pearson or from any Saudi regulator, and no page here will imply one. A tutor's marking history belongs to that tutor and says nothing about this platform's standing. What IB Gram does is record the claim by component, put the tutor in front of you in a free trial lesson, and let you test it before money changes hands. Where a tutor will not name the component, the claim is not recorded and the profile does not carry the word at all.

ib-examiner-tutor.programmesIntro: A marking claim is only meaningful where there is external marking to do. That differs sharply across the three IB programmes, and it is the first sense check on any examiner claim.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: There are no external examinations in the Primary Years Programme, so there is nothing for a board to mark and no marking experience to have. An examiner claim at this stage describes something that does not exist.
programmes.countryNote: In Saudi schools the PYP usually sits under a Middle Years Programme, and useful support here is reading fluency and number confidence.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessment runs against published criteria and is marked in school, with external moderation available. The relevant experience is criterion marking and moderation rather than script marking, and a tutor should say which they have done.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years Programme students in the Kingdom often move into Cambridge IGCSE at the end of Year 11, which is where script-marking experience starts to matter.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where external marking dominates: written papers per subject, plus internally assessed work that is externally moderated. This is the only programme where a script-marking claim is both meaningful and testable.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi Diploma students sit the May session, and the final two terms are when technique work bought from a marker pays for itself most visibly.

ib-examiner-tutor.subjectsIntro: Marking is component-level work, so these are listed by what a tutor would actually have marked. Scarcity differs: Higher Level Physics markers are harder to find than Business Management ones.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Method marks are the whole game. A marker knows which omitted line of working costs a mark and which does not, which is unteachable from a textbook.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 2 extended response, where a mechanism is wanted and a formula is given. Markers see the same twenty wrong answers to that question every series.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and organic mechanisms, plus data booklet use. Near-miss wordings on definitions are where the scheme's tolerance actually sits.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term discipline against a heavy terminology load. A marker can say exactly which synonyms the scheme accepts and which it does not.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram marks and the evaluation sentence. The most common loss is a correct diagram with no labelled shift and no judgement at the end.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application against a case study. Marks go on applying a framework to the stimulus rather than on describing the framework itself.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis and the individual oral. Markers reward writing about construction; students write about content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with heavy technology use. A marker knows how much interpretation a question wants before it stops paying.

sections.heading: What an hour with a marker costs in this market
paragraphs: Start with the money, because it is what families open with and what most rival pages hide behind a contact form. Advertised rates in the Kingdom run from roughly SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms marketing IGCSE one-to-one, through about SAR 50 for general primary tuition in Riyadh, up to SAR 200 and beyond for senior-school examination subjects. Those are published vendor figures and tutor-marketplace guides, not a market average, and not a quote for anything here.

A tutor who has marked for a board sits at the top of that range, and the reason is supply rather than status. A board recruits a limited number of markers per component per series, trains them, and standardises them before releasing live scripts. The number of people who have done that for one particular component is small, and it does not grow because demand in Riyadh rose this term. Scarcity sets the price, which is why the band for Higher Level and premium tracks is quoted at around SAR 200 to 220 on tutoring-company listings.

Four things move the number, in descending order of weight. Level comes first: a Higher Level specialist costs more than a Standard Level one everywhere. Then subject scarcity. Then marking experience on the exact component, which is a narrower and rarer thing than marking experience in general. Then travel, which is the loading online teaching removes completely. Package length moves it last, and a provider discounting heavily before a trial lesson is selling the discount rather than the teaching.

sections.heading: What marking a paper actually teaches a person
paragraphs: The training is the part nobody writes about. Before a marker touches a live script they mark a set of sample scripts already marked by a principal examiner, and their marks are compared against those. Until the two agree closely enough, no live candidate work is released to them. The effect of that process on a teacher is specific and permanent: they stop guessing what a mark scheme means and start knowing where its tolerance ends.

The second thing marking teaches is the shape of the error distribution. Reading several hundred answers to the same question in one series shows a person something no textbook contains: not what the correct answer is, but what the twenty most common wrong answers are, which of them still score, and which one your child is probably writing. That is diagnostic knowledge, and it is why a marker can often name the fault from one page of a student's work.

In a lesson, both of those convert a student who knows the content into one who gets paid for knowing it. An explain question answered with a description. A six-mark answer that lists instead of judging. An evaluate answer with no judgement in the final line. A method mark lost to a missing line of working. None of that is content teaching, and all of it is the fastest-moving work available to a student who is already close. A marker finds the pattern in one page of work; a generalist often needs most of a term to see it.

sections.heading: What examiner experience does not cover
paragraphs: It is component-specific. Marking Paper 2 of one subject does not make a person an authority on Paper 1 of the same subject, let alone on another subject in the same group. The question types differ, the schemes differ, and the error distributions differ. A tutor who has marked one paper and teaches the other should say so plainly, because the honest version still leaves them better placed than a generalist - just not in the way a vague claim implies.

It is also board-specific and it goes stale. A subject guide changes, assessment structures are redesigned, and experience from an earlier version of a course can mislead rather than help. Ask when the tutor last marked, and whether it was on the current specification. A tutor who volunteers that their marking predates a syllabus revision, and explains what changed, has told you more about their judgement than any certificate would.

The last limit is the uncomfortable one: marking is not teaching. They are different skills and the first does not imply the second. Some of the best markers are indifferent explainers, and some superb teachers have never marked a script in their lives. The useful combination is both, which is why a trial lesson matters more than a profile. Watch whether the tutor can make your child say something, or only tell them things. A marking history earns a tutor a hearing rather than a booking, and the trial lesson is where the second one is decided.

sections.heading: What a marker can and cannot show you
paragraphs: Families sometimes ask to see proof of marking, and the honest answer is that most of what they are imagining cannot be shown. Candidate scripts are confidential and never leave the marking system. Pre-release materials are under embargo. A marker cannot show you a child's paper from a past series, cannot share a scheme before it is published, and should refuse if asked. A tutor who offers any of that is telling you something about their judgement, and it is not good.

What can be shown is substantial. Published past papers and published mark schemes, which are available to schools and candidates. The tutor's own annotated copy of those schemes. The component and board named plainly. An account of how standardisation worked for them, which is specific enough that it cannot be improvised. And a worked demonstration: hand them one marked answer of your child's and listen to whether the diagnosis is a topic name or an adjective.

That last test is the whole verification, and it costs you one trial lesson. Three questions do the work: which component and board did you mark, when was that and on which version of the course, and what did marking change about the way you teach it now? Then ask your child's own subject teacher what they would want fixed first. A tutor whose answer matches the teacher's is worth the rate. One whose answer contradicts it may still be right, but should be able to say why in syllabus terms rather than in generalities.

sections.heading: One-to-one against a group class, on value
paragraphs: Group classes are cheaper per hour for an obvious reason: the rate is split across the room. Where the subject is popular and the paper is predictable, that can be good value, and a marker running a revision class for twelve students on one paper will still show them things their school has not. Routine, past-paper volume and a deadline to work to are real benefits, and some students need those more than they need diagnosis.

What a group cannot do is follow one student's error pattern. The pace is set by the median student in the room, the examples are chosen from the paper rather than from your child's own answers, and feedback on assessed work is rarely practical with twelve people present. If the problem is that your child does not know what is going wrong, a group class will not find out, however well it is taught and however experienced the person teaching it.

The decision rule is simple enough to apply tonight. If a set of your child's marked papers shows the same fault repeatedly, buy one-to-one and buy it on that component. If the papers are sound and the problem is volume, pace or motivation, a group class is the cheaper answer and the honest recommendation. Families who buy both usually find the one-to-one slot does the work and the group slot does the practice. Buying only the group slot and hoping diagnosis arrives with it is the common and expensive mistake here.

sections.heading: What a parent actually sees in an online lesson
paragraphs: A session runs in a browser on a shared video call with a shared whiteboard. The tutor opens a published past paper on screen, both of them can write on it, and the student's working appears where the tutor can see it being formed rather than after it is finished. For mathematics and the sciences that matters: the error is usually in line three, and watching it happen is how a marker catches it.

Recordings, where they are made, exist for the student and the family rather than for anyone else, and a family that does not want a session recorded can say so before it starts. After each session the tutor writes a short note: what was covered, what the student got wrong, what to do before the next slot. That note is the thing to read, because a vague note usually means a vague lesson.

Between sessions, written work moves by photograph or scan and comes back annotated to the published scheme with the mark shown. A laptop is better than a tablet because of the writing area, a quiet room matters more than a fast connection, and if a line drops the session resumes or is rescheduled rather than counted. None of this requires an install or a licence a family has to buy separately. Ask for one session before committing, because a family's own room, laptop and connection decide more about how an online lesson feels than any platform feature does, and that is worth testing once at no cost.

sections.heading: Where an examiner's eye changes a grade, and where it does not
paragraphs: Technique work moves marks fastest for a student whose content is broadly in place. A Diploma student sitting at a 5 with sound knowledge and poor command-term discipline is the clearest case: the gap is between what they know and what the scheme pays for, and that gap is exactly what marking teaches a person to close. Four to six weeks of focused work on one paper is often enough to see it in the next set of marks.

It changes much less for a student who is missing content rather than technique. No amount of mark-scheme literacy helps where two years of a Higher Level subject were never securely taught, and a marker who takes that booking without saying so is taking the family's money. The same applies to an unstarted internal assessment close to a school deadline, and to a subject choice that was wrong from the start. Those need different conversations, and sometimes the school rather than a tutor.

So the honest frame. No tutor can promise a grade or a score, and marking experience changes probability rather than outcome. Expect a first diagnosis in one session, a visible change in a mark pattern in four to six weeks, and a plain answer if the ceiling is lower than the family hoped. Where no marker is free for a scarce component at the hour you need, the right response is to say so and offer a subject specialist instead.

faqs.question: What does an hour with a tutor who has marked for a board actually cost in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Published rates put senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 and above in Riyadh, with Higher Level and premium tracks advertised at roughly SAR 200 to 220 by tutoring companies, while general non-specialist online tutoring is marketed from about SAR 35 to 55. A marking specialist sits at the upper end of those published bands. Those are advertised vendor figures and marketplace guides rather than a market average, and the actual figure depends on subject, level and arrangement length.

faqs.question: Why does marking experience push an hourly rate above a non-specialist's?
faqs.answer: Supply, not status. A board recruits a limited number of markers for each component in each series, trains them, and standardises them against a principal examiner's marks before releasing live scripts. The group of people who have done that for one specific paper is small and does not expand with local demand. Add Higher Level and a scarce subject such as Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, and the pool narrows again. Price follows scarcity rather than any claim about quality.

faqs.question: Is a package with an examiner tutor better value than paying lesson by lesson?
faqs.answer: For technique work on one paper, yes, because the gains come from a sequence rather than from single sessions: diagnose, drill, remark, repeat. Six to eight sessions with a stated end point is the usual shape. For a first diagnosis, pay for one session and decide afterwards. Be wary of long packages discounted before a trial lesson has happened, and ask what occurs to unused sessions if the family moves city or the student changes subject.

faqs.question: Does a group revision class taught by a marker beat one-to-one with a subject teacher?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is broken. A group class run by a marker is good value where the subject is popular, the paper predictable, and the student needs volume and routine. It cannot follow one student's error pattern, because the pace is set by the median student and the examples come from the paper rather than from your child's answers. If the same fault keeps recurring in marked work, one-to-one on that component is the better purchase.

faqs.question: What happens in a free trial lesson with a tutor who claims examiner experience?
faqs.answer: Hand them one marked answer of your child's and listen. A marker will name the component, the question type and the specific fault, then show the published mark scheme beside it. Ask which component and board they marked, when, and on which version of the course. Ask what marking changed about their teaching. Thirty to forty-five minutes is enough to tell a specific answer from an evasive one, and it happens before any package is agreed.

faqs.question: Do rates for an examiner tutor rise as the May session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens more than price does. The scarce components fill first, and by the final term the question is usually whether a marker for that paper has an evening free at all rather than what they charge. Families who book technique blocks a term ahead get both the tutor and the slot they wanted. Those who come late are often choosing between a different hour, a short wait, or a subject specialist who has not marked.

faqs.question: How do I verify that a tutor has really marked the component my child sits?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions and compare the answers with your child's subject teacher. Which component and which board? When, and on which version of the course? What did marking change about how you teach it? Specific answers name papers, question types and scheme wordings. Evasive answers offer the word examiner and move on. Certificates prove little in this market, which is why the test is a conversation about one of your child's own marked answers.

faqs.question: Can a tutor show me scripts or mark schemes from their marking work?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to has told you something important. Candidate scripts are confidential and stay inside the marking system, and materials under embargo cannot be shared before release. What a tutor can legitimately show is published past papers, published mark schemes, their own annotations on those, and an account of how standardisation worked for them. Ask for that instead; it is more useful than any document and impossible to improvise convincingly.

faqs.question: Should a tutor who marks Paper 2 teach Paper 1 as well?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but the claim should be stated honestly. Marking one paper does not confer authority over another: question types differ, schemes differ, and the common errors differ. A tutor who marked Paper 2 and teaches Paper 1 is still better placed than a generalist, because they understand how a scheme is written and applied. What matters is that they say which paper they marked rather than letting the word examiner cover both.

faqs.question: What if the examiner tutor we are matched with is wrong for my child after two lessons?
faqs.answer: Say so early rather than waiting out a package. Two or three sessions is enough to tell whether a tutor can get a teenager talking, and marking skill does not guarantee teaching skill - they are separate abilities. Ask for a different tutor on the same component and explain what did not work, because a specific complaint produces a better second match. Four weeks is the natural review point for keeping, changing or stopping altogether.

faqs.question: Does examiner experience go out of date when a subject guide changes?
faqs.answer: Partly. The underlying skill - reading a scheme, knowing where its tolerance ends, seeing the error distribution - transfers across revisions. The specifics do not: assessment structures change, papers are redesigned, and old question types disappear. Ask when the tutor last marked and whether it was on the current specification. A tutor who volunteers that their marking predates a revision, and explains what changed, is demonstrating exactly the judgement you are paying for.

faqs.question: What does a student see on screen when a marker works through a past paper?
faqs.answer: A published past paper open in a shared window, with both people able to write on it, and the mark scheme brought alongside once the student has committed to an answer. The student writes and the tutor watches the working form rather than reading a finished product, which is how a line-three error gets caught. For mathematics and the sciences that live view is the main reason an online session works as well as a desk.

faqs.question: Are lessons with an examiner tutor recorded, and who can watch them?
faqs.answer: Where a recording is made it is for the student and the family to re-watch, not for anyone else, and a family who would rather not be recorded can say so before the session starts. Recordings are genuinely useful for technique work, because a student can watch how an answer was rebuilt. What matters more for most families is the written note afterwards, which should name what was covered and what went wrong.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark my child's written work between online sessions?
faqs.answer: Work is photographed or scanned, sent before the next slot, and comes back annotated against the published scheme with the mark shown and the lost marks explained. That annotation is where a marker's experience is most visible, because the comments point at scheme wordings rather than at general advice. Ask to see one annotated piece early. If the feedback reads as encouragement with no marks attached, it is not what you are paying for.

ib-examiner-tutor.closingHeading: Test the claim before you pay the premium
ib-examiner-tutor.closingBody: An examiner tutor is worth the top of the advertised band when the claim is specific and the teaching is good. Both are checkable in one free trial lesson: name the component and the board, say when the marking was and on which version of the course, and diagnose one of your child's marked answers out loud. Send three marked papers and the component you want fixed, and lessons run one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

intro.heading: Start with the money, because the money explains the rest
paragraphs: Families searching for IB home tuition in Saudi Arabia are usually trying to answer two questions at once: what does this cost, and is it worth it. Almost every page competing for this search answers neither. Rates sit behind a contact form, or one number appears with no indication of what it covers, and the comparison a parent actually needs — between an in-home hour and an online hour, between a specialist and a generalist, between weekly support and a block bought in a panic — is nowhere. So this page opens on the money and works outwards from it.

The published numbers are these. Tutoring companies list IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180 an hour, with Higher Level and Advanced Placement tracks around SAR 200 to SAR 220. Tutor-marketplace guides put general private tuition for senior-school examination subjects in Riyadh at SAR 200 and above, and primary tuition nearer SAR 50. Platforms list general, non-specialist online tutoring from around SAR 55, and budget providers advertise International GCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. International providers quoting in dollars sit near sixty dollars an hour. Those are advertised rates published by those vendors. They are not a market average, and none of them is our price.

A spread of six times between the cheapest and dearest figure is not noise and it is not a negotiating position. It tracks four things: how scarce the subject specialism is, what level the course sits at, whether the tutor has marked for a board, and whether anyone is driving. The last of those is the only one that depends on format rather than on the person, and it is the reason an in-home rate in Riyadh or Jeddah sits above an online rate for the same subject and the same tutor quality. An hour of driving has to be recovered from somewhere, and it is recovered from the fee.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition. We do not run home visits in Saudi Arabia, and a tutor does not travel to a Saudi address — in-home teaching is a service we offer only in India. The URL you arrived on says home tuition because that is the phrase families type, and the honest answer to it is a comparison rather than a promise. In-home teaching has real advantages: a student cannot close a laptop on a person sitting beside them, and a younger child often concentrates better with an adult in the room. It also restricts you to the specialists who live within driving range and have that evening free, which in most Saudi cities is a very short list for Mathematics AA HL or Physics HL.

What follows, in order: what sits inside an hour in each format, what moves the rate and in what order of weight, what a year of support actually adds up to at the published bands, the costs families forget to price, what the fee buys in deliverables, and where the boundary sits on assessed work. The sections on schools and on curriculum switching are at the end because they explain why the fee exists at all — a class of twenty-five, a subject taught by a willing non-specialist, a Higher Level group combined with a Standard Level one.

ib-home-tuition.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes, and the cost of support differs sharply between them because the assessment load does. A family paying for Diploma help and a family paying for Middle Years help are buying different things, and confusing the two is how budgets go wrong.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led units rather than subject syllabuses, no external examinations, and the Exhibition in the final year. Support at this stage is cheap because the content is not specialised: general tutoring rates apply rather than subject-specialist ones, and marketplace guides put primary private tuition in the Kingdom nearer SAR 50 an hour than the Diploma bands.
programmes.countryNote: What a family buys here is foundation rather than remediation. Reading age, written output and arithmetic fluency are the three measurable things, and they predict the next five years better than any report comment. Families across the Kingdom who invest at this stage generally spend less in the Diploma years, because the expensive problems at Higher Level are almost always foundational ones that were never closed.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked out of 8 and converted to a 1-7 grade. Criteria reward investigating, communicating and reflecting as well as knowing, so the work is as much about presenting thinking as holding content. The Personal Project in the final year is assessed on process, and the journal carries much of the mark.
programmes.countryNote: Rates here sit between general and Diploma tutoring, and the commonest request across the Kingdom is Personal Project support rather than subject teaching. That is a short, bounded engagement — a handful of sessions on planning, goal-setting and record-keeping — and it is far cheaper than a term of weekly lessons. Families who buy weekly subject tuition at this stage when the real gap is organisational tend to overspend.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Up to 45 points, of which three come from the core. Higher Level carries more teaching hours, an additional paper in several subjects, and topics with no Standard Level equivalent. Internal Assessment is marked in school and moderated externally.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the published bands bite, because a Diploma student carries six courses at once and families rarely need help in only one. The cheapest version of Diploma support in the Kingdom is to start in the first year at one hour a week; the most expensive is two subjects at two hours a week in the final two terms. Both are common, and the difference between them is when the family started.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Combines two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning component and a personal and professional skills course. It is offered at far fewer schools than the Diploma and the assessment mix is different, with the reflective project carrying weight the Extended Essay carries elsewhere.
programmes.countryNote: Provision in the Kingdom is thin, and most families who ask about it are weighing it against the Diploma rather than already enrolled. The useful cost comparison is the number of examined Diploma courses carried: fewer examined subjects means less subject tutoring, but the reflective project and the career-related study both need supervision a family may need to arrange themselves.

ib-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: Below are the Diploma subjects families across the Kingdom most often buy support for, described by what makes each one expensive or cheap to tutor. Scarcity and level set the rate; what the hour is spent on sets whether it was worth paying.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most expensive subject to tutor at Higher Level, and the clearest illustration of why scarcity drives price: the number of people who can teach proof by induction, complex numbers and the Higher Level calculus strand to examination standard is small in every market. The rate is not a judgement about the tutor; it is a statement about how few of them there are.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Cheaper to staff than Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level and nearly as scarce at Higher Level, where the statistics load is heavy. Hours spent here go further when they are spent on interpretation rather than calculation, because a calculator result left uncommented loses the final marks regardless of how it was obtained.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level Physics competes with industry employment for the same graduates across the Kingdom, which keeps both school staffing and tutoring rates at the top of the band. Value comes from precision work: exact definitions, units, significant figures and graph reading, all of which are quick to teach and expensive to leave alone.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mid to upper band, and one of the subjects where an hour a week across a year genuinely outperforms a block bought late, because energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms each need practice spaced over months. Students who buy support only before the series usually pay more for less movement.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Easier to staff, so nearer the middle of the band, but the highest-volume content in its group. The efficient spend is on command terms and answer structure rather than on content coverage: a student who writes everything they know about a topic is paid for a fraction of it, and that is a technique problem bought cheaply.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Theory is widely taught and mark schemes are not, which is why rates vary so much here for apparently similar tutors. Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the grade, and the Internal Assessment commentaries need article selection help as much as writing help — a short, cheap intervention that changes the ceiling.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Among the cheapest Diploma subjects to find support for and among the easiest to buy badly. Marks come from applying a named tool to the stimulus case rather than explaining the tool, so an hour spent revising definitions is an hour wasted. Ask what a prospective tutor would do with a past case study before booking.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis of literary and non-literary texts, which rewards practised technique rather than revision, so support here is unusually efficient per hour. The individual oral needs a global issue genuinely linked to two extracts, and that planning session is often the single highest-value hour a family buys.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Interdisciplinary, with a terminology load that catches students who treat it as a soft option. Specialists are fewer than in the main sciences, so rates can sit higher than the subject's reputation suggests. Value concentrates on case studies and on the systems vocabulary the mark schemes expect precisely.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Contributes to the three core points alongside the Extended Essay, and is the component families most often ignore until it is late. Support is short and cheap relative to a subject — a few sessions on framing a knowledge question and structuring the essay — and skipping it can cost points the subject grades then have to make up.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research, supervised at school, graded A to E and combined with Theory of Knowledge for up to three points. The cheapest useful intervention is early: one or two sessions testing whether the research question can actually be answered with reachable sources or data, before months are spent on one that cannot.

ib-home-tuition.regionsTitle: Where in the Kingdom this search comes from
ib-home-tuition.regionsIntro: IB home tuition is searched for across the Kingdom, and the economics differ by place. In the three big centres the question is whether a specialist exists locally. Outside them, the in-home option mostly does not exist at any price, which changes the comparison entirely.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The largest pool of Diploma provision and the largest pool of in-home tutors, and also the city where travel loading bites hardest: the capital is roughly an hour across in traffic, so an in-home evening slot can consume two hours of a tutor's day for one paid hour.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north towards Obhur, which makes distance rather than congestion the main driver of an in-home rate. Families at the northern end of the city and tutors based centrally rarely make the arithmetic work twice a week.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One conurbation functioning as a single school and labour market, with families routinely living in one city and schooling in another. In-home tutoring here is priced across that whole area, and the specialist pool is shared between three cities rather than available in each.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city up the coast with international provision tied closely to employer communities. The local pool of Diploma Higher Level specialists is small, so published in-home rates are less relevant than availability: the tutor a family wants often simply is not there.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: International-curriculum provision is limited relative to population, and the practical in-home market for Diploma subjects is thin. Families here are usually comparing an online specialist against no specialist, rather than against a local one at a different price.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST community
regions.note: A concentrated, highly academic community served by its own school, where parents often know the subject content themselves. Requests here skew towards Higher Level extension work and Extended Essay supervision rather than remediation, which is a different and shorter purchase.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Two 'Asir cities about twenty-five kilometres apart sharing a catchment at high altitude. Distance to any Diploma specialist is the binding constraint, and an in-home arrangement for a scarce subject is generally not purchasable at any advertised rate.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: Rapidly changing communities in the north-west with new and relocating families, many arriving part-way through a course. The commonest purchase is a diagnostic and a catch-up block rather than a year of weekly lessons, and almost none of it can be bought locally.

schoolClusters.note: Several schools in the capital appear in IB directories across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes, which makes Riyadh the one Saudi city where a family can usually choose between IB providers. Students we support attend schools of this kind. Subject availability still varies campus by campus and year by year.

Jeddah carries both IB and Cambridge provision, and some long-established international schools follow neither. The practical consequence for a family budgeting for support is that two students at different Jeddah schools may be sitting entirely different qualifications in the same subject.

The International Schools Group operates several campuses in the province, and the Diploma runs at some of them rather than all. British-curriculum provision is wider than IB provision here, which is why many Eastern Province families budgeting for IB support are paying for a subject their school does not examine.

ib-home-tuition.modesIntro: Four purchasing shapes cover almost every request, and they differ in cost by an order of magnitude. Choosing the wrong one is the most common way a family overspends on IB support. All are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, started early
modes.description: One hour a week in a single subject, running from the start of the first Diploma year. This is the cheapest route to a given grade and almost nobody buys it, because the problem does not feel urgent yet. Spread across two years it costs less per grade than any other pattern, and it removes the need for a premium block later.

modes.title: A short diagnostic and review block
modes.description: Two or three sessions: a timed component, a marked analysis of where the marks went, and a written view of what would need to change. Families frequently buy this and then do nothing for a term, which is a reasonable decision made on evidence rather than a wasted purchase. It is the cheapest thing on this list.

modes.title: Internal Assessment and Extended Essay review
modes.description: A handful of sessions scheduled around the student's own drafts rather than weekly. The tutor reads what the student wrote, questions the method and the scope, and names the criterion the draft does not yet meet. Per hour it is the same rate; per grade it is often the best value in the Diploma, because scope errors cap marks no amount of polish recovers.

modes.title: Pre-series intensive block
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week in the final weeks before a session, aimed at paper technique rather than content. The most expensive pattern per grade, because demand concentrates at exactly this point and the scarce specialists have already filled. It works, and it works better when it is topping up weekly support rather than replacing it.

sections.heading: What actually sits inside an hour, by format
paragraphs: An hourly rate is a comparison only if both hours contain the same things, and they do not. In-home tuition and online one-to-one differ in what the hour can include, what happens between hours, and what happens when something goes wrong. A family comparing SAR 220 for an in-home Higher Level hour with a lower online figure is often comparing a shorter lesson with a longer one, and an arrangement with marking between sessions against one without.

The teaching time itself is the first difference. An in-home session is bounded by a journey at each end, and a journey that runs late eats the lesson rather than the fee. Traffic in Riyadh at the end of the working day, or the length of the Jeddah coastal spine, is not a hypothetical: it is the most common reason an in-home arrangement quietly becomes a fifty-minute hour. An online session starts when the hour starts because nobody is in a car.

The second difference is what happens between sessions, and this is where most of the value hides. Written work set at the end of a lesson has to reach the tutor and come back marked before the next one. Over video a photographed script arrives in seconds and comes back annotated the same evening. In an in-home arrangement it usually waits for the next visit, which means a week of a student practising a fault uncorrected. Over a term that difference is worth more than a modest gap in hourly rate.

The third is the pool each format draws from, and it is the one families underweight most. An in-home hour is bought from the set of people who teach that syllabus, live within driving range, and have that particular evening free. An online hour is bought from the set of people who teach that syllabus. For Business Management Standard Level in Riyadh those two sets may overlap usefully. For Mathematics AA HL in Jubail or Abha, the first set is frequently empty.

sections.heading: What moves the rate, in order of weight
paragraphs: Four variables explain nearly all of the spread in published rates, and they are not equally weighted. Subject scarcity is the largest by a distance. A Mathematics AA HL or Physics HL specialist costs more in Riyadh, in London and in Singapore alike, because the number of people who can teach those courses to examination standard is small everywhere and they are in demand from schools as well as from families. No amount of searching changes that, and a rate at the top of the band for one of those subjects is usually a correct price rather than an opportunistic one.

Level comes second: Higher Level above Standard Level, Diploma above Middle Years, and both above International GCSE. This is the variable families most often get wrong in the other direction, buying a cheaper Standard Level rate for a Higher Level problem and discovering four weeks in that the tutor has not taught the extension topics. The Higher Level courses are not harder versions of the Standard Level ones in several subjects; they contain material with no Standard Level equivalent at all.

Marking or examining experience is third, and it is worth paying for selectively. What it buys is not better subject knowledge but knowledge of what a script is actually paid for — which of two correct answers earns the mark, how a mark scheme treats a near-miss, where an examiner stops reading. That is worth a premium in the final two terms of a course and worth very little in the first year, when the job is still building content. Paying for it early is a common and avoidable overspend.

Travel is fourth and it is the only one that belongs to the format rather than to the person. It is also the only one a family can remove entirely. Package length and timing then adjust the figure at the margins: a longer commitment usually lowers the hourly rate, and booking in the weeks before a series usually raises it, because demand concentrates and the scarce specialists fill first.

sections.heading: A year of support, multiplied out at the published bands
paragraphs: Hourly rates are hard to budget against, so it is worth doing the arithmetic a parent actually needs. The table below takes common situations, counts the hours they imply across a school year, and multiplies them by the advertised figures named earlier in this page. Every total is a vendor's published rate multiplied by a number of hours. None of them is a quote from us, and none of them should be treated as a market average — we price per student after a trial lesson, because the honest number depends on subject, level and how many weeks remain.

Two things fall out of the arithmetic immediately. The first is that early weekly support in one subject is a far smaller commitment than families assume. Term-time weekly lessons in a single Standard Level subject come to roughly thirty hours across a year, which at the lower IB listing band is a few thousand riyals — comparable to a term of a group activity, not to school fees. The second is that the late, panicked version costs nearly as much for a fraction of the benefit, because an intensive block bought in the final weeks buys technique at a premium with no time to fix content.

The expensive scenario is the one that arrives most often: two weak subjects in the final Diploma year, both needing two hours a week, across two terms. That is the arrangement families reach when nothing was done in the first year, and the arithmetic is uncomfortable. It is also the arrangement in which the lowest-cost intervention sits: a few hours of Internal Assessment review in the first year, properly used, frequently removes one of those two subjects from the list altogether.

A final note on how to read the table. Hours across a school year assume term time only and no lessons through the long summer break, which is how most families actually run it. If you hold a slot through the breaks, add roughly a fifth. If you pause and release a slot in a scarce subject, budget for the possibility that it is not available in the autumn term.

sections.heading: The costs families forget to price
paragraphs: The hourly rate is the visible cost and rarely the largest one. The first invisible cost is a wrong match. A tutor who knows the subject but not the assessment produces weeks of pleasant, apparently productive lessons and no movement in marks, and a family typically takes a full term to conclude that. At any rate in the published band, a term of that is a significant sum spent on nothing, and the preventive measure costs an hour: ask a prospective tutor what they would do with a specific past-paper question, and listen for whether they talk about the mark scheme.

The second is re-teaching. A cheap generalist working from a textbook rather than from the board's papers will cover content the student has already met and leave the technique faults untouched. The marks do not move, so the family then buys a specialist as well. Paying twice is the single most expensive outcome in this market, and it is reached by economising at the wrong point: the saving on an hourly rate is small, and the cost of a wasted term is not.

The third is cancellation and travel friction, which applies to in-home arrangements specifically. A session lost to traffic, weather or a tutor's other commitment is usually not refunded and is often not rescheduled, because rescheduling requires another journey to be possible. Across a year, a handful of lost sessions is a measurable percentage of what was paid. Over video a missed hour is a scheduling problem rather than a logistics one, so it is more often recovered.

The fourth is the opportunity cost of starting late, which does not appear on any invoice. Content taught in the first Diploma year can be fixed in the first Diploma year cheaply. The same gap met in the final term has to be fixed while five other subjects are also demanding time, and the only remaining lever is intensive hours at the point in the year when they cost most and the specialists are least available. Families who believe they are saving money by waiting are usually deferring a larger bill.

sections.heading: What the fee buys beyond the hour
paragraphs: A fee should buy more than attendance, and the difference between providers is mostly in what surrounds the lesson. The first deliverable is a diagnosis. Before any plan, a student sits something real — a past-paper question in the trial lesson, then a full component under time — and the output is a ranked list of where marks are going, not a general impression. A provider who cannot produce that in the first fortnight is selling hours rather than a result.

The second is marked work. Teaching that stops at the end of the hour leaves the practice unsupervised, and unsupervised practice entrenches whatever the student is already doing wrong. Work set at the end of a session should be marked against the published scheme before the next one, with the annotations visible to the student and the pattern visible to the parent. That is part of the hour's price in our arrangement, and it is worth asking any provider whether it is part of theirs.

The third is a short written note after each session: what was covered, what was set, what was weak. Not a grade, not encouragement, and not a progress percentage, because there is no honest way to compute one over a few weeks. Parents who receive these stop having to extract a summary from a teenager, which is both the most common complaint about tutoring and the easiest one to fix.

The fourth is a term review that is allowed to recommend stopping. At the end of a term, the comparison is between marked scripts: if the fault identified in week one is no longer costing marks on a comparable paper, the teaching is working. If the same marks are going in the same place, the diagnosis or the match is wrong and more hours will not correct it. And sometimes a student has what they need and should stop, which is the recommendation families trust most precisely because it is the one that costs us.

sections.heading: Where the boundary sits on assessed work
paragraphs: Some providers competing for this search will, for a fee, supply finished coursework. It is worth stating the boundary plainly, because a family paying for help on assessed work has a right to know which side of it they are on, and because the student carries the consequence rather than the provider. Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Middle Years Personal Project must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the skills involved, question the method, challenge the scope, and name the criterion a draft is not yet meeting. The writing stays with the student.

In practice, a good session on a draft looks like questioning rather than editing. What is the research question actually asking, and can the data you collected answer it? Which variable did you control, and how do you know it stayed controlled? Where does this graph show what the sentence beneath it claims? Which descriptor does this paragraph satisfy, and can you point at the words that satisfy it? A student who can answer those produces better work than one handed better paragraphs, and the work is defensibly theirs.

Scope is where an outside reader adds the most value and the least risk. A research question too broad to answer with reachable data caps the mark at the planning criterion no matter how well the rest is executed, and it is the single most common reason a hard-working student scores poorly on an Internal Assessment. Catching that in the first session of a project, before months are committed, is cheap. Catching it in the final draft is not, because by then the only options are a weak submission or a restart.

The school supervisor remains the authority throughout. The Extended Essay has a formal supervision structure with reflection sessions, and the number of drafts a supervisor may formally comment on is set by the school and the programme rather than by a tutor. We work inside that structure, keep a record of what each session discussed, and say so directly when a request crosses the line. A provider willing to cross it for a fee has sold a family a malpractice risk and called it a service.

sections.heading: Why the fee exists: what schools in the Kingdom can and cannot staff
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, with school evaluation and accreditation running through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. None of that machinery says anything about whether a particular campus can field a Higher Level physics teacher next year, and that is the question a family's tutoring bill actually depends on.

IB provision in the Kingdom is unevenly distributed. Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province carry most of it; directories disagree on totals and none of them is dated, so the honest description is a concentration in the three large centres and thin coverage elsewhere rather than a number. A school offering the Diploma has to staff every Higher Level subject it lists, and a school that loses one specialist mid-course cannot. What follows is a combined Higher and Standard Level class, or a subject taught by a willing non-specialist, and neither appears in any report a parent receives.

Class size does the rest. A Diploma class of twenty-five in a subject with a heavy Internal Assessment component gives each student a small share of the teacher's marking attention, and the students who most need their drafts questioned are the least likely to ask. This is not a criticism of the schools; it is arithmetic. It is also the clearest honest justification for the fee this page is about: a family is buying individual attention that a class cannot supply at any staffing level.

Expatriate staffing cycles add volatility. Contracts turn over, and a department that was strong one year can be thin the next with nothing visible changing. Parents often read that as declining standards when it is one person leaving. The practical question to ask a school, in writing and before enrolling, is which Higher Level subjects will actually run next year, whether any Higher and Standard Level groups are taught together, and who teaches the Higher Level sciences and mathematics. The answers predict a tutoring budget better than anything else available.

sections.heading: What a curriculum switch costs, and when it is worth it
paragraphs: Families relocating into the Kingdom, or moving between schools within it, regularly face a change of curriculum alongside everything else. The cost of support through that change depends almost entirely on direction. A student moving from a British school into the Diploma usually arrives with the subject content and has to learn an unfamiliar assessment language: criterion-referenced marking, command terms as instructions, and a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service that has no equivalent in their previous school. That is a technique job, measured in weeks rather than terms, and it is comparatively cheap.

A student arriving from an American curriculum typically has breadth and needs depth, and the gap shows specifically at Higher Level in the sciences and in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. That is a content job, and content jobs cost more because they need sustained weekly contact rather than a block. Eight to ten weeks of targeted work on the identified topics, run alongside the school course and measured against past-paper questions, is the usual shape. Trying to do it in a holiday block rarely holds.

A move from a national curriculum into an international one is the case where the diagnosis is most often wrong. The content overlaps more than families fear; the examination culture does not. Marks go on applying knowledge to unfamiliar material and on taking a defensible position in extended answers, rather than on complete accurate recall. Technical English is the other gap, and it is narrower than it looks — a few dozen standard explanatory sentences per science subject, drilled until automatic, cover most of what the mark schemes credit. Buying general language tuition when the need is subject-specific phrasing is a common and expensive misdiagnosis.

The hardest and most expensive case is a move part-way through the Diploma. Internal Assessment work does not transfer cleanly between schools, subject combinations differ, and a student may lose a term of continuity in a two-year course. Where a family has a genuine choice about timing, delaying a move to a clean boundary — the start of Year 10, or the start of the first Diploma year — almost always costs less in support than moving mid-course and buying the recovery.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the weeks remaining
process.description: Those three facts set the realistic cost before anybody quotes an hour. Higher Level Chemistry with two years left and Higher Level Chemistry with one term left are different jobs at different prices, and a provider who quotes the same for both has not asked enough questions.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a real question
process.description: An hour with the tutor we think fits, spent on an actual past-paper question rather than a conversation about goals. You learn whether the student will work with this person; we learn whether the shortfall is content, technique or confidence. There is no charge and nothing to commit to afterwards.

process.title: A baseline and a ranked fault list
process.description: In the first fortnight the student sits a full component under time, marked against the published scheme. The output is a list of where marks went, ordered by how many. That list is what any honest quote should be built on, and it is the thing you can hold a provider to later.

process.title: A written plan with a realistic range, not a target grade
process.description: After four weeks you receive a plan: what has moved, what has not, a realistic range rather than a promise, and the weekly commitment that range assumes. Nobody can guarantee a grade, and a plan that names one is telling you about its sales process rather than your child.

process.title: A term review that can recommend stopping
process.description: At the end of each term we compare marked scripts rather than impressions and make a recommendation: continue, change the subject being supported, or stop. Stopping is a real outcome and we make it when it is right, because the alternative is selling hours that are no longer buying anything.

whyPoints.title: Every figure is attributed, and none of them is our price
whyPoints.description: The rates on this page are advertised figures published by platforms, agencies and tutoring companies, named by source type. We do not present any of them as a market average, and we quote per student after a trial lesson because the honest number depends on subject, level and how many weeks remain.

whyPoints.title: The travel loading is removed rather than absorbed
whyPoints.description: An in-home arrangement in the Kingdom recovers the journey at each end from the fee, and a journey that runs late shortens the lesson rather than the bill. Teaching over live video removes that cost and that risk entirely, and replaces the question of who lives nearby with the question of who knows the paper.

whyPoints.title: Marking between sessions is part of the hour
whyPoints.description: Work set at the end of a lesson is marked against the published scheme before the next one, with the annotations visible to the student. Unsupervised practice entrenches a fault, so a week of it costs more than a small difference in hourly rate ever saves.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work is questioned, never written
whyPoints.description: On an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project, a tutor reads the student's draft, challenges the scope and method, and names the criterion it does not meet. The student writes it and the school supervisor signs it off. We say so before anyone asks.

whyPoints.title: Claims we cannot evidence are not made
whyPoints.description: There are no success percentages, no star ratings, no tutor headcounts and no grade promises anywhere on this page, because none of them could be published with a sample size, a date and a method attached. What we will give you is a marked script and a written plan you can check yourself.

faqs.question: Why do families pay for IB home tuition when a Kingdom international school already teaches the subject?
faqs.answer: Because a class cannot supply individual attention at any staffing level. A Diploma group of twenty-five in a subject with a heavy Internal Assessment component gives each student a small share of the teacher's marking time, and the students who most need their drafts questioned are the least likely to ask in front of peers. Add the possibility that a Higher and Standard Level group is taught together, or that a specialist left mid-course, and the gap becomes structural rather than a comment on the school. The fee buys the individual diagnosis and the marked practice a class timetable has no room for.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are most often taught by a non-specialist in Saudi international schools?
faqs.answer: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics HL and Chemistry HL are the hardest to staff anywhere, and in the Kingdom they compete with industry employment for the same graduates. Computer Science and the less common group two languages follow. Economics and Business Management are easier to staff and harder to staff well, because the gap between knowing the theory and knowing the mark scheme is wide and invisible on a curriculum vitae. The visible signs are a combined Higher and Standard Level class, a teacher change mid-course, or coursework returned with very little written on it.

faqs.question: What does a class size of twenty-five do to the amount of individual attention an IB student gets?
faqs.answer: It limits marking depth more than teaching quality. A teacher with five Diploma classes and coursework in each can give each student's draft a careful read, but not three careful reads with questions in between, which is what an Internal Assessment actually needs. Content delivery survives class size reasonably well; individual technique correction does not, because it requires someone to watch one student work through one question and interrupt at the right moment. That is precisely the thing one-to-one time buys, and why a few well-placed hours often outperform a term of extra group classes.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether a school in the Kingdom will actually run a Higher Level subject next year?
faqs.answer: Ask in writing, and ask four specific questions. Which Higher Level subjects will run next year as opposed to appearing in the brochure. Are any Higher and Standard Level groups taught together. Who teaches the Higher Level sciences and mathematics, and how long have they been in post. And how many students are currently in each Higher Level group. A school that answers openly is giving you useful information about itself as well as about the timetable, and the answers predict your tutoring budget better than any inspection summary.

faqs.question: Do schools in the Kingdom expect families to arrange IB support themselves?
faqs.answer: Many do, implicitly, without ever saying so. Where a Higher Level group is small, or a subject is offered as an online course the school hosts rather than teaches, the practical assumption is that a motivated family will cover the difference. Schools rarely state this because stating it looks like an admission. The useful move is to ask directly what support exists for a student falling behind in a specific subject — whether there is scheduled intervention, who runs it, and how often — and to treat a vague answer as the answer.

faqs.question: What does a fee for Internal Assessment support actually buy, and what can it never buy?
faqs.answer: It buys a reader who knows the criteria and will question the work: whether the research question can be answered with the data collected, whether the method was controlled, whether a graph shows what the sentence beneath it claims, and which descriptor a paragraph currently satisfies. It never buys writing. The work must be the student's own, and a provider who drafts it has sold a malpractice risk the student carries rather than a service. The highest-value hour is almost always the earliest one, spent testing scope before months are committed to a question that cannot be answered.

faqs.question: How many drafts of an IB Internal Assessment can a tutor formally review?
faqs.answer: The number of drafts a school supervisor may formally comment on is set by the school and the programme, not by a tutor, so the first step is to ask the subject teacher or the Diploma coordinator what their policy is. An outside tutor works inside that structure rather than parallel to it. In practice the useful pattern is fewer, earlier conversations: one on scope before data collection, one on analysis once there is something to analyse, and one on whether the write-up actually addresses each criterion. More rounds of comment on a late draft rarely moves the mark.

faqs.question: Can a tutor proofread an Extended Essay before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: A tutor can tell a student that a section is unclear, that a citation is missing, or that an argument does not follow, and ask them to fix it. A tutor cannot correct the text for them, because the submitted essay has to be the student's own work and the reflection process is meant to evidence that it is. The practical distinction is whether the tutor's hands touch the document. Naming a problem and leaving the solution with the student is teaching; rewriting the sentence is not, however small the change looks.

faqs.question: How do I know the Internal Assessment my child submits is genuinely their own work?
faqs.answer: Ask them to explain it to you without notes. A student who did the work can say what the research question asks, why that method was chosen, what the data showed and where the weaknesses are. A student who did not will describe the conclusion and stall on the method. Beyond that, keep the trail: dated drafts, a record of what each tutoring session discussed, and the student's own notes. Schools run plagiarism software and ask questions when something reads unlike a student's other work, and a documented process protects an honest student as much as it exposes a dishonest one.

faqs.question: Is paying for help with a Theory of Knowledge essay different from paying for subject tuition?
faqs.answer: Yes, in shape and in cost. Theory of Knowledge is short to support and disproportionately valuable, because it combines with the Extended Essay for up to three points that subject grades would otherwise have to make up. A few sessions on framing a knowledge question, choosing examples that genuinely illustrate it, and structuring an argument that reaches a position will usually do what is needed. The boundary is identical to any other assessed work: the thinking and the writing are the student's, and a tutor's job is to interrogate the argument rather than supply one.

faqs.question: What happens if a school in the Kingdom suspects malpractice on a Personal Project?
faqs.answer: The school investigates under its own and the programme's procedures, and the consequences fall on the student rather than on anyone they paid. The Personal Project is assessed heavily on process, and the journal is the evidence, which is why a project with a polished artefact and a thin record attracts attention. The protection is a visible trail: dated entries, decisions recorded as they were made, and a note of what any outside tutor discussed. A tutor who helps a student plan, question their own goal and record their reasoning is doing the job properly.

faqs.question: What does it cost to move a student from a British school in the Kingdom into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect, because the gap is technique rather than content. A student arriving from a British school generally has the subject knowledge and has to learn criterion-referenced marking, command terms treated as instructions, and a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service with no equivalent in their previous school. That is typically six to ten weeks of focused work rather than a term of weekly subject lessons, and it is better bought in the first term than discovered in a mock. The core components, not the subjects, are where the unplanned spending usually appears.

faqs.question: How much support does an American-curriculum student need to reach Higher Level standard in the sciences?
faqs.answer: Plan on eight to ten weeks of weekly, targeted work per subject rather than a holiday block. An American high school course usually introduces most of the topics but assesses them less deeply, so students arrive able to recognise material they cannot yet manipulate. The specific gaps in chemistry are energetics, equilibrium calculations and reasoned organic pathways; in physics they are the assumed mathematics and the precision expected in definitions. Measure against past-paper questions rather than textbook exercises, because the textbook will say the content is covered and the paper will say otherwise.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to support a student through a curriculum switch or to delay the move by a year?
faqs.answer: Where there is a genuine choice of timing, delaying to a clean boundary almost always costs less. The start of Year 10 and the start of the first Diploma year are both natural entry points where the cohort begins together and nothing has to be recovered. A move part-way through the Diploma is the expensive case: Internal Assessment work does not transfer cleanly between schools, subject combinations differ, and a student can lose a term of continuity in a two-year course. If the move is forced by relocation, budget for two subjects supported rather than one in the first term.

faqs.question: What subject gaps appear most often after a move into the Diploma, and which cost the most to close?
faqs.answer: Mathematics is the most expensive gap, because the subject builds vertically and an unclosed weakness compounds through every later topic. Physics is next for the same reason, with the added problem that its mathematics is assumed rather than taught. Chemistry is more modular and recovers faster. Biology is content-heavy but shallow in dependency, so a determined late start can work. The cheapest gaps to close are the technique ones that appear across every subject at once — command terms, mark allocations and time budgeting — which is why they are worth fixing before any subject-specific work.

faqs.question: Is IB home tuition cheaper than online tuition in the Kingdom once travel is counted?
faqs.answer: Advertised in-home rates sit above online rates for comparable subjects, and the reason is structural: an evening visit can consume two hours of a tutor's day for one paid hour, and that has to be recovered from the fee. Beyond the rate, the in-home format carries costs that do not appear on an invoice — a journey that runs late shortens the lesson, a cancellation is hard to reschedule because another journey has to be possible, and written work usually waits for the next visit instead of being marked the same evening. The larger difference, though, is the pool each format draws from.

ib-home-tuition.closingHeading: Price the hour, then price the year
ib-home-tuition.closingBody: If you take one number from this page, take the annual one rather than the hourly one. Weekly support in a single subject started early is roughly thirty hours across a school year, and at the advertised IB bands that is a few thousand riyals — much less than most families assume and far less than the late, intensive version of the same problem. The next step costs nothing: a free trial lesson built around a real past-paper question, followed by a written note on where the marks are actually going. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, with the work marked between sessions.

ib-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below is attached to one subject at one level, because the Higher Level extension material and the Standard Level course are different teaching jobs. Where a student needs two subjects, that is two specialists. The experience listed is deliberately specific: which board, which component, and what they have marked or taught.

intro.heading: Start with what the Diploma measures, then decide what help means
paragraphs: The Diploma is six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is graded one to seven, so the six carry up to forty-two points. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are graded A to E and combine through the published matrix to add up to three more, giving a maximum of forty-five. Twenty-four points is the minimum for the award, and there are further failing conditions beyond the total. That structure is the whole reason an IB student needs a different kind of tutor from a national-curriculum student.

Inside each subject the grade is split between externally marked papers and an internally assessed component that the school marks and the IB moderates. In the sciences and in both mathematics courses that internal component is a fifth of the grade; in several humanities and language subjects it is more. A parent who knows only the overall grade is seeing an average of parts that behave very differently. A student can be strong on content and weak on Paper 1 technique, or sound on the papers and adrift on their Internal Assessment, and those two problems need opposite responses.

The second thing that decides a mark is language, not knowledge. Every question carries a command term, and the mark scheme pays for the thing the command term asks for. Describe and explain are paid differently. Evaluate without a judgement caps itself. State does not want a paragraph. A capable student who answers the question they expected rather than the question printed in front of them loses marks steadily across a paper, and that is a teachable habit rather than a gap in ability. It is also the single most common thing a diagnostic session finds.

Around all of this sits a system a Saudi family has to work inside. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. At the end of the Diploma, a foreign or international certificate needs an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. None of that is taught to parents, and all of it has deadlines.

A note on the phrase at the top of this page, because it is the phrase families type. An IB home tutor, in the Saudi market, usually means someone who travels to a villa or a compound and teaches at the dining table. That market exists, it has real advantages, and this page compares it honestly in a table further down. What IB Gram sells is not that: lessons are one-to-one over live video, on a slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time, and nobody is sent to a Saudi address. In-home visiting is a service we offer only in India.

The argument for teaching this way in the Kingdom is not convenience. It is supply. The number of people inside driving distance of any given Saudi district who have taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and know how its Paper 3 mark scheme is applied is small. Remove the drive and that constraint goes away. A student in Madinah and a student in Al Khobar then choose from the same specialists, and the question becomes which tutor knows the paper rather than which tutor is nearby.
