ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four IB programmes run in the Kingdom and they are assessed in completely different ways, which is why a tutor who is excellent in one can be the wrong choice in another. The summaries below lead with the assessment model, because that is what determines whether outside teaching helps or simply adds hours.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across the groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each assessed through written papers marked externally plus an internally assessed component moderated by the IB. Higher Level courses carry additional content and, in several subjects, an extra paper. Grades run one to seven. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are graded A to E and feed the three-point matrix, and Creativity, Activity, Service must be completed for the award even though it carries no points.
programmes.countryNote: Most Saudi IB schools sit the May session, and the Diploma Programme coordinator is the person who confirms what that means for a particular student. The practical Saudi complication is staffing: a school may run one Higher Level group in a scarce subject, and if that teacher leaves mid-course the class is covered rather than replaced. That is the situation most Diploma families in the Kingdom are actually buying a tutor for.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Every subject is assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight, and the criterion marks convert to a one-to-seven grade through published boundaries. The final year carries the Personal Project, assessed on investigating, planning, taking action and reflecting. Some schools enter students for MYP eAssessment, which pairs on-screen examinations with ePortfolios. There are no traditional end-of-year papers in most subjects, which makes progress harder for a parent to read and makes criterion literacy the thing worth teaching.
programmes.countryNote: A Middle Years Programme student in the Kingdom is usually two years away from the Diploma and one year away from the subject choices that constrain it. The useful work at this stage is mechanical: algebraic fluency, written explanation, reading a criterion descriptor before starting, and handling a long task without a weekly deadline. None of that needs a specialist in a scarce subject, which is why it is also the cheapest stage to get right.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led and transdisciplinary, with no external examinations. Assessment is continuous, teacher-led and reported against learning outcomes, and the final year ends in the PYP exhibition, a collaborative piece the student presents. The model works well for conceptual understanding and reports badly in numbers, so the skills that later turn out to be missing are often the mechanical ones underneath the inquiry: written methods, number bonds, reading fluency and the stamina to write at length.
programmes.countryNote: Families relocating into the Kingdom part-way through a primary year meet this programme in the middle of an inquiry that assumes earlier work. Short, specific sessions on arithmetic and written explanation close that gap faster than general homework supervision, and because the sessions are short they fit a weekday evening in any Saudi city without touching the school run.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma Programme subjects paired with a career-related study, plus a core of personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and a reflective project. The Diploma subjects inside it are assessed exactly as they are in the full Diploma, with the same papers, the same command terms and the same internally assessed components. The reflective project is the student's own reasoning about an ethical issue arising from their career-related study.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is far less common in the Kingdom than the full Diploma. Where a family meets it, the subject teaching needed is identical to a Diploma student's, which widens the pool of tutors who can genuinely help. The reflective project needs the same treatment as an Extended Essay: questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts, and nothing beyond that.

ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each entry below leads with how the subject is assessed, because that is what a tutor has to teach to. Weightings differ by subject and by level, and the component where marks are lost is rarely the one a parent assumes. Where a weighting is not published here, it is because it varies by subject within the group.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level runs Paper 1 and Paper 2 at thirty per cent each, Paper 3 at twenty, and the Exploration at twenty. Paper 3 is two long scaffolded investigations and it punishes students who have only practised short routine questions. Proof, calculus technique and reading a multi-part stem are where the early sessions go. Standard Level drops Paper 3 and splits the two remaining papers at forty per cent each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-led and modelling-based, with the same paper structure as Analysis and Approaches at each level. The marks that go missing are interpretive rather than algebraic: a correct regression with no sentence explaining it in context scores below what the student expects. Statistics, graphical display calculator fluency and writing a conclusion in the language of the context are the three teachable wins.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Under the current guide, Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 forty-four, and the Scientific Investigation twenty. Paper 1B is data-based and exposes students who were never formally taught uncertainties and error propagation. The Higher Level extension topics are the second pressure point, because a school teaching Higher and Standard Level in one room often reaches them in the final term.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same split as Physics: Paper 1 at thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 at forty-four, Scientific Investigation at twenty. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are the recurring gaps, together with data booklet skills that no lesson formally covers. The fastest diagnostic is to have the student work a Paper 2 question aloud, because the fault is usually in how the answer is laid out rather than in what is known.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Marked on precise terminology more than any other science, with the same paper weightings. Extended-response questions are scored against named processes in sequence, so a fluent general account can score two out of six. Command terms matter more here than volume of content, and the Scientific Investigation needs a question narrow enough for the apparatus a school actually has.

subjects.name: Language A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: At Higher Level, Paper 1 is thirty-five per cent, Paper 2 twenty-five, the HL essay twenty and the Individual Oral twenty. At Standard Level the two papers are thirty-five each and the Individual Oral thirty. The usual problem is not reading ability but the absence of a method for the unseen paper that holds under timed conditions.

subjects.name: Language A: Literature
subjects.description: Same structure as Language and Literature, with studied literary works in place of non-literary texts. The HL essay is an independent piece on one studied work and is the component students leave latest. Paper 2 is comparative, and the mark scheme rewards a line of argument across two works rather than two separate essays stapled together.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Short-response and extended-response papers, with a data-response paper added at Higher Level, plus an internally assessed portfolio of commentaries. Almost all avoidable loss is in diagram work and evaluation: axes mislabelled on a diagram throws away marks that cost nothing to secure, and an essay that explains without weighing settles in the middle band however much it knows.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Written papers plus a solution developed and documented by the student. Higher Level adds a paper on the case study published for that session. Students who code well often score poorly because the papers reward precise description of algorithms and data structures in prose, and because the documentation of the solution is marked against criteria rather than on whether the program runs.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Written papers on the approaches plus an internally assessed experimental study. The examined skill is the use of named studies as evidence for a claim, in the way the command term asks. A student who can recount studies but cannot deploy them to answer a to what extent question will plateau in the middle bands no matter how much more content is added.

ib-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Where the Diploma is actually taught in the Kingdom
ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: IB World Schools are spread very unevenly across Saudi Arabia, and the IB publishes its own directory of authorised schools, which is the only list worth trusting. What follows is the distribution a tutoring request tends to reflect: the cities where several Diploma schools sit close together, and the places where one school is the whole provision.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest concentration of IB provision in the Kingdom, with several authorised schools running the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes. Riyadh is also roughly an hour across in traffic, so two families attending the same school can have completely different workable lesson hours.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, with IB and Cambridge schools interleaved along it. Families here often have a genuine choice of board, which means the commonest tutoring request is a student who has switched curriculum rather than a student who is simply behind.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: One labour and school market behaving as three cities, with families routinely living in one and schooling in another. The Diploma is available at more than one campus here, which makes this the easiest part of the Kingdom in which to find a Higher Level group that actually ran last term.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with international schooling attached to the workforce, including a Diploma option. The study week here is shaped by shift patterns and camp life as much as by the school timetable, so evening slots are negotiated around a household rather than around a child.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST campus
regions.note: A campus community north of Jeddah on the coast, served by The KAUST School. Provision is concentrated and the academic expectations around it are high, so tutoring requests here skew towards Higher Level sciences and mathematics rather than towards catching up.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: Roughly an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, which puts it outside a comfortable daily commute to the schools there. Distance is the binding constraint, and it is the honest case for teaching over a connection rather than over a road.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Makkah sits about 80km east of Jeddah, and families in both cities often look towards the Jeddah schools for international curricula. Local calendars bend around the Hajj and Umrah seasons, which is a practical scheduling fact rather than anything more, and it is worth agreeing slot changes in advance.

regions.name: 'Asir, Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: Places where international-curriculum provision is thin or new, and where a family may be the only one in their district with a Diploma student in the house. Mid-course arrivals into these regions are common, and catching up on an Internal Assessment started elsewhere is the usual first job.

schoolClusters.note: Schools named in IB directories for the capital include the following. Authorisation to offer an IB programme is granted by the IB to the school, and licensing of the school itself runs through the Ministry of Education; neither says anything about which Higher Level groups ran this term, which is the question a parent should ask directly.

The British International School of Jeddah is both an IB World School and a Cambridge school, Deutsche Internationale Schule Jeddah runs to Grade 12, and several others appear in IB listings alongside long-established international schools. A family choosing here is often choosing between boards as well as between schools.

schoolClusters.city: Eastern Province and the Red Sea campuses
schoolClusters.note: The International Schools Group operates several campuses in the Eastern Province, and the Diploma is offered at the American School of Dhahran and at ISG Jubail, though not at every campus. British and Cambridge curricula run alongside at other Dhahran schools, and The KAUST School serves the Thuwal campus community.

ib-home-tutor.modesIntro: Which of these fits depends on what the assessment structure says is wrong. A student losing marks on command terms needs something different from a student missing a topic, and a student whose Internal Assessment has stalled needs something different again. All of them run one-to-one over live video on a slot fixed to Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on one subject
modes.description: One subject, one specialist, the same hour each week across a term. This is the right shape when there is a content gap to close or a technique to rebuild, because both compound and both need the tutor to see the same student often enough to know what has stuck. It is also the arrangement that survives a school calendar without being cancelled every third week.

modes.title: Command-term and paper-technique work
modes.description: A short, sharply defined run of sessions for the student whose content knowledge is sound and whose marks are not. The sessions are built around past questions and their mark schemes read side by side, and the output is a repeatable method for each question type rather than more notes. Usually six to ten sessions is enough to see it in a mock.

This is deliberately not a drafting service. A provider who offers to produce the piece is offering academic malpractice, and a school that detects it has to report it to the IB.

It works when the syllabus is broadly in place and the student is underperforming their own knowledge, and it does not work as a substitute for a year of teaching.

sections.heading: What the Diploma assesses, paper by paper
paragraphs: Every decision about tutoring follows from the assessment model, so it is worth setting out properly rather than in a sentence. In each of the six subjects, part of the grade comes from papers marked by examiners the student will never meet, and part comes from a component the school marks and the IB moderates. The proportions differ by subject and by level. Knowing them changes what a sensible plan looks like, because a student with a weak internal component and strong papers is in a completely different position from the reverse.

The pattern across the groups is reasonably stable. In both mathematics courses the Higher Level grade is Paper 1 and Paper 2 at thirty per cent each, Paper 3 at twenty and the Exploration at twenty; at Standard Level, Paper 3 disappears and the two papers carry forty per cent each. In the sciences under the current guide, Paper 1 carries thirty-six per cent, Paper 2 forty-four, and the Scientific Investigation twenty, at both levels. In the language A courses, Higher Level adds an HL essay and reduces Paper 2, while Standard Level puts more weight on the Individual Oral.

What that table changes in practice is the order of work. A Standard Level mathematics student with a weak Exploration has a fifth of their grade exposed and no third paper to recover it on, so the Exploration comes first. A Higher Level science student in the autumn term of their final year has Paper 2 as the largest single component and almost half the grade riding on long-answer technique, which makes extended-response practice the priority over another pass through the content. The weightings are not trivia; they are the plan.

One caution worth putting in writing. Weightings are revised when the IB publishes a new subject guide, and a tutor working from the previous guide will prepare a student for the wrong paper structure. Ask any prospective tutor which guide they are teaching to and what changed in it. A tutor who cannot answer that question about their own subject is working from memory, and memory in this system goes out of date.

sections.heading: The core, and the three points nobody plans for
paragraphs: The core is where Diploma families lose points they did not know were available. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are each graded A to E, and the two grades together produce up to three points through a published matrix. Creativity, Activity, Service carries no points at all but must be completed, and a student who has not completed it does not receive the Diploma regardless of their subject grades.

Three points sounds small until you look at where it sits. A student on thirty-four points with two core points is a different applicant from the same student on thirty-two, and the core is also the part of the Diploma that is most often left until it is too late to move. The Extended Essay is an independent piece of up to four thousand words on a question the student sets, supervised inside the school, and submitted with reflections that are themselves assessed. The Theory of Knowledge course ends in an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay.

The useful thing about the core, from a tutoring point of view, is that it is mostly process. An Extended Essay fails to reach the top bands far more often because the research question was unanswerable than because the student could not write. A question that is too broad, or that needs data the student cannot obtain, is a structural problem that no amount of drafting repairs. Spotting it early is the highest-value hour anyone spends on the core, and it is a conversation rather than a lesson.

What a tutor may do here is narrow and worth stating. They may discuss the question, explain what the criteria reward, ask why a paragraph is where it is, and point out that a conclusion does not follow from the evidence. They may not write any part of it, restructure it, or correct its prose line by line. The reflections exist precisely so that a supervisor can see the student's own thinking develop, and a polished essay attached to reflections that say nothing is the pattern schools are trained to notice.

sections.heading: Command terms, and the difference between knowing and being paid
paragraphs: Ask any experienced IB examiner where the marks go and the answer is rarely content. It is the gap between what a student knows and what they are paid for, and command terms are the mechanism. Each question opens with a verb that tells the examiner which mark scheme to apply, and the scheme pays for that operation and nothing else. A student who explains when the question says state has written too much for no extra credit. A student who describes when the question says evaluate has capped their own mark.

The terms are published and there are not many of them. State, outline, describe, explain, analyse, discuss, evaluate, to what extent, justify, compare and contrast, distinguish, deduce, derive, show that. Each has a specific expectation, and the expectations are different in a science paper from a history paper. The work with a student is mechanical: take a past question, identify the term, say in one sentence what the scheme will pay for, then write the answer to that specification and check it against the real scheme.

The second half of this is the mark allocation. A six-mark question in an extended-response paper is not a request for six sentences; it is a request for a specific number of distinct, creditable points, often with one mark reserved for a judgement or a link. A student who writes beautifully and makes three points scores three. This is why past-paper practice without the mark scheme is close to worthless, and why handing a student a mark scheme after they have answered is the single highest-return habit in this system.

Parents sometimes worry that this is teaching to the test rather than teaching the subject. It is worth saying plainly: the command terms are the subject, in the sense that the discipline of distinguishing description from evaluation is exactly what the course claims to develop. A student who learns to answer the question printed in front of them is a better reader and a better writer afterwards, not a more cynical one. The marks are a side effect.

sections.heading: Grade boundaries and predicted grades, and why neither is a promise
paragraphs: Grade boundaries are set after papers have been marked, not before, and they move between sessions. They are set so that a grade means the same standard across sessions even when one paper has turned out harder than another. That is the whole point of them, and it is also why no tutor can tell you what mark your child needs for a seven. Anyone who quotes a fixed boundary as a target is quoting last session's figure and presenting it as this session's.

What that means for planning is simple. Target a margin, not a number. If a student is working at the bottom of a grade band on past papers using previous boundaries, they are not safely in that band, because a one-mark shift in the boundary takes it away. The honest version of a target is a performance level with headroom, and that framing also changes how a student revises: they stop optimising for a threshold and start closing the specific gaps that are costing them marks.

Predicted grades are a separate thing and are often misunderstood. A predicted grade is the school's professional judgement of what a student is likely to achieve, submitted to the IB and used by universities when they make conditional offers. It is produced by the subject teachers, usually from mock performance, coursework and classwork. It is not a negotiation, it is not a target, and a tutor has no standing to set one. What a tutor can do is make sure the evidence the school is judging on is the student's best, which means the mocks matter more than families assume.

If a predicted grade looks wrong, the conversation is with the school and it should be evidence-based rather than aggrieved. Bring the specific pieces of work, ask which components the prediction rests on, and ask what would have to change for it to be revised. Schools do revise predictions when the evidence moves. They do not revise them because a family is unhappy, and a tutor who promises to get a prediction lifted is promising something they cannot deliver.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor means in this market, and what we actually do
paragraphs: The phrase at the top of this page is the phrase parents search, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. In the Saudi market, an IB home tutor normally means a private tutor who travels to the family's villa, apartment or compound and teaches at the table. It is the default model in much of the Kingdom, it is easy to supervise because you are in the room, and for a younger child it is often genuinely the best arrangement. Nothing here argues otherwise.

What it costs is worth knowing before you compare anything. Tutor-marketplace guides put general private tuition for senior-school examination subjects in the Kingdom at SAR 200 an hour and upwards, with primary-level work advertised lower, and tutoring companies list IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180 with Higher Level and premium tracks around SAR 200 to 220. Those are advertised rates published by vendors, not verified averages, and in-home arrangements price the travel on top of them, whether or not the invoice itemises it. A tutor crossing Riyadh for a one-hour lesson spends most of an hour each way.

The constraint that matters more than price is supply. An in-home arrangement limits you to people who already live within a reasonable drive of your district, and the supply of people who have taught a specific Higher Level subject and know how its mark scheme is applied is thin everywhere in the Kingdom. For a scarce subject, a family can search locally for weeks and find nobody. That is the real reason this page exists, and it is not a sales argument so much as an arithmetic one.

So here is what IB Gram does, plainly. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered over live video, on a slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time so it does not drift when a tutor's own country changes its clocks. We do not send anyone to a Saudi address, and in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. The comparison below is laid out so you can weigh the two models yourself rather than take our word for which is better; for a student needing a scarce Higher Level specialist, the right column tends to win on availability alone.

sections.heading: Who licenses your school, and what that licence does not cover
paragraphs: Saudi families are given almost no map of the bodies that stand behind their child's education, and the gaps in that map are where bad decisions get made. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education. School evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services both for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. The IB separately authorises a school to offer its programmes, which is a different process again, run by the IB and not by any Saudi body.

What none of those processes covers is a tutor. There is no Saudi licensing regime for private tutoring, no register of approved IB tutors, and no accreditation a tutoring company can hold from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. IB Gram holds none of those things and does not claim them. Any provider implying otherwise is misrepresenting the system, and that is a useful test to apply while comparing options.

The second gap is subtler and matters more day to day. A school can be fully licensed, well evaluated, authorised to run the Diploma, and still unable to staff Higher Level Physics this term because one teacher left. Institutional approval describes the institution. It says nothing about which groups ran, how many students were in them, or whether Higher and Standard Level are being taught in the same room. Those are the facts that predict where your child will need outside teaching, and the only way to get them is to ask.

So ask the specific version of the question before enrolling or before deciding a subject is safe. Which Higher Level subjects ran last term. How many students were in each. Is Higher Level taught separately from Standard Level. Who teaches the Extended Essay supervision and how many students do they supervise. A school that answers those straight is telling you something good about itself, and a school that deflects to its accreditations has answered a different question.

sections.heading: Equivalency, and what a Saudi university will ask for
paragraphs: A Diploma is not automatically a Saudi secondary certificate. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent, and that applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. It is administrative rather than academic, and it is the step families discover late, usually from another parent rather than from anyone official.

Alongside it sit the Qiyas tests, delivered by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and can be sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Its content follows the Saudi national curriculum, which is the fact that matters most to an international-curriculum family.

That is why Diploma students frequently find Tahsili harder than their own examinations. The material overlaps substantially with what they have studied, but the framing does not: topic order differs, terminology differs, the expected method for a question differs, and the test does not reward the extended reasoning an IB paper is built around. A student with a strong Higher Level science grade can still be caught out, and the preparation needed is translation work rather than new learning. It should start well before the final term, not alongside the papers.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school results with the Qiyas tests, the weightings differ by university and by programme, and competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on Tahsili. Some also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept. No threshold or formula appears on this page because third-party sources disagree with one another and a family acting on a wrong figure loses a year. Read the criteria on the university's own site, and start the paperwork earlier than feels necessary.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, because the IB treats it as a condition of the award
paragraphs: Academic honesty in the IB is not a style guideline. It is a condition of the award, investigated by the IB rather than only by the school, and a finding of malpractice can cost a student the Diploma rather than a grade. That is why this section is specific about what a tutor may and may not do, and why a provider offering to produce assessed work is offering something that endangers the student rather than helping them.

What a tutor may do with an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project is teach the skills the task needs, explain the published criteria it will be marked against, question a draft the student has written, and hand it back for the student to change in their own words. No tutor on this platform will write the Extended Essay, redraft an Internal Assessment or produce a Personal Project for a student. That boundary is also why the feedback cycles described above are spaced rather than continuous: the student needs time to do the work themselves between sessions.

The line in practice is clearer than parents fear. Helping a student narrow a research question so it can actually be answered is legitimate supervision and is what a school supervisor does too. Explaining what an uncertainty analysis is, or showing the difference between describing and evaluating in a mark scheme, is teaching. Supplying a paragraph, restructuring a draft, or correcting the prose of an assessed piece line by line is not, and plagiarism software will not catch it, which is exactly why schools interview students about their own work.

Keep the evidence trail, even when nobody expects a problem. The student's own dated drafts in their own files, a note of what each session discussed, and feedback the student then acted on themselves. That record is what protects a student if authorship is ever questioned. For a Middle Years Programme family the same reasoning covers the Personal Project, which is assessed on investigating, planning, taking action and reflecting, all of which only the student can do. If the work suddenly looks polished and the student cannot explain it, that is the signal to act on.

sections.heading: The first month: diagnosis, plan, and what a report should say
paragraphs: The first session is a diagnostic and should look like one. The tutor sets a past question from the student's own subject and level, then watches how they approach it: whether they read the command term, how they lay an answer out, where they stop, what they reach for when stuck. The point is not whether they get it right. A student who arrives at the correct answer by a method that will fail on a longer question has a problem the mark alone would hide.

By the end of that session a parent should be able to repeat back what the tutor thinks is wrong and roughly how long they think it takes to fix. Vagueness here is the warning sign to act on. A tutor who says the student needs to build confidence has not diagnosed anything; a tutor who says the student is losing two marks a question by answering explain questions as describe questions has. The second kind of statement is checkable against the next piece of work, and that is the test.

The plan that follows should have two or three specific targets, not a sweep of the syllabus. Targets that work read like a behaviour rather than a grade: annotate the command term before writing, show the substitution line in every calculation, write a judgement sentence in every evaluate answer. Targets that do not work read like an aspiration. By the end of the first month a parent should be able to name what their child is now doing differently, and if they cannot, the arrangement is wrong rather than the child.

Reporting should be plain and frequent enough to be useful. A short note after each session saying what was covered, what was set and what the tutor wants done before the next one. A fuller view at the end of a term with a judgement on whether to continue. A tutor who reports only good news is not reporting. If the right recommendation is to stop, to drop to one subject, or to move a Higher Level subject down before the school's deadline passes, a family should hear it from the tutor rather than infer it from a results sheet.

sections.heading: When to start, counted by year group
paragraphs: The question families ask most is whether it is too late. The honest answer depends less on the calendar than on what is still changeable, so the table below is organised around that: what is being decided at each stage, what support should actually be doing, and what has already closed. Reading it backwards from the final row is the fastest way to see where a particular student sits.

The pattern across year groups is that early help is cheap and late help is narrow. A Middle Years Programme student needs mechanical work on fluency and criterion literacy, which any strong teacher can provide and which compounds for years. A student in the first Diploma year can still change a level, choose a better Internal Assessment topic and rebuild technique while there is time for it to show up in mocks. A student in the final term can fix technique and triage, and cannot learn two years of content.

Two decisions are worth flagging because they have hard internal deadlines that nobody chases a family about. The first is a Higher to Standard Level move, which schools allow up to a published internal cut-off and not afterwards. The second is subject entry, where the school's examinations officer holds the real date and it falls months before the papers. Both are decisions where a term of honest tutoring evidence is genuinely useful, and both are irreversible once the window shuts.

The last row matters more than it looks. After results, there is a short window in which a remark, a resit or a November entry is still realistic, and families routinely spend it deliberating. The decision needs to be made in days, not weeks, and it is better made with a tutor who has seen the student's actual papers than on the basis of a disappointing grade alone. A single subject, a short decisive block, and a clear view of whether the mark is recoverable.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not the year group. Chemistry Higher Level, Paper 2 extended response, autumn term of the final year is a brief a specialist can act on. A request for help with science is not. If the problem is an Internal Assessment, say which criterion the school has flagged, because that changes who the right tutor is.

process.title: We propose one named specialist
process.description: One tutor for one subject at one level, with their teaching and marking experience described specifically enough to question. Two weak subjects means two tutors. A single person offered for Physics Higher Level and Language A at once is a staffing convenience rather than a match, and it is reasonable to say so.

process.title: A free diagnostic trial lesson
process.description: A working session rather than an introduction, built on a past question from the student's own board and level. A parent is welcome to sit in. You should leave it able to state what the tutor thinks is wrong and how long they expect it to take. No payment is taken before that session happens.

process.title: Fix the slot in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: The hour is agreed in Saudi local time, so a tutor in a country that changes its clocks absorbs the shift instead of the family rearranging a school night twice a year. Sunday to Wednesday evenings work best; Thursday is the weakest slot of the week and Friday or Saturday blocks are available but need asking for early.

process.title: Two or three behavioural targets, then weekly work
process.description: Targets written as things the student does, not grades they reach: annotate the command term, show the substitution line, write a judgement sentence. Work is set between sessions and marked before the next one, and a short note goes to the parent each time saying what was covered and what was set.

process.title: A term-end judgement, including stopping
process.description: A view on what has moved, what has not, and whether to continue. If the right answer is to stop, to reduce to one subject, or to move a Higher Level subject down before the school's internal deadline, the tutor says so. A report that only contains good news is not a report.

whyPoints.title: Built on the assessment model, not on hours
whyPoints.description: The plan starts from which component is losing marks and how much of the grade it carries. A Standard Level Exploration worth a fifth of the grade and a Higher Level Paper 2 worth almost half need different work in a different order, and a provider selling hours rather than diagnosis cannot tell the difference.

whyPoints.title: Command terms and mark schemes taught explicitly
whyPoints.description: Past questions are answered and then marked against the published scheme in front of the student, every time. The output is a repeatable method per question type, written down by the student. This is the gap between knowing a subject and being paid for knowing it, and it is the most common finding of a first session.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the paper, so geography stops mattering
whyPoints.description: Removing the drive removes the real constraint, which is how few people inside any Saudi district have taught a particular Higher Level course. A family in Al Ahsa and a family in Riyadh choose from the same specialists, and the question becomes which tutor knows the component rather than who lives nearby.

whyPoints.title: Straight about the system around you
whyPoints.description: Schools are licensed by the Ministry of Education and evaluated through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission; tutors are licensed by nobody. IB Gram holds no accreditation or authorisation from any board or regulator and says so. There is no office in the Kingdom either, and the page says that rather than implying one.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Feedback on a draft the student wrote, in the student's own words, with the criteria read against it. No writing, no redrafting, no line-by-line correction of assessed prose. Academic honesty is a condition of the Diploma award, not a formality, so this boundary protects the student rather than inconveniencing them.

whyPoints.title: No claim without evidence behind it
whyPoints.description: No success rates, no star ratings, no tutor headcounts, no grade promises. Grade boundaries move between sessions, so nobody can tell you the mark your child needs for a seven, and nobody here will. Every SAR figure quoted is an advertised vendor rate, labelled as such, and is not our price.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 assess in a Higher Level subject that Paper 1 and Paper 2 do not?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 exists to test sustained work on an unfamiliar problem rather than recall across a syllabus. In Higher Level mathematics it is two long scaffolded investigations carrying twenty per cent of the grade, where each part depends on the one before, so an early error propagates. In other subjects it may be based on a case study or an option topic published for that session. The common feature is length: a student trained only on short routine questions loses the thread, and the fix is practice on whole problems rather than more topics.

faqs.question: How much of a Diploma subject grade is decided inside the school rather than by an examiner?
faqs.answer: In both mathematics courses and in the sciences, a fifth: the Exploration and the Scientific Investigation each carry twenty per cent. In several language and humanities subjects it is more, with internally assessed orals, portfolios and investigations reaching a quarter or a third of the grade. The school marks these and the IB moderates the marking, which can move a whole cohort up or down. For a parent this matters because that portion of the grade is visible months before results, and therefore fixable.

faqs.question: What is a command term, and which ones cost IB students the most marks?
faqs.answer: A command term is the verb a question opens with, and it tells the examiner which mark scheme to apply. The expensive ones are the pairs students treat as synonyms. Describe against explain, where explain requires a mechanism or a reason. Analyse against evaluate, where evaluate requires a judgement that is actually stated. To what extent, which requires a position and a limitation. A student who answers explain questions as describe questions typically gives away a mark or two a question, which across a paper is a grade.

faqs.question: Why do IB grade boundaries move between sessions, and what does that mean for setting a target?
faqs.answer: Boundaries are set after marking, so that a grade represents the same standard even when one paper proves harder than another. That is their purpose, and it is why no tutor can tell you the mark needed for a particular grade. The practical consequence is to target a margin rather than a threshold: a student sitting at the bottom of a band against last session's boundaries is not safely inside it. Aim for headroom, and spend the time closing specific mark-losing habits rather than optimising towards a number that will move.

faqs.question: What exactly is a predicted grade, and who decides it?
faqs.answer: It is the school's professional judgement of what a student is likely to achieve, submitted to the IB and used by universities for conditional offers. Subject teachers produce it, normally from mock performance, coursework and classwork. It is not a target, not a negotiation, and not something a tutor has standing to set. What a tutor can do is make sure the evidence the school judges on is the student's best, which is why mocks deserve more preparation than families usually give them.

faqs.question: How do the three core points work, and can a student lose the Diploma on the core alone?
faqs.answer: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are each graded A to E, and the pair maps onto a published matrix that awards up to three points. A student can also lose the award through the core: a failing condition applies to the lowest core outcomes, and Creativity, Activity, Service must be completed or the Diploma is not issued whatever the subject grades are. The core is therefore worth planning rather than leaving to the school calendar, and it is the part most often left too late to move.

faqs.question: What is the minimum point total for the Diploma, and what else can stop the award?
faqs.answer: Twenty-four points is the minimum, but the total alone is not sufficient. The IB publishes additional failing conditions covering a grade one in any subject, too many low grades, minimum totals across Higher and Standard Level subjects, the lowest outcomes in Theory of Knowledge or the Extended Essay, and completion of Creativity, Activity, Service. A student can reach the point total and still not be awarded the Diploma. Your school's Diploma Programme coordinator holds the current conditions and should be asked directly rather than relied on from memory.

faqs.question: What happens in the first diagnostic session with an IB home tutor?
faqs.answer: The tutor sets a past question from the student's own subject and level and watches them work it, rather than teaching anything. What is being observed is method: whether the command term was read, how the answer is laid out, where the student stops, what they reach for when stuck. Getting the right answer by a method that fails on longer questions is a finding, not a pass. A parent is welcome to sit in, and should leave able to state what the tutor thinks is wrong.

faqs.question: What should a tutor's first written report to a parent actually contain?
faqs.answer: Three things: what was covered, what was set, and one specific, checkable observation about how the student works. A useful observation names a behaviour and its cost, such as omitting the substitution line and losing method marks. A useless one says the student needs to build confidence. The report should be short enough to be read in a minute and specific enough that you can verify it against the next piece of work yourself. Anything longer is usually filling space.

faqs.question: How soon after starting should a parent expect to see something measurable change?
faqs.answer: Behaviour changes inside a month if the targets were specific; marks move more slowly and unevenly. Within four sessions you should see the student doing something differently on paper, such as annotating command terms or setting calculations out in full. A grade shift usually shows at the next assessed piece or mock, which may be a term away. If nothing has changed in how the work looks after a month, the problem is the arrangement rather than the timescale, and it is worth saying so early.

faqs.question: What do we do if the first tutor is competent but the student will not work with them?
faqs.answer: Change the tutor, and do it at two or three lessons rather than at ten. Competence and fit are separate things, and a student who has decided they dislike a tutor will not learn from them however good the teaching is. This is not a failure of either side and does not need justifying at length. A rematch from the same pool costs nothing structural because there is no travel arrangement to rebuild, which is one practical advantage of teaching this way.

faqs.question: When should support start for a student entering the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: The useful window is the break before it begins and the first term inside it. Before it starts, the work is bridging: algebraic fluency for Higher Level mathematics or the sciences, and reading at length for the language A courses. In the first term, the work is technique, because command terms and mark schemes are new and the habits formed now run for two years. Starting in the first Diploma year also leaves time for a level change if the choice turns out to be wrong, which is the single most valuable option a family has.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in the second Diploma year, in the term before the papers?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the job changes. Two years of content cannot be taught in a term, so the work becomes triage: identify the two subjects where marks are most recoverable, drill command terms and timed technique, and secure whatever part of the internally assessed component is still open. Expect a tutor to tell you honestly which subject is not worth the hours. A provider who takes on five subjects in the final term is selling hours rather than giving advice.

faqs.question: What should a Middle Years Programme student be building before the Diploma starts?
faqs.answer: Four mechanical things, all cheap to fix at this stage and expensive later. Algebraic fluency, because every Higher Level science and both mathematics courses assume it. Writing at length without a weekly deadline, because the Extended Essay and the Internal Assessments do not come with one. Reading a criterion descriptor before starting a task. And handling a long project in stages, which is what the Personal Project is actually assessing. None of that needs a scarce specialist.

faqs.question: How does the help a first-year Diploma student needs differ from what a final-year student needs?
faqs.answer: In the first year the work is structural and the options are open: technique being built from scratch, Internal Assessment topics chosen well, levels still changeable, habits forming that will run for two years. In the final year the structure is fixed and the work is executional: timed papers, mark schemes, command terms, mock preparation because predictions rest on it, and deciding what to leave. The same tutor can do both, but a plan written for one and applied to the other wastes most of a term.

ib-home-tutor.closingHeading: Tell us the component, not the year group
ib-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Saudi Arabia, the brief that gets you the right person names the subject, the level and the component that is losing marks. We will propose one named specialist, run a free diagnostic trial lesson you are welcome to sit in on, and fix the slot in Arabia Standard Time so it holds through the year. Teaching is one-to-one over live video; nobody is sent to a Saudi address, and in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. If the specialist your child needs is not free at an hour you can use, we will tell you that rather than offer someone who does not know the paper.

ib-home-tutor-fees.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma, MYP and IGCSE subjects one-to-one over live video. Each profile names the syllabus and the level the tutor actually teaches, because that is the single biggest driver of the hourly figure you will be quoted anywhere in the Kingdom.

intro.heading: Judge the fee against what you can measure by the sixth lesson
paragraphs: Start from the end. A fee is defensible if, six or eight lessons in, you can point at something that moved and say what moved it. For a Diploma student that is usually a mark on a specific past paper under timed conditions, a criterion letter on an Internal Assessment draft, or the number of command terms the student now answers correctly rather than approximately. For an IGCSE student it is often simpler: the tier they are entered for, and whether the mark on Paper 2 has stopped collapsing in the last twenty minutes. If nobody in the arrangement can name the measure, the hourly rate is not the problem - the absence of a target is.

That is an unusual way to open a page about money, but it is the only way the SAR figures further down make sense. Advertised rates in the Kingdom span a factor of six. A budget platform markets IGCSE one-to-one online from around SAR 35 an hour; tutoring companies list IB subject work from around SAR 180 and premium Higher Level tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220; tutor-marketplace guides put general Riyadh private tuition at around SAR 50 for primary and over SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Those are advertised numbers published by the sellers, not a market average, and none of them is what IB Gram charges.

The second thing the figures do not tell you is whether the arrangement will survive the term. Saudi school weeks run Sunday to Thursday. A Diploma student with four Internal Assessments in progress has perhaps three usable evening slots, and those slots have to line up with a tutor who is often not in the Kingdom. A tutor in India sits two and a half hours ahead; a tutor in the United Kingdom sits two or three hours behind depending on whether their country has changed its clocks. The Kingdom does not change its clocks at all, so any slot agreed in the other party's local time drifts twice a year.

This is where most fee comparisons quietly fail. A cheaper tutor whose own working day ends before your child gets home from school produces cancellations, and a cancelled lesson has an hourly rate of infinity. A slightly dearer tutor whose working week genuinely overlaps a Riyadh or Dhahran evening produces thirty consecutive sessions. Over a Diploma year the second arrangement is cheaper per unit of progress, and it is the only one of the two that can still be running in the eight weeks before the May session when it matters most.

ib-home-tutor-fees.programmesIntro: Fees track the programme and the level far more closely than they track the city. These are the four IB programmes Saudi families encounter, with what each one demands of a paid tutor and what that does to the rate you will be quoted.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is transdisciplinary and inquiry-led. There are no external examinations, so paid support here is about literacy, number fluency and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud rather than about papers. Sessions are short, frequent and concrete. A tutor working well at this stage spends as much time with reading stamina and written sentence structure as with arithmetic, because those are what the MYP will immediately start charging interest on.
programmes.countryNote: PYP rates sit at the bottom of every published Saudi band - tutor-marketplace guides put general primary tuition in Riyadh at around SAR 50 an hour. Families usually buy two short sessions a week rather than one long one, and the slot problem is easier here: a primary child is home by mid-afternoon, which opens hours that a Diploma student simply does not have.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against four criteria per subject, each with its own descriptors, and the Personal Project runs in the final year. Marks here are earned by matching the descriptor, not by knowing more content, which is why strong students sometimes score mid-band for years. A tutor earns their fee at this stage by teaching the student to read a criterion strand and write to it, and by closing arithmetic and algebra gaps before the Diploma makes them expensive.
programmes.countryNote: MYP tutoring in the Kingdom is quoted close to general senior-school rates rather than Diploma rates, which makes it the best value stage in the whole sequence. A Saudi family that funds two terms of MYP mathematics usually spends less than one term of DP1 Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL repair, and the second is the bill that arrives if the first is skipped.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal Assessment carries a substantial share of most subject grades and is produced across the two years rather than in an examination hall. The Diploma is where scarcity pricing bites: a Physics HL or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL specialist is quoted higher than a Standard Level counterpart everywhere, and that gap is about supply rather than effort.
programmes.countryNote: Tutoring companies listing IB work in Riyadh advertise from around SAR 180 an hour, with Higher Level and premium tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Saudi Diploma candidates sit the May session, so demand concentrates in the spring term and families who leave booking until then compete for the same narrow Sunday-to-Thursday evening slots as everybody else.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines a career-related study with at least two Diploma courses, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills component. It appears in a small number of international schools rather than across the system, so a family choosing it is usually choosing a specific school. Paid support is normally for the Diploma courses inside it, plus structure and deadline management for the reflective project.
programmes.countryNote: Because CP cohorts in the Kingdom are small, the local pool of tutors who have taught the exact combination is smaller still, and that is the main thing a family pays for. Online delivery matters more here than at any other stage: the right person for a CP student in Yanbu or Jubail is almost never within reach of the school gate.

ib-home-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Subject choice moves the fee more than anything except level. These are the courses Saudi families most often buy help with, and the specific reason each one is priced where it is.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The highest-demand and scarcest Diploma subject in the Kingdom, which is why it tops every advertised band. HL adds proof, complex numbers and vectors on top of an already heavy core, and Paper 3 asks for extended reasoning rather than recall. Fees reflect how few tutors can teach the HL extension properly rather than how hard the SL course is.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy and modelling-led, with a graphical calculator assumed throughout. Cheaper to staff than Analysis and Approaches because more teachers can cover it, but HL hypothesis testing and the modelling paper still need somebody who has marked them. Students often arrive thinking this route is the easy one and lose marks on exactly that assumption.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Priced near the top because the HL extension topics have no Standard Level equivalent and because the subject punishes weak algebra. Marks disappear in the extended-response questions where students describe an effect instead of deriving it. A tutor who has marked the paper is worth the premium here more visibly than in almost any other subject.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and the data-booklet skills are the three places Saudi Diploma students most often need outside teaching. The internal assessment is where many grades are quietly lost, because a weak research question limits the mark ceiling before any data is collected. Rates sit just below Physics in most published listings.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy rather than technique-heavy, so the fee premium is smaller, but the command terms are examined strictly: outline, explain and discuss carry different mark expectations and students treat them identically. Statistical handling in the internal assessment is the component that most often needs a specialist rather than a general science teacher.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the HL quantitative paper are the two cost drivers. Students who write fluent paragraphs without a labelled, correctly shifted diagram score well below their reading level. The internal assessment commentaries need current articles and a tight link to one syllabus concept, which is coaching work rather than content delivery.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Priced moderately but needed constantly, especially by students arriving from a national-curriculum or American school. The guided textual analysis rewards close reading of an unseen passage under time pressure, and the individual oral needs a global issue that can actually be sustained for ten minutes. Both are learnable, which is why this subject responds quickly to a short block of lessons.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Widely taught in the Kingdom, so the tutor pool is larger and advertised rates are lower than for the sciences. The difficulty for an international-school student is the gap between conversational fluency at home and the written register the assessment expects. Families often underestimate how much writing practice the higher levels demand.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study discipline is the whole subject. The pre-released material for Paper 2 at Higher Level has to be worked over for weeks rather than read once, and the internal assessment demands primary or secondary research the student gathers themselves. Rates sit mid-band, and a short intensive block before the series is usually better value here than a year of weekly lessons.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Rarely bought by the hour and frequently the cheapest points on the table. The exhibition and the essay both reward precision about knowledge claims rather than general cleverness, and the matrix with the Extended Essay can swing the Diploma total. A handful of well-timed sessions on the essay prompt is a small bill against the points at stake.

ib-home-tutor-fees.regionsTitle: What the fee looks like from different parts of the Kingdom
ib-home-tutor-fees.regionsIntro: The hourly figure is roughly national, but the value of online delivery is not. Distance from a deep tutor pool is what decides whether a family has any realistic alternative, and that varies enormously across the Kingdom.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest local pool and the only market where in-home tutoring is genuinely available at scale - which is why every published Saudi rate guide quotes Riyadh numbers. The city is about an hour across in traffic, so an in-home tutor prices travel into the rate and a 4pm slot is rarely really 4pm.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, with international schools spread along it. Families in the northern districts pay the same advertised rates as anyone else but wait longer for a tutor willing to cross the city, which pushes evening slots later than the student can usefully work.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market behaving as a single conurbation, with families routinely living in one city and schooling in another. The local pool is real but narrow at Higher Level, so the scarcity premium in advertised rates bites harder here than in Riyadh.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities where the school choice is small and the subject-specialist pool smaller. A Higher Level Physics or Chemistry tutor is often simply not resident, so the comparison is not cheap against expensive - it is online against nothing, and families price it accordingly.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST campus community
regions.note: A concentrated, academically confident community north of Jeddah with a campus school. Parents here usually know exactly which component they want addressed, which makes short diagnostic-led blocks the common purchase rather than open-ended weekly lessons.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Two 'Asir cities about 25km apart sharing one catchment at high altitude. Distance from the central markets means a resident IB specialist in a scarce subject is unusual, and families who try to buy locally often end up paying a general tutor senior-school rates for the wrong expertise.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: The north-west, where families relocating for work frequently arrive part-way through a course. Catching up mid-Diploma is the expensive scenario in this whole market, and it is the one where a fixed online slot pays for itself fastest because nothing local can be arranged quickly.

regions.name: Al Ahsa, Qatif and Ras Tanura
regions.note: An hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, or sitting just outside it on the coast. Commuting to a tutor in Dammam costs an evening, and that lost evening is a real part of the price of in-home tuition that no rate card shows.

schoolClusters.note: The widest spread of curricula in the Kingdom and the only city where several schools run more than one IB programme. Families here are usually choosing between schools rather than between cities, and the subject a school cannot staff is the usual reason a paid tutor appears.

British, IB, German, American and Indian curricula all operate within the same city, and the differences in term structure matter for when support should start. Makkah sits roughly 80km east and Thuwal to the north, both inside the same practical catchment for online lessons.

The International Schools Group operates several campuses across the conurbation and the Diploma runs at some but not all of them, which is the detail families miss when they assume a move within the cluster keeps the curriculum intact.

modes.description: The default and the cheapest per unit of progress over a full course, because the tutor builds a picture of the student rather than restarting every time. sections.heading: What you should be able to measure before the second invoice
paragraphs: A fee is a hypothesis: that paying this much per hour will produce something you could not have had otherwise. The way to test it is to fix the measure before the lessons start, and to pick one a tutor cannot flatter. A past paper marked to the published scheme is the usual choice for a Diploma or IGCSE student, because the mark comes from the scheme rather than from the person teaching. Criterion-referenced work is almost as good: an Internal Assessment draft scored strand by strand against the criteria gives a before-and-after that survives scrutiny.

Six to eight lessons is the right window. Shorter than that and you are measuring noise - a bad week at school, a cold, a single unlucky paper. Much longer and you have funded a term before finding out whether the arrangement works. Inside that window a good tutor should be able to tell you three things: which specific topics or skills were costing marks, which of them have closed, and which need longer than a term. The third answer is the one that marks out an honest tutor, because the pressure is always to claim everything is fixable.

What should not count as evidence: the student enjoying the lessons, the student feeling more confident, or a predicted grade moving. The first two matter but they are not what you are buying. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the school, and it moves for many reasons that have nothing to do with a paid tutor. No tutor can promise a grade, a score or an improvement, and any provider offering a guaranteed result is describing something that is not theirs to give. Measure the work, not the mood.
bullets: Agree the measure before the first paid lesson, in writing if possible
Use a past paper marked to the published scheme, or criterion-referenced strands
Six to eight lessons is long enough to judge and short enough to stop
Ask which gaps will not close this term - the answer tells you who you are dealing with

sections.heading: Advertised IB tutoring rates in the Kingdom, and who publishes them
paragraphs: Every number below is an advertised rate, published by the party selling the lessons. That matters twice over: sellers advertise the figure that makes the phone ring, and a published rate is not a market average. Treat the table as a map of what is being asked, not of what families end up paying. No figure here is what IB Gram charges, and the honest answer to that question is that it depends on the subject, the level and how scarce the right tutor is.

The spread is wide for a reason. At the bottom, a platform marketing IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35 an hour is usually describing an entry-level tutor, a short introductory block, or a class size that is not quite one. In the middle, general private tuition guides for Riyadh quote around SAR 50 for primary and more than SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects - the same tutor pool, priced by what the subject demands. At the top, tutoring companies list IB subject work from around SAR 180 and Higher Level or premium tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220.

Subject scarcity is the heaviest single factor, ahead of everything else. A Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL or Physics HL specialist is dearer than a Standard Level counterpart in every market in the world, because the number of people who can teach the extension properly is small and does not grow when demand does. After scarcity comes marking or examining experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then package length. Some international providers quote in dollars at around USD 60 an hour, which adds currency movement to a budget that is otherwise fixed in SAR.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week is what the fee is really protecting
paragraphs: Saudi school weeks run Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Most tutoring copy on the internet was written for a Monday-to-Friday week and quietly assumes the wrong shape of evening. For a Diploma student that assumption is expensive: the usable slots are Sunday, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday evenings, Thursday evening is thin because it is the start of the weekend, and the two weekend days behave like a British Saturday and Sunday rather than like weekdays.

Inside that week the pressure is not even. Sunday carries the weekend's unfinished work and whatever was set on Thursday. Monday and Tuesday are the strongest teaching evenings for almost every student, which is also why they are the first to be taken. Wednesday works until school assessments cluster at the end of a unit. Thursday is where families schedule optimistically and then cancel. A tutor who holds a Monday slot for thirty weeks delivers more than one who nominally holds Thursday and loses a third of them.

This is the part of the arrangement worth paying a premium for, and the part no rate card prices. Ask any prospective tutor which day and which hour they are offering, in Saudi local time, and whether that hour is inside their own normal working day. If the honest answer is that your 7pm is their 10pm, the slot will erode. The cheapest lesson in the Kingdom is the one that happens; the dearest is the one that is rescheduled twice and then quietly dropped in the spring term.

sections.heading: Why a tutor's own working week decides whether the fee is money well spent
paragraphs: A Saudi family buying online lessons is buying an overlap between two calendars. The Kingdom works Sunday to Thursday; most of the countries where IB and IGCSE specialists live work Monday to Friday. That mismatch is not a detail. A tutor in the United Kingdom who teaches full time has a Sunday free and a Thursday evening that is the middle of their working week; a tutor in India sits two and a half hours ahead, so a 7pm lesson in Riyadh lands at 9.30pm for them.

Both arrangements can work, and both have a failure mode you can predict in advance. The tutor whose Sunday is free is excellent for the Sunday slot and worse for the mid-week one. The tutor two and a half hours ahead is fine at 5pm and unreliable at 8pm. The tutor eight hours behind is not a weekday-evening option at all, whatever the rate says. Asking the question before money changes hands is free; discovering it in the spring term costs a replacement tutor and a restart.

There is a second-order effect on price. A tutor for whom your slot sits inside their normal working day will hold it at their normal rate. A tutor for whom it sits outside - late at night, or on their own weekend - either prices that in or absorbs it, and absorbed inconvenience does not last thirty weeks. If two quotes differ and the cheaper one is asking the tutor to work at an odd hour in their own time zone, the cheaper quote is the one with the hidden cost. Pin the slot to Arabia Standard Time in writing, because the Kingdom never changes its clocks and several of these countries do.

sections.heading: What the fee looks like stage by stage, from the MYP to a resit
paragraphs: The same hourly figure buys very different things at different points in a school career, and families routinely fund the wrong stage. The cheapest intervention in the whole sequence is MYP mathematics, because it closes the algebra and proportional-reasoning gaps that later turn into Diploma repair work at Higher Level rates. The dearest is a Diploma rescue in the final two terms, when the content is done, the Internal Assessments are submitted and the only thing left to buy is examination technique.

IGCSE sits in between and carries one decision that no amount of tutoring can undo after the fact: tier entry. Cambridge IGCSE is tiered on many subjects, with Core graded C to G and Extended graded A* to E. A student entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C however well the paper goes. That is a school decision, reversible only before the entry deadline, and it is worth confirming the tier and the component list with the school in writing well before the deadline rather than assuming. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 and is not tiered the same way.

For DP1 the honest advice is to buy less than you think and start earlier than feels necessary. One subject, one slot, through the autumn and spring terms, aimed at the subject that will be hardest to recover later. For DP2 the shape inverts: fewer weeks, more hours, almost entirely past papers and mark schemes, with Internal Assessment review timed to the school's own draft deadlines. A November-series resit candidate needs the decision made early enough to plan a block rather than a panic, because entries close months ahead and the school's examinations officer holds the dates.
