sections.heading: One-to-one, a pair, or a group: when the cheaper option is the right one
paragraphs: One-to-one is not automatically correct. It is correct when the problem is diagnostic - when nobody yet knows which topics are costing the marks, or when the student needs to be asked questions rather than told answers. It is poor value when the student simply needs volume: twenty past-paper questions worked through at pace, or a topic everyone in the class found hard. Paying one-to-one rates for something a pair could do together is the most common way Saudi families overspend.

A pair works when two students sit the same syllabus at the same level and are within a grade of each other. Siblings in the same year group, or two friends at the same school in the same Higher Level subject, can share a session and halve the per-student cost with very little loss. The arrangement fails when the levels differ - a Standard Level and a Higher Level student in the same hour means one of them is being taught the wrong course for part of it.

Groups larger than three change the product rather than the price. The tutor can no longer adapt in real time, and the session becomes a class, which is what the school already provides. Where a group genuinely earns its place is in technique work with a shared artefact - a Theory of Knowledge prompt, an Economics case study, a pre-released Business Management case - because the discussion is part of the learning. The honest rule is to buy one-to-one for diagnosis and for Internal Assessment feedback, and to consider sharing for drill and for discussion.
bullets: One-to-one for diagnosis, Internal Assessment feedback and anything criterion-referenced
A pair for same-syllabus, same-level students within a grade of each other
Small group for shared artefacts: a case study, a prompt, a pre-released text
Never mix Higher and Standard Level in one paid hour and expect both to be served

sections.heading: What the fee does not buy, and why that is the point
paragraphs: A tutor may not write, draft or produce the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay or the Personal Project. Not a section, not a 'model version', not a rewritten paragraph. The work has to be the student's own, and the school is required to be satisfied of that. A provider who offers coursework completion is offering the student a malpractice investigation with a grade attached to it, and the IB's authentication requirements exist precisely to catch that.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial, and worth paying for. They can teach the skills the component assesses, explain what each criterion strand is actually asking, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short of the descriptor, suggest methods or sources to investigate, and ask the questions that make a weak research question into a workable one. The student then does every edit themselves. That is the difference between supervision and production, and it is the line a good tutor states out loud in the first session.

The fee also does not buy an outcome. Nobody can guarantee a grade, a score, a point total or a university place, and a provider who does is pricing something they do not control: grade boundaries move between series, predicted grades are the school's judgement, and admission decisions belong to universities. What a fee can honestly buy is a measurable change in how a student answers a specific kind of question. Hold the arrangement to that, and refuse to pay for anything phrased as a promise about results.
bullets: Teaching the skill, explaining the criteria and reviewing the student's own draft: legitimate
Writing, rewriting or supplying any part of assessed work: malpractice, and we decline it
Keep a record of drafts so the work's authorship is never in question
No guarantee of a grade, a point total or an admission decision is ever on offer

sections.heading: The university endgame families forget to budget for
paragraphs: An IB Diploma is not automatically treated as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision - mu'adalah - from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent, and that applies to the Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. This is administrative rather than academic, but it has a timetable, and families who discover it late are the ones who pay for urgency.

The two tests matter more for budgeting. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, and it examines verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content; it can be sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers science-stream subjects - mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English - and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last point is the one worth paying attention to.

An IB or IGCSE student has usually met most of the Tahsili material, but framed differently, examined differently and in a different sequence. The overlap is real and the presentation is not, which is why international-curriculum students frequently find Tahsili harder than their own examinations. Preparation for it is separate work, usually a short block rather than a term, and it is not what a Diploma subject tutor does by default. Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with these tests, and those criteria differ by university and by programme - check the university's own published requirements rather than a third-party summary.

sections.heading: Booking, paying and the questions that save the most money
paragraphs: The order of operations matters. Decide the subject and the component first, then the measure, then the slot, then the tutor, and only then the money. Families who start with the budget end up buying an hour of something generic. Families who start with 'Chemistry HL, the organic mechanisms questions in Paper 2, measured on a past paper, Monday at 6pm Saudi time' get a quote they can compare against another quote, which is the whole problem with this market solved in one sentence.

Four questions do most of the work in a trial lesson. Which syllabus and which level have you actually taught, and for how long? Which paper or component do you think is costing this student marks, and what in the first hour made you think so? Which day and hour are you offering in Saudi local time, and is that inside your own working day? And what will you not be able to fix this term? A tutor who answers all four plainly is usually worth more than one who answers none of them and quotes less.

On the commercial side, agree what happens to a missed lesson, how much notice a reschedule needs, and whether the slot is held during the long summer break or an autumn break. Agree whether written work marked between sessions is inside the fee. Ask whether the rate changes as the spring term approaches - demand genuinely concentrates before the May session, and a slot booked in the autumn term is easier to get than the same slot booked in the spring. A free trial lesson comes first, before any fee is agreed, and its job is to produce a diagnosis you can read rather than a recommendation to buy a package.
bullets: Subject, component, measure, slot, tutor, price - in that order
Ask what the tutor cannot fix this term; the answer is diagnostic about the tutor
Settle reschedule notice, missed lessons and holiday slot-holding before the first invoice
Book the slot in the autumn term if the series is the one in June

process.title: Say what is actually going wrong
process.description: Name the subject, the level and, if you can, the component. 'Physics HL, the extended-response questions in Paper 2' is a brief; 'Physics is hard' is not. If you do not know which component is bleeding marks, say that too - finding out is a legitimate first job and should take one lesson, not a term.

process.title: Fix the slot before the tutor
process.description: Work out which Sunday-to-Thursday evenings genuinely survive your family's week, in Saudi local time, and treat the strongest one as the constraint. Matching a tutor to a real slot is straightforward; matching a slot to a tutor you have already chosen is where arrangements quietly fail in the spring term.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: No fee is agreed before it. The lesson should end with a diagnosis you can read: which topics or skills are costing marks, what the first six lessons will target, and what the measure will be. If it ends with a package recommendation and no diagnosis, you have learned something useful about the provider.

process.title: Agree the measure and the money together
process.description: Write down the measure, the number of lessons before you review it, the reschedule notice, and what happens to a missed session. Agree whether marking between lessons is inside the fee. This conversation takes ten minutes and prevents almost every dispute families have with a tutor.

process.title: Review at six to eight lessons, not at the end of term
process.description: Re-run the measure. Ask what closed, what did not, and what needs longer. Continue, change tutor, or stop - all three are reasonable outcomes and all three are cheaper than discovering in the spring term that nothing moved. Changing tutor after two or three lessons should cost you nothing but the lessons taken.

whyPoints.title: The rate is explained, not just quoted
whyPoints.description: Advertised Saudi rates appear on this page with the kind of source that published them, because a number without a source is marketing. What moves a quote - subject scarcity, level, marking experience, package length - is set out in order of weight so you can tell whether a high figure is expertise or simply a rare subject.

whyPoints.title: Slots are pinned to Arabia Standard Time
whyPoints.description: The Kingdom is UTC+3 and does not change its clocks. Any slot agreed in a tutor's local time drifts twice a year when their country changes theirs, which is how a stable Monday evening becomes an awkward one. Agreeing the hour in Saudi local time removes a failure that costs families a tutor mid-course.

whyPoints.title: The tutor pool is not limited to who lives nearby
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a family in Jubail, Abha or Tabuk reaches the same Higher Level specialists as a family in north Riyadh. In scarce subjects that is the difference between the right tutor and the nearest one, and it is the honest argument for buying lessons over live video rather than looking for someone local.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. Writing, rewriting or supplying any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project is malpractice, and we decline it. That line is stated in the first session rather than buried in terms.

whyPoints.title: A free trial lesson before any fee
whyPoints.description: The trial exists to produce a diagnosis and to test whether the slot and the tutor actually work for your child, not to close a sale. If the match is wrong after two or three lessons, changing tutor is normal and expected - the arrangement is per-lesson and the slot belongs to the family rather than to the tutor.

faqs.question: Do IB home tutor fees change if the slot sits inside the Sunday-to-Thursday week rather than at the weekend?
faqs.answer: The hourly figure usually does not move, but the reliability does, and that is what you are really paying for. Sunday to Wednesday evenings are the slots that hold for thirty weeks. Thursday evening is the most cancelled hour in the Saudi week because the weekend has effectively begun, and Friday and Saturday sessions compete with the only unstructured days a student has. Where the weekend genuinely earns its place is a long intensive or Internal Assessment work, where two uninterrupted hours beat two scattered ones. Book a weekday evening for the standing lesson and keep the weekend for blocks.

faqs.question: Why is a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL tutor quoted higher than an Applications and Interpretation SL one?
faqs.answer: Supply, not effort. The HL Analysis and Approaches extension covers proof, complex numbers and vector geometry, and Paper 3 asks for sustained reasoning rather than recall. The number of people who can teach that properly is small and does not grow when demand does, so the rate carries a scarcity premium. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is taught competently by a far wider pool, which pushes the advertised figure down. Published Saudi listings show the same pattern across the sciences: Higher Level Physics and Chemistry sit at the top of every band for exactly this reason, and marking experience adds a further step on top.

faqs.question: What should a free trial lesson produce before we commit to a term of fees?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis you can read back later. By the end of the hour you should know which topics or skills are costing marks, which component the tutor thinks is the problem and what in the lesson made them think so, what the first six lessons will target, and what the measure of progress will be. A trial that ends with a recommended package and no diagnosis has told you about the provider rather than about your child. The trial is also where you test the slot and the rapport, both of which matter more over thirty weeks than a small difference in the hourly rate.

faqs.question: Are we paying for the lesson or for the slot when a school examination week swallows two sessions?
faqs.answer: Agree this before the first invoice, because both models exist in this market and they behave differently. Paying per lesson is cleaner for families whose weeks are unpredictable, but the slot is then not guaranteed to be there when you come back. Holding a slot for a term costs more in a light week and much less in a heavy one, and it is the safer choice in the spring term when every good evening is already taken. Whichever you choose, settle the reschedule notice period and what happens to a lesson cancelled at short notice in the same conversation.

faqs.question: Is a group class of four ever better value than one-to-one for Diploma Paper 1 practice?
faqs.answer: For volume drill on a shared paper, sometimes yes. If four students at the same level need to work through twenty multiple-choice or short-answer questions at pace, a group does that at a quarter of the cost per student and the discussion adds something. It stops working the moment the problem is diagnostic: a group cannot find out which of four students has a specific algebra gap and fix it in the same hour. Use a group for drill and for shared artefacts like a case study or a Theory of Knowledge prompt, and keep one-to-one for diagnosis and for Internal Assessment feedback.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay for Internal Assessment feedback as opposed to weekly teaching?
faqs.answer: Internal Assessment review is usually sold by the session rather than by the term, because the work happens between sessions rather than inside them. The tutor reads the student's own draft against the published criteria, marks where it falls short of the descriptor, and the student does every edit. Advertised rates for this sit at the upper end of a provider's band, since it needs somebody who knows the criterion strands rather than just the subject. Sessions are timed to the school's own draft deadlines, so three well-placed hours across a term is a common shape rather than a weekly commitment.

faqs.question: When should we start paying for support if our child is entering DP1 in the autumn term?
faqs.answer: Early and small. One subject, one hour a week, starting in the autumn term of DP1, aimed at whichever subject will be hardest to recover later - normally a Higher Level science or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL. The reason is arithmetic rather than ambition: a gap carried from the first term compounds across two years, and closing it in DP2 costs two or three times the hours at a higher rate. Families who buy three subjects from the start usually overspend and exhaust the student; families who buy nothing until the spring term of DP2 pay the most of all.

faqs.question: What does a DP2 student need in the final eight weeks before the May session, and how many hours is that?
faqs.answer: Almost entirely past papers and mark schemes, two to three hours a week, with the content phase closed. The work is timing, command-term accuracy and the discipline of answering the question actually asked rather than the one revised for. Internal Assessment work should be finished by then, so the hours go to written papers. The constraint at this point is availability rather than price - the same narrow set of good evening slots is wanted by every family in the Kingdom at once, so a block booked in the autumn term is far easier to arrange than the same block booked in the spring.

faqs.question: Is it worth funding an MYP tutor before the IGCSE years, or is that too early to spend money?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest useful money in the whole sequence. MYP mathematics support closes the algebra, proportional-reasoning and graph-reading gaps that otherwise reappear at Higher Level rates three years later. The second thing it buys is criterion literacy: MYP marks come from matching descriptors, and a student who learns to read a criterion strand in Year 8 carries that skill into every Internal Assessment afterwards. Rates at this level sit near general senior-school figures rather than Diploma figures, so one to two hours a week is a modest commitment against what DP1 repair work costs.

faqs.question: What changes in the schedule and the bill between the first and second year of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The shape inverts. DP1 is low intensity over a long period: one hour a week per supported subject, building the base and starting Internal Assessment work properly rather than late. DP2 is high intensity over a short period: two to three hours a week concentrated into the terms before the May session, almost all of it past papers, plus review sessions timed to draft deadlines. Total spend is often similar; the cash flow is not. Families who plan both years at the start can book the DP2 slots while they are still available, which is the practical saving.

faqs.question: How much notice does a November-series IGCSE resit need, and what does that block of lessons look like?
faqs.answer: Decide early enough to plan rather than panic. Entries close several months ahead of the series and your school's examinations officer holds the exact dates, so the sequence is: confirm with the school that the resit is being entered, confirm which components are being re-sat, then book the teaching block around that. The block itself is narrow by design - one or two components, rebuilt from the mark scheme outward, roughly two hours a week. Saudi candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is an India-only arrangement and does not apply here.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education equivalency step for an IB Diploma cost anything in tutoring time?
faqs.answer: No, and that is worth knowing before you budget for it. Equivalency, or mu'adalah, is the Ministry of Education's formal decision that a foreign or international certificate is equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and it applies to the IB Diploma, A Levels and an American high school diploma alike. It is a documentation process rather than an academic one, so no tutor can help and none should offer to. The people who can help are the school's own office and the Ministry's published guidance. The cost of getting it wrong is time, usually at the worst point in the application year.

faqs.question: Why do international-curriculum students in the Kingdom need separate preparation for Tahsili?
faqs.answer: Because Tahsili's content follows the Saudi national curriculum, while an IB or IGCSE student has met most of the same material in a different order, with different framing and different question styles. The overlap in topics is genuine; the overlap in presentation is not. A student who can derive a result from first principles in a Diploma paper can still misread a Tahsili item that assumes a specific national-curriculum treatment. Preparation is therefore a mapping exercise rather than new learning, usually a short block rather than a term, and it is separate work from Diploma subject teaching.

faqs.question: What does Qudurat test that a Diploma subject tutor would not normally cover?
faqs.answer: Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment and examines verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content. It can be sat in Arabic or in English. Nothing in a Diploma subject course teaches it directly, which is why a Physics or Economics tutor is the wrong person to ask. What helps is technique and timing practice on the question types, plus the decision about which language to sit it in. Universities set their own admission criteria using the results, so check the university's own published requirements.

faqs.question: Do overseas universities care which Mathematics route a Diploma student took, and should that change what we fund?
faqs.answer: For quantitative degrees, yes, and it is worth planning two years out rather than discovering it in the final year. Engineering, physics, economics and computing courses commonly expect Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, as a subject prerequisite; a student on Applications and Interpretation may find the course list narrows. That makes the Mathematics route the single highest-leverage thing to support in DP1, because it is a choice with consequences rather than a grade that can be improved later. Read the prerequisites each university actually publishes - they differ by institution and by programme, and no tutor can promise an admission outcome.

ib-home-tutor-fees.closingHeading: Start with the measure, then the slot, then the fee
ib-home-tutor-fees.closingBody: The published SAR bands on this page are a map of what sellers in the Kingdom are asking, not a price list and not what IB Gram charges. What decides whether any of it is money well spent is narrower: a named component, a measure a mark scheme can settle, and a Sunday-to-Thursday slot on Arabia Standard Time that both the family and the tutor can actually hold for thirty weeks. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, anywhere in the Kingdom. The free trial lesson comes before any fee, and its job is to tell you what is wrong and what the first six lessons will do about it.

intro.heading: What a near-me search is really asking, and the evidence that answers it
paragraphs: Start with what you would be able to check in a month, because that is the only honest way to judge whether a tutor was worth the money. Five things are visible to a parent without any specialist knowledge: whether the student's answers now match the command term in the question, whether full working appears on calculations, how many of the available mark-scheme points an answer captures, whether the student can explain what they did without the page in front of them, and whether the sessions are actually happening at the agreed hour. The last of those is the one a near-me search is trying to solve, and it is the one most families get wrong.

Search engines sort tutor results by distance, which is the wrong sort order for this purchase. A list of the ten people closest to your district tells you nothing about whether any of them has taught Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, read its Paper 3 mark scheme, or is free between the school run and dinner. Those three facts decide the outcome. Proximity decides only how long somebody spends in a car, and in most Saudi cities it does not even decide that reliably.

So the useful reframing is this: near me, in the Kingdom, means available and suitable rather than close. A family in north Riyadh looking for a Chemistry Higher Level specialist is not realistically choosing between neighbours; they are choosing between the handful of people anywhere who teach that course and have an hour free at a time their child can work. That set is small, it changes through the year, and it tightens sharply in the term before the session. Knowing its shape is worth more than any amount of local searching.

The value question follows from that, and it is the angle this page is built on. A well-matched hour and a badly-matched hour cost roughly the same and produce entirely different things. A specialist in the right subject at the right level, at an hour the student is awake and fed, moves one of those five measures within a fortnight. A competent generalist at a difficult hour produces attendance. Most of the money wasted in this market is not wasted on expensive tutors; it is wasted on adequate ones aimed at the wrong thing.

Prices appear further down with the type of vendor that publishes them attached. Nothing here is a verified market average and nothing here is our rate card. The point of publishing a band at all is that a parent should be able to tell whether a quote is reasonable, and the Saudi norm of answering a price question with a contact form makes that impossible. The figures are a reference, discounted by the fact that a vendor published them to attract enquiries.

On delivery, plainly, because the phrase at the top of this page implies something we do not sell. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, on a slot agreed in Arabia Standard Time. We do not arrange a tutor at a Saudi address, and in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. That is not a limitation dressed up as a feature; it is the reason the specialist pool is large enough to match on subject and level at all, which is what the search was actually about.

ib-home-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: The matching problem is different in each IB programme, which is why a tutor who is excellent for one of your children can be the wrong choice for the other. What follows is each programme described by how hard it is to match for, and what a good fit looks like at that stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, converted to a one-to-seven grade. The final year carries the Personal Project. Matching here is easy and families often overcomplicate it: the work that pays is mechanical, which means algebraic fluency, writing at length, and learning to read a criterion descriptor before starting a task. A strong generalist teacher does this well, and paying a scarce Higher Level specialist for it is a straightforward waste.
programmes.countryNote: The fit question at this stage is about the student rather than the syllabus. A thirteen-year-old who has decided they are bad at mathematics needs someone they will talk to, and that is worth testing in a trial lesson before anything else. Availability is rarely the constraint, so a family in any Saudi city can usually have the hour they want, which makes this the easiest stage to get right cheaply.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject pairs externally marked papers with an internally assessed component. This is where matching becomes genuinely hard, because the pool narrows at every step: the subject, then the level, then the specific component, then the hour. A tutor who ticks three of those four is a near miss rather than a match.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom the hour is usually the binding constraint rather than the subject. Most Saudi IB schools sit the May session, so demand for the scarce Higher Level specialists concentrates in the same months across every city at once. Families who book a term earlier get the hour they want; families who start in the spring take what is left. That is the single most useful piece of timing advice on this page.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and continuous teacher assessment reported against learning outcomes. The final year ends in the PYP exhibition. Because nothing is examined, the fit that matters is with the child and with the parent's own reading of progress: a tutor here has to be able to tell you, in plain words, what your child can and cannot do, since the school's reports are written in a different register.
programmes.countryNote: Mid-year arrivals into the Kingdom are the common case, and a child who joins a unit of inquiry halfway through can look lost without having any real gap. The useful first session is diagnostic rather than remedial. Short sessions suit this age, which also means a family in any city can fit one into a weekday evening without touching the school run.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: At least two Diploma Programme subjects with a career-related study, plus personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and a reflective project. The Diploma subjects inside it are assessed exactly as in the full Diploma, which is good news for matching: the pool of tutors who can teach them is the same pool. The reflective project needs feedback on the student's own drafts and nothing beyond that.
programmes.countryNote: Rare in the Kingdom, which means a family on this programme often cannot find anyone locally who has heard of it. The practical answer is to stop searching for a Career-related Programme tutor and search instead for a tutor in the specific Diploma subject at the specific level, because that is what the student is actually being examined on.

ib-home-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: The entries below are written from the matching side: how large the specialist pool is for each, what a tutor needs to have actually done, and what therefore counts as a near miss. A tutor who knows the subject but not the component is the most common near miss in this market, and it costs a term.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level the pool is small, because Paper 3 is two long scaffolded investigations and teaching it well requires someone who also handles post-16 mathematics. A near miss here is a tutor strong on Standard Level content who has never prepared a student for Paper 3. Ask what their last Paper 3 session covered. Standard Level is a much larger pool and most hours are available.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The largest pool of any Diploma subject at Standard Level, so availability is rarely the problem. Fit is. The course is modelling and calculator led, and a tutor trained on Analysis and Approaches often teaches the algebra and skips the interpretation, which is where the marks actually go. Ask how they would mark a regression answer with no sentence of context.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Among the scarcest requests in the Kingdom at Higher Level. A genuine match has taught the Higher Level extension topics and can explain how the data-based section of Paper 1 treats uncertainties, which is where confident students lose marks. Many tutors offering Physics are mathematicians who can do the calculations; that is a near miss and it shows up on long-answer questions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Scarce at Higher Level and in heaviest demand in the term before the session, which is exactly when the pool is thinnest. A match can talk about energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms as teaching problems rather than as topics, and knows the data booklet well enough to teach from it. Booking a term early is the difference between a specialist and whoever is free.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A moderate pool, and the fit test is unusually specific: this subject is marked on named terminology in sequence, so a tutor who teaches concepts beautifully and does not drill the wording will not move the grade. Ask them what a six-mark extended response on osmosis has to contain. A good answer lists terms; a weak one describes understanding.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Written papers plus an internally assessed fieldwork investigation, and the fieldwork is the part that needs a specific kind of tutor. A match can advise on a question that is answerable with data the student can realistically collect, and can mark to the criteria. A subject generalist will help with content and leave the component carrying a fifth of the grade untouched.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A reasonable pool and an easy subject to mis-match, because so many tutors have an economics degree and no familiarity with the mark scheme. Almost all avoidable loss is in diagram accuracy and in evaluation that states a judgement. Ask what the commonest diagram error is on the papers; a real answer names axes and labels, not general advice about practice.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The pool looks large and narrows fast, because the prescribed subjects and regional options a school teaches vary. A tutor who knows twentieth-century Europe is not a match for a student doing the Americas option. Confirm which options the school teaches before matching, and ask the tutor which of them they have taught to an examined cohort.

subjects.name: Language A: English
subjects.description: Large pool, narrow fit. The studied works differ school to school, and a tutor who has not read the texts a student is being examined on can only teach unseen analysis. That is often the right purchase, since Paper 1 is unseen, but it should be a decision rather than a discovery in week four. Ask which of the student's works they have taught.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision
subjects.description: The smallest pool of all, because few tutors do this properly and the ones who do are usually teachers already supervising at a school. Sessions are spaced rather than weekly, which makes them easier to fit into a week and harder to book. The work is questioning a student's own drafts and reading the criteria against them, never writing or restructuring.

ib-home-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: What a near-me search returns, city by city
ib-home-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The results a distance-sorted search gives you differ sharply across the Kingdom, and so does what those results are worth. These notes describe what a family in each place actually finds when they search locally, and where the gap between that and a match tends to sit.

regions.name: North Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest local market in the Kingdom, so a near-me search returns plenty of names. The gap is specificity: most of those names teach several subjects across several year groups, and the Higher Level science specialist a Diploma family needs is often not among them at any distance.

regions.name: South and central Riyadh
regions.note: A search returns many of the same names, because the city is roughly an hour across and tutors list themselves city-wide. The practical result is enquiries that go nowhere once the drive is discussed, which is why families here often conclude the market is thin when it is simply unreachable at the hour they need.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine, so a near-me search in the north returns a different set from one in the historic centre, and neither covers the whole city. Board confusion is the extra risk here, since Cambridge and IB schools sit close together and a local tutor's experience may be with the other one.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: The one part of the Kingdom where a local search can realistically produce two comparable options for the same subject, because three cities behave as one market. It is also where families are most likely to find a tutor who has taught at a school running the Diploma, which is a genuine fit advantage.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: A small pool attached to the industrial workforce, and a near-me search returns few names for senior subjects. Household schedules shaped by shift patterns make the hour harder to agree than the subject, so the negotiation is usually about availability rather than about price.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: An hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, which puts those tutors out of daily reach. A local search here returns general tutors rather than Diploma specialists, and the honest reading is that the subject match has to come from outside the area entirely.

regions.name: Makkah, Madinah and Thuwal
regions.note: Families in Makkah and Madinah often search towards Jeddah and find names that will not travel; Thuwal is a concentrated campus community where the local pool is the school itself. In all three, availability rather than distance is what a search is failing to show.

regions.name: 'Asir, Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: A near-me search in these regions frequently returns nothing relevant, and that is the accurate result rather than a failure of the search. There is no local Diploma specialist pool to find, which makes the question of who is available anywhere the only question worth asking.

schoolClusters.note: Schools named in IB directories for the capital include the following. For matching purposes the useful thing to know about your own school is narrower than its name: which Higher Level groups ran last term, whether Higher and Standard Level share a room, and which prescribed options or studied works the subject teachers have chosen.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah, Thuwal and the Eastern Province
schoolClusters.note: The British International School of Jeddah is both an IB World School and a Cambridge school, The KAUST School serves the Thuwal campus community, and the Diploma runs at the American School of Dhahran and at ISG Jubail among the International Schools Group campuses. A tutor matched to the school's actual option choices rather than to the subject name is the difference between help and general revision.

ib-home-tutor-near-me.schoolDisclaimer: Schools and school groups are named here only as context for how IB provision is distributed in the Kingdom. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation, endorsement, contract or commercial relationship with any of them.
ib-home-tutor-near-me.modesIntro: Each of these solves a different availability problem rather than a different academic one, which is why the right choice often depends on your week rather than on your child's marks. All of them run one-to-one over live video on a slot agreed in Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: A fixed weekly hour, held for the term
modes.description: The arrangement to ask for if you can protect one hour a week. A held slot is the scarcest thing in this market for a Higher Level science or mathematics subject, and holding it through a quiet term is what guarantees it exists in the busy one. Families who book only when results disappoint are competing for hours that were taken months earlier.
bullets: One named tutor for one subject at one level
The hour agreed in Saudi local time, so it does not drift
Held across the term rather than booked session by session
A short note to the parent after each session

modes.title: Fortnightly spaced sessions
modes.description: The right shape for Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Internal Assessment work, where the student needs time between sessions to do the writing themselves. It is also easier to schedule, because a fortnightly hour fits into a tutor's diary that a weekly one does not, which makes the scarcest specialists reachable.
bullets: Feedback on a draft the student has already written
The published criteria read against the work
Easier to book with a tutor whose weekly hours are full
No writing, redrafting or supplying of text by the tutor

modes.title: Two subjects back to back on one evening
modes.description: For a household where the school run leaves only one usable evening. Two shorter sessions with two different specialists, one after the other. Concentration drops in the second hour, so it suits the earlier part of a course rather than the weeks before papers, and it is worth reviewing after a term rather than assuming it works.

Shorter sessions than a single-subject evening, deliberately
Better earlier in the course than in the final term
One combined note so the two tutors are not describing the same student differently

modes.title: A weekend block
modes.description: Friday or Saturday sessions, which are the honest answer for families whose weekday evenings are taken by a long school run or by a shift pattern. Harder to staff, because a tutor in a Monday-to-Friday country is working then, so these need asking for a term ahead rather than in the week you want them.
bullets: Longer single sessions rather than two short ones
Suits timed past-paper work, which needs an uninterrupted stretch
Scarcer than weekday hours, so book well ahead
Agreed in Saudi local time like any other slot

sections.heading: The five things you can check, and what near me cannot tell you
paragraphs: Work backwards from the evidence. In a month, a parent with no specialist knowledge can check five things from the student's own work and from their own calendar. Whether answers now match the command term printed in the question. Whether full working, including the substitution line, appears on calculations. How many of the available mark-scheme points a given answer captured. Whether the student can explain what they did with the page turned over. And whether the sessions actually happened at the agreed hour.

Four of those are academic and the fifth is logistical, and the fifth is the one that quietly destroys the other four. A tutor who is a perfect subject match but only free at an hour your child cannot reliably make will deliver perhaps two thirds of the sessions you pay for, and the missing third will be the weeks when something else went wrong too. That pattern is common enough in the Kingdom that it deserves naming before any discussion of qualifications.

This is why a distance-sorted search answers the wrong question. The list it returns is ordered by a variable that affects none of the five measures. What affects them is whether the person has taught this subject at this level, whether they know the component where marks are going, and whether they can be in the same hour as your child every week. Distance is at best a weak proxy for the third of those and is irrelevant to the first two.

The table below sets out the three questions a near-me search is actually standing in for, and what can and cannot answer each. Reading it is the fastest way to work out whether to keep searching locally or to change what you are searching for. For a common Standard Level subject the local answer may be perfectly adequate. For a scarce Higher Level one it usually is not, and no amount of refining the search radius changes that.

sections.heading: The availability intersection, subject by subject
paragraphs: Availability is not a single number. It is the overlap between how many people teach a given course, where those people sit in the world, and which hours your child can actually use. That overlap is wide for some subjects and very narrow for others, and knowing which you are dealing with changes how early you need to book and how much flexibility to offer.

Pool size is the first dimension. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level has the largest pool of any Diploma subject, so almost any reasonable hour can be covered. Higher Level Physics and Chemistry sit at the other end, partly because fewer people can teach the extension material and partly because many of those who can are still teaching in schools and are therefore only free in their own evenings. Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision is scarcer still.

Where the pool sits geographically is the second dimension, and it interacts with the first in a way that is genuinely useful to know. Tutors in India are two and a half hours ahead of Arabia Standard Time, so a mid-afternoon Saudi slot is their evening and works well. Tutors in the United Kingdom and Europe are two or three hours behind, depending on their season, which makes a mid-afternoon Saudi hour their late morning or midday, an easy slot to fill. A late Saudi evening suits almost nobody except tutors inside the Kingdom.

The practical conclusion is counter-intuitive and worth stating plainly: the easiest hour to fill with a scarce specialist is earlier than most families ask for. A mid-afternoon Saudi slot lands inside a working day across most of the tutor world, while the seven-to-nine evening window every parent requests competes with the whole Kingdom at once. A family who can get their child to a desk by mid-afternoon has access to specialists that a family asking for a late evening does not.

sections.heading: What a mismatch costs, by kind
paragraphs: The cost of getting this wrong is not usually an expensive tutor. It is an adequate one aimed at the wrong thing, and the loss is measured in terms rather than in riyals. Five kinds of mismatch account for almost all of it, and four of the five are visible inside three weeks if a parent knows what to watch.

The two most expensive are the hardest to see. Right subject and wrong level produces teaching that is entirely sound and aimed at the wrong paper: the Higher Level extension topics never appear, the student does well in sessions, and the mock arrives looking like their fault. Right level and wrong guide or board produces practice papers from a superseded syllabus and command-term expectations that no longer apply. Both feel like progress while they happen, which is what makes them costly.

The third, right specialist and wrong hour, is the one a near-me search is meant to prevent and routinely causes. A tutor who can only teach late, in a household where the student is finished by then, produces cancelled sessions, moved sessions and a child arriving tired with the week's work undone. On the usual pattern a family loses about a third of what they paid for, and the lost sessions cluster in the weeks that mattered.

The fourth and fifth are human rather than structural. A competent tutor the student has decided against will not teach them, however good the subject match, and the only sensible response is to change at two or three lessons rather than at ten. And a good match with no reporting leaves a parent unable to decide anything: the tutor says it is going well, the marks have not moved yet, and nobody can tell whether to continue. That is the loss that compounds, because it removes the ability to act on any of the other four.

sections.heading: What it costs in the Kingdom, and what the money buys
paragraphs: Figures first, with their provenance attached. Tutor-marketplace guides list general private tuition in the Kingdom at around SAR 50 an hour for primary work and SAR 200 and upwards for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring companies list IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180, with Higher Level and premium tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Tutoring platforms advertise general non-specialist online tutoring from around SAR 55, and budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one online from around SAR 35. International providers quote around sixty dollars. Every one of those is an advertised figure a vendor published to attract enquiries, not a measured average, and none of them is what IB Gram charges.

What those numbers do not show is the part this page is about. Two tutors at the same rate can produce entirely different results depending on whether the subject, the level, the component and the hour all line up. The rate is a poor predictor of outcome and a good predictor of scarcity: a higher quote usually means fewer people can do the job, which is honest pricing rather than a markup. A flat rate offered across every subject and level means the provider is not matching on specialism at all.

Three things reliably add to a quote without adding teaching, and all three are worth naming because they are usually presented as value. Travel, where a tutor attends an address, puts the drive inside the hour whether or not the invoice says so. Proximity to the session prices the diary rather than the teaching, which is why booking a term ahead is the cheapest version of the same arrangement. And a package length discount is a cash-flow structure, so the question to ask is what happens to unused lessons and whether the slot is held.

The value calculation that actually matters is narrower than a rate comparison. Take one subject, the one where marks are most recoverable, and ask what moving it by a grade is worth to the student's post-16 options. Then weigh that against a term of weekly hours. For most families the answer is that one well-matched subject beats three adequately matched ones at the same total cost, and that is the decision a near-me search is not helping them make.

sections.heading: The trial lesson as a fit test
paragraphs: A trial lesson is worth almost nothing as an introduction and a great deal as a test, and which one you get depends on what you ask for. The version that works has the tutor set a past question from the student's own subject and level in the first few minutes and watch them work it unaided. Nothing is taught until something has been observed. A session that opens with the tutor describing their experience and the platform's features is a sales call with a lesson attached.

Four things should be visible by the end, and a parent sitting in can judge all of them without knowing the subject. Whether the tutor watched before they talked. Whether their diagnosis names a behaviour and its cost rather than a quality: losing method marks by omitting the substitution line is a diagnosis, needing to build confidence is not. Whether they gave an estimate of how long the fix takes, with reasoning. And how the student responded, which matters more than parents allow themselves to admit.

Ask the tutor to mark one piece of the student's own work aloud during the session. This is the single most revealing thing available in a trial. Someone who has marked for a board allocates marks point by point against the scheme, says which point earned which mark, and names what was missing. Someone who has not gives an impression and a number. The difference is audible inside a minute and does not require you to know the subject at all.

On the student's reaction: take it seriously but interrogate it. A teenager who says the tutor was fine is giving you no information, and one who says the tutor talked the whole time is giving you a great deal. The useful question after a trial is not whether they liked it but what the tutor asked them to do, because a student who can answer that was engaged and a student who cannot was watching. Nothing is charged for this session, and it should be possible to say no afterwards without a conversation about it.

sections.heading: How a match is actually made
paragraphs: Matching sounds like an algorithm and is mostly a sequence of filters applied in a strict order, because applying them in the wrong order produces the near misses described above. Subject first, then level, then the specific component where marks are going, then the hours the family can genuinely sustain. Only after those four does anything else enter, and the fourth filter is where most requests fail rather than the first.

That order has a consequence worth being honest about. Sometimes the intersection is empty. A Physics Higher Level specialist with marking experience, free at a late Saudi evening, in the term before the session, is a narrow set and it does occasionally contain nobody. When that happens there are three straight answers: hold for the slot and start later, take a different hour including a weekend block, or begin with a strong generalist on technique while the specialist hour opens up. The fourth option, putting the student with someone who does not know the paper and calling it a match, is the one this page exists to argue against.

A family can widen the intersection themselves, and it is worth knowing how. Offering an earlier hour helps most, because mid-afternoon Saudi time is a working hour across most of the tutor world. Offering a weekend block helps second. Accepting fortnightly spaced sessions instead of weekly helps for core components and for Internal Assessment work, where the student needs the gap anyway. Booking a term before the session helps more than all three put together.

What happens after the match is the part that determines whether it holds. The slot is agreed in Arabia Standard Time, so a tutor in a country that changes its clocks absorbs the shift rather than the household rebuilding a school evening twice a year. Two or three behavioural targets are written down. Work is set between sessions and marked before the next one. And a short note goes to the parent each time, which exists so that the fifth kind of mismatch, the good match nobody can evaluate, does not happen.

sections.heading: Fit with the school, not just with the syllabus
paragraphs: A tutor can know a subject guide perfectly and still be a poor fit for your child's class, because schools make choices inside the guide that change what is examined. History schools choose prescribed subjects and regional options. Language A schools choose the studied works. Science departments choose which practical work the Internal Assessment grows out of. A tutor matched to the subject name rather than to those choices will teach something adjacent to what the student is being assessed on.

So the brief that produces a good match includes four things most families do not think to send. The syllabus and level, obviously. The specific options or texts the school has chosen. Which component the school has flagged, if any, in a report or a parents' evening. And the school's own assessment calendar, because a tutor who knows a mock is in six weeks plans differently from one who does not. None of that requires the school's cooperation; it is all on a scheme of work or in a report already in your possession.

There is a second kind of school fit that matters for Internal Assessment and the Extended Essay, which is the relationship with the school supervisor. A tutor working against a school supervisor is worse than no tutor, because the student receives two sets of direction and satisfies neither. A tutor who asks what the supervisor has already said, and works inside it, is doing the job properly. If a tutor suggests ignoring the school's advice, that is a signal rather than confidence.

What a tutor cannot and should not do is substitute for the school. They do not hold the entry, they do not set the predicted grade, they do not supervise the assessed work formally, and they have no standing with the board. Being clear about that is part of a good fit, because a family who expects a tutor to fix an administrative problem will be disappointed by someone who was never able to. The school holds those levers; a tutor helps the student pull them.

sections.heading: What a lesson looks like from the student's side
paragraphs: Families considering online teaching for the first time usually want to know what actually happens, and the honest answer is that it looks less like a video call and more like two people sharing a page. The student needs a laptop rather than a phone, a connection that holds a call, headphones, and a door that closes. A tablet with a stylus is useful for mathematics and the sciences because the student can write naturally on a shared board, but it is not required and a notebook under a camera works.

The shape of a good session is consistent. It opens with the student working something unaided while the tutor watches, because that is the only way to see method rather than knowledge. It moves to the shared whiteboard, where the better pattern is the student writing and the tutor questioning each line rather than the tutor producing a neat solution. Past-paper extracts are pasted onto the board and annotated live. Marking happens aloud, against the published scheme, with the student allocating the marks where possible.

What a parent sees afterwards is deliberately more than a summary. The saved whiteboard is the working rather than the conversation, which is usually the more useful artefact. A short note says what was covered, what was set and what the tutor wants done before the next session. Where a recording exists it is arranged with the family rather than assumed, and it is for the student's revision rather than for anybody else.

Two practical points specific to the Kingdom. Keep a phone hotspot available as a fallback, because a dropped connection mid-paper is irritating rather than fatal if the alternative is already open. And agree in advance what counts as a lost lesson, so that the conversation is not happening for the first time while a session is failing. The whiteboard persists through a reconnection, so a short outage costs minutes rather than a session.

sections.heading: Changing tutor without losing the term
paragraphs: Rematching is normal and should be cheap, and a family that treats it as a failure will put up with a wrong fit for far too long. The right moment is two or three lessons in, when enough has been seen to judge and little has been lost. At ten lessons the decision is the same but the term is half gone, and the student has usually built a view of the subject around a teacher they did not get on with.

Three signals justify a change on their own. The student cannot say what the tutor asked them to do after a session, which means they were watching rather than working. The tutor's account of progress does not match what is visible in the work, which means either the diagnosis or the reporting is wrong. And nothing in the five checkable measures has shifted after a month, which means the plan was aimed at the wrong thing. None of those requires a confrontation or a long explanation.

Because teaching is delivered over live video, a rematch is administrative rather than disruptive: there is no travel arrangement to rebuild, no new household logistics to agree, and the slot can often be kept. That is a genuine advantage over an in-home arrangement, where changing tutor means starting a local search from nothing and renegotiating a drive. It is also why the honest answer to a wrong fit here is to change rather than to persevere.

What should carry across to the new tutor is the diagnosis, the targets and the work already marked, so that the first session with the replacement is not another diagnostic. Ask for that explicitly. A provider who hands a new tutor nothing is charging a family twice for the same diagnosis, and the second one is both an expense and a fortnight the student did not have to spare.

sections.heading: Near me, at my address, and why they are different questions here
paragraphs: This page should finish where the search began. An in-home tutor is a real service with real advantages, and a family that wants one is not making a mistake. You can see the lesson happen, a younger child is easier to settle, and there is no equipment to arrange. Across much of the Kingdom it is the default model, and much of the local market is built around it.

Its limitation is arithmetic rather than quality. An in-home arrangement restricts you to people who already live within a reasonable drive of your district and are willing to make it at your hour. For a common Standard Level subject that set is adequate in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster, and thin almost everywhere else. For a scarce Higher Level subject it is frequently empty, and refining the search radius does not create a specialist who is not there.

What IB Gram sells is the other side of that trade. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, on a slot agreed in Arabia Standard Time, which removes distance from the selection and makes the national pool available to a family in Al Ahsa on the same terms as a family in north Riyadh. We do not arrange a tutor at a Saudi address, and in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. The table below lays out the comparison so the decision is yours rather than ours.

The last row of that table is the one worth reading twice. A near-me search and an at-my-address search are different requests, and conflating them is what sends families down a route that cannot answer their actual question. If what you need is someone in the room, say so and look locally with clear eyes about what is available. If what you need is someone who knows the paper, the room is the part to give up.

process.title: Send the four things that make a match possible
process.description: The subject and level, the specific options or texts the school has chosen, whichever component the school has flagged, and the hours your household can genuinely sustain in Saudi local time. The fourth is where most requests fail, so be realistic rather than optimistic about the hour.

process.title: We apply the filters in order
process.description: Subject, then level, then the component, then the hour. Nothing else enters until those four are satisfied, because applying them out of order is what produces a tutor who knows the subject and not the paper. Where the intersection is empty, we say so instead of offering a near miss.

process.title: A free trial lesson run as a fit test
process.description: The tutor sets a past question in the first few minutes and watches the student work it before teaching anything. Sit in. By the end you should have a diagnosis naming a behaviour and its cost, an estimate with reasoning, and your own read on how your child responded. Nothing is charged.

process.title: Fix the hour in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: The slot is agreed in Saudi local time, so a tutor whose own country changes its clocks absorbs the shift. Mid-afternoon hours are easiest to fill with a scarce specialist because they sit inside a working day across most of the tutor world. Weekend blocks exist and need asking for early.

process.title: Two or three behavioural targets, written down
process.description: Targets phrased as things the student does rather than grades they reach: annotate the command term, show the substitution line, count the marks before answering. Work is set between sessions and marked before the next, with a short note to the parent naming what was covered and set.

process.title: Rematch or stop, deliberately
process.description: If the student cannot say what they were asked to do, if the tutor's account does not match the work, or if none of the five measures has moved in a month, change the tutor and carry the diagnosis across. If the right answer is to reduce to one subject or stop, we say that at the term review.

whyPoints.title: Sorted by availability and fit, not by address
whyPoints.description: The filters run subject, level, component, hour, in that order, and nothing is offered that fails one of them. A distance-sorted list cannot answer any of the first three, which is why a near-me search feels unproductive in most of the Kingdom even where plenty of names come back.

whyPoints.title: The empty intersection is admitted
whyPoints.description: Sometimes no specialist is free at an hour a family can use, particularly for Higher Level sciences in the term before the session. The three honest responses are to hold for the slot, take a different hour, or start on technique with a generalist. Offering someone who does not know the paper is not among them.

whyPoints.title: Rematching is cheap by design
whyPoints.description: Teaching over live video means there is no travel arrangement to rebuild, so changing tutor at two or three lessons costs the lessons taken and nothing structural. The diagnosis, the targets and the marked work carry across, so the replacement does not start with another diagnostic a family has already paid for.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their provenance
whyPoints.description: Advertised SAR and dollar figures appear here with the type of vendor that published them, and are labelled as advertised rather than as averages. None has a sample size or a date behind it, and none is our price. In a market that answers price questions with a contact form, a band is worth more than a form.

whyPoints.title: What a parent can check, stated up front
whyPoints.description: Five measures, all visible from the student's own work and your own calendar, listed before any fee. The fifth is logistical, because a perfect subject match at an impossible hour delivers about two thirds of what it was paid for, and that loss is the one nobody warns a family about.

whyPoints.title: No claim that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No success rates, no ratings, no headcounts, no grade promises. IB Gram holds no accreditation or authorisation from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and there is no office in the Kingdom. Those are facts worth stating rather than facts worth implying.

faqs.question: What platform do lessons run on, and does anything need installing on a Saudi connection?
faqs.answer: Lessons run in a browser-based video session with a shared whiteboard, so in most cases nothing needs installing beyond an up-to-date browser. Where a tutor prefers a specific tool, you are told before the trial rather than on the day. A laptop with a reasonable connection is sufficient; the bandwidth demand of a one-to-one session is modest compared with streaming video. If a household connection is unreliable, say so at the start so the tutor plans around it rather than discovering it mid-session.

faqs.question: Can a parent see the whiteboard from a lesson they did not sit in on?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually the more useful artefact. The board holds the working, the annotated past-paper extract and the marks allocated, which is what you want to see; a recording holds the conversation, which mostly is not. Ask for the board to be saved and sent after each session, and read it alongside the short note saying what was covered and what was set. Between them, those two items let a parent check progress without needing to know the subject.

faqs.question: Is a tablet with a stylus better than a laptop for a Higher Level maths lesson?
faqs.answer: For mathematics and the sciences a tablet with a stylus is genuinely better, because the student can write naturally on the shared board and the tutor sees the working form rather than the finished answer. It is not required. A laptop plus a notebook positioned under the camera works perfectly well, and many students prefer writing on paper. What matters more than the hardware is that the tutor can see the student's working as it happens rather than after it.

faqs.question: How does a tutor work on an Extended Essay draft on screen without touching the text?
faqs.answer: The student shares their own document or a copy of it, and the tutor works through it by questioning rather than editing: why this paragraph sits here, what the criterion actually rewards, where a conclusion outruns the evidence. Comments and questions go in a separate note, and the student makes every change themselves in their own sitting. Nothing is typed into the document by the tutor. That separation is what keeps authorship provable, and it is also why these sessions are spaced rather than weekly.

faqs.question: What does a tutor do when a student goes quiet on camera halfway through a session?
faqs.answer: Hand the work back to them. A silent student in a one-to-one session is almost always one who has stopped following, and the correct response is to stop explaining and set something small they can attempt. Good tutors talk considerably less than parents expect, because the student writing on the shared board while being questioned is the format that produces learning. If a tutor spends most of a session presenting, that is worth raising, whatever the student's marks look like.

faqs.question: What exactly does the free trial lesson cost if we then decide not to continue?
faqs.answer: Nothing. No payment is taken before the trial and declining afterwards needs no explanation. The session is useful in itself even if you go elsewhere, because you leave with a diagnosis you can test against the next piece of work and an estimate of how long a fix should take, both of which are things to ask any other provider to match. A trial that functions as a sales pitch rather than a working session is not worth having free.

faqs.question: Do we pay per lesson or per package, and what happens to an unused lesson?
faqs.answer: Ask this before committing and get the answer in writing, whoever you buy from. Per-lesson payment is the cleanest arrangement and lets a family stop without an argument. Packages are usually cheaper per hour and are a cash-flow structure rather than better teaching, so the questions that matter are whether unused lessons expire, whether the slot is held if you pause, and what notice is needed to cancel a single session. Vague answers to those three are the warning sign.

faqs.question: Why would the same tutor quote more for an hour in the spring term than in the autumn?
faqs.answer: Because the diary is scarcer, not because the teaching is better. Demand for Higher Level specialists concentrates in the months before the session across every Saudi city at once, and a tutor with two hours left prices them accordingly. That is ordinary scarcity pricing and it is not dishonest. The practical response is to book in the autumn for a slot you will need in the spring, which is the cheapest version of exactly the same arrangement.

faqs.question: Is a shared session with a sibling ever worth the saving on an IB subject?
faqs.answer: Only where both students are on the same subject at the same level and genuinely at a similar point, which is rarer than families hope. Two siblings a year apart in the Diploma are studying different material, and a shared hour becomes two half-hours with an audience. Where it does work, the saving is real and the sessions can be effective because the pair explain things to each other. Where it does not, it is the most expensive discount in this market.

faqs.question: How many lessons a week does a Diploma student with two weak subjects actually need?
faqs.answer: One hour per subject per week is the standard answer and it is usually right, with a strong preference for two separate evenings over a double session if the week allows. Two hours in one subject is justified only in the term before the session and only where content is genuinely missing rather than technique. More than three tutored hours a week across a Diploma is normally a sign that something structural is wrong, such as a level that should have been changed, and more teaching will not fix it.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor knows my child's school's scheme of work and not just the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Send them the specifics and watch what they do with them. Which prescribed options or studied works the school chose, which component was flagged in the last report, when the next mock falls. A tutor who reads those and adjusts their plan is working with the school; one who ignores them and teaches the subject generically is not. The sharper test is to ask what they would teach differently given the school's option choice, because a vague answer means they did not look.

faqs.question: How many students does one tutor carry, and why should a parent ask?
faqs.answer: Ask because the answer tells you two things at once. A tutor with very few students in your subject is either new to it or not in demand, and a tutor with a very full week has no capacity to mark work between sessions or to move a lesson when a school trip lands on it. The useful follow-up is how many students they currently teach in this specific subject at this specific level, which separates a specialist from someone covering a timetable.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need to have read the studied works our school chose for Language A?
faqs.answer: For Paper 1, no: it is unseen textual analysis and the method transfers between texts. For Paper 2 and the Higher Level essay, yes, because both rest on the specific works the school selected, and a tutor who has not read them can only teach argument structure in the abstract. Both are legitimate purchases. What matters is knowing which one you are buying in week one rather than discovering it in week four. Ask which of your child's works the tutor has taught to an examined cohort, and if the answer is none, agree explicitly that the sessions target Paper 1 technique.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor becomes unavailable halfway through the Diploma?
faqs.answer: A replacement is matched from the same pool and the diagnosis, the targets and the marked work carry across, so the new tutor does not begin with another diagnostic. Ask for that handover explicitly, whoever you are with. Where the subject is scarce there may be a wait for an equivalent specialist at your hour, and the honest options are the same three as at the start: hold the slot, move the hour, or bridge with technique work. A sudden silent substitution is not acceptable practice.

faqs.question: Can we choose the tutor's gender, and what practical difference does it make?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a normal request that needs no justification. One-to-one online lessons let a family specify it directly, which is one practical advantage over taking whoever is locally available. The academic difference is none; the difference is in whether a student speaks freely in a session, which varies by family and by child and is worth getting right rather than reasoning about. State the preference at the start, because it narrows the pool and therefore affects which hours are available.

ib-home-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Ask for availability and fit, not for a postcode
ib-home-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB home tutor near me in Saudi Arabia, the four things that produce a match are the subject, the level, the component losing marks and the hour your household can sustain. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time; nobody is sent to a Saudi address, and in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. Where no specialist is free at an hour you can use, we will tell you that and set out the three real options rather than offer a near miss.

ib-home-tutors.tutorsIntro: The tutors below hold weekly slots with students across the Kingdom, in named Diploma subjects at a named level. A slot is only useful if it holds for a year, so the match considers the tutor's own working week and time zone alongside their subject, not after it.

intro.heading: A tutor you can actually keep every week
paragraphs: A family searching for IB home tutors is almost never asking an abstract question about teaching methods. They are asking whether this can happen reliably at seven in the evening, every week, from now until the examinations, through a term that includes mock papers, a relocation and at least one week when nobody is in the mood. Everything else is secondary, because a brilliant tutor who cannot hold a slot teaches a student far less than a good one who never misses.

That makes logistics the right starting point. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, so four weekday evenings are genuinely available and Thursday evening behaves the way a Friday evening does elsewhere. Saudi Arabia keeps Arabia Standard Time at UTC+3 and does not change its clocks, which means a slot agreed with a tutor in a country that does change them will drift twice a year unless it is pinned to Saudi local time in writing. Those two facts settle more scheduling disputes than any amount of goodwill.

The school run is the third constraint and the one families underestimate. Riyadh is about an hour across in traffic, Jeddah runs as a long coastal spine, and the Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran cluster behaves as one market with families living in one city and schooling in another. A lesson timed to begin the moment a car is supposed to arrive is a lesson that gets moved twice a term and eventually abandoned. A lesson that begins when the student sits down at a desk does not depend on traffic at all, which is the practical argument for teaching this way rather than sending somebody across a city.

On that point we are direct, because the search phrase deserves an honest answer. Tutoring for families in Saudi Arabia is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits in Saudi Arabia are not a service we sell, and in-home teaching is something we offer only in India. What a Saudi family gets instead is a choice made from everyone who teaches their child's exact syllabus in a compatible time zone, rather than from whoever lives within a twenty-minute drive and has a free evening.

The fourth constraint is the calendar, and it is the one this page is organised around. A Diploma year has a shape: content first, internally assessed work threaded through it, mock papers, then the series. Support that arrives in the right part of that shape is cheap and effective, and support that arrives late can only do the narrower job that remains. No year is named anywhere on this page, because the shape repeats and the dates belong to your school's own calendar and its examinations officer. What follows is the year counted backwards from the papers.
