ib-home-tutors.programmesIntro: Four IB programmes, described here by where the work falls in the year rather than by their philosophy. The timing is what decides whether support is cheap or expensive.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No papers and no external marking, so the year has no single pressure point. Units of inquiry run through it and the final year ends with an exhibition the students research themselves. Progress is judged from reasoning and extended writing, which means a weekly slot can sit anywhere in the week that suits a young child's energy.
programmes.countryNote: The scheduling question at this age is attention rather than the calendar. A thirty to forty-five minute session early in the evening, before a long school run has flattened a seven-year-old, achieves more than an hour later on. Families in the larger cities often move the slot earlier once they see the difference.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Four published criteria per subject group, marked out of eight, with the Personal Project assessed and moderated in the final year. The work is distributed across the year rather than concentrated, so the pressure points are internal deadlines set by the school rather than an external series.
programmes.countryNote: The Personal Project is the item that catches families out, because it has a long runway and no weekly homework to keep it visible. Ask for the project's internal deadlines at the start of the year and put them on a wall. That one action removes most of the risk without buying a lesson.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Two years, six subjects, and a core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The year has a clear shape: content and internally assessed work in the first year, consolidation and paper practice in the second, with the core running underneath both and competing for the same weeks.
programmes.countryNote: Almost every Saudi IB school sits the May session, so the second year is organised around it and the first year is where the quiet work has to happen. Families who start support in the first year buy teaching; families who start in the final term buy technique. Both are worth having and they are not the same purchase.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: An IB route combining Diploma courses with a career-related study and its own core. Subject assessment in the Diploma courses works the same way, so support for those subjects is identical; what differs is the surrounding structure and the absence of the full six-subject requirement.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is far less common in the Kingdom than the Diploma, so a family should check the IB's own school directory rather than assume local availability. Where it runs, confirm with the coordinator exactly which Diploma courses the student is registered for before planning any outside support.

ib-home-tutors.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects families most often cover from outside school, described by when in the course the difficulty arrives. Timing matters because a topic met late leaves no room to consolidate before the papers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The step change arrives when calculus meets function work and proof, usually well into the first year, and it exposes any weakness in manipulation from the year before. Students who were comfortable until then suddenly are not, and the cause is almost always algebraic fluency rather than the new topic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The exploration is the timing risk here, because it usually needs real data and data has to be found, cleaned and understood before anything can be analysed. Students who leave the data-gathering until the drafting stage lose weeks they do not have in the second year.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level extension topics tend to land late in the course, when paper practice should be starting, and they are the ones with no Standard Level equivalent to fall back on. The internally assessed investigation needs equipment access, which means it has to be planned around the school's timetable rather than the student's.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium are the hinge: they arrive early enough to be forgotten and are examined in ways that punish vague language. Organic chemistry at Higher Level comes later and rewards sequence over recall, which is a different kind of revision from the one students default to.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume is the problem rather than difficulty, and the volume is back-loaded. Students who have not built a habit of writing to the command term during the first year find the final months consumed by content, with no time left for the technique that actually moves the mark.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy can be fixed quickly at any point in the course. Evaluation cannot: it is a way of thinking that takes a term to build, which is why starting in the final weeks limits what is achievable. Higher Level quantitative work adds a second front late in the second year.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The internally assessed work governs the timetable. It needs a real organisation and a question the available evidence can answer, and both take time to settle. Students who choose an organisation they cannot get information about discover the problem months after it was fixable.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessment is spread across the two years rather than concentrated, so a weak start is both easier to hide and harder to recover. The skill that pays is connecting technique to effect on a reader, and it builds slowly through regular written work rather than through a late intensive.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: The productive skills respond to steady weekly work and almost nothing else, because register and text-type convention are habits. A student who writes one piece a week for a year will outperform one who writes twenty pieces in the final month, whatever their vocabulary.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: The decision between the two courses is made at the start and shapes everything after it, so it should be reviewed on written evidence in the first term rather than taken on fluency in conversation. Set texts in the A course need reading time that cannot be compressed late on.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internally assessed solution has a long tail: a real client, agreed success criteria, development and documentation. It has to start in the first year. Written paper technique, including pseudocode conventions and trace tables, can be built later and usually is.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The two components with the longest runway and the least weekly pressure, which is exactly why they slip. Both contribute up to three points through the published matrix and a failing grade in either is a condition on the award, so they belong on the calendar in the first year.

ib-home-tutors.regionsTitle: What the journey looks like, wherever the family is
ib-home-tutors.regionsIntro: The case for teaching online rather than travelling is different in each part of the Kingdom. In the big cities it is about time lost to traffic; in the smaller ones it is about whether the specialist exists within driving distance at all. Both arguments end in the same place.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Roughly an hour across in traffic, which means an evening arrangement involving a car costs somebody between forty minutes and two hours on top of the lesson. Families in the northern districts and families near the centre have different school runs to the same schools, and the slot has to be set accordingly.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north towards Obhur, so a cross-city journey can take most of an evening. The common pattern here is a slot set later than the parent first proposes, after the school run rather than during it.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One conurbation behaving as a single school and labour market, with families routinely living in one city and schooling in another. The King Fahd Causeway to Bahrain adds further movement. A fixed online slot is the only part of the week that does not change when the commute does.

regions.name: Compounds and company communities
regions.note: Life on a compound or camp is tightly scheduled and the school is usually close, which removes the travel problem and replaces it with a subject-choice problem: cohorts are small and a subject group can be strong one year and absent the next. Outside support fills whatever this year's cohort does not.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities on either coast where international provision is built around the plants. Small candidate numbers narrow subject choice at Higher Level, so the request here is more often for a whole subject than for a top-up, which changes the frequency and the schedule.

regions.name: Makkah, Taif and Madinah
regions.note: Makkah sits roughly 80km east of Jeddah, Taif climbs into the hills beyond it, and Madinah is further north with limited provision at Diploma level. Visitor seasons change traffic patterns enough that a slot depending on a journey is unreliable for parts of the year.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: The north-west sees constant arrivals as families relocate for new projects and heritage development. Students turn up mid-course with subjects started elsewhere, and the first job is an audit of what transfers rather than a general revision programme.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait and the south-west
regions.note: Two cities about 25km apart at altitude sharing a catchment, a long way from the main international-school markets. Here the question is not how long a tutor would spend driving but whether a specialist in a given Higher Level subject exists within several hundred kilometres.

regions.name: Al Ahsa, Qatif and Ras Tanura
regions.note: Al Ahsa lies about ninety minutes inland from the Eastern Province cluster, with Qatif and Ras Tanura on the coast to the north. Close enough for a school commute, far enough that a travelling evening arrangement rarely survives a full academic year.

regions.name: Buraidah, Ha'il, Najran and Jazan
regions.note: Provincial cities where a Diploma cohort may not exist locally at all and families often work with a school that offers part of an international programme. Support here is frequently the main teaching for a subject rather than a supplement to it.

schoolClusters.note: The International Schools Group runs several campuses across the province and the Diploma is offered at some of them rather than all, which is worth confirming before enrolling. British and Cambridge curricula are also well established around Dhahran. Students we support attend schools including these; no affiliation is implied or held.

The capital holds the deepest concentration of IB World Schools in the Kingdom, listed in directories across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes. Depth of choice means the useful questions here are about subject-level staffing rather than about which school to pick.

The western region carries both IB and Cambridge provision along the coastal spine, with The KAUST School serving the research campus community north of the city. Families in Makkah, Taif and Madinah comparing options are usually comparing schools on this list.

ib-home-tutors.modesIntro: Four ways a weekly arrangement is usually shaped, all of them delivered online over live video and all of them pinned to Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: One slot, held all year
modes.description: The arrangement that works best and costs least per unit of progress. The same hour, the same day, the same tutor, from the start of the year through to the series, with written work set and marked between sessions. Continuity is what makes small weekly gains add up, and it is the thing a travelling arrangement is worst at.

modes.title: A second session added for the final stretch
modes.description: Most families need one hour for most of the year and two for the last stretch before the papers. Adding the second session at a planned point is cheaper and calmer than negotiating it in a panic, and the tutor can reserve the time in advance rather than finding it when demand across the market is at its highest.

A tutor questions the research question, checks work against the published criteria and gives feedback on drafts the student has written. No part of an assessed piece is produced for the student.

modes.title: Catching up after a move mid-year
modes.description: Relocation inside the Kingdom and into it is constant, and a move costs a student their school, their teachers and their cohort in one week. This arrangement begins with an audit of what was covered and what assessed work exists, then teaches to the gap while the new school settles the timetable.

sections.heading: What a search for IB home tutors is really asking
paragraphs: The literal answer first. In-home tutoring in the Kingdom means a tutor who travels to a family's address for a fixed hour, and it exists mainly in the larger cities because that is where enough tutors and enough families are close enough together to make the journey worth anyone's while. Published figures for private tuition in Saudi cities include a travel loading in the price, and marketplace guides quote senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 an hour and above, with the premium reflecting the commute as much as the teaching. Outside Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster, the practical problem is not the price. It is that the specialist in a given Higher Level subject may not live anywhere nearby.

What families actually want from that search is usually four things: somebody who knows the exact syllabus, a slot that holds every week, no wasted evening, and continuity if the family moves. Three of those four are easier to deliver without a car in the arrangement. The fourth, knowing the syllabus, is where the difference is largest: a family restricted to tutors within a reasonable drive is choosing from a handful of people, while a family choosing online is selecting from everyone who teaches that subject at that level in a workable time zone.

This is where IB Gram is explicit rather than coy. Lessons for Saudi families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and no tutor is sent to a Saudi address. That is not a limitation dressed up as a feature; it is the reason a family in Abha can work with a Higher Level Physics specialist at all, and the reason a family in Riyadh can keep that specialist after moving to Al Khobar. The comparison below is the honest version, including the two things a travelling tutor genuinely does better.

Those two things are worth naming. A tutor in the room can read a teenager's body language more easily, and a tutor in the room is harder for a distracted student to ignore. Both are real, and both are addressable: a camera at the right angle, work shared on screen rather than read out, a parent who knows when the session runs, and a tutor who sets written work that has to come back. What a travelling tutor cannot do is be the right specialist when the right specialist lives four hundred kilometres away.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and the slots that actually exist
paragraphs: The Saudi school week runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. A surprising amount of tutoring material written for this market ignores that, because it was written elsewhere and the place names were changed. The consequence is advice about Monday-to-Friday routines and weekend intensives that does not fit the week a Saudi student actually lives in.

In practice the week has four usable weekday evenings. Sunday is the hardest, because it is the first day back and students arrive flat. Monday through Wednesday are the strongest, and Wednesday is often the best single slot of the week for a subject that needs concentration. Thursday evening behaves the way a Friday evening does in a Monday-to-Friday country: the student has mentally finished, and a demanding session scheduled there wastes everybody's time. Friday and Saturday suit longer work, a full timed paper or a drafting session on assessed work, because nothing follows them.

There are two local rhythms worth planning around rather than being surprised by. School days shorten during Ramadan and evening patterns shift substantially, so most families move their slot later in the evening for that period; the dates move each year, so the sensible approach is to agree the change as it approaches rather than to assume a particular arrangement. The long summer break is the other, and the question of whether a slot is held or released through it should be settled at the start of the year rather than in the week you want to pause.

The practical recommendation is dull and it works. Pick the second or third weekday evening, keep it for the whole year, and protect it the way a family protects a sports fixture. A slot that moves every week is not a routine, and a student who does not know when the lesson is has not prepared for it.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against a tutor's own working week
paragraphs: Saudi Arabia keeps Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not observe daylight saving. That single fact causes more cross-border scheduling failures than any other, because the Kingdom's clock stays still while the tutor's may not. A slot agreed as 'six in the evening' with a tutor in a country that changes its clocks twice a year will move twice a year, and it will move in whichever direction nobody wanted.

The fix takes one sentence in writing: the lesson is at a stated time in Saudi local terms, and the tutor adjusts their own diary when their clocks change. That sounds obvious and it is routinely not done, which is why a term that started smoothly falls apart halfway through for no apparent reason.

Beyond the clock change, a tutor's own working week decides whether a weekly slot is sustainable. A Saudi early-evening lesson is a late-evening one for a tutor in India, which works but is not comfortable for a year. The same lesson lands in the afternoon for a tutor in the United Kingdom, which is the most comfortable overlap available and the reason so many arrangements end up there. A tutor already in the Gulf shares the clock entirely, and a tutor far to the east or west is agreeing to work at an hour they will eventually resent. Ask where the tutor is and what time the lesson falls for them. A tutor who answers that question comfortably will still be holding the slot in the final term.

One more detail matters on a Kingdom-wide page: the time zone is the same everywhere in Saudi Arabia, so none of this changes between Riyadh, Jeddah and Jazan. What changes between cities is the school run, which is why the slot inside a Saudi evening differs by city even though the clock does not.

sections.heading: The school run, and the slot that quietly fails
paragraphs: Ask a parent what time a lesson should start and they will answer with the time the school day ends plus the drive home. Ask again after a month and the real answer is forty minutes later, because the school day ends when the last sibling is collected, the drive home is longer on three days of the week, and a teenager who walks in the door hungry is not ready to think about calculus.

This is why the slot families choose in September is often not the slot that works in November. A lesson set too early turns into a sequence of apologetic messages about traffic; a lesson set too late runs into homework and sleep. The reliable answer in most Saudi cities is to set the time generously, eat first, and start when the student is at a desk rather than when they are expected to be.

The city matters. Riyadh is about an hour across, so a family whose school sits on the opposite side of the city should not plan an early-evening start at all. Jeddah's coastal spine has the same effect in one dimension. In the Eastern Province cluster, families living in one city and schooling in another routinely add half an hour each way. On a compound the journey is short and the schedule is busy with everything else, which produces the opposite problem: a slot that competes with activities rather than with traffic.

None of this applies to the lesson itself once the format removes travel from the arrangement, which is the point. The only journey left in the week is the student's walk to a desk, and that is the one journey nobody has ever cancelled. Families who have previously used a travelling tutor usually notice the difference not in the teaching but in the number of lessons that actually happen across a term.

sections.heading: The Diploma year, counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Everything above is logistics. This is the part that decides what support can achieve, and it is the thing almost no competing page sets out. A Diploma year has a shape, that shape repeats, and the cost of an intervention depends almost entirely on where in the shape it lands. No calendar year appears below, because the structure is what is useful and the dates belong to your own school.

Working backwards: the papers sit at the end, and almost every Saudi IB school sits the May session, which the Diploma coordinator confirms. Before them come mock examinations, which are the school's main evidence for a predicted grade and therefore matter far more than students assume. Before those, the final stretch of teaching, by which point internally assessed work should be finished or close to it. Before that, the entry administration, which has its own deadlines held by the examinations officer rather than by a teacher. Before that, the whole first year, which is where the content and the assessed components are supposed to happen. For Cambridge and Pearson candidates in the same household, the main sitting is the June series with a November series used for resits and late entries.

Read that list in reverse and the economics become obvious. Support starting in the first year can teach content, build technique, settle the Extended Essay question and keep assessed work on schedule, and it has time to fix a foundation gap underneath all of it. Support starting after the mock papers can sharpen technique, fix timing, and work on a short list of repeated errors, which is genuinely valuable and much narrower. Support starting in the final weeks can do the third of those three. Each of those is worth buying; a family should simply know which one they are buying.

One practical step is worth more than a plan: ask the school for its internal deadlines, in writing, at the start of the year. Internal dates sit earlier than external ones and they are what a student is actually judged against day to day. A family with those dates on a wall has already removed most of the avoidable risk in the Diploma year, and they also have the information a tutor needs to schedule anything at all.

sections.heading: Two calendars in one city
paragraphs: A family can live on one street in a Saudi city and have children in schools running two different academic years. Ministry of Education public schools run a two-semester year, beginning in late August and ending in late June, with an autumn break in November, a midyear break in January and a break for Eid Al Fitr. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars, and most run three terms with dates that differ school by school within the same city.

That has three consequences for anybody arranging weekly support. Siblings in different systems have different holidays, so a household's quiet weeks are not the same for every child. A tutor who assumes one calendar will schedule into the other child's break. And a family comparing schools has to read each school's own published calendar rather than a general statement about the Saudi year, including this one.

The second consequence is about when support should start. A three-term school has two natural points to begin, at the start of the autumn term and at the start of the spring term, with the third term too late for anything but technique. A two-semester school has one clean start and one mid-year restart. Beginning at the start of a term rather than in the middle of one is worth more than it sounds, because the teaching sequence at school and the teaching sequence at home stay aligned.

The practical instruction is to collect two documents at the start of the year: the school's own calendar and its list of internal assessment deadlines. Neither is hard to get and together they let a family and a tutor plan a whole year in one conversation. Families who skip this end up planning in four-week increments, which is how a Diploma year gets away from a household.

sections.heading: Which subjects need outside teaching, and when they bite
paragraphs: Scarcity in this market is specific rather than general. Nobody struggles to find somebody to teach introductory mathematics, and almost everybody struggles at some point with Higher Level Physics, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry at Higher Level, and the less widely chosen languages. The reason is arithmetic: a school needs enough candidates to timetable a class and enough specialists to teach it, and the subject with the fewest students loses out on both counts.

Timing compounds it. Higher Level extension topics tend to arrive late in the second year, when paper practice should be starting, and they are precisely the topics with no Standard Level equivalent to fall back on. A student who meets them for the first time in the final term is meeting new content in the weeks they most need to be consolidating. Internally assessed work has the opposite profile: it needs to start early, has no weekly pressure to keep it visible, and punishes a late start with a deadline that does not move.

Then there are the foundation topics that bite twice. Algebraic manipulation is the clearest: weak manipulation shows up in calculus, in physics rearrangement, in chemistry proportion work and in statistics, and every one of those looks like a topic problem. Repairing the foundation fixes four symptoms at once, which is why a good tutor insists on a diagnosis before a schedule. Graph work behaves the same way across the sciences, and so does precision in written definitions in Biology.

The practical move is to ask the school which Higher Level options are actually running this year, who teaches each one, and where the internally assessed work is carried out. Those three questions, answered in writing, tell a family exactly which subjects will need support and roughly when. Asked a year earlier, they also tell a family whether a subject choice is realistic before it is locked in.

sections.heading: Assessed work on a calendar, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Internally assessed work is where a weekly arrangement earns its money, because it is the part of the Diploma with a long runway and no weekly homework to keep it visible. The exploration, the investigation, the Personal Project and the Extended Essay all reward an early start and punish a late one, and none of them can be rescued by effort in the final weeks if the research question was wrong at the beginning.

The method is a calendar, not inspiration. Collect the school's internal deadlines, work backwards to a date for settling the question, a date for a first full draft and dates for the feedback rounds the school allows, then hold those dates the way a weekly slot is held. A student who knows that a draft is due in three weeks writes differently from one who knows it is due 'soon'. Most of the value here is administrative, which is unglamorous and happens to be true.

The boundary is fixed and it is not ours to move. A tutor may teach the skills a task needs, interrogate a research question, explain what a criterion is asking for, point out that a conclusion describes rather than evaluates, and give feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not write any part of an assessed piece, may not rewrite a paragraph into better English, and may not hand over a structure to be filled in without understanding. Work that is not the student's own is academic misconduct, the school is obliged to act, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on whoever produced it.

A family can audit this easily, which is worth knowing when the tutor is in another country. Keep the dated drafts, keep a short record of what each session covered, and ask the student to explain out loud why a paragraph changed. A student who can do that owns their work. A draft that arrives transformed from a student who cannot defend it is a problem regardless of how convincing the finished piece looks, and the time to notice is before it is submitted.

sections.heading: What the school controls, and what a family has to arrange
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, with school evaluation and accreditation running through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. That system establishes whether a school may operate and how it has been evaluated as an institution. It does not establish whether one Higher Level subject has a specialist this year, and that is the question that decides a grade.

The school controls the entries, the internal deadlines, the predicted grades, the supervision of assessed work and which options are timetabled. A family controls the rest: whether a weekly routine exists, whether assessed work is started early, whether a foundation gap is repaired, and whether somebody with the right specialism is teaching the subject the school could not staff. Confusing the two lists is how a year gets lost, because a family waits for the school to solve a problem that was never theirs to solve.

There is a third category that catches people out, which is the subject a school offers only online or through a shared arrangement with another provider. That can work perfectly well and it shifts responsibility: nobody in the building is tracking the student's progress day to day, and the family has to ask for evidence more often than they would otherwise. Treat that subject as the one most likely to need outside support, because the feedback loop is longest.

The useful habit is to ask specific questions and write down the answers. Which Higher Level options are running and who teaches each. Who supervises Extended Essays and how many each supervisor carries. Where internally assessed investigations happen and with what equipment. What the internal deadlines are. Schools answer specific questions straightforwardly; general questions produce reassurance, and reassurance is not information a family can plan around.

sections.heading: What a weekly arrangement costs, with the travel loading removed
paragraphs: Rates in this market are advertised rather than regulated, and everything quoted here is somebody else's published figure attributed to the kind of source that publishes it. None of it is a market average and none of it is what IB Gram charges. Tutoring companies list IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180 an hour, with Higher Level and premium tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Tutor-marketplace guides put senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 and above and general private tuition for a primary child at around SAR 50. Non-specialist online tutoring is advertised from about SAR 55.

What moves a figure, in order of weight: how scarce the specialist is, marking or examining experience, the level of the course, whether anybody travels, and the length of the commitment. Only one of those five disappears when the format changes, and it is the travel loading, which buys a family no teaching at all. That is the whole of the cost argument on this page, and it is smaller than the scarcity argument.

The more useful question for a year-long arrangement is what the hour includes. Reading a draft properly against published criteria, marking a full past paper against its mark scheme and writing a note a parent can use all take time outside the lesson, and two providers quoting the same hourly figure can differ substantially once a term of that work is counted. Ask how many drafts and papers are covered, what the turnaround is, and what the parent actually receives.

Then do the arithmetic over a year rather than a month. A weekly hour across three terms is somewhere around thirty to thirty-four sessions once holidays and examination weeks come out, plus whatever additional sessions the final stretch needs. Budgeting at that resolution makes the decision about the second session later in the year a planned one rather than an emergency, which is cheaper in every sense.

process.title: Start with the week, not the subject
process.description: Tell us which evenings genuinely work once the school run and siblings are accounted for, and what time the student is realistically at a desk. A slot set honestly at the beginning survives the year; a slot set optimistically gets renegotiated in the second month and abandoned in the fourth.

process.title: Send the school's calendar and deadline list
process.description: The published term dates and the internal deadlines for assessed components let a tutor plan a whole year in one conversation instead of in four-week increments. Both documents are easy to request and most families have never asked for the second one.

process.title: Meet a matched specialist in a free trial lesson
process.description: A working session, not a sales call. The tutor should say where the marks are going in the work you have sent, what the first month covers, and where in the year the difficulty in this subject usually arrives. Ask where they are based and what time the lesson falls for them.

process.title: Pin the slot to Saudi local time in writing
process.description: Agree a stated time in Arabia Standard Time so that a clock change in the tutor's country moves their diary rather than your lesson. Settle the summer and Ramadan arrangements at the same time, while nobody needs them, rather than in the week they arrive.

process.title: Review at the end of each term
process.description: Check progress against components rather than against a feeling: a paper type, a criterion, a topic, a timing budget. Term boundaries are the natural points to add a second session, reduce frequency, or change tutor if the agreed measure has not moved.

whyPoints.title: A slot built to survive a year
whyPoints.description: The arrangement is agreed in Saudi local time against a Sunday-to-Thursday week, with the Ramadan timing change and the summer break settled in advance. Nothing in it depends on anybody completing a journey, which is the single biggest cause of lessons quietly disappearing from a term.

whyPoints.title: The year mapped before the teaching starts
whyPoints.description: Internal deadlines, term dates and the point in the course where this subject gets difficult are established at the start, then everything schedules backwards from the series. Families who plan at that resolution make the decision about extra sessions early, when it is cheap.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, wherever they are
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Physics or Analysis and Approaches specialist is scarce in every market in the region and absent from much of the Kingdom. Choosing online means selecting from everyone who teaches that syllabus in a compatible time zone rather than from whoever lives within a drive.

whyPoints.title: Continuity through a relocation
whyPoints.description: Moves inside the Kingdom are common and they cost a student their school, their teachers and their cohort at once. A tutor matched on the syllabus rather than the district keeps working through the move, which is worth considerably more in that month than it was before it.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work kept honest and on schedule
whyPoints.description: Explorations, investigations, the Personal Project and the Extended Essay are planned backwards from the school's own dates, with criterion feedback on drafts the student wrote. No part of an assessed piece is produced for them, and the limit is explained to the family at the start.

whyPoints.title: Nothing asserted that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no success rates, no ratings and no tutor counts. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform holding no approval, accreditation or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or ETEC, and no relationship with any school named here.

faqs.question: How many terms before the submission deadline should internally assessed work actually begin?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's first formal checkpoint, and the reason is the research question rather than the writing. A question that cannot be answered with the evidence available will produce a weak conclusion no matter how much work follows it, and discovering that late leaves no room to change course. In practice the question should be settled around a term before the first full draft is due, with data gathering or reading beginning immediately afterwards. Ask the school for its internal deadlines at the start of the year and work backwards from them; the external dates are later and less useful for planning.

faqs.question: What does feedback on a draft look like when the tutor cannot hold the paper?
faqs.answer: Better than it sounds, because everything is on screen and both people are looking at the same thing. The draft is shared, the published criteria sit beside it, and the tutor works through it naming which criterion each section is serving and where a paragraph describes rather than evaluates. Comments are written so the student can act on them afterwards, which is more useful than verbal remarks nobody remembers. The student makes every change themselves. A session record of what was discussed is kept, which also answers the question a school may later ask about outside support.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark a practice version of an internal assessment so my child sees how the criteria work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most useful things a tutor can do without going anywhere near the real piece. A short practice task on a different topic, marked strictly against the published criteria, shows a student exactly where the band boundaries sit and what the wording is actually asking for. The learning transfers and nothing assessed has been touched. The alternative, learning criterion wording on the piece that counts, is how students end up two bands below their ability on work they genuinely did themselves.

faqs.question: What does plagiarism software catch in an IB essay, and what does it miss?
faqs.answer: It catches text matching published sources, other students' submitted work and material it has previously seen, which covers copying and poorly handled quotation. It is weaker on work written to order by somebody else, on ideas taken without wording, and on citation that exists but misrepresents what a source said. That is why schools do not rely on software alone: supervisors ask students to talk through their own argument, and a student who cannot explain their own reasoning is visible in a conversation long before any report is run. Keeping dated drafts and research notes is the simplest protection a family has.

faqs.question: How do we keep a Theory of Knowledge essay the student's own when the whole argument has to be reshaped?
faqs.answer: By changing the question rather than the text. A tutor can say that an argument has no counter-position, that an example does not support the claim being made, or that two paragraphs are making the same point twice, and then stop. The student decides what to do about it. Where a tutor begins supplying the counter-argument or the better example, the thinking being assessed stops being the student's. Keep each version of the essay, and if the student can explain why the argument changed between two drafts, the work is theirs.

faqs.question: If the school asks whether we are using outside support, what should we be able to show?
faqs.answer: Tell them plainly, because schools generally prefer to know and some have a stated position on it. What is worth having to hand is a short record of what each session covered, the dated drafts of any assessed work, and a clear statement of what the tutor does and does not do with that work. Nothing about having a tutor is irregular; what a school needs confidence about is that assessed pieces are the student's own. A family who can produce a session history and a draft trail has answered the question before it becomes a problem.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level Physics topics most often need teaching from outside the school?
faqs.answer: The extension topics that have no Standard Level counterpart, because there is nothing to fall back on and they tend to arrive late in the course when paper practice should be starting. Fields, induction and the more mathematical treatments of waves and circular motion are the usual candidates, and they are hard for a school running a single small class to resource properly. The second recurring need is the internally assessed investigation, which requires a question narrow enough to control with the equipment that actually exists rather than the equipment a textbook assumes.

faqs.question: Why do strong Chemistry students lose marks on energetics and equilibrium questions?
faqs.answer: Because both topics are examined on precision of language rather than on recall. A student can state Le Chatelier's principle correctly and still lose marks describing a shift without naming the change in concentration, pressure or temperature that caused it. Energetics punishes sign errors and loose use of terms like endothermic and spontaneous. The topics also arrive early enough in the course to be half-forgotten by the time they are examined. The fix is written practice marked strictly against the mark scheme, which exposes vague language that sounds right when spoken aloud.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level Biology topics have no Standard Level equivalent, and when do they bite?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level extension material, which sits on top of the shared content rather than deepening it, and which therefore cannot be approached by revising the Standard Level treatment harder. It usually arrives in the second year, competing with revision time for everything else. Biology's particular difficulty is volume: the extension content is substantial, precisely examined and back-loaded. Students who have built the habit of writing to the command term during the first year cope; students still learning that technique in the final months end up doing two jobs at once.

faqs.question: Where does weak algebra show up later in Higher Level Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Everywhere, and it never announces itself as an algebra problem. It appears in calculus, where a differentiation is correct and the simplification that follows is not. It appears in function work and in proof, where a student cannot see that two expressions are the same thing written differently. It appears in physics and chemistry as an apparent weakness in those subjects. The diagnosis takes ten minutes: a short set of pure manipulation questions with all context removed. The repair is dull, fast and pays out in four subjects at once.

faqs.question: What does an Economics mark scheme want in an extended response that a textbook answer does not give?
faqs.answer: A judgement, supported both ways, that answers the question actually asked. Textbook answers explain a concept thoroughly and stop. Mark schemes reward application to the specific context in the question, a weighing of the argument against a counter-argument, and a conclusion that commits to a position with a reason. Diagrams are part of it: a correct diagram with unlabelled axes and no stated shift scores badly. The pattern to look for in a student's work is well-informed writing that never reaches an evaluative sentence, and it takes a term of regular written practice to change.

faqs.question: Which part of English A: Language and Literature is most often rushed at the end of the course?
faqs.answer: The reading. Assessment in this subject is spread across both years, which makes it easy to postpone, and set texts cannot be absorbed quickly in the final months. Students arrive at the last stretch having read some of the material carefully and the rest only in outline, and the difference shows immediately in how specific their analysis can be. A reading schedule agreed in the first year is worth more than any amount of late revision, because the skill being assessed depends on familiarity nobody can manufacture in a fortnight.

faqs.question: How should a student revise a language B subject differently from a science?
faqs.answer: By producing rather than reviewing. Science revision can involve reading, recalling and practising question types; language B improves mainly through writing and speaking regularly, with correction. One piece a week for a year, marked for register and text-type convention rather than only for grammar, will outperform twenty pieces written in the final month. The same applies to the oral components, which reward rehearsed fluency in a format rather than vocabulary breadth. The implication for scheduling is that a language subject needs continuity more than intensity.

faqs.question: Why do families in one Saudi city commute to a school in another?
faqs.answer: Because international provision is unevenly distributed, and the right curriculum at the right stage may simply not exist locally. In the Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran cluster this is routine and the distances are manageable. Elsewhere it means a long daily journey, a weekly arrangement or a relocation, and families in Makkah, Taif or Madinah often look towards Jeddah for a Diploma. The cost of that commute is paid in the student's evening, which is also why a slot that requires no further travel tends to be the part of the week that survives.

faqs.question: What happens when a school cannot run a Higher Level subject after subject choices have been made?
faqs.answer: Usually the option is withdrawn because candidate numbers fell below what justifies a class, and the student is offered the subject at Standard Level, a different subject, or self-study with some supervision. All three change the student's position materially, and the third is the one that needs outside teaching rather than encouragement. Ask the school in writing at what candidate number an option is withdrawn, and raise it the moment numbers look marginal. A family who finds out early has choices; a family who finds out in the second year mostly does not.

faqs.question: How does an international school's three-term year differ from the Ministry of Education's two semesters?
faqs.answer: Ministry of Education public schools run two semesters from late August to late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and a break for Eid Al Fitr. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, with dates that differ school by school in the same city. For a household with children in both systems the holidays do not line up, which matters when scheduling weekly lessons. Always work from the individual school's published calendar rather than from any general description of the Saudi year.

faqs.question: What does a family have to arrange itself when a school offers a subject online only?
faqs.answer: The monitoring, mostly. A subject taught remotely by a provider the school has contracted can work well, and the difference is that nobody in the building is watching the student's day-to-day progress or chasing a missed deadline. Ask who marks the work, how often feedback arrives, who holds the internal deadlines for any assessed component, and who the family contacts when something slips. Treat that subject as the likeliest candidate for outside support, because the feedback loop is the longest one in the student's timetable.

faqs.question: Can we keep the same tutor if we move to another Saudi city mid-year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the few things that goes right in a month when everything else changes. A move costs a student their school, their teachers, their cohort and often their timetable in the same week. Keeping the one adult who knows how they write and what they were working on means there is a continuous thread through the disruption. The practical points are small: the time zone is the same everywhere in the Kingdom, so the slot itself does not need changing, and the new school's calendar and internal deadlines have to be collected again.

ib-home-tutors.closingHeading: Set the slot, then map the year
ib-home-tutors.closingBody: If you have been looking for IB home tutors in Saudi Arabia, the two things worth settling first are not about teaching at all. Decide which weekday evening genuinely works once the school run and siblings are counted, and get your school's term dates and internal assessment deadlines in writing. With those in hand, a free trial lesson with a specialist in your child's subject and level will tell you where the marks are going and what the rest of the year should do about it. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, pinned to Arabia Standard Time, around the Sunday-to-Thursday week.

ib-igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: Each coach below states the board, the level and the components they have taught and marked. Ask about the component carrying the lost marks rather than the subject as a whole; that is where coaching earns its fee or does not.

intro.heading: Coaching is bought to move marks, so start with where marks live
paragraphs: A family paying for coaching is buying a change in a number, and the number has a structure. An IGCSE grade is the sum of marks on named components, awarded against a published scheme, then converted to a grade by a boundary set after the papers are marked. Nothing about that process rewards general improvement. It rewards a specific answer to a specific question in a specific form, which is why coaching that targets a component tends to pay and coaching that revisits a whole syllabus tends not to.

The honest first question is therefore not what an hour costs but what the hour is being asked to do. Advertised rates in the Kingdom run from around SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to roughly SAR 200 to 220 for advanced tracks at tutoring companies, with general private tuition in Riyadh quoted above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects and IB subject tuition listed from around SAR 180. Those are rates providers publish about themselves. They are not a market average and none of them is our price, which is quoted once the subject, level and scarcity are known.

The second question is whether the ceiling has already been set. Cambridge tiers many of its subjects, and a Core entry is graded C to G, so a Core candidate who answers every question correctly is still awarded a C. An Extended entry is graded A* to E and examines content the Core papers never contain. Pearson Edexcel grades 9 to 1 and tiers mathematics at Foundation and Higher. If the tier is wrong for the target, no amount of coaching reaches it, and that conversation belongs with the school rather than with a coach.

The third is technique, which is where the cheapest marks in the paper sit. Command terms are instructions with mark allocations attached: outline, explain, distinguish, suggest, evaluate and calculate are paid differently, and a correct paragraph written against the wrong term earns very little. Boundary movement, significant figures, units, labelled diagrams and the habit of showing credited working belong in the same category. None of it requires new content and all of it is teachable in weeks rather than terms.

Everything here is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Arabia Standard Time and fitted to the Sunday to Thursday week. IB Gram does not send a coach to a Saudi address; in-home visits are a service we offer only in India. What follows prices the formats, works through tier, boundaries and command terms, compares one-to-one with a small group, sets out when each year group is worth spending on, and ends with what coaching cannot move. Each part names something a family can check with the school or on an invoice.

ib-igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: Four courses are coached in the Kingdom at this stage and the money goes to different places in each. The useful distinction is how much of the grade is decided before the papers begin.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Written papers at the entered tier, with a practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences and coursework in a few subjects. Almost all of the grade is decided in the examination room, which makes technique coaching unusually good value here.
programmes.countryNote: Tier is the decision Saudi families most often discover late, because it is made by the school and does not appear on a report card. Ask for it in writing, and ask what evidence it was based on.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1 on terminal written papers, with mathematics tiered at Foundation and Higher and the sciences entered without tiers. Practical skills are examined inside the written papers rather than separately.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school enters some subjects with Edexcel and others with Cambridge, the two grade scales do not translate into each other. Comparing a 6 with a B across a report card is a false comparison a coach should refuse to make.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed with no terminal papers and a Personal Project at the end. Coaching here buys habits rather than marks: structured writing, research that can be cited, and the ability to work to a published descriptor.
programmes.countryNote: Spending heavily here and stopping at the examination year is the wrong order. The expensive year is the one carrying an entry, so plan the budget backwards from that.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. A substantial share of each subject grade is internally assessed at school and moderated by the board.
programmes.countryNote: Internally assessed work is marked long before the May session, so the Diploma coaching calendar starts earlier than families expect and the final term is rehearsal.

ib-igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: These entries say where the marks sit, because that decides whether an hour of coaching is well spent. Levels are given since a Higher Level course is not a longer Standard Level one.

subjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Method marks are available even when the answer is wrong, so unshown working is the commonest avoidable loss here.

subjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Observation and inference marks on the practical component are awarded separately from the chemistry, and candidates routinely answer one while losing the other.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
subjects.description: Extended-response items pay for the sequence of reasoning. A correct conclusion with no steps scores a fraction of the available marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
subjects.description: Definitions are marked against specific wording and diagrams are credited for labelling, so a paraphrase that reads well can score nothing.

subjects.name: Cambridge Economics 0455
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the data-response question carry more credit than prose, and evaluation marks need a stated judgement.

subjects.name: Cambridge First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Reading marks are awarded for selection and reshaping rather than coverage, which is why fluent summarisers score below their apparent level.

subjects.name: Edexcel Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: The tier overlap means a borderline candidate's grade can be higher on Foundation than on Higher, which makes the entry decision worth real attention.

subjects.name: Diploma Higher Level sciences
subjects.description: The third paper and the internally assessed investigation are separate jobs, and the investigation is marked at school before the papers are sat.

ib-igcse-coaching.regionsIntro: What coaching costs in practice depends on who is available, and availability is local. A city with several schools entering the same board has a deeper pool of people who have taught the paper.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest provision and the most contested evening slots. Scarce specialists fill Sunday and Monday first, so flexibility on the evening buys more than negotiation on the rate.

regions.name: Jeddah and Makkah
regions.note: Cambridge and Diploma provision sits in different schools, and the Makkah calendar bends around Hajj and Umrah seasons, so blocks are better bought short.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: Short commutes make early evening coaching workable, which is why this is the easiest part of the Kingdom to hold a standing weekly slot in.

regions.name: Jubail, Yanbu and Ras Tanura
regions.note: Small school rolls mean a subject can rest on one teacher, so the gap a family is paying to fill is usually a whole course rather than a component.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait and Najran
regions.note: High-altitude 'Asir and the far south, with limited international provision and no realistic local specialist in a tiered science.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: Project timetables set the household's evening and families arrive mid-course, so notice periods matter more than headline rates.

schoolClusters.note: Schools in the capital enter Cambridge, Edexcel and the Diploma, sometimes within one campus, setting tier decisions on their own evidence. Two children in one compound can face different ceilings in the same subject.
Dammam, Al Khobar, Dhahran and Jubail behave as one market, and not every campus runs the Diploma. The commonest coaching request here is a single Higher Level subject the school cannot staff.

sections.heading: What coaching costs, and what the money is buying
paragraphs: Price in this market is quoted per hour and spent in formats, and the formats are not substitutes for each other. A block of one-to-one hours on a failing component is expensive per hour and cheap per mark, because the work is targeted and the result is visible on the next marked paper. A term of general weekly support is cheaper per hour and frequently more expensive overall, since nothing in particular finishes and there is no point at which a family can judge whether it worked.

The advertised range gives the shape of the market. Tutoring-platform listings in the Kingdom advertise general online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour, and some budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Tutor-marketplace guides put general private tuition in Riyadh near SAR 50 for primary work and above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring companies list IB subject tuition from around SAR 180, with Higher Level and advanced tracks advertised at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Each of those is a provider's own published rate.

What a family should compare is not the headline but the contents of the hour. Marking between sessions, written notes, past-paper supply and the cost of a cancelled slot either sit inside the fee or appear later. Two quotes that look twenty riyals apart can be fifty apart once those are counted. Ask for the inclusions in writing, ask what a cancellation costs, and ask whether the rate changes closer to a series.

sections.heading: Tier entry: the ceiling set before coaching starts
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake in this market is paying for coaching towards a grade the entry does not allow. Cambridge Core is graded C to G. A Core candidate who sits a perfect paper is awarded a C, and a family coaching that candidate towards a B is buying something that cannot be delivered. Cambridge Extended runs A* to E and examines content absent from the Core papers, so the two entries are different courses in practice rather than two difficulties of one.

Edexcel works differently and the difference matters. Mathematics is tiered at Foundation and Higher on the 9 to 1 scale, the tiers overlap in the middle, and the sciences are entered without tiering at all. A borderline candidate can score a higher grade on Foundation than on Higher, because the Higher paper spends its marks on content the candidate will not reach. That is a judgement about which range is realistic, not a judgement about ability.

Tier is a school decision, made on classwork, internal assessments and mock evidence, and it can be changed only while the entry window is still open. A family who disagrees has one useful argument, which is marked work showing the candidate handling the harder questions. Ambition is not evidence. So the first thing coaching should establish, before any teaching, is what tier the candidate is entered for and whether the target grade is reachable inside it. Ask for the tier and the target in the same message, and compare them before booking anything.

sections.heading: Grade boundaries, raw marks and why the same score moves
paragraphs: A raw mark is not a grade. After a series is marked, the board sets the mark required for each grade on each component, and that threshold moves between series because papers are not identical in difficulty. A candidate who scores the same percentage in two different series can be awarded different grades, which is not unfairness but the mechanism that keeps a grade meaning the same thing when one paper turns out harder than another.

Two consequences follow for coaching. The first is that a mock percentage converted into a grade using last series' boundaries is an estimate and should be described as one. A coach who announces a grade from a mock mark is overstating what the number supports. The second is that marks near a boundary are worth more than marks in the middle of a band, which is the honest argument for spending the final weeks on the components where a candidate is losing marks cheaply rather than on the topics they find most interesting.

It also explains why a remark is rarely the answer a family hopes for. A remark checks that the scheme was applied, not that the boundary was kind, and schools can advise on when one is worth requesting. The useful work sits before the papers: finding the marks being dropped for reasons that have nothing to do with knowing the subject, and removing those. That is what the next section is about.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest marks in the paper
paragraphs: Every question carries an instruction and a mark allocation, and the two are connected. State and outline want short answers and are over-answered constantly. Explain wants a mechanism, not a description. Distinguish wants both sides in one sentence. Suggest wants an applied idea rather than a recalled fact. Evaluate wants a judgement with the reasoning behind it, and a list of advantages answered against it loses roughly half the credit available. None of this is subject knowledge.

The mark allocation is the second instruction. A six-mark answer wants six creditable points or three developed ones depending on the scheme, and a candidate who writes a page for two marks has spent minutes they needed elsewhere. Coaching this is mechanical work: take past-paper questions, read the command term aloud, predict what the scheme pays for, then compare with the published scheme. Most candidates improve measurably within a handful of sessions, which is why it is the best value coaching available at IGCSE.

The same discipline applies to the surrounding habits that lose marks silently. Working shown in the form a method mark requires. Units written on a final answer. Significant figures carried consistently. Diagram labels placed where the scheme expects them. Graph gradients read from the line rather than from data points. A coach who marks to the published scheme and explains why a mark was withheld teaches all of this incidentally; one who writes a score at the top of a script teaches none of it.

sections.heading: One-to-one against a small group, priced honestly
paragraphs: One-to-one is the right purchase when the problem is specific to the student. A content gap, a misconception that keeps reappearing, an internally assessed piece that needs feedback against criteria, a component that has failed twice. The value comes from the diagnosis as much as the teaching, and nothing in a group setting substitutes for a coach reading one candidate's script line by line.

A small group is the right purchase when the problem is general. Command terms, time per mark, question order, how to read a mark scheme, what to do in the last twenty minutes of a paper. These are the same lessons for every candidate sitting the paper, they coach well with four or five students, and the cost per student is lower. A group also produces something one-to-one cannot: a candidate sees how someone else answered the same question, which is frequently more persuasive than being told.

What a group cannot do is repair an individual. A student who has not understood moles, or cannot factorise, will sit quietly in a technique group and leave no better. The practical arrangement for a family with a limited budget is a short block of one-to-one hours on the specific gap, then group technique sessions through the final term. Buying group sessions because they are cheaper, when the problem is content, is how a term disappears. Spending the cheaper budget first on the wrong problem is the common error here, and a short written diagnosis is what prevents it.

sections.heading: Year group by year group: when coaching is worth paying for
paragraphs: Spending early is not automatically better. In the Middle Years Programme and in Year 9 the useful purchase is habit: structured writing, arithmetic fluency, the ability to work to a published descriptor. Those are cheap to build and expensive to retrofit, but they do not need weekly paid hours for two years. A term of targeted work in Year 9 often removes the need for a term of expensive repair later.

Year 10 is where content accumulates and where a gap first becomes compounding, because the Extended papers assume earlier topics rather than revisiting them. Coaching here is best bought in short blocks aimed at the specific topic a mock has exposed. Year 11 is the technique year, and it is the year where command-term coaching and timed-paper work earn more per hour than anything else. Buying content coaching in the final eight weeks is triage rather than teaching, and a coach should say so.

The Diploma inverts the calendar. Internally assessed work is produced and marked at school long before the May session, so the first Diploma year carries real deadlines and the second is mostly rehearsal. A family planning Diploma coaching around the final term has already missed the part where the money would have mattered most, which is the first year's internal assessment and the Higher Level subject choices made at the end of the IGCSE year. The money that counts in the Diploma is spent in the first year rather than the last.

sections.heading: Predicted grades, and what coaching cannot move
paragraphs: A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by a school from the evidence it holds, and it is used by universities and post-16 courses as an indication rather than a promise. It is not a target a coach can be paid to produce, and a coach who offers to raise one has misunderstood who issues it. What coaching can do is change the evidence the school is looking at, which is a slower and more honest route to the same place.

Several other things sit outside what any coach controls. The tier a school has entered, once the window has closed. The boundary a raw mark falls against. Whether a university or a post-16 provider accepts a given grade. Whether a Ministry of Education equivalency decision, which an international certificate needs before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate, is granted and when. Each of those belongs to an institution, and a family should check the relevant one's own published criteria.

What a coach is accountable for is narrower and checkable. Marked work returned on time with the reason a mark was withheld. Teaching against the published specification rather than a general version of the subject. An honest account of what the weeks remaining allow. And a willingness to say that a target is not reachable, or that the problem is the subject list rather than the hours, which is the part a family is least likely to hear and most likely to need.

faqs.question: How much of an IGCSE grade is decided before the written papers begin?
faqs.answer: Less than families assume. In most Cambridge and Edexcel courses the written papers carry the overwhelming share, with coursework in only a few subjects and practical skills either sat as a component or examined inside the papers. The tier, however, is decided long beforehand, and it sets the range the papers can award. The grade is open; the ceiling is not.

faqs.question: Why can a Core-tier candidate's best possible grade be lower than a weaker Extended candidate's?
faqs.answer: Because the two entries are graded on different scales. Cambridge Core runs C to G and Extended runs A* to E, so a flawless Core performance is awarded a C while a modest Extended performance can be awarded a B. The Extended papers also contain content the Core papers never reach. The entry decision therefore deserves as much attention as the teaching, and has to be raised before the window closes.

faqs.question: How many marks does a single misread command term usually cost in one paper?
faqs.answer: More than families expect, because the same misreading repeats. A candidate who treats evaluate as describe will do it in every question that asks for a judgement, and on a paper with three such questions that is a substantial share of the available marks. The repair is mechanical: read the command term aloud, predict what the scheme credits, compare with the published scheme. Most candidates change measurably within a few sessions.

faqs.question: How is the alternative-to-practical paper marked differently from a practical examination?
faqs.answer: It examines the reasoning rather than the manipulation. Instead of performing a procedure, the candidate reads a described experiment and is credited for identifying variables, spotting sources of error, recording observations in the expected form and drawing a supported inference. The subject knowledge is necessary and not sufficient. It is a distinct skill, rarely taught as its own thing, and it coaches well in a short block.

faqs.question: Does a resit grade replace the first one on a statement of results, or sit beside it?
faqs.answer: That depends on the board and the qualification, and the school's examinations officer is the person who can confirm it for your entry. What matters for a coaching decision is narrower: the second sitting examines the same specification, so repeating the same preparation produces close to the same mark. A resit earns its cost only where something specific changes: a component never properly taught, or a paper missed through documented illness.

faqs.question: What does a coaching plan look like when three subjects are weak at once?
faqs.answer: It protects two and lets the third run on school teaching for a term. A Saudi week offers about four usable weekday evenings, and a teenager holds one substantive hour of new teaching per evening, so three subjects at once means three thin arrangements. The honest plan names the subject being left alone and sets a date to revisit it.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether we are paying for teaching or for supervision?
faqs.answer: Look at what comes back. Teaching produces marked work with the reason each mark was withheld, a stated sequence of topics, and work set between sessions. Supervision produces a session in which the student did their homework with company. Both have a place and should not cost the same. If the session notes describe activity rather than diagnosis, you are buying the second.

faqs.question: What should a coach do when the school and the family disagree about tier?
faqs.answer: Produce evidence and then stay out of it. A coach can set the candidate Extended-level past-paper questions, mark them to the published scheme, and give the family a document showing what the candidate can actually do. That is a useful contribution to a conversation with the school. Arguing the case on a family's behalf is not a coach's role; the decision rests with the school.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for coaching in a subject the student actively dislikes?
faqs.answer: Only with a narrow target and an endpoint. Coaching a disliked subject towards general improvement rarely works, because the student will not do the work between sessions. Coaching it towards a specific threshold, in a block with a stated number of hours and a visible finish, sometimes works well. Agree the target and the block, and judge it on the marked papers rather than on enthusiasm.

faqs.question: Which Year 9 habits decide how much IGCSE coaching a family ends up buying?
faqs.answer: Three of them. Whether the student writes down working rather than doing arithmetic in their head, since method marks are unavailable to anyone showing nothing. Whether they can read a question for what it asks rather than for what it reminds them of. And whether they can finish a timed piece of writing. A term spent on those in Year 9 removes a surprising amount of paid repair in Year 11.

faqs.question: Is coaching in Year 10 cheaper over two years than concentrating it in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually yes in total cost and definitely yes in outcome, provided the Year 10 hours are targeted. Short blocks aimed at the topic a mock has exposed prevent the compounding gap that makes Year 11 expensive, since the Extended papers assume earlier content rather than revisiting it. Spreading light weekly support across both years costs more and delivers less, because nothing ever finishes.

faqs.question: What does a Year 11 student need in the term after mocks?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis from the mock, then technique. The mock script is the best evidence a family gets before the real papers, and it should be read question by question for cause: content, a misread command term, timing, or unshown working. The term after mocks is then spent on whichever of those dominates, with timed papers marked to the published scheme in the final weeks.

faqs.question: Does a student going into the Diploma need coaching over the summer between courses?
faqs.answer: A small amount, aimed narrowly, is often the best value purchase of the whole two years. Useful targets are the algebraic fluency Higher Level mathematics assumes, the topics a Diploma science treats as known from IGCSE, and writing against criteria rather than to a mark allocation. Pre-teaching a term of content is not useful, since nothing reinforces it before the autumn.

faqs.question: At what point in the final year does extra coaching stop adding anything?
faqs.answer: When the student is spending lesson time being taught rather than practising. In the last two or three weeks the marginal value of new teaching falls close to zero while the value of timed papers, command-term drilling and a written plan for the final fortnight stays high. Adding hours then displaces the candidate's own revision, which nobody else can do.

ib-igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Check the ceiling, then buy the marks
ib-igcse-coaching.closingBody: Before paying for anything, get three facts in writing from the school: the board, the four-digit syllabus code and the tier for each subject. Then find the most recent marked paper. With those a coach can say whether the target is reachable inside the entry, which component is losing marks, and how many hours it needs. Send them to IB Gram and the first session is free; you keep the written diagnosis either way. Coaching runs one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.
