intro.heading: Find the entry, then count the weeks back
paragraphs: A search for home tuition usually starts with a worry rather than a plan: a mock result, a parents' evening, a child who has stopped showing working. The useful first move is not booking lessons. It is finding the entry already lodged with the board. Every IGCSE candidate in the Kingdom is entered for a named syllabus, at a named tier, for a named series, and that entry decides what the next few months have to achieve. A family who knows the entry can count backwards from it. A family who does not is paying for lessons against a syllabus nobody has confirmed.

The entry is also where the honest bad news lives. Cambridge IGCSE is tiered on many subjects. A Core entry is graded C to G, so a Core candidate who answers everything correctly is still capped at a C. An Extended entry is graded A* to E and examines content the Core papers never reach. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 and tiers mathematics rather than the sciences. None of this appears on a report card, and the tier is a school decision that can be changed only while the entry window is open. Ask the examinations officer for the tier and the component list in writing, and ask early.

With the component list in front of you, the year stops being a stretch of terms and becomes a sequence with a deadline at the end. Coursework and practical preparation sit earlier than families expect. Timed past-paper work sits later than most students want. The eight weeks before the June series are for rehearsal, not for first teaching, and a family starting inside those eight weeks is buying triage. That is sometimes the right purchase. It should be a decision rather than an accident, and the component list is the only honest basis for making it. A tutor should say plainly which of the two is on offer.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one tuition over live video. The phrase in this page's address says home tuition because that is what Saudi families type, and the honest answer is that the in-home market in the Kingdom is thin and expensive outside Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam cluster. A tutor who can reach a villa in Al Malqa by five o'clock is chosen from whoever lives twenty minutes away and is free. A tutor on a video call is chosen from the people who have actually taught the paper your child sits. We do not send anyone to a Saudi address; in-home teaching is a service offered only in India. What follows is the syllabus, the countdown, the market, the assessed-work line and the mid-course arrival, in that order.

ib-igcse-home-tuition.programmesIntro: Three courses account for nearly every request at this stage, and they are assessed in genuinely different ways. What matters for tuition is the component list rather than the badge on the gate: what is marked at school, what the board marks, and what is tiered.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Most British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom enter candidates across eight to ten Cambridge subjects. Assessment is by written paper, with a practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences. Many subjects are tiered, and the school picks the tier at entry.
programmes.countryNote: The practical component is the one families discover late. A school without a staffed laboratory timetable usually enters candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper, which tests experimental reasoning on paper rather than at a bench.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Edexcel runs on the 9 to 1 scale, built around terminal written papers, with mathematics at Foundation and Higher tier and the sciences entered without tiering. Paper structures differ from Cambridge's even where topic lists overlap.
programmes.countryNote: Some Saudi schools run both boards in one building, entering mathematics with one and the sciences with another. Ask which board each subject is entered with, because the mark schemes reward different working.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries internally assessed work marked at school and moderated by the board, plus written papers in the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Families searching for IGCSE help are often a year from this. The Higher Level set is the decision that matters, usually made in the spring term on mock grades.

ib-igcse-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: One grid, both boards, because a family at this stage is usually juggling an IGCSE candidate and a Diploma decision. Each entry names what the course is marked on and where the weeks go.

subjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: The Extended paper examines topics Core never reaches, so a Core entry is not an easier version of the same paper. Algebra and transformations carry the losses.

subjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Three papers, with practical skills assessed at a bench or through the alternative-to-practical paper. Qualitative analysis is the reliable source of lost marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
subjects.description: Extended-response questions want a chain of reasoning, and most candidates write the conclusion without the steps that earn credit. Graph gradients and units are examined throughout.

subjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
subjects.description: Definitions are marked strictly and diagrams are credited for labelling. Extended adds depth in transport, genetics and homeostasis, where a candidate moved up from Core feels the jump.

subjects.name: Cambridge First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Directed writing and the analysis of two linked texts. Fluent writers lose marks by summarising when the task asks them to select and reshape material.

subjects.name: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Higher Level mathematics. It assumes fluency rather than building it, so weak Year 9 algebra surfaces here first.

subjects.name: Edexcel Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Graded 9 to 1 across two papers with no coursework. Higher overlaps the top of Foundation, so a borderline tier decision is about which grade range is realistic.

subjects.name: Edexcel Sciences 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Entered without tiering, with practical skills examined inside the written papers. A candidate arriving from Cambridge keeps the content and relearns the question style.

subjects.name: Diploma mathematics and sciences
subjects.description: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches adds an unlabelled third paper at Higher Level, and the sciences add internally assessed investigations.

ib-igcse-home-tuition.regionsIntro: Distance changes the calendar more than the syllabus. Where several schools in a city enter the same board, a family can calibrate against other candidates' mocks. Where there is one school, or none, planning has to start earlier.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Several schools enter both boards, so mock timetables cluster and comparison is possible. The city is an hour across in traffic, so evening slots are agreed to the minute.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur. Families choose the school over the commute, then find the commute chooses the lesson time.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One school and labour market across three cities. Children sit the same series in different buildings, so a neighbour's mock mark is a poor benchmark.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Few international schools and a small local tutor pool, so a second opinion on a tier entry is rare.

regions.name: Makkah, Madinah and Taif
regions.note: Fewer international schools, and a Makkah calendar that bends around Hajj and Umrah seasons. A tutor in another time zone is the default.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: Rapid in-migration, families arriving mid-course, schools still building subject coverage. The question is what can be recovered before the series.

schoolClusters.note: Schools around the capital enter Cambridge, Edexcel and the Diploma, sometimes in one campus. Entry deadlines and mock timetables differ, so two children in one compound can be on different countdowns.

Along the Jeddah spine, Cambridge and Diploma provision sits in different schools, with German and Indian schools adding further calendars. A mid-course move changes the component list, not just the timetable.

sections.heading: How an IGCSE grade is actually built
paragraphs: A grade is not an average of what a student knows. It is the sum of marks awarded on named components, each carrying a fixed share and each marked against a published scheme. On a Cambridge science that usually means a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper, and either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper. On Edexcel it usually means two longer written papers with the practical skills examined inside them. That difference changes what revision should look like for six months.

Tiering is the second structural fact and the one with the hardest edge. Cambridge Core is graded C to G, so a Core candidate who sits a flawless paper is awarded a C and no amount of teaching lifts that ceiling. Cambridge Extended is graded A* to E and contains content the Core papers do not. Edexcel grades 9 to 1 and tiers mathematics at Foundation and Higher. The school chooses the tier at entry, and the choice is reversible only while the entry window is open.

This is why a good tutor's first question is not how your child is finding the subject. It is which code, which tier, which components. A family who can answer that in one message is matched to someone who has taught those papers. A family who cannot usually spends the first fortnight of paid lessons finding out, which wastes the weeks left. The examinations officer holds all three facts and will put them in writing if asked.

sections.heading: Counting back from a series
paragraphs: Working forwards produces a plan that runs out of time. Working backwards produces one with dates in it. Fix the series first, June for most Saudi candidates and November for resits, then place the fixed points behind it. Entries close several months ahead of the papers, and the entry carries the tier. Coursework deadlines sit earlier still in the subjects that carry it. Mocks sit roughly a term out, and their real job is to generate evidence rather than a grade.

The eight weeks immediately before a series are the ones families most often try to buy, and they are the least elastic. A candidate can rehearse in eight weeks. A candidate cannot meet organic chemistry for the first time in eight weeks and hold it under examination conditions. Where a family arrives late, the honest plan sacrifices topics on purpose: it drills the ones that recur in every paper and leaves the rest alone rather than touching everything thinly.

The fixed points also move, and they move per school. International and British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom set their own calendars, and most run three terms while Ministry of Education schools run two semesters, so two children in one neighbourhood can be a fortnight apart on mocks. Ramadan drifts about eleven days earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, landing in a different part of the course for each cohort and shortening school days. Plan from your own school's published calendar, because a general one is not a substitute.

sections.heading: What the November series is for, and when it is not
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series and a November series, and Saudi candidates are entered for one of those two. The February and March series is run for candidates in India and is not an option here. Much of the tutoring copy circulating online was written for an Indian audience and quietly assumes a third entry point, so a family planning around a series that does not exist in the Kingdom loses a term.

November suits three situations. A candidate who missed a paper through illness and has documentation. A candidate who sat June and needs one grade lifted for a post-16 requirement. And a candidate entered late by a new school, where November buys back the time a relocation cost. It suits nobody who wants another attempt without changing anything, because the second sitting examines the same specification and a repeat of the same preparation produces close to the same mark.

What carries over varies by subject and board, and the school has to confirm it rather than the family assuming it. Coursework marks sometimes carry; practical components sometimes do not. Do the arithmetic before committing: a November entry costs the fee, a term of teaching, and a student revising an old course while starting a new one. Where the grade is not a prerequisite for anything, putting the hours into the next qualification is often better, and a tutor who never says so is selling lessons rather than advice.

sections.heading: What the in-home market in the Kingdom charges
paragraphs: Advertised rates in this market sit wide apart. Tutoring-platform listings advertise general online tutoring in the Kingdom from around SAR 55 an hour, and some budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Tutor-marketplace guides put general private tuition in Riyadh near SAR 50 for primary and above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring companies list IB subject tuition from around SAR 180, with Higher Level tracks advertised at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Those are advertised rates published by providers, not a market average, and none is our price.

What moves the number is mostly scarcity. A Higher Level Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specialist costs more than a Standard Level mathematics tutor everywhere, because there are fewer of them. Marking experience for the relevant board moves it again, and level moves it, with Higher Level above Standard Level, above Middle Years Programme work, above IGCSE. Package length moves it down; travel moves it up.

In-home teaching in the Kingdom carries a travel loading that is rarely itemised. An hour of teaching in Al Olaya at six in the evening can cost a tutor ninety minutes of driving, and that time is priced in whether the invoice says so or not. It also narrows the pool to whoever lives nearby and is free at that hour, which is why families outside the three large urban clusters often cannot find a tiered-science specialist at all. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in Saudi Arabia; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

sections.heading: Entries, tiers and the deadline that cannot be reopened
paragraphs: Entries are lodged by the school rather than the family, and most families never see the form. What they do see, closer to the papers, is the statement of entry: a list of the exact components the candidate will sit, with codes. Read it the day it arrives. It is the only document that states, without interpretation, what has been entered, and it occasionally contains a surprise, because a subject can be entered at a different tier from the one discussed in the autumn term.

Tier decisions are made on evidence the school holds: classwork, internal assessments, mocks, and a teacher's judgement about what a candidate can sustain. A family who disagrees has a narrow window and one useful argument, which is evidence rather than ambition. The arithmetic deserves stating plainly. A Core entry caps the grade at C, so a candidate needing a B for a post-16 course cannot get there on a Core paper. An Extended entry a candidate cannot sustain risks a worse outcome than a strong Core performance.

Within an entry there are further choices worth asking about. In the sciences, whether the practical component is sat at a bench or as the alternative-to-practical paper. In some languages and humanities, whether a coursework route is offered at all, because the school chooses that at entry too. In mathematics, whether Additional Mathematics is being entered alongside the main course. Each changes what tuition should cover, and each is a question the examinations officer can answer in a sentence.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on assessed work
paragraphs: IGCSE coursework, a Diploma internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and a Middle Years Programme Personal Project share one rule: the work has to be the candidate's own. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, explain the criteria, read a draft the student has already produced and say what the criteria would reward. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a paragraph, supply the analysis, or hand over a model answer to adapt. Crossing that line puts the whole entry at risk.

Useful feedback sounds different from editing. It names the criterion and the band: this paragraph describes where the criterion asks for evaluation; this method section would not let another student repeat the experiment; this research question is too broad for the word limit. It sends the student back to their own draft with a decision to make rather than a sentence to paste. A good tutor will also tell a family how many drafts the school's own policy allows to be formally reviewed, and will decline to read more than that.

Keep a record. Dated drafts, the student's own notes, and a short log of what each session covered are what answer a question later if one is ever asked. Schools in the Kingdom take academic honesty seriously and run their own procedures; a tutor cannot speak for them. If a provider's offer includes producing assessed work for a candidate, that is not a service with a grey area in it. It is the thing that invalidates the qualification a family is paying for.

sections.heading: Arriving mid-course, and what can be recovered
paragraphs: Families arrive in the Kingdom part-way through a course more often than tutoring copy admits: into Riyadh for a posting, into Tabuk or NEOM for a project, into the Eastern Province for a company move. The first fortnight goes on establishing three things, none of them academic. What the new school has entered the candidate for. What it has already taught. What coursework was completed at the previous school and whether it carries across. Only then is there a plan worth paying for.

What transfers depends on where the student is coming from. A candidate moving from a national-curriculum school into Cambridge IGCSE usually brings the content and lacks the question style, particularly the command terms and the habit of writing to a mark allocation. An American-curriculum student arriving into Year 11 brings breadth and less depth, and feels it most in the tiered sciences. A student moving from a British school into the Diploma brings examination technique and has to learn criterion-marked work from scratch. Each is a different six weeks.

The recovery arithmetic has to be done honestly. A term is enough to close a technique gap in one subject. A term is not enough to teach an unstudied Extended-tier syllabus from the beginning while the student keeps up with five other courses. Where the series is close and the gap is wide, the better conversation is about which subjects to protect, and whether a November entry buys back the time the move cost.

faqs.question: Our child is entered for the June series: when should weekly IGCSE tuition start?
faqs.answer: Count back from the papers rather than forward from today. For a candidate broadly on track, a weekly slot from the start of the year before the series leaves time to teach content in the school's order and keep the final eight weeks clear for timed papers. For a candidate with a specific gap, start as soon as a mock has been marked, because the mock is the evidence the plan is built on.

faqs.question: How many evening slots does a Sunday-to-Thursday week realistically leave for two IGCSE subjects?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families assume. Thursday evening starts the weekend and is usually lost, and the night before a school assessment is rarely productive. That leaves four workable evenings, and most teenagers hold one substantive hour of new teaching on a school night rather than two. Two subjects therefore means two evenings, not one evening twice. Friday and Saturday suit longer timed-paper practice.

faqs.question: Our tutor is in the United Kingdom: what happens to our slot when their clocks change and ours do not?
faqs.answer: The Kingdom stays on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, all year and does not observe daylight saving. A tutor in the United Kingdom moves by an hour twice a year, so a slot agreed in their local time quietly shifts against your evening. Pin the slot to Saudi local time and let their side absorb the change. A seven o'clock Riyadh lesson is four in the afternoon for them in their winter.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly IGCSE slot when Ramadan shortens the school day?
faqs.answer: The slot usually moves rather than pauses. School days shorten and the household's rhythm shifts later, so many families move a late-afternoon session to after the evening meal and shorten it. A tired student in a full hour learns less than a focused one in forty minutes. Ramadan drifts about eleven days earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, so it falls in a different part of the course for each cohort.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach an IGCSE candidate and a younger sibling in the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, where the subjects are close enough that one tutor genuinely covers both, and it is often the practical answer for a family running two timetables. Two consecutive one-to-one slots work better than a shared session, because an Extended-tier candidate and a Year 8 student need different pacing. Where both study the same subject at different stages the same tutor is an advantage.

faqs.question: What does a student moving from a Saudi national-curriculum school into Cambridge IGCSE have to learn first?
faqs.answer: Usually the question style rather than the content. Topic lists overlap more than families expect; what differs is that marks are awarded against a published scheme for a specific command term, in English, under time. The first weeks are best spent writing to a mark allocation and showing working in the form the scheme credits. Technical vocabulary in English is the second task.

faqs.question: Our child joins a British-curriculum school here in Year 11: can they still sit IGCSE at the end of that year?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the answer depends on the entry rather than on ability. Ask the new school which subjects it can still enter the candidate for and at which tier, because the window closes months before the papers. Then ask what coursework is required and whether anything from the previous school carries across. Where a subject cannot be entered in time, a November entry beats a rushed one.

faqs.question: An American-curriculum student is moving into Year 10 here: which subjects will feel hardest?
faqs.answer: The tiered sciences, almost always. An American middle-school course covers breadth; a Cambridge Extended entry wants depth across a narrower topic list, with calculations, defined terms and a practical skills component. Mathematics is the second pressure point, because the IGCSE course assumes algebraic fluency a different sequence may not have built. English transitions easily in content and awkwardly in form.

faqs.question: If we move cities inside the Kingdom mid-term, does the entry move with the student?
faqs.answer: The entry sits with the centre that lodged it, so the receiving school either makes a new entry or accepts a transfer, and that conversation belongs before the move completes. Ask which board the new school uses for each subject, because two Saudi schools can enter the same subject with different boards. Ask about tier too, and get the answers in writing from both examinations officers.

faqs.question: Our child did the Middle Years Programme and is moving into a Cambridge IGCSE school: what is missing?
faqs.answer: Research and project habits usually transfer well; timed examination writing often does not. Criterion-marked Middle Years Programme tasks reward process and sustained work over weeks, while an IGCSE paper rewards a precise answer produced in minutes against a mark allocation. The gap shows up in the first mock as unfinished papers rather than wrong answers. Build timed practice early, starting with short questions.

faqs.question: What should the written diagnosis from a first session actually contain?
faqs.answer: Four things. The board, code, tier and component list the tutor is working from, so you can check it against the statement of entry. A list of topics in priority order, each with a reason drawn from marked work. An estimate of the weeks each item needs. And what the tutor is not proposing to cover, with the reason, because a diagnosis saying everything needs work is not a diagnosis.

faqs.question: How soon after starting should we expect marks to move, and what moves before them?
faqs.answer: Technique moves first and marks follow, usually a full paper later. In the first month look for fewer blank responses, working set out in the form the scheme credits, units handled consistently, and command terms answered as written. Those are visible on any marked script. A grade moves in whole steps, so it can lag real improvement by several weeks, which is normal.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether a stalled student needs a different tutor, fewer subjects or more hours?
faqs.answer: Separate the three causes before buying any of them. If the tutor's account of the problem does not match the school's, the match or the diagnosis is wrong. If the student is not doing the work between sessions, more hours will not help and the subject list is probably too long. If both are sound, the tier or the target may be wrong.

faqs.question: Can we stop after the first month without losing what we have paid for?
faqs.answer: Set a review date before the first payment and the question answers itself. Pay in short blocks rather than long packages until the match is proven, and ask in writing what happens to unused sessions. The diagnosis from the first session is yours whether you continue or not. Four to six weeks is long enough to see whether the work between sessions has changed.

With those, a plan can be counted back from the June or November series. Send them to IB Gram with a piece of marked work and we will arrange a free trial lesson with a tutor who has taught those papers, delivered one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

ib-igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: Each profile states the board, the specification code and the papers that tutor has taught or marked, plus the levels they cover. That is deliberate: a subject degree and a teaching qualification tell you different things, and neither tells you whether somebody knows Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 or Edexcel 4MA1 Higher tier. Read the specification line first.

intro.heading: The money first, then the person, then the logistics
paragraphs: Start with the number, because that is what most families are trying to establish and what almost every page in this market avoids. Published rates in the Kingdom are advertised figures from providers rather than any measured average. Tutoring platforms advertise general, non-specialist online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour and budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Tutor-marketplace guides put primary-age private tuition at roughly SAR 50 and senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 and upwards. Tutoring companies list IB subject tutoring from about SAR 180, with Higher Level and premium tracks advertised at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Some international providers quote around USD 60 an hour.

Those bands only become useful once you know what sits inside the hour. An in-home arrangement prices travel into the rate whether or not anybody itemises it, which is why senior-subject quotes in this market start where they do. An online hour has no travel in it, but it may or may not include marking between lessons, past papers and mark schemes, or a written note afterwards. Two quotes that look twenty riyals apart can differ by an hour of marking a week, and marking is where a loss pattern is actually identified rather than discussed.

Then comes the part that decides whether the money works at all: who the tutor is. This market is full of claims that sound equivalent and are not. A subject degree proves content knowledge well beyond IGCSE. A teaching qualification proves training in assessment and planning. A current classroom post proves live knowledge of schemes of work and almost no free evenings. Examiner or marking experience for the board proves something different again, and it is the one that matters most when a student knows the content and still scores poorly. None of them proves familiarity with the specific specification your child is entered for, and that is the thing to check.

Checking it is quick, and a family does not need subject expertise to do it. Ask which board and which specification code the tutor has taught, how recently, and what the commonest avoidable loss is on the paper your child is struggling with. A specialist answers in specifics within seconds, naming papers, tiers and mark-scheme behaviour. A generalist answers in adjectives about building confidence. The difference is audible, it costs nothing to test, and it is more predictive than any badge, rating or years-of-experience figure.

Logistics then shapes what is possible. Lessons for families in the Kingdom are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, inside a week that runs Sunday to Thursday. IB Gram does not run home visits in the Kingdom; they are a service we offer only in India. The search phrase is the one parents type, and it is targeted here honestly: this page explains what in-home tuition involves locally, what it costs, and why a family choosing on specification rather than on distance generally ends up with a better-matched teacher.

ib-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four frameworks account for nearly every IB and IGCSE request from the Kingdom, and each one asks for something different from a tutor. Two are externally examined by a board with published specification codes; two are assessed against criteria inside the school. A tutor who is strong in one is not automatically useful in another.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses with numbered syllabus codes, examined by written papers and, in the sciences, a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Mathematics 0580 and the sciences are tiered: Core papers cap the grade range, Extended papers open the top of it. Grades run A* to G. The tier a school enters a candidate for sets the ceiling before the paper is opened.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the commonest international qualification in the Kingdom's British-curriculum schools, and the tutor requirement is specific: somebody who knows that code's paper structure, not somebody who knows the subject in general. A tutor who cannot say which papers 0620 Extended candidates sit has probably not taught it recently.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other main route, with its own specification codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics and 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 for the sciences. Current specifications are graded 9 to 1. Mathematics is tiered Foundation and Higher; the sciences are untiered and assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical component.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving between schools in the Kingdom sometimes move board without realising it, and a sibling on each board cannot be compared grade for grade. It also changes what a student has rehearsed: an Edexcel science candidate may never have sat a practical or alternative-to-practical paper, which matters if they transfer to a Cambridge school.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and each subject marked against four criteria out of eight rather than by examination. The Personal Project closes the programme, assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. Some schools enter candidates for MYP eAssessment, which pairs on-screen examinations with ePortfolios towards the MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: A tutor for MYP work needs to be fluent in criterion descriptors, which is a different competence from paper technique. Families often hire an examination-focused tutor for an MYP student and wonder why the criterion grades do not move: the student was never losing marks on content.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at two levels graded 1 to 7, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, with the core adding up to three points through a matrix. Most subjects carry an internally assessed component worth a fifth to a third of the subject grade. Higher Level carries more taught hours, extra content and in several subjects a further paper.
programmes.countryNote: At Diploma level the qualification question gets sharper, because Higher Level content goes well beyond what a general subject graduate has used since university. For a Higher Level science or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, recent teaching experience at that level is the credential worth paying for.

ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: For Diploma subjects, what a family should look for in a tutor differs by subject, because the components differ. These entries name the component that usually needs outside teaching and the kind of experience that addresses it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without technology, so the tutor has to be fluent at manipulation on paper at speed, not merely able to reach answers. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is two extended problems where marks run along a chain of reasoning. Recent experience teaching at Higher Level is the credential that matters here more than any other subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology is allowed throughout, so the examination rewards tool choice and interpretation rather than arithmetic. Look for a tutor who talks about contextual conclusions and model limitations, because that is where the marks are lost, and who knows the calculator the school actually uses.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The written papers carry eighty per cent between them and the scientific investigation twenty. Definitions are marked strictly and graph questions are marked on values taken from the line. A tutor who has marked for a board will usually name both of those within a minute of being asked where students lose marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Multi-step calculations and organic mechanisms are the two recurring problems, and the investigation carries twenty per cent. Ask a prospective tutor how they teach mechanisms: an answer about curly arrows drawn rather than described signals somebody who has seen real scripts marked.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments and an investigation worth twenty per cent. The common loss is writing at length when a question pays for three developed points, which is a technique problem. A tutor whose plan starts with mark allocation rather than with topic coverage is reading the problem correctly.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: At Higher Level, Paper 1 is twenty per cent, Paper 2 thirty, the quantitative Paper 3 thirty and the commentary portfolio twenty. Paper 3 is the component most often unsupported in school, so a tutor's experience with quantitative Economics specifically is worth establishing before booking.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1, the guided analysis of an unseen text, is thirty-five per cent at both levels. The only thing that improves it is weekly timed practice with detailed marking, so what matters in a tutor is willingness to mark unseen responses every week rather than literary enthusiasm.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Five prescribed themes with text types that must be produced in the right register. Confident speakers lose marks in writing, where structure and tense accuracy are assessed. A tutor here needs to be a writing teacher, not merely a fluent speaker of the language.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: A pre-released case study underpins one paper, and evaluation rather than tool knowledge decides the top marks. Ask how a tutor teaches evaluation: naming criteria before judging is the technique, and a tutor who cannot describe it will teach the tools your child already knows.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case studies have to be specific to earn credit, and fieldwork is internally assessed. A student in the Kingdom often has strong local material for water, coasts and food systems; the tutoring job is turning general knowledge into named, dated, quantified examples.

ib-igcse-home-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: At IGCSE the specification code is the single most useful thing a family can quote when asking for a tutor, because paper structures differ between boards and between tiers. These are the courses requests concentrate on, with what a tutor should be able to tell you about each.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 with a capped grade range; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach the top grades. A tutor should be able to state that distinction immediately, and should teach written method deliberately, because Paper 4 awards method marks only when the method is visible.

igcseSubjects.name: Edexcel Mathematics 4MA1
igcseSubjects.description: Two papers at each tier, graded 9 to 1, with a calculator permitted in both. The content overlaps heavily with Cambridge but the question style and the mark scheme's wording do not, so a tutor who has only taught 0580 will need to work from the 4MA1 papers rather than from memory.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
igcseSubjects.description: Multiple-choice, theory and either a practical test or the alternative to practical. Moles and stoichiometry come first in almost every plan, then electrolysis and organic chemistry. The alternative-to-practical paper is its own skill and a tutor should say how they rehearse it.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
igcseSubjects.description: Forces and motion, thermal physics, waves, electricity and atomic physics. Definitions are marked strictly, so a nearly correct definition earns nothing, and graph questions reward labelled axes, units and read-offs from the line of best fit rather than from plotted points.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
igcseSubjects.description: From characteristics of living organisms to ecology and human influence. Extended candidates meet longer structured questions on unfamiliar data, where the command word suggest expects reasoning rather than recall. A tutor should distinguish those two in their first answer about the subject.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge First Language English 0500 and ESL 0510
igcseSubjects.description: Two different qualifications that families regularly confuse. First Language English assumes native-level fluency and assesses directed writing and composition; English as a Second Language assesses reading, writing and listening with speaking handled separately. Entering the wrong one caps a strong candidate or overwhelms a developing one.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge Economics 0455 and Business Studies 0450
igcseSubjects.description: Frequently taken together and frequently taught by one teacher. Both reward precise definitions, specific examples and careful reading of the stimulus material before anything is written. Data-response questions are where a tutor's paper experience shows most clearly.

igcseSubjects.name: Edexcel Sciences 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1
igcseSubjects.description: Untiered, graded 9 to 1, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than by a separate practical component. A candidate transferring to a Cambridge school will not have sat a practical or alternative-to-practical paper before, which is a specific gap worth naming early.

ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsTitle: What the local tutor pool looks like, city by city
ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: The in-home market behaves differently across the Kingdom, and that is the practical reason the search phrase and the service on offer diverge. These notes describe what a family typically finds locally when they look for somebody to teach a named specification.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest local pool in the Kingdom and still thin for scarce courses. The city is roughly an hour across in traffic, so a tutor who knows your specification may be geographically available and practically unreachable at five o'clock on a school day.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre up to Obhur, with good school provision and a travel problem of its own: the length of the city means an in-home tutor's working evening covers two or three families at most, which is priced into the rate.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One school and labour market in practice, which widens the pool usefully: a tutor living in Khobar can reach families in all three. Board coverage is mixed across the cluster, so establishing Cambridge or Edexcel before anything else saves a wasted trial.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities with small international cohorts. The local pool for a named Higher Level course is often empty rather than small, and the realistic choice is between a willing generalist nearby and a specialist taught over video.

regions.name: Al Ahsa and Qatif
regions.note: Al Ahsa sits roughly an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, with Qatif on the coast between it and Jubail. Travel time at that distance makes in-home arrangements expensive and fragile, particularly in the final term before a series.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Makkah is roughly eighty kilometres east of Jeddah, so some families draw on the Jeddah market. Household calendars here bend around the Hajj and Umrah seasons, which belongs in the lesson plan rather than being discovered mid-term.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About twenty-five kilometres apart in 'Asir at altitude, sharing one catchment. International-curriculum provision is limited relative to the population, so a family wanting a specific specification taught well usually has to look beyond the two cities.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: The north-west is growing quickly and mid-course arrivals are common. A student joining a specification part-way through needs sequencing work rather than general support, and the local pool is rarely able to supply either.

regions.name: Buraidah, Ha'il, Najran and Jazan
regions.note: Provincial centres where international provision is thin and a named-specification tutor is unlikely to live within reach. Distance, not willingness, is the binding constraint, and it is the honest argument for teaching over video rather than a sales line.

schoolClusters.note: The capital's international schools span IB programmes and Cambridge provision, and some run both, which means two students at the same school can be entered for different boards in the same subject. Establish the board and the specification code from the school before hiring anybody, because the paper structures differ even where the content looks identical.

The International Schools Group operates several campuses in the Dhahran area, with the Diploma offered at the American School of Dhahran and at ISG Jubail though not at every campus. British School Dhahran and Multinational School Dhahran follow British and Cambridge curricula, which is where most of the cluster's IGCSE cohort sits.

ib-igcse-home-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named only to describe where each curriculum sits in the Kingdom; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and a family should confirm board, specification and subject availability with the school itself.
ib-igcse-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three arrangements, priced and scoped differently, cover almost every request. The first is deliberately small, because the commonest waste in this market is committing to a term before anybody has established what is actually wrong.

modes.title: A diagnosis, then a decision
modes.description: A free trial lesson followed by one or two paid sessions whose only output is a written diagnosis: what the student knows, which component is leaking marks, and what a term of work would target. A family can then buy teaching, go back to the school's own clinic, or do nothing. It is the cheapest way to find out whether tutoring is the right purchase at all.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one by subject
modes.description: One subject, one fixed slot, work set after each lesson and marked before the next. The hour starts from the marking rather than from a recap, which is what makes a technique problem shift. Lessons run Sunday to Thursday on Arabia Standard Time and the slot is held through school holidays if a family wants to pause.

modes.title: Paper rehearsal before a series
modes.description: A short block in the weeks before the June or November series, built from whole timed papers rather than topic revision. By that stage the content is what it is; the available marks come from pacing, question order, command-term discipline and showing method. Families take two or three sessions a week for a fixed number of weeks and then stop.

sections.heading: What an hour costs, and what is actually inside it
paragraphs: A home tutor in this market is usually quoted at the upper end of the general tuition band, and the reason is arithmetic rather than greed. A tutor who drives to three families in an evening spends an hour or more in traffic that nobody pays for separately, so it is priced into the lesson. Tutor-marketplace guides put senior-school examination subjects at SAR 200 and upwards, which is the band that absorbs travel. Online, the same hour has no travel in it, which is why tutoring companies advertise IB subject tutoring from about SAR 180 and premium Higher Level tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220.

The more important comparison is not the rate but the contents. Ask explicitly whether work set between lessons is marked and by whom, whether past papers and mark schemes are supplied, whether a written note follows each session, and what happens to the fee if a tutor has to be changed after two lessons. Two providers twenty riyals apart can differ by an hour of marking a week, and the marking is where a loss pattern is identified. A cheap hour with no marking is often the more expensive purchase.

One figure deserves scepticism in both directions. A rate at the very bottom of the band usually buys availability rather than expertise, which is a reasonable purchase for supervised practice and a poor one for a diagnosed component problem. A rate at the very top should come with a specific reason: a named specification taught recently, marking experience for the board, a scarce Higher Level subject. A premium with no reason attached is just a premium, and the question to ask is what the extra buys that the band below does not.

sections.heading: Who the tutor actually is: which credentials predict a result
paragraphs: This market presents several very different things as if they were one qualification, and the differences matter more than the price. A subject degree proves content knowledge far beyond IGCSE and most Standard Level work, and proves nothing about paper structures or mark schemes. A teaching qualification proves training in planning and assessment, which is valuable, and says nothing about depth at Higher Level. A current classroom post proves live knowledge of how schools report and plan, and also means very few free evenings, so availability becomes the limiting factor.

Examiner or marking experience for the board is the credential families understand least and should probably value most in one specific case: when a student knows the content and still scores poorly. Somebody who has marked a paper has seen several hundred scripts fail in the same four or five ways, and they teach against those failures rather than against the syllabus. It is not a general superiority, because marking and teaching are different skills, and a brilliant examiner can be an indifferent teacher. It is a precise advantage on a precise problem.

What no credential proves is familiarity with your child's specification. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 cover similar mathematics with different tiers, papers, grade scales and mark-scheme wording. A tutor who has taught one will need to work from the other's past papers rather than from memory, and an honest one says so. That single question, asked early, filters this market faster than any other: which board, which code, how recently, and what is the commonest avoidable loss on the paper we care about.

sections.heading: Checking a claim in ten minutes, without subject expertise
paragraphs: A parent does not need to know the syllabus to test whether somebody else does. Three questions do most of the work. First, name the board and the code and ask what the paper structure is. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 will say Core or Extended, theory papers, and either the practical test or the alternative to practical, without pausing. Second, ask where students lose marks on that paper. A specialist answers with specifics: units dropped in multi-step calculations, mechanisms described instead of drawn. Third, ask what the first three weeks would look like. A plan that begins with a marked timed paper is a diagnosis; a plan that begins with revising topic one is a syllabus tour.

The trial lesson is the real test, and it should be used as one. A good trial opens the student's most recent marked script and ends with a statement a parent can repeat to the school: your daughter is losing marks on structured questions because she answers the command term she expected rather than the one printed. If the hour ends in encouragement with no diagnosis, nothing has been established, and there is no reason to buy a second hour however pleasant it was.

Two claims deserve particular care. Any figure about past results that cannot be verified should be treated as marketing, because self-reported success rates and star ratings in this market carry no method, sample or date. And a guarantee attached to a grade is not a credential at all: no tutor controls the paper, the boundaries or the candidate on the day, so an offer to promise an outcome tells a family something about the seller rather than about the teaching. Ask instead for a sample of marked work and a written report from another student, with names removed.

sections.heading: Home tutor or online: the comparison, made honestly
paragraphs: The case for a tutor in the room is real and worth stating properly. A younger student who cannot yet work alone on screen for an hour benefits from somebody physically present, and some families simply prefer the arrangement. A tutor at the table also sees a schoolbag, a planner and a bedroom desk, which occasionally explains more than any diagnostic. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student with poor study habits rather than a component problem, that visibility has genuine value.

The case against it in this market is availability. The local pool is everyone who both knows a named specification and lives within a short drive, and for a scarce course in most Saudi cities that intersection is small or empty. Families then do one of two things: hire a generalist and hope, or widen the search. Widening it is what online teaching is for, and the honest framing is that it trades physical presence for selection. The second thing it trades is cost structure, because travel leaves the equation.

IB Gram sells the second arrangement only. Lessons for families in the Kingdom are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. What that means in practice is that the match is made on board, specification and component, that a parent needs to be in the house rather than in the room, and that the tutor's gender, language and marking experience can all be chosen directly because the pool is large enough to choose from. The table sets the two side by side, including where the in-home option wins.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: the same subject, different papers
paragraphs: Board matters more than families expect, and the first question to settle before hiring anybody is which one your child is entered for. The content overlaps heavily; the assessment does not. Cambridge IGCSE grades A* to G, tiers mathematics and the sciences into Core and Extended, and assesses practical skills through a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Current Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications grade 9 to 1, tier mathematics into Foundation and Higher, and leave the sciences untiered with practical skills examined inside the written papers.

Those differences change what a student has rehearsed. An Edexcel science candidate transferring into a Cambridge school has usually never sat a practical or alternative-to-practical paper, which is a specific gap and a quick one to close if it is identified. A Cambridge candidate moving the other way meets a 9 to 1 scale, untiered papers and a different question style. Neither board is harder in general; each is harder in particular places, and the particular places are what a tutor needs to know.

Series availability is identical and worth stating because copied-in advice gets it wrong. Both boards run a June series, which is the main one for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series for resits and November-entry candidates. Cambridge also runs a February and March series, and that one is sat in India rather than in the Kingdom, so a Saudi family should ignore any entry deadline quoted for it. Entries close months ahead of the papers, and the school's examinations officer holds the exact dates.

sections.heading: The week, the clock, and the parts of the year that move
paragraphs: The school week runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and the Kingdom stays on Arabia Standard Time at UTC+3 all year with no daylight saving. Both facts have to be written into an arrangement rather than assumed, because tutoring copy produced for other markets takes a Monday to Friday week for granted. A slot offered on a Saturday morning is being offered inside your weekend, which some families want and most do not.

The clock is where arrangements quietly break. A tutor in India is two and a half hours ahead of Saudi time, one in Pakistan two hours ahead, one in the United Kingdom three hours behind during their winter and two during their summer. Write the slot in Saudi local time and the tutor absorbs their own clock change; leave it in theirs and the lesson moves by an hour twice a year, which a family usually discovers when a student is sitting in front of an empty screen. It takes one sentence at the start to prevent.

Three parts of the year move predictably. School days shorten during Ramadan and household activity shifts into the evening, so lessons usually move later and often shorten, agreed before the month starts rather than improvised during it. The autumn and midyear breaks fall differently for Ministry of Education schools and for international schools setting their own calendars, so two children in one family can be on holiday in different weeks. And the long summer is the only period when a student can work in the morning, which is why it is the right window for rebuilding a weak foundation rather than for pre-teaching next year's content.

sections.heading: Switching into IGCSE, and out of it
paragraphs: A large share of requests from the Kingdom involve a student who changed system recently, and what transfers depends on where they came from. From a national-curriculum school, factual recall and mathematical technique are often ahead of the IGCSE cohort while open-ended writing, source use and the habit of justifying a method are behind. The first month is therefore about question style: what each command word demands, how marks are allocated across a structured question, and why a correct answer with no working can still lose most of the marks available.

From a CBSE or ICSE background the pattern is similar in mathematics and different in the sciences, where the Indian curricula go deeper on some topics and lighter on practical write-up and data handling. From an American curriculum, breadth is familiar and the depth of an Extended-tier paper is not. In every case the useful first step is the same: sit one real past paper, marked to the published scheme, and sort the losses into content, style, method and timing. That sort tells a family which of the four they are buying help with.

Leaving IGCSE matters too, because the tutor who was ideal for Year 11 may be wrong for what follows. The Diploma assesses criteria-marked internal work, Theory of Knowledge and extended independent writing, none of which appears at IGCSE; A Levels go deeper in fewer subjects with a different examination style. A student moving into Higher Level sciences or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches needs somebody teaching at that level now, and the handover is worth planning in the term before the move rather than in the first panicked month of it.

sections.heading: The first month, the reporting, and how to stop paying
paragraphs: A first month should produce evidence and an exit. The evidence is a marked timed paper from week one, a written diagnosis, and a plan that names what will be different in four weeks and how it will be visible. The exit is a review date agreed before any money changes hands. An arrangement with no review date is a subscription, and subscriptions in this market survive on inertia rather than on results, which is how a family spends two terms on a problem that was misdiagnosed in week one.

Reporting should be short and checkable. The paper, the topic, the loss pattern, whether the work set arrived, and what the next fortnight targets. Four concrete lines beat four paragraphs of encouragement, and a note that could have been written about any student in the Kingdom should be sent back. Read in sequence across a term, those notes answer the only question that matters at the review: has the weakness identified at the start actually moved?

At the review there are three honest answers and a parent is entitled to one of them. It is working, continue. It is working too slowly, and here is the specific change: a different component, a different tutor, a different frequency. Or it is not working, and here is why, which might be that the work between lessons is not being done, or that the real gap is a year below where we are teaching, or that the match is wrong. Changing tutor after a month is routine. Stopping is a legitimate outcome, and a provider who cannot say it is not giving advice.
bullets: Agree the review date before the first payment, not after the first term
Four concrete lines per report, naming paper, topic and movement
Weekly marking is what shows whether a loss pattern is shifting

sections.heading: What a tutor can and cannot be held to
paragraphs: Outcomes are the end of the cost conversation and the place where this market makes its least defensible claims. No tutor controls the paper a candidate is handed, the grade boundaries set after marking, or how a sixteen-year-old performs on a particular morning. A promise of a specific grade, a pledge that marks will rise by a fixed amount, or a refund tied to a result is therefore a sales device rather than a professional commitment, and it is worth treating as information about the seller. What a tutor can be held to is process: lessons delivered, work marked, reports written, and a diagnosis that is revisited when the evidence says it was wrong.

Within that, the realistic expectation depends entirely on what was wrong. Pacing and command-term discipline move quickly, often within weeks, because they are habits rather than knowledge. Technique on a specific paper moves over a term with weekly marked practice. A missing foundation from the year below takes longer than a term and is best attacked in a holiday, when there is time to work slowly. Anybody offering the same timeline for all three has not diagnosed the problem.

Assessed coursework has its own hard line, and it is worth knowing before somebody offers to cross it. A tutor may teach the published criteria, review a draft the student wrote, test whether a research question is answerable within the word limit, and teach a method or referencing convention. A tutor may not write, redraft or supply any part of an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or a Personal Project, and editing a student's draft sentence by sentence is the same breach in better clothing. The candidate signs a declaration, the school supervisor authenticates the work, and the consequence of malpractice lands on the student's qualification.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE lesson run on a Friday or a Saturday for a family in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: It can, and some families prefer it, but understand what is being asked. Friday and Saturday are the weekend here, so a session then sits inside family time rather than after the school day. Where it works best is a longer block in the weeks before the June or November series, when a student needs two hours on whole timed papers that will not fit into a school night. For regular term-time teaching, a weekday slot is usually more durable, because weekend lessons are the first thing a family cancels.

faqs.question: How long should an IGCSE session be, and why is ninety minutes often wrong on a school night?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes is the usual length for a student who has already done a full school day, and the reason is attention rather than policy. By the second hour of an evening session most fifteen-year-olds are copying rather than thinking, which produces pages of work and no learning. Ninety minutes or two hours makes sense in a holiday morning or a weekend block, where the student starts fresh. If a subject genuinely needs more time in term, two separate hours on different evenings almost always beats one long one.

faqs.question: If a tutor teaches a full school day elsewhere, which Saudi evening slots are realistically free?
faqs.answer: Fewer than a profile suggests, and the direction of the clock decides it. A full-time teacher in India finishes their own school day in the early afternoon Saudi time, which leaves the whole Saudi evening open to them. One in the United Kingdom finishes mid-afternoon their time, which is early evening here, so a seven o'clock Saudi slot sits neatly after their day. One in eastern Australia is asleep. The useful question is therefore not whether a tutor is available in principle but which single evening is genuinely free for the whole term, because a slot that moves every month stops being a routine the student prepares for.

faqs.question: How much notice is needed to move a standing weekly slot once the term has started?
faqs.answer: A week is comfortable and a fortnight is better, because a tutor's other slots are already committed and a good tutor's diary is largely full. Moving a single lesson is usually possible with a couple of days' notice wherever a gap exists in the same week. Permanently relocating a slot is a different request, since it may mean a different tutor if the original one has no free evening at the new time. Say early if a school activity is about to change the school week.

faqs.question: What happens to an IGCSE slot during the autumn break when school and Ministry calendars differ?
faqs.answer: The slot follows your school's calendar rather than any national one. Ministry of Education schools run a two-semester year with an autumn break in November and a midyear break in January, while international and British-curriculum schools set their own terms, so two children in one family can be on holiday in different weeks. Tell us the dates your school publishes and the slot is either paused and held, or kept and used for lighter work. Families with children in both systems usually keep the slot running through one break and pause the other.

faqs.question: Do lessons continue through the week of a school's internal examinations?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, but with the content changed. During internal examination weeks a lesson is most useful as timed practice and immediate marking on the paper being sat next, rather than as new teaching that nobody has capacity to absorb. Sometimes the right answer is to move the hour to the evening before the subject's paper and keep it very short. What does not help is cancelling the week and resuming afterwards, because the marked internal papers are the cheapest diagnostic evidence available all term.

faqs.question: What transfers from a CBSE or ICSE school into Cambridge IGCSE, and what does not?
faqs.answer: Mathematical technique and factual recall usually transfer well and are often ahead of the cohort. What does not transfer is the assessment style: structured questions marked by command word, practical write-up and data handling in the sciences, and the expectation that method is shown on the page rather than carried in the head. The alternative-to-practical paper is frequently entirely new. The first month is therefore better spent on question style and practical skills than on content, which tends to look after itself.

faqs.question: Should a student finishing Year 11 abroad complete IGCSE there or restart in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Finishing where they started is almost always better if the timing allows, because IGCSE is a two-year course assessed at the end and a mid-course board change can mean different papers, tiers and even a different specification. Where a move is unavoidable, the questions for the receiving school are which board and code they enter, whether any coursework can transfer, and whether the student can be entered in the same series. That conversation belongs before the move rather than after it, because entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to pick up late after a mid-year move?
faqs.answer: The ones with a practical or coursework component and the ones that build cumulatively. Sciences are difficult late because the practical paper or the alternative to practical rehearses skills developed over two years in a laboratory. Mathematics is more forgiving in content and less forgiving in technique, since weak manipulation from earlier years surfaces everywhere. Languages with an assessed speaking component need the earliest start of all. Subjects that are largely content plus essay technique, such as Business Studies or Economics, are the most recoverable in a single term.

faqs.question: Does moving from IGCSE into the IB Diploma need a different kind of tutor?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and families lose a term by assuming otherwise. IGCSE tutoring is largely paper technique against a known question style. The Diploma adds criterion-marked internal assessment, Theory of Knowledge, extended independent writing and, at Higher Level, content well beyond what a general graduate has used recently. A tutor who was excellent for Year 11 may have no Higher Level teaching experience at all. Ask the question directly in the term before the move, and plan the handover rather than discovering the gap in the first month.

faqs.question: What happens to IGCSE coursework already completed at a previous school?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board, the subject and whether the new school enters candidates for the same specification, so the only reliable answer comes from the receiving school's examinations officer. Some components can be carried across where the specification matches; others have to be redone, and in a few cases a school will enter a candidate for an alternative paper instead. Ask before the move, in writing, and ask specifically which series the student will be entered for, because that determines how much time exists to redo anything.

faqs.question: What should the first month of support produce before a family pays for a second month?
faqs.answer: Three documents and one answer. A marked timed past-paper section from the first week; a written diagnosis naming the component and the loss pattern; and short weekly notes showing what was taught and whether the work set arrived. The answer is to a single question: has the weakness named at the start begun to move? If nobody can show you those three things, the month has produced reassurance rather than evidence, and buying a second one is a decision taken on hope.

faqs.question: How do we avoid an open-ended tutoring subscription that nobody reviews?
faqs.answer: Fix the review date before the first payment and write down what will be compared at it. Arrangements drift because no date exists, so each month renews quietly and a misdiagnosis from week one survives two terms. A review needs three things in front of it: the opening baseline, the latest comparable marked paper, and the weekly notes in between. It should end with a decision stated in one sentence: continue, change this specific thing, or stop. Any provider unwilling to schedule that is relying on inertia.

faqs.question: What does a first report from an IGCSE tutor need to contain to be worth reading?
faqs.answer: The specification and paper worked on, the topics covered, the loss pattern identified, whether the set work arrived and was marked, and what the next fortnight targets. One line each is enough. What makes a report worthless is generality: a note about growing confidence and good engagement could describe any student in the Kingdom and cannot be checked. A useful report is one a parent could hand to the subject teacher at school, who would recognise the diagnosis or disagree with it specifically.

faqs.question: What is a realistic expectation over one term for an Extended-tier IGCSE candidate?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is wrong, and an honest tutor says which case yours is. Pacing and command-term errors are habits and often improve within weeks of marked timed practice. Technique on a specific paper improves across a term with weekly marking. A missing foundation from the year below is slower than a term and is better attacked in a holiday. Nobody can promise a grade, because the paper, the boundaries and the day are outside anyone's control. What can be promised is marked evidence each week showing whether the gap is closing.

intro.heading: The hours you can use, not the hours you can afford
paragraphs: Families usually begin with the rate and discover the real constraint later. The constraint is the calendar. A Saudi school week runs Sunday to Thursday, the usable teaching window is the two or three hours between the school run and the point where a teenager stops absorbing anything, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. That window holds perhaps four substantive sessions a week across all subjects, which is the ceiling on what any amount of money buys. That ceiling is the first thing to establish, because every decision about how many subjects to support and how much to spend follows from it.

The rate matters too, and it is worth setting out honestly. Advertised prices in the Kingdom span from about SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to around SAR 220 for advanced tracks at tutoring companies, with general private tuition in Riyadh quoted above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Those are rates providers publish, not a market average and not our price. What moves a number inside that span is scarcity first, marking experience second, level third, and travel fourth, which is the part that disappears when teaching happens over video.

The second hidden cost is drift. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. Every country that does will shift against your evening twice a year, so a slot agreed in a tutor's local time quietly moves by an hour and then has to be renegotiated mid-term. Pinning the slot to Saudi local time costs nothing and removes the single most common reason a weekly arrangement collapses in its third month. It matters for the tutor as well: an hour that is reasonable in their winter can be unreasonable in their summer, and the person who agreed to it will start cancelling rather than renegotiating.

The third is calendar mismatch. International and British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom set their own term dates and most run three terms, while Ministry of Education schools run two semesters. Two children in one neighbourhood can sit mocks a fortnight apart and break for the autumn at different times. Ramadan drifts about eleven days earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, so it lands somewhere different in the course for each cohort and shortens the school day while it does.

All teaching here is one-to-one over live video, timed to Arabia Standard Time, and work is marked between sessions rather than read out during them. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; in-home visits are a service we offer only in India. What follows prices the hour, counts the usable evenings, sets the clock against a tutor's own week, and ends with what a term should have produced. Each part names something you can ask a school, a tutor or an invoice to confirm in writing.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE

programmes.countryNote: Most families in the Kingdom buy one or two IGCSE subjects rather than a full set, which is the right instinct. Four evenings a week cannot carry five subjects, and spreading the budget thin produces a term of light contact with nothing finished.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1 across terminal written papers, with mathematics tiered at Foundation and Higher and the sciences entered without tiers. There is no coursework to schedule around, which makes the hours easier to plan and the final term heavier.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school enters mathematics with Edexcel and the sciences with Cambridge, a family is buying two different past-paper libraries. Ask which board each subject sits with before agreeing a block, because one tutor rarely covers both well.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed with no terminal papers, ending in the Personal Project. Hours here are cheaper per session and better spent earlier, because what is being built is writing and research habit rather than examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: Buying heavily in the Middle Years Programme and then stopping at the IGCSE year is the wrong way round. The expensive year is the one with the entry in it, so budget backwards from that rather than forwards from now.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625

subjects.name: Cambridge First Language English 0500

subjects.name: Cambridge English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: The written papers respond to regular short practice, which makes a shorter weekly session better value here than a long one.

subjects.name: Edexcel Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: The tier decision shapes the hours. A borderline candidate moving to Higher needs the overlap content taught properly, which is a term's work.

subjects.name: Diploma Higher Level sciences

sections.heading: What online tuition is advertised at in the Kingdom
paragraphs: The published numbers in this market sit far apart, and the spread is information rather than noise. Tutoring-platform listings advertise general online tutoring in the Kingdom from around SAR 55 an hour. Some budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Tutor-marketplace guides put general private tuition in Riyadh near SAR 50 for primary work and above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring companies list IB subject tuition from around SAR 180, with Higher Level and advanced tracks advertised at roughly SAR 200 to 220.

Every one of those is a rate a provider has published about itself. None is a market average, none is what a family necessarily ends up paying, and none is IB Gram's price, which is quoted per arrangement once the subject, level and scarcity are known. International providers quoting in dollars add a currency question on top, since a figure near sixty dollars an hour converts into a riyal number that moves with the exchange rate rather than with the teaching.

What should worry a family is not a high number but an unexplained one. A rate that comes with no statement of what the hour contains is the expensive option whatever it says, because marking, note-writing and paper supply either happen inside the fee or get billed later. Ask what is included, ask what a cancellation costs, and ask whether the rate changes closer to a series. A provider that answers all three in writing is easier to compare than one that quotes a lower headline.
