sections.heading: Hours, not rates: what a term of one subject costs
paragraphs: A rate is only half of a price. The other half is the number of hours a problem actually takes, and that is where families either overspend or underbuy. One weak IGCSE subject with a content gap is usually a term of weekly sessions, because the content has to be retaught before paper practice means anything. One weak component in an otherwise sound subject is often eight to ten focused hours. A technique problem across several subjects is not a tuition problem at all until the subject list is cut.

The arithmetic is worth doing on paper before agreeing anything. Twelve weekly hours across a term at a mid-range advertised rate is a real sum of money, and it should be set against what it is replacing. Against a year of the same arrangement it is cheap; against two targeted blocks of six hours each with a review between them it is often not. Buying in short blocks with a stated endpoint keeps the comparison possible.

There are costs that sit outside the hourly figure and they are worth naming. Marking between sessions, which should be included and sometimes is not. Past papers and mark schemes, which are published by the boards. Written reports, which some providers charge for separately. And the cost of a cancelled slot, which is the one families only discover when a school trip appears. None of these is large on its own; together they are the difference between two quotes that looked identical.

sections.heading: Why the Sunday-to-Thursday week limits what you can buy
paragraphs: Five school nights sound like five opportunities. In practice the week yields four, and often three. Thursday evening is the start of the weekend and most households have already stopped working by then. The night before a school assessment is not teachable time, because the student needs it for their own revision. That leaves Sunday, Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday, minus whatever sport, music or family commitment already sits in them.

Inside each of those evenings the window is narrow. The school run finishes somewhere between half past three and half past four depending on the city and the commute, and a teenager is reliably useful for about two hours after that before concentration falls away. One substantive hour of new teaching per evening is the realistic maximum; two hours back to back produces one good hour and one expensive one.

The consequence for spending is direct. Two subjects means two evenings, not one evening twice over. Three subjects means the weekend gets used, which works for paper practice and badly for first teaching. More than three subjects at once means the family is buying contact rather than progress, and the honest advice is to protect two subjects properly and let the others run on school teaching alone until something finishes. A family that supports two subjects for a term and finishes them is ahead of one that touched five and finished none, which is the shape most budgets end up in by accident rather than by choice.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against a tutor's own clock
paragraphs: The Kingdom sits at UTC+3 and does not observe daylight saving, which makes it the stable side of any arrangement. Everyone else moves. A tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, so a seven o'clock Riyadh lesson is four in the afternoon for part of the year and five for the rest. If the slot was agreed in their time, it silently becomes six or eight o'clock on your side.

The offsets decide sustainability as much as convenience. India is two and a half hours ahead, so an early Saudi evening lands late at night there and a seven o'clock lesson is half past nine for the tutor. Western Europe is an hour behind the United Kingdom's position relative to us. Australia and the Far East are far enough ahead that a Saudi evening is the small hours, which rules out anything weekly. A tutor who agrees to an unsustainable hour will cancel in week five rather than week one.

The fix is one line in writing: the slot is stated in Saudi local time and does not move when any other country changes its clocks. Ask a prospective tutor what their local time would be at your preferred hour, and ask what else they teach then. A tutor who has to work it out, or who answers vaguely, has not thought about whether the arrangement survives a year. Put it on the invoice rather than only in a message, so both sides hold the same record.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the autumn break and a prepaid block
paragraphs: Three parts of the year interrupt a weekly arrangement and all three are predictable. School days shorten during Ramadan and the household's rhythm shifts later, so the slot usually moves to after the evening meal and shortens rather than pausing. A tired student in a full hour learns less than a focused one in forty minutes, and agreeing the revised time for the whole period in one conversation is better than rescheduling weekly.

The autumn break and the midyear break come at different times for different schools in the same city, because international schools set their own calendars while Ministry of Education schools run a two-semester year with fixed breaks. A family with children in two schools will have two sets of dates. Hours bought as a rigid block across those weeks are hours at risk, which is the practical argument for short blocks over long packages.

So ask the question before paying: what happens to an unused session, and how much notice cancels one without charge. A reasonable answer is a stated notice period, a small number of carried sessions, and an expiry. An unreasonable answer is silence followed by a credit note nobody can spend. The same applies to the long summer break, which is the one period where buying ahead genuinely works, because specialist hours are easier to get when term-time demand drops. That is also the one point in the year when a scarce specialist's weekly hour is genuinely available, so it is worth asking in the spring term rather than waiting for the autumn.

sections.heading: Three-term and two-semester calendars in one city
paragraphs: Saudi cities run two school years at once. Private and international schools, licensed by the Ministry of Education and evaluated through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, mostly follow a three-term pattern inherited from the curriculum they teach. Ministry of Education schools run two semesters, starting in late August and ending in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. Neither is the other's variant.

This matters for tuition in two ways. The first is timing: a three-term school sits mocks earlier relative to the June series than a two-semester one, so the point at which a family has real evidence to plan from differs by weeks. The second is the mixed household, where one child's half term is another child's ordinary fortnight and a single weekly slot has to survive both. A family moving between two Saudi schools mid-year can also find that the term they had planned around has already happened at the receiving school, which changes what a tutor should be teaching in the first month.

The practical move is to work from your own school's published calendar and nobody else's, and to put the three dates that matter into the tuition plan: when mocks are sat, when coursework is due in the subjects that carry it, and when the school's examination fortnight closes normal teaching down. A tutor who asks for those three dates in the first week is planning. One who asks for none of them is improvising.

sections.heading: What a term of online tuition should have produced
paragraphs: Value is judged on evidence, not on a results day months later. By the end of a term a family should hold four things: the written diagnosis from the first session, a set of marked papers with the reasons marks were withheld, a record of which topics were taught in which order, and a short written verdict on what has changed. If three of those are missing, the term produced lessons rather than progress.

Movement in the evidence looks specific. Fewer blank responses on a marked script. Working set out in the form the scheme credits. Units and significant figures handled consistently. Command terms answered as written rather than as remembered. Grades move later and in whole steps, so a term that shows all four of those and no grade change has still worked, while a term that shows none of them and one lucky grade has not.

The decision at the end of a term is three-way and stopping is one of the options. Continue where the evidence is moving and the student is doing the work between sessions. Change the tutor where their account of the problem does not match the school's. Stop, or cut to one subject, where the plan is sound and the work is not being done, because more hours of the same thing is the most expensive mistake available in this market. Writing the verdict down, even in three lines, is what makes the next term's decision quick rather than another conversation about impressions.

faqs.question: Is a ninety-minute session better value than two separate hours in a Saudi week?
faqs.answer: For writing subjects, often yes: drafting and redrafting needs a run at it, and two short sessions spend half their time restarting. For mathematics and the sciences, usually no: they reward frequent short practice with marking in between, and a ninety-minute block on a school night runs past the point where a tired student is learning. The question is whether the work is cumulative within one sitting or across the week.

faqs.question: Which weekday evening is the most contested in a Sunday-to-Thursday week?
faqs.answer: Sunday and Monday, because they are the first teachable nights after the weekend and every family wants them. Specialist tutors fill those two first, which means a family insisting on Monday at six is choosing from a shorter list than a family offering Tuesday or Wednesday. If the subject is scarce, flexibility on the evening buys more than flexibility on the rate does, so ask what hours a tutor has left before naming a preference.

faqs.question: Can a Friday morning block replace two weekday evenings?
faqs.answer: For paper practice, comfortably. Timed papers need an uninterrupted stretch that a school night cannot give, and a Friday morning is the best two hours in the Saudi week for that purpose. For first teaching it is weaker, because a single weekly contact leaves six days for the content to fade. The usual compromise is one weekday evening for teaching and a weekend block for papers from about a term out.

faqs.question: Do we keep paying for the slot during a school's examination fortnight?
faqs.answer: That depends on what you agreed, which is why it should be agreed in writing beforehand. The sensible arrangement is to keep the slot and change its use: shorter sessions aimed at the papers being sat, or a pause with the hour held open for a stated number of weeks. Losing the slot usually means losing the tutor, since a good one will fill it.

faqs.question: How does a tutor in Australia or the Far East fit a Saudi evening at all?
faqs.answer: Mostly they do not, and it is better to know that at the start. A Saudi early evening falls in the small hours for eastern Australia and late at night across much of the Far East, so a weekly arrangement is not sustainable however willing the tutor sounds. Where the specialist is rare, a short block of Friday morning sessions can work, since that is a reasonable evening there.

faqs.question: We are moving from a two-semester school to a three-term school: when should tuition start?
faqs.answer: After the first set of marked work at the new school, which usually means four to six weeks in. The two calendars place assessments differently relative to the June series, so a plan built on the old rhythm will be wrong by weeks. A diagnosis against the new school's scheme of work, rather than the old one's reports, avoids paying to reteach covered material.

faqs.question: Does switching board mid-course change what a term of tuition costs?
faqs.answer: It changes the hours rather than the rate. The content carries across between Cambridge and Edexcel almost entirely, so nothing has to be relearned, but the paper structure, the mark scheme wording and the practical arrangement all differ. Expect six to ten hours of technique work on the receiving board's past papers, which is cheaper than a content rebuild and more than most families budget for an administrative move.

faqs.question: Our child is repeating a year after a relocation: how many hours does that actually need?
faqs.answer: Fewer than a first pass, and concentrated in different places. The content is largely familiar, so the useful hours go on the components that failed rather than on the syllabus as a whole. A realistic shape is a diagnosis, then eight to twelve hours on the weakest two components, then paper practice. Buying weekly hours in every subject for a repeated year is the common and expensive mistake.

faqs.question: After a relocation, which subject should get the first hour of tuition?
faqs.answer: The one where the new school's entry is at risk, not the one with the lowest mark. A subject whose tier decision is still open, or whose coursework has not been carried across, can cost a grade band through an administrative gap rather than a knowledge one. Once those are settled, the first teaching hour goes to the subject others depend on, which is almost always mathematics.

faqs.question: Does a student arriving from a Monday-to-Friday school adapt to the Saudi week?
faqs.answer: Quickly in school and slowly at home. The school week itself resolves in a fortnight, but study habits take longer, because the weekend now falls on Friday and Saturday and the old pattern of leaving work for Sunday no longer exists. The practical move is to set the tuition slot early in the Saudi week, so the homework rhythm resets around it.

faqs.question: What should the first invoice itemise?
faqs.answer: The number of sessions, the length of each, the rate, and what the rate includes: teaching, marking between sessions, written notes, and any papers supplied. It should state the notice period for cancelling a single session and what happens to an unused one. Anything called a package without those lines is not comparable with another quote, and the comparison is the only real protection.

faqs.question: How do we judge value after four weeks rather than after a results day?
faqs.answer: Read a marked script rather than asking how it is going. Look for fewer blank responses, working laid out in the form the scheme credits, and command terms answered as written. Then check the tutor's notes against the original diagnosis: has the priority list changed for a stated reason, or been quietly abandoned? Four weeks answers both questions and is too early to expect a grade.

faqs.question: What is a reasonable number of hours a week for one IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: One hour of teaching plus whatever marking the tutor does between sessions, for most of the year. Two hours a week on a single subject is rarely twice as effective, because the limit is what the student consolidates rather than what is delivered. The exception is the eight weeks before the June series, where a second weekly session on timed papers earns its place.

faqs.question: When is it right to reduce from weekly to fortnightly?
faqs.answer: When the student is generating their own questions and the marking is coming back clean. At that point the tutor's value shifts from teaching to checking, and a fortnightly session with work set in between costs half as much for most of the benefit. It is the wrong move while content is still being retaught, and a useful way to hold a slot through a quiet term.

ib-igcse-online-tuition.closingHeading: Count the evenings, then price the hours
ib-igcse-online-tuition.closingBody: Before comparing rates, write down the evenings your household can actually use and the three dates that matter: mocks, coursework deadlines, and the school's examination fortnight. Send those with the board, the four-digit syllabus code and the tier, and we will come back with tutors who hold those hours open on Saudi local time and a rate with the hour itemised. The first session is free, you keep the written diagnosis, and hours are bought in blocks small enough to stop.

intro.heading: Start with the specification, then ask who has taught it
paragraphs: Most searches for an online tutor are really searches for a person, and most tutoring pages answer with a brand. The useful information is narrower than either. A Cambridge IGCSE candidate sits a named set of components at a named tier, and the question that decides whether tuition works is whether the tutor has taught those components to candidates at that tier. A physics graduate who has never taught the alternative-to-practical paper will teach physics well and prepare a candidate badly for the paper they are entered for.

So the first move is to get the specification in front of you. Ask the school for the board, the four-digit syllabus code, the tier and the component list, in writing. Cambridge tiers many subjects: Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, and the two are examined on different papers rather than on easier and harder versions of one. Pearson Edexcel grades 9 to 1 and tiers mathematics at Foundation and Higher. A tutor who asks for none of this is going to teach the subject in general and hope the overlap is enough.

The second move is to treat the claim as a claim. Examiner experience, syllabus familiarity and years in a classroom are all checkable in a ten-minute conversation if you know which question to ask, and none of them is checkable from a profile photograph. This page sets out what each credential actually buys, which ones matter at IGCSE and which only matter at Higher Level, and the specific questions that separate a specialist from a confident generalist.

Everything is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Arabia Standard Time. That is deliberate rather than a limitation. The in-home market in the Kingdom narrows the choice of tutor to whoever lives near enough to drive to your district and is free at the hour your child is home, which outside Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam conurbation is frequently nobody with the right component experience. Teaching over video widens the pool to the people who have taught the paper. We do not send a tutor to a Saudi address; in-home visits are a service we offer only in India.

The order below follows the specification outward. First what a code tells you about the person you need, then what a subject degree, a teaching qualification and years in a classroom each buy, then what marking for a board actually changes inside a lesson. After that the trial lesson, the tutor's own working week set against the Saudi one, the staffing gaps that create the demand in the first place, and finally the honest options for when the right specialist is not free. Each section ends with something you can ask a school or a tutor directly.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The qualification a tutor needs changes with the programme, because the programmes are assessed on different things. These three cover nearly every request, and each asks something different of the person teaching it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Written papers at a tier the school chooses, with a practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences and coursework in a smaller number of subjects. What a tutor needs here is paper-level familiarity: which command terms recur, how the mark scheme splits a six-mark answer, what the examiner report says candidates got wrong.
programmes.countryNote: At IGCSE the most common staffing gap in Saudi international schools is not the subject but the tier. A teacher carrying a mixed Core and Extended class teaches to the middle, and the Extended candidate loses the harder content.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against published criteria rather than terminal papers, ending with the Personal Project. A tutor here needs to understand criterion language and the difference between a task that is incomplete and one that is unevidenced, because the two look identical to a parent and attract different marks.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Kingdom run the Middle Years Programme and then move students straight into the Diploma. A tutor who has only taught examination courses is good at content and poor at the reflective writing the criteria reward.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internally assessed work is marked at school and moderated by the board, and the written papers are sat in the May session. Higher Level adds a third paper in most sciences.
programmes.countryNote: This is where specialism stops being optional. A Higher Level third paper is not an extension of the Standard Level course, and the pool of tutors who have taught and marked it is genuinely small, which is why the rate for one is higher everywhere.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each entry names the component that most often needs outside teaching. Use the second half as the question you ask a prospective tutor.

subjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Ask what they do with qualitative analysis and the alternative-to-practical paper. A tutor who has only taught theory will teach the chemistry and miss the observation marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
subjects.description: Ask how they teach the longer extended-response item. The marks sit in the chain of reasoning, and a tutor who accepts a correct final answer is not teaching the paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
subjects.description: Ask which definitions they drill. Biology is where strict wording costs most, and a tutor who paraphrases in lessons trains a candidate to paraphrase in the paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Ask which topics appear only on the Extended papers. A tutor who cannot answer that has not read both tiers and will teach a Core candidate content they cannot be credited for.

subjects.name: Cambridge Economics 0455
subjects.description: Ask how they handle diagram accuracy and the data-response question. Prose fluency is not what carries the marks, and the diagrams are credited against specific labelling.

subjects.name: Cambridge English as a Second Language 0510
subjects.description: Ask how they separate fluency from accuracy. Confident speakers lose marks on structure and register, and a tutor who only converses will not move the papers.

subjects.name: Edexcel Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Ask whether they have taught both tiers and the 9 to 1 scale. Higher overlaps the top of Foundation, and the tier decision is where a tutor's judgement is worth most.

subjects.name: Diploma sciences and mathematics
subjects.description: Ask which components they have marked rather than taught. At Higher Level the third paper and the internal investigation are the usual gaps.

regions.name: Riyadh

regions.name: Jeddah and Thuwal
regions.note: Cambridge and Diploma provision sits in different schools along the coast, so a family wanting both often needs an outside tutor.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: Strong British-curriculum coverage across the conurbation. Not every campus runs the Diploma, so the gap is usually a single Higher Level subject.

regions.name: Jubail and Ras Tanura
regions.note: Industrial towns where school rolls are small and a subject can rest on one teacher. A single resignation removes a course for a cohort.

regions.name: Al Ahsa and Qatif

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait and Najran
regions.note: High-altitude 'Asir and the far south, with limited international provision. Online teaching is usually the only route to a tiered-science specialist.

sections.heading: What a syllabus code tells you about the tutor you need
paragraphs: A four-digit code is the most useful thing a parent can quote, because it fixes the paper structure, the tier options and the practical arrangement all at once. Two courses with the same subject name can be examined completely differently. A tutor who has taught one of them has read a different specification, used a different mark scheme and seen different examiner reports, and the overlap is smaller than the shared title suggests.

The code also tells you where the difficulty is likely to be. In the Cambridge sciences the practical arrangement is the usual surprise, because a school without a staffed laboratory timetable enters candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper, which examines experimental reasoning on paper. In mathematics the surprise is tiering, since content on the Extended papers is absent from Core. In the languages it is the component split between reading, writing and speaking, which differs by course.

So the first question to a prospective tutor is not whether they teach chemistry. It is which codes they have taught, at which tier, and which components they have marked. A specialist answers in a sentence and usually volunteers what they have not done. A generalist answers with reassurance. That difference is audible in the first few minutes and it is the single most reliable signal available to a parent who does not know the subject. A family who asks it in the opening message saves the fortnight of paid lessons otherwise spent discovering the answer.

sections.heading: Degree, teaching qualification, or years in a classroom
paragraphs: Three credentials get offered and they buy different things. A subject degree buys depth, which matters most at Higher Level and least at Core tier, where the risk is a tutor pitching above the paper. A teaching qualification buys explanation and sequencing, which is what a student who has understood nothing for a term actually needs. Years in a classroom buy pattern recognition: a teacher who has taken five cohorts through 0620 knows which misconception arrives in which week.

None of the three is sufficient alone and the right mix depends on the problem. A bright Extended candidate stuck on technique needs paper familiarity more than a doctorate. A student who has fallen behind on content needs someone who can teach from the beginning without condescension, which is a trained skill rather than a knowledge one. A Diploma Higher Level student working on an internally assessed investigation needs someone who has marked them.

What is not a credential is a general claim about results. A statistic with no sample, no date and no method tells you nothing, and the honest version of the question is narrower: how many candidates have you taught through this component, and what did the examiner report say they got wrong. A tutor who has taught the course will have an opinion about the examiner report. A tutor who has not will change the subject. The reports are published by the board after each series, and a specialist has usually read the most recent one for the paper they teach.

sections.heading: What examiner experience actually is
paragraphs: Marking for a board is a job with grades inside it, and the differences matter. Someone who has marked a paper has read hundreds of scripts against one mark scheme and knows exactly where candidates are not credited. Someone who has moderated internally assessed work has seen how school marks get adjusted and why. Someone who has only sat in training has seen the scheme but not the scripts. All three are sometimes described with the same phrase in tutoring copy.

What marking buys in a lesson is specific. The tutor can tell a student which word in their answer stopped the mark, because they have withheld that mark from other people's answers. They can predict which parts of a question a candidate will be given the benefit of the doubt on and which will be marked strictly. They can say when an answer is long enough and when more writing adds risk rather than credit.

What it does not buy is insight into your child's school, a shortcut through the content, or any claim about what grade is coming. Ask which board, which paper and which series window the marking was done in, and ask what the tutor learned from it. Vagueness on any of those three is worth noticing. A tutor who has genuinely marked will talk about the scheme in detail and will be careful not to overstate what the experience predicts. Ask about the paper, not the board alone.

sections.heading: The trial lesson as an audition
paragraphs: A trial lesson is the only part of the process where a family gets evidence rather than description, so it should be set up to produce evidence. Send the specification and one piece of marked work in advance. A tutor who opens the session by reading the marked work has already told you something; a tutor who opens by describing their methodology has told you something else.

Listen for four behaviours. The tutor names components and command terms without being prompted. They ask what tier the candidate is entered for before teaching anything. They say at least one thing they have not taught. And they leave the session with a short written list of what to work on first, in an order, with reasons drawn from the script rather than from the conversation. Three of those four is a good match; none of them is a sales call. The written list that names a component and gives the reason is the artefact worth keeping.

The student's reaction matters as much as the content. A teenager who answered questions in the session will do the work between sessions, and one who listened politely will not. Ask your child afterwards what the tutor explained differently from school. A specific answer is a good sign. A shrug means the lesson was a repeat of a classroom they have already stopped listening in, and a second trial with a different tutor costs nothing. Two auditions before committing a term is a reasonable amount of looking.

sections.heading: A tutor's own working week, and which Saudi evenings survive it
paragraphs: A tutor's availability is a function of their own week, and the Kingdom's week does not line up with most of the world's. Lessons here are wanted Sunday to Thursday, after the school run and before a teenager stops being useful, which is a narrow window of two or three hours. A tutor who teaches a full school day in a country running Monday to Friday has Sunday free and Thursday crowded. One who tutors full time has the reverse problem: their busiest hours are the same as everybody else's.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A tutor in India sits two and a half hours ahead, so a seven o'clock Riyadh lesson is half past nine at night for them, which is workable occasionally and corrosive every week. A tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, so an early Saudi evening is their late afternoon, which is the most sustainable arrangement available.

The practical consequence is that a slot has to be pinned to Saudi local time in writing, and the tutor's own week has to be asked about directly rather than inferred from a calendar tool. A tutor whose stated availability collapses in week three was never available; they were hopeful. Asking what else they teach at that hour, and on which days, is a fair question and the answer is usually immediate.

sections.heading: What Saudi schools cannot staff, and why that matters
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates services for national school accreditation and for approving international accreditation bodies. None of that speaks to whether a particular subject is staffed by a specialist this year, which is the thing a family actually needs to know. A licence covers the school as an institution rather than any individual timetable.

Staffing is a timetable problem rather than a quality problem. A school with one chemistry teacher and a mixed Core and Extended class will teach to the middle of the room. A school running the Diploma alongside IGCSE will put its most experienced science teacher on the Higher Level group, which is the right decision and leaves the IGCSE Extended set with someone newer. A subject offered online by the school itself, or dropped for a year, is a clear signal that there is nobody to teach it.

So the question to ask a school, before enrolment and again each year, is which subjects it will run at which level, and who will teach them. The answer explains most of the demand for outside tutoring in the Kingdom better than any argument about standards. It is also the honest basis for choosing a tutor: you are filling a specific gap in a specific timetable, not buying a general improvement. Ask the question in writing, and keep the answer for next year.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free: the honest options
paragraphs: Sometimes the right person is not available. A Higher Level physics specialist with marking experience and a free Sunday evening is a small intersection, and pretending otherwise wastes a family's term. There are four honest responses and a tutoring platform should say which one it is offering rather than filling the slot and hoping. Saying so in the first week is cheaper for everyone than discovering it in the sixth.

The first is to wait for the right tutor and start later with a compressed plan, which is often better than twelve weeks with the wrong one. The second is a different slot: a Friday morning session with a specialist beats a Tuesday evening with a generalist, and families usually find the weekend easier than they expected. The third is to split the work, with a specialist on the component that is failing and nobody on the rest. Splitting it also makes the result legible afterwards: one component, one tutor, one verdict, rather than a term of general support nobody can evaluate.

The fourth is to decline. If the gap is a whole unstudied syllabus eight weeks from the papers, no tutor fixes it and the useful conversation is about which subjects to protect and whether a November entry is the better plan. A platform that never declines is matching on availability rather than on fit, and a family can test this directly by asking what they would refuse to take on. A compressed plan with the right person beats a long one with the wrong one in almost every case.

process.title: Send the specification, not the subject
process.description: Board, four-digit code, tier and component list, plus one piece of marked work. The examinations officer will confirm the first four in writing.

process.title: Read a shortlist stated by component
process.description: Each tutor is described by what they have taught and marked, gaps included. You choose, and you can ask for a second name.

process.title: Use the trial lesson as an audition
process.description: A full session at no charge with the marked work on screen. You keep the written priority list either way.

process.title: Agree the slot, the reporting and the handover
process.description: One standing slot per subject pinned to Saudi local time, written notes after each session, and a plan for the tutor becoming unavailable.

whyPoints.title: Tutors described by component
whyPoints.description: Profiles state the codes, tiers and components a tutor has taught and marked, and say where they have not. That is the part a parent cannot otherwise check.

whyPoints.title: No unverifiable claims
whyPoints.description: No ratings, no success percentages, no headcounts. A statistic without a sample, a date and a method is decoration.

whyPoints.title: One named tutor, one plan
whyPoints.description: The same person each week per subject, so the plan builds instead of restarting, with the handover agreed in advance.

whyPoints.title: The week is treated as a constraint
whyPoints.description: Availability is checked against the tutor's own working week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, so a slot does not drift when another country changes its clocks.

whyPoints.title: We say what we will not take on
whyPoints.description: Where the gap is too wide for the weeks left, the honest answer comes first. Filling a slot with the wrong person costs more than waiting.

faqs.question: How do we check an online tutor's stated availability is real before booking a term?
faqs.answer: Ask what else they teach at the same hour and on which days, and ask it as a direct question rather than reading a calendar tool. A tutor with a genuine window answers immediately. Then book the first four sessions at the exact slot you intend to keep, so an availability problem surfaces in week two, when it is still cheap to fix.

faqs.question: What does the half-hour offset to India mean for an early evening lesson here?
faqs.answer: India runs two and a half hours ahead of Arabia Standard Time, so a seven o'clock Riyadh lesson is half past nine at night for a tutor there. That is sustainable for a short block and corrosive as a year-long arrangement. If the match is right, move the slot earlier or to a Friday morning, agreed in Saudi local time and written down.

faqs.question: Can we ask an online tutor to teach through the long summer break to get ahead?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better uses of a specialist's time, because the hour you want is available when term-time demand drops. Keep the aim narrow: pre-teach the two topics the school will cover first, or repair a component that failed in the summer examinations. Trying to cover a year ahead of time rarely holds, since nothing reinforces it before the autumn term.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether an online tutor has ever taught inside a Saudi school?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect for the subject, more than they expect for the logistics. The specification is the same wherever it is taught, so component experience travels. What local experience buys is familiarity with the Sunday to Thursday week, the way term dates differ between schools in one city, and the shortened days during Ramadan. A tutor without it works well if they ask rather than assume.

faqs.question: How many standing weekly slots can one IGCSE tutor hold before quality drops?
faqs.answer: The limit is marking rather than teaching. An hour of lesson time generates twenty to forty minutes of marking and note-writing if it is done properly, so a tutor carrying thirty teaching hours is doing something else with the written work. Ask how many students they carry and what their marking turnaround is. A specific answer in days is the one to trust.

faqs.question: After a move from an American school, do we need a different tutor for Year 10 than for Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually not a different person, but a different job in each year. In Year 10 the work is content and vocabulary: closing the gap between a broad middle-school course and a narrower, deeper Cambridge topic list. In Year 11 it shifts to paper technique and timed practice. A tutor who can do both should be able to describe the handover point, and one who cannot is better used for a single year.

faqs.question: Our child is switching from Edexcel to Cambridge mid-course: does the tutor have to change too?
faqs.answer: Only if the current tutor has never taught the receiving board. The content carries across almost entirely; the paper structure, the mark scheme wording and the practical arrangement do not. Ask the tutor directly whether they have taught the Cambridge code and at which tier. If the answer is no, a short written handover beats expecting them to learn a new scheme in term time.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor take a student from IGCSE through to the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking early because continuity is genuinely valuable. The test is whether they have taught the Diploma course at the level the student will take, including the internally assessed component. A tutor who has only taught IGCSE will be strong for two years and then out of their depth at Higher Level, which is a worse outcome than planning a change at the transition.

faqs.question: Which kind of tutor suits a student who has recently switched to learning in English?
faqs.answer: One who separates subject language from general English and teaches the first explicitly. The marks are lost on technical vocabulary and on command terms, not on conversational fluency, so the useful tutor drills the words the mark scheme uses and insists on them in writing. A language tutor improves the English and not the grade; a subject tutor who ignores the language does the reverse.

faqs.question: Does a student moving from the national curriculum need a tutor who speaks Arabic?
faqs.answer: It can help in the first few weeks and it is not the main thing. What matters is that the examinations are sat in English against a scheme written in English, so lessons that drift into Arabic delay the transition the papers require. A practical arrangement is a tutor who can explain a stuck concept in Arabic when necessary and teach the answer in English. One-to-one lessons let a family specify this directly.

faqs.question: What should a tutor send us after the first session, and what does a weak version look like?
faqs.answer: A strong version names the code, tier and components, lists three or four topics in priority order with the evidence for each taken from the marked work, and says what it is not covering. A weak version describes the student as capable but lacking confidence, promises a tailored plan, and names no component. The second kind cannot be checked against anything, which is why it reads well and tells you nothing.

faqs.question: How do we tell in week two that we have been matched to a generalist?
faqs.answer: Three signals. The lessons follow a textbook or a general worksheet rather than past-paper items from the actual code. The tutor cannot say what the mark scheme rewards in a specific question. And the marking comes back with ticks and a score rather than the reason a mark was withheld. Any one of those is worth raising immediately; together they mean the match is wrong rather than slow.

faqs.question: If we change tutor after three lessons, what should carry across to the new one?
faqs.answer: The written priority list from the diagnosis, the marked work with the first tutor's annotations, a note of which topics were taught and in what order, and the slot itself. Handing a new tutor a blank page wastes a second diagnosis. Ask the outgoing tutor for a short written handover, and note that a refusal tells you something useful about the first choice.

faqs.question: Who decides what a lesson covers once teaching has started?
faqs.answer: The tutor sets the sequence, the student brings the week's problems, and the parent holds the review. That order matters. A tutor who only ever teaches what the student asks for will drift towards the comfortable topics, and a parent who sets the agenda weekly prevents the plan from building. If the sequence changes, the tutor should say why in the written note rather than silently.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.closingHeading: Ask about the component, not the credential
ib-igcse-online-tutor.closingBody: Send the board, the four-digit syllabus code, the tier and one piece of marked work, and we will come back with tutors described by what they have taught and marked, gaps included. The trial lesson is free and built as an audition rather than a sales call: the specification on screen, the marked work read question by question, and a written priority list you keep. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

intro.heading: Four free documents decide whether a private tutor is worth paying
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson publish almost everything a parent needs in order to judge a tutor, and they publish it at no cost. The syllabus lists every component, its duration and its share of the final grade. The specimen and past papers show the question styles that share is earned in. The mark scheme shows what an examiner is paid to tick, phrase by phrase. The examiner report, written after each series, says plainly where candidates lost marks and why. A private tutor who works from those four documents is doing the job that was advertised. One who works from a textbook and a memory of their own schooling is doing something adjacent to it, and the difference shows up in a mark rather than in a conversation.

The same holds on the Diploma side, where the IB publishes a subject guide for every course and schools hold the assessment outline that goes with it. A household running an IGCSE child and a Diploma sibling at once is managing two sets of documents, two mark schemes and two internally assessed regimes that use similar words for different things. A Diploma mathematics exploration is not an IGCSE coursework folder. A scientific investigation is not an alternative-to-practical paper. A tutor who treats one like the other gives feedback that costs marks instead of earning them, and the damage is usually invisible until a moderated mark comes back.

This matters more in the Kingdom than it does in a city with twenty international schools on one road. Private and international schools here are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation and accreditation run through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Both bodies act on the school. Neither of them owns the syllabus a child is examined against: Cambridge, Pearson and the IB do, and they revise it on their own cycles. A family that confuses the two ends up asking a school about a component the school does not set, and asking a tutor about a licence the tutor has nothing to do with.

The practical version of all this is five questions. Which board? Which syllabus code? Which tier, if the subject is tiered? Which papers, and what is each one worth? Which component is marked inside the school and moderated outside it? A tutor who answers those five without hesitating has read the specification for the course your child is sitting. A tutor who answers with the subject name and a reassurance has not, and years of general classroom experience do not close that gap. The questions take two minutes and they sort a long shortlist faster than any profile page.

Everything below runs in that order: the four documents, the Cambridge IGCSE component list code by code, where a Diploma grade is actually earned, the command terms the mark schemes are written in, the components that carry a published word or page limit, how an internally assessed mark is built criterion by criterion, and how to test a tutor's claim inside a single trial lesson. Any riyal figure quoted on this page is an advertised market rate taken from published vendor listings, never our price. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled around a Sunday-to-Thursday school week on Arabia Standard Time.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.programmesIntro: IB Gram supports four programmes for families in the Kingdom, and the document a private tutor has to read differs at each stage. The notes below say which body sets the assessment, which parts are marked inside the school, and what a tutor can usefully do at that point in a child's schooling.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme has no external examination and no published mark scheme, so there is nothing for a tutor to work backwards from. What exists instead is a set of learner expectations the school assesses continuously, plus whatever reading, number and writing benchmarks the school has adopted. Useful support at this stage is narrow and diagnostic: number facts, place value, decoding, sentence control, and the habit of showing working. A tutor who talks about examinations here has misread the programme.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families in the Kingdom often arrive from three or four different systems inside one class, so a Year 4 cohort in Riyadh or Al Khobar can hold children who have been taught long division four ways. One-to-one online sessions are mostly used to close a specific gap created by a move, rather than to run a parallel curriculum alongside the school.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme assesses against four criteria per subject, each reported on a band rather than a percentage, and it ends in the Personal Project. Criterion language is the whole game: a student who can state a conclusion but not evaluate one will sit in the middle band however much content they know. A private tutor working here reads the subject's criteria, finds which band descriptor the student never reaches, and teaches the thinking move that descriptor describes.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Kingdom run the Middle Years Programme and then enter candidates for IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, so a student can meet criterion-based assessment and then meet a mark scheme within eighteen months. Online sessions are commonly used to bridge that change in assessment language, which is a different job from teaching more content.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: IGCSE is the first qualification where a tutor can work from a published mark scheme and a grade threshold table. Cambridge tiers many subjects: Core is graded C to G, Extended A* to E, and a Core entry caps the grade however well the papers go. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades on the 9 to 1 scale with its own component list. Everything a tutor needs is public, which makes vagueness here a choice rather than a limitation.
programmes.countryNote: Both boards run a June series and a November series for candidates in the Kingdom, with November used for resits and November-entry candidates. Tier entry and the component list are school decisions, and they are reversible only before the entry deadline, so a family that wants a tier reviewed has to raise it with the school's examinations officer in writing and early.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service, totalling up to 45 points with up to three of them coming from the core. Each subject publishes its own split between written papers and an internally assessed component, and the internal piece is marked by the teacher and moderated by the IB. A tutor who cannot say what that split is for a given course cannot plan a term around it.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi IB schools sit the May session, and families should take examination and results dates from their own Diploma Programme coordinator rather than from any third-party page. A Diploma certificate issued abroad also needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the national secondary certificate, which is a step worth knowing about in the first Diploma year rather than the last term.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: The Diploma courses below are the ones Saudi families most often ask about by name. Each note states where the marks sit and what the mark scheme is strict about, because that is the information a private tutor should already have before the first lesson rather than after the first report.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level the three written papers carry 80 per cent between them, with Paper 3 a pair of long investigative questions, and the exploration carries the remaining 20 per cent. Standard Level drops Paper 3. Marks go missing in proof, in reasoning that is correct but unwritten, and in Paper 3 questions where the student answers part (a) and abandons the thread the rest of the question depends on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same paper architecture, a different course. Applications leans on modelling, statistics and technology, and expects the graphical display calculator to be used rather than tolerated. Candidates who transfer from a heavily algebraic school system often under-use the calculator and lose method marks they were entitled to. The exploration again carries a fifth of the grade and is the most controllable part of it.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Two written papers carry 80 per cent of the grade between them and the scientific investigation carries 20 per cent. Paper 1 mixes multiple choice with data-based questions; Paper 2 is extended response. The common failure is not calculation but explanation: a candidate who can find the right number and cannot say which principle produced it leaves most of the marks on an explain question untouched.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Written papers take 80 per cent, the scientific investigation 20 per cent. The Higher Level extension is not more facts but more linking, and multi-topic questions that join energetics to equilibrium to kinetics are where strong candidates slip. Data booklet fluency is assumed and rarely taught, so a tutor should be able to work a question using the booklet rather than recalled constants.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume makes this feel like a memory subject and the mark scheme treats it as a precision subject. Definitions are examined strictly, and a near-synonym scores nothing. The written papers carry 80 per cent between them, with the scientific investigation at 20 per cent. Most lost marks on extended response come from describing a process when the command term asked the candidate to explain or evaluate it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is guided textual analysis of unseen passages, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied works, and the individual oral is internally assessed. Higher Level adds a written essay on a studied text. Candidates who write fluently but do not organise around a line of argument lose marks under the focus and organisation criterion rather than under knowledge.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds a policy paper that asks for quantitative work on real data, which changes what revision has to look like. The internally assessed portfolio of commentaries is written against published criteria and carries a substantial share of the grade. Diagram accuracy is the cheapest set of marks in the course and the most frequently thrown away through unlabelled axes.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Both levels sit a case study paper released in advance, which rewards preparation and punishes candidates who treat it as unseen. The internally assessed project is written against criteria that reward the use of a tool rather than its description. Higher Level content extends into areas the Standard Level syllabus never visits, so a shared revision plan across levels fails quickly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together the core contributes up to three points to the 45 and can decide whether a Diploma is awarded. The Theory of Knowledge essay is externally assessed against a prescribed title and the exhibition is internally assessed. The Extended Essay is supervised in school, carries a published word limit, and is marked against five criteria, with critical thinking worth more than any other.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: IGCSE support in the Kingdom is requested by subject name and should be delivered against a code. The notes below name the Cambridge code most Saudi schools enter and say what the paper structure actually demands, so a parent can check that a tutor is talking about the right document.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
igcseSubjects.description: Extended candidates sit Paper 2, a shorter non-calculator-style question set, and Paper 4, the longer structured paper carrying roughly two thirds of the grade. Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 and cannot be awarded above a C. Most avoidable losses are method marks: an answer written with no working earns nothing when the final figure is wrong.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
igcseSubjects.description: Three components: a multiple-choice paper at 30 per cent, a theory paper at 50 per cent, and either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper at 20 per cent. The practical component is where candidates who have done little laboratory work are exposed, because it asks about apparatus, precision and sources of error rather than recalled theory.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
igcseSubjects.description: Same 30, 50 and 20 per cent split as the other sciences. Equation writing and the mole are the two places a grade is usually decided, and both reward drill rather than discussion. Candidates lose marks for unbalanced equations and missing state symbols far more often than for not knowing the chemistry being asked about.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
igcseSubjects.description: The syllabus is long and the definitions are examined tightly, so the subject punishes paraphrase. The alternative-to-practical paper asks candidates to read a method, spot its weakness and suggest an improvement, which is a skill rather than a recall task and is usually the lowest-scoring component on a school's own analysis.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 and 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading and writing, listening and speaking are assessed separately, and the writing tasks are scored against register and purpose as well as accuracy. Many candidates in the Kingdom are entered here rather than for First Language English, and the two have different mark schemes, so a tutor needs to know which code the school has used.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Two equally weighted papers, the second built on a case study. Data-response marks are lost by candidates who quote a figure without doing anything with it. The evaluation marks at the end of the longer questions are the ones most often left blank, and they are the difference between a middle and a top grade.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
igcseSubjects.description: One paper on computer systems and one on algorithms, programming and logic, weighted equally. Pseudocode conventions are assessed, so a candidate who writes working code in an unexamined style still drops marks. Trace tables and logic diagrams reward practice on past papers more directly than almost any other component at this level.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: The Edexcel route runs two papers, both calculator-permitted, on a 9 to 1 grading scale, with a Higher and a Foundation tier. The content overlaps Cambridge 0580 heavily but the question presentation and the formula support differ, so past-paper practice has to come from the board the school actually entered.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.regionsTitle: Which boards and codes families meet, city by city
ib-igcse-private-tutor.regionsIntro: Board coverage is not even across the Kingdom. The notes below describe what a family in each place is likely to be examined against and where the local specialist pool thins out, because that is what decides whether outside support is a convenience or a necessity.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The widest spread of boards in the Kingdom, with IB World Schools including Al Faris International School, Advanced Learning Schools, Al Hussan International Academy and SEK International School Riyadh, alongside Cambridge and Edexcel centres. One cohort can hold candidates sitting three different codes for the same subject.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: The British International School of Jeddah is both an IB World School and a Cambridge school, so IGCSE and Diploma candidates sit in the same building. Jeddah Knowledge International School, Alkawthar International Schools and Bright Minds International School also appear in IB listings, and the city runs as a long coastal spine north to Obhur.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market: families routinely live in one of the three and attend school in another. International Schools Group operates several campuses here, with the Diploma offered at the American School of Dhahran. British School Dhahran and Multinational School Dhahran follow British and Cambridge routes.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with a small international sector in which ISG Jubail offers the Diploma. Subject choice at Higher Level is the constraint rather than school quality, and a family wanting a course the local campus does not run has to look outside the city for teaching.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST campus
regions.note: The KAUST School serves the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology campus community north of Jeddah on the coast. Campus families often arrive mid-course from several different systems at once, which makes code-level diagnosis more useful here than a general subject review.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: Roughly an hour and a half inland from the Dammam cluster, which is far enough that a weekday in-home arrangement with a specialist based in Al Khobar rarely survives a term. Online teaching removes the drive from the decision entirely.

regions.name: Makkah, Madinah and Taif
regions.note: Makkah sits about 80km east of Jeddah, so some families attend school across that gap rather than locally. International provision is thinner than on the coast, and Higher Level sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are the courses most often short of a local specialist.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About 25km apart in 'Asir at high altitude, sharing one catchment. The specialist pool for a named syllabus code is the smallest of any populated part of the Kingdom, which is the plain argument for teaching that is not limited by who lives nearby.

schoolClusters.note: Riyadh holds the Kingdom's broadest mix of IB, Cambridge and Edexcel provision, and the city is about an hour across in traffic, so two families attending the same school can have very different evening timetables. Students we support in Riyadh attend schools including those below.

Jeddah's international sector mixes British, IB, American, German and Indian provision along the coastal spine, and Thuwal adds a campus community to the north. Students we support on the western coast attend schools including those below.

The Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation behaves as a single school market, with Jubail and Al Ahsa drawing from it. The King Fahd Causeway links Al Khobar to Bahrain, which widens the options for some families and not others. Students we support in the Eastern Province attend schools including those below.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the systems families in the Kingdom work inside; IB Gram has no affiliation with any of them and claims none.
ib-igcse-private-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways families use one-to-one support, all delivered online over live video. Which one fits depends on whether the problem is content, a single component, or the distance left before a series, and the honest answer sometimes is that none of them is needed yet.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one against a named code
modes.description: A standing weekly slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time, taught against the syllabus the school actually entered. The tutor works through the component list in the order the school's scheme of work reaches it, marks written work between sessions using the board's own mark scheme, and reports what changed. This is the arrangement that suits a student whose problem is cumulative rather than sudden.
bullets: Same slot each week, fixed to Saudi local time so a tutor's clock change cannot move it
Written work marked between lessons against the published mark scheme
Short note to the parent after each session naming the component covered
Plan reviewed at the end of each month against the specification, not against a feeling

modes.title: Single-component clinics
modes.description: Some students need one component rather than one subject. An alternative-to-practical paper, a data-response section, a Paper 3 technique, a set of criterion descriptors for an internally assessed piece: each of these can be taught in a short run of focused sessions without committing to a year of weekly hours. Families often use a clinic to test whether a tutor is worth a standing slot.
bullets: Four to six sessions aimed at one named paper or criterion
Diagnosis from a marked past paper rather than from a general conversation
Used widely for practical and alternative-to-practical components
Ends when the component moves, not when a package expires

modes.title: Pre-series intensive blocks
modes.description: Short, denser runs of sessions in the weeks before a series, built around timed papers and the examiner report for that component. Intensive work suits a student who knows the content and loses marks in the room, and it suits nobody who has not covered the syllabus. A tutor who promises to cover two years in six weeks is describing something that does not exist.
bullets: Timed papers marked to the board's mark scheme and returned with annotations
Built from the examiner report for the component, not from a revision guide
Scheduled around school mock examinations rather than on top of them
Honest limit stated before booking: technique moves faster than coverage

sections.heading: The four documents a private tutor is actually being hired to read
paragraphs: Start with what is public. For every IGCSE subject, the board publishes a syllabus that names each component, its duration and its percentage of the final grade. It publishes past and specimen papers. It publishes the mark scheme for each of those papers. And after each series it publishes an examiner report describing, question by question, what candidates did well and what they got wrong. On the Diploma side the IB publishes a subject guide for each course, and the school holds the assessment outline that comes with it. None of this is behind a paywall and none of it requires a teaching qualification to read.

A parent who downloads those documents can run the hiring process themselves. The syllabus answers which components exist, so a tutor who does not know there are three science papers rather than two is immediately out. The past paper answers what the questions look like, so a tutor who teaches content but has never set a timed question can be caught in a trial lesson. The mark scheme answers what is rewarded, which is almost never what a textbook summary contains. And the examiner report answers where the marks actually went last time, which is the single most useful page in the set and the one almost nobody opens.

The reason this is the opening move rather than a footnote is that every other question a family asks depends on it. Rate, frequency, tutor background, group or one-to-one, when to start: all of them are downstream of knowing which components the grade is made of. A family that skips this step is left choosing between people on the strength of their self-description, which is exactly the market the vendor pages in this search result are built for. A family that does not skip it has a short checklist that no amount of marketing can satisfy.

One caution about the documents themselves. Specifications are revised, and a tutor who learned a subject under an earlier version can be fluent and out of date at the same time. Ask which version of the syllabus the school entered and whether the tutor has taught that version. The honest answer is sometimes no, followed by a description of what they will read before the first session, which is a better answer than a confident yes.

sections.heading: The Cambridge IGCSE component list, code by code
paragraphs: IGCSE subjects are not uniform. One subject is two papers of equal weight, another is three with a practical, another has a coursework route the school may or may not have chosen. A tutor who says they teach IGCSE science is describing a region, not an address. The address is a code, a tier and a component list, and until all three are known no sensible plan exists. Cambridge codes are short and stable, which makes this easy to pin down: a parent can read the code off a school report or an entry confirmation and have the whole architecture in a minute.

Tiering is the part of this with consequences a family cannot undo later. On many Cambridge subjects the school enters a candidate for either the Core or the Extended route. Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E, which means a Core entry caps the possible grade at a C whatever happens in the room. That decision belongs to the school, it is made on evidence the school holds, and it can be revisited only before the entry deadline. A tutor's first job on a tiered subject is often to produce evidence worth taking to a conversation about tier, rather than to teach around a ceiling nobody mentioned.

The practical components deserve separate attention because they behave differently from the theory papers. In the sciences, 20 per cent of the grade sits in either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and both ask about apparatus, precision, variables and error rather than recalled content. A student who has done limited laboratory work can be strong on theory and weak here, and that pattern is common in cohorts that have moved between schools. It is also one of the easiest components to improve, because the question types repeat across series with very little variation.

sections.heading: Where a Diploma grade is actually earned, component by component
paragraphs: The Diploma hides its arithmetic better than IGCSE does. A subject grade from 1 to 7 is assembled from written papers and at least one internally assessed component, in proportions the subject guide states and most families never see. The consequence is that two students with the same written-paper performance can land a grade apart on the strength of a piece of work completed months before the examinations, with no invigilator in the room. That piece is usually the most teachable part of the course and it is routinely the least planned.

Higher Level is not Standard Level with extra homework. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches the Higher Level course adds an entire third paper of long investigative questions, which changes what preparation has to look like rather than how much of it there is. In the sciences the Higher Level extension is mostly about linking topics that were taught separately, so a candidate who revises topic by topic can know everything and still answer a joined-up question badly. A tutor who teaches both levels from one plan is teaching one of them wrongly.

The core sits on top of the six subjects. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points towards the maximum of 45, and the way they combine can decide whether a Diploma is awarded at all rather than merely how high the total is. Families tend to treat the core as administrative until the term it becomes urgent. A student who starts the Extended Essay with a research question that cannot be answered in the published word limit has created a problem that costs weeks, and the fix is a conversation in the first Diploma year, not the last.

sections.heading: Command terms are the price list of a mark scheme
paragraphs: Both the IB and Cambridge write their questions in a controlled vocabulary, and the mark scheme pays out according to that vocabulary rather than according to how much the candidate knows. State and explain are different transactions. Describe and evaluate are different transactions. A candidate who answers an explain question with an accurate description has written something true that earns a fraction of the available marks, and will usually leave the examination certain the paper went well. This is the most common gap between a student's sense of their own performance and the mark that arrives.

The pattern is visible in any examiner report. Candidates lose marks on the longer questions not because the content was missing but because the thinking move the command term asked for never happened: no comparison was drawn, no judgement was reached, no limitation was named. Those moves are teachable in a way that content volume is not, which is why a good diagnostic session starts with a marked extended-response answer rather than with a topic test. The topic test tells you what a student knows. The extended answer tells you what they get paid for.

A practical test for a tutor follows from this. Hand them a six-mark question from the right paper and ask them to say, before answering it, how the marks will be distributed and which command term governs the answer. A specialist will describe the structure the mark scheme wants. A generalist will start explaining the science or the mathematics. Both may be knowledgeable; only one of them is teaching to the document that decides the grade.

sections.heading: The components with a published limit, and what an overrun costs
paragraphs: Several of the highest-stakes pieces of work in both qualifications carry a published cap on length, and the cap is enforced rather than advisory. Work beyond the limit may simply not be read, which means a strong conclusion sitting past the cut-off counts for nothing at all. This is an entirely avoidable loss and it happens every series, usually to conscientious students who wrote more because they had more to say. A tutor who has supervised these components knows the limits by heart and plans the structure backwards from them.

The limits also shape what a sensible research question looks like. An Extended Essay question that needs eight thousand words to answer properly cannot be answered properly in the published limit, so the student either writes a truncated argument or runs over and loses the end of it. The same logic applies to a mathematics exploration with too wide a scope and to a scientific investigation with too many variables. Scope is set at the planning stage, which is where a tutor's involvement is both most useful and most clearly permitted.

Alongside length there are presentation requirements that carry marks of their own: referencing, a contents page, labelled diagrams, a word count where one is required. These are the cheapest marks in the Diploma and among the most frequently dropped, because they are nobody's idea of interesting work. A single session spent on the presentation criterion of an internally assessed piece typically returns more marks per hour than a session on content.

sections.heading: Criterion letters, and the line a private tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Internally assessed work is not marked out of a hundred and then scaled. It is marked criterion by criterion, each criterion carrying its own small number of marks, and a candidate can be excellent on one and absent on another. That structure is published, which means a student can be shown exactly which descriptor their draft currently reaches and what the next band asks for. This is the clearest teaching target anywhere in either qualification, and it is also where a family is most likely to be sold something they should refuse.

The line is simple to state. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what a descriptor means, work through a published exemplar, ask questions that make a student rethink a conclusion, point out that a section does not address the criterion it is meant to address, and teach the referencing and presentation conventions the component requires. A tutor may not write, redraft, edit or supply any part of the work, and no tutor should ever offer to. Every word submitted has to be the student's own, the school records supervision, and a school that suspects otherwise has a malpractice process that can cost a candidate the subject or the Diploma.

That boundary is a differentiator rather than a limitation. The essay mills visible in this search result compete on doing the work; a tutor competes on making the student able to do it, which is also the only version that survives an authenticity check. Families should treat an offer to produce assessed work as disqualifying rather than as a convenience, and should expect a legitimate tutor to say no to the request without being asked twice.

sections.heading: Testing a private tutor's claim inside one trial lesson
paragraphs: A trial lesson is a verification exercise, not a sales call, and a parent who has the four documents open can run it without knowing the subject. The method is to ask for specifics and listen for whether the answer names a document. A tutor who refers to the paper number, the command term, the criterion letter or the examiner report is working from the specification. A tutor who answers in adjectives about rapport and confidence may still be good, but has not yet shown the thing you are trying to check.

Examiner experience is the claim families find hardest to evaluate, partly because the words are used loosely. Marking for a board is real and relevant, and a tutor who has done it can usually describe the process in detail: the standardisation, the sample scripts, the tolerance checks, the kinds of answer that cause discussion. Someone who has never marked will describe the outcome instead of the process. Nobody can verify a marking contract from the outside, so treat the quality of the description as the evidence and discount vague claims entirely.

The other claim worth probing is currency. A tutor may have taught a subject for years under a previous version of the specification and be genuinely unaware that a component has changed. Ask which version the school entered, ask what has changed in it most recently, and accept an honest I will check over a confident answer that turns out to be wrong in week three. A tutor who reads the current syllabus before the first paid session has told you something useful about how they work.
