sections.heading: The first month, and what this market charges for it
paragraphs: A first month should produce documents, not impressions. Session one is diagnostic: a timed section from a real past paper, marked against the board's own mark scheme, with the marks broken down by component and by command term rather than reported as a percentage. From that comes a short plan naming which components will be worked on in which order and what evidence will show whether it worked. At the end of four weeks a parent should be able to compare a second marked piece against the first and see movement in a named component, or see that there was none.

If there was none, the useful question is which of three things failed: the diagnosis, the plan or the match. A diagnosis that mistook a technique problem for a content gap produces lessons that feel productive and change nothing. A plan that chased the hardest topic first often leaves the cheap marks untouched. And a match can simply be wrong, which is nobody's fault and is cheaper to fix in week four than in week fourteen. A tutor who cannot tell you which of the three it was has not been measuring.

On price, the Saudi market advertises a wide range and publishes very little context. Tutoring platforms list general online tutoring from around SAR 55 an hour and budget IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. Tutor marketplaces describe general private tuition in Riyadh at roughly SAR 50 an hour for primary and SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring companies list IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from about SAR 180, with Higher Level and Advanced Placement premium tracks around SAR 200 to 220, and some international providers quote near 60 US dollars an hour. All of those are advertised rates published by vendors, not a market average, and none of them is our price.

What moves the number, in order of weight: subject scarcity, marking or examiner experience, level, whether the tutor travels to the student, and the length of the commitment. A Higher Level Physics or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specialist costs more than a Standard Level mathematics tutor everywhere in the world, and the Kingdom is no exception. In-home arrangements carry a travel loading that pays for a drive rather than for teaching. IB Gram does not send a tutor to any Saudi address; home visits are a service we run only in India, and every lesson for a family in the Kingdom is taught online, one-to-one, over live video.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is the board, the syllabus code, the tier if the subject is tiered, and the component the student is struggling with. A school report or an entry confirmation usually has all four on it. With that we can tell you whether a genuine specialist for that exact course is free in your evening window before anything is booked.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a marked paper
process.description: The trial is a diagnostic session, not an introduction. The student works a timed section from a real past paper and the tutor marks it against the board's mark scheme in front of them, breaking the result down by component and command term. A parent gets the marked script and a short note on what it shows, whether or not anything is booked afterwards.

process.title: A written plan with named components
process.description: The plan says which components will be worked on, in what order, and what evidence will be used to judge whether it worked. It is written against the specification rather than against a general improvement target, so it can be checked. If the school's scheme of work reaches a topic later than the plan assumes, the order changes rather than the student being taught something twice.

process.title: Weekly teaching and marking between sessions
process.description: A standing slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time, with written work set and marked between lessons using the board's own mark scheme. The parent gets a short note after each session naming the component covered and what the marking showed. Nothing in this stage involves a tutor touching a piece of assessed work the student has to submit.

process.title: A monthly review that can end the arrangement
process.description: At the end of each month the marked evidence is compared with the month before. If a named component has not moved, the honest options are a different plan, a different tutor or stopping, and all three are put on the table. A review that always concludes that more hours are needed is not a review, and a family should be suspicious of one.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a code, not to a subject name
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed for the specification the school actually entered, with the tier and component list confirmed first. This removes the most common cause of wasted terms, which is a competent teacher working from the wrong document, and it is the reason the first question we ask is about paperwork rather than about personality.

whyPoints.title: Distance stops being a constraint
whyPoints.description: A family in Al Ahsa, Abha or Yanbu is not limited to whoever lives within a reasonable drive. Teaching online over live video means the pool is the set of people who know the named course and are free in a Saudi evening, which in scarce Higher Level subjects is a materially different list from the local one.

whyPoints.title: Marking you can read
whyPoints.description: Written work is marked against the board's published mark scheme and returned annotated, so a parent can see where marks were awarded and withheld rather than being told that progress is being made. Over a term this produces a record that can be compared, which is what makes a decision to continue or stop an evidence-based one.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria, explain descriptors, work through published exemplars and question a student's reasoning. They do not write, redraft, edit or supply any part of an internal assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. The boundary is stated before the first session rather than negotiated when a deadline gets close.

whyPoints.title: Timed to the Saudi week, not to someone else's
whyPoints.description: Slots are fixed to Arabia Standard Time, which does not change through the year, so a tutor whose own country shifts its clocks cannot quietly move your lesson. Sessions are built around a Sunday-to-Thursday school week, with Friday and Saturday used for longer work when a family wants it.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE science paper carries the practical marks, and can a candidate avoid it?
faqs.answer: It cannot be avoided, only chosen between. In Cambridge IGCSE Physics, Chemistry and Biology, 20 per cent of the grade sits in either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school decides which one its candidates sit. Both examine apparatus, measurement, variables, precision and sources of error rather than recalled theory. Students who have done limited laboratory work often score well on the theory papers and poorly here, which looks like bad luck and is actually an untaught component. Ask the examinations officer which of the two your child is entered for, because the preparation differs.

faqs.question: How are the three Cambridge IGCSE science papers weighted against each other?
faqs.answer: The multiple-choice paper carries 30 per cent, the theory paper 50 per cent, and the practical or alternative-to-practical paper the remaining 20 per cent. That split matters for planning. Half the grade sits in one extended-answer paper, so technique on structured questions is worth more revision time than the multiple-choice drilling most students default to. The practical fifth is the component schools have least room to teach and the one that improves fastest with past-paper work, because the question types repeat across series with very little variation in what is being asked.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma Programme Paper 3 ask for that Papers 1 and 2 do not?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 exists only on some Higher Level courses and it changes the preparation rather than adding to it. In Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches it is a small number of long investigative questions, each built in stages where later parts depend on earlier ones, so abandoning part way through costs far more than it would on a paper of independent questions. In Economics the Higher Level policy paper asks for quantitative work on supplied data. In both cases the skill is sustaining a line of reasoning, which is practised on whole questions rather than on topic exercises.

faqs.question: How much of a Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches grade sits outside the written papers?
faqs.answer: A fifth of it. The exploration is internally assessed, marked by the teacher against five published criteria and moderated by the IB, and it carries 20 per cent of the final grade at both levels. It is also the most controllable part of the course, because it is written over months rather than in two hours under invigilation. Families who plan it early tend to bank a strong mark before the examination term; families who leave it late lose marks on the reflection and presentation criteria, which are the two that reward time rather than mathematical ability.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a raw mark, a grade threshold and the grade on a result slip?
faqs.answer: A raw mark is what the examiner awarded on a component. Components are combined according to the weightings in the syllabus to give a total, and that total is compared with a grade threshold table to produce the grade. Thresholds are set after each series, once the board has seen how candidates performed, which is why the mark needed for a given grade is not identical every time. The useful consequence for a family is that a target should be set in marks on named components, since that is the thing a student can actually influence.

faqs.question: Why does the same percentage score produce a different grade in different series?
faqs.answer: Because grade thresholds move. Boards set them after marking, adjusting for how demanding a particular paper turned out to be, so a series with a harder Paper 4 will usually have a lower threshold for the same grade. Past threshold tables are published and are useful for setting a realistic target, but they are a guide rather than a promise, and no tutor can tell you what a future threshold will be. Treat anyone who quotes a precise future requirement as guessing, and plan for a margin above the historical figure instead.

faqs.question: Which command term do IGCSE candidates most often answer as though it said describe?
faqs.answer: Explain. Examiner reports return to it every series: the question asks for a mechanism or a reason and the candidate supplies an accurate account of what happens, which reads well and collects a minority of the marks. The fix is mechanical rather than intellectual. A student learns to find the command term first, say out loud what shape of answer it demands, and check that the word because or its equivalent appears in the response. Evaluate and justify fail the same way, with the judgement left implied rather than written down.

faqs.question: What should a diagnostic session produce if the tutor has never taught my child's syllabus code before?
faqs.answer: It should produce an honest sequence rather than a confident plan. A tutor who has not taught that exact code can still mark a past paper against the published mark scheme and tell you which command terms and which topics lost marks. What they should not do is design a term around a component list they have not read. The reasonable answer is a diagnosis now, the current syllabus read before the first paid session, and the plan written afterwards. A tutor who skips the reading and starts teaching is guessing at the architecture.

faqs.question: What belongs in a private tutor's first written report, measured against the specification?
faqs.answer: Four things: which component was worked on, what the marked evidence showed at the start, what it shows now, and what happens next. Marks should be reported by component and ideally by command term, not as a single percentage, because a percentage hides whether the gain came from content or technique. The report should also name what has not improved. A first report that contains encouragement and no marked work is not a report, and a family that accepts one has given up the only evidence available for deciding whether to continue.

faqs.question: After four weeks, how do we tell whether the problem was content or technique?
faqs.answer: Compare two marked pieces on the same component. If the student now gets further into the question before stopping, the gap was content. If they attempt everything and still lose the same marks on explain, evaluate and justify, it was technique. If the marks moved on structured questions but not on the practical paper, the gap is a component nobody was teaching. This is why the diagnostic has to be marked rather than discussed: a conversation about how lessons are going cannot distinguish between those three, and they need different responses.

faqs.question: What does a private tutor do differently when the school is teaching topics in a different order?
faqs.answer: Follow the school, with one exception. Teaching a topic three weeks before the class reaches it wastes the lesson and confuses the student, so the sensible default is to work slightly behind the scheme of work and consolidate what has just been covered. The exception is a prerequisite: if the next unit depends on algebra or on a definition the student never secured, that gap is worth fixing out of order. Ask the tutor to see the scheme of work in the first week, because a plan written without it will collide with the class by week three.

faqs.question: If progress stalls after a term, do we change the tutor, the subject or the number of hours?
faqs.answer: Look at the evidence before changing anything. A stall with rising marks on one component and flat marks on another usually means the plan is aimed at the wrong place, which is a plan problem rather than a people problem. A stall across every component, with a student who has stopped doing the work between sessions, is usually a match or a motivation problem, and more hours make it worse. Adding hours is the correct response in only one case: a genuine coverage gap with limited time left before a series.

faqs.question: What should a Year 9 student do before IGCSE option choices are locked in?
faqs.answer: Find out which subjects the school can actually run and which are tiered, then be realistic about mathematics. A weak algebra foundation shows up later in physics, chemistry and the quantitative parts of business and economics, so the cheapest intervention available at this point is a term of foundation work before the IGCSE content starts. Ask the school which subjects are entered at Core and which at Extended, and ask what evidence it uses to make that decision, because the answer tells you what the next eighteen months have to produce.

faqs.question: At what point in the Middle Years Programme does a private tutor become useful?
faqs.answer: When a student keeps landing in the same band across different units and nobody has explained why. Middle Years Programme assessment is criterion-based, and a child who can describe but not evaluate will sit in the middle band however much content they absorb. That is a teachable move and it is worth teaching before IGCSE, where the same gap reappears as lost marks on extended response. Before that point, support is usually better aimed at a specific weakness such as number fluency or writing structure than at the programme as a whole.

faqs.question: Which pieces of Diploma internal assessment should already be drafted before the second year starts?
faqs.answer: As many as the school's deadlines allow, and at minimum the Extended Essay should have a workable research question with a supervisor's agreement, plus a mathematics exploration or scientific investigation topic narrow enough to finish inside the published word limit. The reason is arithmetic rather than ambition: the second Diploma year contains the written papers, the remaining internal deadlines and any university applications, and all three compete for the same weeks. Work banked in the first year is the only version of this that does not end in a compressed spring term.

faqs.question: Is it realistic to hire an IB IGCSE private tutor in the final term before the June series?
faqs.answer: It is realistic for technique and unrealistic for coverage. In the last stretch, timed papers marked against the mark scheme, command-term drill, and work on the components with the worst marks per hour of effort all move a grade. Teaching a syllabus that was never covered does not, and a tutor who promises otherwise is selling reassurance. Scarce specialists are also hardest to book at exactly this point, so if a Higher Level science or mathematics tutor is needed, ask early and accept that the honest answer is sometimes that nobody suitable is free.

ib-igcse-private-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the specification, then choose the person
ib-igcse-private-tutor.closingBody: Send us the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component that is costing marks, and we will tell you whether a genuine specialist for that exact course is free in your evening window on Arabia Standard Time. The free trial lesson is a diagnostic: your child works a timed section from a real past paper, the tutor marks it against the board's own mark scheme, and you keep the marked script whether or not you book anything. Lessons for families in the Kingdom are taught online, one-to-one, over live video, and no tutor will ever write any part of work your child has to submit.

intro.heading: Start with the mark scheme, not the subject
paragraphs: Most families looking for IB IGCSE tuition near me in Saudi Arabia begin by naming a subject. Chemistry is weak, maths is slipping. That is a diagnosis one level too coarse to act on. A Cambridge IGCSE subject is examined through two or three papers, each carrying a published share of the grade, and an IB Diploma subject usually carries three papers plus an internal assessment. A student can be strong in the material and still lose the grade on one component. The first useful question is which one.

Once that question is on the table everything else follows from it. How many lessons a week, whether the work is content or technique, whether a tier should be argued about, whether a group class would do: all of it is answered differently depending on whether the problem is a multiple-choice paper, an extended-response paper, or a piece of coursework that has stalled. This page is built in that order — structure first, then tiering, then mark schemes, then the week the lessons have to fit into.

That week is the part nobody writes about honestly. The Saudi school week runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. A tutor in India or the United Kingdom works Monday to Friday. The two calendars do not line up: your Thursday evening is the start of a weekend, and the tutor's Saturday is their day off but your child's best long session of the week. Whether weekly tuition survives three months depends on solving that properly at the start.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A tutor in a country that does will drift against you twice a year unless the slot is written down in Saudi local time. It sounds like a detail. It is the most common reason a working arrangement quietly stops working, because the lesson moves an hour into homework time and nobody renegotiates it; the student simply starts missing sessions and the parent concludes the tutoring is not helping. Put it in the first message: the day, the hour, and the words Arabia Standard Time. A tutor who will not commit to that has told you something useful about how they run their own week.

Lessons here are delivered online, one to one, over live video. We do not send anybody to a Saudi address — in-home teaching is something we offer only in India — and this page makes the case for the online format on its merits rather than hiding it in a footnote. A family in Al Ahsa or Tabuk gets the specialist who knows their paper, on a slot that fits a Saudi evening, instead of whoever lives close enough to drive.

sections.heading: How IGCSE and IB are actually assessed, component by component
paragraphs: A grade is not a single number a student earns; it is a weighted sum of components, and the weighting is published. A Cambridge IGCSE subject typically runs two or three written papers, with some subjects adding coursework or an alternative-to-practical paper. An IB Diploma science carries three written papers plus an internal assessment. Each of those pieces has a stated percentage, and the student's marks are rarely spread evenly across them.

That asymmetry is where the leverage sits. Losing a third of the marks on a component worth thirty-five per cent of the grade costs far more than losing half the marks on one worth fifteen. Families almost always revise what feels uncomfortable, which is usually the topic the student dislikes rather than the paper that is bleeding marks. Putting the published weightings alongside a recent set of component scores takes twenty minutes and usually reorders the whole plan.

Get the weightings from the right place: the school, from the syllabus or subject guide it is actually teaching to, with the code. Boards revise specifications, and schools choose different option topics within the same subject, so a figure copied off a revision site is a guess. Ask the subject teacher or the examinations officer in writing for the component list and the percentages. Nobody minds being asked, and the answer makes every later decision cheaper. Keep that reply, because it is also the document a tutor needs in order to plan anything useful, and it saves repeating the question every time a new term starts or a teacher changes.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: the tier decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers many IGCSE subjects, and the tier is not a difficulty setting. Core is graded C to G. Extended is graded A* to E. A student entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C no matter how well the paper goes, because the grades above it are not available on that entry. Every year some families discover this after mock results, when the entry has already been made and the ceiling is fixed for the series.

The decision belongs to the school, and it is made on predicted performance, set placement and timetable practicalities. It is reversible, but only before the entry deadline, which closes several months ahead of the June series. So the conversation to have is early and specific: which tier is my child entered for in each subject, what would need to change to move them to Extended, and by what date must that decision be made? Ask for the answer in writing.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades on the 9 to 1 scale and does not tier most subjects, which changes the question rather than removing it. A family moving a child between the two boards should expect a different paper structure under the same subject name, and should not assume a grade on one scale maps cleanly onto the other. Where a student sits near a tier boundary, two terms of targeted work on the weakest component is usually what moves the decision.

sections.heading: Command terms and mark schemes: the gap between knowing and being paid
paragraphs: Both boards write questions with command terms, and each term buys something different. State wants a bare answer with no reasoning. Outline wants a brief account. Describe wants detail without a mechanism. Explain wants the mechanism. Discuss and evaluate want both sides and a judgement. A student who answers every question with everything they know scores well on the questions that wanted everything and loses marks on all the others, which looks like weak knowledge and is not.

Mark schemes make this visible, and they are published. Sitting with a student and a scheme for one past paper is often worth more than a month of content revision, because the pattern is usually consistent: six-mark answers written as four points, no linking words, a diagram with no labels, a judgement never actually made. The student can see where the marks went rather than being told their answers were not detailed enough.

Practising it properly means marking against the scheme instead of checking against a textbook. The student writes the answer, then marks their own work with the scheme beside them and writes down which mark they missed and why. It is slow, and it is the single most reliable way to move a grade without learning new content. A tutor's job here is to teach the marking, not to do it for the student forever. Two months of that habit changes how a student reads a question: they start counting the marks available before writing, which is the behaviour every examiner report asks for and almost no revision guide teaches.

sections.heading: A Sunday-to-Thursday week, and the tutor's own working week
paragraphs: The school week here runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Almost every piece of tutoring advice online was written against a Monday-to-Friday assumption, and it breaks on contact with this one. Sunday evening is a school night with a tired student at the start of their week. Thursday evening is the beginning of a weekend and the worst slot in the week for new content, though a good one for a long paper nobody has to recover from in the morning.

Now put the tutor's week next to it. A tutor in India, Pakistan, the United Kingdom or most of Europe works Monday to Friday and rests Saturday and Sunday. That means the two Saudi weekend days are, for them, one working day and one rest day — and your child's school nights are their ordinary working evenings. The overlap that works for both sides is Sunday to Wednesday evening in the Kingdom, plus Saturday morning if the tutor treats Saturday as a working day.

This is worth settling explicitly before the first lesson rather than discovering it in week five. Ask the tutor which days they do not teach, and whether Saturday is one of them. A tutor whose own weekend falls on Friday and Saturday has the easiest fit of all, and tutors based in the Gulf often do. The arrangements that collapse are the ones where nobody said out loud that the proposed slot was the tutor's day off.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against the clock your tutor keeps
paragraphs: Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not observe daylight saving, so the local clock never moves. Tutors in countries that do observe it move twice a year, which means a slot agreed as six in the evening in loose terms becomes five or seven without anyone deciding to change it. Write the slot down as a Saudi local time and let the tutor's clock be the thing that adjusts. That one sentence in a first message prevents most of the scheduling friction that follows.

The offsets are worth knowing before choosing which time zone a tutor works from, because the zone decides how comfortable the slot is at the far end. India is two and a half hours ahead, so a comfortable Saudi evening is a late evening there. The United Kingdom is three hours behind in its winter and two in its summer, which makes a Saudi evening slot a British afternoon — easy for the tutor, and the reason the drift matters. The Gulf states are within an hour and share the working week, which is the cleanest fit of all.

The practical rule is to check the far end of the arrangement, not just your own. A tutor teaching at half past ten at night will be reliable for a few weeks and then start rescheduling. Pick a slot that is unremarkable on both clocks, confirm it in writing against Saudi local time, and agree what happens when a clock change comes round, because it will.

sections.heading: What a live online lesson looks like, and what it cannot do
paragraphs: The mechanics are unremarkable once seen. The tutor shares a screen with the past paper open, and a shared whiteboard carries the working so both people write on the same surface. For a handwritten solution the student photographs the page and drops it in, which also gives the tutor the thing they most need: the student's own working, with the error still in it. Graphs, free-body diagrams and organic structures are drawn live rather than described.

What a parent should expect to see is a short written note after each session saying what was covered, what was set, and what the student struggled with. Ask at the start whether sessions are recorded, who can access a recording and for how long; the answer should be a policy, not an improvisation. If a connection drops mid-lesson, the tutor should pick up from the same question rather than restarting, and the time should be made up.

The honest limits are worth stating. Online teaching cannot replace a laboratory. It can teach the experimental reasoning that written papers and alternative-to-practical components assess, which is most of what the marks are for, but the practical work itself belongs to the school. It also struggles with a student who will not speak. A teenager who sits silently on camera needs a different approach, and a tutor who does not notice within two lessons is the wrong tutor. Say so early if it happens at home, because the fix is usually a change of tutor rather than a change of format.

sections.heading: What the hour costs, and how to check a tutor before committing
paragraphs: Advertised figures in this market sit in bands, and they come from the providers themselves. A platform marketing page advertises IGCSE one-to-one online from about SAR 35 an hour. A tutor-marketplace guide quotes general private tuition in Riyadh at around SAR 50 for primary and above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. A tutoring-company listing puts IB subject tutoring from roughly SAR 180, with Higher Level tracks around SAR 200 to 220. Those are advertised rates, not an average, and not what we charge.

A small group can be better value than one-to-one, but only in specific conditions: the students are at the same tier, working on the same component, and the session is about technique rather than individual gaps. Mark-scheme practice works well in a pair. Rebuilding one student's algebra does not. Ask what happens to an unused lesson in a block, how much notice a cancellation needs, and whether the rate is held if the family pauses over the long summer break.

Then check the tutor rather than the brand. Ask which board and which component they have marked, and what the most frequent reason for losing a mark on that paper is. Ask them to look at one piece of your child's work before the trial lesson and say what they would do first. A specialist answers in the language of the mark scheme. No tutor can promise a grade, and an unverifiable success rate tells you only that somebody wrote it down.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE lesson look like from the student's side of the screen?
faqs.answer: A video call, a shared whiteboard and the past paper open on screen. The student writes on the same whiteboard the tutor does, so working is visible as it happens rather than described afterwards. Handwritten solutions get photographed and dropped into the session. Most of the hour is the student working with the tutor interrupting, which is the opposite of a recorded lecture and the reason live teaching is worth the money.

faqs.question: How does a tutor work through a Physics past paper on a shared screen?
faqs.answer: The paper goes up alongside the mark scheme, hidden at first. The student attempts the question, the tutor watches the working appear, and the scheme comes into view afterwards so the student can see which mark went where. Diagrams are drawn live, not pasted in. Marks lost to units, symbols or an unstated assumption get logged, because that log is what the next session works from.

faqs.question: Are IB tuition sessions recorded, and who can see the recording afterwards?
faqs.answer: Ask before the first lesson and expect a clear policy rather than an improvised answer. Where recording happens it should be with the family's knowledge, available to the student and the parent, and kept for a stated period. Recordings help with a dense derivation the student wants again. They are no substitute for attending, and a student who starts skipping the live session to watch later has stopped learning actively.

faqs.question: If the video call fails halfway through a marked IGCSE paper, how is the lost time handled?
faqs.answer: The tutor notes the clock and the question number, and the session resumes from exactly there rather than restarting. Lost minutes are made up at the end or in the following slot. On a genuinely timed paper the clock is paused and the remaining time honoured, otherwise the exercise measures the household internet rather than the student. Agree that rule once and it never needs discussing again.

faqs.question: Is a tablet enough for an online Mathematics lesson, or is a laptop needed?
faqs.answer: A tablet with a stylus is often better than a laptop for mathematics, because the student can write naturally on the shared whiteboard instead of fighting a trackpad. A laptop is better where the student needs to read a long paper and write at the same time. The arrangement that works least well is a phone: the paper is unreadable and the working space is too small to think in.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark an IGCSE written answer between two lessons?
faqs.answer: The student photographs or scans the work and sends it. The tutor marks it against the published mark scheme, annotates where each mark was earned or missed, and returns it before the next session so the student reads the comments cold rather than being talked through them. The following lesson starts from the two or three errors that repeat, not from a line-by-line walk through everything that was wrong.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level Physics hour quoted higher than a Standard Level Biology one?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, mostly. Far fewer teachers can handle the Higher Level Physics extension topics and the Paper 2 extended responses than can teach Standard Level Biology well, and a thin supply of specialists raises the advertised rate wherever you look. Level adds to it, and marking experience on that specific component adds again. Travel loading is the one factor that disappears entirely when the lesson is delivered online.

faqs.question: Is a small group class ever better value than one-to-one for IGCSE English as a Second Language?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, under conditions. A pair or trio at the same tier working on summary-task technique or reading comprehension can work well, because the comparison between answers teaches something. A group is poor value when one student needs their own foundation rebuilt, or when they sit at different tiers, because the session drifts towards the middle and nobody gets what they came for.

faqs.question: What happens in a free trial lesson, and what should a parent watch for?
faqs.answer: The student brings work with marks lost on it and the tutor works through the errors. Watch for three things: does the tutor name the component rather than the topic, does the student do most of the talking by the halfway point, and is there a concrete next step at the end? Reassurance and a general plan to build confidence is not a diagnosis, and it is worth noticing early.

faqs.question: Do we pay per lesson or per block, and what happens to an unused lesson?
faqs.answer: Both arrangements exist in this market and the terms matter more than the headline rate. Ask what notice a cancellation needs, whether an unused lesson in a block expires, and whether the slot is held if the family pauses over the long summer break. A block discount that quietly expires is not a discount. Get the answers before paying rather than after the first missed week.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate change as the June series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates in this market tend to firm up as a series approaches, because demand concentrates and the specialists with free slots are the ones who were not booked earlier. That is a scheduling problem as much as a cost one: the tutor you want may simply have no evening left. Families who settle a slot two terms out pay less attention to this than families who start eight weeks out.

faqs.question: What does examiner experience on a named component actually buy?
faqs.answer: Knowledge of what the band descriptors reward, which is not the same as knowing the content. Somebody who has marked a paper can say why an answer scored four rather than six, and can predict the error a student is about to make. Ask which board, which component, and what the most common reason for losing a mark on it is. A specific answer arrives in one sentence; a vague one tells you plenty.

faqs.question: How do we verify that a tutor has taught this exact syllabus and not just the subject?
faqs.answer: Three questions do it. Which syllabus code and components does my child sit? What is in the Higher Level extension that is not at Standard Level? Show me a mark scheme and tell me why this answer scored what it did. Somebody teaching the course answers all three without looking anything up. A subject graduate revising alongside the student will stall on the second.

faqs.question: Should a Higher Level candidate and a Standard Level sibling share the same tutor?
faqs.answer: They can share a tutor, but not a session. The content overlaps and a good teacher handles both, so one tutor across two separate slots often works well and keeps the reporting simple. Putting them in the same hour does not work: the Higher Level extension material is dead time for the Standard Level student, and the pace needed by one is wrong for the other.

ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Send the component list and the clock will take care of itself

ib-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below show the kind of background that matters for this search: a named subject, a named level, recent teaching on the current syllabus and, where it exists, marking experience described by board and component rather than claimed in general. The pool changes weekly, so treat these as representative rather than as a roster.

intro.heading: Judge the tutor on what they can show you, not on what they claim
paragraphs: The honest version of this search is that a family is trying to buy a person, and almost nothing published about tutoring in the Kingdom helps them judge one. Rival pages list qualifications in the abstract, attach a satisfaction figure nobody can verify, and leave the parent exactly where they started. The useful approach is the reverse: decide what a competent tutor would be able to demonstrate within three sessions, then treat anything short of that as a reason to meet somebody else.

After three sessions with a student, a tutor who knows what they are doing can put four things in front of you. A baseline: a timed paper or a piece of assessed work, marked against the published scheme, with the marks lost identified by component. A diagnosis: which of a short list of faults is actually costing those marks, written in a sentence you could repeat to a third party. A plan: the sequence of work that follows from the diagnosis, in order, with a rough duration. And a date: when the comparison will be made and what document it will be made against.

None of that requires you to understand the subject. It requires the tutor to have read the student's work against a mark scheme, which is the whole of the job and the thing a generalist cannot fake for long. A tutor who after three sessions offers encouragement, a description of the student's attitude and a recommendation to continue weekly has told you only that they are pleasant. That is not a small thing for a teenager, and it is not what you are paying for.

Which qualification matters depends entirely on the level, and this is where the two kinds of family searching this phrase diverge. At IGCSE, the binding constraint is knowledge of the specification and the question style: a capable graduate who knows 0620 or the Edexcel equivalent inside out will do more for a Year 11 student than a university researcher who knows far more chemistry. At Diploma Programme Higher Level, the balance shifts: the extension topics, the Internal Assessment criteria and the command-term discipline mean recent teaching of that exact course matters more than general subject depth, and marking experience starts to pay for itself.

Delivery is online. Lessons arranged through IB Gram are one-to-one video sessions on Arabia Standard Time, available to families anywhere in the Kingdom; we do not arrange home visits anywhere in Saudi Arabia, and visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. For this particular search that is the structural advantage rather than a limitation, because the question "who is the right tutor" and the question "who lives near us" have no relationship to each other, and only one of them affects the grade.

ib-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: The programmes below are described from the tutor's side: what a person has to know to teach each one properly. That is a more useful filter for this search than a description of the courses, because it tells you what to ask about.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: A tutor working at this level needs the specification code, not the subject. They should know which topics appear only in the Extended papers, what the mark scheme does with an answer that shows no working, which definitions are examined to the word, and how the two boards differ in question style for the same content. Subject depth beyond the syllabus adds very little here; familiarity with the papers adds a great deal.
programmes.countryNote: Across the Kingdom, British-curriculum schools use both boards and sometimes different ones for different subjects in the same school, so a tutor who teaches the subject but not the specification will prepare a student well for a differently structured paper. Saudi candidates sit the June series as the main sitting, with the November series for resits, which makes the entry route a question for the school's examinations officer rather than the tutor.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: A tutor here needs to work from the four published criteria in the relevant subject group, because nothing else determines the mark. They should be able to say what each criterion rewards, which one students most often ignore, and how a school's task-specific clarifications change the descriptors. They also need to understand the Personal Project as a process with recorded supervision rather than as a piece of work to be improved.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the Kingdom often move into the MYP from a national-curriculum or an American-curriculum school, and the criteria come as a shock to students used to being marked on content. A tutor who has taught the MYP recently treats that as the first thing to fix. One who has only taught examined courses tends to teach the subject and leave the criteria to the school, which is where the marks are.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The highest bar for a tutor, and the level at which general subject expertise stops being sufficient. They need the current subject guide, the Higher Level extension topics, the Internal Assessment criteria by name, the command-term list, and the paper weightings. They should know what the core adds through the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. Marking or moderating experience shows up most visibly here, in how precisely they predict what an answer will score.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Saudi schools are usually in small cohorts, which means a school can rarely offer a second pass through a Higher Level topic. A tutor for this level is therefore doing teaching rather than reinforcement, and needs to be able to deliver a topic properly from the start rather than revise one the student has already met. Ask what they would do if the student has not covered the topic at all.

programmes.name: The IGCSE to Diploma Programme step
programmes.ageRange: Ages 15-17 · The summer and first term between them
programmes.description: The least served and most useful brief of the four. A tutor working this transition needs both ends: what an IGCSE student has actually been taught, and what the first term of a Diploma course assumes they know. The gap is specific and subject by subject — notation, proof, the volume of independent reading, and a command-term vocabulary nobody has mentioned before.
programmes.countryNote: This is the brief most often fulfilled badly in the Kingdom, because the tutor who taught the IGCSE successfully is kept on into the Diploma year without having taught the Diploma course. The student is then taught a harder version of IGCSE. Ask directly whether a tutor has taught both ends; many have, and the ones who have will describe the differences without prompting.

ib-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each entry below names what a specialist in that subject should be able to do, rather than what the syllabus contains. Read it as a checklist for the conversation before you agree to a first session.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A specialist should be able to name the Higher Level topics with no Standard Level counterpart, explain why Paper 1 without a calculator exposes manipulation weakness, and set out what the exploration criteria reward beyond correct mathematics. They should be able to write an induction proof out in full without reference, because that is the standard the student is being marked to.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The test here is whether the tutor teaches interpretation or calculation. A specialist knows the marks go to explaining what calculator output means in context and to justifying the choice of statistical test, not to the output itself. They should also be clear about which university courses expect this route and which expect Analysis and Approaches, because families often discover that too late.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Look for someone who talks about the experimental paper and the internal investigation as readily as about mechanics. A specialist can explain what a graph question needs beyond the gradient, how method marks survive a wrong final answer, and which extension topics are routinely taught last and fastest. They should be able to say what a weak investigation design looks like before any data is collected.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: A specialist knows the mechanism conventions precisely enough to mark them, and will say so in those terms. They should be able to describe what the data booklet is used for under time pressure, what a six-mark answer needs that a correct explanation does not, and how organic chemistry taught approximately at IGCSE has to be unlearned before the Diploma treatment lands.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The useful signal is command terms. A specialist will volunteer that describe, explain, outline, suggest and evaluate license different answers with different lengths, and will name the topics where Higher Level goes well past Standard Level. On the internal investigation they should talk about controllable variables and sufficient data points rather than about interesting ideas.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A specialist treats the diagram as the answer and can say which diagrams are worth drilling to automaticity. They should know what the quantitative paper at Higher Level actually asks, and what makes a commentary extract usable or hopeless. A tutor who discusses economics as a subject without mentioning the commentaries has not supervised them.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask what changes between IGCSE English and this course, and listen for the analytical vocabulary answer rather than the harder-texts answer. A specialist can set out a repeatable method for an unseen non-literary text under time pressure, and can explain how the individual oral is assessed, which is the component students prepare least and lose most on.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The scarcest specialism at both levels, and the one where a practising developer is not automatically a good tutor. A specialist knows that pseudocode conventions and hand-traced algorithms carry marks, and can talk about the client-facing solution component as an assessed artefact with criteria rather than as a programming project.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: A specialist talks about source work and the mark bands before they talk about periods. They should be able to explain what the source-based paper rewards, how the Higher Level regional option differs in demand, and what makes a historical investigation question narrow enough to answer in the word limit, which is where most of them fail.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: A frequent choice for students arriving from other systems, and one where marks hinge on using studies as evidence rather than recounting them. A specialist can say how many studies an essay actually needs, what the Higher Level extensions add, and what makes the experimental study report comply with the ethical requirements.

ib-igcse-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: At IGCSE the same principle applies with a narrower focus: the specification, the components and the mark scheme. These are the subjects most often requested alongside a Diploma sibling or ahead of a Diploma transition.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel equivalents)
igcseSubjects.description: A specialist asks which tier before anything else, because it caps the grade. They should be able to say which topics appear only on the Extended papers and how the working is credited when the final answer is wrong. For a student heading into Diploma mathematics they will also flag the notation and manipulation gaps that are about to matter.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
igcseSubjects.description: Look for someone who treats the practical-skills paper as a separate skill with its own marks. They should know what the formula sheet does and does not provide, and why recall drills still matter. A specialist can also name which 0625 topics are assumed knowledge in the first weeks of a Diploma physics course.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
igcseSubjects.description: A specialist names ionic equations, state symbols and the qualitative analysis tables as the high-yield repairs, rather than suggesting a general revision of the syllabus. They should also know how the mole calculations are credited stage by stage, which is the difference between a dropped question and a part-marked one.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
igcseSubjects.description: The examined definitions are the test of a specialist here: they will say that a paraphrase scores nothing and will have a method for drilling the wording. They should also know which diagrams students are expected to draw and label themselves rather than only interpret, which is routinely underprepared.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
igcseSubjects.description: A specialist talks about the reading questions first, because that is where the marks are least often claimed. They should be able to explain how detail from the passage earns credit that general fluency does not, and what directed writing is actually assessed on, which is rarely the quality of the prose alone.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
igcseSubjects.description: Trace tables and pseudocode conventions are the marks that confident programmers lose, and a specialist says so immediately. They should also be able to explain why writing an algorithm by hand is examined at all, which is the question a student who codes fluently will ask in the first session.

ib-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where the specialists are, and where they are not
ib-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The subject a family needs is available somewhere in the Kingdom; whether it is available within driving distance of their address is a different question, and the answer varies enormously. This is a map of where the staffing pressure sits, because it determines whether you are choosing a tutor or finding one.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest pool for most subjects and the only market where a family can realistically compare several candidates for the same Diploma Programme subject. Even here, Computer Science and Design Technology specialists are scarce, and a family wanting a choice rather than a single option will look beyond the city.

regions.name: Jeddah and Thuwal
regions.note: A long coastal spine with several IB and Cambridge schools along it, plus the campus community at Thuwal to the north. Subject cover is good at the common Diploma subjects and thin at the minority ones, and a tutor at one end of the spine is not a practical visiting option at the other.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar, Dammam and Jubail
regions.note: One school market in practice, with an engineering-led demand profile: Higher Level physics, chemistry and mathematics dominate enquiries, which is exactly where school cohorts are too small to carry a second specialist. Demand and scarcity point at the same subjects here.

regions.name: Makkah, Madinah and Taif
regions.note: Private school provision with narrower international-curriculum choice than the big three markets. Families typically have one local option per subject rather than several, so the question is usually whether a specialist exists at all rather than which one to pick.

regions.name: Tabuk and NEOM
regions.note: Communities growing faster than school provision in the north-west, with a high proportion of mid-course arrivals. The commonest brief here is not a weak subject but a syllabus taught in a different order at the previous school, which needs a tutor who can map gaps rather than teach a course.

regions.name: AlUla, Ha'il and Buraidah
regions.note: Interior centres with small, dispersed international-curriculum cohorts. For a scarce subject there may be nobody locally at any price, which makes the choice of tutor a national question rather than a local one, and makes the hour of the evening the only real constraint.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait and Jazan
regions.note: The main southern school market sits in 'Asir, with Abha and Khamis Mushait roughly 25km apart and sharing a catchment. Subject breadth is limited and the distance to Riyadh or Jeddah is considerable, so specialist cover is routinely sourced from outside the region.

regions.name: Najran and the southern border provinces
regions.note: Geographically distant from every international-school cluster in the Kingdom. The nearest specialist in a scarce Higher Level science may be several hundred kilometres away, which removes any visiting arrangement from consideration and makes the match entirely about syllabus and availability.

regions.name: Al Ahsa, Qatif and Ras Tanura
regions.note: Satellites of the Eastern Province cluster, with Al Ahsa about an hour and a half inland. Families here commonly attend school in the cluster, so a long drive is already part of the day and an evening slot has to start after it rather than before.

schoolClusters.note: The capital carries the widest IB provision in the Kingdom, including schools running the full continuum from the Primary Years Programme through to the Diploma. Because subject availability at Higher Level depends on how many students opt in, the question worth asking any of these schools is which Higher Level subjects actually ran last year rather than which appear in the prospectus.

schoolClusters.city: Thuwal, Dhahran and the campus communities
schoolClusters.note: Schools attached to university and industrial communities serve a concentrated and highly international population, and their cohorts are small by design. The Diploma Programme is offered at the American School of Dhahran and at ISG Jubail, while other campuses in the same groups follow British and Cambridge pathways, so a move between them can mean a change of board as well as of school.

ib-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Four briefs cover what families ask for under this search, and the right person differs for each. All sessions are one to one and delivered live over video on Arabia Standard Time, Sunday to Thursday, with weekend slots kept for blocks.

modes.title: One subject, one level, one specialist
modes.description: The default and the most effective. A single tutor working on one named course at one named level, with written work set and marked between sessions. Two weak subjects means two specialists, not one tutor stretched across both, because the thing you are buying is depth in a particular paper rather than general availability.

modes.title: A transition block between IGCSE and the Diploma
modes.description: A short, scoped programme bridging the two levels, usually taken across the summer or in the first term of the Diploma. It covers the specific gaps rather than revising IGCSE: notation, proof, the volume of independent reading, command-term vocabulary and what an Internal Assessment is. It ends when the student is working comfortably at the new level.

modes.title: Two children, two levels, one evening
modes.description: Separate sessions for siblings at different levels, scheduled back to back so one evening carries both. The tutors are usually different people even when the subject is the same, because the IGCSE specification and the Diploma subject guide reward different knowledge. The convenience is in the scheduling, not in sharing a tutor.

modes.title: Coursework review across both boards
modes.description: Scheduled sessions on the student's own Internal Assessment, exploration, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay, Personal Project or IGCSE coursework. The tutor reads what the student has produced, maps it against the published criteria and asks the questions an examiner would ask. They do not contribute text, data or analysis, and nothing in the submitted work originates with them.

sections.heading: What a tutor should be able to show you after three sessions
paragraphs: This search is about a person, so the most useful thing a page can give you is a test. Three sessions is enough for any competent tutor at either level to produce four specific outputs, and the absence of them is more informative than any qualification. The test costs you three sessions and tells you whether to buy a term.

The first output is a baseline. For an examined subject that is a timed paper or a timed section, marked against the published scheme, with the marks lost attributed to components rather than to topics. For coursework it is the criterion grid with the weak criterion identified. The point of the baseline is not to upset the student; it is to create a document that exists before the teaching starts, so that the comparison at the end means something. Without it, the review conversation in three months is about impressions.

The second is a diagnosis: one sentence naming the fault. Marks are being lost to command terms, or to missing method steps, or to definitions learned approximately, or to timing, or to answering from general knowledge rather than from the source, or to a topic genuinely not covered. These are not interchangeable and they need different interventions. A tutor who cannot reduce the problem to one of a short list after reading marked work is still guessing, however pleasant the sessions are.

The third is a plan with an order and a rough duration, and the fourth is a date with a document attached to it. Together those four things turn tutoring from a standing cost into something you can audit. They also reveal the single most common failure mode in this market, which is a tutor teaching the topic the student raises at the start of each session. That is responsive, it feels useful, and over a term it covers whatever happened to be on the student's mind rather than whatever is costing the marks.
bullets: A baseline document, marked against the published scheme and kept
A one-sentence diagnosis naming the fault, not describing the student
A plan with an order and a rough duration
A review date with the comparison document named in advance

sections.heading: Five tutor backgrounds, and what each one is actually good for
paragraphs: The word tutor covers people with very different training, and the right one depends on the level and the fault rather than on which background sounds most impressive. A family who understands the five common profiles can choose deliberately instead of accepting whoever is offered, and can also tell when a high rate is buying something they do not need.

A serving schoolteacher brings the current subject guide, the rhythm of an academic year and the instincts of someone who has sequenced coursework for a whole cohort. They are strongest on planning and on what the school will expect, and weakest on availability: they are teaching during the hours a tutor is wanted, and a tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind Saudi local time in their winter, which puts a Riyadh evening in the middle of their school afternoon.

A full-time tutor has usually marked far more student work across more boards than a classroom teacher, which shows in how quickly they name a fault. A board-appointed examiner or moderator adds precise knowledge of how marks are awarded at the boundaries. A postgraduate or researcher brings subject depth that is genuinely valuable at Higher Level and frequently irrelevant at IGCSE. And a capable graduate generalist is the right and cheapest answer for fluency work that needs setting and marking rather than teaching.

The mistake families make is buying the deepest subject expertise for the shallowest problem. A doctoral chemist is not better than a 0620 specialist at getting a Year 11 student to write state symbols consistently, and may be worse, because the specialist has marked a hundred scripts where that cost somebody a grade. Conversely, a generalist who is fine at IGCSE will not see what is wrong with a Higher Level answer that reads correctly and scores four out of six.

sections.heading: What examiner experience means, and what it does not
paragraphs: Examiner experience is the claim most often stretched in this market, partly because the terms are unfamiliar to parents. Examination boards appoint people to mark particular components of particular subjects, with senior appointees responsible for standardising and checking the work of others, and separate appointments for moderating work that schools assess internally. These are specific, component-level roles for specific series, not a permanent status conferred on a person.

That matters practically. Somebody who has marked one component of one subject knows that component extremely well and has no special insight into the others. Somebody who has moderated internally assessed work knows what pushes a criterion mark up or down, which is different knowledge again. Neither appointment makes a person a better teacher automatically; what it reliably gives them is calibration — the ability to look at an answer and say what it will score, and why.

So the question is never whether a tutor has examiner experience. It is which board, which subject, which component, and what they learned from it. Somebody who has marked a batch of scripts will tell you how a borderline answer is treated, what the commonest error was across the pile, how method marks are allocated when the final answer is wrong, and what standardisation felt like. Somebody who has not will talk about examinations in general terms. You do not need to inspect a certificate to hear the difference, and the specific answers come instantly because they are memories rather than claims.

Two cautions. First, an examiner is bound by confidentiality and will not share scripts, unpublished mark schemes or anything about a live series; a tutor who offers that is telling you something bad about themselves. Second, no appointment of any kind implies a relationship between a tutoring business and a board. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and any provider implying otherwise is misrepresenting what an individual's marking work means.

sections.heading: The step from IGCSE to the Diploma Programme, subject by subject
paragraphs: The family searching for one tutor across both levels is often really asking about this step, and it is worth setting out properly because almost nothing in the market does. A student can finish IGCSE with excellent grades and struggle badly in the first term of the Diploma, and when that happens it is usually not about ability. It is about four specific changes arriving at once.

The first is assessment philosophy. IGCSE rewards content delivered accurately against a mark scheme; the Diploma rewards content delivered against command terms and, in every subject, an extended piece of independent work assessed by published criteria. A student who has never been marked by criteria does not know that writing more can score less. The second is independent reading volume, which roughly steps up and is rarely explained as a requirement.

The third is notation and technique, which is subject-specific and precisely the thing a tutor who has taught both ends can map. In mathematics it is function notation, proof and the non-calculator paper. In the sciences it is uncertainty, significant figures and the expectation of designing an investigation rather than following one. In the humanities it is sourcing and evaluation rather than narrative. In languages it is analysis of how a text works rather than comprehension of what it says.

The fourth is the simultaneity of the second year, when several independent components fall due in the same stretch. That is a planning problem rather than an academic one and it is the most common reason a capable Diploma student underperforms. A tutor working the transition brief properly spends part of the first term on sequencing, which feels like a detour and prevents the thing that actually goes wrong.

sections.heading: One tutor for both boards, or two specialists?
paragraphs: This is the practical question behind the search phrase, and the answer is usually two people, with one real exception. The reason is that the knowledge that makes someone good at IGCSE and the knowledge that makes someone good at the Diploma overlap less than the shared subject name suggests. One is specification and question-style knowledge; the other is subject guide, criteria and command-term knowledge, plus the extension topics.

The exception is the transition brief. A tutor who has genuinely taught both levels recently is the right person to carry a student across the step, because the value is precisely in knowing both ends. Those tutors exist and they are worth asking for by name. What does not work is keeping the tutor who did a good job at IGCSE into the Diploma year purely because the relationship is working. That is how a student ends up being taught a harder version of IGCSE for a term, which is comfortable and leaves the actual gap untouched.

For siblings at two levels, the honest answer is that the saving from one tutor is scheduling convenience rather than quality or money. Two specialists in consecutive slots on the same evening gives the household one committed night and each child a person who knows their papers. One tutor covering both children usually means one child is being taught by someone outside their strongest level, and it is rarely the older one who loses.

There is also a case where one tutor across two subjects is wrong for the same reason. A tutor who offers mathematics and physics, or chemistry and biology, may be strong in both; many are. But ask about both separately, because the second subject is sometimes a filler offered to keep a timetable full. The question that settles it is the same one that settles everything else on this page: ask about the papers, not about the subject.

sections.heading: Where students most often need outside teaching, and why those topics
paragraphs: A pattern holds across Saudi schools and it is not random. The topics that need outside teaching are the ones that are conceptually dense, taught late in a course, or dependent on something the student was supposed to have secured earlier. Knowing the pattern lets a family act before the problem is urgent rather than after.

Late and dense is the first category. Higher Level extension topics are usually taught last because they sit on top of the core, which means they arrive when the timetable is thinnest and revision has already started. In physics that is the extension work in fields and in nuclear topics; in chemistry it is the later organic and analytical material; in biology it is the physiology detail. A school with one specialist cannot run those twice, so a student who does not get them the first time does not get them.

Dependent on something earlier is the second and the more expensive. Algebraic manipulation that was never secure resurfaces in every topic requiring rearrangement. Loose organic conventions learned at IGCSE have to be unlearned before the Diploma treatment lands. Weak command-term discipline carried up from IGCSE caps a student in every subject at once, which is why it is worth fixing before subject content. These repairs mean going back before going forward and are the reason a diagnosis should precede a timetable.

The third category is the independent components, and it is not about topics at all. Internal Assessments, explorations, essays and projects need design decisions early and supervision throughout, and they are where schools are stretched thinnest because twenty students need individual attention in the same fortnight. An outside tutor is unusually well placed here, as long as the boundary around assessed work is clear, which is the subject of the next section.
bullets: Higher Level extension topics, because they are taught last and fastest
Anything resting on manipulation or notation that was never secure
Command-term discipline, which caps every subject simultaneously
Independent components, where schools have least individual time

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with assessed work, component by component
paragraphs: Every component with the student's name on it has to be their own work, and the providers in this market who are vague about that are vague deliberately. The rule is uniform across both boards, but who owns the process differs by component, and so does where a tutor fits. The table sets that out; the principle underneath it is simple and worth stating first.

A tutor may teach, explain, question, challenge and give feedback on work the student has produced. They may help a student choose a research question that can actually be answered in the word limit, explain what each published criterion rewards, read a draft and identify which criterion is underserved, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the evidence, and teach the referencing convention. They may teach any content the student needs in order to do the work. None of that puts a single word of theirs into the submission.

A tutor may not contribute text, data, analysis or structure to assessed work, and may not edit a draft into a better version. The test a parent can apply without subject knowledge is to ask the student to justify a paragraph or a calculation without notes. If they cannot, something has gone wrong regardless of what anyone called it. Schools keep records of supervision and require students to reflect on their own process, and an experienced supervisor notices a mismatch between a student's demonstrated ability and a submitted text.

If a school suspects malpractice it is obliged to follow a formal process, and the consequences can reach the qualification itself. That is the exposure a family takes on when a provider offers to handle a draft rather than discuss one. The correct response to that offer is to end the conversation, and the fact that it is a common offer in this SERP is a reason to be careful rather than a reason to assume it is normal.
