sections.heading: How a match is made, and what happens when it is wrong
paragraphs: Matching is a process rather than a lookup, and it turns on four pieces of information: the exact course and level as the school writes it, the board and specification or subject guide, the fault if it is already known, and the hour of the evening that is genuinely free on Saudi local time. Those four decide the shortlist. Everything else — a preference about teaching style, about the tutor's gender, about whether they are a serving teacher — refines it.

The hour is the constraint families underestimate. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks, so a slot agreed with a tutor in a country that observes daylight saving will move by an hour twice a year unless it is pinned to Saudi local time. Pin it at the outset. A tutor in India is two and a half hours ahead and teaching in their own evening, which is sustainable; a serving teacher in the United Kingdom is being asked to teach in the middle of their working afternoon, which frequently is not.

Then there is the case nobody advertises: sometimes no suitable specialist is free at the hour you need. A scarce Higher Level subject in a narrow evening window is a small intersection, and the honest options are a different hour, a wait, or starting with a related subject while the right person becomes available. We would rather say that than put a Standard Level teacher in front of a Higher Level student and let a family discover the difference in week three. A provider who never says no is not better staffed; they are less careful.

If a match turns out to be wrong after two or three sessions, the outcome should be a different tutor rather than a conversation about persevering. Mismatches at this level are usually about pace, assumed knowledge or rapport rather than competence, and none of those improve by being endured. What makes the second match better is specificity: the explanations assumed knowledge the student does not have, the pace lost them in the first ten minutes, the student will not speak up with this person. That is the same information the next tutor needs anyway.

sections.heading: Qualifications, verification, and the claims nobody can check
paragraphs: A qualification tells you what somebody studied, not what they can teach, and at these levels the two diverge more than families expect. A subject degree is the floor rather than the evidence. A teaching qualification indicates training in how to teach and says nothing about the specific syllabus. Recent teaching of the exact course is the single most predictive signal, and it is the easiest of all of them to test in conversation because it produces specific, immediate answers.

Four questions do most of the work, and none require subject knowledge. Which board, specification or subject guide do you teach, and which components? Which topics appear only at the higher tier or level? What does the mark scheme do with an answer that shows no working, or with a borderline extended response? And what will you set between lessons, and will it come back marked before the next one? Specific answers come from recent teaching. General answers come from reading about the subject.

Language and gender preferences are practical matters rather than sensitive ones, and online one-to-one teaching makes both straightforward to accommodate, because the pool is national rather than limited to whoever lives nearby and nobody is travelling to a family's address. State the preference at the enquiry stage with the subject, the level and the hour. In most subjects it narrows the pool far less than families expect.

Finally, the claims that cannot be checked at all. A satisfaction percentage, a star rating, a count of successful candidates, a promised grade improvement — offered without a sample size, a date and a stated method, none of these is evidence, and the confident version deserves more scepticism rather than less. The honest answer to how much a student will improve is a description of what will be measured, against what baseline, on what date. That answer is less satisfying to read and is the only one you can hold anybody to.
bullets: Recent teaching of the exact course predicts more than any qualification
Ask about components and mark schemes, not about the subject
Gender and language preferences are straightforward to match online
Treat any unverifiable figure as a reason to ask one more question

process.title: Name the course exactly as the school does
process.description: The subject, the level, the board, and the specification or subject guide. Mathematics is several different courses at Diploma Programme level and two tiers at IGCSE, so a vague subject line produces a vague match. For an IGCSE subject the code on the front of a past paper settles it in seconds.

process.title: Send marked work, not a grade
process.description: A recent script with the mark scheme, a criterion grid for coursework, or a predicted grade with the teacher's reasoning. This is what a specialist reads before the first session, and it is what makes the difference between a diagnosis and a conversation about how the term has been going.

process.title: Interview the tutor in a free session
process.description: Use the four questions: components, higher-level-only topics, what the mark scheme does with weak working, and what gets set and marked between lessons. Then let them work with your child. You are judging specificity and calibration, not warmth, though warmth matters for a teenager too.

process.title: Fix the slot on Saudi local time
process.description: Agree the weekly hour against Arabia Standard Time rather than the tutor's clock, so nothing moves when another country changes its own. Late afternoon and evening suit most Saudi school runs; Friday and Saturday are available for blocks before a series.

process.title: Audit against the four outputs
process.description: After three sessions you should hold a baseline, a one-sentence diagnosis, an ordered plan and a review date. If any of the four is missing, ask for it. If it still does not arrive, change the tutor before you buy a term rather than after.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the course, not to the subject
whyPoints.description: A match starts from the specification or subject guide the student is actually sitting, the level, and the components in question. The same subject name covers courses that reward different knowledge, and a tutor who knows the subject but not the papers prepares a student well for the wrong assessment.

whyPoints.title: Marking experience described, not claimed
whyPoints.description: Where a tutor has marked or moderated, we say which board and which component, because that is the only form in which the claim means anything. No appointment of that kind implies any relationship between IB Gram and an examination board, and we hold none with the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

whyPoints.title: Evidence after three sessions
whyPoints.description: A baseline document, a one-sentence diagnosis, an ordered plan and a review date. Those four outputs are what let a family tell competence from pleasantness, and they are the standard we expect a tutor to meet before anybody commits to a term of hours.

whyPoints.title: Both ends of the IGCSE to Diploma step
whyPoints.description: The transition brief is a specific skill: knowing what an IGCSE student was actually taught and what the first Diploma term assumes. Where a family needs that, we match a tutor who has taught both levels recently rather than keeping the IGCSE tutor on into a course they have not taught.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, challenges and gives feedback on what the student has produced. They contribute no text, data, analysis or structure to anything submitted, and nothing in a student's Internal Assessment, essay or project originates with them. That line is not a formality and it is not negotiable.

whyPoints.title: An honest no
whyPoints.description: A scarce subject at a narrow hour sometimes has nobody suitable free. We say so and offer a different slot, a wait or a different starting point, rather than substituting a tutor from an adjacent level and leaving a family to notice the difference themselves a few weeks in.

faqs.question: Which Mathematics AA HL topics have no Standard Level equivalent, and why does that change who should teach it?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level course adds material that Standard Level students never meet, including proof by induction, complex numbers, vector geometry and substantially harder calculus. That matters for matching because a tutor whose experience is Standard Level has not taught any of it and will teach around it. Ask a prospective tutor to name those topics unprompted: somebody who teaches the Higher Level course answers immediately, because those are the units that take the most preparation and generate the most questions. A hesitation there is the clearest signal available at this level.

faqs.question: What is the hardest transition inside the Diploma Programme physics course?
faqs.answer: Moving from applying a given equation to deciding which model applies and justifying it. The early topics reward recognising a question type; the later ones require choosing an approach and defending it, often across two topics at once. Students who scored well on mechanics by pattern-matching stall at that point, and it reads as a sudden difficulty rather than a shift in demand. The other hard step is the experimental component, where designing an investigation is a different skill from following a method, and almost nobody has practised it before.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE topics are treated as assumed knowledge in the first weeks of a Diploma course?
faqs.answer: In mathematics, confident algebraic manipulation, indices, surds and function notation. In the sciences, mole calculations, the basic structure of the atom, forces and energy, and cell structure, along with the ability to read and plot data accurately. In English, the ability to read a text closely and quote precisely. None of these get retaught, and a student who is shaky on them meets the gap in the second or third week of the Diploma rather than in the examination, which is actually good news if someone is looking for it.

faqs.question: Why do strong IGCSE English students sometimes score lower on Diploma Programme Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Because the task changes from understanding a text to analysing how it produces its effects, often on an unseen non-literary text under time pressure. A student who writes fluently about what a passage says can score in the middle bands while a less fluent student who analyses structure, register and audience scores higher. The repair is a repeatable annotation and planning method rather than more reading, and it typically takes a few weeks to install and a term to become automatic under timed conditions.

faqs.question: What does a Chemistry HL mark scheme want in a six-mark extended answer?
faqs.answer: Distinct, credit-worthy points rather than a well-written paragraph. Six marks usually means six separate ideas, each of which has to be present and recognisable: a statement, a reason, a consequence, a named example, a comparison, a qualification. Students who write a flowing explanation often make four of the six points implicitly and are credited for the explicit ones only. The technique is to plan in bullet points and then write, which sounds mechanical and is exactly what the scheme rewards.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a teaching qualification, or is a subject degree enough at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Neither is the deciding factor. A subject degree is the floor; a teaching qualification shows training in how to teach but says nothing about a specific syllabus. The strongest predictor is recent teaching of that exact course, because it produces knowledge of the subject guide, the criteria, the command terms and the extension topics all at once. Many excellent tutors at this level hold a teaching qualification and many do not. Test the course knowledge directly instead of using the qualification as a proxy for it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover an IGCSE child and a Diploma Programme sibling in the same subject?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but the saving is scheduling convenience rather than quality. The knowledge that makes someone good at IGCSE is the specification and the question style; the knowledge that makes someone good at the Diploma is the subject guide, the criteria and the extension topics. Many tutors have both; plenty have one. The better default is a specialist per level in consecutive slots on the same evening, which gives the household one committed night and each child someone who knows their papers properly.

faqs.question: What does a board mean by an assistant examiner, a team leader and a moderator?
faqs.answer: Boards appoint people to mark specific components of specific subjects for a series, with senior appointees who standardise and check other markers' work, and separate appointments for moderating work that schools assess internally. They are component-level roles rather than permanent titles. For a family, the practical point is that the role is narrow: somebody who marked one paper knows that paper very well and has no particular insight into the others, so the useful question is always which board, which subject and which component.

faqs.question: Should a Diploma Programme student change tutor between the first and second year?
faqs.answer: Not usually, and the exception is instructive. Keep the tutor if the first year went well and the diagnosis still holds, because continuity is worth a great deal in a two-year course. Change if the second year's demands sit outside what that tutor has actually taught: coursework supervision, the extension topics, or examination technique at the level the final papers require. The question to ask is whether they have taken students through the whole course before, not whether the first year was pleasant.

faqs.question: How is a tutor matched to a student in the first place, and what information decides it?
faqs.answer: Four things decide the shortlist: the exact course and level as the school writes it, the board and specification or subject guide, the fault if it is already known from marked work, and the hour that is genuinely free on Saudi local time. Preferences about teaching style, the tutor's gender or whether they are a serving teacher refine it from there. The hour is the piece families underestimate, because a scarce subject in a narrow evening window is a much smaller intersection than it looks.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor becomes unavailable part-way through a course?
faqs.answer: The handover is the thing that matters, and it should not be your job to perform it. The replacement needs the baseline document, the diagnosis, what has been covered, the recurring-error list and the current state of any coursework, which is exactly why those records are kept from the first session. A changeover with those in hand costs a session of settling. One without them costs several weeks, because the new tutor starts by rediscovering what the previous one already knew.

faqs.question: How does the academic honesty line differ between IGCSE coursework and a Diploma Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: The principle is identical — the submitted work must be the student's own — but the supervision structures differ. Diploma components sit inside a formal process with named supervisors, recorded meetings for the Extended Essay and a student reflection requirement. IGCSE coursework and practical write-ups are supervised by the subject teacher with less formal recording. The practical consequence is that a tutor's role is the same in both cases, while the documentation trail that would reveal substituted work is stronger in the Diploma than at IGCSE.

faqs.question: What may a tutor legitimately do with a Theory of Knowledge essay?
faqs.answer: They may discuss the prescribed title and what it is actually asking, challenge the claims and counterclaims the student has chosen, press on whether a chosen example genuinely supports the point, explain how the assessment instrument is structured, and teach the student to distinguish an argument from an assertion. They may not supply arguments, examples or text for the student to use as their own, and they may not restructure a draft. The distinction is between being questioned and being supplied, and a student notices which is happening.

faqs.question: How many drafts of an Extended Essay can a tutor legitimately read?
faqs.answer: Reading is not the constraint; contributing is. The school's own supervision structure limits the formal feedback a supervisor gives on full drafts, and an outside tutor works alongside that process rather than around it, which means the supervisor should know they are involved. A tutor can discuss the argument and identify which criterion is underserved as often as is useful, provided every change to the text is made by the student and reflects their own judgement rather than being transcribed from a correction.

faqs.question: Can a tutor proofread a Diploma Programme mathematics exploration before submission?
faqs.answer: They can tell a student that a section is unclear, that notation is inconsistent, or that a step is not justified, and the student then fixes it themselves. They cannot correct the document, rewrite passages or mark up a copy for transcription, because at that point the finished text reflects the tutor's judgement rather than the student's. The practical test is whether the student could explain each change and why they made it. If the answer is that somebody told them to, the line has been crossed.

faqs.question: What does a school do if it suspects an outside tutor contributed to assessed work?
faqs.answer: It follows its own malpractice process, which typically means investigating, interviewing the student, examining drafts and supervision records, and reporting to the board where appropriate. Outcomes range up to the loss of the component or the qualification. Detection is not primarily software: supervisors notice when a submitted text does not match a student's demonstrated ability, and the reflection and meeting records exist partly for that reason. This is the exposure a family accepts when a provider offers to handle a draft rather than discuss one.

ib-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Interview the tutor before you buy the term
ib-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Send the course exactly as the school writes it, the board and specification or subject guide, a recent piece of marked work, and the hour that is genuinely free on Saudi local time. We will put a specialist in front of your child for a free session, live over video, and you can ask the four questions: which components they teach, which topics exist only at the higher level, what the mark scheme does with weak working, and what gets set and marked between lessons. After three sessions you should hold a baseline, a diagnosis, a plan and a review date. If you do not, change the tutor rather than the plan.

intro.heading: What a near-me search is really asking for
paragraphs: A search for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Saudi Arabia is almost never about distance. Outside Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam–Khobar–Dhahran cluster there may be no one within an hour's drive who has taught Cambridge Extended Mathematics or IB Chemistry at Higher Level at all. Inside those cities a pool exists, but it is thin in exactly the subjects families need most, and it empties as a series approaches. So the question behind the query is availability and fit: is there a teacher free at seven in the evening on a Tuesday who knows this paper, this tier and this mark scheme?

Money comes first on this page because it is the thing most providers hide. Published Saudi figures fall into bands. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general private tuition in Riyadh at around SAR 50 an hour for primary and over SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. A tutoring-company listing advertises IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from about SAR 180, rising to roughly SAR 200 to 220 for Higher Level and Advanced Placement tracks. Budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one online from about SAR 35. Each of those is one provider's advertised rate. None is a market average and none is our price.

What moves a quoted figure, in rough order of weight: how scarce the subject specialist is, whether the tutor has marked for the board, the level, whether anyone has to travel, and how long the package runs. A Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches teacher at Higher Level costs more everywhere than a Standard Level one, because far fewer people can teach the Paper 3 extension material. Travel loading disappears when the lesson is online, which is why the same hour buys more actual teaching.

The middle of this page counts backwards. Almost every decision a family makes — when to start, how many lessons a week, whether to add a second subject, whether to argue about a tier — is set by how far the student sits from a series. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series, the main one for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series for resits and November-entry candidates. IB Diploma candidates at Saudi schools almost all sit the May session. Count back from whichever applies to your child.

Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video on Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is stated plainly because the alternative is a family waiting on somebody who was never coming. What online delivery buys is the thing a twenty-minute radius cannot: a specialist in the exact component your child is losing marks on, rather than whoever happens to live nearby and is willing.

ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover almost every request that reaches us from the Kingdom.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of subject courses examined by written papers, with coursework or alternative-to-practical options on some. Cambridge tiers many subjects: Core grading runs C to G, Extended A* to E. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 and does not tier most subjects.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools across the Kingdom run both boards, sometimes in one building for different subjects. Confirm the board, the tier and the component list with your school in writing, because a tier decision is reversible only before the entry deadline.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against published criteria rather than terminal papers, ending in the Personal Project. Subject grades run 1 to 7, built from criterion levels, so a student can know the content and still score poorly by missing what a criterion strand asks for.
programmes.countryNote: Some Saudi international schools run the Middle Years Programme to Year 11 and then the Diploma; others move students to IGCSE at Year 10. A family switching needs to know which, because the written-paper habit does not arrive on its own.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment carries real weight in every subject, and the core adds points through a matrix.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates at Saudi schools sit the May session, so the final year is short and front-loaded with internal assessment. A mid-course arrival into Riyadh, Jeddah or NEOM often lands with work already due against another school's deadlines.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and the Higher Level Paper 3 extension. Marks go on unjustified steps more often than on wrong answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-heavy questions. A procedural background loses the interpretation marks rather than the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Physics

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms. The data booklet is allowed and few students practise using it against the clock.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term precision decides the mark. Explain, outline and describe pay for different things, and students answer all three alike.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE)

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Sciences (IGCSE)

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (IGCSE)

sections.heading: What an IB or IGCSE tutor is advertised at across the Kingdom
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a straight price list, which is why a parent comparing providers ends up comparing marketing instead. The figures in the table are advertised rates taken from tutoring platforms, tutor-marketplace guides and tutoring-company listings aimed at Saudi families. They are what those providers say they charge. They are not a market average, they are not what IB Gram charges, and each should be read as a band with a reason attached rather than a number to haggle over.

Read down the column and the pattern is plain: the cheapest hour is a generalist and the dearest is a scarce specialist. A platform advertising IGCSE one-to-one from about SAR 35 an hour is not selling the same product as a listing quoting SAR 200 to 220 for a Higher Level track. The first buys supervision and company over homework. The second is meant to buy somebody who has taught the component and knows exactly what the mark scheme pays for.

In-home tuition also carries a travel loading that never shows up as its own line on a quote. A tutor crossing Riyadh for a five o'clock lesson commits two hours of their evening to earn one, and the quoted rate absorbs it. Online delivery removes that cost entirely, which matters twice over. The hour is cheaper to supply, and the pool you are choosing from stops being limited to the people who happen to live within comfortable driving distance of your own district.

sections.heading: Why the same subject is quoted at two different prices
paragraphs: Scarcity does most of the work. In any city on earth there are more people who can teach Mathematics at Standard Level than at Higher Level, and more who can teach Biology than Physics. In a Saudi school cluster that effect is sharper, because the cluster is small to begin with. A school that loses its one Higher Level Physics teacher mid-year has no bench, and every family in that cohort starts looking in the same fortnight. The rate for that subject moves because twenty parents are chasing the same handful of teachers.

Examiner experience is the second lever, and it is the one most often claimed and least often checked. A tutor who has marked a component knows what the band descriptors actually reward, which is not the same as knowing the content. Ask which board, which component and which years of marking, and ask what the most common reason for losing a mark on that paper is. Somebody who has marked it answers in specifics within a sentence. Somebody who has not talks about confidence and exam technique in general terms.

Level, travel and package length finish the picture. Higher Level costs more than Standard, Standard more than Middle Years Programme work, and all of them more than a general homework slot. A cheaper non-specialist is sometimes the right call: for organisation, for keeping a Year 10 student working steadily, for a subject the student is already passing comfortably. It is the wrong call for a Paper 3 problem or an internal assessment that has stalled, where the whole value is in knowing the component.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the series your child is sitting
paragraphs: Work from the series, not from the calendar on the wall. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series and a November series. June is the main sitting for schools in the Kingdom; November carries resits and November-entry candidates. Cambridge also runs a February and March series, but that one is for candidates in India, so a Saudi family plans around June and November only. IB Diploma candidates at Saudi schools almost all sit the May session, and your school's Diploma Programme coordinator holds the exact timetable.

The dates that actually bind a family are not the examination dates. They are the entry dates. Entries close several months ahead of the June series, and the tier decision on a Cambridge subject closes with them: a student entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C whatever happens in the room. If there is any argument to be had about moving a student from Core to Extended, it has to happen before that deadline, in writing, with the school. After it, the ceiling is fixed for the year.

Count back in blocks. Roughly two terms out is when content gaps can still be closed without cutting into revision. One term out, the work shifts towards full papers under timed conditions. Eight weeks out it is almost entirely technique: command terms, mark-scheme phrasing, and the discipline of reading how many marks a question carries before answering it. Three weeks out, adding a new subject rarely helps anybody, and a tutor who says otherwise is selling hours rather than teaching.

sections.heading: How to check a tutor knows this syllabus, not just the subject
paragraphs: A graduate in a subject is not automatically a teacher of a syllabus. The gap shows up fast under three questions. First: which syllabus code and which components does my child sit? Somebody who teaches this course answers without looking. Second: what is on the Higher Level extension that is not on Standard Level? That one separates a teacher of the course from somebody revising alongside the student. Third: show me a mark scheme and tell me why this answer scored four rather than six.

Trial lessons are where this gets decided, so use them properly. Send the tutor a question the student got wrong, with the student's own working, before the lesson. Then watch what happens. A specialist diagnoses the error rather than re-teaching the topic, names the component it would cost marks in, and sets one short piece of follow-up work. A generalist explains the topic again, more slowly, and the student leaves having understood the explanation without knowing what to do differently next time.

Be sceptical of anything numeric and unverifiable. A published success rate, a star rating or a headcount tells you nothing you can check, and this market is full of all three. What you can check is whether the tutor describes your child's actual paper correctly, whether they will put a written plan in front of you after the diagnostic session, and whether they say plainly what they cannot fix in the time available. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone offering one has told you something useful about themselves.

sections.heading: A Sunday-to-Thursday week with a tutor in another country
paragraphs: The school week here runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Most tutoring copy on the internet is written against a Monday-to-Friday assumption and quietly breaks when it meets this one. A Thursday evening in the Kingdom is the start of a weekend, not the end of a working week, so it is a poor slot for new content and a good one for a long paper. Sunday evening is the opposite: the student has school the next morning and tires early.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A tutor in India is two and a half hours ahead, which makes a seven o'clock lesson here half past nine at night for them. A tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, so a slot agreed in loose terms will drift twice a year unless it is pinned to Saudi local time in writing. Pin the slot to the student's clock, not the tutor's.

School timings shorten during Ramadan and evening study patterns change with them, which is a scheduling fact rather than a reason to stop. Families usually move the lesson later and shorten it. The long summer break and the autumn break are the other two interruptions worth planning for: a student in the Diploma's first year who stops entirely for ten weeks comes back with the internal assessment timeline moved against them, and recovering that costs more hours than keeping one fortnightly session would have.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: This matters more in IB and IGCSE than in most systems, because a real share of the grade is produced at home. An internal assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay, a Personal Project: all of them have to be the student's own work, and a school that suspects otherwise opens a malpractice process that can cost the qualification. The essay mills advertising in this market do not explain that part, and a family that buys from them is the one carrying the risk.

What a tutor may legitimately do is still substantial. They can teach the criteria so the student knows what each strand is paid for. They can discuss a research question and say honestly whether it is answerable in the word limit. They can read a draft the student wrote and give feedback on it, pointing at where an argument is unsupported or a method is not reproducible. They can teach referencing, and they can teach the data-handling the student needs to analyse their own results properly.

What no tutor here will do is produce the piece. We do not write, draft or complete any part of an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Personal Project, and a tutor asked to will refuse and say why. The line is simple enough to hold: the student's hands on the keyboard, the tutor's comments in the margin. Keep your own record of drafts and dates as you go, because that record is what answers a question later if one is ever asked.

sections.heading: After the papers: equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili
paragraphs: A certificate from an international school does not walk straight into a Saudi university. It needs an equivalency decision — mu'adalah — from the Ministry of Education before a university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. Start the question in the first year of the Diploma rather than after results, because the documents a family needs are easier to collect while the school is still in front of them.

Alongside that sit the two Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with these tests, and the weightings differ by university and by programme.

Tahsili is the one that catches international-curriculum students, and almost nobody writes about why. Its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. An IB or IGCSE student has usually met the material, but not in that framing, in that order or with that vocabulary. Tahsili preparation for international curriculum students is therefore a mapping job before it is a revision job. No tutor can promise an admission outcome, and we publish no cut-off numbers here: check the figures with the university itself, because they change.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE Extended Mathematics slot be held at the same evening time right through the autumn term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it should be. A fixed weekly slot lets a tutor track the school's scheme of work rather than react to whatever went wrong that week. Agree the time against Arabia Standard Time explicitly, so a tutor abroad changing their clocks does not move it. Most families settle on an early evening slot after the school run, adding a longer weekend session only in the final term.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly IGCSE lesson when the school day shortens during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School hours compress and evening routines shift, so most families move the lesson later and shorten it rather than cancelling. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so it lands at a different point in the course each time and the right adjustment depends on how close a series is. Agree the revised slot before the month starts and put the return date in writing.

faqs.question: If our tutor is in India, how early in the evening can a Sunday lesson realistically start here?
faqs.answer: India is two and a half hours ahead of Arabia Standard Time, so five in the afternoon here is half past seven there, and seven here is half past nine there. Early evening Saudi time is comfortable for both sides. Anything after about eight in the evening here pushes a tutor in India past half past ten, which is workable occasionally and poor as a weekly habit.

faqs.question: Our family lives in Al Khobar and the school is in Dhahran — does that commute change when a lesson should be booked?
faqs.answer: It changes the earliest workable start rather than anything else. The Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation behaves as one school market, and a crossing that takes twenty minutes mid-morning can take three times that at the end of the school day. Book the slot against the time your child is actually home and settled, and keep fifteen minutes of margin for a bad run.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the June series should an IGCSE Extended candidate move from one lesson a week to two?
faqs.answer: Roughly a term out, once whole papers rather than topics are the unit of work. Two sessions a week lets one be a timed paper and the other the follow-up on what it exposed, which is the pairing that moves marks. Earlier than that fills time with content the school is about to teach anyway. In the last three weeks there is no room left to act on what a paper exposes.

faqs.question: What transfers when a student leaves a Saudi national-curriculum school for Cambridge IGCSE in Year 10?
faqs.answer: The mathematics and science content transfers better than families expect; the assessment habits do not. Cambridge papers pay for command terms, structured working and a written register, so a student used to recall questions will know the material and still lose marks on how answers are built. Spend the first weeks on paper technique and the English demand of the subject papers. Ask the school in writing which tier it intends to enter.

faqs.question: Our child took Coordinated Sciences at IGCSE — what has to be rebuilt before Chemistry at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Coordinated Sciences compresses three subjects into fewer papers, so the chemistry is real but shallower where it matters later. Moles and stoichiometry, energetics, and the mechanism-level thinking behind organic reactions are the usual gaps. Bonding is normally covered, but not at the depth Higher Level questions assume. A sensible first term maps those areas against the Diploma syllabus and closes them, rather than restarting the course and arriving late everywhere.

faqs.question: We are arriving in NEOM part-way through the first Diploma year — what does catching up actually involve?
faqs.answer: Three separate jobs, in order. First, a syllabus comparison: what the previous school covered against what this one assesses, option topics included, because options differ between schools. Second, the internal assessment timeline, usually the urgent part, since the new school's deadlines will not match the old ones. Third, the teaching itself. Families who start with the teaching and find the assessment problem later lose the most time.

faqs.question: Is it realistic to move from the Middle Years Programme into IGCSE Extended one term late?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, with one caveat. The content overlap is good and a Middle Years Programme student is often strong at extended writing and investigation. What is missing is the terminal-paper habit: pacing, mark allocation, and answering the question asked rather than the topic it came from. That is trainable in a term if it starts at once. The caveat is the tier decision, which must be settled with the school before the entry deadline.

faqs.question: An American-curriculum student is joining a Cambridge school here — which IGCSE subjects are hardest to pick up late?
faqs.answer: Extended-tier Mathematics and the separate sciences are the usual difficulties, for different reasons. Extended Mathematics assumes algebraic fluency built over two years, and it shows immediately in the harder questions. The separate sciences go deeper than a general science course and carry practical or alternative-to-practical demands. Subjects assessed largely through extended writing transfer more easily, because the thinking is already there and only the paper conventions are new.

faqs.question: What does the first diagnostic lesson for a near-me IGCSE request actually cover?
faqs.answer: It works from evidence rather than conversation. The student brings a recent paper or test with the marks lost on it, and the tutor works through the errors rather than re-teaching topics. By the end there should be a written list of the components costing marks, ranked by how many each is worth, plus one short piece of follow-up work. A session that produces only reassurance has told you something.

faqs.question: How is the starting point reported back to a parent in the first month?
faqs.answer: After the diagnostic session you should have the written gap list and the order it will be worked through. After each lesson a short note says what was covered, what was set and what the student found hard. At about four weeks there should be a longer review saying whether the original diagnosis held, because a first assessment is sometimes wrong. Vague progress language instead of named components is the signal to ask harder questions.

faqs.question: What should a family do if the first tutor match is wrong after two lessons?
faqs.answer: Say so immediately and ask for a different specialist. A mismatch is usually about pace, personality or the student not speaking up, and none of those improves by waiting a month. Tell us what specifically did not work, because that is what makes the second match better than the first. Changing tutor early costs two lessons; changing tutor in the final term costs continuity when it matters most.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether to keep going after one term of weekly IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: Judge it against the gap list from the diagnostic rather than the last test score, because a single paper can swing on topic luck. Have the named components that were losing marks actually been closed, and is the student doing the follow-up work unprompted? If both are yes, continue and reduce frequency where a subject is now safe. If the components are unchanged after a term of steady attendance, change the approach rather than adding hours.

intro.heading: The hour has to exist before the teaching matters
paragraphs: Parents searching for an in-home Middle Years tutor in the Kingdom are solving a logistics problem. School finishes, the drive home takes what it takes, there is a younger sibling and a meal, and somewhere in what is left an eleven-to-sixteen-year-old has to concentrate for an hour. The honest reason families want somebody at the kitchen table is that it removes one journey from an evening that has no slack in it. That is a real constraint and it deserves a real answer rather than a sales line.

Here is what the in-home market actually involves in a Saudi city. The tutor has to live within driving distance, which means the choice is not everyone who teaches the subject but everyone who teaches it nearby. They have to cross a city that is an hour across in Riyadh traffic, or run the length of Jeddah's coastal spine, which is why in-home quotes carry a travel loading whether the quote itemises it or not. And because they travel, they can offer fewer hours a week, so the hours they do offer go to whoever books first.

IB Gram teaches this programme online, one-to-one, over live video, with the student's own work on a shared screen. We do not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The argument for teaching this way is not convenience, it is supply: the Middle Years Programme runs in a limited number of schools here, so the people who have marked work against its four published criteria are few and are already teaching full time in those schools. A family in Yanbu or Taif is not choosing between a video lesson and a local MYP specialist. They are choosing between a video lesson and nobody.

The rest of the page runs in the order the logistics run. First the Sunday-to-Thursday week and the window that genuinely exists inside it. Then Arabia Standard Time against a tutor's own clock and their own weekend, which is the thing that quietly breaks a weekly arrangement. Then who the tutor has to be for this programme and how a parent checks the claim, what a parent actually sees during an online MYP lesson, where marks go missing subject by subject, and how a slot survives breaks, Ramadan and a relocation.

Nothing here names a calendar year, because term dates belong to each school and a date printed on a page is wrong inside twelve months. Where the page refers to a reporting cycle or a break, it means your school's published one. The programme also has no external written papers unless a school opts into eAssessment, so progress is measured by the school's own criterion marks, cycle by cycle, rather than against a published grade boundary.

sections.heading: What an IB MYP home tutor search is really asking for
paragraphs: The literal request is somebody at the table at five o'clock. Underneath it are three separate questions: can anyone teach this programme near us, can they come at a time that exists in our evening, and do they know what the four criteria reward. In most Saudi cities the first two are in direct conflict. The people who have taught the Middle Years Programme are clustered around the schools that run it, and the hours they can offer shrink with every kilometre they have to drive.

So a family searching this phrase usually ends up with one of three outcomes. They find a university student who is comfortable with the content and has never seen a criterion descriptor. They find a genuine specialist whose only free slot is the one their child cannot use. Or they find nobody and conclude the programme is impossible to support from outside school, which is the most expensive conclusion of the three because it is wrong.

The answer this page argues for is a video lesson at a fixed hour, taught one-to-one by somebody matched to the subject group and the year. IB Gram does not send tutors to Saudi addresses; home visits are a service offered only in India. What a family gets instead is a wider pool and a slot that does not depend on traffic: a tutor who has marked MYP sciences against the investigation criteria, available at the hour the household actually has, every week, without a journey at either end.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and the window that genuinely exists
paragraphs: The school week here runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Any schedule imported from a British or Indian page is therefore wrong in both directions: it treats Sunday as a rest day and Friday as a school night. For a Middle Years student the practical consequence is that Sunday and Monday evenings are the strongest teaching slots of the week, Wednesday carries the heaviest homework load, and Thursday evening is the one everybody in the house wants to protect.

Inside each of those evenings the usable window is narrower than parents expect. An eleven-year-old is finished as a learner by about half past seven; a fifteen-year-old can work later but has more homework competing for the same hours. A sixty-minute lesson at the wrong end of the evening produces a tired student and a parent who concludes that tutoring does not work, when the real fault was the hour chosen. The school run is the variable nobody controls: a cross-city drive or a late bus can eat forty minutes of a window that was never longer than three hours.

The honest planning rule is to pick the hour the family can defend every single week, then build the teaching around it. Two shorter sessions suit the early years better than one long one; MYP 4 and 5 can hold a full hour and sometimes need ninety minutes before a summative task. Write the slot down, tell the school if it clashes with an activity, and treat changing it as a decision rather than a convenience.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against the tutor's own clock and weekend
paragraphs: The Kingdom keeps Arabia Standard Time at UTC+3 and does not change its clocks. A tutor in a country that does will therefore drift by an hour twice a year unless the booking is pinned to Saudi local time rather than theirs. That one administrative choice prevents the most common failure in this market, which is not a bad lesson but a missed one. Pin the booking once, in writing, and the lesson stops moving twice a year for reasons nobody in the house can see.

The second half of the problem is the tutor's week rather than their clock. A tutor whose other students are on a Monday-to-Friday timetable treats Sunday as a weekend day, so a Sunday evening slot in Riyadh is a deliberate commitment on their part. Ask directly whether the slot is standing or opportunistic, because a tutor who is quietly fitting a Saudi family around a British or Indian week will eventually have a conflict, and the family will lose the hour mid-term.

None of this is an argument against a tutor abroad. Most of the people who have marked against the MYP criteria work outside the Kingdom, and the time differences involved are small and manageable. It is an argument for settling the question before the first lesson: which clock the booking lives in, which days the tutor genuinely works, and what happens when their own public holidays land on a teaching day. Ask for the tutor's own term dates as well as the school's.

sections.heading: Who an MYP tutor has to be, and how a parent checks it
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme has no external written papers unless a school opts into eAssessment, and most schools in the Kingdom do not. That changes what a qualification means. There is no paper for a tutor to have marked for the board, so the usual shorthand of examiner experience does not transfer. The question becomes narrower and more answerable: has this person marked student work against the four published criteria, in this subject group, and can they describe what moves a four to a six.

A useful check takes four minutes. Ask which criterion the student is weakest on and why. Ask what the command term in their last task required. Ask how a criterion mark out of eight becomes a grade out of seven, and listen for whether they know that boundaries are applied by the school. A tutor who has taught the programme answers all three without hesitating; a strong subject teacher who has never taught it will answer the first and stumble on the rest.

Subject knowledge still matters, particularly in MYP 4 and 5 where extended mathematics and the sciences start to look like early sixth-form work. The order of priority is what changes: for this programme, criterion fluency first and content depth second, because a student who understands the material is usually losing marks on how the answer is built rather than on what it contains. Both matter, and a tutor who can manage only one of them is the wrong appointment for MYP 4 or MYP 5.

sections.heading: What a parent actually sees in an online MYP lesson
paragraphs: A lesson is a shared screen with the student's own work on it. The tutor annotates a science investigation, a mathematics write-up or a paragraph of analysis while talking it through, and the student types or writes alongside. Nothing about that requires a laptop with a graphics card; a laptop or a tablet with a keyboard, a decent connection and a quiet corner covers it. Headphones help more than a camera does.

Parents reasonably want to know what oversight looks like. A session ends with a short written note: what was covered, which criterion it was aimed at, and what the student should do before the next one. A parent is welcome at the start and the end of a lesson, and for younger students it helps if somebody checks in briefly; sitting through the whole hour usually makes an eleven-year-old perform rather than think. If the connection drops, the lesson resumes or is rescheduled, not written off. Whether a session is recorded is a question to settle before the first one: ask what is kept and who can see it.

The practical difference from a lesson at the kitchen table is that everything is recorded in writing rather than in a doorstep conversation. The marked work, the note, the criterion aimed at and the task set are all on the screen or in the inbox. Over a term that paper trail is what lets a parent judge whether the hour is worth keeping, which is a harder judgement to make from impressions alone.

sections.heading: Where MYP marks actually go missing, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: In the sciences the marks are in the investigation, not the knowledge. A student with a good grasp of the topic routinely loses a band for a hypothesis that is not testable, for variables that are listed rather than controlled, or for an evaluation that says the experiment went well instead of identifying what the method could not rule out. None of that is content teaching, and none of it is fixed by reading the textbook again. It is diagnosable from one marked investigation, which is why a first session should use a real piece of the student's own work.

In mathematics the loss splits by year. Early on it is arithmetic and algebraic fluency, which surfaces later as an inability to generalise a pattern into a rule. In MYP 4 and 5 it is the investigation criteria: finding the pattern is only part of the task, and the marks sit in justifying the general rule and explaining the reasoning in writing. Extended mathematics adds material that standard does not cover, which matters for anyone heading towards Analysis and Approaches.

In language and literature, strong readers retell. The criteria pay for explaining how a text produces an effect, with evidence chosen for that purpose. Individuals and societies fails in the same way: the source is described rather than weighed for origin, purpose and limitation. In both, the fix is a short cycle of write, mark against the descriptor, rewrite - which is exactly what an hour a week is for.

sections.heading: Holding the slot through breaks, Ramadan and a move
paragraphs: A Middle Years student may be with the same tutor for several years, so continuity is the thing worth protecting. Public schools in the Kingdom run two semesters from late August to late June with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break, while most international and British-curriculum schools run three terms on calendars they set themselves. Term dates therefore differ school by school within one city, and a tutor working with several families cannot assume them.

School days shorten during Ramadan and the household's evening pattern shifts with them, which usually means moving the lesson rather than pausing it. The long summer is the opposite problem: a family that stops entirely in June often finds the slot gone in September, because the tutor filled it. A reduced summer pattern of one session a fortnight keeps the slot, keeps the relationship and costs a fraction of the term-time arrangement. A tutor working with several Saudi families keeps a note of each school's own dates rather than assuming one calendar for the city.

Relocation inside the Kingdom changes nothing about a video lesson: the tutor, the hour and the plan survive a move from Jeddah to Riyadh, because Arabia Standard Time applies in both. What changes is the school, and that is worth one session of its own - a new unit sequence, different criterion emphasis, sometimes a different mathematics route. Send the new school's unit outlines to the tutor before the first lesson in the new city.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor need to have marked against the four criteria, or is subject knowledge enough?
faqs.answer: For this programme, criterion experience comes first. A tutor who knows the subject but not the criteria will teach content the student may already have and leave the marks where they were. Someone who has marked against the descriptors can look at a task and say which band the work sits in and what moves it up. Ask them to do exactly that with a recent piece during the trial lesson, and the answer is obvious within ten minutes.

faqs.question: There are no external MYP papers, so what does examiner experience mean for a Middle Years tutor?
faqs.answer: Very little, and a tutor who leans on the phrase at this level is borrowing credibility from the Diploma. Unless a school has opted into eAssessment there is no external paper to have marked. The equivalent credential here is classroom and moderation experience: has this person taught MYP units, marked summative tasks against the published criteria, and sat in a standardisation meeting where two teachers disagreed about a band. That is the claim worth checking.

faqs.question: Should an MYP 5 student have a different tutor from an MYP 2 one in the same subject?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. MYP 2 work is about building habits: reading a question properly, laying out method, writing a conclusion that answers something. MYP 5 work is close to early sixth-form material, with extended mathematics and sciences that reward depth. Tutors tend to be strong at one end or the other, and the gentlest teacher for an eleven-year-old is not always the person who can push a sixteen-year-old towards a seven.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor knows my child's school's MYP unit plans rather than the subject in general?
faqs.answer: Send them the unit overview and the task sheet before the trial lesson and watch what they do with it. A tutor who knows the programme will name the criteria the task is assessed against, point out the command terms, and ask which parts the class has already covered. One who does not will talk about the topic. Schools write their own units inside the framework, so this is a real check rather than a formality.

faqs.question: Our MYP tutor is leaving mid-unit - what should the handover to a new one contain?
faqs.answer: Four things: the school's unit overview and upcoming task sheet, the last two marked pieces with the criterion marks visible, the notes from recent sessions, and a short summary of which criterion the student is weakest on. With those, a new tutor loses one session rather than a month. Without them the replacement starts with a diagnostic the family has already paid for once, which is the avoidable cost of a bad handover.

faqs.question: What does an online MYP lesson look like from a 12-year-old's side of the screen?
faqs.answer: Their own work, large, on a shared screen, with the tutor's annotations appearing as they talk. The student writes or types alongside rather than watching. Good lessons at this age run in short moves: read the question, attempt a step, check it, move on, with the tutor stopping to mark aloud. A laptop or a tablet with a keyboard, headphones and a quiet corner are all the equipment needed.

faqs.question: How does a tutor work on an MYP science investigation write-up on a shared screen?
faqs.answer: Section by section, in the order the criteria are marked. The hypothesis is tested for whether it can actually be disproved, the variables are sorted into controlled and measured, the processed data is checked for whether it answers the question asked, and the evaluation is pushed from what went wrong to what the method could not rule out. The student edits their own document throughout; the tutor comments and teaches.

faqs.question: What does a parent receive after each online MYP session?
faqs.answer: A short written note naming what was covered, which criterion it was aimed at, what the student did well and what they should do before the next lesson. Marked work comes back with the descriptor beside it, so the band is explained rather than asserted. Over a term those notes become the evidence for deciding whether the hour is worth keeping, which is far more reliable than a weekly impression.

faqs.question: Can two siblings in different MYP years share one online session?
faqs.answer: It rarely works well. Two years apart in the Middle Years means different units, different criteria emphasis and different attention spans, so an hour split between them gives each child half a lesson aimed at the wrong level. Where a family wants to reduce cost, two shorter separate sessions usually buy more progress than one shared hour. Siblings in the same year group and subject group are a different case and can sometimes work.

faqs.question: How does a tutor hold a 13-year-old's attention for a full hour on video?
faqs.answer: By making the student do the work rather than watch it. The pattern that holds attention is short cycles: a question attempted, a mistake found, a correction made, with the tutor's screen showing the student's own writing. Silence while a student thinks is part of the lesson. Where attention genuinely will not stretch, two half-hour sessions a week beat one long hour, and that is worth saying out loud rather than pushing through.

faqs.question: Which MYP mathematics topics most often need teaching from outside school?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation in the early years, then the shift from spotting a pattern to justifying a general rule in MYP 4 and 5. The investigation criteria catch students out because finding the rule is only part of the task; the marks sit in the reasoning written around it. Extended mathematics adds content that standard does not cover, and a student heading towards Analysis and Approaches needs that gap closed before the Diploma starts.

faqs.question: Why do strong readers lose marks on MYP language and literature criterion tasks?
faqs.answer: Because the criteria pay for analysis and strong readers deliver retelling. A student who has understood a text well will often write a fluent account of what happens in it, choose evidence that proves the events, and score in the middle band. The marks are in explaining how the writing produces an effect on a reader, with evidence selected for that purpose. The fix is a short write, mark against the descriptor, rewrite cycle.

faqs.question: What goes wrong in MYP individuals and societies source-based work?
faqs.answer: Students describe sources instead of weighing them. A full-band answer treats origin, purpose and limitation as part of the argument, and uses one source against another rather than listing both. The second common loss is a conclusion that restates the question. Both are structural problems with how the answer is built, which is why one marked attempt rewritten teaches more than another hour of reading around the topic.

faqs.question: Which MYP sciences skills show up as a problem only in MYP 4 and 5?
faqs.answer: Data processing and evaluation. In the early years an investigation can score well on a clear method and a tidy table, but the later criteria expect calculated uncertainty, a graph chosen deliberately, and an evaluation that identifies the limitation the method could not remove. Students who were comfortable in MYP 2 often drop a band or two here without their content knowledge changing at all, which is why the diagnosis matters.

If the hour cannot hold every week, we will say so and suggest a different one rather than selling you a slot that falls apart in the second month.

intro.heading: The same hour is worth different amounts in different months
paragraphs: Most pages about Middle Years tutoring price an hour as though an hour were a fixed thing. It is not. A criterion band is a judgement a teacher makes from a body of work gathered across a reporting cycle, so an hour spent eight weeks before that judgement can change what the teacher sees, and an hour spent the week after it cannot. Any honest discussion of value for money in this programme has to start with the calendar, which is why this page is built around it rather than around a price list.

The second thing worth knowing is that Middle Years support is genuinely cheaper than Diploma support, and families are often surprised by that. Level is one of the strongest drivers of an advertised rate in this market: Higher Level above Standard Level, Standard Level above the Middle Years Programme, with IGCSE somewhere alongside. A tutoring platform here advertises general online tutoring from about SAR 55 an hour, and IB subject tutoring in Riyadh is listed by tutoring companies from around SAR 180. A Middle Years subject group sits lower than a Diploma Higher Level subject because the content ceiling is lower and more teachers can reach it.

That makes the scarce resource time rather than money. A family can afford more weeks of Middle Years teaching than Diploma teaching for the same budget, which is an argument for starting early and spending less per month over a longer run. The common mistake is the opposite: wait until the final report of MYP 5 looks wrong, then buy an intensive block that cannot touch the judgements already made. The arithmetic is worth doing once on paper, because a fortnightly hour across four reporting cycles costs less than six weeks of intensive support and it arrives while the evidence is still being gathered. Nothing about that is a special offer; it is simply where the leverage sits in a programme with no external papers.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with the student's own marked work on a shared screen. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For this programme the online route is less a compromise than a widening of the pool, because the Middle Years Programme runs in a limited set of Saudi schools and the people who have marked against its criteria are mostly teaching in them.

No calendar year appears anywhere on this page. Where it refers to a reporting cycle, a summative task or a break, it means your school's own published one, because international and British-curriculum schools here set their own calendars and the dates differ school by school inside a single city.

sections.heading: Where the year has reached, and what an hour can still change
paragraphs: A criterion grade is not a test score. A teacher gathers evidence across a reporting cycle and makes a judgement against published descriptors, which means the useful question for a parent is not how good the tutor is but how much evidence is still to be collected. Eight weeks before a report, almost all of it. One week after, none of it. The price per hour does not move across that range but the value does, by a factor nobody advertises.

This is why the first conversation should be about dates rather than rates. Which reporting cycle is running, which summative tasks fall inside it, and how much of the subject's assessment is still ahead. A family that knows those three things can tell whether they are buying a changed grade, better work habits for the next cycle, or reassurance. All three are legitimate purchases; only the first is what most families think they are paying for. Ask the programme coordinator for the assessment schedule if the school does not publish it: most will send it, and it turns a guess into a plan.

The table sets the year out as a sequence of decisions. It names no months and no calendar year on purpose, because international schools here set their own three-term calendars while public schools run two semesters from late August to late June, so the same week of the Gregorian year is a different point in the cycle depending on the school. Read it against your own school's published calendar and the spending decision usually makes itself.

sections.heading: What Middle Years teaching is advertised at, and why it is cheaper than Diploma support
paragraphs: The published numbers in this market are easy to find and hard to compare, because each one describes a different product. A tutoring platform advertises general online tutoring from about SAR 55 an hour. Budget platforms list IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general private tuition in Riyadh at about SAR 50 for primary and over SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring companies list IB subject tutoring in Riyadh from about SAR 180, with Higher Level premium tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220.

Middle Years work sits below the Diploma figures and above the general ones, and the reason is supply. Scarcity is the strongest driver of price in this market, followed by marking experience and then level. There is no external paper in this programme for a tutor to have marked, so the premium that examiner experience commands at Diploma level does not apply in the same way, and the pool of teachers comfortable with MYP content is wider than the pool comfortable with Higher Level mathematics.

Two cautions about every figure above. They are advertised rates published by providers, not an average of what families pay and not our price, so treat them as a floor that marketing has chosen rather than as evidence. And a rate advertised from a low number is the starting point for the cheapest subject at the lowest level; the figure for extended mathematics in MYP 5 on the same site will be higher. Ask what the rate is for your child's exact subject group and year before comparing anything.

sections.heading: The opening cycle: buying a baseline instead of a diagnosis
paragraphs: At the start of a cycle the cheapest useful purchase is a baseline, and the school has already produced one. The previous report carries criterion marks out of eight for every subject group, and the marked tasks behind them are usually still in the student's folder. Those two documents let a tutor arrive knowing what to work on, which removes the diagnostic session a family would otherwise pay for. Send the folder before the first session rather than after it, because a tutor who has read it arrives with a question instead of a questionnaire.

What a first session should then produce is narrow and written: which criterion is weakest, what in the student's own work shows it, and what the next four weeks will do about it. A parent who has that in writing can measure the arrangement against it at the next reporting cycle rather than relying on the feeling that lessons are going well. It also gives the school something concrete if the family wants to ask about placement or set.

Starting here is also where the long-run economics sit. A weekly hour across two cycles costs more in total than a block before a deadline but less per band moved, because the work compounds and because the tutor is teaching into a cycle rather than against it. Families who can only fund one or the other usually get more from the early steady hour than from the late intensive one, even when the late block feels more urgent at the time.

sections.heading: Mid-cycle: timing a block so a practice attempt still counts
paragraphs: The highest-value booking in this programme is a short block placed four to six weeks before a summative task. That is long enough for the student to attempt the task once, have it marked against the actual criterion descriptors, see where the band sits, and rewrite it before the real submission. Any closer and there is no time for the rewrite, which is the part that moves marks.

What that block costs depends on the subject group rather than on the tutor's enthusiasm. A science investigation takes two sessions and a marking turnaround. An extended written task in individuals and societies takes three, because the argument has to be rebuilt rather than corrected. A mathematics investigation in MYP 4 or 5 often takes two plus a check on the general rule and its justification. Ask for the number of sessions before agreeing a block, and ask what happens if the task is set earlier than expected. Blocks that ignore the marking turnaround are the commonest waste in this market.

The common mistake is booking by month rather than by task. A family buys four hours in a convenient fortnight, the school sets the summative task a week later, and the hours have been spent on content while the assessed work goes in unrehearsed. Send the tutor the school's assessment schedule for the cycle at the start and the block places itself without anyone having to guess. A tutor who asks for that schedule before quoting is telling you something useful about how they work.

sections.heading: MYP 5 and the handover: what cannot be bought late
paragraphs: The final Middle Years year carries decisions rather than examinations. Whether a student takes extended or standard mathematics shapes what they can pick up in the Diploma, particularly Analysis and Approaches. The Personal Project runs alongside everything else and is supervised at school. And the final report is the document a sixth form reads, whether that is the Diploma at the same school, a Cambridge route elsewhere in the city, or a school in another country entirely.

What money cannot buy at this stage is the evidence the report is built from, because it has already been gathered. What it can buy is readiness for whatever comes next: closing the extended mathematics gap before the Diploma starts, learning to write under timed conditions for a Cambridge sixth form, or building the independent research habits that an Extended Essay will later demand. Those are real purchases, but they are purchases about next year rather than this one, and a provider who blurs the two is selling hope.

On the Personal Project the line is strict and worth stating plainly. A tutor may discuss the topic, teach the planning and research skills, ask hard questions about the process journal, and give feedback on what the student has produced. Nobody may draft, write or produce any part of it for them. That is not a policy we invented; it is what the programme requires, and a provider offering anything else is selling a malpractice risk with a tutoring label on it.

sections.heading: Auditing the tutor you are already paying for
paragraphs: Value in this programme is auditable, which is unusual and worth using. After four sessions a parent should be able to point at three things: the criterion the lessons are aimed at, the student's own work showing movement on it, and the school's marking agreeing or disagreeing. If all three exist, the arrangement is working. If only the tutor's own enthusiasm exists, it is not, and another month will not change that.

Two cheap checks make the audit easy. Ask the tutor, without warning, which criterion the last piece of work was weakest on and why - a tutor who is teaching the programme answers in one sentence. Then look at the written notes from the last four sessions and see whether they name tasks and criteria or only describe topics covered. Notes that could have been written about any student are a sign that one tutor is carrying more families than they can hold in mind.

Changing tutor mid-cycle is cheaper than most families fear if the handover is right: the unit overview, the last two marked pieces, the session notes, and one line on the weakest criterion. That is a single session of lost time rather than a month. Nobody should pay twice for the same diagnosis, and a provider that cannot hand a student over without repeating it has organised itself around its own convenience. Ask for the handover in writing and keep a copy yourself, because it is your child's record rather than the provider's.

sections.heading: What an online hour contains, and what you should not be billed for
paragraphs: A lesson is the student's own work on a shared screen, annotated live while they work alongside. For a design cycle project that means the documentation open beside the product; for a science investigation, the processed data and the evaluation; for language and literature, a paragraph being rebuilt sentence by sentence. A laptop or a tablet with a keyboard, headphones and a quiet corner are enough, and a camera matters less than a stable connection.

Three things should come with the hour rather than as extras: work set and checked between sessions, a short written note naming the criterion aimed at, and marked work returned with the descriptor beside it. Past tasks, mark schemes and practice material are part of teaching, not a product to be sold separately. If a provider itemises those, the hourly rate is not the real rate and the comparison a family thought they were making was never valid. Ask what is included before the first invoice rather than after the second one.

What a fee cannot include is any claim about an outcome. No tutor can promise a band, a grade or a place at a particular sixth form, because the judgement belongs to the school and the evidence belongs to the student. The honest version is that teaching makes more marks available from the same understanding, and that is checkable against the school's own marking at the end of every cycle. What a fee can include is evidence, cycle by cycle, which is the only promise worth having.
