faqs.question: Is a qualified MYP teacher worth twice the rate of a university student for an MYP 2 child?
faqs.answer: For content help in the early years, often not. A capable graduate can take a thirteen-year-old through mathematics or a science topic perfectly well. The difference appears the moment the work is assessed, because a criterion band is awarded against descriptors a graduate has never read. A reasonable compromise is a cheaper tutor for weekly maintenance plus one experienced session before each summative task, which buys the expensive judgement only where it changes the mark.

faqs.question: What should the first written report from an MYP tutor contain before we pay for a second month?
faqs.answer: Four things. The criterion the lessons are aimed at, named exactly as the school's descriptor names it. Evidence from the student's own work showing where the band sits. What has been taught, in specifics rather than topics. And what the student should do before the next session. A report that describes attitude and effort without naming a criterion tells you nothing you could not see at home for free.

faqs.question: How many students can one MYP tutor carry before the notes stop being specific?
faqs.answer: There is no published number and anyone quoting one is guessing, but the symptom is easy to spot. When session notes could be swapped between two students without anyone noticing, the tutor is working from memory rather than from the work. Ask to see the last three notes for your own child and look for named tasks, named criteria and quoted sentences from their writing. Specificity is the only test that matters here.

faqs.question: Can we change MYP tutor after two sessions without losing the term's plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the handover carries the unit overview, the last two marked pieces, the session notes and one line on the weakest criterion. That is a single lost session rather than a lost month. No family should pay twice for the same diagnosis, so ask before starting what happens to the written plan if the match turns out to be wrong. A provider that cannot answer has not thought about it.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor need to have taught in a Saudi school to be useful to us?
faqs.answer: No, but they do need to understand two things about the setting: the week runs Sunday to Thursday, and term dates come from your school rather than from a national calendar. Beyond that, what matters is whether they have taught and marked this programme. Local knowledge helps with context such as which schools run which subject groups, and that is useful background rather than a qualification.

faqs.question: Does an online MYP lesson need a laptop, or will the school tablet do?
faqs.answer: A school tablet works if it has a keyboard and the student can open their own documents on it. Without a keyboard, writing tasks become painful and the lesson turns into dictation. For mathematics and sciences a larger screen helps, because the tutor's annotations and the student's working need to be visible at the same time. Headphones matter more than a camera, and a wired connection matters more than either.

faqs.question: How is a design cycle project shared and discussed in an online lesson?
faqs.answer: The documentation goes on the shared screen and the product is shown to the camera or photographed into the document. Lessons follow the cycle: the investigation is checked for a real research base, the design brief for specifications that can actually be tested, and the evaluation for honest testing against those specifications. Since the written cycle carries much of the assessment, most of the hour is spent on the document rather than on the making.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor set and check work between MYP lessons?
faqs.answer: Work is set at the end of the session in writing, usually one task rather than a list, and submitted as a document or photograph before the next lesson. The tutor marks it against the relevant descriptor and returns it with the criterion wording beside the comments. That marking is part of the hour's value, not an add-on, and a family should check at the start whether it is included or billed separately.

faqs.question: What happens to an online MYP lesson if the student has no quiet room that evening?
faqs.answer: Move the lesson rather than teaching through the noise. A thirteen-year-old working at a kitchen table during a family evening will spend the hour managing interruptions, and the session produces nothing worth the fee. Where a quiet room is genuinely never available, an earlier slot before the household fills up usually works better than a later one, and headphones with a microphone make a surprising difference.

faqs.question: How is progress tracked across a whole MYP unit online?
faqs.answer: Against the unit's own assessed tasks rather than against a weekly feeling. At the start, the unit overview shows which criteria the unit will be marked on. Each session note records what was taught and which criterion it served. The marked practice attempt gives a band before the real submission, and the school's own mark closes the loop. Four documents, all of which a parent can keep and read.

faqs.question: Which MYP language acquisition problems need teaching from outside school?
faqs.answer: Phase placement first. A student put into a phase above or below their real level will either drift or drown, and neither shows clearly in a single report. After that, the usual gap is productive work: listening and speaking carry real weight in this subject group, and most home practice is reading. One diagnostic session that produces written evidence a parent can take to the school is often worth more than a term of general practice.

faqs.question: Why do capable students score poorly on the MYP design cycle documentation?
faqs.answer: Because they build first and write afterwards. The criteria reward an investigation that informs the design, specifications that can be tested, and an evaluation measured against those specifications. A student who makes something impressive and then writes a justification backwards loses marks in several criteria at once. The fix is sequencing rather than effort: write the brief before building, and test against what was actually written down.

faqs.question: What goes wrong in the MYP arts process journal?
faqs.answer: It gets treated as a scrapbook. The journal is assessed evidence of developing thinking, so it needs reflection on what was tried, what failed and what changed as a result, with references to the artists or practitioners behind each decision. A beautiful final piece with a thin journal scores below a modest piece with a rigorous one, which students find hard to believe until they see the descriptors side by side.

faqs.question: Which part of MYP physical and health education is actually assessed in writing?
faqs.answer: Planning for performance and reflection, both of which are written criteria. A capable athlete can score in the middle band because the training plan has no measurable targets or the reflection lists what happened without analysing it. This is the clearest example in the programme of a grade that content knowledge cannot fix, and it is usually a one-session problem rather than a term-long one.

ib-myp-online-tutor.closingHeading: Tell us where the year has got to
ib-myp-online-tutor.closingBody: Send the last report, two marked tasks and the school's assessment schedule for this cycle, and the spending decision becomes straightforward: which subject group, how many sessions, and where in the cycle they should sit. We will match a tutor who has marked against those criteria, pin the slot to Arabia Standard Time, and start with a free trial lesson on work your school has already marked. If the cycle is too far gone for the hour to change this report, we will say so and plan for the next one.

ib-myp-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched by subject group and by year, because MYP 2 and MYP 5 are different jobs. One teaches sciences against Criterion B and C for a student whose investigations keep losing marks; another takes language and literature in MYP 4; another supervises nothing and teaches everything behind a Personal Project.

intro.heading: Parents compare the MYP with something, and the comparison is usually wrong
paragraphs: Almost every family who asks about Middle Years Programme tutoring in the Kingdom is weighing it against something else. Against Cambridge IGCSE, which their neighbour's children sit at the same ages. Against the national curriculum, which has public examinations and a familiar shape. Against the American middle school they moved from, which had grade point averages and tests they recognised. The comparison matters because it drives the question they actually ask, which is usually some version of whether their child is behind.

The honest answer is that the MYP is not measured on the same axis, so the question cannot be answered in those terms. There are no external papers in the programme unless the school opts into eAssessment, and most Saudi schools do not. A student is assessed against four published criteria in every subject, each marked out of eight, and converted to a grade from one to seven by boundaries the school applies. A parent looking for a percentage finds a Criterion C mark of five and has no idea whether that is good.

So this page starts by setting the MYP against the alternatives properly: what each actually assesses, what each prepares a student for, and what a family gains and gives up by being in one rather than the other. That comparison is also the most useful diagnostic available, because once a parent understands what the criteria reward, a mark that looked arbitrary becomes legible and a specific weakness becomes visible.

The second half of the page runs the MYP year backwards, from the handover into the Diploma or a British sixth form at the end of MYP 5 to the first reporting cycle of MYP 1. No year is named anywhere here, because term dates and reporting cycles belong to each school and a date on a page goes stale; the order is what matters, and the order does not change. Deciding where in that order a family currently sits is what determines whether support changes anything.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, with the work on a shared screen. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For the MYP that is less of a compromise than it sounds, because the scarce thing is not proximity but a teacher who has marked against these criteria before, and in many Saudi cities only a handful of schools run the programme at all. A family in Tabuk or Abha looking for someone who has assessed MYP sciences against Criterion B is not choosing between an online tutor and a local one; they are choosing between an online tutor and nobody. Even in Riyadh and Jeddah, where the programme is better established, the people who know it are teaching it full time in the schools that run it.

ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: The programme is usually discussed as a single thing and behaves as four. The early years build habits, MYP 4 and 5 make decisions, the Personal Project runs alongside them, and then the whole thing hands over to a sixth-form route that assesses differently. Support is worth different amounts in each.

programmes.name: MYP 1 to 3, the habit-building years
programmes.description: Eight subject groups taught through units framed by a key concept, a global context and a statement of inquiry. Assessment is against the four criteria from the start, with no external examination at any point. The skills being built are investigation, structured writing, method, and the ability to reflect on a process rather than only report a result.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom these years are where mid-course arrivals land most often, because families relocate and a child joins MYP 2 or MYP 3 from a national-curriculum, Indian or American school. The content gap is usually narrow. The criterion gap is wide, and nobody explains it to the family, so the first set of reported marks reads as a shock.

programmes.name: MYP 4 and 5, the decision years
programmes.description: The same criteria applied at a higher standard, with mathematics splitting into standard and extended routes and sciences sometimes taught as separate disciplines. Subject choices made at the end of MYP 5 shape the Diploma or a British sixth form, and those choices rest on criterion marks rather than on examination results.
programmes.countryNote: This is where most Saudi families start looking for a tutor, often because a Criterion D mark has not moved for two reporting cycles. It is also the point at which the extended mathematics decision is made, and that decision quietly determines how comfortable Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level will be two years later.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent piece of work assessed against three criteria: planning, applying skills, and reflecting. The product itself is not what earns the marks. The process does, which means the goal, the success criteria the student sets, the evidence of skills applied, and the quality of the reflection in the report. Schools supervise it formally.
programmes.countryNote: The project is the item that catches Saudi families by surprise, particularly where a long school commute leaves only fragments of weekday time for work that needs sustained independent planning. Weekend mornings are free here, and they are the right place for it. A tutor may teach the skills and question the plan, and may not write any part of it.

programmes.name: After MYP 5: the Diploma, or IGCSE and A Levels
programmes.description: The Diploma adds six subjects at once, internal assessment in almost every one, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. A British sixth form narrows instead, to three or four A Levels, usually after IGCSE. The MYP prepares a student well for the first and leaves a gap in examination technique relevant to the second.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Saudi school that runs the MYP also runs the Diploma, so some families move schools at this point and a few move cities. A student switching from the MYP into a British route meets timed written papers as a new experience, and that transition is worth a term of deliberate preparation rather than an assumption.

ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP subjects are assessed by subject group, each with four criteria that are published and that a school marks against directly. Knowing which criterion a student is losing marks on is more useful than knowing the topic, because the criteria are where the teaching has to happen.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · standard and extended in MYP 4 and 5
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Most students score adequately on A and lose marks on B and D, because investigating a pattern requires generalising and justifying rather than calculating, and the real-life context criterion wants interpretation of a result rather than another answer.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Criterion B fails on variables that are not properly controlled or a method that cannot be repeated; Criterion C fails on data presented without analysis of trends or discussion of reliability.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. The characteristic loss is in analysing, where students summarise content rather than examining how a writer's choices create an effect for a particular audience, and in using language, where register and accuracy are marked separately from ideas.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · phases 1 to 6
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing, each as its own criterion, assessed within a phase rather than a year group. A student can be strong in reading and weak in speaking and receive a middling overall grade that hides both. Phase placement matters more than age, and families are rarely told which phase their child is in.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Thinking critically is the criterion that separates grades: it wants evaluation of sources, recognition of different perspectives and a judgement that is argued rather than asserted. Content recall alone caps a student well below the top bands.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. Students who build something impressive and document it thinly lose heavily, because three of the four criteria assess the process around the product. The design folder is the assessed artefact as much as the solution itself.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.levels: Criteria A to D · visual, music, drama
subjects.description: Investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. As in design, process documentation carries much of the mark, and the developmental workbook is examined rather than decorative. Students arriving from systems where art was graded on the finished piece find this the hardest adjustment in the subject.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting and improving performance. It is a written as well as a practical subject, and a capable athlete can score poorly by neglecting the planning and reflection components entirely, which surprises families every reporting cycle.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Units that combine two or more subject groups and are assessed against their own criteria, including the ability to synthesise disciplinary knowledge. They are often the least prepared-for assessment in the programme, because they do not belong to a single teacher and students treat them as a side project.

subjects.name: Approaches to Learning
subjects.description: The skill framework running underneath the whole programme: research, communication, thinking, social and self-management skills. It is not separately graded, but it is what the criteria actually measure in practice, which is why a student with weak organisation loses marks in every subject at once rather than in one.

ib-myp-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: Because most families weighing MYP support are also weighing the British route, here is what the alternative looks like at the same ages. These are the Cambridge codes a Year 10 or 11 student in a Saudi British-curriculum school would sit instead.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: Two timed written papers at the entered tier, one without a calculator, graded A* to G. Compared with MYP mathematics it tests speed and accuracy under time rather than investigation and communication, and the tier chosen by the school caps the grade available.

igcseSubjects.name: Coordinated Sciences 0654
igcseSubjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics examined together, with a practical component taken as a test or a written alternative paper. The practical assessment is externally marked rather than teacher-assessed against criteria, which is the sharpest difference from MYP sciences.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English 0500
igcseSubjects.description: Reading, directed writing and composition under timed conditions. An MYP student moving into this course usually has stronger analytical habits and weaker examination timing, because the MYP rarely requires a complete response in an hour without notes.

igcseSubjects.name: Global Perspectives 0457
igcseSubjects.description: Research, collaboration and individual report work, which is the closest the Cambridge suite comes to the MYP's interdisciplinary and project assessment. Families moving between systems often find this the easiest transfer of skills in either direction.

igcseSubjects.name: ICT 0417
igcseSubjects.description: A theory paper plus practical document and data tasks completed at a computer. It contrasts usefully with MYP Design, where the process folder is assessed; here the output is marked against a specification and the process is not examined.

igcseSubjects.name: History 0470 and Geography 0460
igcseSubjects.description: Source analysis, case studies and timed extended writing. The MYP equivalent, Individuals and Societies, builds the same critical thinking but assesses it through longer coursework-style tasks, so the gap on transfer is examination stamina rather than understanding.

ib-myp-tutor.regionsTitle: Where the MYP is actually taught in the Kingdom
ib-myp-tutor.regionsIntro: The programme is not evenly distributed. A few Saudi cities have several schools running the full continuum, many have one, and some have none within reach. That distribution shapes what a family's realistic options are, including whether changing school at the end of MYP 5 means changing city.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The widest choice in the Kingdom, including schools running the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes in sequence. A family here can usually stay in one institution from primary to the Diploma, which removes the handover problem that forces moves elsewhere.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long-established international market along the coastal spine, with several schools appearing in IB listings alongside strong British, American, German and Indian provision. Families often choose between a continuum school and a British-curriculum one at the MYP 4 point rather than at the start.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST campus
regions.note: A campus community north of Jeddah with its own school serving university families. Cohorts are small, which has the usual two-sided effect: a great deal of individual attention, and a narrow set of subject options once students reach the upper MYP years.

regions.name: Dhahran, Dammam and Al Khobar
regions.note: One school market across three cities, with Diploma provision concentrated in Dhahran and British-curriculum schools alongside it. A student in the MYP here may be the only one in their street doing it, with neighbours on an entirely different assessment calendar.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city in the north east whose international provision includes Diploma teaching, serving both expatriate and Saudi professional families. Subject availability in the upper years depends on cohort size more than on anything else, which is worth asking about before MYP 4 choices.

regions.name: Makkah, Madinah and Taif
regions.note: Thinner and more dispersed international provision, with school calendars in Makkah bending around the Hajj and Umrah seasons. Families here are the most likely to be comparing an MYP place at a distance against a closer British-curriculum school.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait and the south
regions.note: 'Asir's two neighbouring towns share a catchment at altitude, and the southern centres of Najran and Jazan are further again from any large school market. Where the programme is not available locally, the practical question becomes which route is actually reachable.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: The north west, where relocating families are arriving faster than established international provision has grown. Mid-course entry into the middle years is common here, which makes a diagnostic against the receiving school's criteria more useful than general subject support.

schoolClusters.note: The capital holds the largest group of schools running IB programmes in sequence, which is why families who want to avoid a change of system at sixteen tend to concentrate here. Programme availability differs by school and by year group, and the IB's own school directory is the authoritative check.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah, Thuwal and the Eastern Province
schoolClusters.note: Coastal and eastern provision is a mix of continuum schools, Diploma-only schools and British-curriculum schools, so the handover at the end of the middle years sometimes means a change of institution. Ask early which programmes a school runs at which year groups rather than assuming continuity.

modes.description: One hour a week on one subject group, taught against the four published criteria rather than the topic list, with work set between lessons and marked against the same criteria the school uses. This is the pattern for a student whose grade has sat still across two reporting cycles despite reasonable classroom effort.

modes.description: A short run of sessions across MYP 5 that teaches the three criteria, tests the goal against them, pushes on the success criteria the student has written, and rehearses the kind of reflection the report requires. The project remains entirely the student's own work from goal to final report.

modes.title: Handover preparation for MYP 5 leavers
modes.description: A term of deliberate work on whichever gap the next route exposes. Into the Diploma, that is internal assessment habits and the load of six subjects at once. Into a British sixth form or an IGCSE year, it is timed written papers, which an MYP student may never have sat under examination conditions.

sections.heading: The MYP against Cambridge IGCSE at the same ages
paragraphs: This is the comparison nearly every Saudi family makes, and it is usually made on the wrong terms. The two are not easier and harder versions of each other. They assess different things, report differently, and prepare a student for different kinds of work, and either can be the better fit for a particular child. What follows is the comparison set out plainly so a family can judge it for themselves rather than being told which to prefer.

The short version is that IGCSE is examination-led and the MYP is criterion-led. An IGCSE grade is overwhelmingly decided on a given day under timed conditions, with a tier chosen in advance that caps the result. An MYP grade is accumulated across a year from tasks marked against published criteria by the student's own teachers, moderated internally rather than externally unless the school enters students for eAssessment. The two results are therefore not comparable, and trying to translate one into the other is where most of a parent's anxiety comes from.

What each gives up follows from that. IGCSE produces a student who can perform under time and who has an externally verified certificate at sixteen, which matters for some school transfers and for some employers. The MYP produces a student used to investigation, independent planning and reflection, which maps directly onto Diploma internal assessment, and who may never have sat a two-hour paper. Neither weakness is permanent, and both are cheaper to fix if a family sees them coming a year ahead rather than in the first month of the course that exposes it.

sections.heading: What the four criteria actually reward
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group has four criteria, each published, each marked out of eight, and each reported separately. That design is the programme's most useful feature for a parent and its least understood. A single overall grade hides which of the four is failing; the criterion marks name it exactly. A student with a strong Criterion A and a weak Criterion D in mathematics does not have a mathematics problem, they have an interpretation problem, and those need opposite lessons.

The pattern across subject groups is consistent enough to be worth knowing. Criterion A is almost always knowledge and understanding, and it is the one students score best on because it most resembles what they were assessed on in whatever system they came from. The later criteria are where grades are decided: investigating, designing, processing, evaluating, reflecting, thinking critically. These reward process and judgement, and they cannot be revised for in the ordinary sense.

The practical move for a family is to ask the school for the criterion breakdown rather than the grade, and then ask the subject teacher which single criterion would move the grade most. That question gets a specific answer from almost every teacher, and it converts a vague worry into a term of targeted work. It is also the first thing a tutor should ask for, and a tutor who does not ask is not teaching to the programme but to a topic list that happens to share its name.

sections.heading: From four marks out of eight to one grade out of seven
paragraphs: The conversion is where most of the confusion lives. Each criterion is marked out of eight, so a student carries four marks totalling up to thirty two in each subject. Those are added and then mapped onto a grade from one to seven using boundaries, and the boundaries are applied by the school in line with the programme's published guidance. A parent who tries to read a criterion mark as a percentage will misjudge it badly in both directions.

Two consequences are worth understanding. First, the criteria are not usually all assessed in every task: a unit might report A and C only, and the next one B and D, so a reported mark reflects the most recent evidence for that criterion rather than an average of everything. Second, the total is what converts, which means a four across all four criteria and a pair of sevens with a pair of ones can land close together on the grade while describing completely different students.

For a family deciding whether to buy support, that arithmetic is the whole argument for asking which criterion to target. Moving one criterion by two marks is a realistic term's work with a specialist. Moving all four at once is not, and a tutor who promises general improvement across a subject is describing an outcome nobody can plan. Ask the school which criterion has the most room in it, and spend the term there rather than spreading an hour a week across four.
bullets: Four criteria, each out of eight, totalling up to thirty two per subject
The total converts to a grade of one to seven via school-applied boundaries
Not every task reports every criterion, so marks are recent rather than averaged

sections.heading: Standard and extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5
paragraphs: Mathematics is the one subject where the MYP makes a structural decision in the upper years, splitting into a standard and an extended route. Extended covers additional content and is intended for students likely to take mathematics further, which in practice means Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in the Diploma, or a mathematics-heavy A Level pathway. The decision is made with the school, usually in MYP 4.

Families underestimate how far forward this reaches. A student who takes the standard route and then chooses Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level two years later begins the Diploma with a genuine content gap and, more importantly, without the algebraic fluency the course assumes from the first week. It is recoverable with work, and it is far cheaper to avoid. The reverse error, taking extended mathematics and finding it demoralising, costs confidence in a subject that appears in every reporting cycle.

The useful conversation with the school is about evidence rather than ambition. What are the current criterion marks in mathematics, which criteria are they strong and weak on, and what does the department think the student would find in each route. Where a family wants extended and the marks do not yet support it, a term of targeted work on the weak criterion before the decision is a far better purchase than two years of catching up afterwards. Ask also what the school does for a student who takes the extended route and finds it too hard: a department that can move a student back without drama is a safer place to take the risk.
bullets: Extended mathematics is the route into Higher Level Analysis and Approaches
The decision is usually taken with the school during MYP 4
A standard-route student can still reach Higher Level, with a real content gap to close
Work on the weak criterion before the decision, not after it

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project runs through MYP 5 and is assessed against three criteria: planning, applying skills, and reflecting. The product is not the assessment. A student who builds something ambitious and documents it thinly scores poorly, and a student with a modest product and an exact, honest, well-evidenced process scores well. That inversion is counter-intuitive to most families, and it is the single most useful thing to understand about the project.

The marks follow from four things. A goal that is specific enough to be evaluated. Success criteria the student wrote themselves and can measure against. Evidence that particular skills were learned and applied, with the process log to show it. And reflection that is genuinely reflective, which means identifying what did not work and why, rather than reporting that the student enjoyed the project and learned a lot.

The boundary here is firm. A tutor may teach the three criteria, question whether a goal is assessable, push back on vague success criteria, teach a skill the project requires, and give feedback on a draft of the report that the student has written. A tutor does not write the report, does not design the project and does not produce any part of the submitted work. Schools supervise the project formally and set limits on the help a supervisor may give; ask the coordinator what those limits are before any outside support begins. Keeping dated drafts of the report is a sensible habit for the same reason it is at Diploma level: it makes authorship demonstrable if anyone ever asks, and it costs nothing to do.
bullets: Three criteria: planning, applying skills, reflecting
The process log is assessed evidence, not administrative paperwork
Reflection means naming what failed and why, not what was enjoyed

sections.heading: MYP eAssessment, where a school opts into it
paragraphs: Most of the programme is internally assessed, but the IB does offer an optional external route in the final year, which schools choose whether to enter students for. Where a school opts in, students sit on-screen examinations in a set of subjects and submit ePortfolios in others, and the results can lead to a formal IB certificate rather than only a school report. Many Saudi schools do not use it. Some do, and the difference changes a student's final MYP year considerably.

If your school does enter students, the practical implication is that the final year acquires a timed external component the rest of the programme does not have, sat in a May session. A student who has spent five years being assessed on process then meets an on-screen paper with a clock on it, which is a different skill and needs rehearsing. Preparation is mostly technique: reading the question, managing the time, and producing a complete answer rather than a thorough one.

The only reliable way to know what applies to your child is to ask the MYP coordinator directly: whether the school enters students, in which subjects, and what the internal deadlines for ePortfolio work are. Nothing on this page should be taken as a statement about your school's arrangements, because this is a school-level choice and it changes. Ask before planning the final year around an assumption either way, and ask again the following year if a sibling is coming through, because a school can change its decision between cohorts.
bullets: eAssessment is optional and chosen by the school, not by the family
Where it is used, on-screen examinations and ePortfolios both feature
A timed external component needs technique work the programme otherwise skips
Ask the coordinator what applies to your child's year group and subjects

sections.heading: The MYP year, counted backwards
paragraphs: Because the programme has no single examination to aim at, families lose the sense of a deadline and then discover one at the end of MYP 5. Running the year in reverse fixes that. The last event is not a paper, it is a handover: subject choices made, criterion marks final, and a student walking into the Diploma or a British sixth form carrying whatever the MYP did or did not build. Everything before it is a reporting cycle, and each one is a chance to act or a chance missed.

No dates appear in the table below, for the same reason none appear anywhere else on this page: reporting cycles, unit sequences and term dates are set school by school in the Kingdom, and international schools here mostly run three terms while Ministry of Education schools run two semesters. Two children in neighbouring houses can be in different parts of their year. The order, though, is the same everywhere, and the order is what a family can plan against.

Read it as a sequence of closing doors. A criterion weakness identified in the autumn term of MYP 4 has three reporting cycles left to move. The same weakness identified in the final term of MYP 5 has none, and the only useful work left is preparing for whatever comes next. This is also the honest answer to a parent asking whether it is too late: it is never too late to prepare for the next course, and it can certainly be too late to change this one.

sections.heading: Fitting MYP lessons into a Sunday-to-Thursday week
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and that single fact reorders every piece of scheduling advice written for a British or Indian audience. For a middle-years student the implications are sharper than for an older one, because an eleven or thirteen year old cannot productively start a lesson at eight in the evening, and the usable window after the school run is genuinely narrow.

Sunday is the first school day and the strongest evening for anything demanding, because there is no accumulated homework behind it. Wednesday is the weakest, with three school days of work already waiting. Thursday evening belongs to the weekend and suits review and feedback rather than new content. For a younger MYP student a shorter session more often usually beats a long one weekly: attention, not content, is the binding constraint at this age.

The time zone is the other half of it. The Kingdom keeps Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and never changes its clocks, so a slot agreed in a tutor's own time will drift by an hour twice a year if that tutor is in a country that observes daylight saving. Agree the hour in Saudi local time from the first lesson. Ask also about the tutor's own working week: a tutor in India or the United Kingdom is on their weekend on a Sunday, and that needs agreeing rather than assuming. Getting both of those settled in writing before the first lesson prevents the two most common scheduling failures in this market.

sections.heading: The first month: diagnostic, reporting, and what if it is not working
paragraphs: The first session is a diagnostic, and in the MYP that means something specific: looking at marked tasks against the criteria, not at a general sense of how the subject is going. What is the current mark on each of the four criteria, which tasks produced them, and what did the teacher's comments say. From that, a tutor should be able to name one criterion to target and say what evidence would show it moving. If they cannot, the diagnostic has not been done.

Reporting then follows the school's cycle rather than a weekly one, which is a real difficulty in this programme. Criterion marks may only update once or twice a term, so a family waiting for the school report to tell them whether tutoring is working will wait a long time. The interim measure is the work itself: tasks marked against the same criteria between lessons, with the mark and the reason given, so a parent can see movement before the school confirms it.

If it is not working, the signals are clear enough to act on. A student who cannot say what the last lesson covered. Work that is not being set, or is set and not marked. Sessions that drift into general conversation about school. A tutor who has never mentioned a criterion by name. Any of those is a reason to change tutor after two or three lessons rather than at the end of a term, and saying so early costs a family nothing.
bullets: A real diagnostic reads marked tasks against the four criteria
Expect one named criterion as the target, with evidence of what would move
Interim progress comes from work marked between lessons, not the school report
Change tutor after two or three lessons if the signals are wrong, not after a term

process.title: Tell us the year, the subject group and the criterion
process.description: The useful opening is the MYP year, the subject group and, if you have it, the criterion breakdown from the last report. That is enough for a specialist to say whether the problem is knowledge, process or communication before anyone is matched, which is a better starting point than a subject name alone.

process.title: A diagnostic against marked tasks
process.description: A short first session reading the student's own marked work against the four criteria, with the teacher's comments alongside it. The output is one named criterion to target and a statement of what evidence would show it moving, rather than a general impression of the subject.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: Taught by the specialist who would keep the slot, on something the student has already found difficult once. Listen for whether the criteria are mentioned by name. A tutor teaching MYP without reference to the criteria is teaching a topic list, which is not what the school is marking.

process.title: A weekly slot, with work marked between lessons
process.description: One named hour a week in Arabia Standard Time, held for the term, with tasks set after each session and marked against the same criteria the school uses. For younger students a shorter session twice a week often works better than a single long one.

process.title: Reviewed against the reporting cycle
process.description: Progress is judged against the school's next criterion report and against work marked in between, not against how many lessons have happened. At each review we say plainly whether to continue, change the target criterion, change the pattern, or stop.

whyPoints.title: Taught against the criteria, by name
whyPoints.description: Lessons work from the four published criteria the school marks against, because that is what a grade is built from. A tutor who teaches the topic and ignores the criteria can leave a student knowing more and scoring the same, which is the most common disappointment in middle-years tutoring.

whyPoints.title: One criterion a term, not general improvement
whyPoints.description: A realistic target is moving one criterion by a couple of marks in a term, and we say which one and why. Promising improvement across a whole subject sounds better and describes nothing anyone can plan, measure or be held to.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the comparison a family is making
whyPoints.description: The MYP and the British route assess different things, and either can suit a particular student. This page sets them side by side rather than arguing for one, because a family choosing between schools in the Kingdom deserves the comparison rather than a sales case.

whyPoints.title: The Personal Project kept the student's own
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the three criteria, questions the goal and the success criteria, and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. Nobody here designs a project or writes a report. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the candidate, which is why the line is stated first.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled for a Saudi school week
whyPoints.description: Slots are built around Sunday to Thursday and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, with shorter sessions for younger students where attention rather than content is the limit. A tutor's own weekend is checked before a Sunday hour is agreed rather than discovered afterwards.

faqs.question: What does a first MYP diagnostic session actually cover?
faqs.answer: Marked work, read against the four criteria. The tutor looks at recent tasks, the criterion marks they produced and the teacher's comments, and works out which criterion is holding the grade down. In mathematics that might be a strong Criterion A with a weak Criterion B, which points at generalising and justifying rather than at calculation. The session ends with one named criterion as the target and a statement of what evidence would show it moving. A diagnostic that produces only a general impression of the subject has not been done properly.

faqs.question: How is a starting point diagnosed for a student in MYP 3 with no examination marks to look at?
faqs.answer: From the criterion marks and the tasks behind them, which is more informative than an examination result anyway. Four separate marks out of eight per subject say where a student is strong and weak in a way a single percentage cannot. Where a family has arrived mid-course and has no MYP marks at all, a tutor sets two short tasks of the kind the school uses and marks them against the criteria, which produces a baseline in a week rather than waiting a reporting cycle to find out.

faqs.question: What should a parent expect to see in the first month of MYP support?
faqs.answer: Three things. A named target criterion rather than a general aim. Work set after each session and returned marked against that criterion, with the reason for the mark written out. And a change in how the student talks about tasks, because criterion language is learnable and its absence is usually the real problem. What a parent should not expect in a month is a changed school report: criterion marks update on the school's cycle, and that cycle is slower than a month almost everywhere.

faqs.question: How is progress reported when MYP criterion marks only update once or twice a term?
faqs.answer: Through the work in between. Tasks set between lessons are marked against the same criteria the school uses, with the mark and the reason given, so movement is visible before the school confirms it. That interim evidence is also what makes the end-of-term conversation honest, because it shows whether a criterion is moving or static. Ask any prospective tutor how they will evidence progress between school reports; a tutor without an answer to that is asking a family to wait a term on trust.

faqs.question: What should we do if an MYP tutor is not the right fit after three lessons?
faqs.answer: Change, and say so early. The signals are specific: a student who cannot say what the last lesson covered, work that is not set or not marked, sessions that drift into conversation about school, or a tutor who has never named a criterion. None of those means tutoring is the wrong idea, and all of them mean this tutor is the wrong one for this student. A mismatch at middle-years level is often temperament and pace rather than competence, and three lessons is enough to know.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether MYP support is worth continuing after a term?
faqs.answer: Compare the target criterion's mark and the marked work against what was predicted at the start. If the named criterion has moved and the work between lessons shows why, continue, possibly with a new target criterion. If it has not moved and nothing in the marked work explains why, change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours. Sometimes the honest answer is to stop: a student whose criterion marks are solid across the board is being served well enough by their school.

faqs.question: Can an MYP student in the Kingdom fit lessons around a Sunday-to-Thursday school week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the week shapes which evenings work. Sunday is the first school day and the best evening for anything demanding, because no homework has accumulated behind it. Wednesday is the weakest, with three school days of work already waiting. Thursday evening belongs to the weekend and suits review rather than new teaching. Friday and Saturday mornings are free and are the right place for Personal Project work or anything needing uninterrupted thought. Most families settle on one weekday evening plus a weekend morning.

faqs.question: How long should a lesson be for a student in MYP 1 or MYP 2?
faqs.answer: Shorter than a parent expects, and more often. For an eleven or twelve year old, attention rather than content is the binding constraint, so two shorter sessions a week usually achieve more than a single long one. A full hour of concentrated one-to-one work is demanding for a child who has already had a school day and a car journey, and the last fifteen minutes of a tired session teach very little. Older middle-years students manage a full hour comfortably, and MYP 5 students working on a project sometimes need longer.

faqs.question: What happens to an MYP lesson slot during a school's midyear break?
faqs.answer: It can be paused or kept, and the choice should follow the year rather than the calendar. A student in MYP 5 with a Personal Project in progress usually benefits from keeping a reduced pattern through a break, because the project needs the uninterrupted time a holiday provides. A student in MYP 1 or 2 is generally better off stopping and returning. Either way, say which in advance so the tutor holds the hour; an unannounced pause is the usual way a good slot is lost to another family.

faqs.question: Our tutor works a Monday-to-Friday week — can an MYP student still have a Sunday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but it has to be agreed rather than assumed, and it is the most common reason a promising match falls apart in the first fortnight. A tutor based in India, the United Kingdom or most of Europe has Sunday as a weekend day, and some are glad of the work while others are not. A tutor in Jordan or Egypt already works a Sunday-to-Thursday week, which removes the question. Ask where the tutor is based and what their own weekend is before booking the slot.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change how a weekly MYP session is scheduled?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. School days shorten, which brings the school run forward, and family routines shift later into the evening, so the slot that worked in the autumn term often does not work during it. The practical approach is to agree a single alternative time for the whole period rather than rearranging week by week, which rarely survives. Because it falls earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, it lands in a different part of the academic year over time, so ask the school early how its timetable will change.

faqs.question: Why is an MYP criterion marked out of eight rather than as a percentage?
faqs.answer: Because it is a judgement against descriptors rather than a count of correct answers. Each criterion has bands with written descriptions of what work at that level looks like, and the teacher decides which band the work best fits. That is why reading a criterion mark as a percentage misleads badly: a five out of eight is not sixty-two per cent, it is a described standard. The useful question is what the next band up requires, because that is a specific, teachable difference rather than a vague instruction to do better.

faqs.question: How do four criterion marks become a single MYP grade from one to seven?
faqs.answer: They are added, giving a total of up to thirty two per subject, and that total is mapped onto a grade from one to seven using boundaries applied by the school in line with the programme's published guidance. Two consequences follow. A student with four moderate marks and a student with two very high and two very low marks can land on the same grade while needing completely different teaching. And moving one weak criterion by two marks can move the overall grade, which is why targeting one criterion is a workable plan.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Criterion C and Criterion D in MYP sciences?
faqs.answer: Criterion C is processing and evaluating: handling the data from an investigation, presenting it correctly, identifying trends, drawing a conclusion that the data supports, and discussing the reliability of the method. Criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science: discussing the application of the science in a real context, including implications for people and the environment, and using and documenting sources properly. Students often lose Criterion D marks not from weak science but from thin referencing and an absent discussion of context, which is quickly fixable.

faqs.question: Are there command terms in the MYP, and do they work as they do in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are a genuine bridge into the Diploma. MYP task questions use published command terms, and they carry the same obligations: describe wants an account, explain wants reasons, analyse wants the parts and their relationships, evaluate wants a judgement with support. Students who learn to read the command term before writing gain marks immediately and arrive in the Diploma already fluent in its most important habit. A student who writes everything they know regardless of the term loses marks in every subject group at once.

faqs.question: Does an MYP 5 student need extended mathematics to take Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It is not a formal requirement in most schools, and it is a significant practical advantage. Extended mathematics covers additional content and, more importantly, builds the algebraic fluency the Higher Level course assumes from its first weeks. A standard-route student can reach Higher Level, but starts with a real gap to close while six other subjects are also beginning. If Higher Level mathematics is a likely destination, the cheaper intervention is a term of targeted work before the MYP 4 route decision, not two years of catching up afterwards.

ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Send the criterion breakdown, not just the subject
ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: The quickest route to a useful answer is the MYP year, the subject group and the criterion marks from the last report. From those, a specialist can usually say which criterion is holding the grade down and whether a term of work would move it, before anybody is matched or paid. If the honest answer is that the school is already serving your child well, we will say that. Lessons are one-to-one and delivered online over live video, pinned to Arabia Standard Time and timed to the Sunday-to-Thursday week, and the trial lesson is free and taught by the proposed tutor.

ib-online-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme subjects to students across the Kingdom over live video. Matching is by subject and level, and then by component, because a tutor who can carry a Mathematics AA Higher Level student through Paper 3 is not automatically the right person for a Standard Level exploration.

intro.heading: Six subjects, one budget: start from the assessment structure
paragraphs: A Diploma student carries six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, an Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run from one to seven, giving 42 points, and up to three more come from the matrix that combines Theory of Knowledge with the Extended Essay. Almost no family buys support for all six. So the practical question is not what tuition costs per hour but which of six subjects, and which component inside that subject, repays an hour of outside teaching best. That answer comes from the assessment structure, which is why this page starts there rather than with a price.

Inside each subject the grade splits between externally marked written papers and an internally assessed component: an exploration in mathematics, a scientific investigation, an oral in a language, a commentary or portfolio elsewhere. The internally assessed part typically carries somewhere between a fifth and a third of the subject grade depending on the subject and level, and your subject teacher can confirm the current split. That component has three properties that matter financially. It is submitted months before the papers, it can be worked on calmly, and it is the one part of the grade a student can still move deliberately in the middle of the course. Hour for hour it is usually the cheapest grade protection available.

Higher Level is not a harder version of Standard Level. In several subjects it is a different course with additional components: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches adds a third paper at Higher Level, the sciences add topics with no Standard Level equivalent, and the language courses add an essay on studied works. This is why a Higher Level specialist costs more everywhere in the world, and why a late move down from Higher to Standard is harder than it sounds. A tutor who has taught the Standard Level course for years has not necessarily taught the Higher Level components at all, and that is a fair question to ask before any money changes hands.

Delivery here is online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Diploma work that is an advantage rather than a concession. The subjects a Saudi family most often needs are the scarce ones, and an in-home search narrows the pool to whoever happens to live nearby while adding a travel loading to the rate that buys no teaching. A session on a shared screen is also the natural format for this work: past papers, mark schemes, graphs and drafts are documents, and documents are easier to annotate together on a screen than across a kitchen table.

What follows is the structure in detail, then the money. How the 45 points are assembled, what Higher Level adds subject by subject, where the internally assessed marks sit, what the market advertises in SAR and what moves the number, where a limited budget does the most good across six subjects, and what an online hour actually contains: platform, whiteboard, marking between lessons, recordings, what a parent sees, and what happens when the connection drops. Then how to check a Diploma tutor's claims, and where the line sits on the Extended Essay and the internal assessment. No figure on this page is our price; each one is another provider's advertised rate, labelled with the kind of source it came from.

ib-online-tuition.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes and a Saudi family may meet three of them in one school. Each is described here from the point of view of a parent deciding whether outside teaching is worth buying at that stage, and what an hour can realistically achieve.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and an exhibition in the final year. There is no grade to protect here, which changes the value calculation completely: an hour buys fluency in arithmetic, reading stamina and the ability to explain reasoning in English. Those three are examined indirectly for the next decade, so the return is real but it arrives slowly and it is impossible to attribute to the tuition.
programmes.countryNote: For most families in the Kingdom this stage is worth a short block rather than a standing weekly commitment, usually aimed at one thing: a child who can produce an answer and cannot say how they got it. Online works well at this age in short sessions with a parent nearby, and badly in long ones.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and reported as a grade from one to seven, with a Personal Project in the final year. Parents find the marking hardest to read, because a strong answer can score poorly against the criterion actually being assessed. An hour spent decoding the criteria with a student is often worth more than an hour of content.
programmes.countryNote: The most useful purchase in these years is preparation rather than repair: extended mathematics for a future Analysis and Approaches candidate, and written-answer structure for everyone. Families who wait until the Diploma starts pay for the same work later under far more time pressure.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, the core, and 45 available points across two years. This is where outside teaching earns its rate, because every component has a published mark scheme or set of criteria and the gap between knowing the content and being credited for it is wide and diagnosable. It is also where the subject scarcity premium is highest, particularly in Higher Level sciences and mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Almost every IB school in the Kingdom sits the May session. Within the Diploma the cheapest effective purchases are usually internal assessment feedback early in the first year and paper technique in the final two terms; the most expensive mistake is buying general content teaching in six subjects at once.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The fourth IB programme, combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is far less common than the Diploma and families sometimes meet it when comparing schools internationally. Where a school offers it, the Diploma courses inside it are assessed in the same way as elsewhere.
programmes.countryNote: Provision in this region is limited and changes, so check the IB's own school directory rather than any summary, including this one. If your child's school offers it, the subject courses inside it can be supported exactly as Diploma courses are; the reflective project needs the same academic honesty discipline as an Extended Essay.

ib-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: What an online hour actually does differs by subject, and so does whether Higher or Standard Level changes the value. These are the Diploma subjects Saudi families ask for most, described in terms of what a session is spent on and which component it is protecting.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: An hour here is mostly the student working while the tutor watches the method, which a shared screen handles better than a classroom does. At Higher Level the third paper is the usual reason families call: it is a long investigation-style problem and students abandon unfamiliar contexts rather than working through them. The exploration needs a mathematical idea, not a data set.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Sessions divide between the graphical calculator and interpreting a model back into its context, which is a writing skill the mark scheme is strict about. Screen sharing a calculator view alongside the question is genuinely easier online than on paper. Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and more inference than most students expect.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 2 extended responses dominate the time: explaining a mechanism in full sentences, with every causal link present. Diagrams and graphs are annotated together on screen. The practical work and the investigation happen at school, so an online hour supports the write-up and the analysis rather than the laboratory itself.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics take most sessions, with the data booklet open on screen beside the question so its use becomes habitual rather than occasional. For the investigation the work is on choosing a measurable variable and on uncertainty, both of which are design decisions the student makes and the tutor interrogates.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The terminology volume makes this look like memory work and the papers reward application to unfamiliar data. Command terms decide more marks here than in any other science, so sessions tend to be structured around answer length and structure, with content filled in around them rather than the other way round.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram discipline is the whole first month for most students: labelled axes, correct shifts, and a written link from the diagram to the question. Drawing them on a shared whiteboard while the tutor marks each component aloud is the fastest route. Higher Level adds quantitative work and the policy paper.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools are the easy part and application to the stimulus is where the marks are. The Higher Level pre-released case study rewards work started months ahead, which makes it one of the few Diploma components where early weekly support is clearly better value than a late intensive.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the unseen analysis paper carry most of the grade. Sessions are spent on how a text produces an effect rather than on what it says, and on rehearsing the oral with a recording the student can review. Higher Level adds the essay on studied works, which needs an argument rather than coverage.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written papers want formal reasoning about algorithms on paper, so confident programmers often need the opposite of more coding. Higher Level adds abstract data structures, resource management and the case study. Screen sharing suits this subject particularly well because code, pseudocode and trace tables sit side by side.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The essay must be analysed against the prescribed title with real-world examples doing argumentative work, not decorating it. Sessions are discussion, which is why this is one subject where a tutor with no connection to the student's school can be an advantage: they ask questions nobody in the room has already answered.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words on a question of the student's choosing, supervised at school. An hour with a subject specialist is best spent on whether the research question is narrow and answerable, and on whether the method will produce evidence. The student writes every word; the tutor questions, explains criteria and gives feedback on what the student has written.

ib-online-tuition.regionsTitle: What online lessons need, place by place
ib-online-tuition.regionsIntro: Live video lessons depend on three things that vary across the Kingdom: bandwidth, a quiet place to work, and a household rhythm that leaves an hour intact. None of these is about teaching, and all three decide whether a weekly arrangement survives a term.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Connectivity is rarely the constraint; space and noise often are, particularly in apartments with younger siblings. A desk away from shared rooms with a door that closes is worth more to the lesson than any upgrade in equipment, and a headset solves most of the rest.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long city where the commute decides when a student is home and settled. Families further north towards Obhur often prefer a slightly later start with a wired connection at a fixed desk rather than an earlier session taken on a phone hotspot in a car.

regions.name: Al Khobar, Dammam and Dhahran
regions.note: Compound and company housing is common, and shared infrastructure can mean a busier network in the early evening than later. If lessons stutter at the same hour each week, that pattern is the clue, and moving the slot usually fixes it faster than changing anything else.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: Industrial shift patterns mean the household is awake at unusual hours and the quiet hour may not be the obvious one. Sessions earlier in the evening tend to work better here, and agreeing who will be at home during the lesson matters for younger students.

regions.name: Yanbu and the Red Sea coast
regions.note: Smaller communities attached to industrial and port facilities, where the nearest alternative school is a long way off. That makes a reliable weekly slot more valuable and makes it worth testing the connection properly in the trial lesson rather than assuming.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST campus
regions.note: A university campus community with strong infrastructure and a highly mobile population, so students arrive and leave mid-course more often than elsewhere. Handover notes matter here: a student who changes school in the middle of DP1 should not also have to rebuild a diagnosis.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Household rhythms shift noticeably across the Hajj and Umrah seasons, with travel and visitors affecting availability more than bandwidth does. Agreeing in advance which weeks will be skipped works better than cancelling one session at a time.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and the north-west
regions.note: Project housing and long distances, with families arriving part-way through the course. Connection quality varies more here than in the big cities, so test a full lesson rather than a call, and keep a mobile hotspot as a fallback for the sessions that matter.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait and 'Asir
regions.note: High-altitude towns sharing a catchment with a small international-school market and no realistic local fallback for a scarce Higher Level subject. Weekly reliability is the thing worth optimising for, ahead of the exact hour.

schoolClusters.note: Several schools in the capital appear in IB directories across the three programmes, so a family here may be choosing between Diploma providers rather than compensating for the absence of one. The question to put to any of them is which Higher Level subjects can actually be timetabled next year.

A mixed market where IB World Schools and Cambridge schools sit close together, and where some schools run both. Families relocating within the Kingdom often move between this cluster and the capital, which makes continuity of a tutor more valuable than it first appears.

The Diploma is offered at some campuses in this cluster and not at others, and British-curriculum schools sit alongside them. Because contracts rotate, Diploma cohorts here turn over more than in the capital, and mid-course arrivals into DP1 are routine rather than exceptional.

ib-online-tuition.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as context for the market families work inside; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied or exists.
ib-online-tuition.modesIntro: Four purchases, with very different cost shapes. Picking the right one is most of the value, because the same number of hours spent on the wrong component is the commonest way families overspend on the Diploma.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a single Higher Level subject
modes.description: A fixed slot per week in the subject that is costing the most points, running alongside the school's teaching. The hour goes on what the class moved past quickly and on the components the school has least time for. Over two or three terms this is the arrangement that changes a grade rather than a mark.
bullets: One subject at a time, chosen by where the points are being lost
Work set between sessions and marked against the published criteria
A short written note to the parent after each lesson
Slot agreed in Arabia Standard Time so it survives a clock change

modes.title: An internal assessment feedback block
modes.description: A finite run of sessions on the exploration, investigation or commentary: whether the question is answerable, whether the method produces usable evidence, whether each criterion is being addressed. Usually a handful of hours spread across a term rather than a weekly commitment, which makes it the cheapest effective purchase in the Diploma.
bullets: Feedback against the published criteria, criterion by criterion
Early attention to the research question, where most drafts fail
The student writes every word; nothing is drafted or edited for them
Fits around the school's own supervision process, which stays in charge

modes.title: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay support
modes.description: Discussion-led sessions on the core, which is where up to three points sit and where students get least help because no single department owns it. For the essay the work is argument and example; for the Extended Essay it is the research question and the method. Both are better bought early than late.
bullets: The matrix is worth up to three points on the final total
Real-world examples interrogated rather than collected
Reflections and the research process documented by the student
Nothing written, redrafted or edited on the student's behalf

modes.title: An intensive run before the May session
modes.description: Longer, less frequent sessions in the final weeks, built around whole papers under timed conditions and marked line by line. Content teaching largely stops. Intensive hours are advertised at higher rates across this market, and they are worth it only when coverage is broadly complete already.
bullets: Whole papers under time, then marked against the published scheme
Paper-by-paper analysis of where the marks actually went
Exam-day decisions rehearsed: order, timing, when to move on
Friday and Saturday mornings carry the long sessions

sections.heading: How 45 points are assembled, and which parts respond to teaching
paragraphs: The Diploma total is built from parts that behave very differently, and a family deciding where to spend should know which is which. Six subjects produce 42 points at seven each. The matrix combining Theory of Knowledge with the Extended Essay produces up to three more. Creativity, Activity, Service produces none and is a requirement rather than a component, which does not make it optional. Inside each subject the grade splits again between externally marked papers and an internally assessed piece of work.

Those parts differ in how late they can be changed. The written papers can be improved until the week before the session, because technique is learnable quickly and much of what is lost there is method, command terms and presentation rather than knowledge. The internally assessed component cannot be changed after submission, and submission is months earlier. The core is the most neglected and often the most available: up to three points sit in the matrix, and students routinely treat both the essay and the Extended Essay as administrative obligations rather than as points.

So the honest ranking of value, for most students in the middle of the course, runs roughly like this. Protect the internally assessed components while they are still live, because they are a fixed share of the grade and they can be worked on calmly. Take the core seriously early, because three points is often the difference between two university offers. Buy paper technique in the final two terms, when it converts existing knowledge into marks. And buy general content teaching only where there is a genuine gap, because it is the slowest and most expensive way to move a grade.

sections.heading: Higher Level is a different course, not a harder one
paragraphs: Families and some tutors treat the two levels as the same syllabus at different speeds. In several subjects that is simply wrong, and the error has a price. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches adds an entire third paper at Higher Level, an extended investigation-style problem that no Standard Level candidate ever sees. The sciences add topics with no Standard Level equivalent rather than extending the existing ones evenly. The language courses add an essay on studied works. Economics adds a policy paper and quantitative questions.

This is the mechanism behind the rate difference everybody notices and few providers explain. The pool of people who have actually taught the Higher Level components is much smaller than the pool who have taught the subject, and smaller again if you want someone who has prepared candidates for a specific Higher Level paper. Scarcity, not prestige, is what sets the price. It also explains why a tutor can be excellent and still the wrong choice: years of Standard Level teaching does not imply any experience of the extra components.

It has a second consequence families meet in the second year. A late move from Higher to Standard Level looks like a simple reduction and is not, because the content covered does not map neatly and the entry has already been made. The decision is realistic in the first year and progressively less so afterwards. If a Higher Level subject is clearly not working, the time to raise it with the school is early in the first year, with evidence from marked work rather than from a feeling, and a specialist read on that work is a cheap way to get the evidence.
