sections.heading: The internally assessed component is the cheapest grade protection there is
paragraphs: Every Diploma subject contains a piece of work the student produces and the school marks, with the board moderating the school's marking. It carries a meaningful and fixed share of the subject grade, and the exact share differs by subject and level, which your subject teacher can confirm for the current syllabus. The financial point is not the percentage but the predictability: it is a known fraction of the grade, available to be worked on for months, in conditions the student controls.

Almost everything that goes wrong with it goes wrong in the first fortnight, which is why support is cheapest and most effective early. The research question is too broad to answer or too narrow to sustain. The method will not produce evidence that supports a conclusion. The topic is interesting and does not meet the criteria. None of these are writing problems, and all of them are expensive to discover in a final draft. An hour of interrogation at the planning stage saves several hours of rescue later and usually produces a better grade than the rescue would.

The second common failure is deadline arithmetic. The school's internal deadline sits well ahead of the board's submission date, because teachers need time to mark, moderate within the department and assemble a sample for the board. A student working to the later date has created a problem for their teacher and for themselves. Ask for the school's internal date in writing at the start of the task and build backwards from it, leaving room for the number of drafts the school's own policy actually permits to be formally reviewed.
bullets: Spend the first hour on the question and the method, not on the writing
Ask the school for its internal deadline, not the board's submission date
Find out how many drafts the school will formally review before you plan
Keep notes, data and version history from the first week of the task

sections.heading: What the market advertises, and what actually moves the number
paragraphs: Providers in this market publish rates inconsistently, so families compare figures that describe different products. What is advertised, with the kind of source each figure comes from: general online tutoring with no subject specialism stated from about SAR 55 an hour on tutoring-platform listings; budget platform rates for one-to-one work from about SAR 35 on platform marketing pages; general private tuition for senior-school examination subjects at 200 and above in tutor-marketplace guides, with primary-level work around 50 in the same guides; IB subject tutoring from about SAR 180 on tutoring-company listings, and Higher Level or premium tracks at roughly 200 to 220. Some international providers quote around USD 60 an hour on their own sites. None of those is our price, and none is a market average.

What moves the number, in order of weight: subject and level scarcity first, because a Higher Level Physics or Analysis and Approaches specialist is scarce everywhere and a Standard Level mathematics tutor is not; then marking or examiner experience, which is what converts general advice about technique into specific knowledge of what gets credited; then level, with Higher Level above Standard Level above Middle Years work; then whether the tutor travels; and last, package length. Of those five, only the first two reliably change what happens during the hour.

Travel is worth isolating because it is the one factor that adds cost without adding teaching. An in-home rate quoted in Riyadh or Jeddah carries the time it takes to get there, which nobody teaches during, and it restricts the search to tutors within a drive of the address. That is the financial argument for live video, and it is separate from the academic one. The academic argument is simpler: the person who has taught the Higher Level component your child is failing probably does not live nearby, and in most Saudi cities outside the three largest clusters they certainly do not.

sections.heading: Six subjects, one budget: where the money goes furthest
paragraphs: Most families can fund one subject properly or two thinly, and the choice between those is not obvious. Thin support across two subjects tends to produce two sets of homework help and no change in either grade. Concentrated support in one usually moves that grade and does nothing for the other five, which is fine if the right subject was chosen. The right subject is rarely the one with the lowest grade; it is the one where the most points are recoverable for the fewest hours.

Three questions settle it. Which subject's grade is furthest below what the student is capable of, judged on marked work rather than reports? Which component inside that subject is losing the marks, and is it content, technique or an internally assessed piece still in play? And does the university plan depend on that subject specifically, as engineering depends on Higher Level mathematics and medicine on Higher Level chemistry? A subject that is weak, recoverable and required is worth every hour. A subject that is weak and irrelevant to the plan may be worth dropping to Standard Level instead of funding.

The table ranks the common purchases by what they tend to return. It is a guide rather than a rule, and the honest caveat is that the ranking changes with where the year is: internal assessment support is unbeatable value early and worthless once submitted, while paper technique is the reverse. A provider who recommends the same package regardless of the month is not doing this arithmetic, and the question to ask them is simply which component the hours will be spent on.

sections.heading: What actually happens in an online Diploma lesson
paragraphs: The format matters more in some subjects than others, and families are right to ask what the hour looks like before paying for it. The spine of a good session is a shared screen with the question on it and the student working, not watching. A past paper is opened, the student attempts a question, and the tutor annotates what they wrote: the missing step, the command term that was not answered, the graph axis chosen without thought. The mark scheme is then opened alongside it, which is the part most students have never seen done.

Different subjects use the screen differently. Mathematics and physics need handwriting, so the student should have paper and a pen and either hold the work up to the camera or write on a tablet shared to the session; a student who only types will not practise the thing that is examined. Economics diagrams are drawn on a shared whiteboard with the tutor marking each element aloud. In languages the oral is rehearsed and recorded so the student can hear themselves. In computer science code, pseudocode and trace tables sit side by side on one screen, which is genuinely easier than on paper.

Work between lessons is where the learning consolidates, and the mechanics are worth confirming with any provider. Questions are set, the student attempts them, and they are returned marked against the published scheme with the reason for each lost mark written down rather than ticked. That record is the diagnosis. If a provider cannot describe how written work is collected, marked and returned, the lessons are likely to be conversation rather than teaching, which is pleasant and does not move a grade.

sections.heading: Recordings, privacy and what a parent is entitled to see
paragraphs: Families ask about recordings for two different reasons, and they deserve different answers. The first is revision: a student wants to watch a difficult explanation again. That is a good use, and where a session is recorded for it the recording should be available to the student and the parent and to nobody else. The second reason is oversight, and recordings are a poor tool for it. A parent watching an hour of footage learns less than they would from a two-line note saying which component was worked on and what was set.

What a parent is entitled to is simpler and more useful: a short written note after each session naming the topic, the questions attempted, what was lost and why, and what has been set. Marked work returned with reasons rather than ticks. A direct way to raise a concern that does not involve the student relaying it. And a straight answer about progress at the end of a block, including the possibility that it is not working. Any provider can supply all four, and a provider who supplies none of them is selling hours.

Two practical points on privacy and setup. A lesson should happen in a shared part of the home rather than behind a closed door for a younger student, which is both safer and better for concentration than it sounds. And the student's own documents stay the student's: a draft is shared for comment, not handed over for editing, and a tutor who asks for editing access to an assessed piece of work has misunderstood their role. Recordings of a session should not be redistributed by anyone, which is a rule that protects the student as much as the tutor.
bullets: A two-line session note is worth more oversight than an hour of recording
Marked work should come back with reasons, not ticks
A draft is shared for comment; editing access is not appropriate
Ask how a concern is raised without the student having to relay it

sections.heading: Checking a Diploma tutor's claims before you pay
paragraphs: Scarcity means Diploma tutors are expensive, and expense attracts claims. There is no independent ranking of tutors in this market, so every provider describing itself in superlatives is making the same empty statement. What can be checked is narrow and sufficient: which subject, which level, which components, how many cohorts, and whether they have marked for the board recently.

Ask which components your child sits and listen to how the answer arrives. A Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist will mention the third paper before you do, and will have an opinion about why students lose marks on it. A Standard Level tutor asked the same question will be vague about it, which is useful information rather than a failing. The same test works in every subject: a genuine specialist talks in components, criteria and command terms, and a generalist talks in topics and revision.

Marking experience is worth a sentence of its own because the phrase is elastic. It can mean current marking for the board on this component, or one session long ago, or a colleague's experience written loosely into a company biography. Which board, which component, and when did you last mark it is the question, and a real answer comes back immediately and specifically. Treat any figure offered without a number of candidates, a date and a method as decoration. What a provider can legitimately offer is a named tutor, a stated component, a free trial lesson you can judge, a past paper marked with reasons, and a clear statement of what happens if the match is wrong.
bullets: Which components does my child sit, and which have you prepared candidates for?
Which board and which component did you last mark, and when?
How many cohorts have you taught through to a result in this subject at this level?
What happens, administratively, if the match is wrong after two sessions?

sections.heading: Academic honesty on the exploration, the essay and the Extended Essay
paragraphs: This market contains providers who will produce assessed work, usually described in language chosen not to look like that. The line is worth stating plainly, because a family can cross it without intending to and the consequence falls on the student. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback. The student produces the work.

In practice that means a tutor may interrogate a research question, challenge a method that will not generate usable evidence, explain what a criterion is asking for, show a worked example of an entirely different investigation, teach the skill of checking work against the criteria, and comment on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of it, choose the topic, supply the data, or produce text the student then submits. Online delivery makes the boundary easier to keep rather than harder: a draft shared read-only receives comments and questions in the margin, and the student makes every change in their own document.

The school owns the supervision process, including how many drafts may be formally reviewed and what its academic honesty policy permits, and those rules take precedence over anything a tutor suggests. Keep the student's own notes, data, drafts and version history from the first week; a version history is the simplest possible evidence of authorship if a question is ever raised, and it costs nothing to accumulate as you go. If a provider offers to produce the work, that is not a shortcut. It is malpractice carried out in the student's name, and the student is the one who answers for it.

sections.heading: The May session counted backwards, and how to start
paragraphs: Almost every IB school in the Kingdom sits the May session. Specific examination and results dates are published by the board and by your school and they move, so the Diploma Programme coordinator is the only reliable source; nothing on this page is a substitute for asking them. What does not move is the order of events, and that is what a family can plan against. Internally assessed work is submitted months ahead of the papers, with the school's own deadline earlier still. Mocks sit earlier again, because they are the evidence a predicted grade rests on. Predictions reach universities long before any result.

The practical consequence is that improvement has to arrive before the evidence is collected, not after. A student who starts working seriously once the mocks are over may finish with a strong grade and a modest prediction, and the prediction is what the application carried. Working backwards from the mocks rather than forwards from today is the single most useful planning move available, and it is free.

Starting is short. Tell us the subject, the level, the components and where the student is in the two years. We arrange a free trial lesson with a specialist in that subject and level, used as a diagnostic: a real session, a past-paper question worked and marked, and a written summary of whether the problem is content, technique or an internally assessed piece still in play. You keep the summary either way. Two honest caveats. The scarcer the specialism, the longer a particular hour takes to fill, and when nobody suitable is free we will say so rather than putting a generalist in the room. And if the match is wrong after two or three sessions, tell us and the tutor changes, with the diagnosis carrying across.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not the subject alone. Higher Level or Standard Level, which papers the candidate sits, and whether the internally assessed piece is still in play. Those three answers decide which specialist is needed and what the hours should be spent on, and they take one email to the subject teacher to confirm.

process.title: A free trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: A specialist in that subject and level teaches a real session and works a past-paper question with the student. You receive a written read separating content gaps from command terms, method marks and presentation. It is yours whether or not you continue, and it usually changes which subject a family decides to fund.

process.title: Agree what the hours are for
process.description: Internal assessment feedback, weekly teaching, core support or paper technique: these are different purchases with different time shapes, and mixing them produces hours nobody is accountable for. Pick one, state the goal, and set a point at which it will be reviewed.

process.title: Fix the slot in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: Agreed in Saudi local time so a clock change in the tutor's country moves their evening rather than your child's. Sunday to Wednesday evenings carry weekly work; Friday and Saturday mornings carry the long sessions and whole papers closer to the session.

process.title: Work set, submitted and marked with reasons
process.description: Questions attempted between lessons and returned marked against the published scheme, with the reason for each lost mark written down. That marking is the diagnosis and it decides what the next session does. Ask any provider to show you a marked example before committing.

process.title: Review against marked work, not impressions
process.description: At the end of a block: what the marked work shows, whether answer length now tracks the mark allocation, whether the internally assessed piece is on course. Then continue, reduce, switch subject or stop. A review that cannot end in stopping is not a review.

whyPoints.title: The rate reflects scarcity, and we say which
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Analysis and Approaches or Physics specialist is scarce everywhere, and that is what sets the price in every market including this one. Travel, by contrast, adds cost and no teaching. Teaching over live video removes the second and gives access to the first, which is the whole financial case in one sentence.

whyPoints.title: Hours aimed at a component, not a subject
whyPoints.description: Support is agreed against a specific component: the third paper, the exploration, the individual oral, the policy paper. That is what makes the spend measurable, because a component has a published mark scheme or set of criteria and you can see whether the marks moved.

whyPoints.title: A free trial lesson that changes the decision
whyPoints.description: The trial is a real teaching session with a written read on where the marks are going, and families frequently use it to change which subject they fund. It costs nothing, it is yours whether you continue or not, and it is a better basis for a decision than any profile.

whyPoints.title: Marked work, returned with reasons
whyPoints.description: Work set between sessions comes back marked against the published criteria with the reason for each lost mark written, not ticked. That is the record a parent can actually read, and it is the difference between teaching and an hour of pleasant conversation about a subject.

whyPoints.title: The line on assessed work is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor interrogates a research question, explains criteria and comments on the student's own draft. Nothing is written, redrafted or edited for the student, and the school's supervision process stays in charge. A draft is shared read-only for exactly that reason, and the student makes every change themselves.

whyPoints.title: No claims that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: No pass rates, no star averages, no counts of families taught, and no ranking claim in a market where nobody independently ranks tutors. Every SAR figure here is another provider's advertised rate with its source type named. What is offered before any commitment is a trial lesson and a written diagnosis.

faqs.question: What does an IB online lesson look like from the student's side of the screen?
faqs.answer: A shared screen with a past paper or a worked question on it, and the student working rather than watching. They attempt a question on paper or a tablet, the tutor annotates what was written, and then the mark scheme is opened beside it so the student sees where each mark sat. Most sessions end with work set for the week. A good lesson is quiet for stretches, because the student is writing. A lesson where the tutor talks for fifty minutes is a lecture, and lectures are available free.

faqs.question: How does a tutor work through a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 question on a shared screen?
faqs.answer: Usually by refusing to start. Paper 3 is a long investigation-style problem and the common failure is abandoning an unfamiliar context, so the first move is making the student write down what the question has actually given them and what it is asking in stages. The tutor shares the question, the student writes their own working and shows it, and the tutor marks the structure of the attempt rather than the final answer. The skill being taught is staying in an unfamiliar problem long enough to find the route, and it cannot be taught by demonstration.

faqs.question: Are IB lessons recorded, and who can see the recording?
faqs.answer: Where a session is recorded it should be for the student's revision, available to the student and the parent and to nobody else, and not redistributed by anyone. It is genuinely useful for a difficult explanation the student wants again. It is a poor oversight tool, though: a parent learns more from a two-line note naming the component worked on and the work set than from watching an hour of footage. Ask any provider who holds recordings, for how long, and whether the student can request one, before the first lesson rather than after.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a lesson?
faqs.answer: The tutor reconnects, and the lost time is either made up at the end or carried to the next session, which should be stated in the session note rather than quietly absorbed. If drops happen at the same hour each week, the cause is usually network congestion rather than equipment, and moving the slot by an hour fixes it more reliably than new hardware. It is worth keeping a mobile hotspot as a fallback for sessions close to a deadline or a mock, and worth testing a full lesson rather than a short call during the trial.

faqs.question: Is a tablet enough for an online Diploma lesson, or does a student need a laptop?
faqs.answer: A tablet works and a laptop is better, but the thing that actually matters is handwriting. Mathematics and the sciences are examined on paper, so a student who only types is not practising the skill being tested. The workable setups are a laptop with paper and a pen beside it, holding work up to the camera or photographing it, or a tablet with a stylus shared into the session. A headset solves most audio problems and costs little. A phone is adequate for a conversation and not for a lesson.

faqs.question: How are diagrams, graphs and working shared in an online Physics or Chemistry session?
faqs.answer: On a shared whiteboard, drawn by the student rather than the tutor. That ordering is the whole point: a student who watches a perfect free-body diagram appear learns less than one who draws a flawed one and has each element marked aloud. For chemistry the data booklet sits open on screen beside the question so using it becomes habitual. Whiteboard images should be saved and sent afterwards, which gives the student a record of their own corrected work rather than a set of someone else's notes.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark a student's written work between lessons?
faqs.answer: Work is submitted as a photograph or a document, marked against the published mark scheme or criteria, and returned with the reason for each lost mark written down rather than ticked. That record is the diagnosis: it shows whether a mark went because of a content gap, a command term that was not answered, or presentation such as a missing unit or an unlabelled axis. Ask any provider to show you an anonymised marked example before you commit, because the quality of marking varies far more than the quality of talking.

faqs.question: Can a parent sit in on an online IB lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth doing once early rather than regularly. Once tells you whether the teaching is specific and whether your child is working; regularly tends to change how a teenager behaves in the session, usually by making them quieter and less willing to be wrong in front of you. For younger students a lesson in a shared part of the home works better than a closed door. After the first observation, the session notes and the marked work are a more useful ongoing window than attendance.

faqs.question: How does a student ask a question between sessions?
faqs.answer: There should be a stated route and a stated expectation, because an open promise of unlimited availability usually means neither. A photograph of a stuck question answered within a day or so is a reasonable arrangement and genuinely useful the night before a deadline. What it should not become is a substitute for the student attempting the work, which is why a good tutor often answers with a question rather than a solution. Ask what the arrangement is and what response time is realistic before assuming either.

faqs.question: How is an Extended Essay draft handled on screen without the tutor editing it?
faqs.answer: The draft is shared read-only, and the tutor leaves comments and questions rather than changes: this paragraph asserts rather than argues, this section does not yet answer the research question, this source is described but not used. The student then makes every edit in their own document. Online delivery makes this easier to keep clean than working on paper, because the file history shows who changed what. Your school's supervision rules on how many drafts may be formally reviewed take precedence over anything a tutor offers.

faqs.question: What does a term of weekly online support for one Higher Level subject actually add up to?
faqs.answer: Arithmetic rather than a quote: one or two hours a week across a school term is roughly twelve to twenty-four hours, and you can apply whatever rate a provider quotes you to that. Advertised rates on tutoring-company listings for IB work start from about SAR 180 an hour, with Higher Level and premium tracks at roughly 200 to 220, which are their published figures and not ours. What varies more than the rate is what the hours are spent on, so agree the component before agreeing the number of hours.

faqs.question: Is a group revision course better value than one-to-one for a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: For some students, yes. A group course buys structure, pace, a fixed schedule and company, at a much lower cost per hour, and it suits a student who revises badly alone and responds to being in a cohort. What it cannot do is diagnose one student's pattern of lost marks, which is the specific thing one-to-one is for. The sensible combination is often a group course for structure plus two or three one-to-one sessions on whichever component the student's own marked work shows is leaking.

faqs.question: Do I pay per lesson or per block, and what happens to an unused lesson?
faqs.answer: Both models exist in this market and the difference matters. Per-lesson is flexible and makes it easy to drift without review. A block is usually cheaper per hour and commits you, so the question to ask is what happens to unused hours and whether they expire. Ask it before paying, get the answer in writing, and ask the same about cancellation notice for a single session. A provider who will not state either plainly is telling you how the rest of the arrangement will go.

faqs.question: Why does a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level tutor cost more than a Mathematics Applications Standard Level one?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, and the extra component. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level includes a third paper that no Standard Level candidate sits, and the pool of people who have actually prepared candidates for it is small. Applications at Standard Level is taught by far more people, including good general mathematics teachers. The rate gap is about how many people can do the job rather than about how good any of them are, which is why a Standard Level tutor at a lower rate can be excellent and still the wrong choice for a Higher Level paper.

faqs.question: Is internal assessment feedback charged differently from weekly teaching?
faqs.answer: It is usually bought differently rather than priced differently: a handful of hours spread across a term at the planning and draft stages, instead of a standing weekly slot. That shape makes it one of the cheapest effective purchases in the Diploma, because it protects a fixed share of the subject grade and most of the value sits in the first hour, on the research question and the method. Ask a provider to quote it as a finite block with a stated purpose rather than folding it into open-ended weekly hours.

faqs.question: If we can only afford one subject out of six, which should it be?
faqs.answer: Not automatically the lowest grade. Ask three questions. Which subject sits furthest below what the student is capable of, judged on marked work rather than on a report? Which component inside it is losing the marks, and is anything still in play that can be worked on calmly? And does the university plan depend on that subject specifically? A subject that is weak, recoverable and required is the answer. A subject that is weak and irrelevant to the plan may be a candidate for dropping to Standard Level rather than funding.

faqs.question: Should an IB Diploma tutor be a current school teacher or a full-time tutor?
faqs.answer: Either, for different reasons. A current teacher brings the scheme of work, the recurring pitfalls, realistic pace and often marking experience, and brings less availability, usually only one or two evenings. A full-time tutor brings one-to-one diagnostic skill honed across many students and more flexible hours, and may never have taken a cohort through to a result. The test is the same for both: ask which components they have prepared candidates for and how many cohorts, then judge the trial lesson and the marked work.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor has taught the current Diploma syllabus rather than an earlier version?
faqs.answer: Ask what changed. A tutor teaching the current syllabus can say which components exist now, what the internally assessed piece is called in their subject, and what moved when the course was last revised. Someone working from an older version will describe assessments by names and structures the school no longer uses, which a parent can check in one question to the subject teacher. Ask also which cohort they most recently taught to the end of the course, because recency matters more here than total years.

faqs.question: What does it tell me if a tutor will not name a component they have never taught?
faqs.answer: That they are selling rather than teaching, and it is the most useful signal available in a first conversation. Nobody has prepared candidates for every component of every Diploma subject at both levels, so a specialist will volunteer the limits of their experience without being pushed: taught the Higher Level papers for several cohorts, never supervised an Extended Essay in this subject, no marking experience on the third paper. That answer is reassuring precisely because it is bounded. A tutor whose experience expands to match whatever you ask for has told you that none of it is specific.

faqs.question: What happens if our IB tutor becomes unavailable part-way through the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: The handover is the thing to ask about in advance, not at the time. Diagnostic notes, the topics covered, the work set and marked, and where the internally assessed piece stands should all transfer, so a replacement starts from what is known rather than rebuilding it. Done properly a change costs one session of overlap. In the final year it is also worth asking whether the new tutor has prepared candidates for the specific papers at that level, because there is no time left to discover otherwise.

ib-online-tuition.closingHeading: Decide which component you are buying, then compare
ib-online-tuition.closingBody: Get three things from your child's subject teacher: the level, the components the candidate sits, and where the internally assessed piece currently stands. Those three answers tell you which of six subjects to fund and what the hours should be spent on, which is a harder and more valuable question than what an hour costs. Then take a free trial lesson with a specialist in that subject and level, ask for a past-paper question worked and marked with reasons, and keep the written summary whatever you decide. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, around the Sunday-to-Thursday week. No tutor travels to a Saudi address, which removes a travel loading from the rate and widens the search to whoever has actually taught the component.

ib-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: Every tutor below is listed against the subjects and levels they have actually taught, not the subjects they could cover. That distinction is the whole point of this page: a Diploma subject guide is a specific document, and the useful question is whether the tutor has worked to that one.

intro.heading: The rate is the easy part; the tutor is the thing you are buying
paragraphs: Search for IB tuition in the Kingdom and you will find a spread of advertised hourly rates with no explanation attached to any of them. One listing starts around SAR 35 an hour, another around SAR 180, a third quotes about 60 US dollars, and a fourth asks you to make contact for pricing. All four are selling something they describe as IB tutoring. None of the four pages tells you what the difference is, because the difference is the tutor and the tutor is harder to describe than a number.

So this page runs in the order a parent actually needs. The money first, because every family has a budget and the bands are knowable. Then what sits behind the money: subject scarcity, level, marking experience, and whether anyone is absorbing travel. Then the verification, which is the part nobody writes about and the part that decides whether the hour is worth anything. Then the logistics, and then what to expect at the end of a term.

The quiet fact underneath all of it is that an IB subject at Higher Level is taught by a smaller group of people than parents assume. A Diploma school needs six subject groups, two levels, options and extensions, plus Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay supervision. Schools in the Kingdom recruit against the same shortage as schools everywhere: Physics, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry with real organic depth, Computer Science, Economics at Higher Level, and languages beyond the first two. When a school cannot field a second specialist, the family goes looking outside.

Teaching online changes what "outside" means. A family in Riyadh is not restricted to tutors who can reach Riyadh, and a family in Tabuk or Jubail is not restricted to a pool of nearly nobody. The search becomes a search over everyone who has taught that subject guide at that level and can hold an evening slot on Arabia Standard Time. That is a much larger group, which is useful, and a much harder group to check, which is why the questions in the middle of this page matter more than the rate at the top of it.

A word on what is not sold here. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. We also do not produce assessed work: a tutor teaches the skill, reads the student's own draft and explains what the published criteria reward, and the student writes it. Both of those are stated plainly because a parent should know what they are buying before the first lesson rather than after it.

Nothing on this page carries a success rate, a star rating or a tutor headcount. Any figure without a sample size, a date and a method is decoration, and decoration is what the rest of this market is already full of. What is checkable is set out so you can check it.

ib-online-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and a family usually meets it at one point rather than all four. What matters for hiring is that each stage needs a different kind of teacher, and the qualification that signals competence changes as you move up.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and reporting against learning outcomes rather than paper marks. The teaching skill here is diagnostic: finding out whether a seven-year-old's reading, number sense or written explanation is actually behind, when the report card does not say so in those terms. A primary specialist is the right hire. A Diploma subject specialist is usually the wrong one, however strong they are.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom the PYP question is nearly always about a transition. A child who starts in an inquiry-led primary may move into a Cambridge Lower Secondary stream, or arrive from a national-curriculum or American primary and need to adapt to being asked to explain reasoning rather than produce answers. The useful hire is somebody who has taught both sides of that change, not somebody who has only ever worked inside one of them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessment runs against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with command terms carrying much of the weight. The Personal Project is the first substantial independent piece most students produce. A tutor who has only taught examination courses often misreads MYP marking, because a strong answer that never addresses one criterion still caps low. Ask specifically whether they have marked against MYP criteria.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision thins out quickly outside the largest cities here, so plenty of students in the Kingdom reach the Diploma from a Cambridge or MoE route instead. If your child is in an MYP stream, criterion literacy and Personal Project supervision support are the two things worth buying. If they are not, the gap to close before the Diploma is independent written research, which neither route teaches as explicitly as the MYP does.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, assessed by external papers plus Internal Assessment in almost every subject. Higher Level adds content and, in several subjects, an additional paper. This is where subject qualification stops being negotiable: a Higher Level Physics student needs somebody with a physics background who knows the extension topics, and a confident generalist will be found out inside two lessons.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students across the Kingdom share one recurring problem: the school has one specialist per subject, and that person is also running Internal Assessment supervision, Extended Essay supervision and a Standard Level class. The request that follows is narrow and sensible — one or two Higher Level subjects taught in the evening by somebody who has examined them — and it is the single most common reason a Saudi family hires online.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core contributes points through the matrix combining Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and both are marked against published criteria. TOK is not an opinion piece: marks come from specific knowledge claims, real examples and answering the prescribed title as written. The Extended Essay is a supervised piece of independent research with a reflection requirement attached to it.
programmes.countryNote: Core support is where the academic-honesty line matters most, and where this market behaves worst. A tutor may teach research method, explain the assessment criteria, question an argument and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not write, restructure or supply any part of it. Families in the Kingdom are offered the other thing routinely; a school that detects it is dealing with a malpractice case, not a grade.

ib-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Subject by subject, the qualification and experience actually worth paying for differs. This grid is written as a hiring brief rather than a syllabus summary: what to look for in the tutor, and what a weak match looks like in each subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level, look for a mathematics or engineering degree and someone comfortable with proof, complex numbers and Paper 3's extended reasoning. A tutor who can only work through standard questions will manage Standard Level and stall at Higher Level. Ask them to describe what Paper 3 rewards that Paper 1 does not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A different hire from Analysis and Approaches, not a lesser one. The course leans on modelling, statistics and technology, and the graphic display calculator is assumed. Look for somebody who teaches interpretation of output rather than button sequences, and who can explain when a statistical test is an argument rather than a procedure.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Higher Level extension has no Standard Level equivalent, so ask directly which extension topics they have taught to examination standard. The other thing to test is mathematical fluency: much of what students call difficult physics is logarithmic scales, gradients with units, and uncertainty propagation in the internal investigation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask about organic mechanisms specifically. A chemist who teaches reactions as mechanisms gets students through unfamiliar-substrate questions; one who teaches them as lists does not. Data booklet fluency and a sensibly scoped internal investigation variable are the other two things a good hire brings to the first month.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume makes this subject look like a memory exercise and it is not. The useful tutor teaches to command terms and to the mark scheme, and can handle the statistical treatment of data in the internal investigation, which is where Higher Level candidates most often lose marks they earned in the laboratory.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Look for somebody who marks diagrams as diagrams: axes, labels and a correctly shifted curve carry credit on their own. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is quantitative and needs method shown step by step. The commonest teaching failure is leaving evaluation until last and then running out of time to teach it at all.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Ask which prescribed subject and which regional option the school has chosen, because the answer determines whether the tutor's reading is relevant at all. Source work in Paper 1 is a separate skill from essay writing, and the Higher Level regional option essays demand breadth that cannot be improvised in the final term.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen guided analysis, and the failure mode is summarising rather than analysing how meaning is made. For students taught in English who speak another language at home, the gap is usually precise critical vocabulary. The Higher Level essay needs a sustained argument across a whole work, which is a planning skill.

subjects.name: Spanish B, French B and Arabic B
subjects.description: Language B needs a teacher who has marked the productive components, not simply a fluent speaker. Ask about the individual oral and how it is assessed. Students taking a language as a school-supported self-taught option need more outside teaching than anyone else in the Diploma and are the hardest group to staff locally.

subjects.name: Psychology and Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.levels: HL and SL · ESS at SL
subjects.description: Both reward command-term discipline and a precise use of studies or case material. In Psychology, the research-methods content is where marks are won and where non-specialists are exposed. In Environmental Systems and Societies, the interdisciplinary framing means a tutor from a single science background can miss what the question is actually asking.

ib-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Where families hiring online tutors actually are
ib-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Hiring an online tutor does not depend on the city, but what a family is trying to solve does. The local pool of specialists is the variable, and it changes sharply across the Kingdom. These are the places this request comes from most often, and what each one is usually short of.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest local market and still short of Higher Level specialists. The city is roughly an hour across in traffic, so families who could in principle hire locally often find that an in-home tutor's travel window, not their subject, decides whether a weekday slot exists.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, with international schooling spread along it. Families here commonly want a specialist for one Higher Level science while keeping everything else at school, and the drive north or south is what makes an in-home arrangement expensive.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: One labour and school market, with families living in one town and schooling in another. The local tutor pool is better than most of the Kingdom and still thin by subject, so requests here are usually for an option topic or an extension rather than a whole course.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with an international school presence and a transient professional population. Students arrive and leave part-way through courses, which makes mapping what has and has not been covered the first job rather than an afterthought.

regions.name: Al Ahsa and the inland Eastern Province
regions.note: An hour and a half from the coastal cluster, which rules out a daily school run for most families. Requests from here are rarely about preference; they are about a specialist pool that is close to empty at senior level.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: International provision is limited and Makkah sits roughly 80km east of Jeddah, so families either commute, board, or stay and buy subject teaching separately. Pilgrimage seasons shape the local calendar and the practical availability of evenings.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Twin cities about 25km apart in 'Asir at altitude, sharing a catchment. Distance from any large international cluster is the whole constraint, and online teaching is often the only route to a Higher Level specialist in any subject.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: Fast-changing with a growing professional population and newly arriving families. Mid-course transfers are the normal case, and a student may be the only one in their year sitting a particular subject combination.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST community
regions.note: A campus community north of Jeddah on the coast, academically dense and internationally mobile. Students here are often strong and under-served in a specific extension topic rather than in a subject as a whole, which is a precise and easy brief to match.

regions.name: Yanbu and Ha'il
regions.note: Smaller markets where senior international provision is narrow and private candidature is more common. A family here is usually choosing between relocating, boarding a child, or hiring the subject teaching and keeping everything else local.

schoolClusters.note: Between them the city's IB World Schools cover the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma Programmes, which makes a continuous IB route more realistic here than anywhere else in the Kingdom. Subject availability inside a given school is still decided by cohort size.

A mix of IB and Cambridge provision along the coast, plus the campus school at Thuwal. Families moving west mid-course usually keep their board and change their scheme of work, which is where a term of catch-up comes from.

The International Schools Group runs several campuses here and not all of them offer the Diploma, which surprises families who assume a group-wide curriculum. British-curriculum options sit alongside them in the same conurbation.

ib-online-tutor.modesIntro: Four shapes this hire takes in practice. The delivery is identical in each — live video, one tutor, one student — and what changes is the length of the commitment and what the hour is for.

modes.title: One Higher Level subject, weekly
modes.description: The commonest arrangement in the Kingdom and the one that works best. A fixed weekly hour in a single Higher Level subject with a specialist who has examined it, running through the year. The value comes from repetition: the same tutor sees the same student often enough to recognise a pattern rather than treating each lesson as a fresh problem.

It is the cheapest useful thing a relocating family can buy, because it replaces a term of guessing with a map. Sometimes it ends with the conclusion that no ongoing tutoring is needed.

sections.heading: What drives the hourly rate, and how much of it is the tutor
paragraphs: Advertised rates for IB tuition reaching Saudi families run from roughly SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to about SAR 200 to 220 for Higher Level and premium tracks, with general senior-subject private tuition quoted at SAR 200 and above and IB subject tutoring from about SAR 180. Those are advertised rates published by platforms, marketplaces and tutoring companies — marketing material, not survey data, and not what IB Gram charges. They are still useful, because the spread tells you what the market thinks it is selling at each level.

Underneath the spread sit five drivers, and they do not carry equal weight. Scarcity comes first: a Mathematics Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist and a Standard Level mathematics tutor are different markets, and the gap between those markets is wider than the gap between a weak and a strong tutor inside either. Marking experience comes second, because it changes what the hour teaches. Level comes third. Travel comes fourth, and it is the one the online format deletes rather than reduces. Commitment length comes last, and it is the only one a family controls directly.

The question worth asking a provider is not "why is this more expensive" but "which of those five is this price". A rate that is high because the tutor has marked that paper across several series is buying you something specific. A rate that is high because a company has sales staff and an office is buying you the sales staff. Both are legitimate businesses; only one of them turns up in the lesson.

The last practical point is what the hour includes. Ask before comparing two numbers: whether past papers and mark schemes are provided, whether written work is marked between lessons, whether a written report is produced, and whether contact between sessions is inside the rate. Those four add up to real hours of a tutor's week, and a cheaper rate that excludes all of them is not cheaper. A provider quoting in dollars is quoting a different product again; convert first, and expect a currency premium on top of the conversion.

sections.heading: The qualification that matters, subject by subject
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask what qualification an IB tutor should hold, and the honest answer is that it depends on the subject and the level, and that no single credential settles it. Three things carry real information. A degree in the subject itself, which matters most in mathematics and the sciences at Higher Level, where extension content runs past general numeracy. A teaching qualification, which signals that somebody has been trained to explain rather than merely to know. And direct experience of the specific IB subject guide, which is the one most likely to be missing and the one that decides whether the first lesson is useful.

Some tutors have also completed IB professional development workshops, which the organisation runs for teachers at several levels. That is worth knowing and worth asking about. It is not a licence, it is not accreditation of a tutor, and nobody should present it as one — the IB authorises schools, not private tutors, and any provider implying otherwise is describing something that does not exist.

What a degree does not cover is the gap between knowing a subject and being paid for it in an examination. A physicist can be entirely correct and still teach a student to write answers that score five out of eight, because the mark scheme rewards a particular form of words and a particular order of reasoning. That gap is why marking experience is worth a premium and why a parent should ask about it in the specific terms set out in the next section rather than accepting a general claim.

At primary and Middle Years level the hire changes shape. A Diploma specialist is usually the wrong choice for a ten-year-old: the useful person is somebody who has taught that age group, can diagnose a gap that a report card has not named, and knows how MYP criteria differ from examination marking. Hiring upwards — a Higher Level specialist for a Year 8 student — is a common and expensive mistake, and it rarely produces the thing the family wanted.

sections.heading: Four questions that verify an examiner claim
paragraphs: "Examiner experience" appears on a large share of tutor profiles in this market and means several different things, some of them nothing. At its strongest it means the tutor has marked that board's scripts for a live series, applying a published mark scheme to real candidates' work under moderation. At its weakest it means they once attended a session about assessment. The difference is worth money, and it is verifiable in four questions that take a parent thirty seconds to ask.

Which board. Which subject and level. Which component or paper. And across how many series. Somebody who has marked answers all four immediately and without rounding, because those facts are concrete to them: a component number, a subject, a count of series. Someone who has not will generalise, move to adjacent credentials, or answer a different question. You do not need to know the subject to hear the difference, which is what makes this the most useful thing a non-specialist parent can do in a trial lesson.

The follow-up is better still: ask what candidates in that component lose marks on most often. A genuine marker gives a specific, slightly dull answer — a definition stated loosely, working not shown, a command term read as a different command term, evaluation attempted in the last two minutes. A tutor who has only taught the subject answers with topics instead of with marking behaviour. Both can be good teachers; only one of them is worth paying an examiner premium to.

Two cautions. Nothing a tutor has marked permits them to tell you what grade your child will get, and no tutor can promise a grade at all; treat a guaranteed improvement as a marketing claim, not information. And examiner experience is not a substitute for current teaching knowledge of the guide your child is on, since syllabuses are revised and a tutor who marked an earlier version needs to have kept up. Ask both questions, not one.

sections.heading: Online against in-home, for the same subject and the same hour
paragraphs: The in-home comparison is worth making honestly, because in-home tuition has genuine advantages and this page is not going to pretend otherwise. A tutor in the room reads body language more easily, can take a book out of a student's hands, and is harder for a teenager to ignore. Those are real. What they are weighed against is the size of the pool, the cost of travel, and the stability of a weekly slot across a year.

The pool is the decisive factor at Higher Level. An in-home arrangement selects from tutors who can physically reach the house at the hour the student is free. In Riyadh that is a sector of a city that takes an hour to cross; in Jubail or Abha it may be a handful of people; in the inland Eastern Province it can be nobody at all. An online arrangement selects from everyone who teaches that subject guide and can hold an evening slot on Arabia Standard Time. For Standard Level mathematics the two pools may both be adequate. For Physics Higher Level extension topics they are not comparable.

Cost follows the same logic. Travel is either billed or absorbed, and in either case somebody pays for it: the quoted hour rises, or the tutor takes fewer students and prices accordingly. Published rates for senior in-home subject tuition in the Kingdom sit at the top of the local range for exactly this reason. Removing the journey removes that line, which is a cost argument rather than a quality claim.

Scheduling is the quiet third factor. An in-home slot is vulnerable to traffic, to the tutor's other bookings on the same evening, and to a school finishing late; an online slot is vulnerable to a tutor's clock change and to their own working week, both of which are fixable in advance by pinning the slot to Saudi local time and checking that their week is not Monday to Friday. One of those problems recurs every week. The other is solved once, at booking.
