sections.heading: What schools here can and cannot staff, and why that is the real brief
paragraphs: A Diploma school has to field six subject groups at two levels, with options and extensions, plus Theory of Knowledge teaching and Extended Essay supervision across the whole cohort. Doing that with a full set of specialists needs a large cohort. Most schools in the Kingdom are not that large, which means some subjects are covered by one person who also teaches the other level, and some are offered only if enough students choose them.

The pattern repeats across cities. Sciences are covered to Standard Level and stretched at Higher Level, because the extension is the last thing taught and the first thing rushed. Mathematics is structurally hard: offering both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at two levels is four distinct courses, and a department with two senior teachers cannot give all four equal attention. Languages beyond the first two depend on cohort size, so a student may be told that one language will run and another will not, which turns a subject choice into a timetable outcome. Computer Science and Economics at Higher Level are thin everywhere, not only here.

Families usually meet this as a sentence from the school rather than as a staffing fact: the subject is available, the class is large, the teacher is excellent and also responsible for forty other students' Internal Assessments. Nothing in that is anybody's failure. It is what a small cohort does to a timetable, and it is the reason the outside hire exists.

Which turns into a practical instruction for writing the brief. Do not ask for "an IB tutor". Ask for the subject, the level, the option or extension topic, where the student is in the course, and what the next assessment is. A brief at that resolution can be matched to one person who has taught exactly that. A vague brief gets a generalist, and a generalist is precisely what the school already has too few hours of.

sections.heading: The line a tutor may not cross on assessed work
paragraphs: Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and the MYP Personal Project are assessed pieces that must be the student's own work. The rule is simple to state and widely broken in this market, which is why it is set out here in the same words a tutor should use with a student in their first session.

A tutor may teach the underlying skill: experimental design, data handling, statistical treatment, referencing, how to build an argument, how to read the published criteria. A tutor may read a draft the student has written and say what the criteria reward and where the work falls short of them. A tutor may ask hard questions about a research question's scope, point out that a method will not produce usable data, or note that a conclusion does not follow from the evidence. A tutor may teach the student to do the rewriting.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, restructure or supply any part of the submitted work, may not hand over data, and may not edit a draft into a submission. A parent should also know that schools take this seriously in both directions: supervisors are required to confirm authenticity, software is used on submitted work, and a student whose own fluency does not match their submission invites a conversation they cannot win. A malpractice finding does not cost a few marks; it can cost the Diploma, and no tutoring arrangement repairs that afterwards.

The practical safeguard is a record. Lessons on assessed work should leave behind what was discussed and what the student then did, so that if a school ever asks, the answer exists and is boring. Families are entitled to ask a tutor for that record, and a tutor who cannot produce one — or who offers a finished piece instead — is selling a risk rather than a service.

sections.heading: Moving into the IB from another system, and what actually transfers
paragraphs: A large share of this market is transfer students, because the Kingdom's international population moves. Families arrive from British, American, Indian and national-curriculum schooling and meet the IB part-way through, and the quality of the first term depends almost entirely on how precisely the gap is mapped in the first fortnight.

From a British route, the content transfer is usually good and the assessment transfer is not. A student with strong IGCSE grades has the knowledge for DP1 but has rarely written to IB command terms, has not met Theory of Knowledge, and has not produced an independent investigation of Internal Assessment scope. The work is in writing and in research method rather than in content. From an American route it is often the reverse: a student used to continuous assessment and a wide subject spread meets a narrow, deep, examination-weighted course, and Higher Level sciences and mathematics are where the depth gap shows first.

From CBSE, ICSE or a national-curriculum route, the content is frequently ahead in mathematics and the sciences and the written style is the obstacle: answers are compressed, method is implicit, and the extended-response marks that the IB hands out for explanation are left on the table. A student in this group often needs less teaching than their parents expect and a different kind of it. Mid-Diploma moves are the hardest case of all, because Internal Assessment timelines differ even inside one board and a student can arrive with a draft the new school will not accept.

In every version, the same three questions are what the first diagnostic session answers. What has this student actually covered, topic by topic, against what the class has done? Where does the assessed work stand, and what does the Diploma Programme coordinator say about timelines? And what is realistic to recover in one term, written down as a short plan a parent can check at the end of the month? Transfers go badly when a family assumes the board name is the plan.

sections.heading: What the end of a term should look like
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement should be reviewable, and the review should be about school work rather than about mood. Confidence is a pleasant side effect and a terrible metric: a student can feel much better about physics while still writing uncertainty incorrectly, and a parent who asks only how it is going will be told that it is going well for a year.

What to look at instead. School assessment marks, in the component that was the problem. Marked written work, with the tutor's annotations next to the school's marks, which is the single most revealing thing a parent can read. Internal Assessment progress against the school's timeline, if assessed work was part of the brief. And one specific thing the student can now do that they could not do at the start, stated concretely: writes uncertainty correctly, draws a correctly labelled diagram without prompting, finishes Paper 1 with time to check.

If the plan was met, the sensible move is usually to narrow rather than widen: keep the slot, drop the frequency, or shift the focus to the next assessment. If it was not met, there are only three honest explanations, and it is worth naming which. The plan was wrong, the match was wrong, or the student is not doing the work between lessons. Each has a different fix, and only the second one is solved by changing tutor.

A predicted grade is the other thing families ask about at this point. It is a professional judgement made by the school from the evidence it holds, used by universities during applications, and it is not a promise of a final grade in either direction. A tutor can help a student produce the evidence that supports a better judgement. A tutor cannot set one, challenge one on the family's behalf, or guarantee what any grade will be, and should say so when asked.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the next assessment
process.description: The brief that can be matched precisely names the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, the option or extension topic if there is one, where the student is in the course, and what the next piece of assessed work is. That is four lines of a message and it is the difference between getting a specialist and getting whoever was free.

process.title: We shortlist on syllabus experience first
process.description: The search runs over tutors who have taught that subject guide at that level, and marking experience is checked in the same terms a parent would use: board, subject, component, number of series. Availability is filtered last, not first, because a free slot with the wrong tutor is not a solution to anything.

process.title: A free trial lesson, used as a diagnostic
process.description: One hour at no charge with the matched specialist. The tutor establishes what the student can and cannot do and says so plainly afterwards; the student finds out whether this person can explain things. Ask your own four verification questions during it. A tutor who answers them well will not mind being asked.

process.title: Pin the slot and check the tutor's own week
process.description: The slot is written in Arabia Standard Time and the tutor absorbs any clock change at their end. We check that their working week leaves your Sunday and Monday evenings free, because a tutor on a Monday-to-Friday school timetable cannot hold the two most useful evenings in a Saudi week.

process.title: Agree what the first month is for, in writing
process.description: Three or four checkable things, not an aspiration. Writes uncertainty correctly in the investigation. Stops losing diagram marks in Economics. Finishes Paper 1 inside the time. A plan a parent cannot check at the end of the month is a plan nobody can be held to, and it is how a term disappears quietly.

process.title: Review on a date set in advance
process.description: At the end of the first month we look at school marks and marked work rather than at how the lessons felt. If the match is wrong we change the tutor; if the plan was wrong we rewrite it. Either way the review is booked before the first lesson, so it happens whether or not anybody feels like having it.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the subject guide, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: A Diploma subject guide is a specific document with specific options and extensions. Tutors are listed against the ones they have taught, so a Physics Higher Level request does not return somebody whose last physics teaching was a Standard Level class two syllabus revisions ago.

whyPoints.title: Claims written so a parent can test them
whyPoints.description: Marking experience is recorded as board, subject, component and number of series, because that is the form in which it can be checked. Where a tutor cannot state it in those terms, it is not listed as examiner experience, and no premium attaches to it.

whyPoints.title: A national pool rather than a drivable one
whyPoints.description: The search covers everyone who teaches that guide and can hold a Saudi evening slot, which is why a family in Abha or Jubail chooses from the same tutors as a family in Riyadh. That is the practical case for the online format, and it is strongest at Higher Level.

whyPoints.title: The assessed-work boundary is stated first
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the skill, read the student's own draft and explain the criteria. They do not write, rewrite or supply any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, TOK essay or Personal Project. The student hears that in the first session rather than discovering it at a deadline.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their source attached
whyPoints.description: Every SAR figure on this page is an advertised rate published by a platform, marketplace or tutoring company, labelled as such. None of it is a market average, and none of it is our price. A number without a source is marketing, and this market has enough of that already.

whyPoints.title: No statistic we cannot stand behind
whyPoints.description: No success rate, no star rating, no tutor headcount, no guaranteed improvement. Any figure without a sample size, a date and a method tells a parent nothing, and a grade guarantee tells them something that is not true. What we will put in writing is the tutor's experience and the first month's plan.

faqs.question: What degree should an IB online tutor hold for Higher Level sciences?
faqs.answer: A degree in that science, or in engineering where the content overlaps closely, plus teaching experience of the current subject guide. The reason is specific rather than snobbish: the Higher Level extension topics run past general science literacy, and a tutor who is working a chapter ahead of the student cannot anticipate where the question is going. Ask which extension topics they have taught to examination standard, and ask what the internal investigation requires in terms of uncertainty and data treatment. Those two answers separate a subject graduate who has taught the course from somebody who is confident with the first half of it.

faqs.question: Do IB professional development workshops make a tutor accredited by the IB?
faqs.answer: No. The IB runs professional development for teachers at several levels, and attending it is worth knowing about because it indicates familiarity with how the organisation frames assessment. It is not a licence to tutor and it is not accreditation of an individual or a company. The IB authorises schools to offer its programmes; it does not approve private tutors or tutoring businesses. Any provider implying that it holds IB approval is describing something that does not exist, and that is a reason for caution about everything else on the page.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest for a school in the Kingdom to staff at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: The same ones that are hard everywhere, concentrated by smaller cohorts. Physics and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry with genuine organic depth, Computer Science, Economics at Higher Level, and languages beyond the first two. Within those, it is usually the extension and option topics rather than the core that go short, because they are taught last and compressed when the year runs tight. That is why outside requests from Saudi families are so often narrow and late in the course rather than broad and early.

faqs.question: What should a parent ask a school about subject availability before enrolling a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which subjects run at Higher Level this year rather than in the prospectus. How many teachers the department has for the subject your child wants, and whether one person covers both levels. Whether the language your child needs will run, and what minimum cohort it depends on. And who supervises Extended Essays, and how many each supervisor carries. Schools answer these readily. The answers tell you, before you enrol, which subject is likely to need outside teaching in the second year.

faqs.question: How do families here handle a subject their school offers only online or not at all?
faqs.answer: Three routes are common. The school arranges a provider and the student takes the subject remotely while remaining enrolled, which works but leaves the student without a teacher in the building. The student takes it as a school-supported self-taught option, which is the hardest version and the one most dependent on outside teaching. Or the family changes the subject combination, which is the honest answer more often than parents expect, since a subject chosen and then abandoned in the second year costs more than a different choice made early.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an Extended Essay draft my child has written?
faqs.answer: Read it, question the argument, point out where the evidence does not support the conclusion, explain what the published criteria reward, and check that the research question is answerable at the length allowed. They may teach referencing and research method, and they may explain what the reflection component is for. They may not write, rewrite or restructure any part of it, supply material to be inserted, or edit a draft into a submission. The student does the rewriting, every time, and the tutor keeps a record of what was discussed.

faqs.question: How can I be confident the Internal Assessment my child submits is genuinely their own?
faqs.answer: Three practical checks. Ask your child to explain their method and their results to you without notes; a student who did the work can, and one who did not cannot. Read the drafts in order, because genuine work improves unevenly while supplied work arrives finished. And ask the tutor for a record of what each session covered. Schools do their own checks, supervisors confirm authenticity, and submitted work is screened, so the cost of getting this wrong falls on the student rather than on whoever sold the shortcut.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose an Internal Assessment topic without crossing the line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where a good tutor earns their fee. They can explain what makes a topic assessable, test whether a proposed investigation will produce usable data, point out that a variable is unmeasurable with school equipment, and send a student back to narrow a question that is too broad. What they cannot do is hand over the topic as a finished specification, or select it so completely that the student cannot explain why. The test is whether the student can defend the choice in their own words to their supervisor.

faqs.question: Does a tutor's feedback on a TOK essay count as help or as misconduct?
faqs.answer: Feedback on the student's own draft is legitimate and expected; producing or rewriting the essay is misconduct. In practice the useful work is teaching what the prescribed title actually asks, since most weak TOK essays answer a nearby question instead, and showing how a knowledge claim is supported with a real example rather than an opinion. A tutor can mark a draft against the criteria and explain what is missing. The student then writes it again. If the finished essay does not sound like the student, the school will notice.

faqs.question: What does a student moving from a British school into DP1 need to catch up first?
faqs.answer: Usually not content. Strong IGCSE grades generally cover what DP1 assumes, so the gap sits in three other places. Writing to IB command terms, which differ from the phrasing a British examination uses and change what the answer must contain. Theory of Knowledge, which has no equivalent in their previous school and reads as unfamiliar for a term. And independent investigation at Internal Assessment scope, which is longer and more self-directed than coursework they will have met. A term of writing practice usually does more than a term of revision.

faqs.question: What does an American-curriculum student most often struggle with in Higher Level mathematics?
faqs.answer: Depth and examination weighting at once. A student used to continuous assessment, broad subject coverage and frequent small tests meets a two-year course where most of the grade arrives in a few papers at the end, and where Higher Level assumes algebraic fluency built earlier. Proof, rigorous notation and extended multi-step problems are the usual pressure points. The fix is specific: rebuild the algebra until it is fast, then practise whole questions rather than exercises, because the difficulty is sustaining a chain of reasoning rather than performing a step.

faqs.question: Is it realistic to move into the IB Diploma after the first term has started?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends far more on the assessed work than on the content. Content gaps in one subject are recoverable with a weekly hour and honest homework. What is harder is the Internal Assessment timeline, which differs between schools inside the same board, and the Theory of Knowledge and CAS requirements that run across both years. The first conversation belongs with the school's Diploma Programme coordinator in the first week, not the fourth, because the realistic options narrow as the term goes on.

faqs.question: What happens to coursework a transfer student completed at their previous school?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the board and how far the piece had progressed, and only the new school can answer it. Some work carries across because it was produced against the same criteria; some cannot, because the new school's teaching sequence or chosen option differs. Either way the question goes to the Diploma Programme coordinator with the actual drafts in hand during the first week. Outside teaching is useful after that answer exists, not before it, because a tutor cannot sensibly plan around work that may be restarted.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell me what grade my child will get at the end of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to should be treated with real scepticism. Final grades depend on papers sat under examination conditions, on moderation, and on grade boundaries that are set after the series rather than before it. What a good tutor can give you is a position: what the student can currently do against the demands of the paper, which components are furthest behind, and what would need to change. That is more useful than a prediction, because it names something a family can act on.

faqs.question: How is a predicted grade decided, and can tutoring change it?
faqs.answer: The school makes it, as a professional judgement from the evidence it holds — class assessments, mock papers, coursework progress — and universities use it during the application cycle. It is not a promise of a final grade in either direction, and it is not negotiable by a parent or a tutor. What tutoring can do is change the evidence the judgement is based on, by producing better marked work before the judgement is made. That means the useful time to start is before the predictions are set, not after a family is disappointed by one.

faqs.question: What is a reasonable way to compare two tutoring quotes that look very different?
faqs.answer: Convert both into the same currency and the same unit, then list what each includes: past papers and mark schemes, written work marked between lessons, a written report, contact between sessions, and whether a named tutor is guaranteed rather than a pool. Those items are hours of someone's week, and a lower rate that excludes all of them is not lower. Then ask which of the five rate drivers each price reflects. A premium for scarcity and marking experience buys something that appears in the lesson; a premium for overheads does not.

ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Hire for the syllabus, then test the claim in a free trial lesson
ib-online-tutor.closingBody: Send four lines: the subject, the level, the option or extension topic, and what the next assessment is. We will shortlist tutors who have taught that subject guide, record their marking experience in a form you can check, and put one of them in a free trial hour with your child. Use the hour to ask the four verification questions on this page — which board, which subject, which component, how many series — and watch how precisely they are answered. If the match is right, you will both know by the end of it. Everything is taught one to one, live online, on Arabia Standard Time.

ib-private-tuition.heroSubtitle: IB private tuition in Saudi Arabia is bought at the wrong time more often than it is bought from the wrong person. A Diploma grade is assembled over two years from components that close one after another, and by the time a family feels the urgency, several of them are already sealed. So this page runs the year backwards from the May session: what each component is worth, when it stops being changeable, what the word limits are, and where a term of one-to-one teaching over live video still moves a grade.

ib-private-tuition.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB subjects one-to-one over live video. What distinguishes the work on this page is sequencing: a tutor joining in the first Diploma year does a different job from one joining in the final term, and the honest conversation is about which of the two you are buying.

intro.heading: A Diploma grade closes in instalments, not at the end
paragraphs: Parents tend to picture the Diploma as a long preparation followed by examinations that decide everything. It does not work that way, and the misunderstanding is expensive. The grade closes in instalments. An internal assessment is drafted, submitted and effectively finished while the written papers are still a year away. The Extended Essay goes through supervision, reflection and submission on its own timetable. Theory of Knowledge is examined through an essay and an exhibition. By the time the final papers arrive, a substantial share of the total is already banked, for better or worse, and no amount of revision reopens it.

Which means the single most useful question about private tuition is not whether to buy it but when. A term of teaching in the first Diploma year can change a subject choice, close a foundation gap and rescue an internal assessment while it is still a draft. The same term bought eight weeks before the papers can only improve execution: timing, command-term discipline, and the two or three topics that keep costing marks. Both are worth having. They are not substitutes, and a family who buys the second thinking they have bought the first is disappointed for reasons nobody explains to them.

This page therefore runs the course in reverse. It starts with what a Diploma grade is actually made of, component by component, and when each component stops being changeable. It then sets out the word and page limits, because those are the hard constraints a student plans against and most families have never seen them in one place. From there it works through the first Diploma year, the second, mock season and predicted grades, the final eight weeks, and what remains possible after results arrive.

The Saudi context shapes the timetable in ways the IB's own calendar does not describe. Almost every IB school in the Kingdom sits the May session, so the working year runs towards one point. The school week is Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, which decides what a working study week looks like. International and British-curriculum schools set their own term dates and most run three terms, while public-sector schools run a two-semester year, so two families in the same city can be in different terms on the same day. Ramadan drifts roughly eleven days earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, so it lands in a different part of the course for each cohort.

One structural note before any of it. Tuition for families in the Kingdom is delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For the work this page describes, that arrangement is an advantage rather than a compromise: a draft internal assessment is read and annotated on a shared screen more effectively than across a kitchen table, and a Higher Level specialist can be reached from Jubail or Tabuk as easily as from central Riyadh.

ib-private-tuition.programmesIntro: Four stages, described by what closes during each rather than by what is taught. Read them as a sequence of doors shutting: the useful intervention is always the one made while a door is still open, and a great deal of tuition is bought a term after the relevant one has closed.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Marked against four published criteria per subject, each out of eight, rather than as a percentage. The programme's final years carry the Personal Project, assessed on process as much as product, with a report that has its own length requirement. Nothing here feeds directly into a Diploma grade, which is exactly why it is the cheapest stage at which to fix a habit that would otherwise cost marks for five more years.
programmes.countryNote: The door that closes at the end of this programme is subject choice. A student who arrives at the Diploma without the algebraic fluency for a Higher Level mathematics course, or without the writing structure every essay subject assumes, has their options narrowed before anyone discusses them. Families in the Kingdom whose schools offer only part of this programme should ask what the receiving Diploma school expects to see.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: Six subjects with three normally at Higher Level, the Theory of Knowledge course, the Extended Essay begun, and the creativity, activity and service requirement running alongside. Most internal assessment work starts here, and most of it is where the following year's grade is quietly determined. Students who coast through this year on strong IGCSE results are reliably the ones who find the Higher Level extension brutal in the next.
programmes.countryNote: Three doors close during this year, and families rarely notice any of them. The level decision, which becomes difficult to reverse once teaching groups are set. The Extended Essay subject and research question. And the internal assessment topics, which determine whether the work can be done well with the apparatus, data or sources actually available. A Saudi family planning a local university route should also read the target programme's criteria during this year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: Internal assessments are finished and submitted, the Extended Essay completes its reflections, Theory of Knowledge is assessed, predicted grades are issued for university applications, and the written papers sit at the end. The work shifts from building knowledge to converting it: by mock season, a mark is more often lost to a misread command term or to running out of time than to not knowing the content.
programmes.countryNote: The deadline that catches Saudi-based families out is the predicted grade, because it is issued well before the papers and drives every overseas offer. For a local university route the equivalency decision and the Qiyas tests sit in the same year on their own timetable. Two separate deadline sets in one year is the real difficulty of the final Diploma year, and the reason tuition here should be sequenced rather than piled on.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS
programmes.description: The core runs across both years and contributes up to 3 points to the total of 45 through a published matrix combining the Theory of Knowledge grade with the Extended Essay grade. A failing grade in either can prevent the award of the Diploma whatever the six subject grades add up to. The Theory of Knowledge essay answers a prescribed title; the exhibition works from objects and a prompt.
programmes.countryNote: The core is treated as paperwork in the first year and as an emergency in the second, which is the wrong way round in both. Because the Extended Essay is supervised at school and has a fixed word limit, the useful outside help is early and narrow: narrowing a research question until it can be answered within the limit using sources the student can actually reach from where they live.

ib-private-tuition.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by when its grade is actually decided, because that is what determines when tuition is worth buying for it. Some subjects are won in the first year and merely confirmed in the second; others can still be moved eight weeks out. Knowing which is which is most of good planning.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Decided early. Fluency is cumulative, so a gap left in the first year is still being paid for in the final papers, and the Higher Level third paper of extended problems punishes exactly that kind of weakness. The exploration is a fifth of the grade and its topic is chosen in the first year. Late tuition here buys technique; early tuition changes what is possible.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Partly late-moveable. Calculator technique, regression work and the discipline of tying a conclusion back to the data are all learnable in a term, which makes this one of the more responsive subjects close to a series. The exploration is not: its data source has to be chosen early enough that the student can actually obtain the data.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Decided across both years. The Higher Level content layers onto the shared core, so a core topic left weak in the first year is examined twice in the second. The investigation closes earliest of all: its research question must suit the apparatus the school has, which is a first-year conversation and not a second-year one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mixed. Mole reasoning and mechanism notation respond well to a focused term at almost any point, and the data booklet can be taught in two sessions. The investigation is an early door, and the organic and energetics sequences build, so a student who did not consolidate the first year arrives at the final papers repairing two years at once.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mostly late-moveable, unusually for a science. Definitions marked to the word, data-handling technique and the discipline of writing to a list of creditable points are all teachable in a term. What is not late-moveable is the investigation, and students who treat biology as a memory subject until mock season discover the extended responses do not reward fluency.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Decided by habit rather than by date. Guided analysis of an unseen passage rewards close work on technique and structure, which is a practice built over terms, not weeks. The Higher Level essay on a studied work is a separate component with its own window. The individual oral depends on texts chosen much earlier in the course.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Late-moveable on the papers, early on the internal assessment. Diagram accuracy and the discipline of shifting the right curve correctly are drillable in weeks. The three commentaries are each built on a recent article and marked on the application of a named key concept, and they are spread across the course rather than written in one go.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The third Higher Level paper is the earliest-closing component in the subject, because it rests on a pre-released case study that rewards months of preparation. Everything else responds to a term of work. The internal assessment closes early for a practical reason: students choose organisations that cannot supply the information the commentary needs.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Decided by coverage. The Higher Level regional-option third paper is worth more than a third of the grade and cannot be crammed, because it rewards breadth no eight-week push supplies. Source technique on the first paper, by contrast, is one of the most improvable things in the whole Diploma and can move a grade inside a term.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Mostly late-moveable, with one hard early deadline. Using named studies as evidence, with researcher, design and finding attached, is learnable in a term of disciplined work. The internal assessment is a replication written to a strict structure with marked statistical treatment, and it has to be run before it can be written.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The developed product is the earliest deadline and the one most often left latest. Documented design and testing carry criterion marks independent of how good the program is, so students who build first and write up afterwards lose marks that were never about code. Written-paper technique on pseudocode and trace tables is improvable late.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two fixed windows and no content to revise. The essay answers a prescribed title within a hard word limit and is assessed on the quality of the argument about knowledge. The exhibition works from objects and a prompt with its own shorter limit. Both reward early thinking and punish late assembly, and neither can be improved by collecting more examples.

ib-private-tuition.regionsTitle: When families in each part of the Kingdom tend to start, and why
ib-private-tuition.regionsIntro: Enquiries do not arrive evenly across the year, and the pattern differs by city for reasons that have nothing to do with ambition. Relocation seasons, pilgrimage traffic, industrial rotations and the simple fact that different schools are in different terms all shape when a family decides. Starting at the right point matters more than starting early in the abstract.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The largest Diploma cohort in the Kingdom, and the city where families most often start in the term after a disappointing mock rather than at the beginning of a year. The useful correction here is to move the decision one term earlier, because in Riyadh specialist slots for the scarce Higher Level subjects fill well before mock season does.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: School calendars vary widely along the coastal city, so two Diploma students in Jeddah can be several weeks apart in the same syllabus. Families here benefit most from working to their own school's published term dates and internal deadlines rather than to any general account of when the year turns.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: Transfers between campuses inside this single school market happen mid-year more than anywhere else in the Kingdom, and a transfer resets what has been covered without resetting the deadlines. The first job for an arriving student here is a coverage audit against the new school's scheme of work.

regions.name: Jubail and the industrial cities
regions.note: Rotation work shapes when a family can commit, and a parent away for a month cannot supervise a new arrangement. Starting at the beginning of a rotation rather than in the middle of one, and making the student the owner of the sessions from the first week, is what makes a term of tuition survive here.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Pilgrimage seasons bend the household year in ways no school calendar records, so a term plan built here should name in advance the weeks that will be missed and the weeks that will absorb them. A pattern agreed up front holds; week-by-week rescheduling loses a scarce specialist's slot.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: The northwest produces more mid-course arrivals than any other part of the Kingdom, as families relocate into new developments during a Diploma year. Catching up mid-course has a sequence to it, and it begins with establishing what the previous school had and had not taught rather than with new content.

regions.name: Thuwal and the KAUST campus
regions.note: A campus community with a highly mobile population, where a student may be two years into one curriculum and then move. Continuity across a move is the planning problem here, and the written diagnosis and session notes are what make a handover to a new school or tutor quick rather than slow.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait, Al Ahsa and Yanbu
regions.note: Smaller cohorts where the local pool of specialists in a given Higher Level subject is thin for structural reasons. Families in these centres should start earlier than they think necessary, purely because the choice of specialist narrows sharply once the term before a series begins.

schoolClusters.note: Every date that matters to a Diploma student is held locally: the internal entry deadline, the school's own internal assessment deadlines, mock weeks and the issue of predicted grades. These schools run the Diploma or Cambridge programmes in the Kingdom, and students we support attend schools including them.

schoolClusters.city: Where calendars diverge in the same city
schoolClusters.note: International and British-curriculum schools set their own term dates and most run three terms, while public-sector schools run a two-semester year starting in late August and ending in late June. Two students in the same city can therefore be in different terms, which is why no term plan should be built from a national calendar.

The Eastern Province cluster absorbs transfers between campuses during the year, and the Diploma runs at some campuses and not at others. An arriving student's first need is a coverage audit, not a tutor teaching forward from wherever the new class happens to be.

ib-private-tuition.modesIntro: Four shapes of private tuition, defined by where in the course they sit rather than by how many hours they contain. The honest conversation at the start is about which one you are buying, because each can do things the others cannot and none of them does everything.

modes.title: A full-year weekly place
modes.description: One subject, one hour a week, held across a year, with work set after each session and marked before the next. This is the only arrangement that can change what is possible rather than merely improving execution, because it reaches the internal assessment and the foundation gaps while both are still open. It is also the least dramatic and the most effective.

modes.title: A single-term intervention
modes.description: One term, one subject, one named problem: a topic sequence that never landed, a component that keeps costing marks, a drafting process that has stalled. It has a defined end from the start, which is what distinguishes it from open-ended tuition. The right use is between a diagnosis and a deadline, with enough time to actually act.
bullets: One named component, agreed in writing at the start
An end date set before the first session

modes.title: A pre-series block
modes.description: The final weeks, built on timed papers marked against the published mark scheme rather than on new content. The value is in the marking and the pattern it reveals: the same three weaknesses usually account for most of the lost marks, and naming them is what changes the next paper. New content in this window is almost always displacement activity.
bullets: Timed papers under something close to real conditions
Command-term drilling and question-timing work
Scheduled around the school's own revision weeks
Booked early, because scarce specialists fill first

modes.title: A post-results plan
modes.description: After results, two questions matter: whether a remark is worth requesting, and whether a retake or a November entry makes sense. Both are decisions before they are teaching jobs. A retake candidate has an advantage the first attempt did not: the marks and the examiner's report show precisely where the grade was lost.
bullets: Remark and retake decisions taken on evidence, not on feeling
A plan built from the previous attempt's component marks

The school holds the entry route and the deadlines

sections.heading: What a Diploma grade is made of, and when each piece closes
paragraphs: Take the Diploma apart and it stops being mysterious. The total runs to 45 points: up to 7 in each of six subjects, plus up to 3 from the core, where the Theory of Knowledge grade and the Extended Essay grade are read together on a published matrix. Within each subject the grade is assembled from written papers and at least one internally assessed component, and in most subjects that internal component is worth between a fifth and a third of the subject grade on its own.

The part families miss is the sequencing. Internal assessment work is drafted, supervised, submitted and effectively finished while the written papers are still months or a year away. Once it has gone, it is a fixed quantity. A student who submitted a weak investigation and then revises heroically for the papers is competing for a smaller remaining share of the grade, and no one tells them this at the time. The same is true of the Extended Essay and of the Theory of Knowledge components, each of which closes on its own schedule.

Which turns planning into something concrete. For each of your child's six subjects, write down the internally assessed component, what it is worth, and the school's internal deadline for it. That single sheet of paper is a better planning document than any revision timetable, because it shows which parts of the grade are still open. Private tuition bought while a component is open can change the component; bought afterwards it can only work on what is left.

sections.heading: Word and page limits, by component
paragraphs: These are hard constraints and most families never see them in one place, which is why students write to the length that feels thorough and then face a cut they have no time for. A limit is not a target to approach; it is a ceiling that shapes what the piece can attempt. An Extended Essay research question that needs six thousand words to answer properly is the wrong research question, and the moment to discover that is while it is still a question rather than a draft.

The limits also explain the single most common coursework failure, which is scope. A student picks an ambitious topic, writes a long introduction establishing context, and runs out of allowance before the analysis that actually carries the criteria. The fix is structural and it is applied at the planning stage: decide what the piece has to prove, allocate the words to the criteria that reward proving it, and cut the context paragraph that feels necessary and earns nothing.

Treat the table as a planning aid and confirm each figure against the current subject guide with your child's coordinator, because the IB revises guides on a rolling cycle and your school holds the version your child is entered for. What does not change is the discipline: know the limit before the first outline, write to the criteria rather than to the page, and be suspicious of any draft where the analysis begins past the halfway mark.

sections.heading: The first Diploma year, where the grade is quietly set
paragraphs: Everything that is hard to change later is decided in this year, and almost nothing feels urgent in it. The level decision comes first: three Higher Level subjects chosen partly on interest, partly on what the school can actually staff, and partly on what a university course will require two years from now. Reversing it once teaching groups are set ranges from awkward to impossible, and a student carrying a Higher Level subject they cannot sustain spends two years paying for one afternoon's optimism.

Then the internal assessment topics, which look like small decisions and are not. A science investigation needs a research question answerable with the apparatus the school has. A Business Management commentary needs an organisation that will supply real information. An Economics commentary needs articles that genuinely illustrate a key concept. A History investigation needs sources the student can reach. Each of these is a planning conversation worth having before the writing starts, and each is the sort of thing a specialist spots in ten minutes and a student discovers in six weeks.

Content-wise, the first year is where foundations either get consolidated or quietly do not. Higher Level content in most subjects layers onto a shared core, so a core topic left shaky is examined twice over in the second year. This is the cheapest possible moment to buy teaching and the moment families are least inclined to: nothing has gone visibly wrong, the first reports are acceptable, and the papers are far away. A term of weekly work here does what no amount of work in the final eight weeks can.
bullets: Confirm the Higher Level combination against university prerequisites, not interest alone
Vet every internal assessment topic for feasibility before writing begins
Treat a shaky core topic as a second-year problem already in progress
Ask for the school's internal assessment deadlines in writing this year

sections.heading: Mock season, predicted grades and the offers they decide
paragraphs: Mocks are treated as practice and function as something closer to a selection event. The school's predicted grades, which drive every overseas university offer, are issued on the evidence available at the time, and mock performance is usually the largest part of that evidence alongside internal assessment work already submitted. A student who treats the mock as a rehearsal and the real papers as the performance has the order backwards: by the time the real papers arrive, the offers have already been made on the basis of the rehearsal.

That has a clear implication for timing. The term before mock season is the highest-value window in the entire Diploma for private tuition, higher even than the weeks before the final papers, because work done then shows up in the evidence the school uses. Families who arrive after a disappointing mock are asking tuition to repair something that has already been priced into their offers. The work is still worth doing; it is simply a term late.

The second thing mocks produce, if anyone reads them properly, is a diagnosis. Marks lost should be sorted into three categories: content not known, command term misread, and time run out. They have different remedies, and a revision plan that treats all three as a knowledge problem addresses the wrong one. A student who ran out of time does not need more content; they need question allocation practised under a clock. Most mock papers get a grade and a sigh rather than this analysis, which is a waste of the only full-length diagnostic a student gets before the real thing.
bullets: Predicted grades are issued before the papers and decide the offers

sections.heading: How 45 points are built, and why the core is not paperwork
paragraphs: Six subjects at up to 7 points each gives 42, and the core supplies up to 3 more through a matrix that reads the Theory of Knowledge grade and the Extended Essay grade together. The arithmetic matters for a reason beyond the total: a failing grade in a core component can prevent the award of the Diploma regardless of how strong the six subject grades are. A student can be comfortably above the points requirement and still not be awarded the Diploma because of a core condition, and that outcome arrives as a complete surprise to families who treated the core as administration.

Grade boundaries add the second piece of the picture. Boundaries are set after papers are marked, not before they are sat, because they exist to hold the standard constant when a paper turns out harder or easier than intended. A past paper's boundaries are therefore a guide and never a target, and the sensible approach is to aim a clear margin above the boundary a student is chasing rather than at it. Families who plan to a boundary to the mark are planning to an unknown.

Put the two together and a planning rule falls out. Points are won in whole marks across many components, not in a heroic final push on one. A core point secured in the first year through a decent Extended Essay is worth exactly as much as a point squeezed out of a final paper, and it is enormously easier to obtain. That is the argument for treating the core as examined work from the start, and it is also why a tutor whose first question is about the Extended Essay rather than about the papers is reading the situation correctly.

sections.heading: The last eight weeks: execution, not teaching
paragraphs: In the final stretch the work changes character completely, and tuition that does not change with it is being sold rather than taught. Nothing new can be built in eight weeks, and attempting it displaces the work that still pays. What pays is a cycle: a paper sat under timed conditions, marked against the published mark scheme, the pattern in the lost marks named out loud, and that pattern drilled before the next paper. Three or four rounds of this moves grades. A sweep through the whole syllabus does not.

The pattern that emerges is usually smaller than anyone expects. Most students lose most of their remaining marks to the same two or three things: one topic sequence that never landed, a habit of answering a command term with the wrong shape of answer, and poor time allocation across a paper. Naming those three and working on nothing else feels irresponsibly narrow and is the correct strategy. Breadth in the last eight weeks is comfort, not method.

Two practical points for Saudi families. The school's own revision weeks and study-leave arrangements should be known before a block is booked, so paid sessions do not duplicate school provision. And the Sunday-to-Thursday week means the natural home for a full timed paper is Friday or Saturday, when a student is not post-school tired and the two or three hours a real paper needs actually exist. Sitting a full paper properly once a week in the final stretch is worth more than three partial attempts squeezed into school evenings.
bullets: A timed paper, marked to the real scheme, then the pattern drilled
Work on two or three named weaknesses and nothing else
Check the school's revision weeks before booking a block

sections.heading: Where private tuition fits beside the school, without competing with it
paragraphs: A tutor who teaches against the school produces a confused student, and it happens more than families realise. Schools order the syllabus differently, choose different options within a subject, and set internal deadlines that are theirs rather than the board's. A tutor who covers topics in a different sequence, or who teaches an option the school did not choose, is adding load rather than removing it. The fix is to ask for the scheme of work or term plan at the start, and to expect a good tutor to request it unprompted.

On assessed work the boundary is not a matter of etiquette but of rules. The Extended Essay is supervised at school, and internal assessments are the student's own work submitted through the school. A tutor's legitimate role is to read what the student has written, map it against the published criteria, ask the questions an examiner would ask, and send the student away to redraft. They do not write any of it, including when a deadline is two days away and everybody is anxious. A provider willing to cross that line is trading a malpractice risk that can cost an entire Diploma for a few marks.

Keeping a written feedback trail serves the student twice. It records what was discussed and what the student then changed, which is the clearest available evidence that the work is genuinely their own. And it gives the school something concrete if a question ever arises. Families sometimes assume discretion is safer here; the opposite is true. Documented, criterion-referenced feedback on a student's own draft is both the legitimate form of help and the easiest to defend.
bullets: Ask for the scheme of work; a good tutor asks first
Teach in the school's sequence, not a tutor's preferred one
Assessed work is written by the student, with no deadline exception
Keep written feedback as the record of the drafting process

sections.heading: After results: remarks, retakes and the November route
paragraphs: Results day produces decisions before it produces teaching, and the decisions have short windows. The first is whether to request a remark, which is worth considering when a grade sits just below a boundary that matters and the component marks suggest an anomaly rather than a pattern. It is not worth doing on disappointment alone, because a remark can confirm the original or occasionally move the other way, and the school holds the process and the deadline.

The second decision is a retake. For Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel candidates, both boards run a June series, which is the main one for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and November-entry candidates. The February and March series Cambridge operates is available only in India, so a Saudi family planning around a spring sitting has read advice written for another market. Diploma retake arrangements run on their own terms and your coordinator is the authority on what is possible and by when.

A retake candidate has one real advantage over their first attempt, and it is worth using properly. The component marks and the examiner's report show precisely where the grade was lost, which turns a vague revision plan into a targeted one. A student who lost the grade on one paper does not need to retake the whole course in their head. That is the difference between a second attempt that repeats the first and one that fixes it, and it is also the argument for planning the retake in the week after results rather than three months later.

sections.heading: Starting at the right point, and what each starting point can achieve
paragraphs: The honest version of this conversation names a ceiling. A family starting in the first Diploma year can change what is possible: levels, internal assessment topics, foundations, and the core. A family starting in the term before mocks can change the evidence the school uses for predicted grades, which changes the offers. A family starting in the final eight weeks can change execution, and execution is worth a grade in many cases but not three. A family starting after results can target a retake precisely. All four are legitimate purchases and they are not the same purchase.

What a provider should never do is accept a late start and imply an early one's outcome. If a student is four weeks from the papers and two years behind in a Higher Level subject, the useful answer involves triage and expectation-setting, not an intensive package. We would rather tell a family that than sell them twenty hours against an outcome nobody can deliver. Equally, a family arriving early should be told when tuition is not needed at all, which happens: a well-staffed subject with a specialist teacher and a student doing the work may need nothing.

In practice the sequence we recommend is dull and it works. Audit the six subjects for internally assessed components and deadlines. Identify which two matter most for the university route being considered. Buy weekly teaching in those, starting a term before it feels necessary. Add a pre-series block only if the diagnosis says execution is the remaining problem. Review at the end of each term with stopping on the list. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, and the slot is written in Saudi local time so it does not drift.

process.title: Audit the six subjects first
process.description: Before buying any hours, list each subject's internally assessed component, roughly what it carries, and the school's deadline for it. That sheet shows which parts of the grade are still open. Send it to us with the subject and level and we will tell you which one we would work on first.

process.title: Agree which purchase this is
process.description: A full-year place, a single-term intervention, a pre-series block or a post-results plan. Each can do things the others cannot, and naming it at the start prevents the commonest disappointment in this market, which is a late start measured against an early start's expectations.

process.title: A free trial lesson, taught not pitched
process.description: The tutor teaches something real, usually a question your child has already got wrong or a paragraph of a draft. You are watching whether they locate the component, explain it in a way your child follows, and name what they would change first. Ask them what is still open and what is already closed.

process.title: A written diagnosis with dates in it
process.description: After the first working session: the component and topics where marks are being lost, the order of work, and the deadlines it has to fit around. Dates make it checkable. It is also the document that survives a change of tutor or a change of school, which happens more often than families plan for.

process.title: Weekly work, marked before the next session
process.description: Work set after each session and marked before the next, with a short written note of what was taught, what was set and what the work showed. The marking is where the diagnosis gets refined, and the notes are the record of the process if a coursework question ever arises.

process.title: Review each term against the dates
process.description: Whether the open components are moving, whether a different subject is now the bigger risk, and whether to continue. Stopping is on the list. So is moving the hours: a term spent on the wrong subject is a worse outcome than a term not bought, and we would rather say so in week twelve than in month six.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the deadline backwards
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from what closes when: internal assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay, mock season, the predicted grade, the May session. That ordering is what lets a family spend on the component that is still open rather than on the one that already closed, which is where most tuition budgets are quietly wasted.

whyPoints.title: Honest about ceilings
whyPoints.description: A term in the first Diploma year changes what is possible; eight weeks before the papers changes execution. We will tell you which one you are buying and what it can realistically achieve, including when the answer is triage rather than a package. No grade, score or improvement is guaranteed by anyone in this market.

whyPoints.title: The limits and the structure, in writing
whyPoints.description: Word and page limits by component, what each component carries, and when it closes, all on one page rather than scattered across subject guides. Confirm the figures with your coordinator, because guides are revised on a cycle and your school holds the version your child sits.

whyPoints.title: Built for the Saudi week and the May session
whyPoints.description: Almost every IB school in the Kingdom sits the May session, the school week runs Sunday to Thursday, and term dates differ school by school. Slots are written in Arabia Standard Time, full timed papers are placed on Friday or Saturday, and plans are built from your own school's calendar rather than a national one.

whyPoints.title: Assessed work stays the student's
whyPoints.description: On an internal assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay the tutor reads, questions and maps against the published criteria, and the student redrafts. Nothing is written for them, including two days before a deadline. The written feedback trail is deliberate, because it evidences whose work it is.

whyPoints.title: We work with the school, not around it
whyPoints.description: We ask for the scheme of work and teach in the school's sequence, because a tutor running a different order produces a confused student. The school holds every date that matters, issues the predicted grade and supervises the Extended Essay, and we will send you back to them rather than guess.

faqs.question: Which parts of a Diploma grade are already decided before the written papers begin?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. Each subject has at least one internally assessed component, usually worth between a fifth and a third of that subject's grade, and it is submitted through the school long before the papers. The Extended Essay and both Theory of Knowledge components are also finished and submitted on their own schedules. Together that is a substantial share of the total, fixed and unreopenable. Listing each component and its school deadline on one sheet is the most useful planning exercise a Diploma family can do.

faqs.question: How long may an Extended Essay be, and what happens to the part that runs over?
faqs.answer: The limit is 4,000 words, and examiners are not required to read beyond it, so anything past the limit simply does not count towards the criteria. That is harsher than a penalty: a student whose conclusion sits in the overrun has effectively submitted an essay with no conclusion. The practical consequence is that length discipline belongs at the planning stage. A research question that genuinely needs more than the limit is the wrong research question, and that is a fixable problem while it is still a question.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on a Theory of Knowledge essay, and is it strictly applied?
faqs.answer: The essay has a maximum of 1,600 words and the limit is applied, so material beyond it does not help. The exhibition commentary has its own shorter maximum. Both are tight for the job being asked, which is why the component rewards argument and punishes description: a student who spends four hundred words explaining an example has spent a quarter of the essay on something the criteria barely credit. Plan the argument first, allocate words to the parts that carry marks, and cut context without sentiment.

faqs.question: How many words does a Diploma science investigation get, and what sits outside the count?
faqs.answer: The investigation runs to 3,000 words on the current science guides, and material such as raw data tables, calculations and references normally sits in appendices rather than in the body count. Confirm the detail with your child's coordinator, because the guides are revised on a cycle. The common overrun is method detail: students write a procedure thorough enough for a technician when the criteria reward the analysis and evaluation that follow. Trim the method, protect the analysis, and keep the appendices for the data.

faqs.question: Why is the mathematics exploration given a page count rather than a word limit?
faqs.answer: Because mathematical communication is partly visual. Graphs, diagrams, derivations and worked steps are the content, and counting words would penalise exactly the work the criteria reward. The recommendation is in the region of twelve to twenty pages, and the usual failure is not length but substitution: pages of calculator output or spreadsheet printouts standing in for reasoning. Personal engagement and communication are marked, so an exploration that explains why each step was taken scores better than one that merely performs them.

faqs.question: When should internal assessment work actually begin in the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's deadline implies, because the first job is feasibility rather than writing. A science investigation needs a question answerable with the apparatus available. A Business Management commentary needs an organisation willing to supply real information. A History investigation needs reachable sources. Each of those can be checked in a single conversation and each takes weeks to discover by failing. Settle the topic and its feasibility in the first year, and the writing becomes a manageable task rather than an emergency.

faqs.question: What should a student have finished by the end of the first Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Four things, none of them a complete piece of coursework. A Higher Level combination they can sustain and that satisfies the prerequisites for the courses being considered. Internal assessment topics chosen and checked for feasibility in every subject. An Extended Essay research question narrow enough to be answered within the limit. And a consolidated grasp of the shared core in each subject, because Higher Level content layers on top of it and a weak core topic is then examined twice in the second year.

faqs.question: How is the Extended Essay graded, and how does that combine with Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: The essay is marked against published criteria covering the focus and method of the research, knowledge and understanding, critical thinking, presentation, and the formal reflections on the research process. The resulting grade is then read together with the Theory of Knowledge grade on a published matrix that awards up to 3 points towards the Diploma total of 45. A failing grade in either core component can prevent the award of the Diploma, which is why the two should be treated as examined work from the first term.

faqs.question: Why do mock papers matter more in the Diploma than they did at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Because they feed the predicted grade, and the predicted grade decides overseas offers before the real papers are sat. At IGCSE a mock is practice with no external consequence. In the Diploma it is usually the largest piece of evidence the school has when it issues a prediction, alongside internal assessment work already submitted. A student who treats the mock as a rehearsal has misjudged the order of events: by the time the real papers arrive, the offers have been made on the rehearsal.

faqs.question: How is internally assessed coursework moderated, and can a school's mark change?
faqs.answer: Yes, it can move in either direction. The school marks the work against the published criteria and a sample is reviewed externally to check that the school applied the criteria as intended. If the sample suggests the school was consistently generous or severe, marks across the cohort can be adjusted. The practical consequence for a family is that a school's internal mark is an estimate rather than a result, and that criterion-referenced feedback on a draft is more valuable than a number attached to it.

faqs.question: What does a remark involve, and when is it worth requesting one?
faqs.answer: A remark is a re-examination of a component through the board's own process, requested via the school within a short window after results. It is worth considering when a grade sits just below a boundary that materially matters and the component marks look anomalous against the rest of the profile. It is not worth doing on disappointment alone: the original mark can be confirmed, and in some processes it can move the other way. Your school holds the procedure, the cost and the deadline.

faqs.question: How does a Diploma retake work, and what carries over from the first attempt?
faqs.answer: Retake arrangements run through the school and your coordinator is the authority on which components can be retaken and in which session. The important planning point is that the first attempt leaves behind component-level marks and an examiner's report, which show precisely where the grade was lost. That turns a second attempt from a repeat of the whole course into targeted work on one or two components. Decide in the week after results rather than three months later, because entry windows close early.

faqs.question: What is realistic to recover in a single term of private tuition?
faqs.answer: One component, or one topic sequence, or one habit. That is a genuine grade movement in many subjects and it is not a transformation across six. A term of weekly work with marked homework between sessions will reliably fix source technique in History, diagram discipline in Economics, or data-handling in a science. It will not rebuild two years of a Higher Level mathematics course. Any provider promising the second thing from the first amount of time is selling against an outcome they cannot control.

faqs.question: How does support change between the first and the second Diploma year?
faqs.answer: In the first year it is about what is still open: levels, internal assessment topics, the Extended Essay question, and the shared core that Higher Level content will later sit on. The work is slow and the gains appear a year later. In the second year it is conversion: timed papers, mark-scheme reading, command-term discipline and time allocation. A tutor who runs the second-year method in the first year wastes the window, and one who runs the first-year method in the final term wastes the term.

faqs.question: When is it worth dropping a subject from Higher Level to Standard Level, and who decides?
faqs.answer: The school decides, within whatever windows its own arrangements and the IB's allow, and the honest trigger is sustained evidence rather than one bad test. A student failing to keep pace on the Higher Level extension while their other five subjects suffer is losing more than one grade. Before moving, check the prerequisites for the university courses under consideration, because some require a specific subject at Higher Level and a change closes those doors. Have that conversation with the coordinator early, not after mocks.

faqs.question: What should a student do in the break before their final Diploma year?
faqs.answer: Three things, in order. Finish or substantially advance the internal assessment work that is still open, because term time will not provide a better window. Consolidate the shared core topics in the Higher Level subjects, since the second year layers on top of them. And read the published admission criteria for the universities and programmes under consideration, including the equivalency requirements for a Saudi route. Revision for papers that are still a year away is the least useful thing available in that break.

ib-private-tuition.closingHeading: Send the six subjects and their deadlines
ib-private-tuition.closingBody: The quickest way to a useful answer is the audit: your child's six subjects, the internally assessed component in each, and the school's deadline for it, alongside the level and the university route being considered. We will tell you which component we would work on first, what is already closed, and what a term can and cannot achieve from where you are standing. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, written in Saudi local time so the slot cannot drift, and the trial lesson is free and is taught rather than sold. If a late start cannot deliver what you are hoping for, we would rather say so now.

ib-private-tutor.tutorsIntro: The specialists families ask for by name are the scarce ones: Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Physics, Chemistry, and History or Psychology for students whose school covers them with a generalist. Each tutor works to one board and one level, and each will name the component costing your child marks in the first session.

intro.heading: Start with what the hour costs, and what sits inside it
paragraphs: Most pages about private tuition in the Kingdom hide the money behind a contact form. That is the wrong way round, because the rate is the only part a parent can compare before buying, and a family that knows the bands can spot a bad quote immediately. Advertised figures across the Saudi market run from about SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms selling group-ish online lessons, through roughly SAR 55 for general non-specialist tutoring, to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects. IB subject listings commonly open near SAR 180, and Higher Level or Advanced Placement tracks are advertised around SAR 200 to 220. International providers quoting in dollars typically sit near USD 60 an hour. Every one of those numbers is published by a company about its own services, so treat them as a band, not as a market average, and never as our price.

What sits inside the hour is where the difference actually lives. At the bottom of the band you are buying time with somebody who knows the subject. At the top you are buying somebody who knows the specification, has read the mark schemes repeatedly, and can tell you within one session whether your child is losing marks on content, on method or on command terms. That distinction is worth more than any amount of enthusiasm, and it is the single thing most worth paying a premium for in the final year of the Diploma.

The second half of the value question is timing, and it is the reason this page is organised backwards. An hour bought in the first term of DP1 does different work from the same hour bought eight weeks before the May session. Early hours build foundations and fix the habits that the previous course left missing. Late hours convert marks the student has already earned the content for. Both are worth buying; they are not substitutes, and a family that buys only the late ones pays the same rate for a smaller result.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, everywhere in the Kingdom. IB Gram does not send tutors to Saudi addresses; home visits are something we run only in India. That restriction is not a limitation on what a family gets, it is the mechanism that gives them a choice. A household in Al Khobar or Abha matched locally picks from whoever lives nearby. Matched online, the same household picks a Physics Higher Level specialist from a national pool, and keeps that person through a move to another city.

The rest of the page runs in the order a parent actually decides in. First the money and what moves it. Then quality: how to verify that a tutor knows the specification rather than the subject, and what a weak answer sounds like. Then the subject trouble spots, because the component bleeding marks determines who you need. Then the logistics, including the year counted backwards from the series and the Sunday-to-Thursday week. Then academic honesty, in plain terms. Then outcomes, including what a Diploma transcript actually tells each audience that reads it.
