sections.heading: The syllabus-version problem, and the other claim nobody checks
paragraphs: Courses are revised, and a tutor who taught a subject brilliantly under a previous specification can be subtly and invisibly wrong. The failure mode is not teaching the wrong content, which a student would notice. It is teaching the right content with the wrong emphasis: spending time on a topic that has been reduced, under-weighting one that has grown, preparing a component in a format that has changed, or assuming an assessment structure that no longer applies. A student cannot detect any of that, and it costs marks in a way that looks like underperformance.

The question that catches it is the one in the table above: when did you last teach this course, and what changed in the syllabus since? Someone currently teaching it answers immediately and specifically. Someone who taught it four years ago and has kept the materials will often not know what changed, which is the honest and disqualifying answer. This is worth asking even of a tutor with an otherwise outstanding history, because the gap is created by a gap in time rather than by a gap in ability.

A related claim nobody checks is the school-context claim: that a tutor knows how your child's school teaches the course. Schools sequence topics differently, set internal deadlines for coursework at different points, and make different choices on options. A tutor who asks for the school's scheme of work, or at least asks which topics have already been covered and when the Internal Assessment is due internally, is going to be useful in week one. One who starts at the beginning of the textbook is not.

The final unchecked claim is capacity. A tutor carrying too many students cannot mark written work between sessions, and marking between sessions is where a large part of the value sits. Ask how many students they currently teach, how much written work they mark each week, and what their turnaround is. A specific answer is reassuring whatever the number is; an evasive one tells you the marking will not happen.
bullets: Ask when they last taught the course and what changed in the specification
Ask for the school's topic sequence and the internal coursework deadlines
Ask how much written work they mark weekly and what the turnaround is
A specific answer is the signal; the number itself matters less

sections.heading: Who can honestly teach the core: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
paragraphs: The core is where the gap between honest tutoring and something else is widest, and where the market is least trustworthy. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points through a published matrix, and those points regularly decide whether a Diploma total reaches an offer. The work is also, by design, the student's own: supervised at school, certified by a supervisor, and submitted on the understanding that the ideas and the writing belong to the candidate.

What a tutor can legitimately do is substantial and specific. They can teach how a research question is narrowed from a topic to something answerable in the word limit. They can teach what each assessment criterion rewards and how a reflection differs from a summary. They can read a student's own draft and ask the questions a good supervisor would ask: what is your evidence for this, which counterclaim have you not addressed, does this conclusion follow. They can work a complete example on a question the student is not being assessed on, which is often the fastest way to make a criterion visible.

What a tutor cannot do is write any of it. Not a paragraph, not a handed-over research question, not a rewritten introduction, not a methodology tidied into shape. We decline requests to produce or complete an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay, an Internal Assessment or a Personal Project, and we decline them explicitly rather than quietly, because a student who submits work that is not their own risks the whole Diploma rather than one grade.

There is a reason to tell you this on a page about choosing a tutor rather than on a terms page. How a provider answers the Internal Assessment question is the most reliable single test of what they are. Ask it early, and listen for whether the answer distinguishes between teaching a skill and producing a product. An answer that slides between the two, or that offers to "help with the writing" without saying whose hands are on the keyboard, has answered the question.

sections.heading: The Saudi week and the clock: how availability narrows the pool of real specialists
paragraphs: Everything above is about finding the right person. This section is about the constraint that removes most of them. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and the usable teaching window for a school-age student is the evening. The Kingdom keeps Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not observe daylight saving, so a slot agreed with a tutor whose country does change its clocks will drift by an hour twice a year unless it is pinned to Saudi local time.

Pin it to Saudi local time. The tutor absorbs the shift, because the student's school day is the fixed object in the arrangement. The consequence is that a tutor must be someone whose own working day still has teaching in it at 6pm or 7pm Arabia Standard Time. For a tutor in the Gulf or South Asia that is a normal evening hour. For a tutor in the United Kingdom or continental Europe it falls inside their working afternoon, which is comfortable. For a tutor in East Asia it is late at night and for a tutor in the Americas it is the morning, which works for them and limits how many Saudi families they can carry.

The Sunday-to-Thursday week removes more candidates than the time zone does, and most imported tutoring copy ignores it completely. A tutor whose own week runs Monday to Friday has their quietest day on your weekend and their busiest on your Sunday. Arrangements built without noticing that fail in the third week, not the first, which is the worst possible timing. We build the week from the Saudi school calendar outwards and ask tutors to fit it rather than the reverse.

Ramadan reshapes the whole pattern, and because the Islamic calendar moves against the Gregorian one by roughly eleven days each year, it drifts across the academic year rather than sitting in one term. School days shorten and productive study hours move later into the evening. Slots move later for that period rather than being cancelled, and families who prefer to pause keep their slot at no charge. Nobody should publish dates for it: the start is confirmed by moon sighting and differs by a day between countries.

sections.heading: Equivalency and the Qiyas tests, and who can actually prepare a student for them
paragraphs: A Diploma does not connect automatically to a Saudi university place, and the mechanism is poorly covered anywhere a family can easily find it. An international or foreign school certificate needs an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. It is an administrative process with document requirements, and it is worth understanding during the Diploma rather than after results arrive.

Alongside it sit the Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment within the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. The point that matters for an IB family is that Tahsili content follows the Saudi national curriculum, so the material overlaps what a Diploma student has studied while the framing, sequencing and expected method often do not.

That has a direct bearing on who can prepare a student for it, which is why it belongs on this page. A superb Higher Level Chemistry teacher is not automatically the right person for Tahsili chemistry, because the task is not teaching chemistry; it is mapping what the student already knows onto a differently organised syllabus and a different question style. Ask a prospective tutor which of the two jobs they have actually done. Someone who has prepared international-curriculum students for Tahsili will describe the mapping problem unprompted.

We publish no score thresholds and no university's weighting formula, and you should treat any page that does with suspicion. Weightings differ by university and by programme, the most competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on Tahsili, and some universities set a maximum age for the secondary certificate they will accept. The only reliable source is the admission page of the specific programme, read in the year of application.

sections.heading: Starting, reporting, and what happens when a tutor becomes unavailable
paragraphs: The first session is free and is a diagnostic rather than a demonstration. Bring two pieces of marked work, ideally a recent past paper and a coursework draft. The hour is spent establishing where the marks are going and whether the cause is content, technique, pace or something outside the subject entirely. You get that in writing afterwards, including the recommendation, which is sometimes that no weekly tuition is warranted or that a different subject is the real problem.

If it proceeds, the plan names components and a review point rather than a target grade. Reporting is written and arrives after every session: what was covered, what the student got wrong, and one specific thing to do before the next lesson. Short, because a long report does not get read. At the review we compare marked work against the plan. If the component is paying out, we continue or step down to periodic review. If nothing has moved, that is information and we change the approach rather than selling another month.

Tutors become unavailable sometimes — illness, a change in their own teaching commitments, a move. This is the risk families worry about least in advance and most in the moment, because a mid-Diploma handover is genuinely costly. Our answer is that the written record travels: session notes, the diagnosis, the plan and the marked work go to the new tutor before their first session, so the replacement starts from where the student is rather than from the beginning. We also tell you as soon as we know, not when the next lesson is due.

Changing tutor because the fit is wrong is a separate thing and is free. Tell us what did not work — too fast, pitched too high, the student not talking — and we use it to make a better second match. Discovering a mismatch at lesson two is a good outcome. Discovering it at lesson twelve, with a series approaching, is the expensive one, which is why the six questions are at the top of this page rather than in a footnote.

process.title: Ask us the six questions first
process.description: Before anything else, put the six questions in the table above to whoever we propose. That is the right order, and it is why they are published. If an answer is vague or slides around the Internal Assessment boundary, say so and we will either explain or propose someone else.

process.title: Send the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not just the subject. Which level, which option where the school chooses one, and which paper or component the marks are going missing in. If you are unsure, send the last two marked papers and we will work it out. Add the earliest evening hour that works in Saudi time.

process.title: Free diagnostic session
process.description: An hour spent on the marked work rather than on a sample lesson. At the end you get a written view of where the marks are going and what kind of support, if any, the evidence justifies. Buying nothing is a legitimate outcome and happens regularly.

process.title: A plan with components and a review point
process.description: The plan names the components being worked on, what will be measurably different, and when we check. It does not name a target grade, because grade boundaries move between series and a tutor's prediction is a guess in a confident voice. It does name the number of sessions.

process.title: Written notes after every session
process.description: What was covered, the specific errors, and one task before next week. Short enough to read on a phone. These notes are also the handover document if a tutor ever has to change, which is the main reason they are kept in a consistent form rather than written freehand.

process.title: Review against marked work, then continue, reduce or stop
process.description: The review uses marked papers, not impressions. If the component is fixed we step down to periodic review or stop. If the fit is wrong we reassign at no cost. If the problem turns out not to be academic we say that, even though it ends the booking.

whyPoints.title: We publish the test, not just the pitch
whyPoints.description: The six questions and the credential table on this page are the tools for interrogating any tutor, including ours. A provider confident in their matching has no reason to hide them, and a family armed with them stops choosing on price and tone of voice, which is how most IB tuition is currently bought in the Kingdom.

whyPoints.title: Matched on level and syllabus version
whyPoints.description: The match is to subject, level, option and syllabus version, not to the subject name. Higher Level and Standard Level in the same subject are different teaching jobs, and a tutor who last taught the course under an older specification is subtly wrong in ways a student cannot detect.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before purchase
whyPoints.description: The first session is free and is spent finding where the marks are going. Three of the four common failure patterns are technique rather than content, which means the honest recommendation is often four to six sessions instead of a year. We would rather sell the short version and be the people you return to.

whyPoints.title: Explicit on the assessed-work boundary
whyPoints.description: We teach criteria, technique and referencing, and we question the student's own drafts. We refuse to write or complete an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project. How a provider answers that question is the most reliable single test of what they actually sell.

whyPoints.title: Built for the Saudi week and the Saudi clock
whyPoints.description: Sunday to Thursday, Arabia Standard Time, slots pinned to Saudi local time so a tutor's own clock change cannot move them, and later start times during Ramadan rather than cancellations. Imported tutoring copy assumes a Monday-to-Friday week, and arrangements built on that assumption fail in the third week.

whyPoints.title: Nothing asserted that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no success percentages, no ratings, no tutor headcounts, no accreditation. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or ETEC, no connection to any school named here, and no office in the Kingdom.

faqs.question: What does a workable weekly timetable look like for a Saudi student taking three Higher Levels?
faqs.answer: Rarely more than two tutored hours a week in total, and often less. Three Higher Levels already fill a student's independent study time, and a third or fourth tutored hour usually displaces the practice that makes the tutoring work. The common pattern is one weekly hour on the weakest subject plus a short block on a second subject around an internal deadline. Sessions sit on different evenings, Sunday to Thursday, and the student keeps at least two evenings with no scheduled tuition in them at all.

faqs.question: How much notice does it take to move a regular IB slot to a different evening?
faqs.answer: About a week in normal term time, because the tutor is holding other slots around yours and a permanent change has to be matched against their whole timetable. A one-off move for a school trip or an internal examination can usually be handled with two or three days' notice. Permanent changes requested in the weeks before a series are harder, since that is when every family wants the same hours, so flag an anticipated change as early as you know about it.

faqs.question: Does the Kingdom's lack of daylight saving actually cause problems with an overseas IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Only if the slot is recorded in the wrong time zone. Saudi Arabia stays on UTC+3 all year, so when a tutor's own country changes its clocks the gap between you shifts by an hour. If the booking lives in their local time, your lesson silently moves and collides with dinner or homework. If it lives in Arabia Standard Time, the tutor's stated hour moves instead and your evening is untouched. We record every slot in Saudi time for exactly that reason.

faqs.question: How do three-term and two-semester calendars change when IB support should start?
faqs.answer: They change the deadlines, not the content. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, while Ministry of Education schools run two semesters, and the two can differ by weeks in the same city. What matters is your own school's internal deadlines for Internal Assessment work and its mock examination dates, because those are what support has to be timed against. Ask the school for its published calendar and plan backwards from the internal deadlines rather than from the external series.

faqs.question: What happens to IB tuition during the weeks a school runs mock examinations?
faqs.answer: The work changes shape rather than pausing. In the run-up, sessions move to timed past papers under examination conditions with the marking done afterwards, which is the most useful possible use of the hour. During the mock weeks themselves many families drop to a single session or pause entirely, since the student's time is fully committed. Afterwards the mock scripts become the best diagnostic material available all year, and the session immediately following them is usually the highest-value one of the term.

faqs.question: How hard is the move from a Saudi national-curriculum school into the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: The content is usually the easy part, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, where national-curriculum students often arrive ahead of the sequence. The hard parts are writing to a command term in English, the volume of independent work the Diploma assumes, and the Internal Assessment as a self-directed research task rather than a set exercise. Those three are learnable and they take a term of deliberate work. A tutor who treats the move as a content gap will spend that term on the wrong thing.

faqs.question: What does a British GCSE student have to add when they start the IB Diploma in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Breadth and the core. A GCSE student is used to depth in fewer subjects and arrives into six at once plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Timetable management becomes an actual skill rather than a background condition. Subject content transfers well, especially in the sciences, and examination technique transfers partially, since IB mark schemes reward a different structure. The students who struggle are usually those who under-estimate the core, which is worth three points and considerable time.

faqs.question: Does a student switching into the Diploma need a different kind of tutor from one who has always been in it?
faqs.answer: At first, yes. A transferring student needs someone who will audit what actually transferred, topic by topic, and separate genuine gaps from differences in treatment. That is a diagnostic job and not every excellent subject teacher enjoys it. Once the audit is done and the gaps are mapped, the requirement reverts to a normal subject and level match. Ask a prospective tutor how they would establish what a transferring student already knows; if the answer is a standard first lesson, they have not understood the problem.

faqs.question: How long does it take a transferring student to get used to IB command terms?
faqs.answer: Two to four weeks of explicit work to recognise them reliably, and a term before writing to them becomes automatic under examination pressure. The method is unglamorous: before answering anything, say what the command term requires and how many marks are available, predict the scheme, write the answer, then compare. Students find it uncomfortable for a fortnight and then stop noticing they are doing it. It is the single highest-yield piece of teaching available to a transferring student.

faqs.question: What happens to a Middle Years Personal Project if a student switches schools before submitting it?
faqs.answer: The new school's coordinator decides, and the answer varies, so ask during admission rather than after. Sometimes the project continues with a new supervisor and the existing process journal carries across; sometimes the student restarts with a new topic under the new school's timeline. Either way the process documentation is what has value, because the assessment rewards evidence of the process rather than the finished product. Keep the journal complete and dated through the move, whatever happens to the topic.

faqs.question: What should the first IB tuition session produce, if it is not a lesson?
faqs.answer: A written diagnosis. It should name which component the marks are leaving through, say whether the cause is content, technique or pace, and state what the shortest route to fixing it looks like, including the number of sessions. It should be specific enough that you could hand it to a different tutor and they would know what to do. If the first session produces only an impression that things went well, you have bought a demonstration rather than a diagnosis.

faqs.question: How do I tell after three weeks whether we have the right tutor?
faqs.answer: Look at three things that do not require a grade. Can the student explain, unprompted, what they are now doing differently in an answer? Is marked written work coming back with comments that refer to the scheme rather than to effort? And does the session note each week name something specific rather than describing good progress? If all three hold, the match is working even if no grade has moved yet. If none of them does, three weeks is the right moment to change, not the twelfth.

faqs.question: What should a first written report from an IB tutor contain?
faqs.answer: Four things: which component was worked on, the specific errors the student made, what has measurably changed since the previous session, and one task before the next one. It should not contain a predicted grade, an adjective about attitude standing in for evidence, or a recommendation to increase frequency without a reason attached. It should be short enough to read in two minutes, because a report a parent does not finish is a report that has not been written.

faqs.question: How often should an IB tutor speak to the parent rather than to the student?
faqs.answer: Written notes every session, a conversation roughly monthly, and immediately when something changes materially. For a Diploma student the balance should tilt towards the student: a seventeen-year-old who is being managed through their parent does not develop the independence the Diploma requires. For a Middle Years student the parent is more involved by necessity. What should never happen is important information reaching a parent only through the student, which is how both sides end up with different versions of the term.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor becomes unavailable part-way through the Diploma?
faqs.answer: We tell you as soon as we know rather than when the next lesson falls due, and the written record moves with the student. Session notes, the original diagnosis, the plan and the marked work go to the replacement before their first session, so they start from where the student is instead of from the beginning. A handover mid-Diploma costs something regardless of how well it is run, which is why notes are kept in a consistent form from the first session rather than written freehand.

faqs.question: What should a family do between IB lessons to make the hour worth more?
faqs.answer: One thing, not five. The session note names a single specific task, and doing that task is worth more than any amount of general revision. Beyond that, the useful parental job is logistical rather than academic: protect the hour before the lesson so the student arrives not rushing, make sure marked work actually reaches the tutor between sessions, and resist asking whether the grade has moved every week. Marks move in steps after a technique change, not smoothly.

ib-tuition.closingHeading: Interrogate the match before you buy the hours
ib-tuition.closingBody: If you are weighing up IB tuition in Saudi Arabia, the six questions in the table above are the fastest way to tell a current course teacher from a confident generalist, and you should use them on us. Send the subject, the level, the option where your school chooses one, the component the marks are leaving through, and the earliest evening hour that works in Saudi time. The first session is a free diagnostic and the written view that follows is yours whether you continue or not. Lessons are one-to-one, delivered live online, Sunday to Thursday on Arabia Standard Time.

ib-tuition-near-me.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB subjects at Higher and Standard Level across the Kingdom. What sets the rate for any one of them is scarcity of the subject and the specification, marking experience and level, in that order, and a quote without a named subject and level is an opening position rather than a price.

intro.heading: The money question, answered first
paragraphs: Families looking for IB support in the Kingdom meet a market that hides its prices. Most provider pages end at a contact form, which trains a parent to assume the worst and to treat the first quote they receive as the market. So begin with numbers. Rates advertised by tutoring platforms and companies in this market run from around SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to SAR 200 and above for senior examination subjects, with IB subject tutoring in Riyadh advertised from around SAR 180 and premium Higher Level tracks at about SAR 200 to 220. Some international providers quote in dollars, at around USD 60 an hour.

Those are advertised rates published by other providers, with the source type named in the table further down. They are not a market average, because a collection of marketing pages is not a sample, and none of them is our price. What they are good for is calibration: a parent who knows the spread can tell whether a quote sits at the floor or the ceiling of it, and can ask the only question that matters, which is what the difference between the two ends is actually buying.

The difference is mostly scarcity. The word tutor covers a generalist following a textbook and somebody who has taught a specific IB subject at Higher Level through several sessions and marked a component of it. Those are different products sold under one name, and the price gap between them is the market pricing the second one as rare. A family paying at the top of the range for a generalist is overpaying badly; a family paying at the floor for a scarce Higher Level specialist is not going to find one.

Which brings the search term itself into focus. In a Saudi city, asking for tuition near me is rarely a question about travel. It is a question about availability and fit: is there anybody within reach who actually knows this syllabus. The honest answer in most of the Kingdom is that the local pool is small and gets smaller with every constraint added, and that insisting on local raises the real cost per taught hour while lowering the quality of the match. The arithmetic for that is in the second table.

Lessons from us are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Arabia Standard Time inside the Sunday-to-Thursday week. IB Gram does not run home visits in Saudi Arabia; in-home teaching is a service we offer only in India. The cost argument for teaching this way is not that it is cheap. It is that the whole hour is teaching, the pool is set by the hour rather than by the district, and the match does not have to be rebuilt when a family relocates.

After the money, this page works through quality, logistics and outcomes in that order: what moves a rate, what distance costs, where families waste money, what each starting point can still buy, what can honestly be promised, and the administrative cost of the university endgame that nobody prices into a tuition budget.

ib-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: The IB runs as a continuum, and what support costs changes sharply across it, because the scarcity of the teaching changes. These are the programmes families in the Kingdom buy support for, with a note on the cost reality of each here.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations and reporting against learning outcomes rather than marks. Support at this stage is general rather than specialist: number fluency, reading stamina, writing at length. That is also why it is the cheapest end of the market, since the teaching does not require specification knowledge and the pool of capable tutors is wide.
programmes.countryNote: Primary private tuition in Riyadh is advertised at around SAR 50 an hour according to a tutor-marketplace guide, which is near the floor of this market. A family paying substantially above that for primary support should ask what the premium covers, because specification scarcity, the thing that justifies a high rate later, does not exist yet at this stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four lettered criteria per subject, finishing with the Personal Project. Support here is partly subject teaching and partly learning to write against a descriptor, which is a skill with real transfer value into the Diploma. Rates sit between primary and Diploma levels, because criterion knowledge is a genuine qualification but a less scarce one than Higher Level subject expertise.
programmes.countryNote: The best value available in the whole continuum usually sits here, and most families miss it. Fixing writing structure and command-term reading at this stage costs less per hour than fixing it in the final Diploma year, and it changes marks in every subject at once rather than in one. Families who spend here spend less later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, the core, and two years of internally assessed work alongside external papers. This is where rates peak, and the reason is supply: a Higher Level specialist in a scarce subject who has marked for the IB is genuinely rare, and the ones who exist fill their Arabia Standard Time evenings first. Level, scarcity and marking experience compound here rather than adding up.
programmes.countryNote: Advertised IB subject tutoring in Riyadh starts from around SAR 180 an hour on a tutoring-company listing, with premium Higher Level and AP tracks at about SAR 200 to 220. Those figures are published by providers rather than by us. Families budgeting for two Diploma years should price a term at a time, because the useful intensity is not constant across the programme.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A framework combining Diploma courses with a career-related study and its own core, including personal and professional skills, service learning, a reflective project and language development. Support for it is usually bought for the Diploma courses inside it rather than for the framework, which is the part the school supervises most closely.
programmes.countryNote: Relatively few schools in the Kingdom run this route, so check directly with your school whether it is offered rather than assuming it from the IB's presence there. Where it does run, the cost pattern follows the Diploma courses a student takes inside it, and a family should price those individually rather than as a package.

ib-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: Scarcity, not difficulty, is what sets the price of IB support subject by subject. The notes below say why each subject costs what it does in this market and what the premium is actually paying for, which is a more useful guide to a budget than a syllabus summary.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most expensive single request in this market at Higher Level, because the pool of tutors comfortable with the proof and further calculus content is small and demand for it is universal. Standard Level costs noticeably less for the same reason in reverse. A family quoted the same figure for both is being quoted a rate rather than a price for the work.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Less scarce than Analysis and Approaches and usually cheaper, though the Higher Level course is not an easy option. The modelling and statistics content needs a tutor who teaches interpretation rather than calculation, and that is a narrower qualification than it sounds. Worth asking which of the two courses a tutor has actually taught, since the names are close enough to confuse a profile.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Expensive at Higher Level and consistently hard to staff, which is why schools in smaller Saudi cities run it last. The premium pays for somebody who can teach the extension topics and the extended-response technique that carries them. A cheaper generalist can cover Standard Level content adequately and will struggle visibly with the Higher Level extension.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Priced close to Physics at Higher Level, with internal assessment supervision the component that pushes a quote up. Designing a research question narrow enough to generate real data is a specific skill, and tutors who have supervised several investigations charge for it. Ask explicitly whether internal assessment feedback is included in an hourly rate or billed separately.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A deeper pool than the other two sciences, so rates are typically lower for comparable experience. The value is in command-term discipline and in statistical handling for the internal investigation rather than in content coverage, since the content is wide and well documented. A cheaper tutor who drills past questions against mark schemes is often better value here than an expensive content specialist.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Mid-range and widely available, with the premium attaching to evaluation teaching rather than to content. The marks sit in diagrams and in judgement, and a tutor who has marked the extended responses prices accordingly. Families often buy content support for this subject when the marked script shows a diagram and evaluation problem, which is paying for the wrong thing.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Availability varies by region option, which is the detail that catches families out: a tutor who has taught one prescribed subject may not have taught the one your school entered. That specificity makes a matched History tutor scarcer than the subject's general popularity suggests, and the rate reflects it. Ask which region and prescribed subject before agreeing anything.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: One of the better-supplied subjects, so a reasonable rate buys real experience. The value is in case-study application and in defending a recommendation, which is teachable in a small number of sessions. This is a subject where a short, focused purchase often outperforms a term of weekly lessons, and an honest tutor will say so.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Widely available and mid-priced, with a real quality spread hidden behind that. Many tutors teach this as general essay writing, which is not what the papers assess. The premium that is worth paying attaches to somebody who marks against the actual criteria and can show the difference between analysis and summary on the student's own paragraph.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Scarce and priced like it, because the tutors who exist are often working in the industry rather than teaching, which limits their availability in a Sunday-to-Thursday evening. The internal assessment, built for a real client, is the component that most often drives a family to buy support, and it needs somebody who has supervised the criteria rather than somebody who can code.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Reasonably well supplied, and the rate usually reflects experience with the command terms rather than subject depth. Students lose marks by describing studies instead of using them as evidence, which is a structural fix rather than a content one. A short block aimed at that is cheaper and more effective than extended general support.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Rarely bought and often the highest-value hour in the programme, because the core can prevent a Diploma being awarded and almost nobody teaches it privately. Rates vary wildly for that reason. What a family is paying for is somebody who can teach knowledge argument and read an essay against the published descriptors rather than against general essay standards.

ib-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: The price and the availability of local IB support are not the same across the Kingdom, and in most of it the binding constraint is supply rather than cost. These are the places families write in from, with a note on what a local-only search realistically costs in each.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest local market and the one where advertised rates are highest, which are related facts: demand concentrates here. A local search returns the most names in the Kingdom and still returns almost nothing for a named Higher Level subject with marking experience, and that scarcity is exactly what the top of the advertised range is pricing.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: Real school choice and a reasonable local pool, with rates a little below Riyadh's advertised peaks. The hidden cost here is the coastal spine: a tutor crossing the city from the historic centre to Obhur bills for the journey one way or another, which raises the effective cost of each taught hour well above the quoted figure.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: A single conurbation with more teaching experience in it than the population alone suggests, because corporate and campus communities bring it. Rates are competitive. What is unreliable is specification match, so a family here is often choosing between a well-priced generalist nearby and a matched specialist who is not.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities where the local pool is thin enough that price stops being the variable. Families here are not comparing two quotes; they are deciding whether an arrangement exists at all. The cost that matters is continuity, because a tutor lost to a contract ending part-way through a Diploma year is an expensive restart.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: Far enough inland from the Eastern Province cluster that a commuting tutor is impractical on a weekday evening, so any in-home quote carries a heavy travel loading. For several subjects the local rate is effectively infinite, since no local specialist exists to quote one.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Established markets with limited specialist supply in the scarcer IB subjects and no particular price advantage. The practical cost here is scheduling rather than money: the year bends around Hajj and Umrah seasons, and a plan that does not account for those weeks in advance loses sessions that were already paid for.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Twenty-five kilometres apart in 'Asir, sharing a small catchment. A family wanting a Higher Level specialist in a scarce subject will not find one locally at any price, which makes the cost comparison a straightforward one rather than a difficult one.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: Provision in the north-west is catching up with an arriving workforce, and local specialist supply is close to absent. Families here reach the online answer quickly because the local answer does not exist. The budget question becomes how many sessions, not which tutor is nearest.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend schools including these. Where a school runs the Diploma, ask which Higher Level options actually ran in the last intake, because an option listed but not staffed is the single most common reason a family ends up paying for outside teaching.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: The British International School of Jeddah is an IB World School and a Cambridge school, and Deutsche Internationale Schule Jeddah runs to Grade 12. IB World Schools are spread across the Kingdom unevenly, concentrated in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province, and the IB's own directory is the place to confirm current authorisation for any of them.

ib-tuition-near-me.modesIntro: Three purchases, priced differently, for three different problems. The commonest mistake in this market is buying the first one when the diagnosis called for the second, which is an expensive way to discover what was actually wrong.

modes.title: Weekly support, priced by the term
modes.description: A fixed hour each week on one subject with one tutor. Priced per term rather than per lesson so that a family can see the real figure rather than an hourly one, and so the tutor can plan a sequence instead of improvising each week. This is the right purchase for a genuine content gap or a subject the school covers with a non-specialist.

modes.description: Some families need an opinion rather than a term of lessons. A specialist reads the marked script in advance, works a problem with the student, and produces a written view of the error pattern with a recommendation. Several families act on it without buying anything further, which is a legitimate outcome and the cheapest useful thing in this market.

modes.description: Several sessions a week across the weeks before the papers, built on past papers under time rather than on content. Priced as a fixed package with a stop date, because an open-ended intensive is how a family ends up spending twice what they planned in the most expensive weeks of the year.

sections.heading: What a search for tuition near me actually costs to answer
paragraphs: Start with what the different answers to this search cost and what each one delivers, because the options are not variations on a theme. A family can push harder on the school's own department, which is free. They can hire somebody locally to come to the house. They can join a group class at a centre. They can buy a recorded course. Or they can buy one-to-one teaching from a specialist who is not in the city. Those five sit at wildly different prices and buy wildly different things.

The free option is genuinely underused and should be exhausted first. A head of department can move a student between sets, release past papers and mark schemes, or run a clinic. What a school cannot do is hire a Higher Level specialist for one student, which is usually the real problem. Asking the school what it can and cannot cover, in those words, costs nothing and frequently saves a term of paying for the wrong thing.

At the other end, a recorded course is the cheapest paid option and is priced like a library because that is what it is. For a motivated student filling a known gap it is good value. For a student who is losing marks on command terms or who cannot start work without somebody present, it is money spent on something that will not be opened after the second week. Nobody advertises that distinction, so a parent has to make it themselves.

The table below prices the five routes against what each actually delivers. Read the last column rather than the second: the cheapest row that solves your diagnosed problem is the right purchase, and the expensive row is only correct when the problem is genuinely a scarce-specialist problem. Most families arrive assuming they need the most expensive option and a minority of them are right.

sections.heading: What moves an IB hourly rate, in order of weight
paragraphs: Five things set a rate in this market, and they are not equally important, which matters because a family negotiating on the wrong one gets nowhere. Subject scarcity comes first and dominates everything else. A Higher Level Physics or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches specialist costs more than a Standard Level mathematics tutor in every market on earth, and no amount of negotiation changes a supply constraint. If the subject is scarce, the price is the price.

Second is examining or marking experience. What a family is paying for there is fluency about how marks are awarded rather than a certificate, and it is worth paying for when the diagnosed problem is technique. It is worth considerably less when the problem is a missing topic, because a good subject teacher can teach a topic and a marker's insight adds little. Buying marking experience for a content gap is the most common overpayment in this market.

Third is level, with Higher Level above Standard Level above the Middle Years Programme above IGCSE, which tracks both the depth required and the size of the pool. Fourth is whether the tutor travels, which is a cost with no educational content attached. Fifth is package length, the only one of the five a family has real leverage on: a term booked at once is a different commercial proposition from four lessons, and providers price it that way.

What follows practically is a short list of questions that make a quote comparable. Which subject and level. Which components the tutor has taught and marked. How long the session is in minutes rather than in hours. Whether marking of work between sessions is included or extra. Whether written feedback to the parent is included. What happens to sessions you do not use. Two quotes that look fifty riyals apart often differ by more than that once those six answers are in.

sections.heading: What the insistence on local costs per taught hour
paragraphs: Here is the arithmetic nobody does. A nominal hour with an in-home tutor is not sixty minutes of teaching. A tutor arriving from a previous student across a city that is an hour across arrives late or leaves early, or both, and a realistic figure is fifty minutes of actual teaching in a sixty-minute booking. At an advertised SAR 200 an hour, that is around SAR 240 for each hour genuinely taught, before any explicit travel surcharge is added.

Multiply that across a term. Weekly sessions over a school term lose several full hours of teaching to doorways and traffic, and the family paid for all of them. In a dense district the loss is smaller and in a spread-out one it is larger, which is why the same nominal rate buys measurably different amounts of teaching in Riyadh's north than in its centre. This is not an accusation of bad faith on anybody's part. It is an argument that the headline rate is the wrong number to compare.

The second cost of local is the match, and it is harder to put a figure on because it does not appear on an invoice. A family choosing from the adults within driving distance is choosing from a list measured in individuals once a specific subject, level and component is named. The usual outcome is a competent person teaching adjacent to the thing that is wrong: general mathematics help for a proof problem, general essay coaching for a subject with its own criteria. That is the expensive failure, and it is invisible until a mock.

The third is fragility. One tutor, one car, one evening and one schedule, and a changed school timetable or a family relocation ends the arrangement. Rebuilding it means a new search, a new diagnostic and a new relationship, in the same constrained geography. For a two-year Diploma that risk is worth pricing, and it is the clearest financial argument for removing geography from the filter list altogether.

sections.heading: One-to-one against a group class and a recorded course
paragraphs: Value is not price, and the three formats fail in different places, which is what should decide between them. A group class divides the cost of a teacher across several students and works genuinely well when those students need the same thing in the same order. Content coverage fits that description. A room of six students working through a syllabus together at a sensible pace is good teaching and good value, and a family dismissing it on principle is wasting money.

Where a group fails is anything individual. Technique problems are individual by nature: this student misreads command terms, that one writes six-mark answers in two lines, a third runs out of time on the final question. A group has to pick one of those to address, and it picks the one most of the room shares. A student whose specific error is not that one pays for an hour that was not about them, which is cheap per hour and expensive per unit of progress.

A recorded course fails somewhere else again. It has no accountability, no feedback and no diagnosis, and those three are most of what a struggling student is missing. The students who extract real value from recorded material are the ones who were already organised enough not to need much else, which is a well-documented pattern in every market where both exist. For a self-directed student filling a named gap it is excellent value, and for anybody else it is a subscription that goes unopened.

The honest guidance is sequential rather than comparative. Diagnose first, from a marked script, because the diagnosis determines the format. Content gap in a well-supplied subject: a group or recorded material may be enough. Technique problem, internal assessment work, or a scarce Higher Level subject: one-to-one, because the thing being bought is attention to a pattern that only this student has. A family that buys the format before the diagnosis is guessing with money.

sections.heading: Where families waste money on IB support
paragraphs: Four patterns account for most of the waste we see, and none of them involves a dishonest provider. The first is buying content teaching for a technique problem. A worried family covers the syllabus again, which feels like progress and changes nothing, because the student already knew the content and was losing marks on command terms and timing. A marked script would have shown this in ten minutes and a term of lessons did not.

The second is paying for presence. In the final year, families buy sessions because an evening with a tutor in it feels safer than an evening without, long after the teaching has stopped changing anything. The signal is a tutor who cannot name what the next four weeks will do. An honest tutor says so first and recommends stopping, which costs them the booking; a family should treat that recommendation as the strongest evidence of competence available.

The third is spreading across too many subjects. Support in three subjects at once generates work in three subjects at once, inside a Sunday-to-Thursday week that was already full, and the student acts on none of it. The money is spent, the sessions happen and nothing moves. One subject, properly, beats three subjects nominally, and the choice between them should be made on where the widest gap or the highest stakes sit rather than on where the loudest complaint is.

The fourth is starting late and paying the premium for it. Rates do not formally rise as an examination session approaches, but availability collapses, so the tutor still free in the final weeks is less often the matched specialist and more often whoever had a gap. A family buying in the last term is choosing from the leftovers of a market that allocated its scarce specialists months earlier. Starting earlier is not just better teaching; it is better buying.

sections.heading: The logistics you are also paying for
paragraphs: A tuition budget is not only an hourly rate, and the surrounding terms decide whether a family actually receives what it bought. Session length is the first one, and it should be stated in minutes. An hour that is fifty minutes is a fair arrangement honestly described and an unfair one described as an hour. Ask, and get it in writing, because this is where the quietest value difference between two similar quotes sits.

Marking between sessions is the second, and it is the difference between teaching and talking. Work set and never marked teaches a student that the work is optional. A quote that includes marking of written work between lessons is buying several hours of tutor time that do not appear on the invoice, and a cheaper quote that excludes it is often the more expensive purchase once the student stops doing the work.

Cancellation and notice terms are the third. Schools move mock timetables, trips appear, internal examination weeks collide with evening slots. Reasonable terms let a family move a session with notice rather than forfeiting it, and unused sessions should carry rather than expire. The same applies to a long school break: a slot can be paused and held with notice, which is usually the right call because the marginal value of teaching in the summer is low compared with the same hours in the term before the papers.

Continuity is the fourth, and in the Kingdom it is worth real money. Corporate and industrial postings move families between cities and out of the country part-way through a course. Where teaching is delivered over live video, a relocation changes the address and nothing else: the same tutor, the same slot translated into the new local time, no new search and no repeated diagnostic. For a two-year Diploma that is not a convenience, it is a large avoided cost.

sections.heading: What each starting point can still buy
paragraphs: The same money buys different things at different points in a school career, and the difference is large enough to change what a family should do now rather than later. Early in the continuum, money buys habits: writing structure, command-term reading, visible method, number fluency. Those transfer across every subject at once and never have to be bought again. Late in the final year, money buys conversion: technique on specific papers for a student whose content is already in place.

The expensive middle is a final year with content gaps, because that is the one situation where the work needed exceeds the time available and no amount of spending fixes it. A provider who takes that booking without saying so is selling hope. The honest version is to name what the remaining weeks can realistically achieve, prioritise the components still movable, and accept that some of the loss is already fixed. Families generally respond well to being told this and badly to discovering it.

The table sets out what each starting point can still buy. It is worth reading as a budgeting document rather than as advice about urgency: a family with limited means and a child in the Middle Years Programme gets more for the same money than the same family would two years later, and knowing that changes when to spend rather than how much.

One note specific to the Kingdom runs across every row. Families arriving mid-course, which corporate and campus postings make routine, should buy a syllabus audit before buying teaching. The gap between what a new school expects to have been covered and what the previous one covered is almost never where the family assumes it is, and an hour spent establishing that is the cheapest hour in the whole arrangement.

sections.heading: Outcomes you can buy, and the ones nobody can sell
paragraphs: This is where a cost-led page has to be careful, because the market is full of people selling outcomes they cannot deliver. What money genuinely buys is time with somebody who knows the specification, feedback on work the student actually did, a diagnosis of the error pattern, and accountability that makes the work happen. Those are real goods and they correlate with better marks. None of them is a grade.

What nobody can sell is a grade, a point total, a predicted grade or a university place. A predicted grade comes from the school's subject teacher and coordinator, based on the evidence they hold, and no tutor can issue one or change one. A final grade depends on papers sat under conditions nobody controls, against boundaries set after the fact. A university place is a university's decision. Any provider attaching a guarantee to one of these is describing a sales process rather than a service.

Be equally wary of statistics offered as evidence. A claim about a percentage of students improving, a rating out of five, or a number of families served means nothing without the number of students it covers, the date it was measured and the method used to measure it. Those three are almost never supplied, because the figures are usually self-reported marketing. We publish none of them, which is less reassuring and more honest.

What a family can reasonably ask for instead is specific and checkable: which components the tutor has taught and marked, what they identified in your child's marked script, what the next four weeks will change, and written feedback after each session saying whether it did. Those are verifiable week by week. A provider willing to be judged on them is offering something a guarantee cannot, which is evidence.

sections.heading: The cost of the university endgame nobody budgets for
paragraphs: A tuition budget usually stops at the examination session, and for Saudi families applying inside the Kingdom there is a second workload immediately after it that costs time rather than fees. A foreign or international school certificate needs an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike, and nothing proceeds until it exists.

Saudi universities also read the national testing system. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is administered by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, Qiyas, and tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught content, sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last detail is the one that costs families money when it is discovered late.

It costs money because an international-curriculum student has met most of the underlying material in a different order, with different notation and a different examination style, so the test needs its own preparation rather than revision of school work already done. A family that learns this in the final term buys intensive support in the most expensive weeks of the year, on top of examination preparation. A family that learns it a year earlier spreads the same work over months at a lower intensity. The content is identical; the cost is not.

We publish no threshold for either test and no university's weighting formula, because they differ by university, by programme and by intake, and a number copied from a third-party site is worse than no number, since a family plans around it. Each university publishes its own admission criteria and that is the document to work from. Some also state a maximum age for the certificate they accept. No tutor and no platform can promise an admission outcome, and anyone pricing one is selling something they do not own.

process.title: Exhaust the free option first
process.description: Ask the school's head of department what they can and cannot cover for your child, in those words. Set changes, past papers, mark schemes and a clinic cost nothing and sometimes solve the problem outright. The answer also tells you precisely what you would be buying from anybody else, which makes every later quote comparable.

process.title: Get a diagnosis before a format
process.description: Send a marked script and buy one diagnostic session if you need to. The diagnosis decides whether the right purchase is a group class, recorded material, a short technique block or weekly one-to-one. Choosing the format first and discovering the problem later is the single most expensive sequence in this market.

process.title: Ask the six questions that make a quote comparable
process.description: Subject and level. Which components the tutor has taught and marked. Session length in minutes. Whether marking between lessons is included. Whether written feedback to the parent is included. What happens to unused sessions. Two quotes fifty riyals apart often differ by considerably more once those answers arrive.

process.title: Buy one subject and a term at a time
process.description: One subject, priced per term so the real figure is visible, with the hour fixed in Arabia Standard Time. A term is long enough to show whether it is working and short enough to stop. Adding a second subject before the first has a rhythm buys sessions the student has no evening left to act on.

process.title: Review at four sessions and be willing to stop
process.description: Four lessons produces evidence: whether the same errors persist, what the school has noticed, whether work is happening between sessions. Either side can stop or change tutor. Stopping when the teaching has done its job is a normal outcome, and a provider who never recommends it is not advising you.

whyPoints.title: The market shown, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Advertised rates from other providers and platforms are published on this page with the source type beside each, because a parent who cannot see the spread cannot tell whether a quote is reasonable. Those are not our prices and not a market average, and they are more useful to you than a contact form.

whyPoints.title: Priced per subject, level and term
whyPoints.description: A quote names the subject, the level, the session length in minutes, how many sessions, what marking is included and what happens to unused ones. That makes it comparable with anybody else's. An hourly figure with none of those attached is an opening position, whoever is quoting it.

whyPoints.title: The whole hour is teaching
whyPoints.description: There is no travel at either end, so a booked hour is an hour taught rather than fifty minutes bracketed by a doorway. Across a term that difference is several full sessions, and it is the clearest financial argument for teaching this way rather than the usual appeal to convenience.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis you can buy on its own
whyPoints.description: A single diagnostic session, priced as one session, with the marked script read in advance and a written error pattern afterwards. Plenty of families act on it without buying anything further. That is a legitimate outcome, and recommending less than a parent came intending to spend is the cheapest useful thing we do.

whyPoints.title: Continuity costed in
whyPoints.description: Postings move families between Saudi cities and out of the Kingdom mid-course. Because teaching is over live video, a relocation changes the address and nothing else: same tutor, same slot in the new local time, no repeated diagnostic and no new search. For a two-year programme that is a large avoided cost rather than a convenience.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, and no statistics without method
whyPoints.description: No grade, point total, predicted grade or university place is promised, and no success percentage, rating or headcount is published, because a figure without the number of students, the date and the method behind it is marketing rather than evidence. What is offered instead is weekly written feedback you can judge.

faqs.question: Does a Diploma student applying only to overseas universities still need Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not for the overseas application itself, which reads the Diploma directly. Equivalency matters where a Saudi institution or a Saudi process needs the certificate treated as equivalent to the national secondary certificate. The practical advice is to obtain it anyway if the family will remain in the Kingdom, because plans change, a deferred year happens, and the process is simpler with results freshly issued than it is later. Some universities also state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept, which makes a delayed application a reason to have the paperwork settled early rather than a reason to postpone it.

faqs.question: Is Qudurat sat in Arabic or in English, and how should a family choose?
faqs.answer: It is available in Arabic and in English, and the choice should be made on the student's reading speed under time pressure rather than on the language spoken at home. Qudurat tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught syllabus content, so the verbal section depends heavily on how quickly a student processes unfamiliar prose. A student educated in English throughout will usually be faster in English even in a bilingual household. Sit a timed practice section in each language and compare, because the answer is measurable rather than a matter of preference.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subject choices make the Achievement Test easier to prepare for later?
faqs.answer: Taking mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology seriously at the levels available, because those plus English are the science-stream subjects the Achievement Test covers. A student with Higher Level chemistry and physics has met far more of the underlying material than one who took neither. The caution is that the test follows the Saudi national curriculum, so better subject choices reduce the preparation needed without removing it: the framing, notation and emphasis still differ, and the test still needs its own window rather than being treated as revision.

faqs.question: How do Diploma points translate into an overseas offer?
faqs.answer: Each university sets its own conditions, and they are usually expressed as a total with specific Higher Level subject grades attached, for instance a total plus a named grade in a group four subject. The subject conditions are the ones families underestimate: a student can exceed the total and miss the offer on a single Higher Level grade. Published entry requirements are the document to work from, programme by programme rather than institution by institution. No tutor or platform can promise that any offer will be made or met, and anybody attaching a guarantee to one is not describing a service.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest point in a school career to fix a writing or technique problem?
faqs.answer: The Middle Years Programme years, by a wide margin, and almost nobody spends there. Command-term reading, answer structure and visible method transfer to every subject at once and never have to be bought again, so a term of general technique work at that stage does more than the same money spent in a final Diploma year on one subject. The same work costs more later because it has to be done subject by subject, under time pressure, competing with content revision and internal assessment deadlines in the weeks when specialist availability is at its worst.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting IB support in the first Diploma year when there are no examinations yet?
faqs.answer: It is the best value point in the programme, precisely because there are no examinations yet. The internal assessment, the Extended Essay question and the Theory of Knowledge groundwork are all live in that year, and all three are produced over weeks with feedback rather than under time pressure, which makes them the most teachable marks in the Diploma. A first year with no external examination is also the year a student can drift invisibly. Acting then is cheaper and more effective than reacting in the second year with the same money.

faqs.question: What should a family entering the Diploma spend on in the break before it starts?
faqs.answer: Very little, with one exception that is worth real money: mathematics. The step from IGCSE or the Middle Years Programme into a Higher Level mathematics course assumes algebraic fluency that neither route demanded, and a few hours of fluency work prevents a term of struggling in the subject most likely to be taken at Higher Level. Beyond that, pre-teaching content is poor value because the courses teach their own content in their own order, and a student who spends the whole break tutored starts the hardest two years of school already tired.

faqs.question: My child is arriving into a Saudi school partway through the Diploma. What should we buy first?
faqs.answer: A syllabus audit, before any teaching is scheduled. The gap between what the new school assumes has been covered and what the previous school actually covered is almost never where the family expects, and buying lessons before establishing it means teaching the wrong topics at specialist rates. An audit is an hour or two of a specialist's time reading the two schemes of work against the syllabus, and it produces a priority order. Internal assessment timelines need checking against the new school's deadlines in the same exercise, because those rarely align with the old ones.

faqs.question: Why is a Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches tutor the most expensive request in this market?
faqs.answer: Supply. Demand for that course is close to universal because so many degrees expect it, and the pool of tutors genuinely comfortable with the proof and further calculus content is small. Scarcity sets price in this market more than qualifications or experience do. The practical consequence is that negotiation does not move this one much, and the useful questions are about efficiency instead: whether sessions can be fortnightly with marked work in between, whether a block before the papers beats a year of weekly lessons, and whether Standard Level support would address the actual gap.

faqs.question: What is the real cost of a term of weekly support for one IB subject?
faqs.answer: Multiply the quoted hourly figure by the number of weeks in your school's term, then check four things that change the total. Whether the session is sixty minutes or fifty. Whether marking of written work between lessons is included or billed. Whether written feedback to the parent is included. And what happens to sessions lost to school trips or moved mock timetables. Advertised IB rates in this market run from around SAR 180 an hour upwards according to provider listings, so the term figure is substantial enough to deserve those four answers in writing before the first lesson.

faqs.question: Do IB tuition rates rise as the examination session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Rates usually do not, but availability collapses, which has the same effect on what a family actually gets. Scarce Higher Level specialists fill their Arabia Standard Time evenings months ahead, so the tutor still free in the final weeks is less often the matched specialist and more often whoever had a gap in their week. A family buying late is choosing from what a market already allocated. Starting earlier is better buying as well as better teaching, and anybody advertising a seasonal premium should be asked what changed other than the date.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper non-specialist tutor ever the right call for an IB subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, in one clear case: a student who knows the content and will not sit down to work without somebody present. What they need is structure and accountability, and a capable generalist supplies both at a fraction of a specialist's rate. The case fails as soon as the diagnosed problem is specification-level, such as command terms in a particular paper, internal assessment design or the Higher Level extension topics. Paying a specialist for supervision is as wasteful as paying a generalist for specification knowledge, and the marked script is what tells you which you need.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay for feedback on an IB internal assessment specifically?
faqs.answer: Ask for it to be quoted as a defined piece of work rather than by the hour, because that is how it is actually done: reading a draft, writing feedback against the criteria, then a session to discuss it. Providers who quote it hourly are quoting the discussion and not the reading, which is where most of the time goes. Expect it to sit at the upper end of a subject's range, because supervising investigations is a narrower skill than teaching the course. No tutor may write or redraft any part of it; what is purchased is feedback on the student's own work.

faqs.question: What exactly happens in a free trial lesson, and what should it produce?
faqs.answer: The tutor reads the marked work beforehand, then spends the session working a real problem with the student rather than presenting a method. It should produce three things: a specific statement of the error pattern, a plan for what four weeks will change, and an honest view on whether weekly lessons are the right purchase at all. Judge it on whether your child was writing or listening, and on whether anything said reduced what you were planning to spend. A trial that agrees with everything a parent arrived believing has assessed nothing.

faqs.question: Do we pay per lesson or per package, and what happens to sessions we do not use?
faqs.answer: Per term is usually the clearest arrangement, because it makes the real figure visible rather than disguising it in an hourly rate, and it lets the tutor plan a sequence instead of improvising weekly. Unused sessions should carry rather than expire, with notice, since schools move mock timetables and trips appear without warning. A long holiday can be paused with the slot held. What to avoid is an open-ended intensive with no stop date in the weeks before the papers, which is how a family spends twice what it planned in the most expensive part of the year.

ib-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Price the specific thing you actually need
ib-tuition-near-me.closingBody: The useful version of this search is not who is nearest but who knows the syllabus and what they charge for it. Start by asking the school what it can and cannot cover, because that costs nothing and makes every later quote comparable. Then send the subject, the level and one marked script, and take a free diagnostic lesson: it should tell you the error pattern, what four weeks will change, and sometimes that you need less than you came to buy. Quotes here name the subject, the level, the session length in minutes, what marking is included and what happens to sessions you do not use. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Arabia Standard Time, and no grade, point total or university place is ever promised.

intro.heading: Points leave a Diploma in a small number of predictable places
paragraphs: Almost every family that goes looking for Diploma support in the Kingdom arrives with the same evidence: a report that says the student is working hard and a mark that does not reflect it. The reflex is to buy more content teaching. In most cases content is not where the points went. The Diploma is a tightly specified qualification, and the ways it leaks marks are few enough to list on one page: answers written to the wrong command term, internally assessed work that describes instead of evaluating, papers mistimed so the final question is never properly attempted, a core left until the second year, and a Higher Level choice that was wrong from the start.

Each of those has a price. Not a price in money first, but in points. An exploration sitting two criteria below what the student could reach costs more than most families realise once the internally assessed component is weighed against the papers. A Theory of Knowledge grade or an Extended Essay grade that slips can cost points directly through the published matrix, and a failing grade in either is a condition that can cost the Diploma itself regardless of subject results. These are the losses that do not show up in a mock paper, which is why they are often found late.

Then there is the money question, which is the one this page is organised around. Support in this market is advertised rather than regulated. Tutoring companies publish rates from around SAR 180 an hour for IB subjects, with Higher Level and premium tracks quoted at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Marketplace guides put senior-school examination subjects at 200 and above, and general non-specialist online tutoring starts far lower, from about SAR 55. Those are advertised figures from vendors describing their own pricing; none of them is a market average and none is what IB Gram charges. What they do show is a wide spread, and the spread is not random.

What moves a rate, in order of weight: how scarce the subject specialist is, whether the tutor has marking or examining experience, the level, whether anybody has to travel, and how long the commitment is. Subject scarcity dominates. A Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches Higher Level teacher and a Mathematics Standard Level teacher are not the same hire in any city in the region. That single fact explains most of the difference between two quotes for what looks like the same hour, and it is the question families most often forget to ask.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It is not approved by, accredited by or in partnership with the IB, Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or ETEC, and it holds no relationship with any school or employer named on this page. Lessons for families in Saudi Arabia are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits in Saudi Arabia are not something we sell, and in-home teaching is offered only in India. For a scarce Higher Level subject that is an advantage rather than a compromise, because the choice widens from whoever lives nearby to everyone who teaches that syllabus.
