process.title: Send the board, the tier, the subject and the last marked paper
process.description: The subject name alone tells us almost nothing. We need the board for that subject, the tier intended, and ideally a photograph of the last marked paper. A specialist reads more from a marked script in thirty seconds than from a long conversation, and it is what lets us say honestly whether the right coach is free for your evening.

process.title: A baseline paper, timed and marked to the scheme
process.description: A full paper under real conditions, marked against the published scheme and returned with a breakdown by question type rather than a single total. That breakdown is the plan's foundation and it belongs to you, not to us, so it can be compared against anything later and shared with the school if that is useful.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the coach who would teach
process.description: Your child works with the actual specialist on a real question from the paper they have just sat, not a demonstration exercise. You receive a short written note saying what the coach found and what they would attack first. If the fit is wrong, say so and the coach changes before anything is paid.

process.title: A plan with the evidence named in advance
process.description: The plan states which question types it targets, in what order, and what piece of evidence will show each one has been fixed. Agreeing the evidence before the teaching starts is what makes the arrangement checkable, and it is what lets a family end it confidently when the work is done.

process.title: Re-baseline every six to eight weeks
process.description: A fresh comparable paper on a fixed rhythm, with the breakdown set against the previous one. The plan is revised against that evidence rather than against impressions. Testing more often measures day-to-day variance and eats teaching time; testing less often lets a stale plan run for a term.

process.title: A decision at each review, including stopping
process.description: Each review compares the named targets against what actually moved and ends in a decision: continue, change coach, change frequency, or stop. A candidate whose presentation losses have gone to zero after four sessions does not need the remaining twenty, and we will say so.

whyPoints.title: Measured against papers, not against impressions
whyPoints.description: Every arrangement starts with a timed paper marked to the published scheme and broken down by question type, and is re-baselined on a fixed rhythm. The comparison stays in your hands, which means any claim about progress is one you can check rather than one you have to accept.

whyPoints.title: Board and tier treated as the first facts
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are different specifications with different paper structures, tier labels and reporting scales, and a single student often sits both across one timetable. Coaches are matched to the exact entry, and the past-paper range used matches the board the candidate will actually sit.

whyPoints.title: Tier advice given straight
whyPoints.description: The tier caps the grade and is fixed at an entry deadline, so it is settled on timed-paper evidence and said plainly in both directions. Where the honest answer is the lower route, we say it early, because a candidate preparing for a route they will not sit loses months.

whyPoints.title: The right amount, which is often less
whyPoints.description: Presentation errors, unit losses and command-term failures are cheap to fix and usually need a handful of sessions. We would rather diagnose that, do it, and finish than sell a year of weekly lessons for a problem that takes six weeks.

whyPoints.title: Market bands published, with the source type named
whyPoints.description: Advertised Saudi rates run from roughly SAR 35 to SAR 200 an hour and above depending on level and scarcity, and we say who publishes them. What we charge depends on subject, tier and frequency, and you are told it before a lesson is booked rather than after a trial.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be verified
whyPoints.description: No success percentages, no ratings, no headcounts, no promises about a final grade, and no claim of approval or partnership with any board or regulator. Every figure quoted here is either an attributed market rate or a checkable fact about the qualification itself.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE Mathematics topics most often need outside teaching before the higher-tier paper?
faqs.answer: Algebraic manipulation first, because everything else depends on it: rearranging, factorising and working with indices and surds under time. After that, the usual list is simultaneous and quadratic problems set in words rather than symbols, trigonometry beyond the right-angled cases, and compound probability. The pattern is consistent: candidates manage single-step questions and lose multi-step ones, because each step compounds the error in the last. Measure progress by how many multi-step items are started correctly, since partial credit appears there before the total moves.

faqs.question: Why do IGCSE Physics candidates lose marks on questions they can clearly answer?
faqs.answer: Presentation, almost always. Units omitted or wrong, prefixes mishandled, significant figures inconsistent with the data given, and answers written without the working that earns method marks. None of it reflects physics the candidate does not know, which is why it survives repeated content revision. It is also the cheapest loss in the qualification to recover: a checklist applied to every piece of written work and three or four marked papers usually takes presentation losses close to zero and lifts a grade by itself.

faqs.question: What is the most common error in an IGCSE Chemistry equation question?
faqs.answer: An unbalanced equation, followed closely by missing or wrong state symbols. Both are marked strictly, so a chemically correct product scores nothing when the equation does not balance. The underlying cause is usually that reactions were learned as a list to recall rather than as patterns to apply, which works on familiar examples and fails on unfamiliar ones. The fix is pattern practice across reaction families with deliberately unfamiliar reagents, and then checking equation marks specifically rather than the paper total.

faqs.question: How much of IGCSE Biology is memory and how much is technique?
faqs.answer: The content load is genuinely heavy, so memory matters, but the marks that are usually missing are technique. Candidates write everything they know about a topic when the command term asked them to outline, explain or distinguish, and a shorter answer aimed at the term scores more than a longer one that is not. Definitions are marked tightly, and diagrams must use the scheme's own terms. A candidate who knows the syllabus and plateaus is almost always losing command-term marks rather than content marks.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE English component separates a competent writer from a high scorer?
faqs.answer: Directed writing, where the task names an audience, a purpose and a form, and the marks come from controlling register rather than from the quality of the prose in general. Confident writers often score in the middle because they write well in their own voice instead of the one the task specified. The useful practice is to write the same content three ways for three audiences and have each marked against the band descriptors, with the descriptor above always shown so the gap is visible.

faqs.question: Why do IGCSE Business Studies candidates lose marks on data-response questions?
faqs.answer: Because they answer the topic rather than the question. A data-response item supplies case material precisely so the answer can be grounded in it, and a candidate who defines the relevant term accurately and then never refers to the figures has answered nothing that earns the higher marks. Justify and recommend questions are where this shows most. Track the ratio of marks earned on those commands against marks earned on define commands; when the ratio moves, the technique has genuinely changed.

faqs.question: What goes wrong in the IGCSE Computer Science programming and documentation work?
faqs.answer: The code usually works and the documentation usually does not. Marks are allocated against a task specification: a stated requirement, a design, evidence of testing against sensible and invalid inputs, and a record of what was changed and why. Candidates who build something functional and write the documentation afterwards score below candidates whose work is modest and documented against every criterion. The fix is to read the criteria before writing any code, which is a half-hour conversation rather than a term of teaching.

faqs.question: What should a family ask an IGCSE coach about the specification before paying for anything?
faqs.answer: Four things. Which board and which version of the specification have you taught, and for how many cohorts? What does each paper consist of at this tier? Where do candidates most often lose marks in the question type my child is failing? And what evidence will show that it has been fixed? A specification specialist answers the second immediately, because they have planned a two-year course against it, and offers the fourth without being asked. An answer about confidence and foundations is a different product being sold.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether an IGCSE coach has taught Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than families expect. The content overlaps substantially, so a coach from either board will teach the shared material competently. What does not transfer is paper technique: structures differ, the calculator and non-calculator balance in mathematics differs, tier labels differ, and the question styles in released papers differ. In the final term, paper technique is most of what coaching is for. Ask which board's released papers they use and in what quantity, and match it to the school's actual entry for that subject.

faqs.question: How can a parent tell whether an IGCSE coach is teaching to the right tier?
faqs.answer: Look at the papers being used. A coach preparing a higher-tier candidate should be setting higher-tier past papers under timing from early on, not working through lower-tier material because it builds confidence. Ask to see which papers have been set over the last month and what the breakdown showed. If the material is all below the tier the student is entered for, the candidate will meet unfamiliar question types in the series itself, which is exactly the situation coaching is supposed to prevent.

faqs.question: What should the first written report from an IGCSE coach contain?
faqs.answer: A breakdown of the baseline paper by question type, naming marks lost to content, to presentation and to command terms separately. A statement of which single failure is being targeted first and why. What evidence will demonstrate it has been fixed. And what has been set as written work before the next session. What it should not contain is a projected grade, a percentage, or a paragraph about engagement and attitude. If it reads as encouragement rather than information, say so, because that is a reporting failure and it is fixable.

faqs.question: How do we change an IGCSE coach without losing the term's work?
faqs.answer: By insisting the written record exists before it is needed. A handover should carry the baseline paper and its breakdown, every marked paper since, the plan with its named targets, and a note of the candidate's specific recurring errors. With that, a new coach starts from the diagnosis rather than repeating it, which matters most in Year 11 when there is no spare time. Ask any provider at the outset what they hold on file. If the answer is that nothing is written down, a change will cost weeks.

faqs.question: What may an IGCSE coach do with a coursework assignment, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: They may explain the assessment criteria and the task specification, question a plan, a variable choice or a research approach before any work exists, and give written feedback on a draft the candidate has written. They may not write, restructure or dictate any part of the text, supply data or results, or hand over model answers to adapt. The distinction in practice is that feedback points at the candidate's work while a rewrite replaces it. Ask the question in those words before booking, and note the hesitation if there is one.

faqs.question: Who marks IGCSE coursework, and how is it moderated?
faqs.answer: Where a subject carries an internally assessed component, it is marked in the school and then moderated by the board, which checks the school's marking against the standard rather than remarking every piece. That has a practical consequence: the school's internal standardisation affects the mark a candidate ends up with, and it is reasonable to ask how it is done. It also means no outside provider can influence the mark except by improving the candidate's own work, which is the only legitimate route anyway.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE coach proofread a piece of assessed written work?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense families usually mean. Correcting spelling, grammar and phrasing in assessed work changes the work, and in components where written expression carries marks it changes the mark. What a coach can legitimately do is teach proofreading as a skill, point out that a paragraph is unclear without rewriting it, and have the candidate make the correction themselves. If the candidate cannot find and fix the problem after it has been pointed at, the honest answer is that the skill needs teaching, not that the sentence needs fixing.

faqs.question: What does a Middle Years Programme Personal Project have to do with IGCSE coaching?
faqs.answer: It comes up because students transfer between routes, and a candidate moving from a Middle Years Programme school into an IGCSE cohort may be carrying one while starting new specifications. The same honesty line applies: a coach may explain the criteria and the role of the process journal, and may not build the product or write the report. The more useful observation is that the Personal Project trains planning and reflection, which transfers directly into IGCSE coursework and practical components, so it is worth finishing properly rather than abandoning.

igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Send the paper, and we will send the breakdown
igcse-coaching.closingBody: The most useful first step is a marked paper, or a willingness to sit one properly. From a full timed paper marked against the published scheme we can tell you which question types are costing the grade, whether the cause is content, presentation or pace, how long each one takes to fix, and what evidence will show it has been fixed. Lessons are one-to-one and online, over live video, set in Arabia Standard Time so the slot holds through the term. Confirm the board and tier with your school first, send both with the paper, and ask for the trial lesson with the subject specialist rather than a call with a coordinator.

intro.heading: Where the student sits in the year decides what a block can do
paragraphs: Every honest answer about an IGCSE crash course starts with a date rather than a price. A student in the autumn term of their final year has roughly two terms left, which is long enough to rebuild a topic that was taught badly and then test whether the repair held. A student six weeks out has time to rehearse question types and nothing more. The two families are asking the same question and need completely different answers, and a provider who quotes the same package to both is not reading the calendar.

The Saudi school year complicates this in a way most tutoring copy ignores. Public schools run two semesters from late August to late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, so two families in the same city can be at genuinely different points with the same examination ahead of them. The only reliable reference is the school's own published calendar, not a general guide, and the first thing worth doing is counting the actual teaching weeks it leaves between now and study leave.

The series themselves are fixed. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series, which is the main entry for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and for November-entry candidates. Cambridge also runs a February and March series, but that is open to candidates in India only, so a Saudi family planning a second attempt is planning for November. Rivals who copy Indian pages get this wrong, and a family that acts on it loses half a year.

Entries are the other hard edge. Final entries close months ahead of the papers, and the tier a candidate is entered for caps the grade they can be awarded. On many Cambridge subjects the Core tier is graded C to G and the Extended tier A* to E, so a Core entry cannot produce a B however well the paper goes. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades nine to one. Confirm both the tier and the component list with the school in writing before any block is designed, because a tier entry is a school decision and it is reversible only while the entry window is still open.

What follows works forward through the year: what the autumn term can still rebuild, what the mock scripts after the midyear break actually tell you, what the last six weeks should contain, and what a November resit block is worth. Then the logistics, because an IGCSE candidate is usually carrying eight or nine subjects into one Sunday-to-Thursday week, and a block that ignores that arithmetic takes the hours out of the student's own revision rather than out of nowhere.

sections.heading: Start from where the student sits in the year, not from a package length
paragraphs: The useful first question is how many teaching weeks remain before the papers, counting school holidays out rather than in. A family in the autumn term of the final year has two terms, minus the midyear break, minus whatever mock period their school runs. A family after the mocks has one term. A family six weeks out has six weeks, of which two will be lost to school revision timetables and study leave. The honest block is the one that fits the remainder.

Each window has a different best use, and trying to use a late window for an early purpose is where money disappears. New content in the last month competes with revision the student should be doing anyway. Technique work in the autumn term is wasted on a student who does not yet know the content well enough to apply it. The sequence runs content, then application, then timing, and the calendar decides how much of that sequence a family can still buy.

This is also how to read a quote. A provider who offers thirty hours without asking which term the student is in, which board the school entered, and whether the tier has been confirmed is selling a package rather than planning a block. Ask instead what the hours will target in the first fortnight and how that target was chosen. A specialist will answer with a component and a question type, and will say which of your weeks they are writing off as unusable.

sections.heading: The autumn term is the only window where content can still be rebuilt
paragraphs: In the autumn term of the final year a block can do the thing no later block can: teach something properly from the start. If a topic was covered by a cover teacher, missed during a relocation, or taught at a pace the student could not follow, this is when it can be rebuilt and then tested twice before it matters. Twelve to sixteen hours spent here is usually worth more than twice that number bought in the spring.

The work looks like teaching rather than revision, and parents sometimes find that unsettling. There are few past papers in the first fortnight, because a past paper on content the student does not hold yet only produces a low mark and a demoralised teenager. Instead the hours go on the underlying skill, with short checks rather than full papers, and the first complete paper comes once there is something to measure.

The autumn term is also the right moment to settle the entry questions, because they are still open. Which tier the school intends to enter, which optional components are being taken, and whether the student is on the right specification are all decisions that can still be influenced before final entries close. After the deadline they are facts to work around. A block that opens by establishing those facts rarely wastes its later hours, and the conversation with the school is easier in the autumn term than it will ever be again.

sections.heading: After the midyear break: reading the mock scripts rather than the mock grade
paragraphs: The mock grade tells a family almost nothing useful. The script tells them everything. A paper where marks were lost evenly across every question points at content. A paper where the first half is strong and the last three questions are blank points at timing. A paper where every answer is nearly right points at command terms and at working that was never shown. Those three diagnoses lead to three different blocks, and the grade on the front page distinguishes none of them.

Ask the school for the marked script and the mark scheme, not just the total. Then count: marks lost to questions left blank, marks lost to arithmetic, marks lost to answering a different question from the one asked. Most candidates have one dominant category, and a short block that attacks the dominant one moves the total more than a general revision course covering everything at equal depth.

This is also the point where the tier question becomes a fact rather than a choice. If the entry is Core on a tiered Cambridge subject, the grade is capped at C whatever the block achieves, and a family deserves to know that before paying for hours aimed at a B. If the entry is Extended and the mock mark is low, the conversation with the school is about support rather than about moving down, because the deadline has usually passed. Either way, ask the school to confirm the entry in writing so the block is planned against a fact.

sections.heading: The last six weeks before the June series: timed papers, not new topics
paragraphs: In the final six weeks the block has one job, which is converting what the student knows into marks on a page within the time allowed. That means complete papers, sat in one sitting, marked against the published scheme, and then worked through question by question. Candidates who have only ever done questions untimed are often surprised by how much of their loss is simply pace, and pace responds quickly to practice in a way content does not.

Two subjects is the sensible maximum at this stage, and one is often better. A candidate with nine entries already has a school revision timetable, and every hour of tutoring is an hour taken out of their own study rather than out of thin air. The honest calculation is whether the tutored hour produces more marks than the hour of independent revision it replaced. For a weak subject it usually does; for a subject already secure it usually does not.

Expect the block to get narrower rather than broader as the papers approach. In the last fortnight it should be one paper, one question type, and the specific instructions the student keeps missing: show your working, give your answer to three significant figures, use the information in the extract. These are not glamorous corrections, but they are where marks sit in the final weeks, and they are cheap to fix. A candidate who leaves the last session with three habits rather than three topics has had the better block.

sections.heading: The November series, resits, and what a second attempt is really worth
paragraphs: A November entry is a genuine second chance and it should be planned rather than reached for in panic. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a November series alongside the main June one, and resit candidates in the Kingdom use it. Cambridge's February and March series is open to candidates in India only, so a Saudi family weighing a second attempt is choosing between November and the following June, and nothing earlier.

The useful question is which papers pulled the grade down. A candidate who missed a grade by two marks across two papers is in a different position from one who missed it by thirty. Component-level results, where the school can supply them, show whether the loss was concentrated or spread. A concentrated loss is what a short block fixes well; a spread loss usually needs a term rather than a block, and saying so is more useful than selling the shorter option.

A resit also has to compete with whatever the student is doing next. Many candidates are starting A Levels or the Diploma at the same time, and a November block has to fit alongside new courses that are themselves demanding. Two evenings a week is realistic; four is not. Decide which matters more, the resit grade or the first term of the new course, and plan the hours around that answer rather than hoping both will fit. Writing that decision down makes the later weeks much less fraught.

sections.heading: A Sunday-to-Thursday week with nine subjects already in it
paragraphs: Schools in the Kingdom run Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and an IGCSE candidate is usually carrying eight or nine subjects into that week. A block asking for three or four evenings is therefore competing with homework in every other subject, not with free time. The arithmetic is worth doing out loud with the student present, because a plan they have not agreed to is a plan that produces cancellations in week three.

The clock adds a second constraint. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks, so a slot agreed with a tutor whose country does observe daylight saving will move by an hour twice a year unless the agreement names Saudi local time explicitly. For a block running eight weeks that may never matter; for a programme spanning a change it matters a great deal, and writing the time down costs nothing.

The tutor's own week is the part families rarely ask about. Most strong specialists teach somewhere during their working day, and a Saudi evening slot sits inside the working afternoon of a tutor in Europe and late at night for one in East Asia. Three evenings a week for a month is a commitment on their side as much as on yours. Ask directly whether they can hold it before the block starts rather than discovering the answer halfway through, when there is no time left to replace anyone.

sections.heading: Check the component list and the entry before you buy a single hour
paragraphs: Two documents decide what a block should contain, and neither of them is a textbook. The first is the entry itself: the board, the syllabus code, the tier where the subject is tiered, and the optional components the school has chosen. The second is the specification for that code, which lists exactly what is assessed and how the papers are weighted. Families who ask the school for both in writing avoid the most expensive mistake in this market, which is paying for hours aimed at the wrong paper.

Practical components are where this bites hardest. A school may enter candidates for a laboratory examination or for the alternative-to-practical paper, and the preparation for those is not the same work. A tutor teaching experimental technique to a candidate sitting a written practical paper is teaching something useful in general and irrelevant in particular. One question to the school settles it.

Coursework, where a subject still has it, belongs to the student and to the school. A tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, ask questions about a draft the student has written, and point at where a criterion is not being met. No tutor should produce the text that gets submitted or rewrite a passage into its final form, and a provider offering that is offering malpractice with the consequences falling on the candidate. Keep drafts in the student's own files and let the school's supervisor stay the authority on what the task requires.

faqs.question: What should I ask an IGCSE tutor before committing to a four-week block?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which board and syllabus code have you taught this subject on? What will the first fortnight target, and why that? What will my child write between sessions, and who marks it? And what are you deliberately leaving out given the weeks we have? A specialist answers all four in specifics. Vague answers to the first and last are the ones that predict a wasted block.

faqs.question: Does a crash-course tutor need to have taught our child's exact board, or is the subject enough?
faqs.answer: For a short block, the board matters. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel examine the same subject with different paper structures, different weightings and different command-term habits, and a block has no time to absorb the difference as it goes. A tutor who knows the subject deeply but the other board will teach good content aimed at the wrong paper. Ask for the syllabus code they have taught, not just the subject name.

faqs.question: How do I check a claim about examiner experience when a block has to start next week?
faqs.answer: Ask what the experience actually consisted of: which board, which component, and what it taught them about where candidates lose marks. Someone who has marked a paper describes the scheme's behaviour in detail, including the parts that feel unfair. Someone who has not describes marking in general terms. You cannot verify a contract in a week, but you can hear the difference inside ten minutes of a diagnostic lesson.

faqs.question: Can we change tutor two sessions into a short IGCSE block?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in a short block it should happen quickly rather than politely. Two sessions is enough to know whether the student is being taught or talked at. Tell us what did not work, because the useful switch is to a different kind of tutor rather than simply another one. Unused hours stay unused, and the replacement starts from the diagnostic notes rather than from scratch.

faqs.question: Should a Core-tier candidate and an Extended-tier candidate have different tutors?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily different people, but definitely a different plan. A Core candidate on a tiered Cambridge subject is working towards a ceiling of C, so the hours go on securing the achievable grades rather than on the harder Extended material. An Extended candidate needs the material that only appears on their papers. A tutor who teaches both from the same plan is short-changing one of them, so ask which tier the plan was written for.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE crash-course session actually look like on screen?
faqs.answer: A shared whiteboard, the student's own marked work on it, and the tutor writing alongside them rather than lecturing. A typical session opens with two minutes on last week's marked paper, spends most of its time on worked questions with the student doing the writing, and closes by setting the next timed task. Both sides can draw, so graphs, diagrams and working are handled directly rather than described.

faqs.question: How does a tutor mark a timed IGCSE paper between two sessions in the same week?
faqs.answer: The student photographs or scans the script and sends it the same evening. Marking against the published scheme takes a tutor well under an hour for most papers, and the annotated script comes back before the next session with a breakdown by question type. That turnaround is the point: a paper marked a fortnight later is a historical document, while one marked overnight is still a live memory for the student.

faqs.question: Are intensive sessions recorded, and can a student rewatch them during revision?
faqs.answer: Recording is arranged with the family rather than assumed, and where it is agreed the recording belongs to the student. In a short block it is genuinely useful, because a worked method explained in week two is needed again in week six. What works better than rewatching a whole hour is keeping the whiteboard pages, which are shorter, searchable and easier to revise from than video.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a timed paper?
faqs.answer: Timed papers are usually sat offline by design: the student works on paper to a clock, then sends the script. That removes connectivity from the part of the work where it would do the most damage. For taught sessions, both sides reconnect and the lost minutes are added back, either at the end or to the next session. A short block cannot absorb lost hours, so they are tracked rather than written off.

faqs.question: Is a tablet enough for an intensive IGCSE block, or does the student need a laptop?
faqs.answer: A tablet with a stylus is genuinely good for mathematics and the sciences, because the student can write on the shared board naturally. A phone is not enough for anything. What matters more than the device is a stable surface, paper and a calculator next to it, since most of the work is written by hand and photographed. A second screen helps when a past paper and the board are both open.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE Mathematics topics are worth a short block and which are not?
faqs.answer: Worth it: algebraic manipulation, simultaneous and quadratic work, trigonometry in non-right-angled triangles, and the multi-step problems where marks come from shown working. Less worth it in a short block: topics the student can already do slowly, since speed comes from paper practice rather than teaching. Statistics and probability often need less time than families expect, while the longer structured questions usually repay every hour spent on them.

faqs.question: Why do IGCSE Chemistry candidates lose marks on the practical-skills questions?
faqs.answer: Because those questions are not about chemistry. They examine whether a candidate can read a method, identify the controlled variable, spot the source of error and say what should change, and that is a separate skill from knowing the reactions. Candidates who have done plenty of laboratory work still lose marks here if they have never practised writing those answers. It responds quickly to teaching, which makes it good value in a short block.

faqs.question: What goes wrong in IGCSE English reading questions under time pressure?
faqs.answer: Candidates write too much for low-tariff questions and then run out of time for the ones that pay. A question worth two marks wants two things, not a paragraph. The second common loss is answering from memory of the passage rather than from the passage itself, which costs the specific detail the scheme is looking for. Both are timing habits, and both are fixable in a handful of marked papers.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE Physics topics show up late in the course and catch candidates in a block?
faqs.answer: Electromagnetism, radioactivity and the parts of waves that involve calculation are often taught last and revised least, so they appear in a block as unfamiliar rather than difficult. Add the practical-skills component, which many candidates meet properly only in revision. If a block starts after the mocks, these are usually where the quickest marks are, simply because the student has had least contact with them.

The diagnostic lesson is free and comes before any commitment. igcse-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors families keep for a full year rather than a crisis: subject specialists working to the school's specification code, with a marked piece of written work behind every session.

intro.heading: Preparation is a two-year sequence, and most of it happens before the revision season
paragraphs: The phrase exam preparation usually makes families think of the final term, which is why so much of it is bought too late to work. By the time study leave arrives, the material a candidate can still learn is small and the technique they can still change is limited to the obvious. The preparation that moves grades happens earlier and looks less like revision: securing algebra in the first IGCSE year, learning what a mark scheme pays for, and building the habit of writing answers rather than reading about them.

The Saudi calendar shapes that sequence in ways general guides miss. Public schools run two semesters from late August to late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, which means two candidates in the same city, sitting the same papers, can be at different points in their year. Work from the school's own published calendar and count the teaching weeks it actually leaves between now and study leave, with the breaks taken out rather than left in.

The examination calendar itself is simpler. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series, which is the main entry for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and November-entry candidates. Cambridge's February and March series runs for candidates in India only, so a Saudi candidate has two fixed points to plan around and no third one. Final entries close months ahead of the papers, and the tier a candidate is entered for sets a ceiling on the grade they can be awarded.

The other fact that shapes preparation is how many subjects a candidate carries. Eight or nine entries is normal, which means the revision timetable, not the teaching, is the scarce resource. A student cannot revise nine subjects deeply at the same time, and the schools that handle this well stagger it. A family that buys tutored hours without redesigning the week has simply taken those hours out of the student's own revision, which can leave the total preparation lower than it started. Redesigning the week has to come before buying anything, and it costs nothing at all.

What follows works forward through the two years. The first IGCSE year and what it should establish. The four revision activities families use, ranked by what each one genuinely builds rather than by how productive it feels. The revision timetable that survives nine subjects. How to use the school's mock cycle as evidence. What the last month should contain. Then the practicalities of holding a weekly slot across a whole year in a Sunday-to-Thursday week, and where a parent's help stops being help.

programmes.description: Certificated subject by subject, with tiered entry on many syllabuses. Core carries grades C to G; Extended carries A* to E, so the entry decision has a hard consequence.
programmes.countryNote: The most widespread entry in Saudi British-curriculum schools. Preparation starts by writing down the syllabus code and the component list, because both change what the papers contain.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded nine to one, with its own paper structures, assessment objectives and specification codes that do not translate directly from Cambridge.
programmes.countryNote: Entered by a number of schools in Jeddah and the Eastern Province. A revision plan written for the other board will prepare a candidate for papers they are not sitting.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: An alternative route through the same age range, assessed against published criteria rather than external papers, with the Personal Project in the final year.
programmes.countryNote: Some Saudi families move between this and IGCSE between schools. The transferable part is analytical writing; the part that needs rebuilding is examination timing.

igcse-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Preparation differs by subject because the component that decides the grade differs. These are the IGCSE subjects Saudi families most often arrange a year of support in.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Everything later rests on algebraic fluency. The long structured questions pay for shown working rather than for a correct final line.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside Mathematics in some schools as preparation for A Level. Pace is the usual difficulty rather than difficulty itself.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Equation rearrangement under time pressure, and the practical-skills component that many candidates meet properly only in revision.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles work and strictly marked definitions. The practical paper examines method reading rather than chemistry knowledge.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The largest content load, where topics taught last are revised least and appear in the papers as unfamiliar.

subjects.name: English as a First Language
subjects.description: Reading questions and directed writing, both decided by timing discipline more often than by ability.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study detail and skills questions on maps and graphs, where precision earns marks that general knowledge does not.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Definitions, diagrams and the extended response, which needs a judgement rather than a summary of both sides.

igcse-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: A weekly slot held for a year has to survive local reality, and the local reality differs sharply across the Kingdom.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: Long school runs across a city about an hour wide. A slot that starts after seven in the evening survives the whole year; an earlier one does not.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: Boards vary school by school along the coastal spine, so the first thing a year-long plan records here is which specification the school entered.

regions.name: Al Khobar
regions.note: Part of one market with Dammam and Dhahran, and linked to Bahrain by the King Fahd Causeway, so weekend travel often reshapes Thursday evenings.

regions.name: Ras Tanura
regions.note: A small industrial community where the school roll is limited and a subject may be taught by a non-specialist for a whole year.

regions.name: Taif
regions.note: Inland and higher than Jeddah, with few international entries, so candidates here are often preparing without a local specialist in any subject.

regions.name: Ha'il and AlUla
regions.note: Thin provision and long distances. A year-long weekly slot held remotely is the only arrangement that behaves the same in January as in May.

schoolClusters.note: International provision is concentrated, and a subject's teaching quality can change between years when a specialist leaves, which is often what prompts a family to look outside.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: A long-established international sector running several different curricula, where families compare schools on subject availability rather than on reputation alone.

sections.heading: What the first IGCSE year should establish, and what it usually does not
paragraphs: The first IGCSE year is where preparation is cheapest and least visible. Nothing is being examined, so nothing feels urgent, and families reasonably leave it alone. The cost shows up eighteen months later, when a candidate who never secured algebraic manipulation cannot get through a multi-step question in Physics or Chemistry, and the final year has to pay for the repair at the worst possible moment. One hour a week in the first year is worth several in the last term.

Three things are worth establishing early and they are all habits rather than topics. The first is writing answers rather than recognising them, because a student who can follow a worked solution often cannot produce one alone. The second is reading the command word before answering, which costs nothing and is almost never taught explicitly. The third is keeping marked work, so that by the final year there is a record of recurring errors rather than a vague sense that maths is hard.

This is also the year to settle the administrative facts while they are still open. Which board the school enters, which syllabus codes, whether subjects are tiered, and which optional or practical components are being taken. Ask for that in writing. A family who knows the component list in the first year never buys preparation aimed at the wrong paper, which is the most expensive single mistake available in this market and an easy one to make.

sections.heading: Four revision activities, and what each one actually builds
paragraphs: Most students revise by re-reading, because it feels productive and is almost completely ineffective at producing marks. Recognition is not recall, and a page that looks familiar creates a confidence that collapses in the examination hall. The activities that build marks are the uncomfortable ones: retrieving from memory with the book closed, answering questions without the notes open, and sitting complete papers to a clock. Discomfort is the signal that something is being built rather than reviewed.

Each activity also belongs to a stage. Retrieval practice makes sense as soon as a topic has been taught, so it belongs to both years. Topic questions belong to the term after teaching, when there is enough material to apply. Full timed papers belong to the final two terms, because a paper sat before the syllabus is complete mostly measures what has not been covered yet. Marking is the activity that converts the others into direction, and it is the one students cannot do for themselves.

The practical arrangement that works is simple: the student supplies volume, somebody who knows the scheme supplies the marking, and the tutored hour is spent on whatever the marking exposed. That uses paid time on the part a student genuinely cannot do alone, and it leaves them doing the work that builds stamina. It also makes progress visible as marks by question type rather than as a general impression that things are probably going better than they were.

sections.heading: A revision timetable that survives eight or nine entries
paragraphs: With nine subjects and five school evenings, the arithmetic does not allow deep revision in everything at once, and pretending otherwise produces a timetable nobody follows. The approach that works is staggering: three or four subjects in active revision at any point, rotated every few weeks, with the rest kept warm by short retrieval sessions. That way each subject gets concentrated attention several times rather than a thin slice every week.

Order the rotation by weakness and by distance from the papers, not by preference. Students naturally revise the subjects they enjoy, which is why the subject that needed the work is the one still unprepared in the final month. It helps to write the rotation down and show it to the subject teachers, who will usually say immediately whether a subject has been given too little room. That conversation is free and better informed than any purchased plan.

Protect two things inside the week regardless of rotation. One evening should be completely free, because a week with no slack produces cancellations rather than progress. And coursework, where a subject still has it, needs its own protected time rather than the gaps left over, since coursework deadlines arrive during the same weeks as the heaviest revision. A timetable that respects both tends to survive a term; one that respects neither rarely lasts a month, and the student is usually blamed for a plan that was never workable. Build in the slack first and the rotation around it.

sections.heading: Using the school's mock cycle as evidence rather than as a verdict
paragraphs: Most schools run more than one set of mock examinations, and the sets are not interchangeable. An early mock, often on partial content, tells a family whether revision has started and whether the student can work to a clock. A later full mock tells them where the marks are actually going. Treating the first as a prediction produces unnecessary alarm, and treating the second as just another test wastes the most useful evidence the school will generate all year.

Ask for the marked script rather than the grade, then count the losses by cause. Marks lost to blank questions point at pace. Marks lost on questions that were attempted and nearly right point at command terms and unshown working. Marks spread evenly across everything point at content. Most candidates have one dominant cause, and the preparation that follows should attack that one rather than covering everything again at equal depth.

The mock is also the moment to check the tier question against reality, because it stops being a choice once entries close. On a tiered Cambridge subject a Core entry cannot be awarded above a C however the papers go, and a family is entitled to know that before paying for work aimed at a higher grade. Where the entry looks wrong, the conversation with the school needs to happen immediately, since it is reversible only while the entry window remains open and the school needs time to process a change.

sections.heading: The last month: instructions, paper discipline and small habits
paragraphs: In the final month almost nothing new should be learned, and the work that pays looks unimpressively small. Reading the question twice. Writing the working even when the answer is obvious. Giving the answer to the accuracy the paper asked for. Using the material in the extract rather than remembered knowledge. Leaving nothing blank. Each of those is worth marks in several subjects at once, and each is a habit rather than a topic, which is why a month is enough time to install them.

Full papers under time stay the main activity, but their purpose changes. Earlier in the year a paper diagnoses; now it rehearses. The useful routine is one paper, marked quickly, and then twenty minutes on the two or three question types that lost the most, repeated. Candidates who do this four or five times usually stop making the same mistake, which is a more reliable gain than any amount of additional content revision at this stage.

Protect sleep and the week before the papers. A student who has revised steadily for two terms gains nothing from a final fortnight of late nights and loses real marks to tiredness in the hall. Tutored hours should thin out rather than intensify in the last two weeks, because by then the student needs rehearsal and rest more than they need teaching. Saying that plainly is part of the job, even though it reduces the number of hours sold in the weeks that matter most commercially.

sections.heading: Holding a weekly slot for a year: the Saudi week, the clock and the long holidays
paragraphs: Schools in the Kingdom run Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend, and a slot that has to survive a full academic year needs to be chosen for the worst week rather than the easiest one. Six until eight in the evening is the window that holds across the year once the school run and homework are accounted for. Thursday evening carries a longer session comfortably because Friday follows it, and mid-week evenings are where cancellations accumulate.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks, which matters far more over a year than over a short block. A tutor in a country that observes daylight saving will shift relative to Saudi time twice during the course, and a slot agreed as a bare hour will move without anybody deciding to move it. Write it down as Saudi local time once, and the problem disappears for the rest of the year.

Then there are the breaks. The autumn break, the midyear break, the Eid Al Fitr break and the long summer all interrupt a weekly arrangement, and the two defensible approaches are to pause and hold the slot, or to run a lighter pattern through them. Ramadan shortens school days and shifts study patterns, and because it moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar it lands at a different point in the course for each cohort. Agree all of that in advance rather than week by week.

sections.heading: What a parent can usefully do, and where helping turns into harming
paragraphs: Parents have more useful levers than they are usually told. Protecting the timetable is one, since a student cannot defend their own evening against family plans. Asking to see marked work each week is another, and it changes behaviour simply by being expected. Asking the subject teacher what they would want to see this student doing differently is the single most valuable free action available, and the answer is almost always concrete.

Coursework, where a subject still has it, is where good intentions cause real damage. The work has to be the student's own and the school has to declare it as such. A parent or tutor may ask questions about a draft the student wrote, point out that a paragraph does not do what the task asked, and explain the criterion in plain words. Neither should supply sentences, rewrite a passage into its final form, or correct the text line by line, because what gets submitted then is no longer the candidate's own work.

Keep the record straightforward. Drafts stay in the student's own files, feedback stays as questions and comments rather than replacement text, and the school's teacher remains the authority on what the task requires. If a provider offers to produce a finished piece of coursework as part of a preparation package, that is malpractice being sold as a service, and the consequences of it fall on the candidate rather than on the seller. Walk away from that conversation and tell the school about it.

faqs.question: How often should an IGCSE tutor report during a year-long preparation programme?
faqs.answer: Weekly in one line, termly in detail. The weekly note should say what was covered, what was set and what the marked work showed, which takes a tutor two minutes and tells a parent whether anything is drifting. The termly review should be longer and should include a judgement on whether to continue. A tutor who only reports when asked is a tutor nobody is checking.

faqs.question: Is a current classroom teacher a better choice than a full-time tutor for a whole year of IGCSE work?
faqs.answer: Both work, and the trade-off is real. A current teacher knows how the specification is being taught and how schools interpret it, but has limited availability and marks their own classes first. A full-time tutor has flexibility and usually more experience of one-to-one diagnosis. For a year-long arrangement, availability matters more than it does for a short block, so ask how many weeks of the year they can genuinely hold the same slot.

faqs.question: Does it help if an IGCSE tutor has taught in a Saudi school, or is that irrelevant online?
faqs.answer: It helps at the margins rather than at the core. Someone who has taught here understands the Sunday-to-Thursday week, how school calendars vary and how Ramadan changes a study pattern, which saves explaining. What matters far more is the specification they have taught and the component they know. A tutor who has never worked in the Kingdom but has taught the exact syllabus code is the better choice of the two.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should one tutor cover for the same student?
faqs.answer: One, or two closely related ones at most. A tutor covering four subjects is a generalist in all of them, and IGCSE papers reward specification-level knowledge: the command words a particular board favours, the way a practical component is assessed, the question types that recur. Mathematics with Physics, or Chemistry with Biology, can work when the tutor's background genuinely covers both. Four subjects from one person usually means shallow coverage of three.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether a tutor is teaching to the specification or to a revision guide?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the assessment objectives for the paper and say how the marks are distributed across components. Someone working from the specification answers directly and will often point out where a popular revision guide is out of date or covers the other board. Someone working from a guide talks about topics without reference to how they are examined. The difference shows up within one lesson and it predicts the whole year.

faqs.question: How is progress tracked across a whole year of online IGCSE sessions?
faqs.answer: As marks by question type, held in one running record rather than as a series of impressions. Each marked paper or section is logged against the component and the question type that lost marks, so by the spring term there is a visible pattern. That record is also what makes an honest termly judgement possible: if the same question type is still losing marks after two terms, the approach needs changing rather than repeating.

faqs.question: Can a parent in Saudi Arabia see what happened in each online IGCSE session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it works better as a record than as an audience. The whiteboard pages from each session can be kept and shared, which is more useful than video because they are short and searchable. A weekly note says what was covered and set. Sitting in occasionally is fine and worth agreeing with the student first, since a teenager who feels observed usually stops asking the questions that make the hour worthwhile.

faqs.question: How are past papers and mark schemes shared for an online IGCSE programme?
faqs.answer: Through the school first, because the school knows which syllabus code and which series are appropriate for the entry. Beyond that, the board publishes specimen and past materials, and a tutor will usually set specific papers rather than hand over a folder. The important part is that a paper is sat under time on paper and then photographed, rather than worked through on screen with the mark scheme a click away.

faqs.question: Can two siblings sitting the same IGCSE subject share a session?
faqs.answer: It can work when the two are genuinely at the same point, which is less common than families hope. Two candidates in the same year with similar marks and the same tier can share a session usefully, especially for teaching rather than for marking review. Where one is stronger, the hour drifts towards the middle and serves neither well. Diagnostic sessions and paper reviews should always be individual, because the recurring errors differ.

faqs.question: How does a student ask a question between weekly online sessions?
faqs.answer: By sending the question with a photograph of what they tried, which is more useful to both sides than a description. A short written answer or a two-minute explanation usually resolves it, and anything larger becomes the opening of the next session. Setting a limit is sensible: unlimited messaging sounds generous and tends to replace the thinking a student needs to do alone before asking.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE Biology topics are most often rushed at the end of the course?
faqs.answer: Inheritance and variation, the plant transport and transpiration material, and the ecology and human influence topics usually come last and get the least teaching time. Candidates then meet them in revision as unfamiliar rather than difficult. If a preparation plan is being written in the spring term, these are often where the quickest marks are, because the student has simply had less contact with them than with the earlier cell and nutrition content.

faqs.question: Why do strong IGCSE Mathematics students still lose marks on the longer questions?
faqs.answer: Because they do the arithmetic in their heads and write only the answer. Longer structured questions award method marks for the steps, so a candidate who reaches the right answer by an unwritten route can score far below one who works more slowly and shows everything. The second cause is not reading the accuracy instruction. Both are habits rather than gaps in ability, and both respond to a handful of marked papers rather than to more teaching.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE Business Studies six-mark answer need that a four-mark one does not?
faqs.answer: A judgement, and usually a reason for choosing it. Lower-tariff questions reward accurate definitions and applied points from the case material. The longest questions want two sides considered and then a decision supported by the context given, not a balanced summary that declines to decide. Candidates who write more of the same thing rather than adding evaluation tend to plateau at the same mark however much content they revise.

faqs.question: Where does weak reading comprehension show up outside IGCSE English?
faqs.answer: In Geography and Business Studies case material, in Biology questions built around an unfamiliar context, and in the longer Physics and Chemistry questions that describe a method before asking anything. A candidate who skims the stem answers a question that was not asked. It often reads as a subject weakness when it is a reading habit, and the fix belongs in the subject lesson rather than in extra English work.

intro.heading: Two years, a syllabus code, and a published mark scheme
paragraphs: IGCSE is the most tractable qualification a family will ever buy tuition for, and that is worth understanding before any money changes hands. Every subject has a printed syllabus code, a published specimen paper, past papers going back years, and a mark scheme that states what earns each mark. Nothing about this course is a mystery. When a student is three grades below where they should be, the reason is almost always visible in a marked script, and the cost of fixing it is therefore predictable in a way that very little else in education is.

That is why the money is so often spent badly. The common pattern in the Kingdom is a family buying general tuition in a named subject, at a rate somewhere between what a platform advertises and what a premium agency quotes, with no diagnosis beforehand and no measurement afterwards. The tutor teaches the topic the student mentions, the student feels better, and the grade stays where it was because the fault was never in the content. A year of that costs more than a correctly diagnosed term, and it buys less.

The faults that actually cost IGCSE marks are a short list, and each has a price. A student entered for the wrong tier has a grade ceiling no amount of teaching lifts. A student being tutored against the wrong board's question style is practising for a different examination. A student who knows the content and skips the working loses method marks in every calculation paper. A student who has never sat a full paper to time loses the last extended-response question every single time. None of those is a knowledge problem, and all of them are commonly treated as one.

Delivery needs stating plainly, because the search phrase says home. Lessons arranged through IB Gram are delivered one to one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, to families anywhere in the Kingdom. We do not arrange home visits anywhere in Saudi Arabia; visiting tuition is something we run only in India. The relevant consequence is financial as well as practical: a visiting tutor's rate includes the travel, the settling and the sessions lost to traffic, and in a city an hour across, that is a real fraction of what you pay.

What follows is a cost page with the arithmetic shown. It sets out the advertised SAR bands in this market and who publishes them, what moves an hourly rate, what a visiting arrangement costs per taught minute against an online one, what the Core and Extended tier decision caps, which subjects are cheap to repair and which are not, and what an hour of tuition should contain before you agree to pay for it. The last part matters most: the rate is far less predictive of value than what happens between the lessons.

igcse-home-tuition.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits in the middle of a pathway, and the two years either side of it decide how much tuition the course itself ends up needing. These are the programmes a Saudi family is choosing between and moving through, with the money question attached to each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written paper, each with a four-digit syllabus code printed on every past paper. Many subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, and Cambridge reports grades from A* to G. The tier a student is entered for caps the grade available to them, so it is the highest-stakes decision in the whole qualification and it is frequently made by default rather than deliberately.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi candidates sit the June series as the main sitting and the November series for resits and November-entry candidates. Entries are made by the school through a registered examination centre, so the examinations officer rather than the family controls the deadline. Confirm the subject, the tier and the components your child is entered for in writing; a surprising number of tuition arrangements are built on a parent's assumption about which paper is being sat.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same level of qualification with a different question style, a different specification structure and numeric grading from 9 to 1. Some subjects are untiered where the Cambridge equivalent is tiered, and the balance between short-answer and extended-response questions differs. Content overlap with Cambridge is high; question style overlap is much lower, and that distinction is where tuition money gets wasted.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom use both boards, sometimes different ones for different subjects in the same school. A tutor who teaches the subject but not the board will prepare a student well for the wrong paper, which is the most expensive avoidable error in this market. Ask for the specification code, not just the subject name, and check it against the front page of your child's past papers.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed internally by schools with the optional Checkpoint tests at the end. Nothing here appears on a certificate, which is why families underinvest in it and then pay more later. Almost every expensive IGCSE problem in mathematics and the sciences traces back to a manipulation or arithmetic weakness that was visible and cheap to fix at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: This is the cheapest tuition a family in the Kingdom will ever buy and the most cost-effective. Two terms of work on algebraic manipulation and number fluency before Year 10 costs a fraction of the same repair attempted in the term before the June series, when it competes with an entire two-year syllabus for the student's attention.

programmes.name: What follows: A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE results determine which post-16 courses a student can realistically take, and schools apply entry requirements per subject. A student entered for the Core tier in mathematics will not usually be admitted to a demanding post-16 mathematics course, and a student without the Extended science grades will face the same restriction for Higher Level sciences in the Diploma Programme.
programmes.countryNote: This is the argument for spending on IGCSE rather than waiting. A grade repaired at IGCSE keeps a post-16 option open; the same grade left alone closes it, and reopening it later means a resit in the November series on top of a new course. For Saudi families also considering a Saudi university, the equivalency and Qiyas process sits further down the same road and is best understood early.

igcse-home-tuition.subjectsIntro: Some IGCSE subjects are cheap to repair and some are not, and the difference is worth knowing before you buy hours. The guide below pairs each subject with where the marks are actually lost and roughly how much work the repair tends to be.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580)
subjects.description: Cheap to repair and quick to measure, because the marks are in the working. Most lost marks come from arithmetic slips under time pressure and from writing a final answer with no method, which forfeits every stage mark when the answer is wrong. Timed sets marked against the scheme move this faster than re-teaching topics. The tier decision matters more here than in any other subject.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A harder course taken alongside or instead of 0580 by students heading for demanding post-16 mathematics. Calculus and trigonometry arrive at a pace that exposes any weakness in algebra immediately, so repair work here is usually two layers deep and takes longer. Worth the investment for a student aiming at Higher Level mathematics; poor value as a last-minute rescue.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Formula recall is assumed more than students expect, and the practical-skills paper tests the handling of apparatus and data rather than recall. Marks go on units, on significant figures, and on graph questions that produce a gradient without stating what it means. The data-handling half can be repaired entirely without a laboratory, which makes it efficient tuition.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: The highest-return subject for a few focused hours. Ionic equations, state symbols, mole calculations with the working shown, and the qualitative analysis tables account for a large share of dropped marks, and all four are learnable in a short block. Organic chemistry is the part that takes longer, because the conventions have to be unlearned before they are relearned.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Definitions are examined to the word, so a student who understands a process perfectly can still score nothing for defining it. That makes a cheap, high-yield repair: learn the examined wording, then be tested cold. The practical paper rewards students who have drawn and labelled their own diagrams, which is straightforward to practise on a shared whiteboard.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: One or two award options covering all three sciences in a single qualification. Less depth than the separate sciences, which suits a student who needs breadth, but it narrows post-16 options for Higher Level science. If a student is on this route and aiming at a science-heavy post-16 course, that conversation is more valuable than any amount of content tuition.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: The reading questions are where the marks hide and where students underprepare. Marks go for selecting and using detail from the passage, not for writing well in general, so a fluent and lengthy answer that floats free of the text scores in the middle bands. Repair is structural and reasonably quick: a repeatable method for annotating a passage before writing.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing and listening, with an assessed speaking component in the 0511 variant. Marks are awarded on register and task fulfilment rather than vocabulary range, so the commonest loss is a strong piece of writing in the wrong text type. Practising text types against real prompts is inexpensive tuition with a fast return.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Two papers, one multiple choice and one structured data response. Diagram accuracy carries marks that no amount of prose recovers, and the data-response questions reward quoting the extract rather than answering from general knowledge. A student who learns to draw six diagrams correctly and use the extract gains more than one who reads the textbook again.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: Application and evaluation carry the upper bands, and recall carries the lower ones, so a student who can define every term and apply none plateaus in the middle. The calculations are reliable marks and are routinely left blank. Repair here is about answer structure rather than content, which makes it quick but hard to do without marked examples.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions and trace tables are the highest-yield topics for the time invested, and they are where confident programmers lose marks because they have never written an algorithm out by hand. Systems topics reward precise terminology. A specialist is harder to find for this subject than for any other at this level, which shows in what it is advertised at.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (Cambridge 0417)
subjects.description: Practical papers assessed on precise task completion, where marks go for following an instruction exactly rather than for producing something that looks right. Students lose marks on file naming, on evidence documents and on formatting details that feel trivial and are not. A checklist habit fixes most of it in a handful of sessions.

igcse-home-tuition.regionsTitle: What changes city by city across the Kingdom
igcse-home-tuition.regionsIntro: IGCSE provision is concentrated in a few places and thin in most of the country, and that affects both what families pay and what they can find. The practical differences across the Kingdom are about the local tutor pool and the shape of the school run, not about the syllabus, which is identical everywhere.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest tutor pool and the widest spread of advertised rates, from platform listings around SAR 50 for primary work to SAR 200 and above for senior examination subjects. The city takes about an hour to cross in traffic, so a visiting arrangement carries a real travel loading that an online session does not.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, with British-curriculum and Cambridge schools spread along it. A tutor living at one end of that spine is not a practical visiting option at the other, which narrows a local pool far more than the city's size suggests.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market in practice, with families routinely living in one city and attending school in another. Controlled access at the Aramco and university compounds adds a step to any visiting arrangement that an online lesson does not have to clear.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Makkah sits roughly 80km east of Jeddah, and both cities have their own private school provision alongside a seasonal rhythm that shapes the family calendar. International-curriculum choice is narrower than in Jeddah, so families here often look outside the city for subject specialists.

regions.name: Al Ahsa and Qatif
regions.note: Al Ahsa lies about an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster and Qatif on the coast to its north. Both have families whose children attend school in the cluster, which means a long drive is already part of the day before any tuition is scheduled.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities with their own international provision and small cohorts. A small cohort means a subject may not run at all in a given year, which is the point at which a family is choosing between an online course and changing school rather than between two tutors.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: The north-west, where new communities are growing faster than school provision. Families arriving mid-course are common here, and the first tuition question is usually about catching up on a syllabus taught in a different order rather than about a weak subject.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About 25km apart in 'Asir at high altitude, sharing a catchment. Together they are the main school market in the south, and they are still a long way from Riyadh and Jeddah, so the local specialist pool for any single IGCSE subject is small.

regions.name: Ha'il, Buraidah and the interior
regions.note: Provincial centres where international-curriculum cohorts are small and dispersed. Distance is the binding constraint rather than price: there may simply be nobody locally who teaches a given syllabus, at any rate, which is the honest case for teaching by video.

schoolClusters.note: Cambridge pathways run through a number of the international and private schools along the Jeddah spine, several of which also appear in IB listings. Boards differ by school and sometimes by subject within a school, so the specification code on a past paper is a more reliable guide than the school's prospectus. Fees and subject availability both vary widely across this group.

British and Cambridge curricula are well established around Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam, alongside the International Schools Group campuses. Because cohorts are small, the subjects a school can actually run at IGCSE vary year to year, and a subject offered in the prospectus is not always timetabled. Ask which subjects ran last year rather than which are listed.

igcse-home-tuition.modesIntro: Four formats cover almost every IGCSE enquiry from the Kingdom, and they cost different amounts because they contain different things. All are delivered one to one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, Sunday to Thursday, with weekend slots available for intensive blocks.

modes.title: A four-session diagnostic block
modes.description: The cheapest way to find out whether tuition will help, and the one we suggest first. Four sessions built around the student's own marked work: one to establish a baseline on a timed paper, two to work the errors, one to write down what the pattern is and what a term of work would target. At the end you have a diagnosis you can act on, including the option of not continuing.
bullets: A timed baseline paper marked against the published scheme
The recurring fault named in writing, not described in general terms
A costed plan for a term, or an honest recommendation to stop
No package commitment before the block is finished

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the course
modes.description: A fixed slot each week with written work set and marked between sessions. This is the format that moves a grade over a term or two, and the marking is what makes it work: an hour of teaching with nothing marked in between is roughly half a service at a full price. For two weak subjects, two separate specialists is almost always better value than one tutor covering both.
bullets: Same hour each week, pinned to Saudi local time
Work marked and returned before the following lesson
A written note naming what was covered and what is next

modes.title: Paper clinic before a series
modes.description: A short block of timed papers in the weeks before the June or November series, marked against the published scheme and worked through error by error. The agenda comes from the script rather than from the syllabus. This is where a student who knows the content and loses marks anyway makes the fastest gains, and it is poor value for a student who has not covered the course.

A recurring-error list that gets revisited rather than mentioned once
Two or three sessions a week for a fixed block, then it ends
