modes.title: Single-subject rescue and resit preparation
modes.description: One subject, a fixed number of sessions, a specific target: a tier change, an entry decision, or a resit in the November series. The scope is agreed at the start and the arrangement ends when it is met. Families use this when the rest of the timetable is fine and one grade is standing in the way of a post-16 option.

Built around the specific component that is costing the grade

sections.heading: What IGCSE home tuition actually buys, and five ways the money is wasted
paragraphs: Taken literally, the search means a tutor working with one student outside school hours on an IGCSE course. In the Kingdom the service is sold in three shapes: a tutor who travels to the family, a centre the student attends, and one-to-one teaching delivered live over video. IB Gram does the third. We do not arrange home visits anywhere in Saudi Arabia; visiting tuition is a service we run only in India. The comparison below is about what each shape costs per taught minute, which is the part the advertised rate hides.

Before any of that, though, there is the question of whether the money will do anything, and five failure patterns account for most of the waste in this market. The first is the tier. A student entered for the Core tier has a grade ceiling that no quantity of teaching lifts; if the target grade sits above that ceiling, the only intervention that matters is a conversation with the school about the entry, and it has to happen long before the papers.

The second is the board. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel examine the same content with different question styles and different specification structures, and a tutor who teaches the subject rather than the specification prepares a student thoroughly for the wrong paper. The third is paying for content when the fault is technique: a student who skips working, misreads a command word or never finishes a paper has a technique problem, and a term of re-teaching topics leaves it exactly where it was.

The fourth is spreading the money too thin — an hour a week across three subjects buys a little of nothing in each, where four weeks concentrated on the weakest subject produces a visible change. The fifth is buying hours with no baseline, which makes the whole arrangement unmeasurable: with no timed paper on record from the start, nobody can say at the end whether the hours did anything, and the default is to keep paying.

sections.heading: Advertised SAR rates in this market, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Rates are published inconsistently here, so the only honest treatment is to say who advertises what. The figures in the table are advertised rates drawn from tutoring platforms, tutor-marketplace guides, tutoring companies and international providers serving the Kingdom. They are not a market average, they are not what IB Gram charges, and they are not comparable with each other: the bottom of that range and the top describe different products as much as different prices.

What moves an hourly rate, in rough order of weight, is subject scarcity first. A specialist in a subject few people can teach well — Computer Science and Additional Mathematics at this level, and the separate sciences at Extended tier — costs more than a generalist, everywhere, because the pool is smaller. After that comes marking or examining experience, then level, where IGCSE sits below Diploma Programme Higher Level and above Lower Secondary work. Then whether the tutor travels, and then package length, which is the only one of the five the family controls.

Travel deserves a line of its own because it is invisible in a quoted rate. A tutor who drives across Riyadh or along the Jeddah spine is paid for that time whether the invoice itemises it or not, and the first and last few minutes of the session go on arriving and leaving. In a city that takes an hour to cross, a nominal sixty-minute visit can be forty-five minutes of teaching, which changes the real cost per taught minute considerably.

The question worth asking is not the rate but what the hour contains. An hour that includes work marked and returned before the next session, a written note naming the fault, and a baseline you can compare against is a different product from an hour of conversation about the topic the student raised at the start. There is a legitimate place for a cheap generalist: for arithmetic fluency drills, a capable graduate who sets and marks practice is good value. For Extended-tier chemistry mechanisms, they are not.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against online one-to-one, priced per taught minute
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search phrase is really about, and it deserves arithmetic rather than assertion. Take two nominal hours at the same headline rate, one with a tutor travelling to the family and one over live video, and compare what the family receives. The honest answer is that the online hour contains more teaching, costs less per taught minute, and draws on a far larger pool of specialists — and that there are situations where the visiting arrangement is still the right choice.

On teaching time: a visit includes arriving, settling, and leaving, and in practice a sixty-minute booking often delivers forty-five to fifty minutes of work. A video session starts on the minute and ends on the minute. On the rate itself: travel is loaded in, openly by some agencies and quietly by independent tutors, and the loading rises with the distance and the traffic. On reliability: a session lost to a blocked road in Riyadh or a closure on the Jeddah corniche is a session the family has lost, and in a long arrangement that happens more than once.

The pool is the part families underestimate. A visiting tutor must live within a reasonable drive, which in a large Saudi city means a handful of districts. Within those districts, the number of people who can teach Extended-tier chemistry or 0478 Computer Science to examination standard may be zero. Online, the constraint is only whether someone who teaches that specification is free at your hour, which turns an availability problem into a scheduling one.

The trade-offs are real and worth naming. A young child usually works better with an adult in the room. A student who will not engage on a screen is not fixed by a better platform. A practical subject needs the school's laboratory whatever happens in a tutorial. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student working through past papers with a mark scheme, though, a shared screen is not a compromise on sitting side by side; it is the same activity, starting on time, with a wider choice of teacher.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the grade ceiling nobody mentions
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers a number of IGCSE subjects into Core and Extended, and the two are examined by different papers covering different amounts of the syllabus. Core is graded from C to G and Extended from A* to E, which means a student entered for Core cannot be awarded a grade above C however well they perform. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades numerically from 9 to 1 and tiers fewer subjects. Either way, the entry decision sets a ceiling before any teaching happens, and it is the single most consequential thing a family can get wrong.

Schools make the tier decision on evidence, usually mock results and classwork, and they are generally right. The problem arises when a student improves after the decision, or when the decision was made early and conservatively, or when nobody told the family it had been made at all. A parent paying for weekly tuition to lift a student from a C to an A, in a subject where the student is entered for Core, is buying something that cannot be delivered, and no amount of teaching quality changes that.

The practical steps are short. Ask the school, in writing, which subjects your child is entered for, at which tier, and for which components. Ask when the entry can still be changed and what evidence the school would want in order to change it. If a tier change is the goal, that is the tuition brief: produce work at Extended standard, under timed conditions, early enough for the school to act on it. That is a different programme from general support, with a different deadline and a different measure of success.

The reverse case matters too. A student entered for Extended who is a long way from the standard may do better on Core, where the grade available is lower but achievable and a near-miss is avoided. That is an uncomfortable conversation and sometimes the right one. A tutor who looks at a marked script and tells you the tier is wrong in either direction has given you more value in an hour than a term of hours aimed at the wrong target.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost, and what each repair costs in hours
paragraphs: Marks at this level are lost in a small number of predictable ways, and the useful thing about that is the cost of each repair is roughly knowable. A family deciding how much tuition to buy is better served by this list than by a rate card, because it tells you what you are buying and roughly how long it takes.

The cheapest repairs are the mechanical ones. Examined definitions in biology and economics, where a paraphrase scores nothing, need a few minutes a week of cold testing rather than any teaching. Method marks in calculation papers need the student to mark their own work against the scheme until the penny drops, which is usually three or four sessions. Command-word discipline — answering state in a clause and explain in a causal chain — is a short drill with past-paper stems and a habit afterwards.

The middle band takes a term. Interpreting an extract or a data set rather than answering from general knowledge is a structural habit that has to be rebuilt across many examples. Graph and diagram work, where a correct sketch loses half its marks for missing labels, is quick to explain and slow to become automatic. Timing is the same: a student who runs out of minutes needs full papers under a hard stop, repeatedly, and there is no shortcut that makes that faster than it is.

The expensive repairs are the ones with a layer underneath. Algebraic manipulation that was never secure in Lower Secondary shows up in every topic that follows, and fixing it means going back before going forward. Organic chemistry conventions learned loosely have to be unlearned first. A student who has not covered a substantial part of the course cannot be rescued by technique work at all, and anybody who says otherwise in the final weeks before a series is selling optimism.
bullets: A few sessions: examined definitions, method marks, command words, labelling
A term: extract and data interpretation, timing, answer structure in essay subjects
Longer: algebra from Lower Secondary, organic conventions, uncovered syllabus
Not fixable late: a syllabus that was never taught, or a tier that caps the grade

sections.heading: What an hour of IGCSE tuition should contain before you pay for it
paragraphs: Two tutors can charge the same rate and deliver very different things, which is why the rate is a poor guide to value. The difference is almost entirely in what happens outside the lesson. An hour that is preceded by the tutor reading the student's marked work, and followed by work set, marked and returned before the next session, does several times as much as an hour of live conversation at the same price.

There are four questions that separate the two, and they can be asked in a first email. What will you read before the first session? What is set between lessons, and is it marked and returned before the next one? What do I receive after each session, and in what form? And how will we know in eight weeks whether this worked? A specialist answers all four without hesitating. Anybody who treats them as unusual questions has told you how they work.

The written note after each session is worth insisting on, and it should be specific rather than encouraging. What was covered, named by topic and component. What the student got right. What is still wrong. What has been set. Over a term those notes become the record you review against the baseline, which is the only way to tell the difference between progress and habit. A note that says the session went well is not information, and asking for the specific version is not an imposition.

The baseline is the last piece. A timed paper sat in the first session, marked against the published scheme and kept, is what makes the whole arrangement measurable. Without it, the conversation at the end of a term is about feelings and invoices. With it, the conversation is short: the paper moved or it did not, and if it did not, the right decision is a different tutor or a different diagnosis rather than more of the same hours.

sections.heading: One-to-one, small groups and recorded courses: what each is worth
paragraphs: The three formats sold into this market are not substitutes, and the pricing difference between them is smaller than the difference in what they do. Choosing on price alone is how families end up paying twice: once for the cheap option and again for the one that works.

A recorded course is the cheapest and has one genuine use: covering content the student has not met, at their own pace, with replay. It cannot diagnose, it cannot mark, and it cannot tell a student that the reason they lose marks is that they answer a different question from the one asked. For a student who has missed a term through illness or a move, it is good value. For a student who knows the content and loses marks anyway, it is the wrong purchase at any price.

A small group works when the students share the same gap. Three candidates who all misread data-response questions can be taught together productively, and the discussion is part of the teaching rather than a dilution of it. The rate per student falls, which is the attraction. What a group cannot do is run at one student's pace: a student who needs to go back to algebraic manipulation gets a share of the attention and the full group pace, which is the worst of both.

One-to-one is the expensive option and the only one that adapts. It is the right buy when the fault is specific to the student, when coursework or a tier decision is involved, when the timetable is tight before a series, or when the subject is scarce enough that no group exists. The sensible pattern for many families is a mix: content from a course or the school, technique and diagnosis one to one, and no payment at all for the overlap between them.

sections.heading: Trials, packages, cancellations and what happens to unused hours
paragraphs: The commercial mechanics matter more than families expect, because they determine how much flexibility you have when something is not working. Three things are worth settling before the first paid session: what the trial produces, how hours are bought, and what happens to hours you do not use.

The trial should be diagnostic rather than a sample lesson, and it should be free. A useful trial puts the student's own marked work in front of a specialist and produces a short written account of where the student stands plus one named first target. You should finish it knowing something you did not know before. A trial that produces reassurance has told you nothing actionable, which is a reason to meet a different tutor rather than to buy a package.

On packages: paying per lesson costs a little more per hour and keeps every option open, which is the right default until the match is proven. A package makes sense once you know the tutor works for your child and the plan runs to a series. Before agreeing to one, establish in writing how long unused hours remain valid, whether they survive a long school holiday, and what notice is needed to cancel a single lesson without being charged. Those three answers are the whole of the flexibility you are buying.

On changing tutor: if the match is wrong after two or three sessions, the right outcome is a different tutor rather than a conversation about persevering. Mismatches at this level are usually about pace, style or rapport rather than competence, and none of those improve by being endured. Be specific about what did not work — the explanations assumed knowledge the student does not have, the pace lost them in the first ten minutes — because that is what makes the second match better rather than merely different.

sections.heading: Confirming a tutor is an IGCSE specialist rather than a generalist
paragraphs: At this level the specialism claim is easy to make, because IGCSE content looks approachable to anyone with a degree in the subject. Teaching it to examination standard is a narrower skill, and the difference shows up in what a tutor knows about the papers rather than about the subject. Four questions settle it, and none of them require you to understand the subject yourself.

The first is the code. Which syllabus or specification code do you teach, which board, and which components? A specialist gives the number without looking it up and then asks which one your child is entered for, because they know the answer changes the plan. Someone who says they teach IGCSE chemistry in general, without reference to 0620 or an Edexcel specification, does not teach it regularly.

The second is the tier. Which topics appear only in the Extended papers? The third is the mark scheme: what does the scheme do with a correct final answer that shows no working, and what does it do with a borderline extended response? Somebody who has marked for the board, or who has marked a large volume of student work against published schemes, answers immediately and concretely. The fourth is practical: what will you set between lessons, and will it come back marked before the next one?

Then there is the category of claim that cannot be checked at all. A satisfaction percentage, a star rating, a count of successful candidates or a promised grade improvement, offered without a sample size, a date and a method, is marketing rather than evidence, and the confident version should make you more careful rather than less. The honest answer to how much a child will improve is a description of what will be measured, against what baseline, and when — which is also the answer that lets you hold somebody to it.
bullets: Ask for the syllabus or specification code, not the subject name
Ask which topics appear only in the Extended papers
Ask what the mark scheme does with an answer that shows no working
Ask what is set between lessons and whether it comes back marked

process.title: Confirm the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Ask the school in writing which subjects your child is entered for, with which board, at which tier, and for which components. This takes one email and prevents the two most expensive errors in this market: tutoring towards a capped grade, and preparing for a differently structured paper.

process.title: Send one marked script
process.description: A recent marked paper with the mark scheme if you have it is worth more than a report card, because it shows which marks are being lost rather than how many. Add the subject, the code and the series the student is working towards, and the diagnosis can start before anyone is paid.

process.title: Take the free diagnostic session
process.description: A specialist reads the script with the student, establishes whether the fault is content, technique or tier, and writes a short paragraph naming it with one first target. If what comes back is encouragement rather than a diagnosis, ask to meet someone else before buying any hours.

process.title: Buy a block, not a year
process.description: Start with a short, scoped block on the weakest subject rather than an hour a week across three. Agree what is set and marked between sessions, what note you receive afterwards, and the date on which you will compare a second timed paper with the baseline from the first session.

process.title: Review on the paper, then decide
process.description: Sit the comparison paper on the agreed date and read it against the baseline. Continue, change the plan, change the tutor, or stop. All four are legitimate, and deciding on evidence on a fixed date is what stops weekly lessons turning into an unexamined standing cost.

whyPoints.title: The rate is stated, and so is what it contains
whyPoints.description: Advertised rates in this market run from about SAR 35 to over SAR 200 an hour and describe entirely different products. We set the bands out with their sources and explain what moves the number, because a family cannot judge value against a figure with no context attached to it.

whyPoints.title: A diagnosis before a package
whyPoints.description: The first session is free and diagnostic, built around the student's own marked work, and it ends with the recurring fault named in writing plus one target. Sometimes the honest output is that tuition is not the right purchase, or that the tier is the real problem.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the specification, not the subject
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Edexcel examine the same content differently, and a tutor who knows the subject but not the specification prepares a student for the wrong paper. Matching starts from the syllabus code your child is entered for, which is also the first thing we ask for.

whyPoints.title: Marking between the lessons
whyPoints.description: Work is set, marked against the published scheme and returned before the next session, with a written note naming what is still wrong. That between-lesson work is the part that moves a grade, and it is the first thing to disappear when a tutor is carrying too many students.

whyPoints.title: Measured against a kept baseline
whyPoints.description: A timed paper sat in the first session and kept is what makes the arrangement auditable. Eight weeks later the question is whether the second paper moved, which has a yes or no answer, unlike whether a student seems more confident than they were.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot stand behind
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no satisfaction percentages, no ratings, no counts. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and no affiliation with any school named here.

faqs.question: How does an online tutor mark an IGCSE past paper the student wrote out on paper?
faqs.answer: The student photographs or scans the script and sends it before the session. The tutor marks it against the published scheme in advance, so the lesson starts from annotated work rather than from reading. In the session the marked script is on a shared screen and the tutor works through the errors with the student explaining their reasoning. Writing by hand matters at this level, because that is how the examination is sat, so the paper-then-photograph routine is better practice than typing answers into a document.

faqs.question: Can a parent sit in on an IGCSE session, and does it help?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it helps most at the start and then less. Sitting in on the first session tells you whether the tutor diagnoses or chats, which is the thing worth checking. After that, most students work less freely with a parent in the room, and the written note after each session carries the same information without changing how the lesson runs. A reasonable pattern is to join the first session and the review session, and to read the notes in between.

faqs.question: What platform is used for IGCSE lessons, and does anything need to be installed?
faqs.answer: A standard video platform with screen sharing and a shared whiteboard, which runs in a browser on a laptop without anything needing to be installed. The tutor usually works on a graphics tablet so they can annotate a paper by hand. What matters more than the platform is the setup at the student's end: headphones, a laptop rather than a phone, a separate sheet of paper for working, and somewhere quiet enough that the student will talk rather than nod.

faqs.question: How are past papers and mark schemes shared with the student between lessons?
faqs.answer: As files sent before and after each session, with the specific paper and component named rather than a folder of everything. The useful discipline is that the student sits the paper before seeing the scheme, then marks their own work against it, then sends both. That sequence is what makes a mark scheme teach something; handing a student the scheme alongside the questions turns a diagnostic exercise into a reading exercise and wastes the paper.

faqs.question: Does online teaching work for IGCSE subjects with a practical paper?
faqs.answer: For the data-handling and analysis half, entirely. Reading scales, recording to consistent precision, choosing axes, drawing a line of best fit, calculating a gradient and identifying a relevant source of uncertainty are all taught from past-paper data sets with the student plotting while the tutor watches. What needs a laboratory is the handling of apparatus, and that is the school's part. The sensible division is for the tutor to take the data work and leave the bench work to the teacher with the bench.

faqs.question: What is advertised for IGCSE home tuition in the Kingdom, and what does the range reflect?
faqs.answer: Advertised figures run from about SAR 35 an hour on budget online platforms, through around SAR 55 for general online tutoring and about SAR 50 for primary private tuition in Riyadh, up to SAR 200 and above for senior examination subjects, with subject specialists on international curricula advertised from about SAR 180. Those are published by platforms, marketplace guides and tutoring companies rather than being a market average, and they are not our price. The range reflects specialism, marking experience and travel, not teaching quality in any direct way.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE tuition cheaper than IB tuition for the same number of hours, and why?
faqs.answer: Usually, and the reason is the size of the pool rather than the difficulty of the hour. More teachers can teach an IGCSE syllabus competently than can teach a Diploma Programme Higher Level course to examination standard, so scarcity does less work on the price. Advertised rates reflect that: premium Higher Level tracks sit above the IGCSE bands in the same providers' listings. The exceptions are the scarce subjects at this level, where a specialist in Computer Science or Additional Mathematics can be priced like a Diploma tutor.

faqs.question: Do I pay per lesson or per package, and what happens to hours we do not use?
faqs.answer: Paying per lesson costs slightly more per hour and keeps every option open, which is the right default until the match is proven. A package makes sense once the tutor is working for your child and the plan runs to a series. Before agreeing to one, get three answers in writing: how long unused hours stay valid, whether they survive a long school holiday, and what notice cancels a single lesson without a charge. Those answers are the flexibility you are buying.

faqs.question: How many hours does one weak IGCSE subject usually take to repair?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which fault it is, which is why the diagnosis comes first. Mechanical faults — examined definitions, missing method steps, command-word discipline, diagram labelling — are a handful of sessions. Structural habits like interpreting an extract rather than answering from memory, or finishing a paper to time, take a term of weekly work. A weakness underneath the course, such as algebra that was never secure, takes longer because it means going back before going forward. An uncovered syllabus cannot be repaired by technique work at all.

faqs.question: Is a group IGCSE revision course better value than one-to-one for a resit candidate?
faqs.answer: Rarely, because a resit candidate's problem is specific to them by definition. They have sat the paper and lost marks in a particular pattern, and a group course runs at the pace of a syllabus rather than of that pattern. Where a group does work is when several candidates share one identifiable fault, such as misreading data-response questions. For a single resit in a scarce subject with a tight window before the November series, one-to-one with a scoped block and an end date is almost always the better buy.

faqs.question: Are there costs beyond the hourly rate, such as papers, materials or reports?
faqs.answer: There should not be. Past papers and mark schemes are published by the boards, the written note after each session is part of the service rather than an extra, and marking work between lessons is the service rather than an add-on. Watch for three charges that do appear in this market: a fee per coursework draft reviewed, a registration or matching fee before any teaching, and a separate charge for a written report. Ask what is included in the quoted rate before the first session, not after.

faqs.question: Why do some providers quote IGCSE tuition in US dollars?
faqs.answer: Because they are international operations billing a global client base, and one provider advertises around USD 60 an hour on that basis. For a family in the Kingdom it adds currency risk and a card charge without adding anything to the teaching, and it makes comparison against local SAR rates harder than it needs to be. It is not a quality signal in either direction. If a dollar-priced provider has the specialist you need, convert the figure and compare it honestly against the SAR bands before deciding.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper non-specialist ever the right choice for IGCSE Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, in one specific case. If the fault is arithmetic and manipulation fluency, the work is volume: sets of questions, done to time, marked, with the errors fed back. A capable graduate who will set and mark that reliably is good value, and a specialist's higher rate buys nothing extra for that particular job. If the fault is Extended-tier topics, exam technique on the longer questions, or a tier decision, a non-specialist will not see what is wrong and the cheaper hours cost more in the end.

faqs.question: How do I confirm a tutor teaches the exact IGCSE syllabus code my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask for the code and the board, then check it against the front page of your child's past papers, which prints it. A specialist gives the number without looking it up and then asks which components your child is entered for, because that changes how they plan. Somebody who answers in general terms about IGCSE chemistry or IGCSE maths, with no code and no board, does not teach it regularly enough for the distinction to matter to them, and it matters a great deal to the grade.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE tutor need to have marked for the board, or is teaching it enough?
faqs.answer: Teaching it is enough for most of the work; marking experience shows up at the margins and the margins are often the grade. Somebody who has marked a batch of scripts against a published scheme knows what a borderline answer gets, how method marks are allocated when the final answer is wrong, and which error recurs across hundreds of candidates. You can hear the difference without verifying a certificate: ask what the scheme does with a correct answer that shows no working, and listen for a specific answer rather than a general one.

faqs.question: What should a trial lesson for an IGCSE subject produce before I commit to a package?
faqs.answer: Three things, in writing. A statement of where the student currently stands, based on their own marked work rather than on a conversation. The recurring fault named specifically enough that you could repeat it to someone else. And one first target with a rough timescale. If the trial produces enthusiasm and a recommendation to start weekly lessons, you have learned nothing you can hold anyone to. Ask for the written version; a specialist can produce it in a few minutes because they already know the answer.

igcse-home-tuition.closingHeading: What to do before you buy a single hour
igcse-home-tuition.closingBody: Send three things: the subject with its syllabus or specification code, the tier your child is entered for, and the most recent marked script. A subject specialist will read it with your child in a free diagnostic session over live video, at an hour that fits the Sunday-to-Thursday week, and tell you in writing whether the fault is content, technique or the entry itself — and roughly what fixing it involves. If the answer is that tuition is not the right purchase, you will get that answer too, which is cheaper for you and more useful than a package sold on a hunch.

igcse-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE subjects to students across the Kingdom. Each is matched to one specification rather than to a subject in general, because the same subject name carries different papers, different tiering and different mark schemes depending on which board a school enters its candidates under.

intro.heading: The marks go first, and they go in four predictable places
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is not a measure of how much a student knows. It is a measure of how many marks an examiner could award for what the student wrote, in the time available, against a published mark scheme. Those are different things, and the gap between them is where almost every disappointing grade in this qualification is manufactured. A family that understands the gap can close it; a family that treats a poor grade as a knowledge problem will buy more content teaching and watch the grade stay where it was.

Four failures account for most of the loss, and they repeat across every subject. The first is the command word: a student reads describe where the paper said explain, or gives a definition where the paper asked for a distinction, and writes a competent answer to a question nobody set. The second is invisible method, where the final answer is right, the working is in the student's head, and the method marks go unawarded. The third is length mismatch, with two lines offered for six marks or a page spent on two. The fourth is timing, where the last extended-response question meets a student with eight minutes left.

Notice what is absent from that list. Content gaps cause some lost marks, and they are the easiest thing to diagnose and to teach. The four failures above are harder, because they are invisible to the student and nearly invisible to a parent reading a report. They surface only in a marked script, which is why the single most useful thing you can send a prospective tutor is a mock paper with the examiner's marks still on it.

That diagnosis also decides who the tutor should be, which is the question this page is really about. Fixing a content gap needs somebody who knows the subject. Fixing the other four needs somebody who knows the specification: which command terms this board favours, what the mark scheme pays for in a six-mark answer, how the tier affects the question style, and what the examiner is instructed to ignore. Those are not the same qualification, and the second one is harder to find and harder to verify.

On delivery, the plain version: IB Gram does not run home visits in Saudi Arabia, and in-home teaching is a service we offer only in India. Lessons for families here are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Arabia Standard Time around the Sunday-to-Thursday school week. The reason that is an improvement rather than a compromise is set out in the first table below, and it comes down to the size of the pool a family is choosing from.

What follows works through each of the four failures, then turns to the tutor: what qualification actually matters for IGCSE, how to test a claim in a trial lesson, what the in-home market charges and what the travel inside that price is buying.

igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Families in the Kingdom reach IGCSE by more than one route, and leave it by more than one. These are the four programmes that matter either side of the qualification, with a note on how each behaves specifically for a family here rather than in the United Kingdom.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years per subject, examined externally, with most subjects available at Core and Extended tier. Each subject carries its own syllabus code and its own combination of papers, and the code is what identifies the specification your child is actually entered for. Grading runs from 9 to 1 or A* to G depending on the subject's reporting scale, and schools in the same city may enter candidates for different codes in the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: Candidates in the Kingdom sit the June and the November series. Cambridge's February and March series runs in India only, which matters because rival pages written for an Indian audience and lightly edited for Saudi readers get this wrong, and a family that plans an entry deadline around it plans around nothing. Confirm the code and the series with your school's examinations officer rather than with a search result.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same age band and a similar purpose, with a different specification structure. Paper combinations differ, some subjects are untiered where the Cambridge equivalent is tiered, and the mark schemes reward slightly different things in extended writing. A student who moves between a Cambridge school and an Edexcel school mid-course has not changed subject, but has changed specification, and the difference is concentrated in assessment style rather than in content.
programmes.countryNote: British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom choose their board per subject, so a single student can sit Cambridge sciences and Edexcel mathematics in the same series. Tutoring matched on the subject name alone misses this completely. Ask the school for the board and code for each subject; it takes one email and it changes which past papers are worth working through.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's alternative at the same age, assessed against four lettered criteria per subject rather than by external papers, and finishing with the Personal Project. It builds different habits: criterion-referenced writing and extended inquiry rather than timed examination technique. Students moving from the Middle Years Programme into an IGCSE year, or sitting both in the same school, feel the change in assessment style before they feel it in content.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Kingdom run the Middle Years Programme and then the Diploma without IGCSE in between, which is a legitimate route and not a gap. Families comparing the two at enrolment should ask what the school's leaving cohort actually did next, since that tells you more about the school's strength in a programme than the programme's own description does.

programmes.name: What IGCSE leads into
programmes.description: IGCSE grades set the entry conditions for the IB Diploma or for A Levels, and in practice they set the ceiling on Higher Level choices. A school will not normally allow Higher Level Physics on the back of a weak IGCSE Physics grade, and a Mathematics grade below the school's threshold closes Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. These decisions happen quickly after results and leave little room to argue.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom this compounds, because the school a family can reach may run only one of the two post-16 routes. A student whose IGCSE grades close Higher Level options at their own school and whose alternative is in another city is in a logistical problem rather than an academic one. Which is an argument for taking the IGCSE year seriously a year earlier than most families do.

igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects families in the Kingdom ask for most, with notes on where the marks are actually lost rather than on what the syllabus contains. Paper structure and tiering differ between Cambridge and Edexcel, so confirm your child's board and code before buying past papers.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Method marks dominate, and students who calculate mentally give them away by the handful. The recurring Extended-tier losses are in bounds and accuracy, surds and indices, and transformations described in words rather than notation. Graph questions want the asymptote and the intercept labelled, not drawn and left unnamed. A student who writes every line down scores above a quicker student who does not.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken alongside Mathematics by stronger candidates and treated as more of the same, which it is not. It assumes algebraic fluency as a starting point and spends its marks on calculus, trigonometric identities and series. Students arriving from a comfortable Extended-tier Mathematics course underestimate the step and discover it in the first mock. It is also the best preparation available for a Higher Level mathematics course afterwards.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Unit conversion and significant figures cost marks silently across every paper. Explanation questions are the real divider: a student who writes what happened earns the description mark and misses the explanation one. Graph gradients get read off the wrong scale. The practical component wants a named independent variable, a stated control and a sensible range, and most answers give only the first of the three.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations and ionic equations are the obvious pressure points. The less obvious one is the qualitative analysis section, which rewards a student who has learned the tables as patterns and punishes one who learned them as a list. Observations and inferences are separate marks, so a single sentence doing both work earns one. Balanced equations with the state symbols missing lose a mark that was already won.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The syllabus is long and the definitions are marked strictly, so a near-miss definition earns nothing at all. The commonest single error is an extended-response answer written at two lines when six marks were available. Experimental questions need a measurable variable and a control. Students who revise by rereading notes consistently underperform students who revise by answering past questions against the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into fewer papers, which changes revision strategy rather than difficulty. Topics appear in less depth but the command terms are identical, so the technique matters more, not less. Students entered for this route sometimes assume it closes post-16 science options; the school's own entry requirements decide that, so ask before accepting it as a limit.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Directed-writing tasks are marked on form and audience before accuracy, so a well-written piece in the wrong register loses the marks that were easiest to win. Reading questions want selection and inference, not retelling. The summary task scores points identified rather than prose quality. Timing is where strong candidates lose most: the final extended response meets them exhausted.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Marked on accuracy and on range together, which means playing safe caps the grade. The listening component rewards a precise detail rather than a general understanding, so note-taking technique is worth teaching directly. In speaking, one-sentence answers lose development marks that a slightly longer answer would have earned without any extra vocabulary.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Quotation without analysis is the dominant failure. Marks are awarded for what the writer's choice does to the reader, and a student who narrates the plot of a set text writes a summary that cannot be credited. Unseen poetry questions reward a confident wrong reading over a cautious non-reading. The timing problem is real: three questions on three texts does not forgive an over-long opening.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: The case study is the examination, not background. Marks come from using the printed figures, the stated objectives and the named stakeholders, and generic theory answers sit in the lower bands regardless of accuracy. Evaluation questions need a judgement defended against a rejected alternative. Students who write everything they know about motivation theory score less than students who apply one idea to the business in front of them.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: A labelled diagram, a definition and an applied example carry most of the structured-question marks, and the diagram is where the labels get dropped. Extended answers need a conclusion that chooses a side rather than surveying both. Students who have seen the IB version of this course tend to over-write; the IGCSE mark schemes reward compression and penalise nothing for it.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode on paper is a separate skill from coding on a machine, and students who have only done the second lose marks on the first. Trace tables are worth practising until they are mechanical. The theory papers reward exact terminology, so an answer that describes what a component does without naming it earns less than a shorter precise one.

igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: The in-home tutor pool in the Kingdom is not evenly distributed, and that distribution is the honest argument for teaching over live video. These are the places families write in from, with a note on what a local search realistically returns in each.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest local pool in the Kingdom, and still thin once a request is specific. The city is roughly an hour across in traffic, so an in-home tutor's catchment is a handful of districts rather than the city, and a family in the north and a family in the south are drawing on different short lists.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, which means travel time rather than distance decides who is available. Families here have real school choice and still find scarce subjects unstaffed, because the scarcity is in the specialist supply rather than in the number of schools.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market behaving as a single conurbation, with families routinely living in one city and attending school in another. The local pool is larger than the population alone suggests, because the corporate and campus communities bring teaching experience with them. It remains unreliable for a specific specification.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities where the school population tracks the workforce and the subject range is set by staffing rather than demand. An in-home search returns very little that is syllabus-specific, and mid-course arrivals and departures are routine, so continuity matters more here than price.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: About an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, which puts a commuting tutor out of practical reach for a weekday evening. Families here typically either travel to the coast for schooling or arrange subject teaching separately, and the second is the only one that scales to several subjects.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Established cities with their own school markets, where the calendar also bends around Hajj and Umrah seasons in ways a tutor based elsewhere needs to be told about rather than left to discover. Specialist supply in the scarcer IGCSE subjects is limited, as it is in most cities outside the three largest markets.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Roughly twenty-five kilometres apart in 'Asir at altitude, sharing a catchment and a small international-school provision. This is where the distance argument stops being theoretical: a family wanting an Edexcel Chemistry specialist is not going to find one within driving distance, at any price.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: The north-west, where school provision is catching up with an arriving workforce. Families posted here ask about local tutors first and accept the online answer quickly, because the local answer is usually that there is nobody. Connectivity, not supply, is the constraint worth checking in advance.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: Students we support attend schools including these, several of which run Cambridge programmes alongside or instead of the IB. Term dates differ between them even inside the same city, so a mock timetable from one school tells a family nothing about another.

schoolClusters.city: Dhahran, Dammam, Al Khobar and Jubail
schoolClusters.note: The Eastern Province cluster, where British and Cambridge curricula sit alongside American and IB provision. The International Schools Group operates several campuses here and not all of them run the same programmes, which is worth checking per campus rather than per group.

The widest programme choice in the Kingdom, with schools running the IB continuum, Cambridge and American curricula. Ask any school which subjects it entered candidates for in the last series, and under which board, rather than reading the subject list in the prospectus.

modes.description: A fixed slot on one subject with one tutor, running alongside school through Year 10 and Year 11. The agenda follows the school's scheme of work where it is known, and the tutor builds a picture of the student's specific error pattern over weeks, which no single session can do. This is the right mode when the gap is content or when a subject is being taught by a non-specialist.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE home tutor search in the Kingdom actually returns
paragraphs: The query is a reasonable one and deserves a straight answer rather than a redirect. An in-home IGCSE tutor in a Saudi city is an adult who lives close enough to reach your district on a weekday evening and who has taught the subject. That last clause is where the search narrows. The pool is set by geography first, by subject second and by specification third, and each filter removes most of what the one before it left. A family in Riyadh asking for somebody who has taught Edexcel Chemistry specifically, and marked a component of it, is choosing from a list measured in individuals.

Travel is the second thing the market does not advertise. An in-home arrangement pays for the drive, either as an explicit surcharge or inside an hourly rate that absorbs it, and in a city that is an hour across the loading is substantial. A nominal hour frequently means fifty minutes of teaching bracketed by a tutor who arrived late from the previous student and needs to leave early for the next. Over a term that is a real amount of money and time spent on roads.

The third thing is fragility. A single tutor covering several districts has one car, one evening and one schedule, and a changed school timetable, a family relocation or a traffic pattern breaks the arrangement. Families on compounds and in planned industrial districts add an access question on top. None of this makes in-home teaching bad; it makes it expensive and narrow, which is a different objection.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address, and in-home visits are a service we offer only in India. What we do instead is match on the specification and teach one-to-one over live video, which removes geography from the filter list entirely and leaves subject, specification and hour. The table sets the two formats against each other on the terms that actually differ.

sections.heading: Failure one: the command word nobody read
paragraphs: Open any marked IGCSE script and the first pattern visible is answers to questions that were not asked. A paper says state and receives a paragraph. It says explain and receives a description. It says compare and receives two separate accounts with no comparison in them. The content is often correct. The mark scheme has nothing to award it against, because the mark scheme is written against the command word and the examiner is instructed to follow it.

Students do this because command words look like politeness rather than instruction. In normal English, describe and explain are near-synonyms. In a mark scheme they are different tasks with different structures: describe wants observable detail, explain wants a causal chain, and a student who does not know that reads the question as a prompt for everything they know about the topic. Writing more is the natural response to uncertainty, and it earns nothing while costing the time that the next question needed.

It is also the cheapest failure to fix, which is why it is worth naming first. The remedy is mechanical: take twenty past-paper questions in the subject, sort them by command word, and answer them in sets. After six explain questions in a row a student starts producing causal chains without being asked to. This is drilling rather than teaching, it takes two or three sessions, and it moves marks across every topic in the subject at once rather than one topic at a time.

The tutor's job here is to know which command words this board actually uses and how its mark schemes treat each one. That is specification knowledge, not subject knowledge, and it is exactly the thing a locally available graduate in the subject is least likely to have. It is also the first thing worth asking about in a trial lesson, because the answer is immediately checkable against a published past paper.
bullets: State and give want a short answer and nothing more; extra prose cannot gain
Describe wants observable detail; explain wants the because
Compare and contrast want a connective in every sentence
Calculate wants the working; find sometimes does not
Suggest invites a reasoned answer that is not in the textbook

sections.heading: Failure two: working that never reached the page
paragraphs: Method marks exist because an examiner is paying for a demonstrated process, not for a number. A student who does three steps mentally and writes the answer has shown an examiner nothing to credit, and when the answer is wrong by an arithmetic slip the entire question scores zero where it could have scored most of its marks. Strong mathematicians are the worst offenders, because mental arithmetic is the skill they are proud of and it is the one actively punished by this format.

The same failure wears different clothes in the sciences. A calculation with no substitution line shown, a rearranged equation that appears already rearranged, a unit conversion performed invisibly between two lines. In each case the student knows what they did and the examiner cannot see it. In physics particularly, where answers are expected in a specific unit and to a specific precision, the invisible conversion is where an otherwise correct answer quietly becomes a wrong one.

Fixing it is a habit problem rather than an understanding problem, and habits change slowly, which is why this one needs weeks rather than sessions. The practical approach is to mark the student's own work with them, against the real mark scheme, and show them the marks they could have had. A student who sees three marks available on a question they answered correctly and scored one on does not need persuading twice.

This is also where online teaching has a concrete advantage worth stating plainly. The tutor watches the student write on a shared whiteboard, at full size, in real time, with nothing obscured. A tutor sitting beside a student at a kitchen table sees the page at an angle and over a shoulder. For a failure mode that is entirely about what does and does not appear on the page, that difference is not cosmetic.

sections.heading: Failure three: tiering, and the ceiling a family agrees to without noticing
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects are offered at Core and Extended tier, and the tier decides which papers a candidate sits and therefore which grades are reachable. Core tier caps the available grade range. That is not a secret, but it is frequently a decision made by a school on the basis of a Year 10 mock, communicated to parents in a sentence, and not revisited. A family that did not understand it was a decision discovers the ceiling when results arrive.

The tier question is genuinely two-sided and deserves an honest treatment. Entering a struggling student for Extended tier so they can reach a higher grade, and watching them meet questions pitched beyond them across every paper, produces a worse outcome than a secure Core-tier grade. The right answer depends on where the student actually is, how much time remains, and what the post-16 route requires of that specific subject. It is a conversation to have in Year 10, with evidence, not a formality.

What a family needs in order to have that conversation is a realistic view of current attainment against the Extended-tier paper rather than against the school's internal test. Those are different measurements. A tutor can supply it by giving a past Extended paper under time and marking it against the published scheme, which produces a number the school can discuss rather than an impression. The table sets out what the tier decision actually governs.

One further point specific to the Kingdom: a student who may move schools mid-course, which is common in corporate and industrial postings, has an extra reason to look closely at tier. Boards and tiers do not always travel, and a transfer can land a student in a school entering candidates differently. Asking the question before the move is far cheaper than discovering it after.

sections.heading: Who the tutor needs to be for IGCSE specifically
paragraphs: The qualification that matters here is narrower than most families assume, and narrower than most tutor profiles advertise. A degree in the subject demonstrates that somebody once studied it at a higher level than they will be teaching. It says nothing about whether they know how this board awards marks. For a sixteen-year-old sitting a specific paper under a specific mark scheme, the second is worth more, and the first is close to assumed.

In order of what actually predicts a useful tutor for this qualification: experience teaching this specification repeatedly, through several series; experience marking a component of it, or of something closely comparable; the ability to discuss the mark scheme fluently without looking at it; and then subject depth. That order will look wrong to anybody who has hired on credentials before. It is the order that matches what an IGCSE grade is actually produced by.

There is a second axis, which is whether the tutor is a current classroom teacher or a full-time tutor. Both work and the trade-off is real. A serving teacher knows how schools behave: internal deadlines, mock timings, how a department sets coursework. A full-time tutor usually has more range across boards and more availability inside a Sunday-to-Thursday evening. For a student whose problem is school-shaped, the first is better. For a student whose problem is the paper, the second often is.

Subject scarcity interacts with all of this, and it is the main reason an honest platform sometimes says no. A tutor who has taught and marked Edexcel Chemistry is scarcer than one who has taught Cambridge Mathematics, and the scarce ones fill their Arabia Standard Time evenings first. We would rather tell a family that the match they want is not free at seven in the evening than put a generalist in the slot and let the family work out the difference in March.

sections.heading: How to check the claim, in one trial lesson
paragraphs: A trial lesson is the only verification tool a family has that cannot be gamed in advance, and most families waste it by watching rather than testing. Treat it as a diagnostic in both directions: the tutor is diagnosing your child, and you are diagnosing the tutor. Four questions, asked plainly, separate specification knowledge from subject knowledge, and the answers are checkable afterwards against a published past paper and mark scheme.

Ask which board and which papers they have taught, and over how many series. Ask what the mark scheme awards in a named six-mark question that this board uses, and compare the answer with the real scheme. Ask what the most common way is for a competent student to lose marks on this specific paper. Then ask them to look at your child's marked script and say what the error pattern is. A tutor with the right experience will answer all four in detail and will volunteer the fourth before being asked.

What a weak answer sounds like is also worth knowing. Generalities about building confidence, a pitch about a method or a system, a claim about results with no component or series attached, or any reference to a guaranteed grade. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and the ones who say otherwise are describing their sales process rather than their teaching. Treat a results claim with no number of students, no date and no method behind it as what it is: a sentence written to sound like evidence.

The second half of the trial is your child's view, and it carries more weight than most parents give it. Ask whether they understood the explanation, whether they were doing the work or watching it, and whether they would want another session. A tutor who did all the talking has told you something about the next thirty weeks. A tutor who had your child writing within five minutes has told you something better.

sections.heading: What the in-home market charges, and what the travel is buying
paragraphs: Published rates in the Kingdom are patchy because most providers hide them behind a form. The figures below are rates advertised by other providers and platforms, with the type of source beside each, collected as market context. They are not an average, since a set of marketing pages is not a sample, and none of them is IB Gram's price. Read them as the range you will meet while shopping, and weigh each one against who published it.

What moves a quote, in rough order of weight: how scarce the subject and specification are; whether the tutor has marked for the board; the level, with Higher Level above Standard Level above the Middle Years Programme above IGCSE; whether the tutor travels; and how long the package is. A rate quoted without a named subject, board and level is not a rate. It is an opening position, and the second question is always which specification that number covers.

The travel component deserves its own arithmetic because families rarely do it. If an in-home tutor's nominal hour delivers fifty minutes of teaching, every six sessions have quietly lost an hour. Add any explicit travel surcharge and the effective cost per taught hour rises above the headline figure, in a way that gets worse the further apart the districts are. This is not an argument that in-home tutors overcharge. It is an argument that the headline rate is not the number to compare.

The useful comparison is cost per taught hour against match precision. A cheaper non-specialist is sometimes the right call, for instance for a student who needs company and structure to do the work they already know how to do. For a student losing marks on command terms in a specific Edexcel paper, the cheaper tutor is not cheaper, because the thing being bought is not the thing that is needed. Price the specific purchase, not the hour.
