sections.heading: Coursework, academic honesty and what a tutor may read
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry internally assessed components, and the rules around them are not negotiable. A tutor may teach the skills the task needs, explain the assessment criteria, discuss an approach, and read what the student has written and say where it falls short. No tutor may write the coursework, supply text for it, or redraft a student's paragraph into better prose. There is no framing under which that becomes acceptable, and a school's examinations officer will recognise it when it arrives.

The practical test is whether the words on the page were produced by the student. Showing a student what a criterion asks for, and letting them find the gap in their own paragraph, is teaching. Handing back a tidier version of the same paragraph is substitution. We give written feedback on the student's own work, the student revises, and the record of their drafts stays with them. Some providers competing for this exact search are plainly selling the other thing.

Schools have their own supervision structures and their own limits on formal draft review, and an outside tutor works inside those rather than around them. Tell the school that subject support is in place. There is nothing to conceal, and a teacher who knows will often share the internal deadlines, which makes the tutoring more useful rather than less. A family that hides it loses that coordination for no benefit.

Plagiarism detection is worth understanding accurately. It finds matched text well and originality of thought not at all, so a student can pass a similarity check with work that is not meaningfully theirs, and can fail one for a correctly quoted source. Neither outcome is a verdict. What protects a student is an honest trail: notes, drafts in order, and their own record of where ideas came from.

sections.heading: After IGCSE: equivalency, the Qiyas tests and the two routes out
paragraphs: An IGCSE is a stepping stone rather than a destination, and the two routes out of it look different enough that a family should know which one they are walking towards. Inside the Kingdom, a foreign or international school certificate requires an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies at the leaving-certificate stage rather than at IGCSE, but the subject choices that lead there are made now.

Saudi universities also read the national testing system. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is administered by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, Qiyas, and tests verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught content. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Each university publishes its own criteria combining school results with those scores, and the weighting differs by university and by programme.

The thing worth knowing while a student is still at IGCSE is that the Achievement Test follows the Saudi national curriculum. An international-curriculum student has met most of the underlying material in a different order, with different notation and a different examination style, so the overlap is real and misleading at the same time. Preparation for it is a separate undertaking from revising school subjects, and families who learn that early build time for it instead of improvising in a final year. We publish no threshold for either test, because they differ by university, programme and intake, and the university's own published criteria is the only source worth planning around.

The overseas route reads IGCSE grades mostly as entry conditions for what follows, and then reads the post-16 qualification. What carries forward from IGCSE in both directions is the same short list: the mathematics grade, the science grades, and English. Those three decide which Higher Level and A Level doors stay open, which is why a Year 10 tier decision in mathematics is a university decision wearing a disguise.

process.title: Send the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Not Chemistry, but Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry at Extended tier under the code your school entered your child for. One email to the examinations officer produces all three. With them we can shortlist tutors by specification and point at the right past papers from the first session rather than the fourth.

process.title: Send a marked script
process.description: A mock paper with the examiner's marks still on it is worth more than any description of the problem. It shows which of the four failure modes is actually costing marks, and whether the content is in place. Families who skip this step usually buy content teaching for a technique problem, which is the single most common waste in this market.

process.title: Use the trial to test the tutor
process.description: Ask the four questions, listen for specification fluency rather than reassurance, and watch whether your child is writing or watching. The trial produces an opinion on what the first four weeks should do. If the honest answer is a short technique block rather than a term of weekly lessons, that is what you will be told.

process.title: Fix the hour, then the tutor
process.description: Agree the slot in Arabia Standard Time against your household's Sunday-to-Thursday week, then match inside the pool genuinely working at that hour. Doing it the other way round produces a tutor who suits on paper and cannot hold the time, which becomes a change of tutor two months in and a repeated diagnostic.

process.title: Review after four sessions
process.description: Four lessons is enough evidence to judge. We look at whether the same errors are still appearing in the written feedback, what the school has noticed, and whether the student is doing the work between sessions. Either side can stop or change tutor then, and continuing should be a decision rather than a default.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the specification, not the subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Edexcel versions of the same subject differ in papers, tiering and mark schemes, and a tutor matched on the subject name alone may be working from the wrong past papers for a year. We match on board, code, tier and paper, which is the level of precision an IGCSE grade is actually produced at.

whyPoints.title: Tutors asked what they have marked
whyPoints.description: Marking experience shows up as fluency about how marks are awarded, and that is what we ask tutors to demonstrate: which board, which components, how many series. A family can test the same thing in the trial lesson and check the answer against a published mark scheme afterwards.

whyPoints.title: Technique taught as its own subject
whyPoints.description: Command words, visible method, answer length and timing account for more lost marks than content gaps do, and none of them improve by covering the syllabus again. They are drilled directly, against real mark schemes, with the student's own scripts as the evidence of whether it is working.

whyPoints.title: Honest about tier and about ceilings
whyPoints.description: A timed Extended-tier past paper marked against the published scheme gives a family a number to discuss with the school instead of an impression. Sometimes that evidence supports a secure Core-tier grade, and we will say so. A platform that only ever recommends aiming higher is not advising anybody.

whyPoints.title: Nothing written for the student
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the criteria, reads what the student wrote and says where it misses. No internally assessed work is written, part-written or redrafted on a student's behalf, in any subject, at any level. The student's draft trail stays theirs, and we would rather lose the enquiry than hold a different line on this.

whyPoints.title: No promised grades, ever
whyPoints.description: No grade, score, university place or admission decision is promised here, because nobody honest is in a position to promise them. What is offered is a named specialist, a fixed slot in Arabia Standard Time, written feedback after every session, and a review point where either side can stop.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE grades themselves need Ministry of Education equivalency, or only the final school certificate?
faqs.answer: The equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, applies to the secondary leaving certificate a student presents to a Saudi university, rather than to an intermediate qualification taken at sixteen. IGCSE matters to that process indirectly: it sets the entry conditions for the post-16 qualification that will eventually be submitted. Families should treat IGCSE as the stage where subject doors open or close and treat equivalency as a step that arrives with the leaving certificate. The Ministry's own published guidance is the authority on which documents are required and in what form, and a school registrar will have handled the process before.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects give an international-curriculum student the best grounding for the Achievement Test later?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, because those are the science-stream subjects the Achievement Test covers. A student who takes separate sciences rather than a combined route meets more of the underlying material in more depth, which helps. The caution is that the test follows the Saudi national curriculum, so the content overlaps while the framing, notation and emphasis differ. Taking the right IGCSE subjects reduces the work later without removing it: the test still needs its own preparation window, treated as a separate undertaking rather than as revision of school material already covered.

faqs.question: Does a student who sat Edexcel rather than Cambridge IGCSEs face a different equivalency route?
faqs.answer: Both are foreign qualifications presented to the Ministry of Education, so the mechanism is the same and the board is not the distinguishing factor. What differs between the two is what sits in the file: paper combinations, the grading scale reported, and in some subjects whether tiering applied. Schools and the Ministry handle both routinely. The practical advice is to keep complete documentation for whichever board was used, including statements of results for every series sat, because a resit taken in a November series creates a second document that has to travel with the first.

faqs.question: What do overseas universities actually read from a Saudi student's IGCSE results?
faqs.answer: Mostly they read them as evidence that the post-16 qualification is credible, and they read three specific grades closely: mathematics, the sciences relevant to the degree, and English. English grades sometimes carry extra weight because they can substitute for a separate language requirement at some institutions, though each university sets its own rules on that. Beyond those, IGCSE grades fade once a Diploma or A Level result exists. The exception is an application made before final results, where predicted grades are read alongside the IGCSE profile as the only completed evidence available.

faqs.question: When should a family in the Kingdom start IGCSE support, in Year 10 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10, if the aim is a higher grade rather than a rescue. Two things are decided in Year 10 that cannot be undone later: the tier a student is entered for, and whether the habits that produce method marks are in place. Both take months rather than weeks. Starting in Year 11 is perfectly workable for technique and for specific content gaps, and in the term before a series a focused block of past-paper work is often the highest-value purchase available. What Year 11 cannot recover is a tier decision already made on weak evidence.

faqs.question: What should a Middle Years Programme student be building before an IGCSE year, if their school runs both?
faqs.answer: Timed writing and visible method, because those are exactly what criterion-referenced assessment does not force. Middle Years Programme work rewards extended inquiry and reflection, which builds genuine strengths that an IGCSE paper will not ask for. The transition hurts most in two places: writing a complete answer in the minutes available, and showing every step of a calculation when the student is used to presenting a finished process. Four to six weeks of timed past-paper practice in the term before the IGCSE course begins closes most of that gap before it becomes a pattern.

faqs.question: Is it realistic to start IGCSE help in the final term before the June series?
faqs.answer: For technique, yes, and it is often the best value purchase in the whole qualification. Command-word drilling, timing practice and visible-method habits move marks across every topic at once, and a focused block of past papers against real mark schemes can shift a grade boundary. For missing content it depends on how much is missing: two topics is recoverable, half a syllabus is not, and a tutor who tells you otherwise is selling. The honest sequence is a diagnostic from a marked script first, then a decision about what the remaining weeks can actually achieve.

faqs.question: How does support change between the IGCSE years and the first year of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: The unit of work changes. IGCSE support is paper-shaped: specific papers, specific command words, specific mark schemes, and a syllabus with a visible end. First-year Diploma support is course-shaped, because the assessment is two years away and the immediate work is building the habits and the internal assessment that will be assessed later. A student who had weekly IGCSE technique lessons often needs fewer, longer sessions in the first Diploma year, focused on written work and on the Higher Level extension topics their school covers last.

faqs.question: What should a student do in the break between finishing IGCSEs and starting a post-16 course?
faqs.answer: Very little, deliberately, with one exception. The exception is mathematics, where the step up to a Higher Level or A Level course is the one that catches most students, and a few hours of algebraic fluency work prevents a term of struggling. Beyond that, reading in the subjects chosen for Higher Level is worth more than pre-teaching content, because the courses will teach their own content in their own order. Families who fill the whole break with tutoring produce a student who starts the hardest two years of school already tired.

faqs.question: What does an hour of IGCSE tutoring cost in the Kingdom, and why is the range so wide?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates in this market run from about SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms up to SAR 200 and above for senior examination subjects, according to platform marketing pages and tutor-marketplace guides. The range is wide because the word tutor covers both a generalist following a textbook and somebody who has marked the component your child is sitting. Those are different purchases. Scarcity of the subject and specification, marking experience, level and whether the tutor travels account for most of the spread. None of those figures is our price, and a rate quoted without a named board and code is an opening position.

faqs.question: Is a group IGCSE class ever better value than one-to-one for a technique problem?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and for a specific reason. A technique problem is individual: this student misreads command words, that one writes six-mark answers in two lines, a third runs out of time. A group class has to pick one error to address and does so at the pace of the middle of the room. Where group teaching does earn its place is content coverage, where everyone genuinely needs the same thing in the same order. If the diagnosis is technique, one-to-one is not a luxury, because the thing being bought is attention to a pattern only this student has.

faqs.question: What happens to prepaid IGCSE sessions if my child's school moves the mock timetable?
faqs.answer: Sessions move with the school rather than being lost. A mock timetable shifting is one of the commonest disruptions in this qualification and the planning assumes it: unused sessions stay available, and the sequence of work is re-ordered so that technique drilling lands before the mock rather than after it. What matters practically is notice. A week lets us re-plan the content; a day lets us only move the slot. Tell us as soon as the school tells you, including for school trips and internal examination weeks, which collide with evening slots more often than families expect.

faqs.question: Why would two tutors quote differently for the same IGCSE subject at the same tier?
faqs.answer: Because the subject name is not the product. A tutor who has taught that exact code through several series and marked one of its components is scarcer than a tutor who studied the subject at university, and scarcity sets price in this market more than anything else. Beyond that, the cheaper quote sometimes covers a shorter session, excludes marking written work between lessons, or assumes group delivery. Ask both what is included: session length, marking between sessions, written feedback to the parent, and whether past papers and mark schemes are supplied.

faqs.question: Is the free trial lesson a real diagnostic or a sales call, and how do I tell?
faqs.answer: You tell by what comes out of it. A diagnostic produces a specific opinion: the error pattern visible in the marked script, what the first four weeks should do, and sometimes the recommendation to buy less than you were about to. A sales call produces reassurance and a package. Judge it on three things: did the tutor read the marked work in advance, did your child spend most of the session writing rather than listening, and was anything said that reduced the amount you were planning to spend? A trial that never disagrees with the parent is not an assessment.

faqs.question: Can lessons be paused during a long school holiday without giving up the weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families that is the right move rather than a concession. A student who works through every break arrives at the series tired, and the marginal value of August teaching is low compared with the same hours in the term before the papers. A slot can be held through a planned break with notice, and the tutor picks up the sequence afterwards rather than restarting. The judgement changes for a student with real content gaps, where a short holiday block on two specific topics is better use of the time than general revision.

igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Send the code, the tier and one marked paper
igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: An IGCSE grade is produced by marks on a page, and marks on a page respond to things that are teachable: the command word, visible method, answer length and timing. Tell us the board, the syllabus code and the tier your child is entered for, and send one recently marked script. A free trial lesson follows, and it exists to produce a diagnosis rather than a signature; if the honest answer is a short technique block instead of a year of weekly lessons, you will be told that. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Arabia Standard Time, inside your Sunday-to-Thursday week. IB Gram does not run home visits in the Kingdom, no internally assessed work is ever written for a student, and no grade is ever promised.

intro.heading: Start with the component list, then talk about money
paragraphs: An IGCSE subject is not one thing a family buys teaching for. It is a set of components, each assessed separately and each demanding something different from whoever teaches it. Cambridge IGCSE sciences are examined through a multiple-choice paper, a longer theory paper and either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, and those ask for different teaching. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects are examined through written papers only on most specifications. A tutor who is strong on theory and has never prepared a candidate for an alternative-to-practical paper is not expensive or cheap; they are partial. IGCSE home tutor fees in Saudi Arabia only become comparable once you know which components a quote actually covers.

The second thing that decides value is the calendar your family lives in. Schools in the Kingdom run Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. That leaves five school evenings, and a Year 11 candidate with two weak subjects is competing for the same two or three usable hours a week as every other family in the same city. A tutor whose own working week runs Monday to Friday will offer you Sunday and Thursday last, because those are their weekend edges. The fee you are quoted is partly a bid for a slot that fits both calendars, and slot scarcity moves the number as surely as subject scarcity does.

A parent searching for an IGCSE home tutor usually wants one of two things: somebody who will sit beside the student, or somebody who genuinely knows the paper. In Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam cluster the first is possible and expensive, because travel time is loaded into the rate. Outside those cities it is often not possible at all at IGCSE level, where the pool of specialists for Accounting or Computer Science is thin. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service offered only in India. What we match a family to is one-to-one teaching over live video, pinned to Arabia Standard Time.

This page is organised the way a fee conversation should run. It starts with the component structure, because that is what a tutor is being paid to cover. It then sets out what providers in the Kingdom advertise, with the source type attached to every band, so you can tell a platform listing from a specialist agency quote. After that it deals with the two things that quietly waste money: a slot that collides with the school week, and an hour spent on content when the marks are being lost on technique. The last section covers what a fee can never buy, which is any part of an assessed component itself. Nothing here is a price list for IB Gram.

sections.heading: What a component list does to an hourly fee
paragraphs: Every quote should be read against a component list. A Cambridge IGCSE science candidate is sitting a multiple-choice paper, a longer theory paper and either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, and those three ask for different teaching. The multiple-choice paper rewards coverage and speed. The theory paper rewards command-term discipline. The practical alternative rewards an understanding of apparatus, variables and sources of error that cannot be taught from a textbook in a hurry. A tutor who has only ever taught the theory paper will quote the same hourly figure and deliver two thirds of the course.

Pearson Edexcel builds the practical skills into the written papers instead, which changes the economics. There is no separate session to rehearse, so an Edexcel physics or chemistry candidate needs fewer specialist hours than a Cambridge one sitting a practical examination. That is a real reason two families in the same city pay different totals for what looks like the same subject. It is also why a quote that names only the subject is not a quote at all.

Coursework-bearing components move the number the other way. Where a Cambridge subject still offers a coursework route, the school sets and marks it and the board moderates the sample. A tutor's role there is narrow and the hours are few, but the hours are skilled: reading a draft against published criteria and saying what is missing is harder than teaching content. Expect a specialist to charge their normal rate for that work and to decline anything beyond feedback.

sections.heading: Tier entry caps the grade before a fee is paid
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers many of its IGCSE subjects. Core is graded C to G and Extended is graded A* to E, which means a student entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C however well the paper goes. Pearson Edexcel grades 9 to 1, with Mathematics A tiered Foundation and Higher and most other subjects untiered. These are published board facts, not opinions, and they decide the ceiling a family is paying a tutor to reach for. Ask your school to confirm the tier and the full component list in writing; a verbal answer in a corridor is not a record.

Tier entry is a school decision. It is made from classwork, mock performance and the department's own view of risk, and it is reversible only before the entry deadline your examinations officer works to. A family that discovers in the spring term that their child was entered for Core has usually discovered it too late. The useful hour to buy is the one before the decision: a specialist looking at marked work and saying whether Extended is realistic.

That single diagnostic hour is often the highest-value fee on this page. It is charged at the tutor's normal rate and it produces a written view a parent can take into a meeting with the head of department. It does not override the school, and no tutor can promise it will change anything. What it does is replace a parent's instinct with somebody's reading of the mark scheme, which is a different kind of argument in that room.

sections.heading: What in-home IGCSE tutoring is advertised at in the Kingdom
paragraphs: Published Saudi rates are wide and they are all vendor marketing, so read them as advertised rates rather than as a market average. Tutoring-platform listings start near SAR 55 an hour for general, non-specialist support, and budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35. A tutor-marketplace guide puts general private tuition in Riyadh near SAR 50 an hour at primary level and above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects. Some international providers quote in dollars, near $60 an hour.

An in-home rate carries travel. A tutor crossing Riyadh at six in the evening is selling you two hours of their day for one hour of teaching, and the quote reflects that whether or not it is itemised. The same loading is why the in-home pool shrinks outside the three big urban clusters: there is no rate at which a 4PM1 specialist drives to Al Ahsa twice a week. This is the honest argument for buying the hour online instead.

None of those figures is what IB Gram charges, and none of them should be treated as a typical price. What they are useful for is calibration. If a quote sits at the bottom of the published range for a scarce specialism, ask what is missing: marking between lessons, a written plan, examiner familiarity with the component, or simply the hours. If it sits at the top, ask what the extra buys in terms a parent can check. A free trial lesson is the cheapest way to find out.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week is what the fee is really buying
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. That gives a family five possible lesson evenings, and the usable part of each is narrow: after the school run, after food, before a teenager stops being able to think. For most Saudi households the real window is between about five and nine in the evening, which is four hours a day shared across every subject a child is weak in.

Thursday evening is the worst of the five and Sunday evening is the second worst, for opposite reasons. Thursday is the edge of the weekend and nothing set that night gets done. Sunday carries the backlog of two days off. Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday are where a demanding component belongs, and they are also the evenings every other family is bidding for. A tutor who offers you only Thursday is telling you something about their own book.

This is why a fee comparison that ignores the slot is incomplete. An hour on Tuesday at seven, held every week for a term, is worth more than two hours on Thursday that keep getting moved. Ask for the slot in writing, ask how much notice is needed to change it, and ask what happens to it during the long summer break and the midyear break. A slot given up over the summer is a tutor re-hired in the autumn term, usually at a worse time.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against your tutor's working week
paragraphs: The Kingdom sits on Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and does not change its clocks. Every country that does will drift against you twice a year. A tutor in India is two and a half hours ahead and stays there, so an eight o'clock evening lesson in Riyadh is half past ten for them: workable once, unsustainable twice a week. A tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer.

That drift is a scheduling cost, not a rounding error. A slot agreed in local tutor time will move by an hour in the spring and again in the autumn unless it is pinned to Arabia Standard Time in writing. Pinning it means the tutor absorbs the shift, which they will do only if the slot is worth holding. This is one of the quiet reasons a scarce specialist quotes high: they are being asked to hold an awkward hour permanently.

A tutor's own working week matters as much as their time zone. Somebody teaching full time in a Monday-to-Friday system has Saturday and Sunday free and Thursday evening busy, which is the inverse of what a Saudi family needs. Somebody already teaching Gulf families has a book built around Sunday to Thursday and will offer a mid-week evening without negotiation. Ask which of the two you are talking to before you discuss money at all. It is the most useful question in a first call.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Paying for content when the marks are being lost on technique is the most common waste in this market. A candidate who can describe electrolysis and still scores four out of six does not need the topic taught again; they need to see what the mark scheme pays for. Cambridge command terms are doing real work in that sentence. Describe, explain, suggest and compare are instructions with different mark allocations, and students read them as synonyms. The fee is the same either way; the outcome is not.

The specific trouble spots recur. On Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 it is the physics third, because the tutor is usually a biologist or a chemist. On Computer Science 0478 it is the pre-release material, which rewards a documented approach rather than working code. On Literature in English 0486 it is the passage-based question, where candidates write about the whole text instead of the lines in front of them. On Accounting 0452 it is presentation convention rather than arithmetic.

Diagnosing which of these applies takes a marked paper and about an hour. That is what a trial lesson is for, and a tutor who spends it teaching rather than diagnosing has told you how the rest will go. Ask for the diagnosis in writing afterwards: which component, which question type, which command terms, and how many hours the tutor thinks the repair takes. A number they will put in writing is a number you can hold them to, and it makes the second quote you get comparable to the first.

sections.heading: What a fee can never buy
paragraphs: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback. No tutor may produce any part of an assessed component for a candidate, and no fee changes that. Where a Cambridge subject carries coursework, the school sets it, supervises it and marks it, and the board moderates a sample. An outside tutor can read a draft against the published criteria and say what is thin. They cannot supply sentences, and a provider offering to is selling a malpractice risk. Say this out loud to any provider before the first invoice.

The same boundary applies to the Middle Years Programme Personal Project and to any portfolio component. The student's own record of their process is part of what is assessed, so help that does not appear in that record is help that creates a problem later. Keep the versions. A dated draft before a tutoring session and a dated draft after it is the evidence a school needs if a question is ever asked. Most schools ask for nothing; the few that ask, ask once and expect an answer.

Schools in the Kingdom take this seriously because the consequence falls on the candidate. A malpractice finding can cost a grade, a subject or a whole series, and no appeal recovers the time. The practical rule for a family paying by the hour is simple: if you cannot describe what the tutor did in a sentence you would be happy to read aloud to the head of department, do not pay for it again. That test is easier to apply than any policy document.

faqs.question: Which parts of Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 most often need a tutor's time, and what does that add to the fee?
faqs.answer: Almost always the physics third. The award is usually taught by a biologist and a chemist sharing a timetable, and physics gets the thinnest coverage. A tutor credible across all three sciences is rare, so the hourly figure sits above a single-science rate. Many families buy the physics hours alone and leave the rest to the school, which is the cheaper decision. Ask which teacher at the school actually covers the physics content.

faqs.question: Why do Cambridge Literature in English 0486 candidates lose marks on the passage-based question?
faqs.answer: Because they answer on the whole text. The passage-based question pays for close reading of the lines printed in front of the candidate: word choice, imagery, shifts in tone, the effect of a line break. A student who summarises the plot of the novel has written something true and scored very little. It is a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem, and it responds quickly to an hour spent annotating one extract properly.

faqs.question: What goes wrong in the Cambridge Computer Science 0478 pre-release task?
faqs.answer: Students write code and skip the documentation. The pre-release scenario exists so candidates arrive with a worked understanding of a problem, and the marks go to identifying the data needed, structuring the solution and explaining the design decisions. A candidate who can program fluently but has never written a structured explanation of their own algorithm loses marks that are easier to win than anything in the theory paper.

faqs.question: Where does Edexcel Mathematics B 4MB1 diverge from Mathematics A, and does that change the hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Mathematics B is a single untiered route with more algebraic demand and no Foundation entry, so there is no safety net below it. Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation and Higher. Tutors who teach 4MB1 are a smaller group and tend to quote above the general maths band for that reason. If your school enters Mathematics B, confirm it before you pay for 4MA1 past papers, because the question styles differ.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge Accounting 0452 questions take the longest to repair in one-to-one time?
faqs.answer: The final statements questions, because the marks sit in convention rather than arithmetic. Candidates who calculate a figure correctly still lose marks on where it sits, how it is labelled and what the format demands. Repairing that means working through complete statements rather than isolated calculations, which is slow. Expect several sessions rather than one, and expect the tutor to set full questions as homework and mark them between lessons.

faqs.question: How do I check that a home tutor's quoted fee includes the component my child is actually entered for?
faqs.answer: Send the syllabus code and ask which components the quote covers. A tutor who teaches theory and has never prepared a candidate for the alternative-to-practical paper should say so. Ask for a sentence on each component: what it tests and where candidates lose marks. Vague answers at this stage become expensive later, because you end up buying a second tutor for the component the first one does not cover.

faqs.question: Is a tutor who has taught both Core and Extended worth a higher fee than one who teaches only Extended?
faqs.answer: For most families, no. The useful experience is of the tier your child is entered for. Where it matters is when the tier decision is still open: a tutor who has taught both can say honestly whether Extended is realistic from the marked work, rather than guessing. If the entry is already made and it is Extended, pay for depth in Extended instead of breadth across tiers.

faqs.question: What should a tutor be able to tell me about assessment objectives before I agree a monthly fee?
faqs.answer: Which objectives each paper weights, and what that means for how an answer is written. A specialist will tell you that recall, application and analysis are not interchangeable, and will point at a past question to show which is being asked for. They should also be able to name the command terms that cost their students the most marks. A tutor who talks only about topics has read the textbook, not the syllabus.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE components can one tutor hold at a sensible fee before quality drops?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect. Marking a full paper to the scheme takes close to an hour and setting work takes more, so a tutor teaching many weekly hours either stops marking or stops preparing. Ask how many candidates they currently carry and how much marking is included between sessions. A lower rate with no marking is often more expensive per mark gained than a higher rate with it.

faqs.question: If a tutor's working week is Monday to Friday, what does that do to the fee we are quoted?
faqs.answer: It usually raises it, or it costs you the good evenings. Somebody teaching inside a Monday-to-Friday system is tired on Sunday, busy on Thursday and free at the weekend, which is inverted from a Saudi school week. Holding a mid-week Saudi evening permanently is a real concession and gets priced as one. A tutor whose book is already built around Sunday to Thursday quotes more simply.

faqs.question: Does paying for extra hours change what a tutor is allowed to do with an assessed Cambridge component?
faqs.answer: No. The boundary is set by the board and the school, not by the invoice. A tutor may teach the skills a component needs, read a draft against the published criteria and say what is missing or unclear. They may not supply content that is then submitted as the candidate's own. Buying more hours buys more teaching and more feedback; it does not move the line, and any provider implying otherwise is a risk.

faqs.question: Who keeps the evidence that a paid tutor only gave feedback on a coursework draft?
faqs.answer: The family should, and it costs nothing. Save each version with a date, keep the tutor's written comments separate from the student's text, and keep the session notes. If a school ever asks how a piece developed, a sequence of dated drafts answers in a minute. Verbal reassurance does not. This matters more where a tutor is engaged privately than where the school supervises, because there is no institutional record.

faqs.question: Can a paid session be used to rehearse an IGCSE speaking or presentation component?
faqs.answer: Yes, within limits. Practising delivery, timing, pronunciation and the handling of follow-up questions is ordinary teaching and sits well in a one-to-one hour. What a tutor cannot do is script the content that gets assessed or supply the material the candidate presents as their own thinking. Rehearsing structure is fine; rehearsing somebody else's words is not, and examiners hear the difference more often than families expect.

faqs.question: What does a school do if it suspects a paid tutor contributed to a submitted component?
faqs.answer: It follows its own malpractice procedure and reports to the board if it finds a case. The student is interviewed, drafts and plans are requested, and the submission may be withdrawn. The tutor faces nothing; the candidate carries the outcome, which can be a lost grade or a lost series. That asymmetry is why a family should be the strictest party in the arrangement rather than the most relaxed.

intro.heading: A near-me search for IGCSE help is a question about fit, not travel time
paragraphs: Type IGCSE home tutor near me into Google from a villa in Riyadh, a compound in Dhahran or a flat in north Jeddah and the results look the same: agency pages with a contact form and no rate. The question underneath the search is narrower than the search itself. A family rarely wants the closest tutor. They want a tutor who teaches the exact specification their child sits, Core or Extended, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, the syllabus code printed on the statement of entry, and who is free at the one hour of the week the school run leaves open. Distance stands in for both of those things, and it stands in badly.

In-home tuition in the Kingdom is a real market and worth understanding before you discount it. Agencies advertise senior-school exam subjects from around SAR 200 an hour, and part of that figure is travel: a tutor crossing Riyadh north to south in the late afternoon can lose an hour of billable time to traffic each way. The pool shrinks accordingly. In a city with a handful of schools entering Cambridge candidates, the number of people who teach Extended Physics, live within a twenty-minute drive and are free at seven in the evening is very small. Outside Riyadh, Jeddah and the Dammam cluster it is often nobody at all.

IB Gram works the other way round. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, which takes the drive out of both sides of the arrangement and widens the pool from one district to every tutor who can hold an hour on Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and saying so plainly matters more than winning the click. What a family gets in exchange is specificity: a tutor who has taught the component your child is losing marks on, rather than the nearest person who read science at university.

The rest of this page runs in the order the money gets spent. First what in-home and online IGCSE tuition are actually advertised at in the Kingdom, and what moves those numbers. Then what a higher rate buys, since a tier and syllabus match are worth more than an extra degree. Then the logistics that decide whether any of it survives a term: the Sunday-to-Thursday week, and a tutor whose own working week may run Monday to Friday on a clock three hours behind yours. Outcomes come last, because they depend on all three. A family that settles the rate and the slot in the first week almost never has to renegotiate either one later, and the term is spent on the subject instead.

sections.heading: What a search for an IGCSE home tutor near me is really asking
paragraphs: The phrase is about reach, not metres. A parent typing IGCSE home tutor near me wants to know whether anybody inside the range of their daily life teaches the course their child is sitting. In a Saudi city that range is set by the evening school run and by the small number of schools entering Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel candidates. The honest answer is often that the nearest competent generalist is easy to find and the nearest Extended Chemistry specialist is not.

That distinction decides the money. A generalist can keep a Year 10 student company through homework and will shift a grade if the problem is organisation. A specialist is what moves a stuck Extended candidate, because the problem by then is almost never coverage of the syllabus. It is the way a particular mark scheme pays for a particular kind of answer. Paying a specialist rate for a generalist is the commonest waste in this market, and paying a generalist rate for a problem only a specialist can diagnose is the second.

So the useful version of the search is narrower: who teaches this syllabus code, at this tier, and is free on a Sunday or Tuesday evening on Arabia Standard Time? Asking it by district narrows the field to whoever happens to live nearby. Asking it by subject and slot widens the field to anyone who can hold the hour, wherever they are. Lessons at IB Gram run online over live video for exactly that reason, and the sections below put numbers against the trade.

Read the left-hand column carefully. A platform advertising IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35 an hour is not describing the same product as a company quoting from SAR 180 for a senior-school subject. At the lower end the tutor is frequently a graduate teaching a subject rather than a specification, with no tier match and no marking experience behind the answer. That can still be the right purchase for a Year 9 student who needs supervised practice, and the wrong one for a Year 11 Extended candidate eight weeks out from the papers.

What moves the number, in rough order of weight: how scarce the subject is, whether the tutor has marked for a board, the tier being taught, whether anybody has to travel, and how long a block you commit to. Additional Mathematics and Extended Physics sit at the top of that list in every Saudi city. Travel loading is the one cost that disappears completely when the lesson runs over video instead of across town, which is why the same hour buys more teaching.

sections.heading: What the higher rate buys, and how to check it before you pay
paragraphs: Three things justify a premium at IGCSE level and all three are checkable in one conversation. The first is specification knowledge: a tutor who can name the papers your child sits, their weightings, and whether the entry is Core or Extended without looking anything up. The second is marking experience, which changes what a tutor notices in a written answer. The third is availability at the hour you actually have, which sounds like logistics and behaves like quality.

Ask for the syllabus code. Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, International Mathematics is 0607, Physics is 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, and a tutor who teaches the subject in general terms will hesitate. Ask which tier the student is entered for and what the ceiling is: Core is graded C to G, so a Core candidate cannot be awarded above a C however well the paper goes, while Extended runs A* to E. Pearson Edexcel grades 9 to 1 instead, and the two specifications are not interchangeable.

Then ask what the tutor would do in the first hour. A good answer describes a diagnostic, a past question or two sat to time to find out where the marks are going, rather than a plan to start at the beginning of the textbook. A tutor whose pitch is that they will sit with their coursework, rather than teach the skills the component assesses, has told you something useful about where their own line sits.

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and the tutor's own working week
paragraphs: The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Most tutoring copy on the internet is written for a Monday-to-Friday country and quietly assumes a Saturday morning lesson is available and a Sunday one is not. For a family in Riyadh or Al Khobar the reverse holds: Sunday evening is a school night with homework due, and Saturday morning is free.

This decides which tutors can serve you at all. A tutor in India works Monday to Saturday, so a Sunday lesson falls inside their working week and a Friday one does not. A tutor in the United Kingdom has Sunday free and Friday as a working day, which is the opposite of what a Saudi school week needs. A tutor already teaching to a Gulf week has the same rhythm as your school and understands why a Thursday evening session is the end of the week rather than the middle of it.

Settle this in the trial lesson rather than discovering it in week three. The questions worth asking are whether Sunday is a teaching day for that tutor, whether a Friday or Saturday catch-up is possible when a school trip eats a session, and how the slot is protected through the autumn break, when international school calendars and the Ministry of Education calendar diverge inside the same city. None of it is complicated. All of it is easier to agree before money changes hands.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time, and the slot that quietly drifts
paragraphs: The Kingdom runs on Arabia Standard Time, three hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time, and does not change its clocks at any point in the year. Most of the countries tutors work from do. That single asymmetry costs more lessons than connection problems do, because a slot agreed in one half of the year moves by an hour in the other unless it was written down as a Saudi local time.

The arithmetic is worth doing once. India is two and a half hours ahead of the Kingdom, so a seven o'clock lesson in Riyadh is half past nine for a tutor in Chennai: late, but workable, and stable all year because neither country shifts. The United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two in their summer, so a six o'clock Riyadh slot is three in the afternoon for part of the year and four for the rest. Agree the Saudi time and let the tutor's clock do the moving.

Two practical rules follow. Write the slot as an Arabia Standard Time in whatever confirmation you are sent, not as the tutor's time and not as a vague evening. And ask what happens in the week the tutor's own country changes its clocks, because that is the week a session goes missing with nobody at fault. A tutor who has taught Gulf families before will raise both points without being prompted, which is itself a signal worth noticing.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks go missing, and what a term of work targets
paragraphs: By the second year of an IGCSE course the gap between what a student knows and what they are paid for is usually wider than any gap in their knowledge. Command terms are the mechanism. State, describe, explain, suggest and calculate each buy a different kind of answer, and a candidate who answers describe when the paper said explain loses the reasoning marks while writing more words, not fewer.

The pattern repeats by subject. In Chemistry the equation questions reward balancing and state symbols that get dropped under time pressure. In Biology the strictly marked definitions score nothing for a near-miss paraphrase. In Physics the alternative-to-practical paper asks about method, precision and sources of error, which no amount of extra content revision reaches. In Economics the data-response questions want figures from the stimulus used inside the argument, rather than general theory parked next to it.

A term of work on this looks unglamorous. Past questions sat to time, marked against the published mark scheme, and then rewritten once the candidate can see which four words the examiner was paying for. That loop is also why written work marked between lessons matters as much as the hour on video. The lesson is where a student finds out what went wrong; the week in between is where they prove they can do it unaided, which is the only version of the skill that survives an examination hall with a clock on the wall.

sections.heading: Coursework, drafts and the line an IGCSE tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects still carry a coursework or portfolio component that the school marks and the board moderates. The work has to be the student's own, and the school has to be able to say so. That is the context a tutor operates inside, and it is worth knowing exactly where the boundary sits before anybody is paid, because a family cannot rely on a provider in this market to volunteer it.

A tutor may teach the skills a component assesses, explain the criteria, work through an unrelated example, read a draft the student has written and say which criterion is under-served and why. A tutor may not write any part of it, dictate sentences for a student to copy down, or hand back a rewritten version. No tutor should ever produce a piece of assessed work for a student, and a provider who offers that is selling a malpractice investigation rather than a grade.

The same line applies to a Middle Years Programme Personal Project and, later, to a Diploma Internal Assessment or Extended Essay. Keep the audit trail: drafts dated, feedback kept, a record of what changed and why. If a school ever asks, that file is the answer. Families who want somebody else to deal with their coursework are not short of options in this market; what they are actually buying is risk, and the risk lands on the student rather than on the provider who sold it.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge IGCSE grade is the ceiling on a Core entry, and can the tier still be changed?
faqs.answer: Core papers on a tiered Cambridge subject are graded C to G, so a Core candidate cannot be awarded above a C however well the papers go. Extended runs A* to E. The tier is a school decision taken at entry, and it is reversible only before the entry deadline, which falls months ahead of the June series. Ask your school's examinations officer in writing which tier each subject has been entered for.

faqs.question: What does a four-mark explain question pay for that a longer describe answer does not?
faqs.answer: Explain asks for reasoning: a cause linked to an effect with the mechanism in between. Describe asks only for what is observed. A candidate who writes three accurate descriptive sentences on an explain question can score one mark from four while filling all the space provided. The fix is mechanical. Underline the command term first, then write one linked because clause for each mark available.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE grade boundaries move between the June and November series, and why?
faqs.answer: They do. Boundaries are set after each series against the difficulty of that particular paper and the performance of that cohort, so the same raw total can fall either side of a grade line in two different sittings. This is why a mock marked against an earlier series' boundaries is a rough guide rather than a prediction, and why practising against the mark scheme beats chasing a percentage.

faqs.question: What does a school look at when it fixes a predicted IGCSE grade for a sixth-form application?
faqs.answer: Usually mock papers marked to the published scheme, classwork across the preceding terms, and the subject teacher's judgement about trajectory. It is a professional estimate rather than a promise, and it can be revised. If a prediction looks low, ask which components it rests on and what evidence would change it. That question tends to be more productive than disputing the number itself.

faqs.question: How much of a Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grade comes from the written papers alone?
faqs.answer: In most Edexcel International GCSE subjects the written papers carry the whole grade, with coursework retained on only a few specifications. Cambridge keeps a practical or alternative-to-practical component in the sciences. The split matters when you are deciding where tutoring hours go, so check the component list on the specification your school actually entered rather than assuming the two boards behave the same way.

faqs.question: What does the Extended tier add to the same topic list that Core leaves out?
faqs.answer: Extended covers the Core content plus a supplementary section, and it examines the shared material at greater depth. In Mathematics that means functions, harder trigonometry and vectors. In the sciences it means quantitative treatment of topics Core handles descriptively. A student moving up from Core has both new topics to learn and familiar topics to revisit against a higher standard, which is why the move needs a term rather than a fortnight.

faqs.question: What should the first hour with an IGCSE tutor establish before any teaching begins?
faqs.answer: Where the marks are actually going. A useful first hour has the student sitting two or three past questions to time, marked live against the published scheme, so the tutor can separate a content gap from a technique problem. You should finish it knowing which components are weak, in what order they will be worked through, and what has been set between lessons.

faqs.question: How will I know inside the first month whether this is working for my child?
faqs.answer: Look for three signals rather than a grade. The student can name the command terms in their subject and say what each one demands. Marked work coming back shows fewer lost method marks on the same question type. And the tutor's notes are specific about components instead of general about effort. A grade shift usually arrives a term behind all three.

faqs.question: What does a weekly note from an IGCSE tutor need to contain to be worth reading?
faqs.answer: Four things: the topic or component covered, what the student could not do at the start of the hour, what they can do now, and what has been set before the next session. A note saying the lesson went well tells you nothing. A note naming the paper and the question type lets you check progress against the specification yourself.

faqs.question: What happens if my child does not want the sessions at all?
faqs.answer: Say so before the trial rather than after it. A reluctant student often responds to a tutor who starts from a paper they have already sat and shows them exactly where four marks went, because that is concrete and it is not a lecture. If the resistance holds after two or three sessions, a smaller commitment on one weak component usually works better than a full programme.

faqs.question: Can we pause or change tutor without losing the evening slot we fought for?
faqs.answer: Changing tutor inside the same slot is the normal case and we try to hold the hour, though a replacement specialist in a scarce subject may only be free on a different evening. Pausing across a long school holiday is usually possible with notice, but the slot cannot be held open indefinitely. Agree the notice period at the start rather than at the point you need it.

faqs.question: At what point in Year 10 does an IGCSE mark start telling you something real?
faqs.answer: Roughly from the end of the first full term, once a student has sat something under timed conditions on content that has been taught. Marks from the opening weeks mostly measure how quickly a class settled. The first properly timed assessment is the one worth reacting to, and a weak result there is early enough to fix without changing tier or dropping the subject.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting IGCSE support in the term the papers are sat?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the work changes shape. There is no time to reteach a course, so the hours go where marks are most recoverable: command terms, timed technique, the practical or alternative-to-practical paper, and the two or three topics the mock exposed as weakest. Expect triage and a gap list rather than a plan that starts at the front of the specification.

faqs.question: What should a Year 9 student in a Saudi school have settled before IGCSE sets are decided?
faqs.answer: Three things. Arithmetic and algebra fluent enough that method marks are not lost to slips. Enough technical English in the sciences to read a question accurately under time pressure. And a subject list that does not quietly close a route they may want later. If Additional Mathematics or a science Higher Level course is in view, the Mathematics tier decision is the one to get right.

intro.heading: Work backwards from the evidence, because at IGCSE there is plenty of it
paragraphs: An IGCSE course is unusually well documented. Both boards publish a specification for every subject, naming the components, the duration and mark total of each paper, the percentage weighting each one carries, and the assessment objectives the marks are distributed across. Past papers and mark schemes are published. Grade thresholds are published after each series. This matters because it means progress at IGCSE is genuinely measurable, and any conversation about tuition that stays in the language of confidence and motivation is avoiding the available facts.

So the sensible order is to decide what you will measure before buying anything. The usable unit is a mark on a named component, mapped to the assessment objective it came from. A student who scores fifty-four on a paper is not thereby understood: a tutor needs to know whether the lost marks sat in recall, in application, or in the extended-response and data-handling objectives where most of the gap usually lives. That mapping is the single most useful thing a first session can produce, and it is also the fastest way to find out whether the tutor works from the specification or from memory.

Which brings the question round to the tutor. Online tuition removes distance as a constraint and replaces it with a verification problem: a family in Al Ahsa can now choose from everyone who teaches Cambridge 0620, and has no idea how to tell them apart. The answer is not credentials in the abstract. It is a small set of artefacts a competent teacher can produce on request, each of which is impossible to fake convincingly: the component list for the code, the weighting of each paper, what the mark scheme rewards on a six-mark answer, and the three topics where this specification differs from the one next door.

The two halves of that are the shape of this page. First the evidence about your child: what a mark means, what a mock predicts and does not, what the school already holds and how to ask for it, and the record each lesson leaves behind. Then the evidence about the tutor: the questions that separate a specification specialist from a subject graduate, what the advertised rate bands in the Kingdom actually buy by way of verification, and what no honest provider can show you because the number does not exist.

Two facts frame everything. Delivery is online: lessons are one-to-one over live video, pinned to Arabia Standard Time so a slot agreed with a tutor abroad does not move when that country changes its clocks. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. And the series matter: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series, the main one for Saudi schools, and a November series for resits and November-entry candidates. Cambridge also runs a February/March series, but it is sat in India only, so a Saudi family should disregard any entry deadline quoted against it.
