igcse-online-tuition.programmesIntro: Four structures account for almost every Saudi family arriving at an IGCSE enquiry. Two are the qualifications themselves, one is what some schools run instead at the same age, and one is what the grades are being collected for. The differences are operational, not philosophical, and each changes what a tutor has to know.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Subject-by-subject qualifications with a published syllabus code, usually a four-digit number such as 0580 or 0620. Many subjects are tiered: a Core entry is graded C to G and an Extended entry A* to E, so the tier decides the ceiling before the course begins. Components vary by subject and often include a practical or alternative-to-practical paper. Grade thresholds are set per series and published afterwards.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the most common IGCSE route in Saudi international schools, and the code a student is entered for is a school decision recorded on the entry form. Families should ask for the code and the tier in writing, because a Core entry caps the grade however well the student performs and the decision is reversible only before the entry deadline. Saudi candidates sit the June and November series.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same qualification level with a different architecture. Codes run on a different pattern, 4MA1 for Mathematics A or 4PH1 for Physics, and grading uses the 9 to 1 scale rather than letters. Papers are structured differently from the Cambridge equivalent in the same subject, with different numbers of components and different weightings, and the assessment objective split is defined in its own specification.
programmes.countryNote: A number of British-curriculum schools in the Kingdom run Pearson Edexcel across some subjects and Cambridge across others, which is how a family ends up with two grade scales on one set of results. A tutor who prepares a 4MA1 candidate on 0580 past papers is working from the wrong paper structure, and that is a mistake a parent can catch in a single question.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Some schools run the Middle Years Programme across the same two years instead of IGCSE. Assessment is criterion-referenced, scored against four strands per subject group out of eight, with the Personal Project in the final year. There is no external written examination of the IGCSE kind, so a student moving between the two systems meets timed written papers and published mark schemes for the first time.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi families switch between these routes more often than families in a single-system country, usually because a school place or a posting changes. The transfer exposes examination technique rather than knowledge: a student used to criterion descriptors has to learn how a mark scheme allocates points to specific statements, which is a teachable skill and the first thing a good tutor measures.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The most common post-16 destination for IGCSE students in Saudi international schools, alongside A Levels. Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service, with written papers in the May session. IGCSE grades feed the subject and level decisions directly, and a weak grade in a subject taken forward to Higher Level is the most predictable source of trouble.
programmes.countryNote: This is what the IGCSE evidence is actually for in the Kingdom. A student's component-level profile at sixteen, not just the grade letter, predicts which Higher Level choices are realistic. A family planning to take Mathematics forward should ask the school which Diploma mathematics course the IGCSE route prepares for, because Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation set different expectations.

igcse-online-tuition.subjectsIntro: Subjects are listed with the codes families see on an entry form, because that is the unit a tutor is matched on. The note against each one describes the component structure and the verification question worth asking, rather than a general description of the subject.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Two papers on most routes, with a tier that caps the attainable grade. Method marks are awarded for stated working even when the final answer is wrong, which is why presentation is worth real marks. Verification question: which tier is my child entered for, and how many marks across the papers are available for method alone?

subjects.name: Additional and Further Pure Mathematics
subjects.description: A separate qualification sat alongside the main mathematics entry, covering calculus, matrices, series and trigonometric identities well beyond the standard course. It is the clearest early signal of readiness for Higher Level mathematics later. Verification question: which topics appear here that do not appear in the main specification, and how is the paper weighted?

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Multiple-choice, theory and a practical or alternative-to-practical component, with weightings set in the specification. Extended-response marks depend on using the quantity, the unit and the relationship in the same sentence. Verification question: is my child sitting the practical paper or the alternative, and what does the alternative actually assess?

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Theory papers plus a practical route, with a significant share of marks resting on precise definitions and on reading experimental descriptions accurately. Equation and mole calculations carry method credit. Verification question: how are marks split between recall, handling information and experimental skills in the specification for our code?

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Definition-heavy with an unusually strict marking style: a correct idea expressed in the wrong words frequently scores nothing. Data interpretation and experimental design carry more weight than students assume. Verification question: which definitions in this specification are marked word-tight, and how do you teach them?

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences
subjects.description: One or two grades awarded across biology, chemistry and physics content, with reduced coverage in each. The usual tutoring error is teaching the single-science specification by default, which wastes time on content that will not appear. Verification question: which topics from each single science are excluded from our combined route?

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing assessed against published criteria, with marks for a specific register, audience and form rather than for general fluency. A strong writer who ignores the directed task loses most of the available credit. Verification question: what exactly does the directed-writing task award marks for in our specification?

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification with different papers, including listening and in some routes a speaking endorsement. Fluent speakers often sit it and still lose marks on the exercise types, which reward precision of answer form rather than expression. Verification question: which components does our entry include, and is speaking endorsed or graded?

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Short-answer, case-study and extended-response questions where the marks sit in application to the given business rather than in the textbook definition. Evaluation marks require a judgement with a reason attached. Verification question: how many marks on each paper depend on applying the answer to the stimulus material?

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Data-response and structured essay work, with diagram accuracy worth marks in its own right. Students frequently describe a mechanism correctly and then fail to label the diagram that carries the credit. Verification question: which diagrams are examinable in this specification and how are they marked?

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Theory papers plus a programming or problem-solving component, with pseudocode conventions that differ between the boards. A student fluent in Python can still lose marks writing answers in the wrong notation. Verification question: which pseudocode convention does our specification require, and where is it published?

igcse-online-tuition.regionsTitle: Where the enquiries come from, and what the local school picture changes
igcse-online-tuition.regionsIntro: Online delivery makes the family's location irrelevant to who can teach them, and highly relevant to what they are likely to need. These are the clusters Saudi IGCSE enquiries come from, with the thing that most often has to be verified in each.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The widest board mix in the Kingdom, with Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel entries sometimes sitting in the same year group of the same school. Families here are the most likely to arrive not knowing which board a particular subject is entered under, which makes the entry form the first thing to check rather than the last.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine with British, American and IB provision at different points along it. Students commonly carry a split profile, with sciences on one board and English on another. The practical consequence is that past-paper practice has to be sourced per subject rather than per student.

regions.name: Dhahran and Al Khobar
regions.note: British and Cambridge-curriculum schools sit alongside International Schools Group campuses, and the grade scales a family sees on one results slip can come from two different systems. Compound residence also means study space is predictable and quiet, which makes a fixed weekday evening slot unusually reliable here.

regions.name: Dammam and Qatif
regions.note: Part of a single conurbation with Al Khobar and Dhahran, where families routinely live in one city and attend school in another. Term dates and mock timetables therefore differ between neighbours, and a tuition plan has to be pinned to the child's own school calendar rather than to a regional assumption.

regions.name: Jubail, Yanbu and Ras Tanura
regions.note: Industrial centres where school provision is tied to the plants and the companies around them, and subject choice at sixteen can be narrower than in the big cities. The commonest verification problem is a subject offered only as a combined science when a student is aiming at single-science entries later.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: An hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, far enough that local in-home options thin out sharply. Families here were among the earliest consistent users of online tuition in the Kingdom for straightforward reasons of distance, and tend to arrive with a clear subject brief already.

regions.name: Makkah, Madinah and Taif
regions.note: Large cities with limited international provision relative to population, and calendars that bend around Hajj and Umrah seasons. A fixed online slot absorbs those weeks better than an arrangement that depends on travel, and catch-up is planned around the school's own published calendar.

regions.name: Buraidah and Ha'il
regions.note: Central and northern centres where a family may be choosing between a national-curriculum school and a single international option. Students switching into an IGCSE route mid-course are common, and the first job is usually a component-level gap map rather than general teaching.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: Project-driven relocation brings students into the north-west part-way through a two-year course. Mid-course arrivals need the specification difference mapped before anything else: a student who studied a different board's content for a year has gaps that are specific and findable rather than general.

regions.name: Abha, Khamis Mushait, Najran and Jazan
regions.note: Southern cities where distance is the binding constraint and a specialist in a particular code may not live within hours. Saying that plainly is more useful than implying local choice exists. These are the families for whom online delivery changes the size of the pool rather than merely the convenience.

schoolClusters.note: The capital holds the broadest mix of curricula and the widest spread of board entries at sixteen. Students we support attend schools including these. A family comparing them should ask each school which boards it enters students for, subject by subject, because the answer is rarely uniform across a year group.

Jeddah's international schools span British, American, IB and national-system routes along the coastal spine, and The KAUST School serves the university campus community to the north. Students we support attend schools across this group, and their board profiles at sixteen differ considerably.

International Schools Group campuses operate across the Dammam, Dhahran, Al Khobar and Jubail area alongside British-curriculum schools, and not every campus runs every programme. Students we support attend schools including these, with many commuting between cities daily.

igcse-online-tuition.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named only as context for the IGCSE landscape a Saudi family is working inside; IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to, endorsement from or formal connection with any school, group, board or regulator mentioned here.
igcse-online-tuition.modesIntro: Three arrangements cover nearly every IGCSE booking, and they differ in what evidence they produce rather than in how long they last. All three run one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one against a named component
modes.description: A fixed slot aimed at one paper rather than at a subject. The plan names the component, the assessment objectives where marks are being lost and the topics those objectives sit in. Each session closes with a short written record of what was taught and what the student could then do unaided, so a six-week stretch produces a readable trail rather than a general impression.
bullets: Scoped to one component and its weighting in the specification
Written record after each session, tied to objectives rather than topics
Reviewed at six sessions against the opening mock, not against confidence

modes.title: Lesson plus marked work between lessons
modes.description: The lesson teaches; the marking produces the evidence. A student completes a timed section between sessions, the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme and returns an annotated script showing where each mark was awarded or lost. The next lesson starts from that script. This is the arrangement that produces the clearest month-to-month picture, and the one families most often skip.
bullets: Annotated script against the published mark scheme, not a percentage
Losses attributed to an objective so the next session has a target
Builds a mark trail a school's own reports rarely contain

modes.title: An intensive block before a series
modes.description: A concentrated run in the weeks before a June or November sitting, built on full papers under timed conditions rather than on content coverage. The opening session is a full paper; the block then works through the losses in order of marks available. It suits resit candidates and mid-course arrivals, and it is deliberately finite.
bullets: Opens with a full timed paper used as the baseline measurement
Prioritised by marks available, not by syllabus order
Fixed number of sessions with a stated end point

sections.heading: Four numbers a family is shown, and the one that means something
paragraphs: Progress at IGCSE arrives as numbers, and most of them are less informative than they look. A family is typically shown a raw mark on a school assessment, a percentage, a predicted grade, and occasionally a grade derived from a published threshold. These are not four views of the same thing. They are produced by different processes, they can move in opposite directions in the same term, and only one of them can be acted on in a lesson.

A raw mark becomes useful only once it is attached to a component and broken down by where it was lost. Sixty out of a hundred tells a tutor nothing; sixty out of a hundred with forty of the lost marks sitting in extended-response questions and none in recall tells them exactly what the next six weeks should contain. That attribution is the work, and it cannot be done from a percentage. A school report that gives percentages without components is reporting on effort, whatever it says at the top.

A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by a teacher for a specific purpose, usually an application. It is not a measurement, it is not a promise, and it is not a tutor's to revise. It is still worth having in the conversation, because a predicted grade that sits well above or below the component evidence is a question somebody should be asking the school. Grade thresholds move between series, which is why a mark converted to a grade using last series' threshold is an estimate rather than a result.

The table below sets out what each kind of evidence can carry. The practical takeaway is that a family should ask for component-level marks from the school and from the tutor, and should treat anything that cannot be broken down that way as background rather than as information.

Where marks were lost, by question and by objective

A percentage on a school assessment

Whether the student is engaging with the course

sections.heading: The specification is the tutor's job description
paragraphs: Both boards publish the specification for every code they offer, and it contains everything a family needs to evaluate a tutor. It names each component, the duration and total mark, the percentage weighting the component carries towards the final grade, the assessment objectives and how the marks are distributed across them, the content a candidate is accountable for, and the formulae or data a candidate is given in the examination. A teacher working from the specification and a teacher working from a textbook are doing visibly different jobs.

The difference shows up in where time goes. A textbook treats every chapter as roughly equal. A specification does not: one component may carry a third of the grade while another carries a tenth, and the assessment objectives are weighted too, so marks for applying knowledge may considerably outweigh marks for recalling it. A tutor who has read the weightings prioritises accordingly. A tutor who has not spends equal time on everything, which looks thorough and quietly wastes the scarcest resource a Year 11 student has.

It also decides what the student is allowed to take into the room. A formula sheet or data section provided in one subject's examination is not provided in another, and in some subjects it is provided for one board and not the other. A student who has memorised what they would have been given, or who arrives expecting a sheet that does not exist, has lost marks to a logistical fact rather than to a gap in understanding. This is checkable in a minute and it is checked surprisingly rarely.

The honest use of all this for a parent is as an interview script. Ask a prospective tutor to name the components for your child's code and the weighting of each. Ask which assessment objective carries the most marks. Ask what is supplied in the examination. Those three questions take two minutes and no amount of general subject knowledge will answer them.

sections.heading: Five things a specification specialist can produce on request
paragraphs: Credentials are easy to assert and slow to check. Artefacts are neither. A teacher who genuinely prepares candidates for a particular code has a small number of concrete things lying around, and asking for any of them is a faster filter than any conversation about philosophy or experience. None of the five below takes a competent tutor more than a few minutes to supply, and none of them can be improvised convincingly by somebody who knows the subject but not the paper.

The most useful is an annotated mark scheme extract: a six-mark question with the scheme beside it and a note on which statements earn which marks. A specialist will tell you immediately that the scheme awards a point for naming a quantity, another for stating the relationship and another for the direction of change, and that a fluent paragraph missing one of those three scores two out of three. A generalist talks about explaining clearly. The gap between those two answers is the gap between grades.

The second is a component map for your child's code, which is simply the specification's own structure written out. The third is a worked example of how a loss would be attributed to an assessment objective. The fourth is a short description of what the examination supplies. The fifth is the single thing that most distinguishes the two boards in that subject, which a tutor who prepares candidates for both will answer without pausing and a tutor who has only ever taught one will answer vaguely or not at all.

A family should ask for these before paying for anything, including before a trial lesson. A tutor who supplies them has demonstrated the only thing that matters at this stage. A tutor who responds with reassurance has also told you something, and it is worth hearing.

sections.heading: What the school already holds, and how to ask for it
paragraphs: Families buy tuition before asking the school for information that is free, and then pay a tutor to reconstruct it. The school holds the entry form with the code and the tier, the component list it has entered the student for, the mock papers and the marks, the scheme of work with its sequence and timing, and in most cases a predicted grade with a rationale behind it. All of that is available on request, and all of it makes a first tuition session shorter and sharper.

The requests worth making in writing are specific. Which board and code is my child entered for in each subject? Which tier or route, and by when is that decision reversible? Which components, including any practical or endorsement element? May we have the marked mock script rather than the percentage? And what is the sequence for the remainder of the course, so support can run ahead of the class rather than behind it. Asking in writing matters because a verbal answer in a corridor cannot be checked later.

There is a second reason to ask, which is that the answers sometimes reveal the real problem. A student struggling in a subject they are entered for at Core tier is in a different situation from one struggling at Extended: the ceiling is already set and the honest conversation is about whether the tier is right while it can still be changed. A student entered for combined sciences who is being taught from single-science material at home is being set work that will not be examined.

None of this makes the school an adversary. International schools in the Kingdom set their own calendars and their own sequences, and a tutor working against a school's timing rather than with it creates confusion for the student. The useful arrangement is one where the tutor knows what the class will cover next month, and teaches the prerequisite now.

sections.heading: What the advertised rate bands in the Kingdom buy by way of evidence
paragraphs: Advertised rates in Saudi tutoring span a wide range and the published numbers are easy to find. Budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one online from around SAR 35 an hour. A general online tutoring listing starts near SAR 55 for a non-specialist. A tutor-marketplace guide puts senior-school examination subjects in Riyadh at SAR 200 and above, while tutoring companies listing IB subject support advertise from about SAR 180, with premium Higher Level tracks around SAR 200 to 220. International providers quoting in dollars publish near $60 an hour. Those are vendor-advertised figures, not a market average, and none of them is IB Gram's price.

Read as prices those numbers are confusing. Read as a question about evidence they become clear. The useful question is not what an hour costs but what verification comes with it. At the lowest advertised bands the hour is usually all you get: a session, delivered, with no marked script, no objective-level attribution and frequently no stated knowledge of which board the student is entered for. That can still be worth buying for a student who needs explanation of content they have simply not understood.

What the higher bands are being paid for is partly scarcity and partly work that happens outside the lesson. Marking a timed section against the published scheme, attributing losses to objectives and writing it up takes a specialist the better part of an hour for a single paper. A tutor who does that is selling two things and charging for one and a half. The weight of the drivers, in order, is subject scarcity, examining or marking experience, level, whether the tutor travels, and package length.

So the comparison to make is not riyals against riyals. It is riyals against the artefacts that come back. A lower rate with an annotated script every fortnight is better evidence, and usually a better purchase, than a higher rate with a warm verbal summary. Families comparing a dollar-quoted provider should also compare what leaves the account rather than what appears on the website, since an exchange spread and a cross-border fee are real money.

sections.heading: When a mark starts to be evidence: the year group question
paragraphs: The honest answer to when tuition should start is that it depends on when usable evidence first exists. In Year 9 or the equivalent Middle Years Programme stage, there is no specification yet and no component to measure against. What can be built is the foundation that later marks depend on: algebraic fluency, the ability to write a paragraph that explains rather than describes, and the habit of showing working. Those are worth attention and they are not an IGCSE tuition brief.

The first usable measurement normally arrives a term or so into the course, once the class has covered enough content for a past-paper section to be meaningful. Before that point a full paper produces a demoralising number and very little information, because most losses are simply content not yet taught. A good first intervention at that stage is a single section under timed conditions, marked properly, used to establish how the student handles the question types rather than how much they know.

By the second year the evidence is rich and the clock is the constraint. A student a few months from a June sitting should be working from full timed papers, with the plan prioritised by marks available rather than by syllabus order, and with the uncomfortable discipline of spending most time on the component that carries the most weight. This is where an intensive finite block earns its place, and where a tutor who starts at the beginning of the syllabus is making an expensive mistake.

Resit candidates are a separate case with better evidence than anyone. A November-series candidate already has a component-level profile from a real examination, which is the most informative document in this whole discussion. The first session should be spent on that profile and on the question of whether the lost marks are recoverable in the time available, which sometimes they are not. Saying so is more useful than selling the block.

sections.heading: After IGCSE: what these grades are evidence of, and to whom
paragraphs: IGCSE grades do two different jobs depending on where a student is heading, and families in the Kingdom often need both. Inside Saudi Arabia, the document that matters for university entry is the final secondary school certificate, and a foreign or international certificate requires an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. That applies to an IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike. IGCSE results sit underneath that as the record of the years before.

Alongside the certificate, Saudi universities use the Qiyas tests run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content and is sat in Arabic or English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers science-stream subjects, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That last detail is the one international-curriculum families are most often surprised by: the material overlaps with what a Cambridge or Edexcel student has studied, but the framing does not.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school results with those tests, and the weightings differ by university and by programme, with competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes leaning hardest on Tahsili. The numbers are not for a tutoring page to quote: they move, they differ between institutions, and third-party sites contradict each other. A family should read the criteria on the university's own site, and should check whether a maximum age applies to the certificate they intend to submit. Nobody can promise an admission outcome.

For an application made outside the Kingdom the picture is simpler and the IGCSE profile matters more directly. Overseas universities read post-16 results first, but a subject-by-subject record at sixteen is often what a selector uses to judge whether a stated subject prerequisite is genuinely supported. The practical advice is dull and useful: keep the statement of results, keep the certificate, and keep a note of which board each subject was taken with, because reconstructing that four years later is tedious.

sections.heading: The claim nobody in this market can evidence
paragraphs: Every provider in the Saudi IGCSE market makes a results claim of some kind, and almost none of them can be verified. A pass rate, a satisfaction score, a star rating or a count of successful students is a number produced by the organisation quoting it, from a sample it selected, with no stated method and usually no date. It is not evidence in any sense a parent should accept. It is also unnecessary, because a provider has access to a much better argument.

The better argument is a method. What will be measured, against which component, how often, and what will be shown to the family. A provider who answers that has committed to something falsifiable: if the annotated scripts do not arrive, or the losses are never attributed, the family can see it within a month. A provider who answers with a percentage has committed to nothing at all, and a family cannot check it even in principle.

This matters more online than in person, because the usual informal checks are missing. A parent cannot see the tutor's manner across a kitchen table or hear the lesson from the hallway. What replaces those cues is paperwork: the component map, the marked script, the objective-level note, the six-week review. Families who insist on those artefacts get a readable record. Families who accept reassurance instead often cannot tell whether a term of lessons achieved anything.

So the final piece of advice on this page is a refusal. Do not ask a provider how good they are, because the answer is predictable and unverifiable. Ask what they will send you after each session, what they will send after a month, and what they would say to you if the marks had not moved. The third question is the revealing one, and a tutor who has a real answer to it is worth more than any statistic.

process.title: Send the code, not the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is the board and code for each subject, the tier or route, and the component list from the school's entry form. If the family does not have those, the first task is getting them in writing from the school. A subject name alone is not enough to match a tutor correctly, and matching on it is how preparation ends up aimed at the wrong paper.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a diagnosis
process.description: One session with the matched tutor, built around a section of a real past paper under something close to timed conditions. The output is a short written diagnosis: which objectives the losses sat in, what the first six sessions will address, and what evidence will show whether it worked. Nothing is owed if the family does not continue.

process.title: Fix the slot in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: The weekly slot is set in Saudi local time, not the tutor's, so it holds when another country changes its clocks. Most families place it on a Sunday-to-Thursday evening around the school run, and leave Friday and Saturday for the longer timed papers that need an uninterrupted stretch.

process.title: Teach, then mark, then start from the script
process.description: The lesson teaches; the marking between lessons produces the evidence. Timed work goes back annotated against the published mark scheme, with losses attributed to assessment objectives, and the next session opens on that script. This cycle is what makes month-to-month movement visible rather than a matter of opinion.

process.title: Review at six sessions against the opening paper
process.description: The review compares marks on comparable work rather than impressions, and names one of three outcomes: continue, change the target objective, or stop because the gap has closed. If the marks have not moved, the review says so and explains what we think the cause is, including the possibility that the match is wrong.

whyPoints.title: Matched on a code and a component list
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed against the board, code, tier and components on the school's entry form, not against a subject name. It is a narrower match and it sometimes means the answer is that the right specialist is not free at the slot you wanted, which we say rather than substituting someone and hoping.

whyPoints.title: Marked scripts, not percentages
whyPoints.description: Timed work comes back annotated against the published mark scheme with losses attributed to assessment objectives. A percentage tells a family almost nothing; an annotated script tells them which six weeks of teaching to buy next. It also makes the tutor's own judgement checkable.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, pinned to Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The gain is the pool: a family in Al Ahsa or Jazan chooses from everyone who teaches their code rather than from whoever is nearby.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line on assessed work is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches method, reviews what a student has produced and gives feedback on it. A tutor does not produce coursework, a portfolio piece or any assessed component on a student's behalf. We state that in advance because the alternative is sold openly in this market and it puts the student's own entry at risk.

whyPoints.title: No unverifiable statistics anywhere
whyPoints.description: There is no pass rate, star rating or success percentage on this page, because none of those could be verified by a family reading it. What we offer instead is a method: what will be measured, how often, and what arrives in writing. That is checkable within a month, which a statistic never is.

whyPoints.title: Series and deadlines handled accurately
whyPoints.description: Saudi candidates sit the June and November series. The February/March series is sat in India only, and quoting its deadlines to a Saudi family is a wrong fact they would act on. Exact entry dates come from the school's examinations officer, and we send families there rather than inventing a date.

faqs.question: Who issues the equivalency decision on an international school certificate, and what does a family hand over?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education issues the equivalency, or mu'adalah, decision that allows a Saudi university to treat a foreign or international secondary certificate as equivalent to the Saudi one. The family submits the certificate itself along with supporting documentation the Ministry specifies, and the requirements can include authentication of documents issued abroad. Because the required paperwork changes and differs by country of issue, the current list should be read from the Ministry's own published guidance rather than from a tutoring site. The practical advice is to keep originals and board-issued statements of results in one place from the IGCSE years onward.

faqs.question: What does the equivalency decision do that an IGCSE statement of results cannot?
faqs.answer: Different things entirely. An IGCSE statement of results records subject grades at sixteen, and no Saudi university treats it as a school-leaving certificate. The equivalency decision attaches to the final secondary certificate, whether that is an IB Diploma, A Levels or an American high school diploma, and it is what makes that certificate usable in a Saudi university application. IGCSE results sit underneath as the earlier record. They matter for post-16 subject choices and sometimes for demonstrating a subject prerequisite, but they are not the document the equivalency process is about.

faqs.question: Why does Tahsili feel unfamiliar to a student with strong Cambridge science grades?
faqs.answer: Because its content follows the Saudi national curriculum rather than an international specification. The Achievement Test covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and a student who has studied those subjects on a Cambridge or Pearson route has met most of the underlying material. What differs is the framing: the order topics are introduced in, the terminology, the balance between them, and the question style. Strong grades are a good foundation and not a substitute for preparation against the actual syllabus the test is built on. Families should read the official description of coverage rather than relying on third-party summaries.

faqs.question: Does Qudurat test anything an IGCSE candidate has already been taught to do?
faqs.answer: Partly, but not as a subject. The General Aptitude Test assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, so there is no chapter to revise. What transfers from an IGCSE course is the underlying arithmetic and algebraic fluency, the ability to read a question precisely and the habit of working at speed under timed conditions. It is sat in Arabic or English, and the language choice is a real decision for a student schooled in English. Preparation is about question types and timing rather than about content coverage.

faqs.question: Which records from the IGCSE years should a family keep for an application made years later?
faqs.answer: The board-issued statement of results and the certificate itself, for every subject, plus a note of which board and code each subject was taken under. That last item sounds trivial and is the one families cannot reconstruct later, particularly where a school entered some subjects with Cambridge and others with Pearson Edexcel. Keep anything the school issued showing the component list or tier as well. Universities inside and outside the Kingdom ask for documents in different forms, and having originals and clear records in one place saves weeks at the point of application.

faqs.question: Can a student apply to a Saudi university and an overseas one in the same cycle?
faqs.answer: Yes, and many families in the Kingdom do, but the two routes need different preparation running in parallel. The Saudi route depends on the final certificate, its equivalency decision and the Qiyas tests, with each university publishing its own criteria. The overseas route depends mainly on post-16 results, predicted grades and whatever subject prerequisites the course states. The timetables do not align, so the practical task is a calendar built backwards from both sets of deadlines. Nobody can promise an outcome on either route, and the criteria should be read from each institution's own published pages.

faqs.question: How old can a secondary certificate be before a Saudi university stops accepting it?
faqs.answer: Some universities state a maximum age for the secondary certificate they will accept, and the limit is set by the institution rather than by one national rule. This catches families who intended a gap year, or who return to study after working. Because the rule differs by university and by programme, and because it occasionally changes, the only reliable source is the admission criteria published by the university the student is applying to. It is worth checking before a deliberate pause rather than afterwards, since the decision is hard to reverse.

faqs.question: At what point in the first IGCSE year does a mark become evidence rather than noise?
faqs.answer: Usually about a term into the course, once the class has covered enough content for a past-paper section to be meaningful. Before that, a full paper mostly measures what has not been taught yet, which produces a low number and almost no information. The better early measurement is a single section under timed conditions, marked against the published scheme, used to see how the student handles the question types. That tells a tutor something actionable while the content coverage is still incomplete.

faqs.question: What should a Middle Years Programme student have on paper before an IGCSE course begins?
faqs.answer: Not IGCSE content. Three things that later marks depend on: algebraic fluency to the point where rearranging an equation is automatic, the ability to write a paragraph that explains a mechanism rather than describing a situation, and the habit of showing working so that method credit is available. A criterion-assessed student also benefits from meeting a published mark scheme for the first time, because allocating points to specific statements is a different discipline from writing against criterion descriptors.

faqs.question: What is the earliest honest point at which online tuition can be judged to be working?
faqs.answer: Six sessions, measured against comparable work. The comparison has to be like for like: a section of similar difficulty, marked the same way, with losses attributed to the same objectives. A single better mark proves nothing, because paper difficulty and the student's day both vary. What should be visible after six sessions is movement in the specific objective that was targeted, plus a readable trail of annotated scripts. If neither exists, the honest conclusion is that the arrangement has not produced evidence, whatever the student reports about the lessons.

faqs.question: A candidate is three months from the June papers - what should the first session produce?
faqs.answer: A full timed paper and a prioritised list. At that distance there is no time to work through a syllabus in order, so the opening session establishes where the marks are actually being lost and the plan is then sequenced by marks available rather than by topic order. That often means spending most of the remaining time on the component with the heaviest weighting, even when it is the one the student likes least. It should also produce an honest statement of what is not recoverable in the time, which is information a family can use.

faqs.question: What should a November-series resit candidate bring to a first lesson?
faqs.answer: The component-level breakdown from the examination they already sat, which is the most informative document in any of these conversations. It shows exactly which papers and which question types cost the grade, from a real sitting rather than a mock. The first session should be spent reading it and deciding whether the lost marks are recoverable in the weeks available. Sometimes they are not, and a tutor who says so has given better advice than one who sells a block. Entry arrangements for the November series come from the school's examinations officer.

faqs.question: Does a student need support in every weak subject at once, or is there an order?
faqs.answer: There is an order, and it is usually not the order of weakness. Take the subject where the heaviest-weighted component is also the one being failed, because that is where a given hour buys the most marks. Take subjects with a practical or coursework element earlier, since those have internal deadlines that cannot be moved. Leave until last any subject where the problem is content not yet taught, because the class will cover it. Running three subjects in parallel usually produces three shallow efforts; two done properly beats it.

faqs.question: What verification should a family expect at the lowest advertised online IGCSE rates?
faqs.answer: Honestly, very little beyond the lesson itself. Budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35 an hour, and at that band the hour is generally the whole product: a session delivered, sometimes recorded, often without any stated knowledge of which board the student is entered for. For a student who simply has not understood content, that can still be worth buying. What it will not include is marked timed work, attribution of losses to assessment objectives, or preparation aimed at a specific component. Those are the things that cost a specialist time outside the lesson.

faqs.question: Why would a Further Pure Mathematics tutor cost more than a Business Studies one?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, which is the heaviest driver of rate in this market. Further Pure Mathematics sits well beyond the standard course, covering calculus, matrices and series, and the number of teachers in or reachable from the Kingdom who prepare candidates for it is small. Business Studies has a far larger pool. Nothing about the Business specification is easier to teach well, and a specialist in its application and evaluation marks is genuinely valuable. The rate is reporting on availability rather than on difficulty, which is worth knowing before reading a high number as a quality signal.

faqs.question: Is marking between lessons charged separately, and what should it produce?
faqs.answer: Arrangements differ, so ask before the first session whether marking is included in the hourly rate or billed on top. What matters more is what comes back. A useful marking cycle returns an annotated script showing where each mark was awarded or withheld against the published scheme, with losses grouped by assessment objective and a one-line target for the next session. A percentage and a tick are not marking in any useful sense. A tutor who marks properly spends close to an hour on a single paper, which is why the question of how it is charged is a fair one.

faqs.question: How should a family compare a riyal rate with a provider quoting in dollars?
faqs.answer: Compare what leaves the bank account, not what appears on the page. International providers advertise near $60 an hour, and that arrives on a Saudi card with an exchange spread and sometimes a cross-border transaction fee, so the effective riyal cost is higher than a straight conversion suggests. Ask what the charge looks like on a statement, and ask in which currency a package is denominated if the rate moves. None of this makes a foreign provider the wrong choice; it just means the comparison needs to be made on settled amounts rather than on headline numbers.

faqs.question: Does a free trial lesson produce anything the family keeps if they do not continue?
faqs.answer: It should. The trial here is built around a section of a real past paper, and the output is a short written diagnosis the family keeps either way: which objectives the lost marks sat in, what the first six sessions would have addressed, and what evidence would have shown whether it worked. A family that walks away still has a usable reading of where their child stands. A trial that produces only a pleasant conversation and a quote has given nothing away, which is itself a reasonable signal.

igcse-online-tuition.closingHeading: Send the code and the last marked paper
igcse-online-tuition.closingBody: The two things that make a first conversation useful are the board and code from the school's entry form, and the most recent marked script rather than its percentage. With those we can match a tutor who prepares candidates for that specification and arrange a free trial lesson built around a real section of a paper. You keep the written diagnosis whether or not you continue. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, pinned to Arabia Standard Time, with timed work marked against the published scheme between sessions. If no specialist for your code is free at the slot you need, we will tell you that instead of offering a substitute.

igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are listed by syllabus rather than by subject name, because Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 are not the same examination and a Core entry is not an Extended one. Each teaches a small number of codes, at the tier your child is actually sitting, and marks written work between lessons.

intro.heading: Marks are lost in a small number of predictable places
paragraphs: An IGCSE grade is not a measure of how much a student knows. It is a measure of how many marks they collected, and those two things come apart in ways that are consistent enough to list. A student who understands electrolysis perfectly can lose most of the marks on an electrolysis question by describing what happens instead of explaining why. A student who can solve a quadratic can lose half the marks by writing only the answer. Neither problem is a knowledge gap, and neither is fixed by covering more syllabus.

That is why this page is organised around failure rather than around content. The sections work through the places marks actually go missing, subject by subject: the command term that was not answered, the method line that was never written down, the unit that was dropped, the practical paper nobody rehearsed, the data-response question answered with everything the student knows rather than with what was asked. Each of those is diagnosable from a marked script, and each has a different fix.

The second organising idea is the clock. An IGCSE course runs across two years and ends in a series, and the usefulness of any intervention depends on how far from that series it happens. Rebuilding algebra is a Year 10 purchase. Rehearsing the alternative-to-practical paper is a final-term one. Doing those two in the wrong order is the most common way families in the Kingdom spend money without moving a grade, and there is a section further down that sets the year out backwards for exactly that reason.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video, with the past paper on a shared screen so it can be annotated as it is worked through and kept afterwards. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For IGCSE that arrangement has a particular advantage, because the match can be made on the syllabus code rather than on geography, and a family in Tabuk or Najran has the same choice of a Physics 0625 specialist as a family in Riyadh.

Everything here applies to candidates across the Kingdom, from the Riyadh and Jeddah school clusters to the Dammam, Dhahran and Al Khobar conurbation and the smaller centres where there may be only one international school within reach. The further a family is from a large school market, the more the online argument rests on supply rather than convenience: there may be no specialist in the subject within driving distance at all. One further thing applies everywhere in the Kingdom, and it is worth stating before anything else. Candidates here sit the June series as their main one and the November series for resits and late entries, and the school's examinations officer holds the entry deadlines, the tier decisions and the statement of entry that says which papers your child is actually sitting. Every recommendation on this page assumes you have read that document.

igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Four things sit under the single word IGCSE as families in the Kingdom use it: the two boards most schools here enter candidates with, the lower secondary years that decide whether the course starts from a solid base, and the two routes out of it. Support looks different in each, and the differences are mostly about assessment rather than content.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely entered international qualification in Saudi schools, taken subject by subject and reported on an A* to G scale. Many subjects are tiered, so a candidate is entered for either Core papers, which cap the grade available, or Extended papers. Science subjects add a practical component taken as either a practical test or a written alternative paper.
programmes.countryNote: Across the Kingdom, Cambridge is the default for British-curriculum schools from Riyadh to the Eastern Province, and the codes on the statement of entry matter more than the board name. Two schools in the same city can enter candidates for different tiers in the same subject, which is why support should be bought against the code and tier rather than the subject.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The second route, reported on a 9 to 1 scale, with codes beginning 4 such as 4MA1 for Mathematics and 4PH1 for Physics. Tiering exists in mathematics but the structure differs from Cambridge, and the sciences assess practical skills through written questions about experiments rather than through a separate practical component.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in the Kingdom run a mixed entry, with mathematics and sciences on one board and languages or humanities on the other. A tutor who assumes the wrong board teaches the wrong paper structure, which is a real and avoidable waste of an hour. Check the codes on the entry statement before the first lesson.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The years in which the foundations the IGCSE course assumes are either built or missed: algebraic manipulation, scientific vocabulary and method, extended writing, and the habit of showing working. There is no external series at this stage, which is exactly why gaps here are invisible until a Year 10 test exposes them.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the Kingdom often arrive mid-way through these years, from a national-curriculum school, from the Middle Years Programme, or from an American or Indian system. The content gap is usually narrower than the assessment gap, and a term of work in Year 9 is worth considerably more than the same term in Year 11.

programmes.name: After IGCSE: A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE results decide which sixth-form routes are open. A Level courses typically expect particular grades in the subject; the IB Diploma expects six subjects at once and introduces internal assessment, Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, none of which an IGCSE candidate has met in that form before.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom both routes lead through Ministry of Education equivalency before a Saudi university treats the certificate as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and most Saudi university programmes also expect the Qiyas tests. Those are processes to understand in the final school years rather than after results, and they sit outside what any tutor controls.

igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Cambridge codes Saudi schools enter candidates for most often, written around where the marks go missing rather than around what the topic list contains. Each note is a failure mode a tutor can diagnose from a marked script in a single session.

subjects.name: Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Each tier now carries a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper of equal weight, which exposes students who have practised entirely with a calculator in hand. The larger loss is method: on a multi-step question most of the marks sit in the working, so an answer written alone earns almost nothing even when it is correct.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by stronger candidates, and far less forgiving. Calculus, logarithms, trigonometric identities and vectors arrive quickly, and weak algebraic manipulation from Year 9 shows up here rather than in 0580. Students who cope by pattern-matching worked examples stall on the first unfamiliar arrangement of the same idea.

subjects.name: Physics 0625
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper, an extended theory paper and a practical component. Marks go missing on units and significant figures, and on explanation questions where a candidate describes the shape of a graph without accounting for its gradient or intercept. The six-mark extended response rewards a sequence of linked statements, not a list of facts.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry decide most boundary cases. The predictable losses are unbalanced equations, missing state symbols, and qualitative analysis answers that give a conclusion without naming the reagent and the observation that produced it. The mark scheme wants the sequence, in order.

subjects.name: Biology 0610
subjects.description: Definitions are marked against wording rather than approximation, and osmosis, diffusion and active transport are the ones most often conflated. Labelled diagrams and data-handling questions are the most predictable marks on the paper and the most often rushed. Genetics and transport carry the Extended tier and are usually taught last.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Three sciences in two IGCSE grades' worth of teaching time, which means the content is compressed rather than reduced in difficulty. Students lose marks because a topic was covered once and never revisited, and because the paper moves between the three disciplines faster than a single-subject paper does.

subjects.name: First Language English 0500
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing in one paper and composition in the other. The directed-writing task is where marks disappear: candidates summarise the passage instead of writing for the audience, purpose and form the question specified. Timing is the other recurring loss, because the reading questions reward re-reading that students do not budget for.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: Reading and writing, listening, and speaking, with the two codes differing in how speaking is reported. Fluent speakers at English-medium Saudi schools still lose marks here, because the examination tests exercise technique, register and summary skills rather than conversation. The summary task is the single most trainable component on the paper.

subjects.name: Economics 0455
subjects.description: Structured questions and data response, assessed in a fixed order: define, draw where a diagram applies, explain, then evaluate. Candidates who write everything they know about the topic and never address the command term lose marks on every paper in this subject. Evaluation means a judgement with a reason attached, not a final paragraph of hedging.

subjects.name: Business Studies 0450
subjects.description: Case-study driven, and the loss is almost always application. An answer that explains a concept accurately but never refers to the business in the stimulus forfeits the application and evaluation marks, which together outweigh the knowledge marks. Candidates need to be taught to quote the case back at the examiner.

subjects.name: Computer Science 0478
subjects.description: Theory and problem-solving, with pseudocode and trace tables assessed on paper rather than at a keyboard. Students who can write working code in an editor lose marks on hand-written pseudocode and on questions that ask for a dry run of an algorithm, because the paper rewards a formal notation they have rarely practised.

subjects.name: Geography 0460
subjects.description: Case studies, skills and data interpretation. Marks are lost on skills questions that require accurate measurement or map reading, and on extended answers that describe a pattern without explaining the process behind it. Named examples carry marks of their own, and vague references to a region rather than a place do not.

igcse-online-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: The same subjects on Pearson Edexcel differ in code, structure and sometimes in tiering, and a school may enter candidates with both boards in the same year group. These are the Edexcel codes that come up most often in Saudi schools.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics A 4MA1
igcseSubjects.description: Two calculator papers of equal weight at the entered tier, which makes it structurally different from the current Cambridge arrangement. The Higher tier reaches further into algebra and trigonometry than many candidates expect from the early units, and method marks are allocated in the same unforgiving way: no working, no credit.

igcseSubjects.name: Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1
igcseSubjects.description: An extension qualification taken alongside 4MA1 by candidates heading for A Level mathematics or Higher Level in the Diploma. Calculus and series arrive early and the questions are longer, so stamina and layout matter. Weak algebraic fluency is exposed immediately rather than gradually.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics 4PH1 and Chemistry 4CH1
igcseSubjects.description: Practical skills are assessed through written questions about experiments rather than through a separate practical component, so candidates must be able to describe apparatus, variables, precautions and sources of error in prose. Students taught practical work only as demonstration lose these marks consistently.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology 4BI1
igcseSubjects.description: Content organised differently from the Cambridge specification, which matters when a family switches school or board mid-course. Required practicals and data analysis carry real weight, and the extended questions reward linked reasoning across topics rather than recall of a single section.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language A 4EA1
igcseSubjects.description: Non-fiction and transactional writing, with an anthology of set texts. Candidates lose marks by writing about the writer's technique in the abstract rather than showing the effect of a specific choice on a reader, and by misjudging form in the transactional task.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics 4EC1 and Business 4BS1
igcseSubjects.description: Data response and extended evaluation, with quantitative skills examined explicitly. The failure mode mirrors Cambridge: strong content, no judgement. A candidate who cannot weigh two sides and commit to a conclusion caps their grade regardless of how much theory they can recall.

igcse-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Where IGCSE candidates in the Kingdom are, and what supply looks like
igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Specialist supply is unevenly distributed across the Kingdom, and that distribution is the honest reason online teaching matters more in some places than others. Below is what families in each part of the country tend to be working with when they look for a subject specialist at IGCSE level.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The largest school market in the Kingdom, with a correspondingly larger pool of teachers. Even here the constraint is availability rather than existence: the specialists are employed full time, and a family searching locally is choosing among people free in a narrow evening window after a long school run.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine of schools running from the historic centre north towards Obhur, with both British-curriculum and IB provision. Journey times along that spine are the practical limit on an in-home arrangement, which is why evening slots here are usually set later than parents first propose.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market across three cities, with families regularly living in one and schooling in another. The density of British-curriculum provision is good; the number of specialists free at six in the evening after their own teaching day is not.

regions.name: Jubail and the industrial north east
regions.note: A smaller cluster serving industrial and camp communities, where a school may be the only one offering a particular subject. Where a subject is not offered, or is offered with a single small class, an outside specialist is sometimes the only route to taking it at all.

regions.name: Makkah, Madinah and Taif
regions.note: International provision is thinner and more dispersed than on the coast or in the capital, and the calendar bends around the Hajj and Umrah seasons in Makkah in ways families plan their year around. Online lessons remove the travel question from an already busy week.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Two towns about twenty five kilometres apart in 'Asir, at altitude, sharing a catchment. The local pool of IGCSE subject specialists is small, so a family looking for Physics 0625 or Additional Mathematics 0606 specifically is usually looking outside the region whether they intended to or not.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: The north west, with a growing number of relocating families and limited established international provision. Mid-course arrivals are common here, which means diagnostics against a new school's scheme of work matter more than general subject support.

regions.name: Al Ahsa, Buraidah, Ha'il, Najran and Jazan
regions.note: Inland and southern centres where distance, not price, is the binding constraint. For a family here the choice is rarely between an in-home tutor and an online one; it is between an online specialist and no specialist in that subject at all.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of British-curriculum entries in the Kingdom, with Cambridge dominant and some schools running mixed board entries by department. Term dates are set school by school, so two candidates sitting the same June papers may have had very different amounts of teaching by the spring.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: A long-established international school market with British, IB, German, American and Indian provision along the coastal spine, and Thuwal to the north serving the KAUST campus community. Board choice varies by school and sometimes by subject within a school.

Dammam, Dhahran, Al Khobar and Jubail behave as one school market, with British-curriculum and IB provision close together and camp communities running their own calendars. Families here commute across city boundaries as a matter of routine.

igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Which arrangement is right depends on which failure mode is costing the marks. A content gap, a technique problem and an untested practical component need different patterns of teaching, and buying the wrong pattern is how a term of lessons produces no change in a grade.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a single code
modes.description: One named hour a week on one syllabus code, held for the term, with written work set between lessons and marked against the published scheme before the next session. This is the pattern for a genuine content gap, where the student needs teaching rather than rehearsal, and it is the only one that reliably changes a grade from a long way out.

modes.title: Paper-technique sessions
modes.description: Shorter, sharper work for a student whose content is broadly sound and whose marks are being lost on command terms, method lines, timing or presentation. Sessions are built around whole papers and part-papers under timed conditions, then marked line by line against the scheme so the student sees exactly where a mark was available and not taken.
bullets: Timed papers, marked against the published scheme

modes.title: Practical and alternative-paper preparation
modes.description: Focused work on the component families most often ignore. For Cambridge science candidates this is the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper; for Edexcel candidates it is the written practical questions. It covers apparatus, variables, precautions, sources of error, tabulation and graph work, all of which are examinable in prose.

modes.title: Resit and November-series work
modes.description: For a candidate retaking in November, or entering then after a disrupted year. The plan starts from the statement of results rather than the overall grade, because a theory loss and a practical or coursework loss need entirely different work, and some marks may be carried forward rather than retaken.
