sections.heading: Entries, series and the resit route
paragraphs: Both boards run a June series, which is the main sitting for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and for candidates entering late in a cycle. Entries close well ahead of each series and your school's examinations officer holds the exact dates; a date published on a tutoring website is the wrong source for something a family acts on. The practical rule is that anything requiring a change of entry, of tier or of syllabus has to be raised a long time before the papers.

Cambridge also runs a February and March series, and it is available only in India, so a candidate in Saudi Arabia sits June or November. This matters because a great deal of IGCSE revision content online is written for Indian candidates and assumes a timetable that does not apply here. A family planning backwards from the wrong series will start an intensive block at the wrong time by several months.

The resit route is worth understanding before results arrive rather than after. A candidate who misses a required grade can usually re-enter for the next series, and the useful question is which components went wrong rather than whether the whole course needs repeating. Where a board publishes component-level information to the school, that is the sharpest diagnostic available and it is worth asking the school to share what it has before planning any teaching.

Two further mechanisms are worth knowing. A remark is a review of marking rather than a second chance, and schools weigh whether a result sits close enough to a boundary to justify one. Grade boundaries themselves move between series, because they are set after the papers to account for difficulty, which is why a raw mark from a past paper is only a rough guide to a grade. Any revision plan built on an assumed boundary rather than on the components should be treated carefully.
bullets: June is the main series in the Kingdom; November carries resits and late entries
Your examinations officer holds the entry dates; no website should be your source
The February and March series is an India-only sitting
Ask the school for component-level information before planning a resit
Boundaries are set after each series, so a past-paper mark is a guide, not a grade

sections.heading: What happens to an IGCSE record afterwards: the Diploma, A Levels and the university pathway
paragraphs: An IGCSE is a stepping stone rather than a destination, and the choices made inside it decide what the next two years can look like. Sixth forms and Diploma schools set entry requirements by subject grade, and in mathematics and the sciences the depth of the course taken matters as much as the grade. A student who took the standard mathematics route and scored well can still find Higher Level Analysis and Approaches or A Level Mathematics a steep first term, which is the practical argument for Additional Mathematics beforehand.

Inside the Kingdom, the qualification that eventually needs attention is the secondary leaving certificate rather than the IGCSE. An IB Diploma, a set of A Levels or an American high school diploma all require an equivalency decision, mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats the certificate as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The IGCSE sits below that point and functions as a foundation and an entry requirement, so families should keep the certificates and transcripts from both stages, since the later application generally asks for the full school record.

Alongside equivalency sit the two Qiyas tests, administered by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content and is available in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum. That is the sentence that matters for an international-curriculum family: the subjects are familiar and the framing is not, which is why students who did well in their own examinations can find Tahsili unexpectedly hard.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school results with the Qiyas tests, and the weightings differ by university and by programme, with competitive science and health programmes leaning hardest on Tahsili. No threshold or formula appears on this page, because they vary by institution and cycle and a number quoted here would mislead somebody. Read the university's own published criteria, check whether a maximum certificate age applies, and treat Tahsili preparation as a separate block of work rather than as revision of what the student already covered.

sections.heading: What to ask before paying for anything
paragraphs: The claims in this market cannot be verified by a parent. Success percentages, star ratings and headcounts of tutors are self-reported, carry no sample size, date or method, and should be treated as marketing rather than information. What a parent can assess is the specificity of the answers a provider gives to questions about their own child, and those questions are easy to ask.

Ask which board and which syllabus code the tutor teaches, and which tier. Ask whether they have marked for a board, and what that taught them about where candidates lose marks; a real answer is usually specific and slightly unflattering about typical candidates. Ask what the first month covers, in order. Ask how written work is marked between sessions, how quickly it comes back, and what the parent receives afterwards. Then ask the question that separates a teacher from a salesperson: having seen this past paper, where are the marks actually going?

A good answer names a component and a pattern, and says what will not be achievable in the time available. A poor answer talks about confidence and potential without naming a part of the course. Both can be delivered politely by a well-organised company, which is why the question has to be about the student's own paper rather than about the provider's process.

Finally, settle the practical terms before the first lesson rather than during the first disagreement: what happens if the match is wrong after two sessions, what notice a cancelled lesson needs, whether a slot can be held through a long holiday, and whether marking between lessons is inside the rate. None of those questions is awkward, and a provider who finds them awkward has answered a different question.
bullets: Ask for the board, the code and the tier, not the subject name
Ask what marking for a board taught them about typical candidates
Ask where the marks are going in your child's own past paper
Ask whether marking between lessons sits inside the hourly rate
Settle cancellation, slot-holding and match-change terms before you start

process.title: Confirm the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Ask the school in writing which board, which syllabus code and which tier your child is entered for in each subject. This single step prevents the most expensive mistake available at IGCSE, which is buying teaching aimed at papers the student is not sitting.

process.title: Send a full past paper, marked
process.description: One complete attempt with the school's marks on it tells a tutor more than a term of reports. It shows whether marks are going on content, on method lines, on units, on timing or on reading the question, and those five problems need five different responses.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson as a working session
process.description: The tutor should name the paper structure for that syllabus, say where this student is losing marks, and set out what the first month covers. If the conversation never reaches a component of the course, ask for a different tutor rather than committing to a term.

process.title: Fix the weekly slot to Saudi local time
process.description: Agree the time in Arabia Standard Time, in writing, so a clock change elsewhere cannot move it. Four weekday evenings are genuinely available against a Sunday-to-Thursday school week, and Friday or Saturday suits a longer session when a student needs one.

process.title: Review against papers, not against feelings
process.description: After four weeks, compare a timed past-paper attempt with the one from the start. Marks on a paper are visible evidence; a sense that things are going better is not. If the agreed measure has not moved, change the approach rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code and tier
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0580 Extended candidate, a 0580 Core candidate and a Pearson 4MA1 Higher candidate are sitting different papers. We match on the entry the school registered, and we work from that board's own past papers and mark schemes rather than from generic revision material written for neither.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before hours
whyPoints.description: The first session establishes whether the problem is a skill gap, a technique gap, a timing gap or genuinely missing content. Families regularly find that eight sessions of algebra repair fixes what looked like weakness in three separate subjects, which is a cheaper answer than the one they expected.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every SAR figure on this page is another company's advertised rate, attributed to the type of source that published it. We do not claim a market average, because none exists in the Kingdom, and we never present a competitor's advertised number as our own price.

whyPoints.title: Written work actually marked
whyPoints.description: Work set between lessons is marked against the published mark scheme and returned before the next session, because marking a full paper properly takes about as long as teaching one. Families should check whether that sits inside any rate they are quoted, including when comparing us with anyone else.

whyPoints.title: Built for the Saudi week
whyPoints.description: Lessons are scheduled against a Sunday-to-Thursday school week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time, which does not change all year. A slot agreed in Saudi local terms survives a tutor's own clock change, and nothing in the arrangement depends on anyone completing a drive first.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no success rates, no ratings and no tutor counts. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the IB, the Ministry of Education or ETEC, and no relationship with any school named here.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge IGCSE grades appear anywhere in a Saudi university application?
faqs.answer: They form part of the school record a university may ask for, but the qualification the domestic process turns on is the secondary leaving certificate: an IB Diploma, A Levels or an American high school diploma. That is the document requiring an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education. IGCSE sits below it, functioning as a foundation and as an entry requirement for the next stage. Keep the statements of results and certificates from both stages, because applications commonly ask for the full record rather than the final document, and replacing a lost certificate years later is slow.

faqs.question: Which Tahsili subjects overlap with an IGCSE science course, and which parts do not?
faqs.answer: Tahsili covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, so the subject list looks familiar to any IGCSE science student. The overlap is in content rather than in framing. Tahsili follows the Saudi national curriculum, which orders topics differently, weights them differently and expects its own notation and conventions. A student who has spent two years on an IGCSE syllabus meets recognisable material presented in an unfamiliar sequence. Treat it as a separate preparation block with its own practice material rather than as revision of what the IGCSE papers already covered.

faqs.question: At what stage is Qudurat usually sat, and does an IGCSE student need it yet?
faqs.answer: Qudurat is a university-entrance test, so it belongs to the end of secondary schooling rather than to the IGCSE stage. A student in Grade 9 or 10 does not need it, and preparing for it then would displace work that matters now. What is worth knowing early is what it measures: verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, available in Arabic or in English. Registration arrangements and available sittings are published by the National Center for Assessment, and families should confirm them directly when the final school years approach.

faqs.question: What do universities outside the Kingdom ask for from a student who sat IGCSEs in Saudi Arabia?
faqs.answer: Almost always the next qualification rather than the IGCSE itself: A Level grades, an IB Diploma score with named Higher Level subjects, or an equivalent. IGCSE results are usually read as supporting evidence, with specific exceptions where a university asks for a particular grade in English or mathematics at that level. Some institutions also use them to judge a profile where the final grades are still predicted. Check each university's stated requirements rather than a general conversion chart, because the treatment of international qualifications differs by country and by course.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE in English as a Second Language count as proof of English for a university application?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is never safe to assume. Some universities accept a specified grade in a recognised English qualification at this level as evidence of language proficiency; others require a separate test regardless of school results. The rule varies by institution, by country and sometimes by course, and it can also differ between First Language English and English as a Second Language. Find the policy on the university's own admissions pages before deciding the route, because the answer may influence whether the school enters the student for one code or the other.

faqs.question: How does a Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sit alongside a Cambridge IGCSE on the same transcript?
faqs.answer: Perfectly normally. Schools mix boards for practical reasons, usually because one board's subject suits the staffing or facilities better, and a transcript carrying both is common. The only thing to manage is the grading scales, since one board reports letters and the other numbers, and an institution that states its requirement in one scale may need the other explained. Keep the statements of results for both, and ask the school to confirm which scale appears on each certificate so that nothing has to be reconstructed later from memory.

faqs.question: When should IGCSE support start for a child in Grade 9 at a Saudi school?
faqs.answer: At the start of Grade 9 if there is a skill gap, and at the start of Grade 10 if the issue is examination technique. Grade 9 is when algebraic weakness can still be repaired cheaply, before it has quietly cost marks in four subjects. It is also when the code and tier decisions are being formed, and when the choice about Additional Mathematics has to be made. Waiting until the final term of Grade 10 narrows the available work to damage limitation, which is a worse use of the same money.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking before the Diploma or A Levels?
faqs.answer: For a student heading towards Higher Level Analysis and Approaches, A Level Mathematics or an engineering pathway, it is one of the most useful decisions available at this stage. It introduces calculus, trigonometric identities and function work a year early, so the first term of the next course stops being a shock. The cost is real: it is an additional syllabus in an already full year, and taking it alongside a shaky 0580 performance is a mistake. Decide on evidence from actual papers rather than on ambition.

faqs.question: What should a student do in the break between finishing IGCSE and starting the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Not a full course, and not nothing. Two pieces of work pay off: closing any algebra or graph-work gap that the IGCSE papers exposed, and a short introduction to how the next qualification is assessed, because command terms and criterion-marked internal assessment are unfamiliar to every IGCSE student. Four to six sessions is usually enough for both. Students who arrive in the first Diploma term already understanding that evaluation earns marks spend that term learning content instead of learning the rules.

faqs.question: How much notice does an IGCSE resit in the November series need?
faqs.answer: More than most families assume, because the constraint is administrative before it is academic. The entry has to be made through a school or an examination centre and entries close well ahead of the series, so the first conversation is with the examinations officer rather than with a tutor. Academically, a single-subject resit needs a schedule built backwards from the papers with no gaps, and it works best when it targets the components that went wrong rather than repeating the whole syllabus. Ask the school for any component-level information it holds first.

faqs.question: My child is in Grade 10 with one weak science. Is moving to the Core route the right call?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what comes next, and the decision should be made with two timed past papers rather than an impression. A solid grade on the lower route is worth more than a poor one above it, unless the sixth form or Diploma school you are aiming at requires a grade only the Extended route can produce, or the next course assumes content only that route covers. Ask the school what evidence the current entry rests on and by when it can change, then put the two papers in front of the student and decide from the marks.

faqs.question: For a Cambridge IGCSE candidate, what belongs in the last stretch before the papers and what does not?
faqs.answer: Three things belong, and new content is not one of them. Full papers under timed conditions, so that pace becomes automatic rather than hopeful. Marking against the published scheme, so the student sees which marks they are leaving behind. And a short list of repeated errors, worked on until they stop. Content teaching at this stage is only worth it for a topic that is genuinely absent and genuinely examinable. The commonest final-term mistake is revising what feels comfortable instead of practising what the paper will actually demand.

faqs.question: Why do advertised IGCSE rates start lower than IB rates in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Because the specialist pool is larger. More teachers can credibly teach an IGCSE syllabus than can teach a Higher Level Diploma subject, and price follows scarcity more closely than it follows effort. Level contributes too: published rates in this market rise from IGCSE through Standard Level to Higher Level. The exceptions sit where the pool narrows again, such as Additional Mathematics or a less widely chosen option, where an IGCSE rate can reach the band advertised for Diploma subjects. Ask any provider which of those factors their number reflects.

faqs.question: Is a two-subject package better value than booking two separate weekly hours?
faqs.answer: Only if the two subjects share a diagnosis. Two sciences failing for the same reason, usually calculation technique or method writing, can genuinely be worked on together. Two unrelated subjects are two separate pieces of work, and a package discount that shortens each of them is a saving on paper and a loss in practice. Ask what each hour will cover, week by week, before accepting a bundled rate, and make sure marking time for both subjects is accounted for rather than quietly absorbed.

faqs.question: What does an intensive block before the June series cost compared with weekly lessons through the year?
faqs.answer: Intensives are priced per hour at a similar level or a little above, because demand rises as a series approaches, and the total is larger simply because the hours are compressed. The real comparison is not financial. Weekly work through the year can build content and technique; an intensive can realistically only sharpen technique, timing and a short list of repeated errors. A family choosing an intensive because the year got away from them should expect a narrower result for a bigger invoice, and plan the targets accordingly.

faqs.question: Why do some providers quote in US dollars, and what does that do to an IGCSE budget?
faqs.answer: International platforms often price centrally in dollars, with rates around sixty dollars an hour appearing on provider sites. For a family budgeting in riyals that introduces a second variable, since the monthly total moves with the exchange rate rather than with the teaching. Ask for the figure in SAR, ask whether it is fixed for the duration of a package, and ask who absorbs any payment or conversion charge. A rate that looks competitive on a provider page can land differently on a bank statement.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper non-specialist tutor ever the right call for IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific job. Homework supervision, keeping a student working through a term, or rebuilding confidence in basic skills does not require somebody who has marked for a board, and the lower end of the advertised market is appropriate for that. What a non-specialist cannot do is read a mark scheme as an examiner reads it, which is exactly what a student loses marks to. Match the purchase to the problem: a skills gap can be cheap to fix, and a technique gap on a specific syllabus cannot.

faqs.question: What should we expect to pay for having a full past paper marked between lessons?
faqs.answer: Marking a complete paper against the published scheme and writing usable feedback takes close to the length of a lesson, so providers handle it in one of three ways: inside the hourly rate, as a separate charge, or not at all. The question to ask is which, because two providers quoting the same hourly figure can differ substantially once a term of marking is counted. Ask how many papers are included, what the turnaround is, and whether the feedback names patterns or simply corrects answers.

igcse-private-tutor.closingHeading: Confirm the entry, then find the leak
igcse-private-tutor.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IGCSE private tutor in Saudi Arabia, two steps come before buying any hours. Ask the school, in writing, which board, which syllabus code and which tier your child is entered for in each subject. Then send one full marked past paper. Between them those two documents say whether the problem is the entry itself, a skill gap underneath several subjects, method marks being left on the page, or simply the clock. A free trial lesson with a specialist in that exact syllabus will tell you which. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, around the Sunday-to-Thursday week.

igcse-summer-tuition.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors families ask for after reading a mock script: IGCSE subject specialists who name the syllabus code, the component list and the tier before they say anything about price.

intro.heading: The hourly rate is the least informative number in an IGCSE summer quote
paragraphs: Advertised rates for IGCSE tuition in the Kingdom run from about SAR 35 an hour on budget online platforms to above SAR 200 for senior-school examination subjects, and every provider across that range describes what it sells as IGCSE tuition. Those are published advertised figures taken from vendor pages and tutor-marketplace guides, not a market average and not what any one family pays. The spread is not a sign that somebody is overcharging. It is a sign that the two words cover several different products, and that a holiday block bought on price alone is bought blind. The section below sets the bands out with the kind of source each comes from.

Two quotes at the same number can buy completely different teaching, and over a six-week block there is no time left to discover which one you bought. The question that separates them is narrow: does this tutor teach the exact syllabus the student is entered for, at the tier the school has entered them at? Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are different qualifications with different papers, different grade scales and different component structures. A tutor who knows the subject in general will teach a competent lesson aimed slightly past the paper, and a family finds that out in the autumn term.

Tier is where this becomes expensive to get wrong. Many Cambridge IGCSE subjects are entered at one of two tiers. Core is graded C to G, and Extended is graded A* to E, which means a student entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C however well they perform on the day. Tier entry is a school decision, it is reversible only before the entry deadline, and a long break is often the last practical window in which a family can raise the question at all. Confirm the tier and the component list with the school in writing before buying any hours.

Logistics then decide whether the block survives. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday, which during term caps a family at five usable evenings. Over the long break those hours open up and the specialist's own availability becomes the binding constraint instead, because the obvious candidates are committed weeks before the term ends. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks, so a slot has to be written in Saudi local time if it is going to survive into the autumn term intact. Lessons are delivered live online, one to one, which is what makes a specialist outside the family's own city reachable at all, and it is also the reason the search can be run on specification knowledge rather than on postcode. The rest of this page is in that order: the money, then the tier, then the tutor, then the week, then what the block should leave behind.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE holiday block costs, and what the number is made of
paragraphs: The spread of advertised rates in this market is wide enough to be confusing. The low end is non-specialist general tutoring sold by platform: around SAR 35 an hour for one-to-one IGCSE lessons on budget platforms, and from around SAR 55 for general online tutoring with no subject specialism attached. The high end is subject specialists advertised by tutoring companies from around SAR 180, with premium tracks listed at roughly SAR 200 to 220. Both ends of that range describe themselves in the same words.

Five things move a rate, in rough order of weight. Subject scarcity comes first: an Extended-tier physics or chemistry specialist is harder to find than a mathematics generalist in every market on earth. Then marking or examiner experience. Then level, because a Year 11 examination subject costs more than a Year 8 one. Then whether the tutor travels, which in the Kingdom loads an in-home rate with time nobody is being taught during. Then package length, which usually buys a modest discount.

What this means for a holiday purchase is that the rate should be read backwards from the diagnosis. A timing problem on one paper is six sessions of technique, and a competent generalist can deliver that. A collapsed Extended-tier topic needs the scarce specialist and costs accordingly. Paying a specialist rate for habit-building wastes money. Paying a generalist rate for a scarce topic wastes the whole break, which is the more expensive mistake of the two.

sections.heading: Why the tier sets the ceiling before any tutor is hired
paragraphs: Many Cambridge IGCSE subjects are entered at one of two tiers, and the tier sets the maximum grade available to the candidate. Core is graded C to G. Extended is graded A* to E. A student entered for Core who answers every question on the paper correctly is awarded a C. That is not a mark-scheme quirk; it is the design of the qualification, and it quietly decides which routes stay open afterwards.

Tier entry is a school decision, taken on the evidence the school holds, and it is reversible only before the entry deadline closes. That deadline sits several months ahead of the June series, and the school's examinations officer holds the exact date. A family who discovers the tier question during the spring term has usually missed the window. A family who raises it over a long break still has room, which is why a short tier review is worth buying before a teaching block is agreed.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades 9 to 1 and is not tiered in the same way, so a student moving between the two boards is not moving between equivalent papers. The component structure differs and the mark-scheme wording differs with it. Any family comparing holiday quotes should be able to say out loud which board, which syllabus code and which tier each subject is entered under. If nobody in the household can, that is the first call to make, and it is a two-minute call to the school office rather than a research project.

sections.heading: What subject qualification actually matters in an IGCSE tutor
paragraphs: A degree in the subject is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. The qualification that predicts a useful IGCSE lesson is knowledge of the specification: the syllabus code, the component list, which paper carries which weighting, what the mark scheme accepts as a complete answer, and which definitions the board examines strictly. A physics graduate who has never opened the 0625 specification will teach physics beautifully and leave marks on the table.

Teaching experience ranks next, and the useful kind is recent and in this qualification. A teacher who has taken a cohort through two years of Extended-tier work knows where students fail, which is a different thing from knowing the content. Marking or examiner experience ranks after that, and it is genuinely valuable: somebody who has applied a mark scheme to a pile of real scripts reads a student's answer differently. Ask what they marked, for which board, and how recently.

What matters least is where the tutor sits, which is the one thing a local search optimises for. Nothing on that list requires the tutor to be in the family's city, and insisting on it shrinks the pool to whoever is within driving distance during a holiday month. An Al Khobar family that will only consider an Al Khobar tutor is choosing from a handful of people, most of whom teach something else. Lessons here are delivered online, one to one, over live video. Home visits are a service IB Gram offers only in India, and no tutor is sent to a Saudi address.

sections.heading: Five questions for a trial lesson, and what a good answer sounds like
paragraphs: The free trial lesson is the only real evidence a family gets before paying, and most of them are wasted on introductions. Five questions settle it. First: which syllabus code is my child entered for, and which papers does it carry? A tutor who has read the specification answers immediately and names the weightings. One who asks the parent to look it up has not prepared for the conversation.

Second: looking at this marked script, where did the marks go and why? A good answer is specific — a command term misread across four questions, a practical-skills question left blank — rather than a general remark about revision. Third: what would the homework after our first session be? The answer should be a named past-paper question with a mark allocation attached, not a vague promise of practice. Fourth: what will you do with the coursework element, if the subject has one?

The honest answer to the fourth is narrow: teach the skills the task assesses, explain the criteria, give written feedback on a draft the student produced, and nothing beyond that. Any offer to supply finished text should end the conversation on the spot, whatever discount comes with it. Fifth: what happens if six weeks is not enough? A tutor willing to say that a problem is a term-time project rather than a holiday one is telling you something useful about every other answer they gave, because the easy version of this conversation is to agree with the parent.

sections.heading: The holiday week, the time zone, and a Ramadan that moves
paragraphs: During term, a family in the Kingdom has five usable evenings, because schools run Sunday to Thursday and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Over a long break that constraint inverts: the family has the whole week available, and the specialist's own calendar becomes the limit instead. That is why holiday blocks are booked before the term ends rather than during the first free week of it, when the obvious candidates are already committed.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3, and the Kingdom does not change its clocks at any point in the year. A tutor in the United Kingdom is two hours behind during their summer and three behind once their clocks go back, so a slot agreed in their local time moves quietly when the autumn term starts. Writing the slot in Saudi local time puts that drift on the tutor's side of the agreement, which is where it belongs.

Ramadan moves earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, so it drifts across the school year and will sometimes fall inside a long break and sometimes inside a term. School days shorten while it runs and evening study patterns change, which matters more for term-time slots than for holiday ones. A block that overlaps it is planned with later, shorter sessions agreed in advance. Cambridge and Pearson both run a June series and a November series for Saudi candidates; the Cambridge February and March series is sat in India, not here, and copy that says otherwise has been lifted from an Indian page.

sections.heading: Switching into IGCSE over a long break
paragraphs: Families relocate into the Kingdom all year round, and a student arriving from another system over a break has one clear advantage: it is the only time catching up does not compete with a full timetable. What transfers between systems is content knowledge, and it usually transfers better than parents fear. What does not transfer is assessment style, and that is almost always where the real gap sits. A student can know the chemistry and still lose a third of the available marks because nobody has shown them what the paper is asking for.

A national-curriculum student moving into IGCSE meets English-medium assessment and command terms that pay for precision rather than for completeness. A student from a CBSE or ICSE school usually arrives with strong content and a habit of writing down everything they know, which an IGCSE mark scheme does not reward. A student from an American middle school often arrives with broader coverage and less depth, and the sciences are where that shows up first. Each of the three needs different holiday work.

The practical sequence is the same in all three cases. Get the school's subject list, board and tier in writing. Sit one past paper per subject under time, marked against the published scheme. Rank the subjects by marks lost rather than by how the student feels about them. Then buy hours in the top one or two only. A block spread thinly across four subjects moves none of them far enough to be visible in the autumn term.

sections.heading: What the block should have produced by the first week of term
paragraphs: A holiday block should end in documents rather than impressions. A second timed paper, marked against the published scheme. A written comparison with the first one, question type by question type. A short note on what is still unreliable and why. And a named decision about the term-time slot, made while subject specialists still have evenings free to offer. None of that is onerous to produce, and a tutor who resists producing it is telling a family that the block was not measured at all.

Those documents do two jobs. They tell the family whether the money bought anything, measured against evidence rather than against a feeling in the last week of a break. And they give the school something concrete when a tier, a set or a predicted grade is being discussed. A teacher handed a marked script with a question-level breakdown will engage with it. A teacher told only that the family hired a tutor has nothing to engage with.

The honest version of the outcome is modest and worth saying plainly. Six weeks of good teaching usually recovers marks the student already half-knew: command terms, timing, working set out so that a marker can award method. It rarely delivers a whole tier's worth of new content, and no tutor can promise a grade at either board. A block that leaves a student finishing papers, reading the question before answering it and showing working a marker can follow has done what a break can do. The rest is the two years of teaching the school is paid to deliver, and a holiday block that pretends otherwise sets a family up for a disappointment in the spring.

process.title: Confirm board, code and tier
process.description: Get the school to confirm in writing which board, which syllabus code and which tier each subject is entered under. Everything else in a quote depends on those three facts.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the specialist
process.description: One session, no charge, with the tutor who would actually teach the block. Bring the marked script and ask the five questions. The answers are the evidence.

process.title: Agree hours, weeks and the two papers
process.description: Subject, number of sessions, session times in Arabia Standard Time, and the timed papers that will open and close the run. Written down before any payment.

process.title: Close the block with documents
process.description: A second marked paper, a written comparison by question type, and a decision about the term-time slot before autumn demand takes the usable evenings.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Edexcel are different qualifications. A match here starts from the code on the entry form and the tier, rather than from the word physics.

whyPoints.title: Rates named and attributed
whyPoints.description: Every SAR figure on this page is an advertised rate published by another provider, with the kind of source stated. None of them is a market average.

whyPoints.title: Specialists outside your city
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means an Extended-tier chemistry specialist is reachable from Tabuk or Jubail as easily as from Riyadh, in a holiday month or any other.

whyPoints.title: The student's own coursework stays theirs
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach the skills, explain the criteria and give feedback on the student's draft. No tutor supplies text that then appears in assessed work.

whyPoints.title: An honest ceiling
whyPoints.description: Six weeks moves technique reliably and content slowly. Nobody here will tell a family that a holiday block replaces a year of teaching.

faqs.question: Can an IGCSE holiday block use Friday and Saturday now that there is no school week to protect?
faqs.answer: It can, and over a long break it often should. Friday and Saturday are the weekend in the Kingdom, so during term those days are family time and tutors in other countries are frequently working. In a holiday month the picture changes: a tutor whose own weekend falls on Saturday and Sunday may have Friday free, and a family with no school run has no reason to avoid it. Agree the days when the block is booked.

faqs.question: What happens to a summer IGCSE block if Ramadan falls inside the long break?
faqs.answer: The block moves rather than stops. Ramadan drifts earlier against the Gregorian calendar each year, so in some years it sits inside a term and in others inside a holiday. When it falls in a break, families usually shift sessions later in the day and shorten them slightly, and the tutor is told in advance rather than on the day. Agree the adjusted pattern when the block is planned, not once the weeks arrive.

faqs.question: How is a holiday slot kept stable when the tutor's country puts its clocks back before term?
faqs.answer: By writing the slot in Arabia Standard Time and nothing else. The Kingdom does not change its clocks, so a session agreed as ten in the morning Saudi time stays at ten in the morning for the student forever. The tutor's local hour shifts when their country changes its clocks, and absorbing that shift is their job. A slot agreed in the tutor's own time moves under the student twice a year.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE sessions a week is too many over a six-week break?
faqs.answer: Four in one subject is past the useful point for almost every student. Teaching needs gaps for marked homework to be done and read, and without those gaps a block becomes a lecture series. Three sessions a week in one subject, or two each in two subjects, is where most students stay engaged. If a family wants more hours than that, the better use is a second subject rather than a denser single one.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE syllabus details should a tutor be able to recite in a trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The syllabus code, the number of written papers, roughly what each paper is worth, whether the subject is tiered and whether there is a practical or coursework component. A specialist answers all five without looking anything up, because those facts shape every lesson they teach. A tutor who answers in general terms about the subject may still teach well, but they are teaching the subject rather than the examination.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE examiner experience add to a six-week block, and how is it checked?
faqs.answer: Somebody who has marked real scripts knows what a mark scheme accepts and what it quietly refuses, which is exactly what a short block is trying to teach. Check it by asking which board, which component and how recently, then asking them to mark a question from your child's script and explain each mark. Nobody should be taken at their word on a profile claim, and a marked script is the only verification that actually works.

faqs.question: How should a family compare two IGCSE holiday quotes that look identical on paper?
faqs.answer: Put them side by side on five things: the syllabus code each tutor names, total hours, sessions per week, what happens between sessions, and what you receive at the end. Two quotes at the same hourly rate can differ by a factor of two in marked homework alone. Ask both to describe the first session's homework in detail. The vaguer answer is the cheaper product, whatever the number says.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper non-specialist ever the right choice for an IGCSE holiday block?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a narrow set of jobs. Rebuilding arithmetic and algebraic fluency, drilling timing, keeping a student working through a long break: a competent generalist does these as well as a specialist and costs less. The moment the problem is a specific Extended-tier topic or a mark-scheme habit in a science, the scarce specialist earns the difference. Match the rate to the diagnosis instead of to the budget.

faqs.question: Is a holiday block enough to move a student from Core tier to Extended before entries close?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the decision is never the tutor's. A block can produce the evidence: Extended papers sat under time, marked against the published scheme, with a written note of what the student reached. The school then decides the entry, and only before its deadline. If the Extended papers show a student losing marks on content that was never taught at Core, the answer is usually no, and knowing that early is worth the hours spent.

faqs.question: What does a national-curriculum student have to cover over a break before IGCSE teaching starts?
faqs.answer: Mostly the language of assessment rather than content. English-medium technical vocabulary in the sciences, what a command term requires, how a mark allocation tells you how much to write, and how to show working so a marker can follow it. Content gaps close inside the course. Assessment habits do not close by themselves, and a student who writes everything they know will lose marks in every paper until somebody shows them why.

faqs.question: Can a CBSE student close the gap into IGCSE over one long break?
faqs.answer: The content gap, largely yes. A CBSE student usually arrives ahead on mathematics and the sciences. The gap that takes longer is style: IGCSE papers reward precision and relevance, and reward nothing for extra correct material that does not answer the question. Expect the content work to take weeks and the writing habit to take a term. One subject at a time, with marked past papers, is the fastest route through it.

faqs.question: What transfers from an American middle-school year into IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Breadth transfers and depth usually does not. American middle-school science covers a wide range of topics at a level an IGCSE paper treats as introductory, so a student arrives recognising the words without the quantitative work behind them. Calculation, unit handling and the required practical skills are where the holiday hours go. Pick one science, sit a paper under time, and let the marked script decide which of the three to start on.

faqs.question: What should the first holiday session produce before a family pays for a second?
faqs.answer: A marked paper and a written note. The note should name the syllabus code, the marks lost by question type, the two or three things the block will target, and what the homework pattern will be. If the first session ends with a conversation and no document, the family has no way to judge anything later. A specialist can produce all of that from one timed paper and an hour of marking.

faqs.question: What do we do if the holiday tutor and the school disagree about the tier?
faqs.answer: Treat the disagreement as information and give the school the evidence rather than the opinion. Send the marked Extended papers, with the question-level breakdown, to the subject teacher and ask what they would need to see to reconsider. The school holds the entry decision and sees the student in class daily, which a tutor does not. If the answer is still Core, ask what it would take by the deadline.

igcse-summer-tuition.closingHeading: Start with the entry form, not the hourly rate
igcse-summer-tuition.closingBody: Send three things: the board and syllabus code for each subject, the tier the school has entered, and the most recent marked script. A subject specialist takes a free trial lesson, reads the script and says which problem it shows and what six weeks can realistically reach. Sessions run live online, one to one, at a time written in Arabia Standard Time. Every rate quoted on this page is another provider's advertised number rather than ours.

igcse-tuition.tutorsIntro: Each profile below names the board, the syllabus code and the papers the tutor has prepared candidates for. That is the detail worth reading before the biography: a Chemistry teacher who has never seen an alternative-to-practical paper is a different proposition from one who has prepared forty candidates for it.

intro.heading: The money first, because that is the question families actually open with
paragraphs: Nearly every enquiry about IGCSE support in the Kingdom begins with what it costs, and most tutoring sites answer by inviting a callback. Here is the spread instead. Budget platforms advertise IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35 an hour. General tutoring platforms list non-specialist online tutoring from around SAR 55. Tutor-marketplace guides put general private tuition in Saudi cities at roughly SAR 50 for primary and SAR 200 and above for senior-school examined subjects. Tutoring companies advertise subject tutoring on international curricula from around SAR 180, with premium tracks quoted nearer SAR 200 to 220, and some providers quote in dollars at about USD 60. Every one of those is a provider's own advertised figure rather than a measured market average, and none of them is our price, which we give you directly.

The spread is wide because the thing being sold is not uniform. At the bottom of the range sits a marketplace floor: a tutor who is competent in a school subject and may never have seen the syllabus your child is entered for. At the top sits someone who teaches that exact paper, knows which practical route the entry covers, and has marked work to the published scheme. The difference between those two is not polish. It is whether the hour you pay for is spent on the examined form of the subject or on the subject in general, and that difference shows up in the grade rather than in the lesson.

What moves a rate, in order of weight, is scarcity first and everything else afterwards. A tutor who can teach Extended Physics or Additional Mathematics to examination standard is rarer than one who can teach Core Mathematics, in Saudi Arabia and everywhere else, and that scarcity sets the figure more than negotiation ever will. Then comes marking or examiner experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then how long a block you commit to. Proximity to a series adds a sixth factor, because demand concentrates sharply in the final eight weeks.

Then come the logistics, and this is where arrangements quietly fail after the money has been agreed. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Arabia Standard Time sits at UTC+3 and does not change, which means a slot agreed with a tutor whose country does change its clocks will move under you twice a year unless it is pinned to Saudi local time. A tutor's own working week matters as much as their subject: somebody whose weekend is Saturday and Sunday has a different set of free evenings from somebody whose weekend is Friday and Saturday.

All lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. There is no in-home option anywhere in the Kingdom; the only country where a tutor attends a family's address is India. That is stated early because online IGCSE tuition is the whole proposition here rather than a fallback, and because the argument for it is strongest when it is made plainly: the pool a family chooses from is everyone who teaches that paper and is free in a workable Saudi slot, rather than everyone within a reasonable drive. The rest of this page is quality, then logistics, then what the grades are actually for.

igcse-tuition.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits inside a longer sequence, and families comparing prices often find they are comparing different points in it. These are the stages most often involved in an enquiry, with what each one is assessed on, because the stage changes both the work and the realistic hourly figure.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed through school tests and optional Checkpoint tests marked externally and reported as a scale rather than a grade. Nothing here appears on a certificate, which is why families skip it, and the one thing that genuinely predicts an IGCSE outcome is built in it: algebraic fluency and the habit of writing an explanation rather than an answer.
programmes.countryNote: Support at this stage is the cheapest intervention available in the Kingdom and the one with the longest payback, because the gaps it fixes are the ones that cap Extended entry two years later. Families usually arrive here after a Checkpoint report they cannot interpret, and a single diagnostic session is normally enough to turn it into a list.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, one grade per subject, examined on written papers with a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper in the sciences. Many syllabuses run Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings and overlapping content. The syllabus code on the entry form determines the number of papers, their length and the practical route, which is why a tutor who does not know the code does not yet know the job.
programmes.countryNote: The majority of IGCSE candidates in Saudi Arabia sit Cambridge papers, and they sit them in the June series or the November series. Tiering decisions are usually taken by the school in Year 10, and they are the single highest-leverage conversation available to a family, because no amount of paid support lifts a Core candidate above the Core ceiling.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same qualification level with a different architecture. Edexcel International GCSE runs a papers-only route on most subjects and offers coursework on some, with its own paper structures, assessment objectives and grade scales. Subject content overlaps heavily with Cambridge; question styles and mark-scheme habits do not, and a tutor prepared on one board will not automatically prepare a candidate well for the other.
programmes.countryNote: A minority of schools in the Kingdom run Edexcel, sometimes alongside Cambridge in different subjects within the same school, which confuses families and sometimes confuses tutors. Confirm the board per subject rather than per school, and put the board in the first message you send any prospective tutor.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The alternative route through the same years, assessed against four criteria per subject marked out of eight using published descriptors, with the Personal Project in the final year and external eAssessment where a school offers it. It produces different habits from a paper-based course: strong extended writing, weaker timed answering to a mark allocation.
programmes.countryNote: This appears in IGCSE enquiries more often than it should, because families moving a child from a Middle Years Programme school into an IGCSE class assume the content transfer is the problem. It usually is not. The transfer that costs a term is learning to write to a mark allocation under time pressure, and that is a short, specific piece of work.

programmes.name: Cambridge International AS and A Level
programmes.description: What IGCSE feeds into for students not entering the Diploma. Entry requirements are expressed in IGCSE grades, usually with a named grade in the subject itself and often in mathematics alongside it. The step up in abstraction is real, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, and Additional Mathematics at IGCSE is the standard bridge across it.
programmes.countryNote: The reason this belongs on an IGCSE page is that the grades being paid for now are the currency for the next stage. A family deciding whether to fund support in Year 11 is really deciding which sixth-form subjects remain available, and that is a far more concrete way to judge the cost than comparing hourly rates.

igcse-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects support is most often requested for in the Kingdom, with the Cambridge syllabus code families see on entry forms. Each note says what the entry decides, how scarce that specialist is, and what an hour of support realistically changes, because those three things together are what you are actually pricing.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The entry decision matters more than the tutor here: Core caps the reachable grade regardless of performance, and Extended is what sixth-form mathematics and most science routes expect. Tutors are relatively plentiful at Core level and noticeably scarcer at Extended, which is where the advertised rates separate. An hour a week from early Year 10 does more than three hours a week in the final term.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside Extended mathematics, introducing calculus and formal algebra a year early. The scarcest mainstream IGCSE specialism in this market, because the people who can teach it well are mostly teaching A Level or Diploma Higher Level instead. If you need it, book it early in the year rather than negotiating later; availability sets the price far more than demand does.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Multiple choice, theory, and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper depending on what the centre entered. Which of those two the candidate sits changes the preparation substantially, and families frequently do not know which it is. Extended Physics tutors are scarce enough that the advertised premium is real rather than opportunistic.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry account for more lost marks than organic chemistry, because the arithmetic is unforgiving under time pressure and cannot be bluffed. Qualitative analysis tables are examinable and learnable, and candidates routinely arrive at the paper without them. A short, cheap block of work on those two areas changes a grade more reliably than a general year of support.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Definitions are marked strictly with thin partial credit, so loose recall scores nothing at all. Tutors are comparatively plentiful, which keeps rates near the middle of the band. The best use of paid time is marked written answers rather than taught content, because most candidates in this subject know more than their scripts show.

subjects.name: Combined Science (0653)
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics in a single award with fewer papers and less content than the three separate sciences. It is the sensible entry for many candidates and a trap for those aiming at sixth-form sciences, since some providers expect the separate subjects. Check the next stage's entry requirements before choosing it on workload grounds alone.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing at native-speaker level plus composition. The marks sit in analysing a writer's method rather than summarising content, which is a teachable technique and the single most common reason confident readers underperform. Specialists are plentiful, so there is little scarcity premium and no reason to accept a generalist.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 and 0511)
subjects.description: Reading, writing and listening, with the summary task functioning as a drilled technique rather than a comprehension exercise. A great many candidates across the Kingdom are entered here, and a meaningful number are entered here when First Language English would have served them better. One diagnostic reading task settles that question before the entry, not after the result.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Definitional precision and diagram accuracy carry the marks, and the structured data-response question is where they are lost. It is most candidates' first encounter with evaluation as a separately rewarded skill. Tutors are mid-scarce, and the useful ones are those who mark written answers rather than re-explaining the diagrams.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Applied rather than theoretical, with answers required to use the business described in the case material. Generic advantage-and-disadvantage writing where a justified recommendation was asked for is the standing loss, and it takes a few weeks of marked practice to correct. Plentiful supply keeps this near the lower end of specialist rates.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory papers on data representation, networks and systems, plus algorithms and programming assessed on paper rather than on a machine. Candidates who code well often score poorly because pseudocode on paper is marked differently from working software. Specialists are scarce in this market, and the scarcity is in the examined form rather than in the programming.

subjects.name: Information and Communication Technology (0417)
subjects.description: A written paper plus two practical tests on documents, data handling and website authoring, with software skills examined precisely. It rewards drilled repetition over understanding, which makes it one of the few subjects where a modest hourly rate buys a reliable grade, provided the practice is on the examined tasks rather than on general computer use.

igcse-tuition.regionsTitle: Where IGCSE candidates in the Kingdom actually are
igcse-tuition.regionsIntro: Candidate numbers are concentrated in a few places and thin everywhere else, and that distribution is what decides whether a family has a local option at all. The notes below are about availability and timing rather than about which city is pleasanter to live in.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The largest concentration of international and British-curriculum candidates in the Kingdom, and roughly an hour across in traffic from north to south. Local supply exists, which means families here are usually comparing an online specialist against a named local tutor rather than against nothing at all.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, with British, American, IB and Indian curricula all represented. Journey times along the spine are the practical constraint on any in-home arrangement, and they are the reason evening slots here start later than families expect.

regions.name: The Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran cluster
regions.note: One school and labour market behaving as a single unit, with a large Cambridge population and children routinely living in one city and schooled in another. Supply is the best outside Riyadh, and the gaps are specific: Extended sciences and Additional Mathematics rather than whole subjects.

regions.name: Jubail and Yanbu
regions.note: Industrial cities with international schooling attached to the workforce. Candidate numbers are decent and specialist supply is thin, so these are the places where a scarce subject at Extended tier most often has no local answer and an online slot is the only realistic route.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Large cities with comparatively few international-curriculum candidates, and calendars that bend around the Hajj and Umrah seasons in ways the school year has to accommodate. Families here plan lesson slots around traffic and seasonal pressure more than around the school day itself.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Two cities about twenty-five kilometres apart at altitude in 'Asir, sharing a catchment. The combined international-curriculum cohort is small, which means almost no local specialist supply at Extended tier and a strong practical case for teaching that arrives over a connection.

regions.name: Tabuk and the north-west
regions.note: Including the NEOM development and AlUla, where households are arriving faster than schooling provision is settling. Mid-course arrivals are common, and the first question is usually what the new centre has entered the candidate for rather than what they have been taught.

regions.name: Thuwal, Ha'il and the smaller centres
regions.note: Thuwal serves the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology campus community north of Jeddah; Ha'il and comparable centres have small cohorts and little specialist depth. In all of them the nearest person teaching a given paper is a long way off, and the time zone matters more than the distance.

schoolClusters.city: The Eastern Province, where the Cambridge population is densest
schoolClusters.note: British and Cambridge-curriculum provision in the Dammam, Khobar and Dhahran cluster is the deepest outside Riyadh, with the International Schools Group running several campuses. Candidate numbers here support most subjects locally, which is why the enquiries that reach us are usually for one scarce paper rather than a whole certificate.

The widest curricular mix in one city, with British, IB, American, German and Indian provision within the same coastal strip. Families here change board more often than elsewhere, which is the main reason we ask for the board per subject rather than per school.

The largest market in the Kingdom and the one with the most IB provision, which matters on an IGCSE page because many Riyadh candidates are deciding between a sixth form built on A Levels and one built on the Diploma. That decision changes which IGCSE grades need protecting.

igcse-tuition.modesIntro: Four arrangements cover nearly every IGCSE enquiry, and they differ in price mainly through weekly contact rather than through hourly rate. All of them are one-to-one, live online, on a slot agreed in Arabia Standard Time against a Sunday-to-Thursday school week.

modes.title: One subject, one hour a week
modes.description: The standard arrangement and the right one for a candidate whose school teaches the subject competently and who needs the examined form of it taught properly. Content runs slightly ahead of the class, written work is set each week and marked before the next session, and progress is reported as marks rather than as impressions.
bullets: Matched to the syllabus code, tier and paper combination on the entry
Written work marked to the published scheme between sessions
One fixed hour, chosen to survive a heavy school week rather than an easy one
A short parent note after each session saying what moved

modes.title: Two or three subjects across a week
modes.description: Common in the final IGCSE year, usually the sciences plus mathematics. Separate specialists per subject beat one tutor covering all three, and the weekly cost rises with contact rather than with the hourly figure. The honest limit is around three subjects before homework and school teaching start losing out to tuition.
bullets: A different specialist for each subject rather than a generalist across them
Sessions spread across the week, not stacked on one evening
One combined weekly summary instead of three separate reports
A stated maximum, because more subjects is not more progress

modes.title: An intensive block before a series
modes.description: A compressed run in the weeks before the papers, built on whole papers under timed conditions and marked cold. Content teaching stops. Demand for this concentrates sharply, and advertised rates in the market rise with it, so the block is worth booking a term ahead rather than in the final fortnight.
bullets: Whole papers under the real time allowance, marked to the published scheme
A written list of the recurring mark-scheme misses, updated each week
Three or four sessions a week across a fixed number of weeks
Only worth buying where the content is already largely secure

modes.title: Marking and feedback between school lessons
modes.description: The cheapest useful product on this page. No teaching: the student submits written answers or a whole paper, and a specialist marks it to the published scheme and returns a commentary on where marks were available and not taken. It suits a capable candidate who is coping with the content and losing marks on the form.
bullets: A fortnightly or monthly rhythm rather than a weekly slot
Marks reported against the published scheme, with the misses named
Useful alongside, not instead of, a school that teaches the subject well
Often enough on its own for a candidate already working at a strong grade

sections.heading: What moves an IGCSE hourly rate, in order of weight
paragraphs: Two tutors quoting different figures for the same subject are usually not offering different quality. They are occupying different points on a scarcity curve. The supply of people who can teach Core Mathematics to IGCSE standard is large. The supply of people who can teach Additional Mathematics, Extended Physics or IGCSE Computer Science to examination standard, in English, in a Saudi evening slot, is small. Price follows that, and it follows it far more reliably than it follows experience or qualifications.

The second factor is marking experience, and it is the one families most often pay for without checking. A tutor who has marked for a board has seen a thousand scripts fail to earn marks that were sitting there, and that knowledge is worth a premium. The way to test the claim is to ask which board, which paper and how recently, then ask what the commonest avoidable loss on that paper is. A specific answer is evidence. A general answer about exam technique is not.

After those come the mechanical factors, which behave predictably. Level pushes the rate up: Extended above Core, and IGCSE below Diploma Higher Level in every published band in this market. Travel pushes it up, whether or not it is itemised, which is one reason online delivery is cheaper for the same specialist. Package length pushes the hourly figure down, and should only be committed to after a trial has produced something written. Proximity to a series pushes it up, sharply, in the last eight weeks.

sections.heading: Reading an advertised rate honestly
paragraphs: Published figures in this market are marketing, and they are built to be read optimistically. A rate advertised as starting from a number describes the cheapest tutor on a platform rather than the one a family will end up with, and on a marketplace the platform does not set the fee at all. A rate quoted by a tutoring company for international curricula describes a narrower product, usually with the subject and level stated, which is why those figures sit two to four times higher.

Currency adds another layer. Providers quoting in dollars at about USD 60 an hour are pricing for an international market, and the riyal equivalent moves with nothing a family controls. There is nothing wrong with a dollar quote, but it should be converted before being compared, and it should be compared against what is included: some packages measured in months bundle marking, reports and materials that an hourly arrangement charges for separately.

The useful comparison is not the hourly number at all. It is the cost of the grade. One properly matched specialist hour a week from the start of Year 10, with written work marked between sessions, usually costs less across the two years than six months of panic in Year 11 at an inflated pre-series rate, and it produces a better certificate. Families who price the year rather than the hour reach a different and generally cheaper conclusion, and that is the single most useful arithmetic on this page.
bullets: A rate starting from a figure describes the cheapest tutor available, not the likely one
Ask what the hourly fee includes: marking, reports, materials, or none of those
Convert any dollar quote before comparing it with a riyal one
Price the year, not the hour, and the cheap option often changes identity

sections.heading: What you are buying is the paper, not the subject
paragraphs: Once the money is settled the quality question becomes narrow and answerable. IGCSE is examined on specific papers defined by a syllabus code, and two tutors who both say they teach Chemistry may be prepared for quite different assessments. Cambridge 0620 at Extended tier with a practical test is not the same preparation as the same syllabus with an alternative-to-practical entry, and neither is the same as Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry. The content overlaps; the examined form does not.

This is why every enquiry should carry four pieces of information: the board, the syllabus code, the tier, and which practical route the centre has entered the candidate for. Families frequently do not hold the fourth, and it is worth one email to the school to find out, because it changes several months of preparation. A tutor who does not ask for these four things before quoting has told you something useful about how closely they will work to your child's actual assessment.

The same logic applies to tiering. Core and Extended tiers overlap in content and differ in grade ceiling, and a candidate entered for Core cannot reach the top grades however well the teaching goes. Paying for Extended-level teaching against a Core entry is simply waste, and paying for Core-level teaching when the school intends an Extended entry is worse. Confirm the entry in writing before the first lesson, and if a family believes the tiering decision is wrong, the time to raise it with the school is Year 10 with marked evidence in hand.

sections.heading: How to check a tutor really knows your child's syllabus
paragraphs: There is no accreditation to look up here, and anybody claiming board approval for a tutoring service is overstating their position. IB Gram holds no approval from Cambridge, from Pearson, from the Ministry of Education or from the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and says so. What a family can do instead is ask four questions whose answers are hard to fake, and listen for specificity rather than for confidence.

First: which papers does this syllabus have, and how long is each one? A specialist answers immediately. Second: what is the commonest avoidable mark loss on the paper my child will sit? A good answer is a diagnosis, such as working not shown so method marks die with a wrong final figure, or graph axes left unlabelled. Third: how do you mark written work, and will I see the mark scheme? Fourth: what will you do if my child is in the wrong tier for the grade we are aiming at?

The trial lesson is the other instrument, and it should produce a document rather than a good feeling. A diagnostic hour that works through recent material, marks something the student has already written, and ends with a written note of what is wrong and in what order to fix it is worth having whether or not the arrangement continues. A trial that is a pleasant conversation about goals and ambitions has told you that the tutor is personable, which was never the uncertain part.
bullets: Ask how many papers the syllabus has and how long each one is
Ask for the commonest avoidable mark loss on that specific paper
Ask whether you will see the published mark scheme alongside marked work
Insist the trial lesson ends with something written down

sections.heading: The Sunday-to-Thursday week, and what it actually leaves
paragraphs: Almost all tutoring copy a Saudi family reads was written for a Monday-to-Friday week, and the assumption is invisible until a schedule is built on it. Here the school week runs Sunday to Thursday. Sunday carries the week's first homework load and the first new content. Thursday evening is the start of a weekend and is the worst slot in the week to book, because it will be surrendered first every time something else comes up. Friday and Saturday are the weekend, and they behave quite differently from each other.

That distribution has practical consequences for where a weekly hour should sit. New content taught on a Sunday evening lands badly, because the student has just come off two days away from the subject. Marked work returned early in the week is used; marked work returned on a Thursday is filed. A timed paper works best midweek, when the student is already in working rhythm and has the next day to review it. These are small scheduling choices and they compound across thirty weeks.

Ramadan reshapes the week again, and it moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so it lands at a different point in the school year each time. School days shorten, and the usable study hours move later into the evening. That suits online delivery, where a slot can shift by two hours for a month and shift back afterwards, and it plays badly with any arrangement built on a fixed driving route. Agree in advance what happens to the slot, rather than renegotiating it in week one.

sections.heading: Arabia Standard Time against a tutor's own working week
paragraphs: The Kingdom sits at UTC+3 and does not observe daylight saving, which has one consequence families should insist on in writing: any slot agreed with a tutor in a country that does change its clocks must be pinned to Saudi local time, so that their hour moves and yours does not. Arrangements that are agreed in the tutor's time drift twice a year, and the drift always arrives in the middle of a term when nobody has the appetite to renegotiate it.

The more interesting constraint is the tutor's own week rather than their clock. A tutor in Egypt or Jordan keeps a Sunday-to-Thursday week, so their free evenings line up with yours and their weekend is your weekend. A tutor in the United Kingdom or the United States keeps a Saturday-and-Sunday weekend, which means your Sunday school night is their weekend and their Friday evening is already your weekend. Neither is disqualifying; both change which slots are genuinely available week after week.

Distance also sets a hard floor on what is possible. A tutor on the east coast of Australia is offset far enough that a Saudi school-night evening falls in the middle of their night, so the only workable arrangements are Friday or Saturday mornings here. A tutor in India sits two and a half hours ahead, which puts a Saudi early evening comfortably inside their normal teaching hours, and is one reason Indian specialists are so widely available to families in the Kingdom.
