sections.heading: The series, the entry window and the resit decision
paragraphs: Candidates in the Kingdom sit the June series or the November series. Cambridge also runs a February and March sitting, and it is open to candidates in India only, which matters because a great deal of tutoring copy aimed at Gulf families is adapted from Indian pages and quietly imports the wrong entry calendar. Acting on that error costs a family a sitting, so the series names are worth confirming with your own school rather than with any website.

Final entry windows close several months before the papers, and they are administered by the centre rather than by the candidate. The examinations officer at your school holds the exact dates, the paper combinations and the practical routes, and that one conversation resolves more uncertainty than any amount of reading. For a candidate entered privately through a centre, the same conversation happens with the centre, and it should happen early enough that a missing subject can still be added.

Having two series in the year changes what is worth attempting. A Year 11 candidate who is behind in one subject has a genuine choice: enter in the June series and accept a risk, or enter that subject in the November series and use the summer properly. Neither is automatically right, and the decision should be made on marked evidence rather than on optimism. A resit also needs lead time, because the gap between results and the next entry deadline is shorter than families assume.

sections.heading: Coursework, practicals and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some IGCSE syllabuses carry coursework, and where they do, the work must be the student's own and the school declares it as such. A tutor may not write, draft or produce any part of it. Nobody working through IB Gram will, and a provider who offers to is describing malpractice however pleasantly it is phrased. This is worth saying on a page about price, because the cheapest offers in this market are sometimes cheap for exactly that reason.

What a tutor can legitimately do with coursework is teach the skills the task needs before the task begins, read the student's own draft against the published criteria, and return questions rather than corrections. Every change is made by the student. The most valuable single intervention is catching an unworkable method in the second week rather than the tenth, and it is also the cheapest, because it costs one session rather than a rescue operation.

Practical work needs its own planning. In the sciences a candidate sits either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the two require genuinely different preparation. The alternative-to-practical paper examines experimental reasoning, identifying variables, reading apparatus, spotting a flawed method, and it can be prepared for thoroughly without a laboratory. The practical test cannot. Find out which one the entry covers before buying any support in the sciences, because it determines a meaningful share of what the lessons should contain, and because it is the one piece of information families most often do not hold when they start paying for help.

sections.heading: What the IGCSE grades are actually for
paragraphs: A certificate is not the destination, and judging the cost of support against the grade alone understates what is being bought. IGCSE grades are entry currency for the next stage. A sixth form built on Cambridge International AS and A Level expresses its requirements in IGCSE grades, usually with a named grade in the subject itself and often in mathematics as well. An IB Diploma school looks at the same grades when deciding whether a student can be supported at Higher Level in a subject.

For families planning to stay in the Kingdom for university, the longer chain matters too. A Saudi university requires Ministry of Education equivalency, the mu'adalah decision, before it treats an international certificate as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and the Qiyas tests sit alongside it: Qudurat, which examines verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than taught content, and Tahsili, whose content follows the Saudi national curriculum. The IGCSE years are where the science and mathematics foundations for Tahsili are either laid or not.

That is the honest argument for spending money at this stage rather than later. Not one tutor anywhere can promise a university place, and none should pretend otherwise. What is true is that the subjects and tiers settled at IGCSE decide which sixth-form routes remain open, and the sixth-form route decides which degree applications are possible. Universities publish their own admission criteria and those are the only figures worth trusting; the planning, though, starts two stages earlier than most families realise, which is at the point this page is about.
bullets: Sixth-form entry requirements are written in IGCSE grades, usually naming mathematics
Extended tier, not Core, is what most science and mathematics routes expect
Ministry of Education equivalency applies to the final certificate, whatever the board

Without them, any quote is a guess, and a tutor who quotes anyway has told you how closely they intend to work to your child's actual assessment.

process.title: Get the rate in writing, with what it includes
process.description: We quote our figure directly rather than asking you to request a callback, and we say what sits inside it: the lesson, the written work set, the marking between sessions and the note you receive afterwards. If something is charged separately we say so before the first lesson rather than on the first invoice.

process.title: A free diagnostic lesson that ends in writing
process.description: The first session works through recent material, marks something the student has already produced, and finishes with a written account of what is wrong and the order to fix it in. You keep that regardless of what you decide. A note saying the student needs more practice is not a diagnosis and should not persuade anyone.

process.title: Fix the slot in Saudi time and write it down
process.description: The hour is agreed in Arabia Standard Time, against a Sunday-to-Thursday week, and recorded in your local time rather than the tutor's. If the tutor's country changes its clocks, their time moves and yours does not. We also agree in advance what happens to the slot during Ramadan and during the long summer break.

process.title: Marks, not impressions, every week
process.description: Written work is marked to the published scheme between sessions, and the report you get is a mark with the misses named. Over a term that produces a line on a graph rather than a series of reassurances, which is the only way to tell a productive arrangement from a comfortable one before the results arrive.

process.title: Review at the end of the term and stop if it is not working
process.description: We look at the marked evidence and decide together whether to continue, change tutor, change frequency or stop. If the match is wrong after two or three lessons, say so and we change it at no cost. If no specialist is free for the paper and slot you need, we tell you that instead of offering a generalist.

whyPoints.title: The price is on the page
whyPoints.description: Advertised rates in this market run from around SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to about SAR 220 for premium tracks, and almost every provider hides their own figure behind a form. We publish the bands with the source type attached, explain in order what moves the number, and give our own figure when you ask rather than after three emails.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the paper on the entry form
whyPoints.description: Board, syllabus code, tier and practical route decide what a candidate is actually sitting, and a tutor prepared for a different combination is a worse match than their biography suggests. We ask for all four before quoting, and we say plainly when we do not have somebody for that exact paper in a workable slot.

whyPoints.title: Built for a Sunday-to-Thursday week
whyPoints.description: Thursday evening here is the start of a weekend, Sunday carries the first new content of the week, and Saturday is the most valuable study block available. A schedule designed around those facts survives a term. One imported from a Monday-to-Friday assumption starts failing in about week four, usually on a Thursday.

whyPoints.title: A slot that does not drift
whyPoints.description: The Kingdom holds UTC+3 all year. Tutors in countries that change their clocks move, and the agreement records your local hour so the movement lands on their side of it. Where a tutor's own working week does not fit a Saudi school week, we say so at the matching stage rather than discovering it in November.

whyPoints.title: A firm line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Where a syllabus carries coursework, a tutor reads the student's own draft against the published criteria and returns questions. Nothing is written, redrafted or filled in on a student's behalf. Some of the cheapest offers in this market are cheap precisely because they do the other thing, and that is worth knowing while comparing prices.

whyPoints.title: Clear about what we are not
whyPoints.description: We hold no approval, accreditation or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the Ministry of Education or the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, and we are not connected to any school on this page. There is no office in the Kingdom. No grade, score or place is promised. What remains is a specialist, a paper and a weekly hour that is kept.

faqs.question: Why does an Extended IGCSE Physics tutor cost more than a Core Mathematics one in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Because the supply curves are different, not because one hour is worth more than another. A great many people can teach Core Mathematics to IGCSE standard. Far fewer can teach Extended Physics to examination standard in English, in a Saudi evening slot, with a working knowledge of which practical route the entry covers. Scarcity sets the figure, and marking experience adds to it. The practical consequence is that negotiating rarely moves a scarce subject's price, while booking early in the year often secures the better tutor at the ordinary rate.

faqs.question: What does a rate advertised from SAR 35 an hour actually mean on an IGCSE tutoring platform?
faqs.answer: It describes the cheapest tutor currently listed, not the one a family will be matched with, and on a marketplace the platform does not set fees at all. Tutors there set their own, and syllabus knowledge varies enormously: some have taught the exact paper for years, others are competent in the school subject and have never seen the mark scheme. The figure is a floor, published to win a click. Before comparing it with a company rate, ask which syllabus code the tutor has taught and how many candidates they have prepared for that paper.

faqs.question: Do I pay per lesson or per block for IGCSE support, and what happens to lessons we do not use?
faqs.answer: Both models exist across this market and they price differently. Per-lesson arrangements cost more per hour and carry no commitment, which suits a family testing whether tuition helps at all. Blocks discount the hourly figure in exchange for a commitment, and the terms on unused lessons are where the differences hide: some providers expire them at the end of a period, others roll them forward, others refund nothing. Ask that question before paying for a block, and only commit once a trial lesson has produced a written diagnosis you found useful.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE hourly rate rise in the eight weeks before a series?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates for intensive pre-series work generally sit above ordinary weekly rates across this market, and availability tightens at the same time, which is the bigger problem. Every family in the Kingdom wants the same specialist in the same eight weeks. The two sensible responses are to book the pre-series block a term ahead at the standing rate, or to accept that late booking means choosing from whoever is left rather than from whoever is best. Waiting rarely saves money and frequently costs the specialist.

faqs.question: Is paying for paper marking between lessons worth it on top of the lesson itself?
faqs.answer: For a candidate who is coping with the content and losing marks on the examined form, marking is often better value than more teaching. A script marked to the published scheme shows exactly which marks were sitting there untaken, and the pattern repeats, so three marked papers usually reveal the whole problem. Where it is not worth it is for a candidate with genuine content gaps, since marking a weak script produces a long list and no mechanism for fixing it. Diagnose first, then decide which of the two the money should buy.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects can a family realistically fund support for at once?
faqs.answer: Two or three is the practical ceiling, and the constraint is the student's week rather than the budget. Each subject adds a session plus the written work that follows it, and at four subjects tuition starts displacing school homework, which is self-defeating. Where more subjects are weak, the better response is to sequence: support the two that gate the next stage, usually mathematics and one science, for a term, then reassess with marked evidence. Spreading the same money thinly across five subjects reliably produces five small improvements and no grade changes.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting IGCSE support in the first term of Year 10, or is that too early?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest point in the whole two years to start, and it is routinely dismissed as premature. Year 10 is when the content that everything later depends on is laid down, when tiering decisions are formed, and when a habit of answering to a mark allocation can be installed without time pressure. An hour a week from the first term costs less across two years than a crisis block in the final one and produces a better certificate. The only wrong reason to start early is anxiety; the right one is that the foundations are visibly shaky.

faqs.question: What can a Year 11 candidate realistically recover in a single term before the June papers?
faqs.answer: Technique in full, and content in part. In one term a candidate can learn the command terms properly, learn to write the number of separable points a mark allocation asks for, sit six or eight whole papers under timed conditions, and close two or three specific weak topics. What cannot be done is reteaching a year of unlearned material while also preparing papers. Any tutor who says otherwise is selling comfort. The honest version is a prioritised list ordered by what is examined most heavily, and a frank statement of what is being left out.

faqs.question: Should a Year 9 student in Saudi Arabia be doing anything before the IGCSE course begins?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is pre-reading the syllabus. Algebraic fluency, because it limits mathematics and both physical sciences for the next two years and is almost never revisited once the course starts. Written explanation in English, because every subject pays for it and no subject teaches it. And reading volume, which quietly determines performance in the reading papers. That is a few weeks of focused work rather than a programme, and it is the highest-return support available at any point in the five years that follow.

faqs.question: How does a November-series IGCSE candidate's year differ from a June one?
faqs.answer: The whole rhythm inverts. A November candidate's final eight weeks fall across the start of the school year rather than at the end of it, which means intensive work happens while new teaching is also beginning, and the summer before becomes the main preparation window rather than a break. Entry deadlines sit correspondingly earlier in the year. The advantage is real for a candidate who needed more time, or who is resitting, and the planning has to be deliberate because almost nothing in the school's own calendar is built around it.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE grades matter for Ministry of Education equivalency, or only the final school certificate?
faqs.answer: Equivalency, the mu'adalah decision, concerns the secondary certificate a student finishes with, so an IGCSE result is not itself what is assessed. It still matters in two indirect ways. It determines which sixth-form route is open, and therefore which certificate exists to be made equivalent. And the documents assembled for equivalency include the schooling record, so transcripts and certificates from the IGCSE years are worth keeping in order rather than reconstructing later. Ask your school's counsellor what their process requires, since the paperwork is easier to gather as you go.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects should a student keep if they are aiming at a Saudi science programme?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at Extended tier, and the sciences in the form the next stage expects, which for competitive routes usually means the separate sciences rather than a combined award. The reason runs beyond entry requirements: Tahsili covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English on the Saudi national curriculum, so the foundations laid in these years are the ones that test draws on later. Keeping all three sciences is heavy, and dropping one is a reasonable decision made deliberately in Year 10 rather than by accident in Year 11.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE results appear in a university application made outside the Kingdom at all?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes, though their weight varies by system. Some universities ask for the full certificate history and read IGCSE grades as evidence of sustained performance, particularly where they also want proof of English language competence. Others care only about the final qualification and its predicted grades. A small number of competitive courses name a specific IGCSE grade, most often in mathematics. Since the requirements are published and differ by institution, build the list from each university's own admissions pages in the first term of the final school year.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE student need to think about Tahsili before sixth form?
faqs.answer: Not to prepare for it, but yes to avoid closing doors. Tahsili covers mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum rather than an international syllabus. A student who drops a science at IGCSE and later wants a competitive Saudi science programme has made that test harder than it needed to be. The practical step is simply to know the test exists and what it covers while subject choices are still open, and to leave the serious preparation for the final two school years.

faqs.question: Does a tutor whose own weekend falls on Saturday and Sunday cost a Saudi family more?
faqs.answer: The hourly figure is usually unaffected; the availability is not, and that is where the real cost sits. A tutor keeping a Saturday-and-Sunday weekend has your Sunday school night inside their weekend and their Friday evening inside yours, so the overlap of genuinely free hours is narrower and the good slots go first. A tutor keeping a Sunday-to-Thursday week has the same weekend you do. Ask about the working week at the matching stage rather than the rate, because a cheap hour you cannot reliably book is more expensive than a dearer one you can.

faqs.question: Can IGCSE lessons run on a Friday or a Saturday in Saudi Arabia?
faqs.answer: Saturday is the strongest slot in the week for a long session, because the student is rested and school returns the next day, so a two-hour block of paper work plus review is well placed there. Friday is harder: mornings suit very few students and the middle of the day is shaped by prayers, though a late afternoon session works well by agreement. A tutor whose own weekend falls on Saturday and Sunday will usually decline both, which is one reason a tutor's working week is asked about at the matching stage.

igcse-tuition.closingHeading: What to send if you want a straight answer on price
igcse-tuition.closingBody: Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the practical route on the entry, plus the hour that works on a school night. We will tell you whether a specialist in that exact paper is free in that window, what it costs, and what the figure includes. If nobody suitable is free, we will say so rather than offering a generalist at the same price. The first lesson is free and diagnostic, and it ends with a written account of what is wrong and the order to fix it in. Everything is taught one-to-one, live online, on Arabia Standard Time.

intro.heading: The nearest IGCSE tutor and the right one are two different searches
paragraphs: Parents in the Kingdom type "IGCSE tuition near me" and mean something more precise than the words suggest. In Riyadh, Jeddah or the Dammam–Khobar–Dhahran cluster, there is usually somebody nearby who will teach maths. What is scarce is somebody who has taught Cambridge 0580 Paper 2 and knows that the non-calculator paper is where the method marks go, or who has marked Edexcel 4MA1 and can tell you in ten minutes whether your child's working would earn credit. Distance is not the constraint. Specification knowledge is.

Outside those three population centres the problem changes shape. A family in Ha'il, Najran, Jazan, AlUla or Yanbu may have no IGCSE specialist within a two-hour drive for a given subject, because the only people teaching that specification locally are the two or three teachers at the one school that offers it, and they are already teaching your child. Asking the market for somebody closer produces a general science graduate, not a 0625 Physics teacher. That is the honest reason online teaching exists for this market, and it is worth saying before anything else.

This page is built backwards from the mark scheme. Rather than describing tutoring in general terms, it names the four places IGCSE candidates in Saudi schools most reliably lose marks — command terms read as topics, method marks skipped on the non-calculator paper, the practical component nobody revises, and a tier entry that puts a ceiling on the grade before Year 11 begins. For each one it sets out what the fix involves, roughly how many sessions it tends to take, and what the market charges for that kind of teaching in SAR.

Money is treated the same way. Advertised rates in the Kingdom run from around SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects, and the spread is not random: it tracks subject scarcity, level, marking experience and whether the tutor is building travel time into the hour. Knowing which of those you are paying for is the difference between a sensible decision and a guess. Every figure on this page is an advertised market rate from a named source type, never a quote from IB Gram.

Delivery is online, and stated plainly rather than buried. IB Gram teaches Saudi families one-to-one over live video; we do not arrange home visits in the Kingdom, since that is a service we offer only in India. The practical consequence is that a family in Khamis Mushait and a family in KAFD draw from the same pool of subject specialists, and both pay for teaching rather than for a car journey. It also means the pool is not capped by who happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of your district, which is the single constraint that does most damage to a search for a scarce specification in a smaller Saudi city.

igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: An IGCSE sits between two other things: the programme that fed into it and the qualification that follows. Both change what tuition should be doing. These are the four stages Saudi families most often ask about, with what each one actually demands of a student in the Kingdom.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme assesses against criteria rather than papers, in bands that reward inquiry, communication and reflection. A student can do well in it and still arrive at an IGCSE paper unprepared for timed, closed-book writing against a mark scheme. The transferable strength is investigation and extended reasoning; the gap is examination technique and the discipline of answering the question actually asked.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in Riyadh and Jeddah run the Middle Years Programme and then move students into either Cambridge IGCSE or the Diploma Programme, and families frequently find the first IGCSE mock is the first timed paper their child has ever sat. Tuition in the term before that switch is usually about converting criterion-based writing habits into paper-shaped answers, not about new content.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is a two-year course assessed by syllabus code, with each subject built from a specified set of components. Many subjects are tiered: Core is graded C to G, Extended is graded A* to E. The component list differs between subjects and sometimes between schools, so the first useful question about any Cambridge subject is which papers the school has actually entered a candidate for.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge candidates in Saudi Arabia sit the June series as the main sitting, with November available for resits and November-entry candidates. The February and March series that appears in a great deal of online guidance is an India-only arrangement and is not open to a Saudi candidate, which is one of the more damaging pieces of misinformation circulating about this qualification in the Kingdom.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE grades on the 9 to 1 scale and uses its own specification codes — 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry. Paper structures, formula provision and the balance between short-answer and extended-response items differ from the Cambridge equivalents, so a tutor who knows one board well is not automatically useful on the other without preparation.
programmes.countryNote: Schools in the Kingdom pick boards subject by subject, and a single candidate can end up sitting Cambridge sciences and Edexcel Mathematics in the same June series. Families moving between international schools in Riyadh, Jeddah or Al Khobar mid-course sometimes change board mid-subject, which is the single most disruptive transfer scenario in this qualification and the one worth planning for in writing.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma Programme is where IGCSE grades cash out. Higher Level subject choices are made on the strength of IGCSE performance, and a student who scraped an Extended-tier grade in a science will find the Higher Level version of that subject assumes fluency they never built. Mathematics is the sharpest example: the choice between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation is effectively decided at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma Programme schools in the Kingdom sit the May session, and their internal deadlines for subject selection fall well before it. For a Saudi family, the practical sequence is that IGCSE results arrive, Higher Level choices are confirmed by the school's Diploma Programme coordinator, and any gap left by a weak IGCSE grade has to be closed in the break rather than during the first Diploma term.

igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Saudi families most often ask for by name, with the syllabus or specification codes and where the marks actually go. The description is deliberately about assessment rather than content: a tutor who cannot tell you which paper is hurting your child is not the right tutor.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The non-calculator paper is where most of the damage happens. Students who can reach a correct answer on a calculator lose the method marks that are awarded for setting out the steps, and lose them silently, because the final answer looks right in their head. Algebraic manipulation, surds, indices and exact-form answers are the recurring weak points.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Higher Level Mathematics, 0606 introduces calculus, vectors and more demanding trigonometry. It is the best available bridge into Analysis and Approaches, and it punishes students who learned Extended-tier algebra as a set of procedures rather than as something they can rearrange under pressure.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Two distinct problems sit in this subject. The first is the practical component — whether a candidate sits the alternative to practical paper or a laboratory paper, it rewards experimental reasoning that is never revised. The second is multi-step numerical work where units and rearrangement decide the mark more often than physics does.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: 0620 examines definitions strictly. A nearly-right definition of an ionic bond or of a reversible reaction earns nothing, and students who revise by reading rather than by writing out definitions discover this in the examination. Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables are the standard loss areas.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The content is memorable, which is the trap: students revise the recall and skip the data questions. Graph interpretation, experimental design, control variables and the specific command terms that separate describing a trend from explaining it are where strong students still lose a grade band.

subjects.name: Combined and Coordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 · 0654)
subjects.description: Taken where a school cannot timetable three separate sciences, these award one or two grades across all three disciplines. Tuition here is almost always triage: identifying which of the three strands is dragging the combined grade down, then teaching that strand's papers rather than spreading effort evenly across everything.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response are marked for reading and for writing separately, and a confident writer who does not evidence close reading of the passage caps out quickly. The usual gap is selecting and using textual detail rather than paraphrasing the passage back at the examiner.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · 0511)
subjects.description: A completely different examination from 0500, with its own mark scheme and its own failure pattern: precise information transfer, summary writing to a word limit, and register. Students placed in 0510 when they could manage 0500 frequently discover the ceiling too late to change entry.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 · 0450)
subjects.description: Both subjects are won and lost on the data-response and case-study questions, where command terms carry the marks. Analyse, evaluate and discuss each demand a different structure, and a well-informed answer written to the wrong command term scores in the bottom band regardless of how much the student knows.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 · 0984)
subjects.description: The written papers examine pseudocode, trace tables, logic and data representation, and most candidates are far stronger at writing working code than at reading somebody else's and predicting its output. Trace-table practice is the single highest-yield intervention in this subject.

subjects.name: Geography and History (Cambridge 0460 · 0470)
subjects.description: Both reward structure over volume. Geography needs case-study detail deployed to a specific question rather than recited; History needs source evaluation that engages with provenance and purpose. In both, the extended-response question is where the grade is decided and where timing collapses.

igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsTitle: What a nearby IGCSE specialist looks like, city by city
igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: "Near me" means something different in each of these places, because the local supply of IGCSE teaching differs sharply. The notes below describe what families in each area usually find when they look locally, and what they end up looking for instead.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest local pool in the Kingdom, and still thin by specification. Riyadh is roughly an hour across in traffic, so an Al Olaya family and an Al Narjis family have very different options at 5pm even when the advertised tutor is the same person.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, which makes a single evening slot workable for one household and impossible for the next. Cambridge provision is well established here, so board-specific tutoring matters more than general subject tutoring.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market behaving as three cities. Families live in one and attend school in another, and compound timetables add a layer of their own. The practical effect is that scheduling, not supply, is usually the binding constraint here.

regions.name: Jubail and Ras Tanura
regions.note: Industrial-city populations with a narrow set of schools, which means a subject offered by one school is often offered by nobody else within reach. Outside specialists are the normal arrangement rather than the exception for scarcer IGCSE subjects.

regions.name: Al Ahsa and Qatif
regions.note: Al Ahsa sits roughly an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, far enough that a weekday in-home slot is unrealistic for most households. Families here tend to search for availability on a weekday evening rather than for proximity.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About 25km apart at altitude in 'Asir, sharing one catchment. The combined pool of IGCSE teachers for any single specification is small, and a family needing a 0625 Physics specialist will usually not find one who is not already employed at their own school.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: Mid-course arrivals are the defining pattern in the north-west: families relocate part-way through Year 10 or Year 11 and need to catch up on a specification their previous school did not follow. The gap is content sequencing, not ability.

regions.name: Madinah, Makkah, Taif and Yanbu
regions.note: Makkah sits roughly 80km east of Jeddah and Thuwal lies north of it on the coast, so some families commute into the Jeddah school market and keep tuition separate from the school run entirely. Evening availability at home is what they are buying.

schoolClusters.note: Riyadh's international sector covers British, American and IB provision, with several schools running Cambridge IGCSE into either A Levels or the Diploma Programme. Subject availability varies by campus, and a school that offers a subject at Core tier may not run the Extended papers in the same year.

Jeddah has long-established British, German, American and Indian international schools, and Cambridge provision is common. Thuwal serves the King Abdullah University of Science and Technology campus community, which brings a steady flow of mid-year arrivals into the western school market.

The International Schools Group operates several campuses across the Dammam–Khobar–Dhahran area and in Jubail, and not every campus runs the same programmes. British and Cambridge curricula are well represented, and compound schooling shapes the study week for a large share of these families.

igcse-tuition-near-me.modesIntro: Three ways families use IGCSE tuition in the Kingdom, each priced and scheduled differently. The right one depends on what the diagnostic finds, not on what sounds most thorough — paying for weekly teaching when the problem is a single component is the most common way families overspend.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a fixed slot
modes.description: A recurring session on the same evening each week, pinned to Arabia Standard Time so it does not drift when a tutor's own country changes its clocks. This is the right shape when the gap is content: a student who has fallen behind the scheme of work, or who is sitting Extended-tier papers on a Core-tier foundation and needs the missing year rebuilt in sequence.
bullets: Same tutor, same time, pinned to Saudi local time
Written work marked between sessions, not inside them
A short written note to the parent after each session

modes.title: Single-component paper clinic
modes.description: A short block aimed at one named paper — the 0580 non-calculator paper, the 0625 alternative to practical, the 0455 data-response question. Four to six sessions, each built on a timed attempt the student has already made and the tutor has already marked. Cheaper than a term of weekly teaching and more effective when the diagnosis is narrow.

modes.title: Pre-series intensive block
modes.description: A compressed run of sessions in the weeks before the June or November series, usually two or three a week across one or two subjects. Content teaching is largely over by this point; the work is paper discipline, question selection, timing and the last tranche of definitions. Advertised rates for this kind of block are usually quoted at a premium in this market.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week on a short horizon

sections.heading: What a "near me" search is actually asking, and the honest answer
paragraphs: The literal answer first. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch anywhere in the Kingdom, and no tutor will be arriving at a Saudi address. IGCSE tuition through IB Gram is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Arabia Standard Time, and matched by specification rather than by postcode. If what you need is somebody physically in the room, this is not that service, and it is better to know in the first paragraph than in the fourth.

What makes that worth considering is the arithmetic of supply. For any single IGCSE specification in any single Saudi city, the number of people who have taught it to examination is small, and most of them are employed full-time by the schools that offer it. A family searching within a 20-minute drive is not choosing from the market; it is choosing from whoever lives nearby and is willing to travel in the evening. That filter has nothing to do with whether the person knows Paper 2 of your child's syllabus.

Removing distance from the selection changes what the filter is made of. A household in Khamis Mushait and a household in KAFD draw from the same pool, and both can insist on the thing that actually predicts progress — that the tutor has taught or marked the exact components the school has entered the candidate for. The question stops being "who is close?" and becomes "who has seen this mark scheme applied to fifty scripts?", which is a question a family can ask and verify.

The rest of this page is written on that basis. It does not argue that online teaching is better in the abstract. It names what goes wrong in IGCSE papers, works out what fixing each thing involves, prices it against what the Saudi market advertises, and leaves the comparison to you.

sections.heading: Failure one: the command term is read as a topic
paragraphs: Ask a Year 11 student what "evaluate" requires and most will describe the topic the question was about. That gap is the largest single source of lost marks across Economics 0455, Business Studies 0450, Geography 0460, History 0470 and the extended-response questions in all three sciences. The student knows the material. The mark scheme is paying for a specific operation performed on the material, and performing a different operation scores in the bottom band however much content is on the page.

The mechanics are worth being concrete about. "State" wants a fact with no justification and no credit for extra. "Describe" wants the shape of a pattern without causes. "Explain" wants a causal chain where each link is examinable. "Analyse" wants the chain broken into parts and the relationship between them made explicit. "Evaluate" and "discuss" want a judgement that is supported and that acknowledges what weighs against it. A six-mark "evaluate" answered as a long "describe" typically earns two of the six.

This is also the failure mode that most rewards tuition, because it is technique rather than content and it transfers across subjects. A student who learns to read the command term first, convert it into a structure, and then select content to fill that structure will usually see movement across several papers at once. Four to six sessions working through real mark schemes against the student's own marked attempts is a normal course of treatment, which is why this is the cheapest of the four failures on this page to address.

The diagnostic test for a tutor here is simple. Hand them a six-mark question from your child's specification and ask what the mark scheme rewards. A specialist answers in terms of the mark allocation and the command term. A generalist answers in terms of the topic.

sections.heading: Failure two: method marks given away on the non-calculator paper
paragraphs: Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 both split Mathematics across a paper where a calculator is permitted and one where it is not, and the non-calculator paper is where capable students bleed marks. The pattern is consistent: the candidate performs the manipulation mentally or in fragments, writes a single line, and arrives at a correct or nearly-correct answer. The mark scheme awards marks for the intermediate steps. An unsupported right answer scores less than fully-worked wrong one in a surprising number of question types.

Underneath the presentation problem is usually a real algebra problem. Surds, indices, exact-form answers, rearranging before substituting, and fractional work without a calculator all depend on fluency that was supposed to be built in Year 9. When it was not, the student compensates with a calculator throughout Year 10, and the compensation stops working in one specific examination. This is why the non-calculator paper is a diagnostic as much as an assessment: it reveals exactly which earlier skills never set.

Fixing it is slower than fixing command terms, because it is content rather than technique. A realistic plan is a term of weekly work: rebuilding the algebra in sequence, then re-sitting past non-calculator papers under timed conditions with the working marked line by line rather than the answers ticked. Families who buy a pre-series intensive block for this instead usually find the block gets spent on arithmetic that should have been secure a year earlier.

There is a scarcity consequence too, and it shows up in the price. Mathematics tutors who are comfortable teaching exact-form work and algebraic rigour without a calculator are a narrower group than those who can teach the syllabus, and advertised rates for senior-school examination mathematics in the Kingdom sit well above the general tutoring bands as a result.

sections.heading: Failure three: the practical component nobody revises
paragraphs: Every IGCSE science carries an assessment of experimental skill, and in Saudi schools it is the component least likely to have been practised to time. Whether a candidate sits an alternative to practical paper or a laboratory-based paper depends on what the school has entered, and families often do not know which until the examination timetable arrives. Either way, the component carries real marks and tests a skill set that is not in the revision guide: reading a scale, identifying a control variable, spotting the flaw in a described method, explaining an anomalous result.

The reason it goes unrevised is structural rather than lazy. Content revision has a clear object — a textbook chapter, a set of definitions, a past-paper topic list. Experimental reasoning has none, so students default to what they can see. Laboratory time at school is also finite and is usually spent performing experiments rather than analysing somebody else's flawed method, which is what the paper actually asks for. A student can have done the experiment and still be unable to answer a question about doing it.

This component tutors well online, which is counter-intuitive enough to be worth explaining. The paper does not ask the candidate to handle apparatus; it asks them to interpret a described set-up, read values from a diagram of an instrument, process results into a table, plot and interpret a graph, and criticise a method. All of that is screen work. A tutor who has marked 0625 or 4PH1 practical papers can work through twenty described methods in a few sessions and show the student the pattern in what the mark scheme rewards.

The session count is small and the payoff is disproportionate, which makes it the single best-value intervention in the three sciences. Four sessions per subject is typical, and it is worth doing before the final term rather than during it.

sections.heading: Failure four: a tier entry that caps the grade before Year 11 starts
paragraphs: This is the only failure on the page that is not the student's. Many Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered, and the tier decides the available range of grades. Core is graded C to G: a candidate entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C however well they perform. Extended is graded A* to E. Edexcel grades on the 9 to 1 scale with its own Foundation and Higher structure in some subjects. The entry is a school decision, often made in Year 10, and it is reversible only before the entry deadline.

Families discover this at different moments, and the moment matters enormously. Discovered in the autumn term of Year 11, a Core entry can usually be changed, and the work is to build the extra content and demonstrate to the school that the student can cope with the harder paper. Discovered after entries close, nothing can be changed for that series, and the realistic options are to accept the ceiling or to sit the Extended papers in the November series. The second option has knock-on effects on Diploma Programme or A Level admission timing.

The conversation to have with the school is narrow and specific. Ask, in writing, which tier your child is entered for in each subject, which component codes make up that entry, and what the deadline for changing it is. Ask what evidence the school would want in order to move a student up a tier. None of this is adversarial; schools make tier decisions on the information they have in Year 10, and a student's trajectory in Year 11 is new information.
The table below sets out what each entry route makes available. It is the single most consequential piece of information on this page, and most families in the Kingdom are never shown it.

sections.heading: What fixing each of these costs, and what moves the number
paragraphs: Advertised rates for private tuition in the Kingdom span a wide band, and the spread confuses parents more than the level does. Published figures run from roughly SAR 35 an hour on budget online platforms and around SAR 50 for general primary tuition, up to SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects, with subject-specialist and examiner-experienced tutoring advertised in the SAR 180 to 220 range by tutoring companies. Some international providers quote in USD, commonly around 60 dollars an hour, which lands near the top of the local band once converted.

Those are advertised rates published by platforms, marketplaces and tutoring companies as marketing. They are not a market average, they are not audited, and none of them is IB Gram's price — your own quote depends on the subject, the level and the tutor, and you are told it before anything is booked. What the bands are genuinely useful for is reading a quote: knowing where a number sits in the published range tells you what is being charged for.

Four things move the figure, in roughly this order of weight. Subject scarcity comes first: a 0625 Physics or Additional Mathematics specialist is a smaller population than a Biology one, everywhere. Marking experience comes second, because a tutor who has applied a mark scheme to other people's scripts teaches to it differently. Level comes third, with examination years above pre-IGCSE years. Travel comes fourth, and it is the one families in Riyadh and Jeddah pay most for without noticing: an in-home tutor crossing the city at 5pm is pricing the journey into the hour.

Read against the four failures above, the practical consequence is that the cheapest intervention is not the cheapest hourly rate. A four-session paper clinic with a specialist at the top of the band costs less in total than a term of weekly general tutoring at the bottom of it, and it addresses something specific. sections.heading: One-to-one against a small group, priced per failure fixed
paragraphs: Group classes are cheaper per hour and are genuinely the better buy in one specific case: when several students share the same gap and the gap is content delivery. A group of four Extended-tier candidates who all missed a term of 0620 Chemistry can be taught that term together, and the per-head cost falls substantially. Nothing about one-to-one teaching is superior for broadcasting content that everybody in the room needs.

The economics invert as soon as the gap is diagnostic. Three of the four failures on this page are individual: your child's specific command-term habit, your child's specific algebra hole, your child's specific misreading of a practical method. A group session cannot mark four different scripts line by line in an hour, so it teaches the average student in the room. Families frequently buy a term of group classes, see no movement, and then buy the one-to-one sessions they needed anyway — which is the most expensive route to the same place.

The honest comparison is per unit of problem solved rather than per hour. Six one-to-one sessions aimed at a named paper, with a marked script in front of the tutor each time, is a complete intervention with an observable before and after. Twenty group hours covering a syllabus is a different product entirely. Both can be the right purchase; they are not substitutes, and the per-hour comparison that makes group work look obviously cheaper is comparing two unlike things.

There is a scheduling dimension too. A group runs when the group can meet, which in the Kingdom usually means a weekend or a fixed weekday evening that suits the provider. One-to-one runs when your household can, which matters when the school run in your district finishes late and the realistic window is narrow.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE grades get read later: equivalency, Qudurat and Tahsili
paragraphs: Almost nothing in the Saudi tutoring market explains what happens to these grades afterwards, which is strange, because it changes which subjects are worth defending. An international school certificate does not automatically count as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. It goes through an equivalency decision — mu'adalah — issued by the Ministry of Education, and that decision is what allows a Saudi university to treat the qualification as comparable. This applies to the IB Diploma, to A Levels and to an American high school diploma alike.

Alongside it sit the Qiyas tests, run by the National Center for Assessment under the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content, and is sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects — mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English — and its content follows the Saudi national curriculum.

That last sentence is the one worth reading twice. An IGCSE student has studied the same scientific material in a different order, with different emphases and different framing. Tahsili asks for it the way the national curriculum sequences it, which is why international-curriculum candidates frequently find it harder than their own examinations, despite being well taught. Preparation is translation work rather than relearning: mapping what the student already knows onto the structure the test expects. Starting it late is the standard mistake.

Universities publish their own admission criteria combining school grades with these test results, and the weightings differ by institution and by programme. No specific threshold or formula appears on this page, deliberately — they vary and they change, and a parent who acts on a number from a tutoring site is acting on something unreliable. Check the university's own published criteria, and treat any site that advertises an admission outcome with real scepticism.

sections.heading: When to start, counted by year group
paragraphs: The useful question is not whether tuition helps but what it should be doing at each stage, because the answer changes completely across four school years. In the Middle Years Programme the work is pre-emptive: building timed closed-book writing and the habit of answering the question asked, so the first IGCSE mock is not also the first real paper. Almost no family buys tuition at this point, and it is the cheapest place to spend.

In Year 10 the priority is the tier decision and the algebra foundation. This is the year in which a Core-tier entry gets made, and the year in which the mathematics that the non-calculator paper will test either sets or does not. Work here is content-shaped and weekly. Year 11 autumn is the last point at which a tier entry can realistically be changed and the last point at which a term of missing content can be rebuilt in sequence rather than patched.

By the spring term of Year 11 the arithmetic has changed. Content teaching is mostly behind the student, and the available marks sit in technique: command terms, timing, question selection, the practical component, and the definitions that are examined strictly. A paper clinic or a pre-series block is the right instrument. Starting in this term is not too late, but what it can achieve is narrower, and any tutor who claims otherwise is selling rather than teaching.

After the June series, two decisions arrive at once: whether to resit in the November series, and whether the IGCSE grades support the Higher Level choices the student wants in DP1. The break between IGCSE and the Diploma Programme is the highest-leverage fortnight in the whole sequence, and it is the one families most often leave empty.

sections.heading: When nobody nearby teaches it: how the match actually gets made
paragraphs: The process is deliberately unglamorous. You tell us the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component list, and the specific thing that is going wrong — ideally with a marked script or a mock paper. We look for a tutor who has taught or marked those components, not that subject. A free trial lesson follows, and it is a working session: the tutor reads the script, tests a hypothesis about what is being lost, and tells you what they think the plan is. If the hypothesis is wrong, you have lost an hour and learned something.

Sometimes no specialist is free for the slot a household needs, and saying so is better than improvising. The Sunday-to-Thursday week plus a late school run in a dense district can leave a window of forty minutes on two evenings, and a tutor whose own working week runs Monday to Friday in another country may simply not be able to meet it. In that case the options are an earlier slot, a different tutor with a wider window, or a weekend session — and occasionally a wait. A generalist booked into the gap is not a solution.

Scheduling is pinned to Arabia Standard Time, which does not change all year. A tutor in a country that puts its clocks forward will see their own slot move twice a year; your family's will not. For a tutor in India, who is two and a half hours ahead of Saudi local time, a 6pm Riyadh session is a workable 8.30pm. For a tutor in the United Kingdom the offset moves between two and three hours, which is exactly why the slot is fixed in Saudi terms rather than theirs.

After that it is ordinary teaching. A session a week, written work marked between sessions rather than during them, a short note to the parent afterwards, and a review after a month against the thing the diagnostic identified. If the match is wrong, you change tutor; that is a normal request and not a complaint.

process.title: Send the script, not the symptom
process.description: A marked mock paper, a report, or even a photograph of a question your child could not do tells us more than a description of the problem. Include the board, the syllabus code and the tier if you know them. If you do not know the tier, that is the first thing to ask the school in writing.

process.title: A free trial lesson that does diagnostic work
process.description: The trial is an hour of teaching with a purpose: the tutor reads the evidence, forms a view about which component is leaking and why, tests it against the student, and says what the plan would be. You hear the reasoning, and your child meets the person before anything is committed to.

process.title: Agree the narrowest plan that fits the problem
process.description: A paper clinic if the diagnosis is one component, weekly teaching if a term of content is missing, a pre-series block if the content is done and the technique is not. The plan names the papers it is aiming at and how many sessions it expects to need, so it can be judged rather than renewed by default.

process.title: Fix the slot in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: The session is booked against Saudi local time, inside the Sunday-to-Thursday week, so it holds when the tutor's own country changes its clocks. Rescheduling a single session for a school trip or an internal examination is routine; moving the regular slot permanently needs a little notice.

process.title: Review against the diagnostic after a month
process.description: The same paper, or an equivalent one, sat again under timed conditions and marked. Either the component has moved or it has not, and both answers are useful. A plan that is not working gets changed or stopped; continuing by inertia is how families end up paying for a year of no progress.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the component, not the subject
whyPoints.description: The match is made against the papers your child is sitting — 0580 Paper 2, the 0625 alternative to practical, 4CH1 Paper 1 — rather than against the subject name. That is the variable that predicts whether a tutor can tell you where the marks are going, and it is the one most providers never mention.

whyPoints.title: The price is explained before it is charged
whyPoints.description: You are told the rate for your subject and level before anything is booked, and told what is driving it: scarcity, marking experience, level. The advertised SAR bands on this page come from platforms and tutoring companies and are published here as market context, never as our quote.

whyPoints.title: Nothing assessed is ever written for a student
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. No tutor will write, redraft or complete coursework, a Middle Years Programme Personal Project or any assessed component. Several providers competing for this search do exactly that, and a school that detects it treats it as malpractice.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Saudi week, not retrofitted to it
whyPoints.description: Slots sit inside a Sunday-to-Thursday school week and are pinned to Arabia Standard Time, which does not shift all year. A tutor whose own working week cannot meet that window is not offered, which is a smaller pool and a more honest one than pretending any tutor can teach at any hour.

whyPoints.title: Claims you can check, and none you cannot
whyPoints.description: No success percentages, no star ratings, no tutor headcounts, no grade promises. What we will tell you is which components a tutor has taught or marked, and what the trial lesson found. Any provider quoting a figure without telling you the sample, the date and the method is quoting marketing.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE certificate need Ministry of Education equivalency on its own, or only the qualification above it?
faqs.answer: Equivalency matters at the point a student applies to a Saudi university, and that application rests on the final school-leaving qualification — an IB Diploma, A Levels or an American high school diploma — rather than on the IGCSE certificate sat two years earlier. The IGCSE result functions as evidence inside that package and as the gateway to the qualification that follows. The practical implication is that IGCSE grades are worth defending for what they open up at the next stage, and that the equivalency paperwork is a final-school-year task. Your school's counsellor and the Ministry's own published guidance are the right sources for the current procedure.

faqs.question: Why does Tahsili feel harder to an IGCSE student than the 0620 Chemistry paper did?
faqs.answer: Because the content overlaps but the framing does not. Tahsili's science and mathematics material follows the Saudi national curriculum, which sequences topics differently, emphasises different areas and asks questions in a different style from a Cambridge or Edexcel specification. A student who scored well on 0620 has met most of the chemistry, but met it organised around Cambridge's syllabus structure and examined with Cambridge's command terms. The work is translation rather than relearning: mapping what the student already holds onto the structure the test expects, and practising the question style. It is manageable, and it takes longer than families expect because nobody warns them in advance.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subject choices make the Tahsili science coverage less of a jump later?
faqs.answer: Taking the three separate sciences rather than a combined award leaves a student holding physics, chemistry and biology as distinct bodies of knowledge, which maps more directly onto how Tahsili separates them. Adding Additional Mathematics 0606 alongside 0580 covers calculus and more demanding trigonometry early, which helps with the mathematics strand. Keeping English at a level that stretches the student matters too, since the test includes an English component. None of this is a reason to pick subjects a student will do badly in — a strong combined-science grade beats three weak separate ones — but where the choice is genuinely open, separate sciences leave fewer gaps to close.

faqs.question: Does Qudurat test anything an IGCSE candidate has actually been taught?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense of syllabus content. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, measures verbal and quantitative reasoning — pattern recognition, inference, numerical manipulation under time pressure — rather than a body of taught material. An IGCSE candidate has met most of the underlying numerical skill in Mathematics, but has not met the format, the pacing or the question style. Preparation is therefore about familiarity and speed rather than about learning new topics. It is sat in Arabic or in English, and the choice of language is worth making deliberately rather than by default, particularly for a student whose schooling has been entirely in English.

faqs.question: How do overseas universities read an IGCSE statement of results alongside the qualification above it?
faqs.answer: As context and as a prerequisite check. Overseas admissions tutors look primarily at the final qualification — Diploma points, A Level grades — but they read IGCSE grades to see whether a subject prerequisite was met and to sanity-check a predicted grade. A string of strong IGCSEs behind a modest prediction reads differently from the reverse. Some courses also specify a minimum grade in Mathematics or English at this level regardless of what follows. The practical consequence is that an IGCSE grade is rarely decisive by itself but is frequently the thing that makes a borderline application coherent, which is an argument for not writing off a weak subject early.

faqs.question: What should a Middle Years Programme student fix before the first IGCSE term starts?
faqs.answer: Two habits, and neither is content. The first is writing to time with the book closed: criterion-based assessment rewards process and reflection, and a student can be two years into the Middle Years Programme without ever having produced a finished piece of work in forty minutes under pressure. The second is answering the question actually asked rather than the topic it mentions, which is the command-term skill IGCSE papers are built on. A fortnightly session in the final Middle Years Programme year, working on timed responses to real IGCSE questions, is low-cost and prevents the most predictable shock of the first mock.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start IGCSE tuition in the spring term of Year 11?
faqs.answer: No, but what it can do is narrower and worth being honest about. Rebuilding a missing term of content in sequence is no longer realistic; the available marks are in technique. That means command terms and answer structure, timing and question selection, the practical component, and the definitions that are examined strictly. A paper clinic aimed at one or two named components can move a grade boundary's worth of marks in a few weeks. What it cannot do is substitute for a year of teaching, and any tutor who suggests otherwise in this term is selling rather than diagnosing.

faqs.question: What does a Year 10 student need that a Year 9 student starting early does not?
faqs.answer: Year 10 work has a deadline attached to it that Year 9 work does not: the tier entry. A Year 10 student needs evidence built, in the subjects where a Core or Foundation entry is a live possibility, that they can handle the harder paper — because the school will decide on the evidence it has. A Year 9 student is still building the algebra and literacy foundations that make that evidence possible, with no entry decision looming. The same tutoring looks different as a result: Year 9 is sequence and fluency, Year 10 is sequence and fluency plus demonstrable performance on Extended-tier questions before the deadline.

faqs.question: When does an IGCSE grade start to limit Higher Level choices in DP1?
faqs.answer: At the point the school confirms subject selection, which happens before the Diploma Programme begins rather than during it. A school will usually want to see a strong Extended-tier grade before placing a student into Higher Level Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or a Higher Level science, because the Higher Level course assumes fluency rather than building it. A borderline IGCSE grade does not always close the door, but it moves the conversation to what the student will do in the break. That is the window in which a specific prerequisite gap can be closed, and it is the one most families leave empty.

faqs.question: What should an IGCSE candidate do in the break before DP1 begins?
faqs.answer: Close one named gap rather than revise generally. If Higher Level Mathematics is the plan and the 0580 algebra was shaky, spend the break on algebraic fluency and the beginnings of calculus. If a Higher Level science is the plan and the practical component was weak, work on experimental reasoning, since the Diploma's internal assessment leans on it heavily. A short intensive of six to eight sessions on one thing is worth more than a term of light revision across four subjects, and it is the cheapest point in the whole sequence to buy teaching because nothing is urgent yet.

faqs.question: What does it cost to fix one failing paper rather than tutor a whole IGCSE subject?
faqs.answer: Far less, which is why diagnosing before buying matters. A paper clinic aimed at one component typically runs four to six sessions, each built on a timed attempt the student has already made and the tutor has already marked. Weekly teaching across a term is twelve to fifteen sessions on a wider front. Advertised rates in the Kingdom for specialist examination-subject tutoring sit in the SAR 180 to 220 range according to tutoring-company listings, so the difference between those two plans is substantial in total cost even at the same hourly rate. The cheaper plan is the narrower one, not the lower rate.

faqs.question: Is a four-student group class ever better value than one-to-one for IGCSE Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, in one case: when all four students are missing the same block of content and the work is delivery. Teaching a term of Extended-tier algebra to four candidates who all missed it is efficient, and the cost per head falls sharply. The economics invert the moment the problem is diagnostic. Method marks lost on the 0580 non-calculator paper are specific to one student's working, and an hour split four ways cannot mark four scripts line by line. Families who buy group classes for an individual problem usually end up buying the one-to-one sessions afterwards, which is the most expensive path to the same outcome.

faqs.question: What happens in a free trial IGCSE lesson, and what should a parent watch for?
faqs.answer: It should be a working session rather than an introduction. The tutor reads whatever evidence you sent, forms a view about which component is leaking and why, tests that view against the student with real questions, and then tells you what the plan would be and how many sessions it should need. What to watch for is whether the tutor talks about mark allocation and command terms or about the topic. Ask what a six-mark question in your child's specification rewards. A specialist answers in terms of the mark scheme; a generalist answers in terms of the subject.

faqs.question: Why is an IGCSE Physics 0625 specialist advertised at a higher rate than a general science tutor?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, mostly. The population of people who have taught 0625 to examination, know whether a candidate is sitting the alternative to practical paper or a laboratory paper, and can predict where multi-step numerical work will break down is much smaller than the population who can teach physics. Marking experience adds to it: a tutor who has applied the mark scheme to other people's scripts teaches to it differently. Advertised rates for senior-school examination subjects in the Kingdom start around SAR 200 according to tutor-marketplace guides, against roughly SAR 55 for general online tutoring on platform listings. The gap is specification knowledge, not seniority.

faqs.question: Do advertised SAR rates usually include marking of written work between IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: Often not, and it is worth asking before booking because it changes the real cost of a plan considerably. Marking a full paper properly — annotating against the mark scheme rather than totalling a score — takes a tutor most of an hour, and some providers bill it, some fold it into the rate, and some simply do not do it. A plan built on timed papers that nobody marks line by line is not the plan it appears to be. Ask specifically: who marks the script, against what, and is that time inside the quoted hourly figure or outside it?

faqs.question: Does paying a higher hourly rate reduce the number of IGCSE sessions a student needs?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and for a specific reason: a tutor who knows the component can usually identify what is going wrong in one session rather than three, so less of the plan is spent on diagnosis. That compresses a narrow intervention meaningfully. It does not compress content. A missing term of algebra takes about as long to rebuild whoever teaches it, because the limit is how fast a student consolidates rather than how well the tutor explains. So the higher rate buys accuracy on narrow problems and buys very little on broad ones, which is a useful rule when deciding where to spend.

igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses to students across Saudi Arabia. Matching is done on the syllabus code and the components a candidate is entered for, because the teaching a 0607 Extended student needs is not the teaching a 4MA1 Higher student needs.

intro.heading: Start with the papers, because the papers decide everything else
paragraphs: An IGCSE is not a body of knowledge. It is a set of papers with a published mark scheme, and almost everything a family wants to know follows from that. Which board, which syllabus code, which tier, how many components, whether one of them is practical, whether a coursework route has been chosen: those five answers determine what good teaching looks like, how scarce the right teacher is, and therefore what an hour costs. Parents who start with the price and work towards the syllabus end up comparing quotes for different jobs. Parents who start with the components find that the price explains itself.

A worked example makes the point. Two students both say they need help with Physics. One is entered for Cambridge 0625 Extended and will sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and an alternative-to-practical paper. The other is entered for Edexcel 4PH1, which has no tier, two written papers and no separate practical component, with experimental skills examined inside the theory questions. These are different examinations with different mark schemes and different failure modes. A tutor who has taught one and not the other will teach competently and still leave marks on the table.

Lessons here are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is relevant to the money as well as the logistics. An in-home rate quoted in Riyadh or Jeddah carries a travel loading, which is a real cost to the family and buys no teaching at all, and it narrows the search to whoever happens to live within a drive of the address. Online, the search runs on the syllabus code instead, which is the only criterion that reliably predicts whether a tutor can teach the paper.

The cost of all this is not arbitrary either, and it is not mysterious once the components are in view. An hour of teaching is priced by how many people can do the job, and the number of people who can teach Extended-tier chemistry to the top grades is a small fraction of the number who can teach the Core syllabus securely. Scarcity sits at the top of the list of things that move a rate, followed by marking experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels. Only the first two change what happens inside the hour. The fourth changes only the invoice, which is worth knowing before you compare quotes that look similar and are not.

What follows is the structure of the qualification, board by board and tier by tier, then where the marks are actually lost, then what providers in this market advertise in SAR and what the hour contains at each level. After that: what schools in the Kingdom typically cannot staff, what moving into IGCSE part-way through involves, and where the line sits on coursework. No figure on this page is our price, and none of them is a market average. They are other people's advertised rates, reproduced so a quote stops being a mystery.
