igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: An IGCSE sits inside a longer route, and the two years either side of it decide how well it goes. These are the four stages a family in the Kingdom deals with, and the handover points between them are where most of the avoidable damage happens.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and equivalent
programmes.description: The three years before the course starts, assessed internally and in some schools by Checkpoint tests. Nothing here appears on a certificate, which is exactly why it gets neglected. The two things that matter later are algebraic fluency and the ability to write a paragraph that explains rather than describes. A student who arrives in Year 10 without either will spend the first term of the course catching up instead of starting it.
programmes.countryNote: Schools across the Kingdom vary widely at this stage, and families moving between them often find a Year 9 syllabus that overlaps heavily with what their child already did, or skips something assumed later. A short audit before Year 10 is cheaper than a repair in Year 11, and the summer before the course is the most productive few weeks available.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course examined at the end, reported A* to G. Several subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C. The sciences carry a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper alongside the theory papers, and mathematics is offered as 0580 or as 0607 International Mathematics. Most subjects have no coursework at all, which makes the written papers close to the whole grade.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the more common of the two boards in Saudi international schools, and the syllabus codes are the fastest way for a parent to check anything. Ask the examinations officer for the codes and the tier in writing. A school that cannot produce them quickly is a school where the entry decision has not been thought about.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same two-year shape, reported 9 to 1. Tiering appears in mathematics as Foundation and Higher; most other subjects are single tier, so there is no ceiling to choose by mistake. The sciences have no separate practical paper and examine experimental skills inside the written papers. Several subjects offer a coursework route as an alternative to one written paper, and whether a school has taken it changes the whole year.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel entries in the Kingdom are concentrated in schools following a closely British pattern, often alongside Edexcel A Levels. Because the grade scale is numeric, families comparing siblings across the two boards end up comparing A* with 9 and C with 4, which is approximate at best. Universities publish their own equivalences and those are the ones that count.

programmes.name: A Levels or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: Where the IGCSE result is actually spent. A Level and IB Higher Level courses assume specific IGCSE content, and the assumption is usually the Extended or Higher tier material rather than the Core. A student entering Higher Level Chemistry from a Combined Science background has real gaps, not a weaker grade. The subject choice window closes earlier than families expect, often during Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: This is the step where tiering comes back. A student with a strong Core grade can be told in Year 12 that the sixth-form course assumes topics the Core syllabus never covered. It is recoverable with a deliberate bridging block before the course starts, and much harder to fix once the first term is running.

igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: An IGCSE is bought partly for what it leads to, so it is worth knowing what each subject becomes after 16. These are the IB Diploma courses Saudi students most often progress into, and what the step up from IGCSE actually involves in each.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Assumes Extended or Higher tier algebra as a working tool rather than a topic. Students from 0607 Extended tend to arrive best prepared; Additional Mathematics 0606 is the strongest single predictor of a comfortable first term. From Core or Foundation, the step is a term of work before the course even starts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Lighter on proof and heavier on modelling, statistics and the graphical calculator. An Extended-tier student moves in comfortably. The surprise is the precision the mark scheme wants when a model is interpreted back into its real context, which is a writing skill as much as a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Assumes the Extended-tier mechanics and electricity content as given. The real step up is the extended written answer: Diploma papers want a mechanism explained in full sentences, where an IGCSE six-mark question wants a shorter chain. Higher Level adds fields and quantum topics with no Standard Level equivalent.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles and electrolysis from the Extended tier are assumed on day one. Organic chemistry expands enormously, and the data booklet becomes central. A student from Combined or Co-ordinated Sciences has specific missing topics rather than a general weakness, and they can be listed and taught.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The terminology load roughly doubles and the command terms get stricter. An IGCSE student used to recall questions meets papers that apply a concept to an unfamiliar organism or data set. Students who did well on 0610 definitions sometimes stall here until the answer structure is retaught.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: IGCSE Economics 0455 is good preparation for the concepts and poor preparation for the diagram discipline. Diploma papers award marks for labelled axes, correct shifts and an explicit written link between diagram and question. Higher Level adds quantitative work and a policy paper.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The tools overlap with IGCSE Business Studies 0450; the application does not. Marks come from using a tool on the stimulus in front of the student, and Higher Level adds a pre-released case study that rewards work started months ahead of the paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: A First Language English 0500 background transfers well; an English as a Second Language background needs a bridge, because the Diploma course analyses how a text produces an effect rather than testing comprehension. The individual oral is the component most students underestimate.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: IGCSE 0478 covers the groundwork in systems and algorithms. The Diploma course is more formal: abstract data structures, resource management and reasoning about algorithms on paper. Confident programmers often underperform because the paper wants argument, not working code.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: No IGCSE equivalent exists, which is why it catches students out. Together they contribute up to three points through the matrix. The Extended Essay needs a narrow, answerable research question, and the habit of justifying a claim is the one IGCSE skill that transfers directly into it.

igcse-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects families in the Kingdom ask about most, with the codes from both boards. The codes matter more than the subject names: they are what a tutor is matched on, and they are the one thing a parent can check against the school's entry in a single question.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580; Edexcel 4MA1, 4MB1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Two written papers per tier on both boards, with the current Cambridge syllabus taking one of them without a calculator. Method marks exist independently of the answer, so a student who writes only a final figure throws away marks already earned. Premature rounding is the other recurring leak.

igcseSubjects.name: International Mathematics (Cambridge 0607)
igcseSubjects.description: Written for international schools and the usual feeder into IB mathematics. It adds an investigation paper alongside the calculator and non-calculator papers, which rewards a student who can structure an unfamiliar problem rather than recall a method. Check which components your school enters.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
igcseSubjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. It front-loads calculus and trigonometry and is the best single preparation for the first Diploma term. Smaller schools in the Kingdom often cannot timetable it, which is a common reason families look outside.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625; Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Tiered on Cambridge, single tier on Edexcel
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Edexcel candidates sit two written papers with experimental skills examined inside them. Graph work earns marks every series: scale choice, best-fit lines, gradients.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620; Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Tiered on Cambridge, single tier on Edexcel
igcseSubjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry separate the candidates at the top. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper rewards precise experimental language, which is exactly what a student taught from a textbook rather than a laboratory tends to lack.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610; Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Tiered on Cambridge, single tier on Edexcel
igcseSubjects.description: Definitions are marked against the syllabus wording, so near-enough answers score nothing. Transport in plants, genetics and the human systems carry most of the content, and the data-interpretation questions are where students who revised only notes come unstuck.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654, 0653; Edexcel 4SD0)
igcseSubjects.description: The usual arrangement where a school cannot staff three separate sciences. Both are legitimate routes onward, but a student going to Higher Level or A Level science from here has specific untaught topics. List them and teach them before the sixth-form course starts, not during it.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500; Edexcel 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: A reading paper and a writing paper, with some schools taking a coursework route in place of one of them. Marks go on selecting and using evidence and on writing to a specified form and audience. Fluent writers who do not answer the exact prompt plateau in the middle grades.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510, 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: In 0510 the speaking result is reported separately; in 0511 it counts towards the grade. Which code a school enters matters for a student applying abroad, and it is a single question to the examinations officer. The listening paper is the component most often under-practised.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455) and Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Economics wants diagrams drawn properly and a written link to the question; Business Studies wants recommendations justified against the case material. Both punish definitions offered as answers. These are the two subjects most often taught in the Kingdom by a willing non-specialist.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478) and ICT (Cambridge 0417)
igcseSubjects.description: Computer Science examines pseudocode, trace tables and logic on paper as well as practical problem-solving. ICT is heavily practical and marks are lost on file management and evidence of method. Strong coders routinely lose marks for writing real code where pseudocode was asked for.

igcseSubjects.name: History (Cambridge 0470) and Geography (Cambridge 0460)
igcseSubjects.description: History is source-based and rewards using a source rather than describing it. Geography carries a skills paper and either coursework or an alternative-to-coursework paper, and the skills paper is learnable in a way the content is not. Both reward structure over volume.

igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where IGCSE candidates in the Kingdom actually are
igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: IGCSE provision in Saudi Arabia is unevenly spread, and the pattern is not simply a matter of city size. What varies between these places is which board dominates, how many sets a school can run, and which subjects quietly disappear from the option block.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest option blocks in the Kingdom and the widest board mix, with both Cambridge and Edexcel entries. Even here, Additional Mathematics and a second science at Extended tier are frequently unavailable in smaller schools, and traffic across the city shapes what evening slot a family can keep.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine of schools from the historic centre north to Obhur, with a strong British-curriculum presence alongside IB schools. Families often choose a school on commute rather than on option block, then discover the subject they wanted is not timetabled.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One school and labour market in practice: families live in one of the three and attend school in another. Cambridge entries dominate at the British-curriculum schools here, and company housing means cohorts turn over faster than elsewhere.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with international schooling attached to the plants and the port. Option blocks are narrower than in the Eastern Province cluster to the south, and mid-year arrivals part-way through Year 10 are common as contracts rotate.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: Roughly an hour and a half inland from the Dammam cluster, so a daily commute to a larger school is a serious undertaking rather than an inconvenience. Local IGCSE provision is thinner, and online subject teaching is often the only route to a scarce Extended-tier course.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: International provision is smaller than the population would suggest, and the calendar bends around the Hajj and Umrah seasons in ways that affect school attendance and family availability. Evening slots are the practical option for most of the year.

regions.name: Tabuk and the north-west
regions.note: Thin local provision across a very large area, with NEOM and the Red Sea projects bringing in staff whose children arrive mid-course. Higher-tier sciences are the hardest thing to find a specialist for anywhere in the province.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Two towns about 25km apart at high altitude in 'Asir, sharing a catchment and a small international-school market. Distance to any alternative is the binding constraint, which is the honest argument for teaching over live video rather than a selling point.

regions.name: Yanbu, Thuwal and the Red Sea coast
regions.note: Compound and campus schools serving industrial and university communities. Cohorts are small and self-selecting, so a subject can appear or vanish from the option block between one year group and the next depending on who enrolled.

schoolClusters.note: The capital carries the widest range of programmes, and several schools appear in IB directories across the Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma programmes while also entering Cambridge candidates lower down. Ask any of them which subjects are tiered and who teaches the Extended sets.

A mixed market where IB World Schools, Cambridge schools and long-established national international schools sit close together. The British International School of Jeddah is both an IB World School and a Cambridge school, which is a useful reminder that the two are not alternatives.

The Eastern Province cluster, where British and Cambridge curricula run at some campuses and the IB Diploma at others. The International Schools Group operates several campuses and they do not all offer the same programmes, so the question to ask is about the specific campus rather than the group.

igcse-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as context for the market families work inside; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied or exists.
igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways families across the Kingdom buy IGCSE teaching, set out with what each is good for. The differences matter financially: the same hourly rate buys very different value depending on which of these you are actually doing.

modes.title: Weekly work on the components the candidate sits
modes.description: One or two sessions a week per subject, running alongside the school's scheme of work and built around the specific papers on the entry. The hour is spent on what the class moved past too fast, with questions set between sessions and marked against the mark scheme. This is the mode that moves a grade over terms rather than weeks.
bullets: Built on the syllabus code and the component list, not a generic subject plan
Work set, attempted, then marked line by line rather than ticked
A short written note to the parent after each session
Same tutor and same slot, agreed in Arabia Standard Time

modes.title: A single-subject repair block
modes.description: A fixed, finite run of sessions aimed at one subject that has gone wrong, usually six to ten hours. The first session diagnoses whether the problem is content, technique or confidence, and the block targets whichever it turns out to be. Families use this instead of an open-ended commitment when the budget has to be spent precisely.

modes.title: Past-paper intensive before a series
modes.description: Short, heavier work in the weeks before the June or November series, built around full papers under timed conditions. Content teaching stops. The work becomes reading the question, choosing what to attempt first, and writing answers a mark scheme can reward. Intensive hours are typically advertised at higher rates across this market.

modes.title: A tier and entry review
modes.description: A single session, sometimes two, on the decisions rather than the teaching: which tier the entry has been made at, whether that ceiling matches the student's plans after 16, whether a coursework route has been taken, and which components the candidate will actually sit. Cheap, early, and the one piece of advice families most often get too late.

sections.heading: An IGCSE is a set of components, and that is where to begin
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a parent can hold is the list of components their child is entered for. Not the subject, not the board alone, but the papers: how many, how long, what each one asks for, and whether any of them is practical or coursework. That list is obtainable from the school in one question and it changes every conversation afterwards. A tutor can be matched against it precisely, a revision plan can be built against it, and a quote can be judged against it.

Components differ more than families expect even inside one board. A Cambridge science candidate sits a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and then either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, which are genuinely different examinations requiring different preparation. A Cambridge 0607 mathematics candidate sits an investigation paper that 0580 candidates never see. A First Language English candidate may be following a coursework route that replaces one written paper entirely, which changes the shape of the whole year.

The table below sets out what each subject group is made of and where the grade tends to leak. Read the last column carefully, because it is the part no syllabus document states plainly. A student rarely loses a grade because of one unlearned topic. They lose it in small amounts across every paper, through working not shown, answer length that ignores the mark allocation, graph axes drawn without thought, and explanations that stop one causal step short of the mark.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: the same subject, two different examinations
paragraphs: Families treat the two boards as interchangeable because schools present them that way, and for the content they largely are. For assessment they are not. The grade scale differs, the tiering differs, the practical components differ, and in several subjects the coursework options differ. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 for years and is handed an Edexcel 4CH1 candidate will teach good chemistry against the wrong paper structure, and the student will lose the marks that come from knowing how the questions are built.

The clearest divergence is in the sciences. Cambridge gives practical skills their own component, either a laboratory test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, which examines apparatus, method, sources of error and tabulated results as a distinct skill. Edexcel examines experimental skill inside the theory papers instead. A student who has spent a year preparing alternative-to-practical technique has built something an Edexcel paper will not reward in the same way, and a student who has never practised it will be badly exposed on a Cambridge entry.

The second divergence is tiering, which is covered in its own section below because it carries a grade ceiling. The third is reporting. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G and Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1. Families with children on both boards, which happens often after a school move, end up trying to compare the two directly. Do not rely on a rule of thumb: universities and sixth forms publish their own equivalences, and those published statements are what an application is read against.

sections.heading: Tiering is the one decision with a grade ceiling inside it
paragraphs: Tiering is an administrative word for a decision that can cap a child's result regardless of how well they perform. On Cambridge, mathematics and the separate sciences are entered at Core or Extended, and a Core entry cannot reach the top grades at all. On Edexcel, mathematics is entered at Foundation or Higher, and Foundation has its own ceiling. Most other Edexcel subjects are single tier, so there is nothing to get wrong.

Schools make this decision for sound reasons. A student who would be swamped by Extended papers may well secure a better outcome on Core, and a secure pass is worth more than a failed attempt at a higher grade. The problem is not the decision; it is that families are often not told plainly that a ceiling has been applied, and they discover it when a sixth form asks for a grade the entry made impossible. By then the entry window has usually closed.

So treat it as a question to ask rather than a thing to worry about. Ask which tier each subject has been entered at, ask what grade range that makes available, ask by when the entry could still be changed, and ask it in writing. If your child intends to continue the subject at A Level or at IB Higher Level, the higher tier is almost always the right answer even if the predicted grade is lower, because the sixth-form course assumes that content. A capped grade in a subject nobody will continue costs nothing; a capped grade in a subject the student needs costs a year.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost
paragraphs: A report card records the grade, not the reason. That is why so many families buy content teaching for a problem that is not about content. In a first diagnostic session the most common finding is a student who knows a good deal and is not being paid for it, because the answers they write are not the answers the mark scheme buys. Three patterns account for most of it, and all three respond to practice faster than new content does.

The first is command words. Describe, explain, compare, evaluate and justify ask for different things and are worth different amounts. A student who answers every question at roughly the same length loses marks on the long ones for stopping early and wastes time on the short ones. Explain is the costly one: it wants a causal chain, and a chain missing a link earns part of the marks or none, even when the final statement is correct.

The second is working and method. In mathematics and the sciences, marks exist for the steps, independently of the answer, so a student who writes only a final figure has thrown away marks they had already earned. The third is mechanical presentation: graph scales and best-fit lines, labelled axes, units, significant figures, tabulated results with consistent decimal places. These are examined in every series, they are learnable in a few sessions, and they are the cheapest marks on any paper. A tutor reading the student's own marked work against the published mark scheme finds all three within a session or two, which is why the first session should be diagnostic rather than a syllabus tour.
bullets: Ask for one marked long-answer question back with the mark scheme beside it
Separate the marks lost to method and presentation from the marks lost to not knowing
Check whether answer length tracks the mark allocation on the paper at all
Practise the long questions as a skill in their own right, apart from the content

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor costs in the Kingdom, and what the hour contains
paragraphs: Rates in this market are published inconsistently, which is how parents end up comparing numbers that describe different products. The table below collects what other providers advertise, with the kind of source each figure comes from and what the hour tends to contain at that level. None of these figures is IB Gram's price, and none of them is a market average. They are advertised rates: the opening position of a company that wants the enquiry.

The bottom of the range deserves scepticism rather than dismissal. A headline figure from about SAR 35 an hour for IGCSE teaching is real, and it usually describes a large roster, a non-specialist, a group session, or an introductory rate that moves once a subject specialist is assigned. That can be the right purchase for a student who needs supervised practice and company while they work. It is the wrong purchase for a student losing marks on alternative-to-practical technique, because the person in the room has to know what that paper rewards.

What moves the number upwards, roughly in order of weight: scarcity of the subject and the tier first, because Extended-tier sciences and Additional Mathematics have a small teaching pool everywhere and Core mathematics does not; then marking or examiner experience; then level, with sixth-form work above IGCSE; then whether the tutor travels, which is the one factor that adds cost without adding teaching; and finally package length. Of those, only the first two reliably change what happens in the hour. Travel changes nothing except the invoice, which is the honest financial argument for teaching delivered over live video.

sections.heading: What the higher rate actually buys, and when it is not worth it
paragraphs: A specialist rate is defensible when the thing being bought is specialist. For an Extended-tier science candidate eight weeks from the papers, a tutor who has marked that paper can say which of two plausible answers the scheme rewards and why, and that judgement is the product. For a Year 10 student who needs to be sat down and made to do the exercises, the same money buys an expert doing supervision, which a cheaper and equally diligent person could do.

The honest test is to ask what the hour is for. Supervision and company while working: the lower end of the market is fine and the saving is real. Content teaching on a topic the class rushed: a competent subject teacher, mid-range. Technique, mark-scheme reading, paper strategy, or anything to do with a practical or coursework component: pay for the specialism, because the whole value is in knowing what the examiner does with the answer. Mixing these up is the most common way families overspend and underspend at the same time, buying expensive supervision and cheap technique.

Two further pieces of arithmetic. First, frequency beats duration: two shorter sessions a week usually produce more than one long one, because the work set in between is where the learning consolidates. Second, a finite block with a stated goal is often better value than an open-ended arrangement, because it forces a diagnosis and an endpoint. A provider who never suggests stopping, reducing or switching subjects is selling hours. Ask at the end of a term what has moved, and what would happen if you stopped.

sections.heading: The subjects schools in the Kingdom quietly cannot staff
paragraphs: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. That system governs the institution. It does not tell a parent whether the person teaching Extended-tier chemistry trained in chemistry, and that is the question with a grade attached to it.

The constraint is cohort size. A subject needs enough candidates to justify a specialist and a timetable slot. Where numbers are small, one teacher covers a department, which means the hardest courses receive the least specialist attention because the generalist's time is already spread. The subjects this hits are consistent across the Kingdom: Additional Mathematics 0606, which many schools cannot timetable at all; Extended-tier physics and chemistry; computer science, where the paper wants formal reasoning rather than coding; and economics or business taught by someone who has never marked them.

There is a second, quieter version of the same problem: the subject that exists on paper but is taught in a combined set. A student entered for Extended papers while sitting in a room where most of the class is on Core will get Core teaching with extension sheets. Both problems are visible if you ask the right questions, and none of them is a criticism of a school doing its best with the numbers it has. Ask which subjects are taught by a specialist in that subject, how many candidates are in the Extended set, whether Core and Extended are taught together, and who marks and moderates the mocks.
bullets: Ask which subjects are taught by a specialist in that specific subject
Ask whether Core and Extended candidates are taught in the same room
Ask whether Additional Mathematics can be timetabled, not whether it is offered
Ask who marks the mock papers and whether anyone else moderates that marking

sections.heading: Switching into IGCSE part-way through
paragraphs: Mobility is normal in this market. Families arrive mid-course from India, the United Kingdom, Egypt, the Philippines, North America and from Saudi national-curriculum schools, and a student can land in Year 10 or Year 11 with a background that overlaps the syllabus in an awkward way. The instinct is to audit content first. In practice the assessment style is the bigger gap and the faster win, because a student who knows the material and cannot write to the mark scheme looks exactly like a student who does not know the material.

The table sets out what each background typically brings and what it typically lacks. The pattern worth noticing is that strong systems produce specific rather than general gaps. A CBSE student is often well ahead on mathematics and the sciences and has rarely met a data-response question or a practical write-up. A national-curriculum student may know more chemistry than their new grades suggest and has not been asked to explain a mechanism in English. These are identifiable, finite things, and naming them is most of the work.

Timing caps what is possible. A move early in Year 10 is a normal adjustment. A move into Year 11 is a real piece of work and depends on which components are already behind: a coursework route in progress is harder to join than a purely examined subject, and a tiered science where the new school has already entered the cohort may constrain the entry itself. Ask the new school for the scheme of work, the board, the codes and the tier on day one, and get the audit done in the first fortnight rather than at the first report.

sections.heading: Coursework, moderation and where the line sits
paragraphs: Most IGCSE subjects are examined entirely by written paper, which is why coursework surprises families when it appears. Where it exists, it is usually an alternative to one written component, chosen by the school rather than by the student: a First Language English portfolio, a Geography investigation, a History assignment. The school marks it against the published criteria and the board samples the marking to check that the school's standard is in line, adjusting the whole cohort if it is not.

That sampling process is why a school's own deadline matters more than the board's. Teachers need time to mark, to moderate internally and to assemble a sample, so the internal deadline sits well ahead of the submission date, and a student who treats the later date as the real one has made a problem for their teacher and for themselves. Ask for the internal deadline in writing and work backwards from it.

On the line itself: a tutor may teach the skills the task needs, discuss whether a question is narrow enough to answer, challenge a method that will not produce usable data, explain what a criterion is asking for, show a worked example of a different investigation, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of the work, choose the topic, supply the data, or produce text the student then submits. The school owns the supervision process and its academic honesty policy is the one that applies. Keep drafts and notes as you go: a version history is the simplest possible evidence of authorship if a question is ever raised. Any provider offering to produce the work is offering malpractice with your child's name on it.
bullets: Find out which of your child's subjects carry coursework, and which route the school chose
Ask for the school's internal deadline, not the board's submission date
A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback; the student writes every word
Keep drafts, notes and version history from the first week of the task

sections.heading: The June and November series, and starting from here
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series, which is the main sitting for candidates in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and for November-entry candidates. Cambridge also runs a February and March series, but it is an India-only series and a candidate in Saudi Arabia will not be entered for it, whatever a page written for an Indian audience says. Entries close months before the papers and the exact dates belong to your school's examinations officer, who is also the only reliable source for the internal deadlines that sit earlier still.

The decision families should make early rather than late is the resit. The gap between results and the November entry deadline is short, and a resit chosen calmly in advance is a better piece of work than one chosen in a week. If a single subject is likely to come out below what a sixth form requires, it is worth deciding in advance what you would do, which is a different exercise from hoping it will not happen.

Starting is short. Tell us the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the components, plus where the student is in the course. We arrange a free trial lesson with a specialist in that syllabus, which doubles as a diagnostic: the tutor teaches a real session, works a past-paper question, and reports back on what is missing and whether it is content, technique or presentation. You keep that summary either way. Two caveats worth stating plainly. The scarcer the specialism, the harder the slot is to fill, and when nobody suitable is free at the hour you want we will say so rather than putting a generalist in the room. And if the match is wrong after two or three sessions, tell us and we change the tutor; that is part of matching, not a complaint.

process.title: Send us the codes, not the subject names
process.description: The board, the syllabus code, the tier and the component list, plus how far through the course the student is. That is four lines from the school and it determines everything downstream. A recent marked paper is worth more than a description of the difficulty, because the marks show where the problem is rather than where it feels like it is.

process.title: A free trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: A specialist in that exact syllabus teaches a real session and works a past-paper question with the student. You receive a written summary separating content gaps from command-word problems, method marks and presentation. It is yours whether or not you continue, and it is usually the most useful hour of the whole process.

process.title: Matched on the component, not the subject
process.description: A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 is not automatically right for Edexcel 4CH1, and a tutor who has never prepared candidates for an alternative-to-practical paper should not be teaching one. We match on code and component, and the slot is checked too: a tutor whose own working day suits a Kingdom evening is still there in the final term.

process.title: A stated goal and a stated number of hours
process.description: Before anything recurring starts, an agreed objective and a shape: weekly through the term, a finite repair block, or an intensive run before a series. Knowing which one you are buying is what stops the arrangement drifting into open-ended hours that nobody reviews.

process.title: Work set between sessions and marked properly
process.description: Questions attempted, then marked against the published mark scheme rather than ticked, with the reason for each lost mark written down. That marking is the diagnosis: it tells the next session whether to teach content, rehearse a command word, or drill graph technique.

process.title: A review that can end in stopping
process.description: At the end of a block or a term: what moved, what did not, and whether to continue, reduce, change subject or stop. Sometimes the right answer is fewer hours in a different subject. Any provider whose review never arrives at stopping is reviewing its own revenue.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code is the match, and you can check it
whyPoints.description: Ask a prospective tutor which components your child sits and listen for specifics: paper numbers, tier, whether there is a practical or an alternative-to-practical paper. A specialist answers in that language immediately. It is the single easiest verification a parent can run, and it needs no expertise in the subject at all.

whyPoints.title: No travel loading in the rate
whyPoints.description: In-home tuition advertised in the large Saudi cities carries the cost of getting there, which is time nobody teaches during. Teaching over live video removes that and widens the search from people who live nearby to people who have taught the paper. In scarce subjects that is the difference between a specialist and a willing generalist.

whyPoints.title: Marked work, with reasons
whyPoints.description: Work set between sessions comes back marked against the published scheme with the reason for each lost mark written down, not ticked. That record is what turns a vague sense that a child is struggling into a list of fixable things, and it is what a parent should ask any provider to produce.

whyPoints.title: The tier question asked early
whyPoints.description: A capped entry is the most expensive administrative mistake in this qualification and it is invisible until a sixth form asks for a grade the entry made impossible. We raise it in the first conversation and tell you what to ask your examinations officer, in writing, while the window is still open.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Where a subject carries coursework, a tutor teaches the skills, questions the plan and gives feedback on the student's own draft. No part of it is written, redrafted or edited for the student, and the school's supervision process stays in charge. That boundary protects the candidate, which is why it is stated here rather than left implied.

whyPoints.title: Nothing claimed that cannot be shown
whyPoints.description: No pass rates, no star ratings, no counts of families taught. Every SAR figure on this page is another provider's advertised rate, labelled with the kind of source it came from. What is on offer before any commitment is a free trial lesson and a written read on where the marks are going.

faqs.question: Which boards do schools in the Kingdom actually enter IGCSE candidates with?
faqs.answer: Cambridge is the more common of the two across Saudi international schools, with Pearson Edexcel International GCSE concentrated in schools following a closely British pattern, often alongside Edexcel A Levels. A few schools enter candidates with both boards in different subjects, which surprises parents who assume a school has one board. The only reliable answer is your own school's, and it comes as a list of syllabus codes from the examinations officer. Ask for that list rather than for the board name, because the codes also tell you the tier and the components, which is what any tutor needs.

faqs.question: Why can a school here offer Chemistry at IGCSE but not Additional Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Because a subject needs enough candidates to justify both a specialist teacher and a timetable slot, and Additional Mathematics 0606 is taken by a small, self-selecting group heading for A Level or IB Higher Level mathematics. Chemistry fills a set; Additional Mathematics often does not. A school may also lack a teacher comfortable with its calculus and trigonometry content, which sits above the rest of the IGCSE curriculum. If your child is heading for Higher Level mathematics and the school cannot timetable it, teaching it outside school is the usual solution and the preparation value is real.

faqs.question: What should I ask a school about IGCSE subject availability before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which subjects are taught by a specialist in that subject rather than covered by a generalist. Whether Core and Extended candidates are taught in the same room, because that quietly determines which level of teaching your child receives. Whether Additional Mathematics and a second science at the higher tier can actually be timetabled, not whether they appear in a brochure. And how many candidates are in the sets your child would join. A school that answers these specifically is a school that has thought about them.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are most often taught by a non-specialist in Saudi schools?
faqs.answer: Economics and Business Studies come first, because they look teachable by anyone with a commercial background and are in fact marked strictly on applied answers. Computer Science is next: the paper wants pseudocode, trace tables and formal reasoning, and a practising programmer is not automatically equipped for that. Then the third science in a school that can staff two, and the higher tier of whichever mathematics course the school offers. None of this is a criticism of the teachers involved, who are usually covering a gap rather than choosing one, but it is where outside specialist teaching earns its rate.

faqs.question: How does an international school's term calendar differ from the Ministry of Education school year?
faqs.answer: Ministry of Education public schools run a two-semester year starting in late August and ending in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, so two schools in the same city can have different holidays, different mock weeks and different internal deadlines. There is no single answer for a family to plan against. Use your own school's published calendar, and if you have children in both systems expect the holidays not to line up.

faqs.question: What does the Education and Training Evaluation Commission do about teaching quality, and what does it not do?
faqs.answer: School evaluation and accreditation in the Kingdom runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies, while the Ministry of Education licenses private and international schools to operate. That system governs institutions. It does not tell you who teaches the Extended chemistry set at your child's school, how large that set is, or whether anyone moderates the mock marking. Those are school-level questions, and you get the answers by asking the school directly.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects still carry coursework, and what may a tutor do with it?
faqs.answer: Most IGCSE subjects are examined entirely by written paper. Where coursework exists it is usually an alternative to one written component chosen by the school, most commonly in first language English, geography, history and some creative subjects. A tutor may teach the skills the task needs, question whether the plan will work, explain what a criterion asks for and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, redraft or edit any part of it, choose the topic or supply data. The school's supervision process and academic honesty policy are the ones that apply.

faqs.question: Can a tutor proofread an IGCSE coursework portfolio before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense of correcting it. Proofreading that changes the text makes the submitted work partly someone else's, and the consequence falls on the candidate. What a tutor can legitimately do is teach proofreading as a skill: show the student how to check their own work against the criteria, point out that a section does not yet answer the question, or note that evidence is asserted rather than used, and then have the student make the changes. The distinction is whether the student does the editing. Your school's policy may be stricter still, and it takes precedence.

faqs.question: How is IGCSE coursework moderated once the school has marked it?
faqs.answer: The school marks the work against the published criteria, then the board samples a selection to check that the school's marking matches the standard. If the sample shows the school has been generous or harsh, the board adjusts the cohort's marks accordingly, which means one student's outcome can move because of how the school marked everybody. This is why internal moderation inside a department matters, and why a small school where one teacher marks alone has less internal comparison. It is also why the school's internal deadline sits well before the board's.

faqs.question: What happens if a school suspects malpractice in a coursework submission?
faqs.answer: The school investigates under its own academic honesty policy and, where it judges there is a case, reports it to the board, which can withhold a grade in that subject or across the qualification. The process is about the candidate, not about whoever helped. This is the practical reason to keep drafts, notes, data and a version history from the first week of the task: a clear record of the student's own working is the simplest answer to a question about authorship, and it costs nothing to build as you go.

faqs.question: How is the Middle Years Programme Personal Project different from IGCSE coursework for a tutor?
faqs.answer: The Personal Project is assessed against published criteria on the process as well as the product, with a required process journal and a supervisor inside the school. IGCSE coursework is a piece of subject work marked against subject criteria. For a tutor the practical difference is that the Personal Project rewards documented reflection, so support means teaching a student to record decisions and setbacks honestly rather than tidying them away. In both cases the tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback, and the student produces every part of the work themselves.

faqs.question: What transfers when a student moves from a Saudi national-curriculum school into IGCSE?
faqs.answer: More content than families expect and less assessment technique. Mathematical procedure and a good deal of science content carry across directly. What does not carry is writing an explanation in English under time, answering a command word precisely, and reading a data-response question for what it actually asks. Start there rather than with a content audit, because a student taught the content again will still write answers the mark scheme cannot reward. Then work through the scheme of work topic by topic to find the genuine gaps, which are usually fewer than feared.

faqs.question: How does a CBSE or ICSE student adapt to IGCSE assessment style?
faqs.answer: Usually well, once the question style stops being a surprise. Such students are often ahead of the cohort on mathematics and the sciences, and behind on three specific things: data-response questions that ask for interpretation rather than recall, practical write-ups and the experimental language they need, and source-based humanities questions. The fastest route is past papers early, with the mark scheme visible, so the student meets the question style while their content advantage still gives them room. Expect the first few papers to feel disproportionately hard relative to their actual knowledge.

faqs.question: Can a student join an IGCSE course a term late and still sit the June series?
faqs.answer: Often yes, with conditions. A purely examined subject is the easiest to join, because the work is to cover the untaught topics and then practise papers. A subject with a coursework component in progress is harder, since the school's deadline may already be close. A tiered science may constrain the entry itself if the cohort is already registered. The first fortnight should be an audit against the new school's scheme of work rather than general teaching, and the honest answer on whether the higher tier is still realistic should come out of that audit.

faqs.question: What does an American-curriculum student need to catch up to enter IGCSE in Year 10?
faqs.answer: Depth and algebra, in that order. An American middle or high school background tends to produce confident presentation, discussion and project work, with less depth in any single subject than a two-year linear course assumes. Algebraic fluency is the most common specific gap, and it shows up later in physics and chemistry as much as in mathematics. A bridging block over the summer before Year 10 is the efficient fix: algebra, the specific science topics the course assumes, and an early look at what a mark scheme rewards.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to pick up after a mid-course move?
faqs.answer: The ones with cumulative content or a non-examined component. Chemistry is hard to join late because moles and bonding underpin everything after them, and a student who missed that term is not missing a topic but a foundation. Any subject with coursework already under way is harder still, because the school's deadline does not move for a new arrival. Languages with a speaking component and subjects with a practical paper also take longer, since the skill needs rehearsal rather than reading. Purely examined humanities are the easiest to join.

faqs.question: Does moving from IGCSE into the IB Diploma later depend on which tier was sat?
faqs.answer: It depends on the content the tier covered, which amounts to the same thing. Diploma courses, and Higher Level sciences and mathematics in particular, assume the Extended or Higher tier material as a starting point. A strong Core grade is a real achievement and still leaves topics the Diploma course will not teach again. It is recoverable with a deliberate bridging block before the course starts, and much harder once the first term is running. If the Diploma is the plan, treat the higher tier as part of that plan.

faqs.question: Why does an Extended-tier tutor cost more than a Core-tier one for the same subject?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, mostly. The pool of people who can teach Extended-tier chemistry or 0607 Extended mathematics to the top grades is much smaller than the pool who can teach the Core syllabus securely, and that scarcity shows up in advertised rates everywhere, not only in the Kingdom. The second factor is what the hour has to contain: Extended papers reward judgement about what a mark scheme will accept, which is knowledge of the assessment rather than of the subject. If nobody will continue the subject after 16, the cheaper option may well be the right one.

igcse-tutor.closingHeading: What to do before you compare any quotes
igcse-tutor.closingBody: Get four lines from your school: the board, the syllabus code, the tier, and the list of components your child is entered for. That single email makes every subsequent decision easier. It tells you whether a grade ceiling has been applied while there is still time to ask about it, it tells any tutor exactly what they are being asked to teach, and it turns a set of hourly rates into a comparison of the same job. Then take a free trial lesson with a specialist in that syllabus and keep the written summary of where the marks are going. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, around the Sunday-to-Thursday week, and no tutor travels to a Saudi address.

The experience shown is specific on purpose: the component taught or marked, so that a fee can be weighed against something checkable.

intro.heading: Decide what you will measure before you decide what to pay
paragraphs: The reason fees are hard to compare in this market is not that the numbers are hidden, though many of them are. It is that almost nobody tells a parent what the money is supposed to produce. A rate of SAR 200 an hour and a rate of SAR 60 an hour are impossible to weigh against each other until you know what you are watching for, and once you do know, the comparison usually settles itself inside a month. So this page runs in that order: evidence first, prices second, levers third, and the plan last.

The evidence is more concrete than families expect. Six things can be checked by a parent without any specialist knowledge: marks on the same type of past paper under timed conditions, the number of creditable mark-scheme points the student captured out of those available, whether answers now match the command term in the question, whether full working appears on calculation questions, which tier the school intends to enter, and how long a full paper takes. Four of those six move within a fortnight if the teaching is any good.

That matters because the fastest-moving number is the cheapest to fix. A student who understands chemistry and writes answers that score two out of four is losing marks to a habit, and habits respond to a handful of sessions. A student who has never met half the syllabus is in a different position and will need a term. Paying specialist rates for the first problem is overpaying; paying generalist rates for the second is wasting the term. Diagnosing which one you have is therefore the single highest-value hour in the whole arrangement.

On the prices themselves: everything quoted here is an advertised rate published by a tutoring platform, a tutor marketplace or a tutoring company. None is a verified market average, none is what IB Gram charges, and none should be treated as a benchmark. They are published because a parent deserves a band to argue from rather than a form to fill in. Where a figure is quoted, the type of source behind it is named in the same row, so you can discount it accordingly.

IGCSE is also the level where a single administrative decision moves the outcome more than any amount of teaching. Most subjects are tiered. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 splits into Core and Extended, the sciences into Core and Extended paper routes, and Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher. The tier caps the grade before the paper is sat, it is chosen by the school, and once final entries have closed it cannot be changed. A parent who understands the tier decision has more leverage over the result than one who has bought six more hours of teaching.

Delivery, so that it is not a surprise: IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, on a slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time. We do not send anybody to a Saudi address, and in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. The relevance to a page about fees is direct, because in-home arrangements price the travel whether or not the invoice itemises it, and that cost buys no teaching.

igcse-tutor-fees.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits inside a longer sequence, and the fee a family pays at each stage buys something different. The summaries below name what each stage decides, because paying at the wrong point is the commonest way money is wasted here: heavy spending in Year 11 on a problem that a term of fluency work in Year 9 would have removed.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE, assessed internally with optional Checkpoint tests at the end. Nothing here appears on a certificate, which is exactly why it is undervalued. Everything the IGSCE papers assume is built in this window: arithmetic and algebraic fluency, reading at length, writing a paragraph that answers a question, and showing working as a habit rather than under instruction. It is also the cheapest stage at which to buy teaching, because a strong generalist is enough.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom this is the stage families skip, often because a relocation lands mid-sequence and the school reports look reassuring. A student who arrives from a different system in Year 8 can have real gaps in written method that nothing in a report card exposes. Two terms of general fluency work here costs a fraction of what the same gap costs to repair in Year 11, and it does not need a scarce specialist.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, examined by syllabus code, with most subjects tiered. Mathematics 0580 runs Core and Extended routes; the sciences 0625, 0620 and 0610 each pair a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper to the tier, then add either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. First Language English 0500 and Second Language English 0510 are different qualifications with different papers, and schools occasionally enter a student for the wrong one. The code matters more than the subject name.
programmes.countryNote: Saudi candidates sit the June and November series. Cambridge also runs a February and March series, and that series is available in India only, which matters because much of the tutoring material circulating in Gulf parent groups is adapted from Indian pages and quotes those dates. Acting on it means missing the real entry window, and the only reliable source for your own deadline is your school's examinations officer.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same age band and a similar qualification, structured differently. Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher. The separate sciences 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 run two written papers each with no practical examination, assessing experimental skills inside the written papers instead. English Language A, 4EA1, pairs non-fiction and transactional writing with a literary paper. The question styles and mark-scheme wording differ enough that practice papers do not transfer between the boards.
programmes.countryNote: A family moving between a Cambridge school and an Edexcel school mid-course in the Kingdom needs this difference explained before the entry is made rather than after. The practical consequence for fees is specific: a tutor booked on the strength of Cambridge experience may be learning the Edexcel mark scheme at your expense, and that is a reasonable question to ask in a trial lesson.

programmes.name: AS and A Level, or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: What IGCSE grades are for. A Levels build directly on the subject content, and the IB Diploma builds on skills IGCSE only partly develops: extended independent writing, research, and command-term discipline across six subjects at once. Either route treats IGCSE grades as the entry condition for Higher Level or A Level study, which is why a capped tier in Year 11 narrows choices two years later even when the grade itself looks respectable.
programmes.countryNote: The sequence matters in the Kingdom because the post-16 options available locally vary sharply by city, and a student whose IGCSE profile closes a door may have no second school to try. It is worth asking a prospective post-16 school which IGCSE grades and which tiers it requires for its Higher Level or A Level groups, in writing, during Year 10 rather than Year 11.

igcse-tutor-fees.subjectsIntro: Fees vary by subject far more than by provider, and the reason is supply. The entries below name the syllabus code, the component where marks are most often lost, and whether the subject is one that commands a premium in this market. A rate quoted without reference to any of that is a rate quoted blind.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: The most commonly tutored IGCSE subject in the Kingdom and therefore the least scarce, which keeps advertised rates near the bottom of the band. The marks are lost on multi-step problems where a missing line of working costs method marks, and on the Extended paper's algebraic manipulation. Ask any prospective tutor which tier they would enter the student for and why.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: Chosen by schools pointing students towards the IB Diploma, because its calculator and investigative work sits closer to what Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches expects. Fewer tutors know it than know 0580, so it costs more for the same hour. Calculator technique is examined rather than assumed, and that is teachable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Commands a premium, because the pool of people who can teach the Extended theory paper and the practical reasoning behind the alternative-to-practical paper is smaller. The most expensive marks to recover late are in electricity and in the handling of experimental data, and the alternative-to-practical paper is almost always the component nobody has practised.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Priced similarly to Physics and for the same reason. Moles and stoichiometry are where a term is usually spent, and the Extended theory paper rewards exact wording in a way that catches fluent students. Past papers with the mark scheme read afterwards do more for the grade here than any amount of additional content.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and marked on precise terminology, which makes it look easy to tutor and hard to tutor well. A student who writes a good general account of osmosis can score two out of five because the named terms are absent. Advertised rates sit below Physics and Chemistry, and that is a supply difference rather than a difficulty one.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing with composition. The directed-writing task rewards identifying audience, purpose and form before writing a word, which is the most coachable thing on any IGCSE paper. Rates are mid-band because the supply of competent English tutors is large, but the supply who teach to this specific mark scheme is not.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English, with its own papers and its own ceiling, and schools in the Kingdom occasionally enter a student for whichever one the cohort is doing. Confirm which code your child is entered for before buying any teaching, because the preparation is not transferable and the fee for the wrong one is entirely wasted.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside Extended Mathematics by students heading for A Level Mathematics or Higher Level IB. Scarce, and priced accordingly: very few tutors in this market teach it regularly. The content bridges into A Level calculus and trigonometry, so a tutor who teaches post-16 mathematics is usually a better match than an IGCSE generalist.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Written papers covering theory and algorithm design, plus pseudocode and programming concepts. Students who code well often score poorly, because the papers want precise prose descriptions of algorithms and trace tables rather than working code. A premium subject in this market, because teachers who can mark to the paper are genuinely scarce.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A (4MA1) and the separate sciences
subjects.levels: Foundation and Higher tiers for mathematics
subjects.description: Edexcel runs no practical examination in 4PH1, 4CH1 or 4BI1, assessing experimental skills inside the written papers. The question styles and mark-scheme wording differ from Cambridge enough that past papers do not substitute for each other, so a tutor's board experience is a fair thing to price and a fair thing to question.

igcse-tutor-fees.regionsTitle: Where fees and supply differ across the Kingdom
igcse-tutor-fees.regionsIntro: Advertised rates are broadly national, but what a family can actually buy is not. The size of the local in-home pool, the number of schools competing for the same tutors and the distance a tutor would have to travel all move the real price. These notes are about the tutoring market in each place rather than about the schools.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest in-home market in the Kingdom and the most competitive, which holds advertised rates down for common subjects. The city is roughly an hour across in traffic, so a tutor's willingness to cross it is priced in, and an Extended Physics specialist in the north is effectively unavailable to a family in the south at a weekday hour.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine where families often have a genuine choice of board, which produces the Kingdom's commonest expensive mistake: a tutor hired on Cambridge experience for an Edexcel entry. Supply is reasonable for mathematics and English and thin for Computer Science and Additional Mathematics.

regions.name: Dhahran, Al Khobar and Dammam
regions.note: One school and labour market across three cities, with British and Cambridge curricula well represented. Supply here is the best outside Riyadh, and the practical consequence for a parent is leverage: it is one of the few places in the Kingdom where you can realistically compare two local quotes for the same subject and tier.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with schooling attached to the workforce. Rates reflect a small pool rather than a competitive one, and household schedules are shaped by shift patterns, so the fee negotiation is often really a negotiation about which hour a tutor will accept.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: Roughly an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, which puts it outside a comfortable daily commute. An in-home arrangement here carries a travel loading large enough to dominate the hourly rate, and that is the honest arithmetic behind teaching over a connection instead.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Families in both cities often look towards the Jeddah market for international-curriculum tutoring, which means a Jeddah rate plus a journey. Local calendars bend around the Hajj and Umrah seasons, so slot changes are better agreed a term ahead than renegotiated each time.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: New or thin provision, and in several districts no local IGCSE specialist pool at all. Mid-course arrivals are common, which raises the real cost of the first term because the first job is mapping what has been covered elsewhere before any teaching starts.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: Two 'Asir cities about 25km apart sharing one catchment and a small pool of international-curriculum teaching. Scarcity rather than competition sets the price for a specialist subject here, and for several IGCSE codes the local in-home answer is simply that nobody teaches them.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: The British International School of Jeddah is both an IB World School and a Cambridge school, Deutsche Internationale Schule Jeddah runs to Grade 12, and several long-established international schools sit alongside. For a fees page the relevant point is that boards are mixed within a few kilometres, so a tutor's board experience has to be confirmed rather than assumed.

British School Dhahran and Multinational School Dhahran follow British and Cambridge curricula, while the International Schools Group operates several campuses and the Diploma runs at the American School of Dhahran and at ISG Jubail. The density here is the reason a family can compare quotes locally in a way that is not possible in most of the Kingdom.

Schools named in international and IB directories for the capital include the following, with several running more than one curriculum across their year groups. The capital's tutoring market is the only one in the Kingdom where competition, rather than scarcity, is the main thing setting a price for a common subject.

igcse-tutor-fees.modesIntro: Each of these costs a different amount and buys a different thing, and the right one depends on which of the six measures of progress is failing. Buying the longest option first is the usual mistake. Everything below is delivered one-to-one over live video on a slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: A short diagnostic block, bought before anything longer
modes.description: Three or four sessions with one aim: find out whether the problem is content, technique or pacing, and get a specific written answer. It is the cheapest useful purchase in this market and almost nobody sells it, because a long package is easier to sell. A parent who buys this first usually spends less overall, because the term that follows is aimed at something real.
bullets: A past paper worked under time in the first session
A written finding naming the component and the behaviour costing marks
An estimate of how many sessions the fix needs, with reasoning
No obligation to continue with the same tutor afterwards

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on one subject and tier
modes.description: The standard arrangement where there is content to close: one subject, one named tutor, the same hour each week across a term. Content gaps compound and so does the fix, which is why this works where short blocks do not. It is priced per hour by almost every provider in this market, and the hourly rate is the only part worth comparing.
bullets: One tutor for the subject at the entered tier, not a rota
Work set between sessions and marked before the next one
The hour agreed in Saudi local time so it does not drift
A short note to the parent after each session

modes.title: Paper-technique sprints before a series
modes.description: A compressed run in the weeks before the June or November papers, built on timed past papers and their mark schemes rather than on content. Rates often rise closer to a series, which is scarcity pricing rather than better teaching, so booking a term early is the cheapest version of the same thing. Two subjects at most.
bullets: Timed whole papers, then the published mark scheme, then one correction
Command terms drilled rather than new topics introduced
Capped at two subjects to keep the week survivable
Honest about which subject is not worth the hours

modes.title: Coursework and portfolio feedback cycles
modes.description: Where a subject carries a coursework or portfolio component, short spaced sessions around a draft the student has already written. The tutor asks questions, reads the published criteria against the work and hands it back unchanged. This is deliberately not a drafting service, and a provider who offers to produce the piece is offering malpractice rather than value.
bullets: Feedback on the student's own draft, in the student's own words
The assessment criteria read against the work, line by line
A record of what each session discussed, so authorship stays provable
No writing, redrafting or line-by-line correction of assessed prose

sections.heading: The six things you can measure before you pay for anything
paragraphs: Begin with evidence, because a fee is only comparable once you know what it is supposed to move. The six measures below need no specialist knowledge and no access to the school's systems. A parent can check all of them from the student's own work, and between them they separate the two problems that look identical from outside: a student who does not know the material and a student who knows it and cannot be paid for it.

The fastest-moving of them is mark-scheme capture. Take a past question worth five marks, count the distinct creditable points the student made against the five available, and repeat it a fortnight later. A student losing marks to habit will improve this number inside two or three sessions, because the fix is mechanical: read the command term, count the marks, make that many separate points. A student with a genuine content gap will not move, and that distinction tells you which rate band you should be shopping in.

The slowest is pacing. Timing a student on individual questions tells you almost nothing, because the pressure of a full paper is what breaks a method. Time a whole paper under real conditions once at the start of a term and once at the end. Pacing shifts over months rather than weeks, and a provider who promises to fix it in a short block is selling something they cannot deliver. It is also the measure most often confused with weak content, which leads families to buy the wrong thing.

One measure sits outside the student's control and matters more than the other five put together, which is the tier the school intends to enter. Ask the subject teacher, in writing, every term. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade before the paper is sat, and no amount of paid teaching lifts a ceiling that has already been set. Families routinely spend a year of fees on a subject whose tier has already decided the outcome, and nobody tells them.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition is advertised at in the Kingdom
paragraphs: Every figure below is an advertised rate, published by a vendor to attract enquiries. None is a verified average of what families pay, none has a sample size or a date attached, and none is what IB Gram charges. The reason to publish them anyway is that the alternative in this market is a contact form, and a parent with no band at all cannot tell whether a quote is reasonable or opportunistic.

Read the fourth column as carefully as the second. A rate of around SAR 35 an hour on a budget platform buys an hour of attention from someone who may not know which board your child sits, let alone which tier. A rate of SAR 200 and upwards for a senior examination subject, as published in tutor-marketplace guides, usually assumes a tutor who travels, and the drive is inside that number whether it is itemised or not. Neither figure is dishonest; they are answers to different questions.

The IB rates are included for comparison rather than because they apply here. Tutoring companies in the Kingdom list IB subject tutoring from around SAR 180 an hour and Higher Level or premium tracks at roughly SAR 200 to 220, and families often assume IGCSE sits at a fixed discount to that. It does not sit at a fixed anything. A scarce IGCSE subject such as Additional Mathematics or Computer Science can be quoted above a common IB Standard Level subject, because scarcity is the dominant variable in both markets.

One practical warning about dollar pricing. International providers quoting around sixty dollars an hour are quoting a figure that moves with the exchange rate and usually attaches a package minimum, so the real commitment is a multiple of the headline. Convert it, multiply it by the minimum number of sessions, and compare that total against a term of weekly local teaching before deciding which is cheaper. The headline rate is rarely the decision.

sections.heading: The levers that move a fee, and which are worth paying for
paragraphs: Fees in this market are not arbitrary, and they are not mostly about quality either. Seven levers account for almost all the variation, and only three of them buy teaching. Knowing which is which turns a quote from a number into a conversation, and a provider who cannot explain which lever they are pulling is usually pulling the brand one.

Scarcity does the heaviest lifting. The number of people who can teach Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 or Computer Science 0478 to the paper is small, and the number who can teach 0580 Core is large, so the same hour costs differently. This is honest pricing and worth paying. The check is simple and nobody minds being asked: how many students are you currently teaching in this subject at this tier, and when did you last teach the component we need.

Marking experience is the second lever worth paying for, with one condition. A tutor who has marked the paper knows how the scheme is applied rather than how it reads, which is a different kind of knowledge and genuinely changes a grade. The condition is that the claim must survive a specific question. Which board, which paper, which component, and what is the commonest avoidable error candidates make on it. A precise answer is nearly impossible to fake; a vague one is the answer.

The four levers not worth paying for deserve naming, because they are the ones most often presented as value. Travel buys no teaching. A longer package is a cash-flow structure, not better instruction. A rate that rises as the June series approaches is pricing scarcity in the diary. And a brand name tells you nothing about who will be in the room, which is why the right question to an agency is who is teaching and what their component experience is, not how long the company has operated.
