sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: the same subject, a different fee
paragraphs: Two boards dominate IGCSE in the Kingdom, and a family rarely chooses between them because the school already has. What families do choose is the tutor, and board experience is the most frequently mispriced thing in this market. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 for a decade is not automatically the right tutor for Edexcel 4CH1, and the first few sessions spent learning an unfamiliar mark scheme are paid for by the family.

The structural differences are concrete rather than stylistic. Cambridge sciences pair a multiple-choice paper and a theory paper to the tier, then add either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, which examines experimental reasoning on paper and is almost never practised until the final term. Edexcel runs two written papers per separate science with no practical examination, folding experimental skills into the theory papers. The teaching needed for those two models diverges completely in the last six months of the course.

Mathematics diverges too. Cambridge 0580 is Core and Extended; 0607 International Mathematics is a different syllabus again, with calculator work examined rather than assumed, and it is often chosen by schools heading towards the IB Diploma. Edexcel Mathematics A, 4MA1, tiers as Foundation and Higher with its own question styles. Past papers across these codes are not interchangeable practice, and a tutor handing a student the wrong board's paper is costing them revision time rather than saving it.

The practical upshot for a fee negotiation is one question asked early: which board and which code, and what have you taught or marked on it. It is a fair question, it takes a tutor ten seconds to answer well, and it eliminates the single most expensive mismatch available in this market. Where a family is mid-transfer between a Cambridge school and an Edexcel one, that question becomes the whole brief.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and what getting it wrong costs
paragraphs: No single purchase in IGCSE tutoring returns as much as understanding the tier. Most subjects on both boards are tiered, the tier is chosen by the school, and it caps the grade available before the paper is sat. A family can buy a year of excellent teaching for a subject entered at Core and discover at results that the ceiling was fixed in the autumn. Nobody is hiding this; it simply is not explained.

The decision cuts both ways, which is why it has to be made on evidence rather than ambition. A student entered at Extended who cannot access those papers can score lower than they would have at Core, because the questions assume fluency they do not have and the paper runs away from them. A student entered at Core who could have handled Extended loses the top of the range permanently. Both errors are expensive, and the second is the one families discover too late to act on.

What moves a tier decision is evidence the school accepts, which in practice means performance on the school's own assessments and on past papers at the tier in question. This is the one place where a term of tutoring has leverage over an administrative outcome: a student who can demonstrate Extended-level work on a marked past paper in the autumn gives the subject teacher something to act on. An argument about potential gives them nothing.

Deadlines are the hard part. Final entries for the June series close several months before the papers, and your school's examinations officer holds the actual date. After that, the tier is fixed for that series. Ask for the date in writing at the start of Year 11, and treat the term before it as the window in which teaching can still change an outcome rather than just a mark. For a student who has missed the window, the November series is the next decision rather than a lost year.

sections.heading: Group, centre or one-to-one: what each buys per riyal
paragraphs: One-to-one is not automatically the right purchase, and saying so costs this page nothing because the honest comparison still lands where it lands. A group class is the cheapest per head and is genuinely effective for shared content revision at Core tier or in a common subject, where several students are weak on the same topics and benefit from seeing each other's working corrected. It is poor value for a specific diagnosable gap, because the teaching cannot be aimed.

A tuition centre sits between the two. Rates per hour are usually lower than one-to-one because a room is filled, the structure suits a student who works badly at home, and there is someone accountable if a tutor does not turn up. Against that, you are driving on a school night, often twice, and the pool you are choosing from is whichever staff that centre retains. In a city with a thin specialist market, that pool may not include your subject at your tier at all.

One-to-one is the most expensive per hour and the only format that can be aimed at one student's specific losses. Its real advantage in the Kingdom is not pedagogical, though. It is supply: delivered over live video, it removes distance from the selection entirely, so a family in Al Ahsa or Abha chooses from the same specialists as a family in Riyadh. For a scarce code such as 0606 or 0478, that is often the difference between a specialist and nobody.

The cost-effective pattern most families arrive at eventually is a mix. Group or school revision for the broad content, and a small number of one-to-one hours aimed at the two or three components that are actually losing marks. Spending the whole budget on the most expensive format is how families run out of money in the spring term, which is precisely when the hours matter most.

sections.heading: Verifying an examiner claim before you pay for it
paragraphs: Examiner experience is the most valuable thing a tutor can honestly offer and the easiest claim in this market to make without substance. There is no public register a parent can search, and no Saudi body licenses or verifies private tutors, so verification has to be done by questioning rather than by checking a credential. The good news is that a genuine claim survives questioning easily and a manufactured one collapses in about two exchanges.

Ask four things, in this order. Which board and which syllabus code. Which paper and which component. In roughly which period, described by series rather than by year. And what is the commonest avoidable error candidates make on that component. The fourth question is the one that works, because a real marker has read several hundred scripts and will answer it immediately, with a specific example and usually with some irritation about it. Someone who has not will generalise.

Two further checks are worth doing. Ask what the mark scheme rewards that a textbook answer does not, which tests whether they have worked from the scheme rather than the syllabus. And ask them to mark one piece of your child's work in the trial lesson and talk through the marks aloud. A marker allocates marks point by point against the scheme and says why. A non-marker gives an impression and a number, and the difference is audible within a minute.

A broader point about claims on this page and elsewhere. Any provider quoting a success rate, a star rating or a number of students without a sample size, a date and a method is quoting something unverifiable, and that includes the ones that sound modest. IB Gram publishes no such figures, holds no accreditation from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no office in the Kingdom. Those are facts worth stating rather than facts worth implying.

sections.heading: What coursework feedback should cost, and what it must never include
paragraphs: Where an IGCSE subject carries a coursework or portfolio component, and availability varies by subject, board and syllabus variant, the work is assessed and it must be the student's own. That single condition sets the price and the shape of any legitimate help. Feedback is a small number of spaced sessions rather than a continuous service, because the student needs time between them to act on what was said, in their own words.

The boundary is worth being concrete about. A tutor may teach the skills the task needs, explain the published criteria the work will be marked against, question why a paragraph is where it is, point out that a conclusion does not follow from the evidence, and hand the piece back for the student to change. A tutor may not supply a paragraph, restructure a draft, or correct the prose of an assessed piece line by line. Proofreading an assessed component is not a neutral favour; it is a change to work that is being marked.

Any provider offering a coursework writing or completion service is selling academic malpractice, and the exposure falls on the student rather than on the seller. A school that suspects it is required to investigate, boards have procedures for it, and the outcome can affect a qualification rather than a grade. The reason to say this on a page about fees is that these services are priced attractively precisely because they remove the student's effort, and the discount is paid for with the student's risk.

The record matters as much as the rule. Keep the student's own dated drafts in their own files, keep a note of what each feedback session discussed, and let the changes be made by the student in their own sitting. That trail is what protects a student if authorship is ever questioned, and it is worth maintaining even when nobody expects a problem. Plagiarism software catches copied text; it does not catch work written by somebody else, which is why schools interview students about their own submissions.

sections.heading: Resits, remarks and the money decisions after results
paragraphs: The most time-pressured spending decision in IGCSE comes after results, and it is routinely made badly because families spend the window deliberating. Three options open at once: ask for a remark, enter a resit, or accept the grade and move on. They have different costs, different odds and different deadlines, and the deadlines are short.

A remark is worth considering where a grade is one or two marks below a boundary and the paper was a long-answer one, because that is where marking variation is widest. It costs a fee, it can move a grade down as well as up in some circumstances, and your school's examinations officer manages it. It is not a general appeal against a disappointing result, and a tutor who has actually seen the student's script is far better placed to advise than one working from the grade alone.

A resit is the larger decision. Saudi candidates sit the June and November series with Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, so November is the realistic next window, and preparation for it has to start within days of results rather than weeks. The cost-effective shape is one subject, a short decisive block of teaching aimed at the component that failed, and an honest view on whether the mark is recoverable. Entering three subjects for November because all three disappointed is how a family spends a term's budget for one grade.

Accepting the grade is sometimes the right purchase too, and nobody sells it. If a subject is not required for the student's post-16 route, the money is better spent bridging into the courses they are actually taking. Ask the post-16 school which grades and tiers it requires before paying for a resit in a subject it does not ask for. That conversation costs nothing and has saved families more than any rate comparison on this page.

sections.heading: A year of weekly IGCSE support, costed honestly
paragraphs: Families want a total, not an hourly rate, and providers rarely give one because the total is where the decision actually happens. The arithmetic is not complicated. Weekly one-to-one across three school terms is somewhere around thirty to thirty-four sessions once holidays, examination periods and school trips are deducted. Multiply the hourly rate by that, and add nothing for travel if the teaching is online.

What that total should be weighed against is specific rather than philosophical. One subject moved by two grades, in a subject the post-16 route requires, against the same money spent on a short diagnostic block plus group revision plus six targeted one-to-one hours in the spring. The second pattern wins more often than providers admit, and it wins most clearly for a student whose problem is technique rather than content. For a student with real content gaps across a syllabus, the full year is the honest answer.

Two costs sit outside the hourly rate and are worth asking about before committing. Materials, where some providers charge for past papers and mark schemes that boards publish free. And reporting, where a few charge separately for written progress reports. Neither should cost extra, and a provider that charges for both is recovering a discount on the headline rate. Ask what is included in writing at the start.

Finally, the question nobody asks and everybody should: what happens to the money if it is not working. A term is a reasonable commitment and a year is not, for either side. A provider confident in the teaching will agree a term-end review with a genuine option to stop, and will say plainly if the recommendation is to reduce to one subject or to stop entirely. Our position is that the review happens whether or not a family asks for it, and that a tutor reporting only good news is not reporting.

process.title: Name the board, the code and the tier
process.description: Cambridge 0620 Extended is a brief; help with chemistry is not. If the tier has not been confirmed by the school, say so, because confirming it is the first useful thing anyone can do and it costs nothing. Where a transfer between boards is in progress, that fact changes who the right tutor is.

process.title: Buy the diagnostic before the term
process.description: A free trial lesson, then if needed a short block of three or four sessions with one purpose: a written finding on whether the problem is content, technique or pacing, and an estimate of the sessions a fix needs. Spending here first is what stops a family paying specialist rates for a habit.

process.title: Match on the component, not the subject
process.description: One named tutor for one subject at one tier, with their board and component experience described precisely enough to question. Two weak subjects means two tutors. A flat rate offered across every subject and tier means the provider is not matching on specialism, and it is reasonable to say so.

process.title: Agree the hour in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: The slot is fixed in Saudi local time, so a tutor in a country that changes its clocks absorbs the shift rather than the family rebuilding a school evening twice a year. Sunday to Wednesday evenings work best. Friday and Saturday blocks exist and are harder to staff, so ask early.

process.title: Set two or three behavioural targets
process.description: Targets written as things the student does rather than grades they reach: count the marks before answering, show the substitution line, name the term the mark scheme wants. Work is set between sessions and marked before the next one, with a short note to the parent each time.

process.title: Review at the end of the term, with stopping on the table
process.description: A judgement on which of the six measures moved, which did not, and whether to continue, reduce or stop. If the right answer is to spend the rest of the budget on a different subject, or on nothing, a family should hear that from the tutor rather than work it out from a results sheet.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, none of it our price
whyPoints.description: Advertised SAR rates are published here with the type of vendor that publishes them, and labelled as advertised rather than as averages. No sample size exists behind any of them, so none is presented as one. The Saudi tutoring market usually answers a price question with a contact form, which helps nobody comparing options.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis sold before a term is
whyPoints.description: A free trial lesson and, where useful, a short paid block whose only output is a written finding and an estimate. Almost nobody sells this because a long package is easier to sell, and it is the purchase that most often reduces what a family spends over a year.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a syllabus code, not a subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Edexcel 4CH1 are different mark schemes, and 0580, 0607 and 4MA1 are three different mathematics qualifications. A tutor is attached to the code and the tier, so the first sessions are not spent learning an unfamiliar paper at a family's expense.

whyPoints.title: The tier conversation, raised early
whyPoints.description: The tier caps the grade before the paper is sat and is fixed when final entries close. We raise it in the first session and keep raising it, because a term of teaching that produces evidence a subject teacher can act on is worth more than the same term spent above a ceiling nobody mentioned.

whyPoints.title: Coursework stays the student's own
whyPoints.description: Feedback is questions on a draft the student wrote, with the criteria read against it, handed back unchanged. No supplied paragraphs, no restructuring, no line-by-line correction of assessed prose. Services that offer those are priced attractively because the discount is paid for with the student's own risk.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the hourly rate
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, so nothing in the fee pays for a drive. IB Gram does not attend Saudi addresses and in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India, which is also why a family in Al Ahsa chooses from the same specialists as one in Riyadh.

faqs.question: Which topics on Edexcel IGCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 Higher tier most often need outside teaching?
faqs.answer: Four recur in almost every diagnostic. Differentiation, which the Edexcel Higher papers examine and Cambridge 0580 Extended does not, so a student transferring boards mid-course meets it cold. Algebraic fractions and function notation, including transformations of graphs. Vectors, taught briefly and examined precisely. And the longer structured questions, where an early slip propagates through every later part. The first of those is the one a parent should note, because a tutor working from Cambridge content will skip a topic the Edexcel papers reward, and the family pays for that term.

faqs.question: Why does the alternative-to-practical paper catch out students who are good at science?
faqs.answer: Because it examines experimental reasoning on paper, and almost nobody practises it until the term before the series. A student who is confident in a laboratory can still fail to describe a control variable precisely, read a measuring cylinder to the right precision in writing, identify why a method would give a systematic error, or draw a results table with units in the headings. These are written conventions with their own mark scheme, and they are learnable in a handful of sessions. The marks lost are presentation rather than understanding.

faqs.question: Where do IGCSE Chemistry 0620 students lose the most marks on the Extended theory paper?
faqs.answer: Moles and stoichiometry first, because every calculation depends on them and an early slip costs the whole question. Then the wording of definitions, where the scheme wants specific terms and a fluent paraphrase scores nothing. Then electrolysis and the explanation of ionic half-equations, which students learn to produce without being able to justify. The common thread is that this paper rewards exactness rather than fluency, so the productive work is writing answers to the scheme's specification rather than reading more notes.

faqs.question: What makes the directed-writing task on First Language English so hard to score well on?
faqs.answer: It is marked on form as well as on writing. The question names an audience, a purpose and a text type, and the scheme credits the conventions of that type: a speech needs direct address, a letter needs register, an article needs a structure a reader can follow. Students write well and ignore the brief, scoring in the middle for genuinely good prose. Teaching a student to spend two minutes annotating audience, purpose and form before writing is the single highest-return habit on the paper.

faqs.question: Which part of IGCSE Physics 0625 is most often rushed at the end of the course?
faqs.answer: Electricity and electromagnetism, consistently. They sit late in most schemes of work, they carry heavy marks on the Extended theory paper, and they depend on earlier work on energy and circuits that may itself be shaky. The second casualty is the practical component, which is either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper and is almost never rehearsed. A student arriving in the spring term with gaps in both is why Physics is the subject most often tutored intensively and least often tutored early.

faqs.question: What qualification should I actually look for in an IGCSE tutor, and what is decoration?
faqs.answer: A degree in the subject matters, and teaching or marking experience on the specific board and component matters more. A general teaching qualification is useful but says nothing about the paper. What is decoration: certificates from the tutoring company itself, memberships that cost a fee, and any claim of accreditation from a board or a Saudi regulator, because no such accreditation exists for tutors. The useful signal is whether they can describe the mark scheme for your child's component from memory and specifically.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor has really marked the paper my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: There is no register to search, so question instead. Ask which board, which syllabus code, which paper and which component, described by series rather than by year. Then ask what the commonest avoidable error candidates make on that component is. A real marker answers immediately, with a specific example and some exasperation about it, because they have read hundreds of scripts making it. A generalisation about students not reading questions carefully is not an answer. Then ask them to mark one piece of your child's work aloud.

faqs.question: Should an IGCSE tutor be a current school teacher or a full-time tutor?
faqs.answer: Both work, and they fail differently. A current teacher knows the scheme of work, the moderation process and what a school actually expects, but has limited availability and is tired by the evening. A full-time tutor has more hours, usually more past-paper fluency, and may be further from current classroom practice. The question that matters is not their job title but whether they teach your board and component regularly now. Someone who taught it five years ago is working from memory, and this system changes.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether an IGCSE tutor has taught inside the Kingdom before?
faqs.answer: Less than families expect for the teaching, and more than they expect for everything around it. The syllabus is identical wherever it is taught, so subject expertise transfers completely. What local experience adds is understanding the Sunday-to-Thursday week, knowing that Saudi candidates sit the June and November series rather than the India-only February and March one, and recognising the two parallel school calendars in the same city. A strong subject specialist without Saudi experience is still the better hire, provided those facts are explained to them.

faqs.question: What should I ask in a trial lesson to tell a specialist from a generalist?
faqs.answer: Three questions and one task. Which tier would you enter this student for, and on what evidence. What does this paper's mark scheme reward that a textbook answer does not. What is the first thing you would change about how this student sets out an answer. Then ask them to mark one past question of your child's aloud, allocating marks point by point. A specialist does that in a minute and explains each mark. A generalist gives an impression and a number.

faqs.question: What does it cost us to change tutor after two or three lessons?
faqs.answer: It should cost nothing beyond the lessons taken, and the right time to do it is at two or three rather than at ten. Competence and fit are separate things, and a student who has decided against a tutor will not learn from them however good the teaching is. Where lessons are online there is no travel arrangement to rebuild, so a rematch is administrative rather than disruptive. Ask before committing what the position is on changing tutor and on unused lessons, and get the answer in writing.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with IGCSE coursework, and what counts as malpractice?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skills the task needs, explain the published criteria, question a draft the student has written, point out where a conclusion does not follow, and hand the work back for the student to change themselves. Malpractice begins when the tutor supplies text, restructures the draft, or corrects the prose of an assessed piece line by line. The test is simple: if the improvement did not pass through the student's own understanding before it reached the page, it is not theirs.

faqs.question: Can a tutor proofread an assessed piece of IGCSE writing before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense families usually mean. Correcting spelling, grammar and structure in a piece that is being marked changes the work being assessed, and in several components the quality of written expression carries marks directly. What a tutor can legitimately do is tell a student that a paragraph is unclear and ask them to explain what they meant, which is teaching. The student then rewrites it themselves. If a parent would be uncomfortable showing the annotated draft to the school, that answers the question.

faqs.question: How do I know an IGCSE coursework piece is genuinely my child's own work?
faqs.answer: Ask them to explain a paragraph without looking at it. A student who wrote something can paraphrase their own argument, say why a point sits where it does, and name what they would cut. A student who did not cannot, and the failure is immediate and unmistakable. Keep their dated drafts in their own files so the development is visible, and be suspicious of work that improves in register rather than in substance between drafts. That is the pattern schools are trained to notice.

faqs.question: What happens if a school suspects malpractice on a submitted IGCSE component?
faqs.answer: The school is required to investigate rather than to let it pass, and boards have published procedures for it. The student is normally interviewed about their own work, drafts and evidence of the process are examined, and the matter may be reported to the board. Outcomes range from the component being marked as the student's own reduced work to the loss of a grade in the subject. The exposure sits with the candidate rather than with whoever supplied the help, which is the whole reason a legitimate tutor refuses.

intro.heading: What a parent searching 'near me' is really asking
paragraphs: The phrase is about availability, not geography. A family in Riyadh with three international schools within a twenty-minute drive still searches for an IGCSE tutor near me, because proximity has never been the problem: the problem is finding somebody who has taught the specific syllabus their child is entered for, knows how its papers are marked, and is free at an hour that works on a school night. In Abha, Ha'il, Jubail or Tabuk the same search returns almost nothing, and the honest answer is that no in-home market exists at the level of specialism a Year 11 examination subject needs.

So we answer the question as asked. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to the Sunday-to-Thursday school week and pinned to Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Kingdom; in-home visits are a service we run only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because a parent who books expecting somebody at the door has been misled, and because the online case is strong enough to make on its own: your child gets a specialist in Physics 0625 instead of whoever teaches science within driving distance.

This page is organised around failure first, because that is what actually moves an IGCSE grade. IGCSE papers are short, dense and literal. The mark scheme lists what must appear for each mark, and a student who knows the content can lose a third of the available marks to units, to summary technique, to unlabelled axes, to answering 'describe' with an explanation, or to entering the wrong tier two years earlier. Those are diagnosable losses with known fix times, which is why a competent first session produces a list rather than a feeling.

Then it deals with money, because vagueness about price reads as evasion in this market and most competitor pages hide behind a contact form. Advertised rates in the Kingdom run from around SAR 35 an hour on budget platforms to SAR 200 and above for senior examination subjects. Those are the providers' own published figures, not an average, and the gap between the bottom and the top of that range is almost entirely about what is attached to the hour: marking between lessons, a tutor who has examined the paper, a written note to the parent, or nothing at all.

Finally it deals with verification. 'Examiner experience' and 'IGCSE specialist' are unregulated phrases that anybody can print. There are specific questions that separate a tutor who knows your syllabus from one who knows the subject, and they take about four minutes to ask. The section on checking a claim lists them, along with what a good answer sounds like. Use them on us as readily as on anybody else.

igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Four things sit under the word IGCSE in Saudi Arabia, and families frequently do not know which one their child is in until an entry form appears. The differences change the papers, the grade scale and the tier decision.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The most widely entered international qualification in the Kingdom's British-curriculum schools. Each subject carries a four-digit syllabus code, is examined externally, and is graded A*-G or 9-1 depending on the variant the school enters. Most subjects offer Core and Extended routes with different papers and different grade ceilings. Sciences include an assessment of practical skills. The papers are short and the mark schemes literal, which makes technique unusually separable from knowledge at this level.
programmes.countryNote: Across the Kingdom this is the route most schools enter, and the one where families most often discover a tier problem late. Ask the school in writing which code and which route each subject is entered for. A parent who can quote '0580 Extended' rather than 'IGCSE maths' gets a tutor matched in one step and avoids paying for sessions aimed at the wrong paper.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other major international GCSE route, with its own codes — Mathematics A as 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1, Business 4BS1 — graded 9-1. Content overlaps heavily with Cambridge, and the examining does not: paper structures, the weight given to extended writing, and how practical science is assessed all differ. A tutor who teaches one fluently can still misjudge the other's mark scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Some schools in the Kingdom enter Pearson for mathematics and sciences and Cambridge elsewhere, or switch board between cohorts. That is the single most common cause of a mismatched tutor we see: the family says 'IGCSE physics' and the tutor prepares Cambridge material for a 4PH1 candidate. Check the code on the statement of entry, not the textbook on the shelf.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The two or three years before IGCSE entry, assessed internally with optional Checkpoint tests that give a school a standardised read on each student. Nothing here appears on a certificate, which is precisely why it is underused: Checkpoint results are the earliest reliable signal of whether Extended entry is realistic in each subject, and they arrive while the decision can still be influenced.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the Kingdom often start looking for support in Year 11, when the tier is fixed and the series is months away. Years 8 and 9 are where algebraic fluency and written structure are cheap to build. A term of work at that stage changes which route a student can be entered for, which is worth more than three terms of work afterwards.

programmes.name: What IGCSE leads into here
programmes.description: IGCSE results decide the next two years: A Level or AS Level subject entry, IB Diploma Higher Level options, or an American-curriculum route. Diploma schools generally look for Extended grades for Higher Level subjects, and A Level sciences and mathematics assume the Extended content. A strong grade in the wrong route can still close a door, which is the real reason the tier decision matters.
programmes.countryNote: In the Kingdom the choice is wider than families assume, because schools in the same city run different sixth-form routes, and a foreign secondary certificate later needs a Ministry of Education equivalency decision before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. Checking the destination before Year 10 subject choices is the cheapest intervention available.

igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects Saudi families ask about most, each with its Cambridge code and the specific place its marks leak. The fix times are the ones we see in practice, not promises.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Extended is what sixth-form mathematics and Diploma Higher Level entry assume, and it accesses the top grades Core cannot. The current Extended route includes a non-calculator paper, which exposes years of outsourced arithmetic immediately. Marks leak to algebraic manipulation rather than to topic ignorance, and to answers given without working, which forfeits method marks even when the final number is right.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: Entered by schools running the IB continuum, with a graphic display calculator assumed throughout and an investigation component in some variants. Students who move onto it from 0580 are usually fine on content and unprepared for how much of the paper expects the calculator as a reasoning tool rather than an arithmetic one.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and ionic equations decide the grade, and both respond to drilled practice in a way that re-reading notes does not. The practical skills assessment rewards naming controlled variables and sources of error in the examiner's own vocabulary. Students lose whole questions by writing chemically accurate answers that omit the step the scheme awards the mark for.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: Formula recall is the entry fee, not the exam. Marks go on units, significant figures, graph gradients read from the line rather than from a data point, and the precise wording of explanation questions. Able mathematicians underperform here more than any other group, because they compute the answer and skip the sentence the mark scheme is paying for.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: The most terminology-dependent of the three sciences. A nearly-right word scores nothing, processes must be sequenced correctly, and experimental design questions want the control named explicitly. Diagram labelling and definition drilling are the fastest marks to recover in a short run-up, which makes Biology the subject where a six-week block shows up most clearly.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a double award, entered widely in the Kingdom where option blocks are tight. The content is narrower than the three separate syllabuses and the papers move faster between disciplines, so a tutor who teaches separate Physics cannot assume the same depth or the same question style. Confirm the code before booking anything.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing against tight assessment objectives. Summary technique is where able students quietly lose half the available marks: they narrate the passage instead of selecting and compressing. Directed writing is marked on audience, form and purpose, which are teachable conventions rather than talents.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Reading, writing to a specified text type, and listening. Text-type convention is the recoverable loss — a report is not an article, an email is not an essay — and two sessions on conventions usually move a grade more than a term of general reading practice does.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Short answers, data response and extended evaluation. The evaluation questions are where the grade is decided and where students list advantages instead of reaching a judgement grounded in the stimulus business. Calculation questions are generous marks that get skipped because they look like mathematics.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Definition, diagram, application, evaluation, in that order, every time. Unlabelled axes and a missing new equilibrium cost more marks than a weak paragraph does. Data-response questions reward reading the figures before writing anything, which almost no student does unprompted.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Named case studies with figures attached carry the marks; theme revision without examples caps a student in the middle bands. Map, graph and photograph interpretation are separately examined skills, which makes them quick to improve and easy to neglect.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Theory papers covering data representation, networks, algorithms and programming concepts. Students who code confidently lose marks on trace tables, pseudocode conventions and the exact definitions the scheme expects, because working code and an examinable answer are not the same artefact.

igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: Where in the Kingdom this search comes from, and what the local pool looks like
igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The same query means different things in different places. These are the markets we see IGCSE requests from, with an honest read on what a family can expect to find locally and what that does to the price they are quoted.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest local pool in the Kingdom and the city where in-home rates are highest, because travel across an hour of traffic is priced into the hour. Specialists still thin out sharply at Extended science level, and a tutor advertising four subjects at once is covering, not specialising.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine from the historic centre north to Obhur, which means a nominally local tutor may be forty minutes away in each direction. Cambridge entries are common across the city's British-curriculum schools, so the subject pool is real but concentrated in a few districts.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market behaving as a single city, with families routinely living in one and schooling in another. British and Cambridge curricula are well established here, and the local tutoring market is mostly built around the compound and camp communities rather than around subject specialism.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with an international school presence and a small resident tutoring pool. Requests here concentrate in Extended sciences and mathematics, which is exactly where a local generalist is least able to help and where the price gap between tiers of tutor is widest.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: Roughly an hour and a half inland from the Eastern Province cluster, which puts an in-home tutor's travel cost squarely into the quoted rate. For a single examination subject, the arithmetic almost always favours a video slot with a specialist over a generalist who can drive.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Both have international-curriculum provision and both have calendars that bend around Hajj and Umrah seasons, when travel across the region slows considerably. A fixed online slot is easier to protect through those weeks than a journey is.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About 25km apart at altitude in 'Asir, sharing a catchment. The local pool for an Extended science specialist is effectively empty, which is the clearest case in the Kingdom for matching by syllabus rather than by postcode.

regions.name: Tabuk, AlUla and NEOM
regions.note: The north-west, where international provision is newest and the resident school-age population smallest. Families here are usually weighing boarding elsewhere against keeping the child at their school with specialist support for one or two subjects.

regions.name: Yanbu, Ha'il and Buraidah
regions.note: Smaller markets with established schools and very limited local examination-level tutoring. Requests tend to arrive late — Year 11, with a series approaching — which narrows what is realistic and makes the triage conversation more important than the teaching plan.

schoolClusters.note: British and Cambridge curricula are long established across Dammam, Al Khobar, Dhahran and Jubail, and the International Schools Group operates several campuses here. Not every campus runs the same qualifications, and option blocks differ between them, so a family comparing schools should compare entry codes rather than prospectuses. Students we support attend schools of this kind; no relationship with any of them is implied.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah and the Red Sea coast
schoolClusters.note: A mixed market where some schools run Cambridge courses, some the IB, and several both, spread along the coastal spine from the centre to Obhur. Term dates are set school by school and do not match the Ministry of Education school year, so a tutoring plan should be built from your own school's published calendar rather than from a city-wide assumption.

The widest set of international schools in the Kingdom, and the city where the gap between a school's advertised subject list and the subjects it actually runs in a given cohort is easiest to check, because there are peers to compare against. Several schools here run the IB alongside or instead of Cambridge courses, which changes what IGCSE grades are being used for.

igcse-tutor-near-me.modesIntro: Four arrangements, priced and scoped differently, because an IGCSE family in Year 9 and an IGCSE family eight weeks from a series need completely different things from the same hour.

modes.title: One subject, weekly, by code
modes.description: A fixed weekly slot on a single syllabus — 0620, 4MA1, 0460 — running alongside the school's own teaching for a term or more. This is the arrangement that produces the largest and most durable movement, because it allows content gaps to be closed in sequence rather than triaged. It is also the cheapest per unit of improvement, which is the comparison families rarely make.

modes.title: Paper technique block before a series
modes.description: A short run of sessions built on timed papers and real mark schemes rather than content, for a student whose knowledge is adequate and whose answers are not. Sit the paper under time, mark it honestly, teach from the errors, repeat. Around eight weeks out this is the highest-yield use of money in the whole IGCSE year. Two weeks out it is damage limitation and we will say so.
bullets: Command-term drills first, because that is where the marks leak fastest
The student marks one paper themselves against the scheme, to see what is paid for
Three to five sessions a week for a defined block, not an open commitment

modes.title: Year 11 multi-subject triage
modes.description: For a family facing three or four weak subjects with one series left. Hours are finite, so the first session is an allocation decision rather than a lesson: which subjects move most per hour spent, which are technique problems, which are content problems too large to close in the time available. Honest triage sometimes means explicitly managing a subject rather than fixing it.
bullets: One diagnostic per subject before any teaching is bought
Hours allocated to where a grade boundary is closest, not spread evenly
A named subject that is being managed rather than fixed, stated out loud
Reassessed after mock results rather than at the end of the year

modes.title: November series resit plan
modes.description: Saudi candidates can sit the November series as well as June, which makes a resit a real option rather than a lost year. A resit plan starts from the component breakdown of the original result, not from the syllabus, and concentrates on the papers that actually dragged the grade. It is usually shorter and cheaper than families expect.
bullets: Start from the component marks, which the school can usually obtain
Target the weakest paper rather than re-teaching the whole subject
Entry windows close months ahead — your examinations officer holds the dates
The February/March series is India-only, so November is the Kingdom's resit route

sections.heading: The seven places IGCSE marks actually leak
paragraphs: Start with failure, because the fastest route to a better grade is almost never more content. IGCSE mark schemes are lists. Each one specifies what must appear, in what terms, for each mark, and a correct answer that misses the listed element earns nothing. Seven losses account for most of what we see in the Kingdom, and six of them are technique rather than knowledge, which means they have short and predictable fix times.

The first is the command term. 'State' wants a line, 'describe' wants what happens in order, 'explain' wants a mechanism with a causal link, 'compare' wants both sides handled together, 'evaluate' wants a judgement. Students answer all five the same way. The second is units and significant figures, which silently remove marks across every science paper. The third is working: a right answer with no method shown forfeits the method marks, and in mathematics that is often more marks than the answer itself carries.

The fourth is graph and diagram work — gradients read from a data point rather than from the drawn line, axes without units, a missing new equilibrium on an economics diagram. The fifth is summary and selection in English, where able students narrate instead of compressing. The sixth is the practical skills assessment in sciences, where students describe what they did and omit the controlled variables and error sources the scheme rewards. The seventh is the only one that is not technique: entering the wrong tier, which caps the grade before any paper is sat.

The table puts each loss against the subjects it bites hardest, what it typically costs, and how long it takes to fix in practice. Fix times are what we observe with weekly one-to-one work, not a promise about any individual student. A first session that cannot tell you which of these seven your child is losing marks to has not done its job.

The seventh — tier entry — is decided in Year 10 and cannot be fixed later
A diagnostic should name which losses apply, not describe the subject generally

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the tier decision that caps a grade
paragraphs: This is the one loss on the list that money cannot repair later, and it is decided quietly, often in Year 10, sometimes by a form a parent never sees. Cambridge IGCSE subjects commonly offer two routes. Core papers give access to grades C to G. Extended papers give access to A* to E. A student entered for Core cannot be awarded an A or an A*, however well they perform, and no amount of tutoring in Year 11 changes the route once entries are made. Pearson's International GCSE Mathematics is tiered in the same way, with the lower tier capped below the top grades.

Schools make the decision for defensible reasons. Core entry protects a student who would otherwise sit a paper they cannot access and lose confidence as well as marks. The problem arises when Core is used as a default for a student whose weakness is technique rather than capability, or when a family only learns of the entry after sixth-form applications have assumed Extended grades. Diploma schools generally expect Extended for Higher Level subjects, and A Level sciences and mathematics assume the Extended content.

What a family should do is simple and almost nobody does it. Ask the school, in writing, which route each subject is entered for and when the entry decision is finalised. If a subject is heading for Core and the student's problem is algebraic fluency rather than mathematical ability, that is a term of work in Year 10, not a life sentence. Checkpoint results from Year 9 are the earliest honest read on which route is realistic, and they arrive while the decision can still be influenced.

If the entry is already made and it is Core, the useful conversation changes shape: the target becomes the top of the accessible range and a clean sixth-form route that does not require an Extended grade. That is a legitimate plan, and it is better than a year spent resenting a cap. Pretending the cap does not exist, which some providers do when selling a package, is not.
bullets: Cambridge Core accesses grades C to G; Extended accesses A* to E
Entries are usually finalised months before the series; ask the school for the date

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: same subject, different paper
paragraphs: A surprising share of mismatched tutoring in the Kingdom starts with a board mix-up. A parent says 'IGCSE physics' and means 4PH1; the tutor prepares Cambridge 0625 material; both are competent and the first month is wasted on question styles the student will never meet. Schools here are not consistent on this — some enter Pearson for mathematics and sciences and Cambridge elsewhere, some switch between cohorts, and the textbook on the shelf is not evidence of either.

The content overlap between boards is large. The examining differences are what cost marks: how many papers there are and how long they run, how much extended writing is rewarded, whether practical science is assessed through a written alternative or an assessment of practical skills, how tiering works, and how the grade scale maps. A tutor who has taught both will tell you the differences in a sentence each. A tutor who has taught one will say the syllabuses are basically the same, which is true for revision and false for paper technique.

The fix is a thirty-second check. Find the statement of entry or ask the school for the code. '0580 Extended' and '4MA1 Higher' are different briefs, and a tutor matched against the right one starts useful work in session one instead of session four. If your school enters the 9-1 variants of Cambridge syllabuses, the codes differ from the A*-G ones while the content does not — worth knowing before you buy past papers.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE tutor costs in the Kingdom, and what the hour buys
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are advertised rates set by providers, not a measured average, and the honest way to use them is as the band you will see when you start asking. Tutoring platforms advertise budget IGCSE one-to-one from around SAR 35 an hour and general online tutoring from around SAR 55. Tutor marketplaces quote general private tuition at around SAR 50 an hour at primary level and SAR 200 and above for senior-school examination subjects. Tutoring companies advertising IB and examination-level support quote from roughly SAR 180, with premium tracks around SAR 200 to 220. International providers quoting in dollars sit near sixty dollars an hour.

The five-fold gap between the bottom and the top of that range is not mostly about teaching quality. It is about what is attached to the hour. At the bottom, a tutor is paid for the live hour and nothing else: no marking between sessions, no past papers supplied, no written note to the parent, no familiarity with the code. At the top, the rate carries marking turnaround, examining experience, scarcity of the specialism, and an expectation that the tutor has read your school's scheme of work. Both are defensible purchases; buying the first while expecting the second is where families feel cheated.

What moves a rate, in order of weight: subject scarcity, then marking or examining experience, then level, then whether the tutor travels, then package length. An Extended Physics or Extended Mathematics specialist costs more than a Business Studies one in every market on earth because the pool is smaller. In-home rates carry a drive in the price, which is one reason a video slot with a specialist usually compares well on a like-for-like basis rather than being a budget option.

We publish no price on this page, because a figure that covered both an examiner-experienced 0625 specialist and a Year 9 mathematics tutor would be dishonest for both. What we will do is quote per subject, level and commitment, and tell you what is attached. The table below is the question to ask every provider, including us.

sections.heading: One-to-one against a group class, a recorded course and the school's own support
paragraphs: One-to-one is not automatically the right purchase, and a page that pretends otherwise is selling rather than advising. Four things compete for the same money, and each wins in specific conditions. A group class is genuinely better value when the gap is shared — a class that all missed a topic, or a cohort that all need command-term training. The teaching does not have to be individualised to be useful, and six students splitting a rate changes the arithmetic substantially.

A recorded course wins on cost and loses on diagnosis. It cannot see that your child is losing marks to units rather than to understanding, and it cannot make them sit a timed paper. For a motivated student filling a known content gap, a recorded course plus marked past papers is an efficient and cheap combination, and we will say so. For a student who does not know what they are getting wrong, it is money spent on the illusion of revision.

The school's own support is the most underused option in the Kingdom and the cheapest by a wide margin. Subject clinics, before-school sessions, past-paper packs and a teacher's willingness to mark an extra paper cost nothing and are frequently not asked for. Before buying anything, ask the subject teacher what support already exists and what they would recommend. A tutor worth paying will tell you to do that first, because a tutor working alongside a school produces better results than one working around it.

One-to-one earns its premium in three cases: when the loss is individual and would be invisible in a group, when coursework or a practical component needs supervision-quality feedback, and when the local pool has nobody who teaches the syllabus at all. The last case covers most of the Kingdom outside three cities, which is why this search exists in the first place.

sections.heading: How to check a tutor actually knows your syllabus
paragraphs: 'IGCSE specialist' and 'examiner experience' are unregulated phrases. Anybody can print them and many do, which means verification falls to the parent. Six questions separate somebody who knows your child's paper from somebody who knows the subject, and they take about four minutes. Ask them before the trial lesson, not after, and ask them of us as readily as of anybody else.

First: which syllabus code have you taught, and in which series? A specialist answers with the code and the papers. Second: what are the papers for that code, how long is each, and what weight does each carry? Hesitation here is disqualifying. Third: what is the commonest reason students lose marks on Paper 2 of that syllabus? A good answer is specific and slightly unglamorous — units, or working, or a command term — and a weak answer is about confidence or revision habits. Fourth: what do you not teach? Everyone has a boundary, and a tutor who claims four sciences and two languages is covering rather than specialising.

Fifth, on examining: in what capacity, for which board, and for which paper? Marking a paper for an awarding body is a specific job with a specific name, and somebody who has done it will describe the standardisation process without being prompted. 'Examiner experience' as a bare phrase, with no board and no paper attached, carries no information. Sixth: what will you put in writing after each session, and how quickly is work marked? The answer separates the SAR 35 hour from the SAR 200 one more reliably than any credential.

On results claims, apply one rule: no statistic without a number of students, a date and a method. A provider claiming a success percentage or a star rating has told you nothing verifiable, and the honest version of that claim is an explanation of how they work plus a free trial you can judge yourself. That is what we offer, and it is a weaker-sounding promise than most of this market makes.
bullets: Ask for the syllabus code and the paper structure before anything else
A specific, unglamorous answer about where marks leak is the best signal available
Examining claims need a board, a paper and a capacity attached to mean anything

sections.heading: How an online IGCSE lesson actually runs, and what a parent sees
paragraphs: The mechanics matter because they decide whether the hour works for a technical subject. A lesson runs in a browser-based video room with a shared whiteboard. The tutor writes, the student writes, and both see the same page — which is the part that makes mathematics and physics work on screen at all. A past paper is loaded as a document and annotated live, so a student watches a question being unpacked in the order an examiner reads it rather than watching a finished solution appear.

For working and diagrams, a student uses a mouse, a tablet with a stylus, or paper held to the camera. All three work. What does not work is a student typing mathematical working, which is slow enough to change how they think. A laptop or desktop with a separate keyboard is better than a tablet for a 90-minute session, mostly because of screen size when a paper and a whiteboard are open together; a tablet is adequate for a 60-minute discussion-led subject. A quiet room and a headset matter more than bandwidth beyond a basic threshold.

Sessions can be recorded where a family wants them, and the recording belongs to the family rather than being published anywhere. Students use them to revisit a worked method, which is more useful than re-reading notes. If a connection drops, the tutor waits, reconnects and extends or reschedules the remainder — a dropped session is not a used one. Written work is photographed or uploaded between lessons, marked against the published scheme, and returned annotated.

What a parent sees is a short note after each session: the paper or skill worked on, what the student got wrong, what has been set. Parents can sit in on any lesson, and most do for the first one and then stop, which is the right pattern. The note exists so that nobody is relying on a teenager's summary of their own hour.

sections.heading: The series, the entry window and the resit, counted without a year
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series and a November series, and Saudi candidates sit those two. The June series is the main sitting for schools here. The November series takes resits and November-entry candidates, which makes a disappointing result in June a six-month problem rather than a twelve-month one. Cambridge's February/March series is India-only: a Saudi family told their child can sit in February has been given a wrong fact they may act on, and it appears on competitor pages copied from Indian sites.

Entries close several months ahead of each series and are made by the school, not the family. Your school's examinations officer holds the exact dates and the late-entry window, and that is the only reliable source — we publish no dates here, because they move and a stale date on a page is worse than none. What matters for planning is the shape: entries and tier decisions are settled long before the papers, mock examinations usually fall in the term before, and study leave compresses the final weeks.

Counted backwards, the useful plan looks like this. A year out: content coverage and the tier decision, with Checkpoint or mock evidence behind it. Two terms out: coursework and practical components, where those exist, and the first timed papers under real conditions. One term out: command-term and paper-technique work, marked against published schemes. Eight weeks out: full papers under time, marked honestly, taught from the errors. Two weeks out: nothing new, only consolidation and the logistics of the examination itself.

If a result disappoints, the resit conversation starts from the component breakdown rather than from the syllabus. A school can usually obtain the component marks, and they almost always show that one paper dragged the grade. Re-teaching a whole subject to fix one paper is the commonest waste of money in this market, and a November plan built on component evidence is typically shorter and cheaper than families expect.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, not the subject name
process.description: 'Chemistry 0620 Extended, Paper 4 and the practical component' is a brief we can act on in one step. 'IGCSE chemistry' takes three emails and risks a board mismatch. The code is on the statement of entry, and the school will confirm it. Tell us the year group and the series the student is working towards as well.

process.title: We match on the code, then on the clock
process.description: A specialist in that syllabus and tier first; only then do we check that their own working week can hold a stable slot on a Saudi school night, pinned to Arabia Standard Time. You get their subject background and any examining capacity before the trial lesson, with the board and paper named, so you can question it.

process.title: A free trial run as a diagnostic
process.description: The first session works on real material — a past paper from the right board, a returned school assessment — and ends with a written read: which of the seven common losses apply, in what order to fix them, and the realistic time each takes. That document is yours whether or not you continue, and it is useful even if you buy elsewhere.

process.title: Agree what the hour includes, in writing
process.description: Marking turnaround, who supplies past papers, what note you get after each session, and what happens to a cancelled lesson. This is the thing that actually separates price tiers in this market, and getting it in writing before the first paid session prevents the commonest complaint families have about tutoring anywhere.

process.title: Four weeks, then a decision on marked work
process.description: Weeks two and three teach the first items on the list; week four is a timed paper marked against the published scheme. You then hold marked evidence rather than impressions, and we recommend continuing, changing tutor, changing the target, or stopping. We make the recommendation explicitly, including when it is to stop.

process.title: Re-plan after mock results, not at the end of the year
process.description: Mocks are the best evidence available before the real series and they usually arrive in time to change something. We rebuild the plan from the component breakdown — which paper dragged the grade — rather than from the overall mark, and reallocate hours towards the subject where a boundary is closest.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: Chemistry 0620, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Pearson's 4CH1 are three different papers. Matching on the code is the difference between a first session that starts work and a first month spent on question styles your child will never sit. It costs you thirty seconds to supply and it changes everything downstream.

whyPoints.title: Failure-led diagnosis, with fix times
whyPoints.description: The first session names which of the seven common losses apply rather than describing the subject. Six of the seven are technique with fix times in weeks, which means a parent can tell within a month whether the plan is working — from marked work, not from a conversation about effort.

whyPoints.description: A shared gap belongs in a group class. A known content gap and a motivated student can be served by a recorded course and marked papers. whyPoints.description: June and November are the series Saudi candidates sit, the February/March series is India-only, and entry dates come from your school's examinations officer rather than from a web page. We publish no dates and no year, because a dated page is wrong within twelve months and families act on what they read.

whyPoints.title: No statistic we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No success percentages, no star ratings, no tutor headcounts, no grade promises. What we offer instead is a free diagnostic session you can judge for yourself and a written read you keep either way. It is a weaker-sounding claim than most of this market makes, and it is one you can actually check.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE lesson look like on screen when the subject is Mathematics 0580 and the working matters?
faqs.answer: Both sides write on a shared whiteboard, so the tutor's working and the student's appear on the same page rather than being described over audio. A past paper is loaded and annotated live, question by question, in the order an examiner reads it. The student writes with a mouse, a stylus or on paper held to the camera — all three work, and typing mathematical working does not, because it is slow enough to change how a student thinks. Method marks are the point, so the tutor watches the working appear rather than waiting for an answer.

faqs.question: Are IGCSE lessons recorded, and who is able to watch them back?
faqs.answer: Recording is optional and set by the family. Where it is switched on, the recording is for the student and the parent, not published anywhere, and the most common use is revisiting a worked method weeks later, which is more useful than re-reading notes. Some students work better unrecorded, particularly teenagers who are self-conscious about getting things wrong out loud, and that is a legitimate reason to leave it off. Ask for recording on sessions covering a difficult method and off for discussion-led ones if that suits.

faqs.question: What happens if the connection drops in the middle of a timed IGCSE paper?
faqs.answer: The tutor waits, reconnects, and either extends the session or reschedules the remainder — a session interrupted by a dropped connection is not counted as used. For timed work specifically, the clock is restarted or the remaining time is carried to the next session rather than pretending the interruption did not happen, because a timed paper only measures anything if the conditions hold. If a particular property has recurring connection problems, we move to shorter sessions with work set between them rather than fighting the bandwidth.

faqs.question: How does a tutor share and mark an IGCSE past paper between lessons?
faqs.answer: Papers and mark schemes are shared as documents in the lesson room, and the student's written work is photographed or uploaded afterwards. The tutor marks it against the published scheme — the real one, with its wording — and returns it annotated, showing which sentences earned marks and which earned nothing. That distinction is the single most instructive thing a student sees. Agree a marking turnaround in days before you start paying, because this is exactly the service that disappears at the bottom of the rate range.

faqs.question: Is a tablet enough for an IGCSE science lesson, or does my child need a laptop?
faqs.answer: A tablet is adequate for a 60-minute discussion-led subject and frustrating for a 90-minute science or mathematics session, where a past paper and a whiteboard need to be visible together. A laptop or desktop with a separate keyboard is the better default. A stylus genuinely helps for diagrams and working; a headset matters more than most families expect, because a science lesson involves a lot of precise verbal reasoning. A quiet room with a door is worth more than any equipment upgrade.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor for Physics 0625 cost more than one for Business Studies 0450?
faqs.answer: Scarcity, mostly. The pool of tutors who can teach Extended physics to examination standard is far smaller than the pool who can teach business studies, in the Kingdom and everywhere else, and a smaller pool prices higher. Examining or marking experience adds to it, because somebody who has marked the paper knows what the scheme pays for. Level matters too: Extended costs more than Core. None of this means the physics tutor is better — it means you are buying a scarcer specialism, and the comparison to make is against other physics rates.

faqs.question: Advertised IGCSE rates in the Kingdom start near SAR 35 an hour — what is missing at that price?
faqs.answer: Usually everything except the live hour. At the bottom of the advertised range, expect no marking between sessions, no past papers supplied, no written note to the parent, and no guarantee the tutor has taught your specific syllabus code rather than the subject in general. That can still be a reasonable purchase for homework support or a shared content gap. It is a poor purchase for an examination subject where the loss is technique, because diagnosis and marking are precisely the parts that have been removed to reach the price.

faqs.question: Is a group IGCSE class ever better value than one-to-one for Extended Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Yes, in one specific case: when the whole group has the same gap. A class that all missed a topic, or all need non-calculator arithmetic fluency, or all answer command terms badly, can be taught together efficiently and the rate per student drops substantially. Where a group fails is individual diagnosis — one student cannot manipulate algebra, another shows no working, a third is fine until the final two questions. A group must teach to the common gap, and in Extended Mathematics the common gap is often nobody's real gap.

faqs.question: Do we pay per lesson or per package for IGCSE support, and what happens to lessons we do not use?
faqs.answer: Per lesson or per agreed block, rather than an open subscription, so stopping requires no negotiation and a pause costs nothing. Unused lessons in an agreed block carry rather than expiring quietly, and a slot can be held through a school break if you give the dates reasonably early — worth doing, because a scarce specialist may not be free again afterwards. Be wary of any provider offering a large discount for a long package before a single lesson has happened; the discount is buying your commitment, not your child's progress.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate change in the weeks before the June series?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates in this market tend to firm up as a series approaches, because demand concentrates and the specialists who are any good are already booked. The practical effect is less about price than availability: eight weeks out you choose from who is left, and twelve weeks out you choose. Our rate is set by subject, level and commitment rather than by proximity to a series, but we will not pretend a scarce Extended science specialist is as easy to place in the final term as in the autumn one.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor knows the 0620 syllabus rather than chemistry in general?
faqs.answer: Ask four things. Which code have you taught and in which series. What are the papers for it, how long is each and what does each carry. Where do students most often lose marks on the practical component. And what do you not teach. A specialist answers the first three with specifics and the fourth with a boundary. A generalist describes chemistry, talks about building confidence, and lists six subjects they cover. The whole check takes about four minutes and it is the highest-value four minutes in the process.

faqs.question: What does examiner experience mean for an IGCSE paper, and how would I verify the claim?
faqs.answer: It means somebody has marked that paper for the awarding body under its standardisation process, which teaches you what the scheme rewards in a way that reading it does not. Verify it by asking three questions: which board, which paper, and in what capacity. Somebody who has done the work answers immediately and usually volunteers how standardisation meetings run. 'Examiner experience' with no board and no paper attached carries no information at all, and it is printed widely enough in this market that the bare phrase should prompt the question rather than reassure you.

faqs.question: Should an IGCSE tutor be a current classroom teacher or a full-time tutor?
faqs.answer: Both work and they fail differently. A current teacher knows this cohort's standard, has seen a school's internal moderation, and is tired by 6pm with their own marking to do. A full-time tutor has more hours, more one-to-one experience and more past papers at their fingertips, and may be further from how schools are actually teaching the course now. For a technique problem the full-time tutor usually wins; for coursework or practical supervision, recent classroom and moderation experience is worth more.

faqs.question: Our IGCSE tutor is competent but the match is wrong — how do we change without losing the slot?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and we match again without asking you to justify it. The slot is held where possible, which matters because a workable evening on a Saudi school night is often scarcer than the tutor. Say what did not fit — pace, manner, too much talking, not enough challenge, a personality clash — because that makes the second match better informed rather than a lottery. A mismatch is usually visible by the third session: pleasant lessons, static marked work, and a student who cannot say what was covered last week.

igcse-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Send the code and we will start from the losses
igcse-tutor-near-me.closingBody: Give us the syllabus code, the tier and the series your child is working towards — 0580 Extended, 4PH1 Higher, 0610 Core — and we will match a specialist in that paper and check their working week against a Saudi school night. The trial lesson is free and runs as a diagnostic: it names which of the seven common losses apply and how long each takes to fix, and you keep that read in writing whether you continue or not. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, Sunday to Thursday, on Arabia Standard Time. If a group class or your school's own clinic is the better buy, we will say so.

igcse-tutors.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE courses to families across the Kingdom. Matching is done on the syllabus code a school has entered, not on the subject in general, because a Cambridge 0620 candidate and an Edexcel 4CH1 candidate sit different papers in a different style and their past papers are not interchangeable.

intro.heading: The three authorities above an IGCSE, and the one gap they leave
paragraphs: Begin with the week, because it determines whether any of this is practical. The school week in the Kingdom runs Sunday to Thursday. Friday and Saturday are the weekend. That makes a weekday evening the natural home for a lesson and a Friday morning the natural home for a longer block, and it quietly rules out most scheduling advice written for a Monday-to-Friday country. Any provider still offering you a Saturday-morning timetable as the default has copied its page from somewhere else.

The clock is the second practical fact. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. A great many of the countries a specialist tutor might live in do change theirs, so a slot agreed verbally as 'six in the evening your time' moves by an hour twice a year unless it is written in Saudi local time and left there. We write every slot in Saudi local time for exactly that reason, and it removes the single most common cause of a lesson quietly dying after one term.

The school run finishes the logistics. Riyadh is roughly an hour across in traffic from north to south, so a family in a northern district and a family near the centre are not free at the same hour even when their children attend the same school. The Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation behaves as one labour and school market, and families routinely live in one city and attend school in another. Al Ahsa is around ninety minutes inland from that cluster. Jeddah runs as a long coastal spine. The usable hours differ by address, so the slot is set once against your worst week rather than renegotiated each Sunday.

Now the part this page exists for. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education. School evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for approving international accreditation bodies. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel publish the syllabus, set the papers and award the grade. Those are three separate jurisdictions and most families meet all three without ever being told which is which.

The gap in that arrangement is the one families actually have to close themselves: nobody in the list above vets a tutor. There is no licence, register or evaluation outcome you can look up to confirm that somebody can teach Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 rather than chemistry in general. A school's accreditation status tells you about the school. It says nothing about the person your child sits with on a Tuesday evening. Everything useful on that question has to be checked directly, and the rest of this page is mostly about how.

Delivery is online, one-to-one, over live video with the tutor's screen shared so papers and mark schemes are visible to both sides. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in Saudi Arabia; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That is said here rather than implied, because the honest argument for online teaching in this market is not convenience. It is that the pool of people who have taught your child's exact specification is national rather than local, and in most Saudi cities the local pool for a given subject is one or two people, or none.
