igcse-tutors.programmesIntro: Four stages cover the enquiries that reach us about IGCSE in the Kingdom: the lower-secondary years that decide how hard the course feels, the two IGCSE boards themselves, and the sixteen-plus choice that the IGCSE grades open or close. The notes under each are about schools in the Kingdom rather than about the programmes in the abstract.

programmes.name: Lower secondary, before the IGCSE entry
programmes.description: The three years that set up everything examined later. There is no external certificate at the end, which is exactly why gaps here go unnoticed: a student can pass internal assessments comfortably and still arrive in Year 10 without automatic algebra, without the habit of answering the verb in a question, and without having written anything to a time limit. These are cheap problems to fix early and expensive ones to fix in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the Kingdom commonly change school at this stage, often because a parent's posting moves them between Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster. Each move loses a few weeks and sometimes a topic, and schools set their own schemes of work, so two campuses running the same board can be a term apart in coverage. A short written baseline at the point of a move is worth more than a year of general support afterwards.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written paper, with coursework in some subjects and none in others. Most subjects are graded A* to G in this region. Several, including Mathematics 0580, are tiered into Core and Extended entries, and the tier caps the grade available. The sciences offer either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and which one a school enters changes how a candidate has to be prepared.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge is the more common of the two routes in Saudi private and international schools, and a Cambridge IGCSE tutor is the most frequent request we take from the Kingdom. The practical consequence is a staffing one: a school can be strong across Mathematics and English and still have a single teacher covering all three separate sciences. That is the hole families fill from outside, and it is usually one named subject rather than a general weakness.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The same age band, a different assessment model. Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs are graded 9 to 1, and Mathematics A is tiered into Foundation and Higher entries. Practical skills in the sciences are examined inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical component. Specification codes carry a different shape from Cambridge syllabus numbers: 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics, 4CH1 for Chemistry, 4BI1 for Biology.
programmes.countryNote: An Edexcel International GCSE tutor is a smaller pool in this market than a Cambridge one, which matters most when a family moves school mid-course between the two boards. The content overlaps; the question style does not. A candidate who has spent a year on Cambridge structured questions will not read an Edexcel paper the same way, and the fix is targeted paper practice rather than re-teaching a syllabus the student largely knows.

programmes.name: What the IGCSE grades decide next
programmes.description: A Levels or the IB Diploma, and the IGCSE grades usually set the entry conditions for both. A Diploma school will look hard at mathematics and at English before agreeing a Higher Level choice, and a weak tiered-entry grade is harder to argue away than a weak untiered one. This is why a Core or Foundation entry made for comfort in Year 10 can narrow a sixteen-plus choice two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Provision is uneven across the Kingdom. The Diploma is offered on some campuses and not others, and a family in a smaller city may find the nearest Diploma school is in Riyadh, Jeddah or the Eastern Province. Check which Higher Level subjects a school will actually run next year rather than which it lists in a prospectus, and check it before the IGCSE entry tiers are set.

igcse-tutors.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects families in the Kingdom ask for, with the codes both boards publish. Codes and paper structures change between specification versions, so treat these as orientation: your school's examinations officer holds the entry codes that will actually be used, and those are the only ones that matter on the day.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Cambridge International Mathematics 0607 · Edexcel 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most requested IGCSE subject in the Kingdom and the one where the entry decision does most damage. A Core or Foundation entry caps the grade available, and no amount of work after the entry lifts the cap. 0607 is written for an international cohort and assumes a graphics calculator throughout, which makes it a different teaching job from 0580 rather than a harder one.

subjects.name: Additional and Further Mathematics
subjects.description: Extension courses taken alongside the main mathematics entry, not instead of it. Both are the standard bridge into a Higher Level or A Level mathematics course, and both assume complete fluency in the material of the main syllabus. Students who take one to look strong on an application, without that fluency, generally lose marks on both papers rather than one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical-skills questions do most of the damage. On the Cambridge route a school enters either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the second asks a candidate to read an unfamiliar method and identify variables, errors and improvements. Edexcel examines the same skills inside the written papers. Either way it is a trainable skill and most candidates are never taught it directly.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative-analysis tests account for most lost marks. The tests reward exact recall: the reagent and the precipitate colour have to be right, and partial credit is rare. Organic chemistry arrives late in most schemes of work and is often rushed, which is why it shows up disproportionately in requests for outside teaching in the final two terms.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A memory-heavy syllabus examined with precision, which misleads students into revising by reading. Transport in plants, enzymes and inheritance are the recurring weak spots. The marks go missing on the longer questions, where a candidate names a process correctly but never describes the mechanism the command term asked for.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0654 double award · Cambridge 0653 single award
subjects.description: The route many schools use where timetable or staffing will not support three separate sciences. Content is reduced but the question style is not, and a candidate moving from a combined entry into a Higher Level science at sixteen-plus has real ground to make up. Families are often not told which route the school intends until the entry is close.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Reading and directed writing, where the mark is won in structure rather than vocabulary. Candidates lose marks for answering a question about a text with a summary of the text. The Cambridge route weights directed writing heavily, and the skill of writing in a specified form for a specified audience can be taught in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: The summary task and the directed-writing task carry more weight than the time most schools spend on them. The summary is marked on content points and on language as separate things, so a fluent answer that misses the points still scores badly. 0511 carries a speaking endorsement that 0510 does not, and schools differ on which they enter.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are marked, not decorated. An unlabelled axis or a curve shifted the wrong way costs marks the surrounding prose cannot recover. Data-response questions reward reading the figures in front of the candidate rather than reciting a learned example, and that habit is the quickest available improvement in the subject.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Application to the business described in the paper decides the band. A candidate who recites definitions sits in the lower bands; the same candidate applying the same definitions to the named firm moves up without learning any new content. It is the clearest example in the IGCSE set of technique being worth more than knowledge.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.levels: Cambridge Computer Science 0478 · Cambridge ICT 0417 · Edexcel ICT 4IT1
subjects.description: Two different subjects that families frequently conflate. Computer Science is examined on algorithms, data representation and a programming component; ICT is examined on practical application work and a theory paper. Students who code confidently often write poorly about what they have coded, and the written paper marks the explanation.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.levels: Cambridge Geography 0460 · Cambridge History 0470 · Edexcel 4GE1 and 4HI1
subjects.description: Both are source-and-skills subjects dressed as content subjects. Geography marks the fieldwork-style questions and the map and graph skills tightly; History marks the use of sources and the structure of an argument. In both, a candidate who has memorised cases but never practised the question types scores in the middle and stays there.

igcse-tutors.regionsIntro: IGCSE provision is not spread evenly across the Kingdom, and the reason a family needs an outside tutor differs by city. In the big three clusters it is usually one subject a school cannot staff with a specialist. Outside them it is often whether the subject is available at all. These notes are about that difference.

regions.name: Riyadh
regions.note: The deepest provision in the Kingdom and roughly an hour across in traffic, which means the constraint is the school run rather than the choice of school. Northern districts commonly settle on a later weekday slot; central districts can start earlier. Subject-specialist gaps here tend to be in the separate sciences.

regions.name: Jeddah
regions.note: A long coastal spine running from the historic centre north towards Obhur, so a single traffic incident on the main axis reshapes an afternoon. Several long-established international schools sit along it, and families often choose by commute as much as by curriculum. Makkah is roughly 80 km east.

regions.name: Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran
regions.note: One labour and school market behaving as three cities. Families live in one and attend school in another as a matter of routine, and the King Fahd Causeway links Al Khobar to Bahrain. British and Cambridge-curriculum campuses are well represented here, which makes board switching a live issue.

regions.name: Jubail
regions.note: An industrial city with a school population tied to shift and rotation patterns, which shows up in scheduling rather than in subject choice. A parent on rotation often wants the slot fixed to a day that survives their roster, and an online slot is the only version of that which actually holds.

regions.name: Al Ahsa
regions.note: About ninety minutes inland from the Eastern Province cluster, which is far enough that a visiting tutor is impractical and near enough that families compare themselves to Khobar provision. The gap between the two is the clearest case in the Kingdom for teaching a subject over video rather than not at all.

regions.name: Makkah and Madinah
regions.note: Both have school calendars that bend around the Hajj and Umrah seasons in ways a published term list does not fully capture. Families here plan tutoring blocks around those weeks deliberately, and a slot agreed in advance for the quieter part of the term is more durable than one booked week by week.

regions.name: Thuwal and the Red Sea coast
regions.note: The KAUST School serves the university campus community north of Jeddah, and families on a campus like this have an unusual pattern: strong local schooling with a highly mobile cohort. Mid-course arrivals and departures are routine, so catch-up work on a named topic is the common request.

regions.name: Tabuk, NEOM and AlUla
regions.note: The newest and thinnest provision in the Kingdom, with families relocating in part-way through a course. The question here is rarely which tutor but whether a subject can be continued at all, and an entry already made with a board has to be honoured whatever the new school offers.

regions.name: Abha and Khamis Mushait
regions.note: About 25 km apart in 'Asir at high altitude, sharing one catchment. International-curriculum provision is limited and the terrain shapes the school run, so evening slots start later here than on the coast and weather closes roads rather than connections.

schoolClusters.note: British School Dhahran and Multinational School Dhahran follow British and Cambridge curricula. The International Schools Group operates several campuses in the region, and the IB Diploma is offered at the American School of Dhahran and at ISG Jubail rather than across every campus. Students we support attend schools in this cluster.

Deutsche Internationale Schule Jeddah runs to Grade 12. The British International School of Jeddah is both an IB World School and a Cambridge school, which makes it one of the clearer places in the Kingdom to see the two routes side by side. The International Indian School Jeddah is long established in the city.

Riyadh holds the broadest IB and international provision in the Kingdom, and The KAUST School serves the university campus community at Thuwal on the Red Sea coast. The useful question for a family comparing campuses is not the board but which subjects each one will actually staff with a specialist next year.

igcse-tutors.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as ecosystem context for families comparing provision across the Kingdom; no affiliation, endorsement or partnership with any of them is implied.
igcse-tutors.modesIntro: Four shapes cover nearly every IGCSE arrangement families in the Kingdom ask for. The choice depends on how much of the problem is content and how much is technique, and on how many terms are left. All four run one-to-one over live video, with slots written in Arabia Standard Time.

modes.title: One subject, one fixed slot
modes.description: The default: a single weekday evening held for the term, with written work marked between sessions rather than during them. One subject at a time is deliberate. A student carrying three weak subjects and three new tutors in the same term usually improves in none of them, because nothing gets enough contact to shift a mark.
bullets: Same day, same hour, held through the term
Work marked and annotated between lessons
Written in Saudi local time so it never drifts
Reviewed against a baseline at the end of each block

modes.title: Two subjects on separate evenings
modes.description: Where two subjects genuinely need outside teaching, they go on different days. Two hours back to back on one evening after a Sunday-to-Thursday school day produces an hour of good work and an hour of nodding. Splitting them costs the same and gets twice the retention, and it gives the second tutor a week to mark before the next session.
bullets: Never two subjects in one sitting after school
Separate baselines, separate reviews
Different tutors where the specialisms differ
One shared calendar so the week stays sane

modes.title: Friday paper-practice blocks
modes.description: Friday is the Kingdom's weekend and a working day almost everywhere a tutor might be based, which makes a Friday morning the easiest long block in the week to fill with a busy specialist. Two hours is enough to sit a full paper under timed conditions and mark it against the published scheme in the same session, which a weekday evening never is.
bullets: Full papers under timed conditions, then marked live
Mark-tariff timing drills against the clock
Useful where a parent wants to watch the review
Often paired with one weekday slot in the same week

modes.title: A short diagnostic run before a tier decision
modes.description: A fixed, short series of sessions whose only purpose is to produce evidence for a Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher entry. The student sits questions from both tiers, the work is marked to the scheme, and the family goes into the conversation with the school holding marked scripts rather than an opinion.

A short written summary the school can read
Run early enough to change the entry, not after it
No recommendation made without marked evidence

sections.heading: What a Sunday-to-Thursday week actually leaves for IGCSE work
paragraphs: The Kingdom's school week runs Sunday to Thursday, and Friday and Saturday are the weekend. Almost everything else about scheduling follows from that. A weekday lesson has to sit after the school run and before the point where a fifteen-year-old stops absorbing anything, which in practice is a window of about three hours. A family with two subjects to cover and one evening to cover them in has already made a mistake that no tutor can fix.

Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and the Kingdom does not change its clocks. That is a convenience until the tutor is somewhere that does. A tutor in the United Kingdom is three hours behind in their winter and two hours behind in their summer, so the same conversation about 'half past six' produces two different lessons depending on the month. A tutor in India is two and a half hours ahead, which is stable year round and part of why Indian-based specialists work so well against a Saudi evening. The fix is dull and absolute: the slot is written in Saudi local time, and the tutor converts, not the family.

Then the school run, which differs by city more than families expect. Riyadh is roughly an hour across in traffic from north to south, so two children at the same school can be home forty minutes apart. The Dammam, Al Khobar and Dhahran conurbation functions as one school market and families cross between the three cities daily. Al Ahsa sits about ninety minutes inland from that cluster. Jeddah runs as a long coastal spine from the historic centre north towards Obhur, where one incident on the main axis rewrites the afternoon.

The practical rule we apply is to set the slot against a family's worst week rather than their best one, and then not move it. A slot thirty minutes later than the optimistic answer survives a late pickup, a wet evening and a changed timetable. A slot set at the earliest theoretically possible hour gets rescheduled twice and then abandoned. Online IGCSE tuition in the Kingdom costs nothing extra for a later start, because nobody is driving anywhere to deliver it.
bullets: Weekday evenings for single subjects; Friday mornings for long blocks
Never two subjects back to back after a school day
Slots written in Arabia Standard Time, never in the tutor's local time
Set the hour against your worst week, then leave it alone

sections.heading: Who licenses the school, who evaluates it, and who owns the syllabus
paragraphs: Most families in the Kingdom deal with three different authorities over their child's IGCSE and are never told which is responsible for what. The confusion is not harmless. It is why a parent asks whether a tutor is 'Ministry approved', a question with no answer, and why a school's evaluation outcome gets read as a statement about teaching quality in a particular subject when it is nothing of the kind.

Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education. School evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. The board, Cambridge International or Pearson Edexcel, publishes the syllabus, sets the papers, marks them and awards the grade. The school's examinations officer sits underneath all three and makes the entries.

Read the table below for what each body does not do, because that column is where families lose money. No authority in the Kingdom licenses, registers or vets a private tutor. The boards do not either. Cambridge trains and appoints examiners for its own purposes, and a tutor may well have been one, but that is a relationship between the board and that individual and it is not something a parent can verify from a public register. The claim has to be interrogated directly, and the way to do it is to ask which board, which component and in what capacity.

What follows for a family is simple enough. Treat a school's licensing and evaluation status as information about the school: its governance, its facilities, its processes. Treat the syllabus code as information about what will be examined. Treat the tutor as entirely unverified until you have heard them explain where marks are lost in a specific paper. Nothing on this page claims approval or partnership from the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because we hold none of those relationships and any provider in this market who says otherwise is worth checking carefully.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: the same subject, two different papers
paragraphs: Families treat IGCSE as one qualification and it is two. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both examine mathematics, the sciences, English and the humanities at the same age, and the content overlaps heavily. What does not overlap is the question style, the paper structure, the grading scale and, in several subjects, how practical work is assessed. A tutor who does not know which of the two your child is entered for cannot teach them properly, and past papers from the wrong board are worse than no past papers.

The grading scales differ first. Cambridge grades most IGCSE subjects A* to G in this region. Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs are graded 9 to 1. A parent comparing a sibling's old certificate with a new one is frequently comparing two different scales without realising it, and a school reporting predicted grades in one scale while the family thinks in the other produces conversations at cross purposes.

The sciences are where the practical difference bites. On the Cambridge route a school enters either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the second asks a candidate to read an unfamiliar method and comment on variables, sources of error and improvements. Pearson Edexcel examines those skills inside the written papers instead. A candidate prepared for one and sat in the other loses marks on questions they could answer, which is the most avoidable kind of loss there is.

The table below is orientation rather than gospel. Codes and paper structures change between specification versions, and a school can enter a subject in a form that does not match the general pattern. Your school's examinations officer holds the entry codes that will actually be used, and those are the only ones worth planning against. Ask for them in writing, once, and give them to whoever teaches your child.

sections.heading: Tiering, and the one decision that caps the grade
paragraphs: Tiering is the most consequential administrative decision in an IGCSE and the one families understand least. Cambridge tiers several subjects, including Mathematics 0580, into Core and Extended entries. Pearson Edexcel tiers Mathematics A into Foundation and Higher. The tier determines which paper a candidate sits and which grades are available from it. An entry on the lower tier caps the grade, and once the entry is made no amount of work afterwards lifts that cap.

Schools make the decision, usually on internal evidence, and usually at a point in Year 10 or early Year 11 when a particular student happens to be having a good term or a bad one. A single mock is a thin basis for a decision with a two-year consequence, and a student who was ill, who had just changed school, or who had not yet met a topic can be tiered downwards for reasons that have nothing to do with their ceiling.

The useful response is evidence rather than argument. Ask the school what the decision will be based on and when it will be made. Then get marked work from across a term, including questions from the higher tier, and put that in front of them. A tutor can produce exactly this: a short block of sessions whose only purpose is to sit higher-tier questions under timed conditions and mark them against the published scheme, resulting in a page the school can actually read.

Two honest caveats. A higher-tier entry is not automatically the right answer. A candidate pushed onto Extended who cannot reach the lower grade boundaries can end with a worse outcome than a secure top grade on Core, and the stress in the final term is real. The decision should follow the marks. And it has to be raised early: once final entries are submitted to the board, the conversation is over, and the examinations officer holds that deadline.

sections.heading: What a Saudi school cannot always staff, and what families do about it
paragraphs: The reason a family in the Kingdom hires an outside tutor is usually structural rather than a reflection on the school. International and private schools here recruit from a global market into a specific city, on a specific package, for a specific start date. A school can have an excellent mathematics department and a single teacher covering Physics, Chemistry and Biology because the third science specialist did not arrive. That is a timetable problem, not a quality problem, and it is invisible in any published evaluation.

The pattern repeats by subject. The separate sciences are the most common gap, with Chemistry the most frequently covered by a non-specialist. Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are often taught as an add-on by whoever has a free period. Computer Science 0478 is regularly taught by an ICT teacher, which is a different subject with a different paper. Second-language English is sometimes taught by a first-language specialist, who will teach a good lesson and miss what the summary task is actually marked on.

Smaller cities face a sharper version. Outside Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province cluster, a school may not run a subject at all, or may run it as a self-study entry with supervision rather than teaching. A family in Tabuk, AlUla or Al Ahsa can find the subject their child needs for a sixteen-plus course is simply not on the timetable. The market's answer has historically been a local private tutor if one exists, and nothing if one does not.

What a family should ask before enrolling, and again each year, is narrow and answerable: which subjects will this school run next year, which of them will be taught by a specialist in that subject, and which are entered as self-study. Schools answer that question honestly when it is asked precisely. The reason to ask it in the spring term rather than the autumn is that by the autumn the staffing is fixed and the only remaining variable is what you arrange yourself.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost, subject by subject
paragraphs: Marks in an IGCSE are lost in a small number of repeating, diagnosable ways, and almost none of them are about not knowing the content. In mathematics the loss is method marks: a candidate who reaches a wrong answer with no visible working gets nothing, while the same candidate showing the method keeps most of the marks. Teaching a student to write down the line they would rather do in their head is worth more in 0580 or 4MA1 than another fortnight of topic revision.

In the sciences it is vocabulary and command terms. IGCSE Chemistry 0620 marks the qualitative-analysis tests on exact recall: the reagent, the observation and the colour. IGCSE Physics 0625 loses candidates on units, on graphs drawn without a line of best fit, and on answers that describe when the question said explain. Biology 0610 loses them on longer questions where a correct process is named and the mechanism is never given. All three are trainable in weeks, unlike the content, which takes terms.

In the essay and source subjects the loss is structural. Economics 0455 candidates draw diagrams with unlabelled axes and curves shifted the wrong way, which costs marks the prose around them cannot recover. Business Studies 0450 candidates recite definitions without applying them to the firm in the paper and sit in the middle band indefinitely. History 0470 candidates narrate instead of using the sources. In every case the content was known and the question was not answered.

This is why a diagnosis from marked work matters more than a conversation about how a child is finding a subject. A student who 'struggles with Chemistry' may be losing nearly all their marks on two question types, which is a six-week job. A student who has not met a third of the syllabus is a two-term job. Those need different plans and different budgets, and you cannot tell them apart without reading annotated scripts.

sections.heading: Coursework, the Personal Project and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Some IGCSE subjects carry coursework and some do not, and where they do, the work must be the student's own and the school supervises it. This is the area of the Saudi tutoring market with the most dishonesty in it. Several providers advertise, in plain words, help that amounts to producing assessed work. A family who accepts that offer is exposing their child to a malpractice finding, which is a far worse outcome than a weak grade.

The line is clear and worth stating in full. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, explain what each strand is actually asking for, discuss a topic or research question and stress-test it, read a draft the student has written and explain which band it currently sits in and why, and set the next revision for the student to carry out. A tutor may not write, redraft, rewrite, translate or supply text for assessed work, and may not provide material for a student to submit as their own. We say that to students directly in the first session, not only to parents.

The same line applies to the Middle Years Programme Personal Project, which many students in the Kingdom complete just before or alongside an IGCSE course. The Personal Project is assessed against published criteria on the process as much as the product, and the process journal is part of the evidence. A tutor who helps a student document their own decisions is doing the job. A tutor who contributes the decisions is not, and the journal usually makes it obvious.

Two practical habits protect a family. First, keep the drafts: a sequence of dated drafts with the student's own revisions is the best possible answer to a question about authorship. Second, tell the school a tutor is involved. Schools in the Kingdom are used to this and it is not a confession; supervision records exist precisely so that outside support can be visible and legitimate. A provider who suggests concealing their involvement has told you exactly what they intend to do.

sections.heading: The series, counted backwards from the papers
paragraphs: Both boards run a June series, which is the main one for candidates in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and November-entry candidates. Cambridge runs a February and March series in India only, so a Saudi family reading an entry deadline copied from an Indian page is reading a deadline that does not apply to them. This is one of the more common factual errors in this market and families act on it.

Working backwards from the papers rather than forwards from today changes what a family does with the time. Final entries go to the board several months before the papers and the tier is fixed at that point, so any argument about Core against Extended has to happen before it. Coursework deadlines sit a term or more ahead of the written papers and are internally marked, so they compete with teaching time in a term that already has mocks in it. The deadlines are not negotiable and they do not move for a family's convenience.

The last six to eight weeks should look different from everything before them. By then the syllabus is either covered or it is not, and the available marks sit in technique: reading the command term, allocating time by mark tariff, deciding when to abandon a question, and writing the method line rather than the answer. Introducing new content in the final fortnight has the worst return of anything a family can buy, and it displaces the paper practice that actually moves a grade.

No dates appear in the table below on purpose. Entry windows, coursework deadlines and series dates are published by the boards and administered by the school, and they shift. Your school's examinations officer holds the exact dates for your child's entries. What the table gives you is the order of operations and who is responsible at each step, which does not change from one year to the next.

sections.heading: From an IGCSE certificate towards equivalency and the Qiyas tests
paragraphs: An IGCSE is not the certificate a Saudi university looks at, and families sometimes discover that late. The qualification that needs an equivalency decision, the mu'adalah, from the Ministry of Education is the school-leaving certificate at the end of secondary education: an IB Diploma, a set of A Levels, an American high school diploma. The IGCSE grades matter enormously for what a student is allowed to study at sixteen-plus, which is where their effect on a university application actually happens.

Alongside equivalency sit the Qiyas tests, run by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, assesses verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content and is sat in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Neither has any role in IGCSE assessment, and no part of the IGCSE prepares a student for either.

Tahsili content follows the Saudi national curriculum, and that single fact explains most of the difficulty international-curriculum students have with it. A candidate who has spent two years on Cambridge 0625 Physics knows a great deal of the physics on a Tahsili paper. What they have not met is the order it is taught in, the terminology used for it, or the method a question expects. The overlap is real and the framing is not, which is why preparation for it is a separate strand of work rather than more subject tuition.

Universities in the Kingdom publish their own admission formulas combining school grades with the Qiyas results, and the weightings differ by university and by programme. Competitive engineering, medicine and science programmes lean hardest on Tahsili, and some institutions state a maximum age for the certificate they will accept. No threshold or formula appears on this page, because they differ by institution and intake and third-party sites contradict each other. Read the university's own admissions criteria, and read them during the first sixteen-plus year rather than the second.

process.title: Send the code, not the subject
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier if one applies, year group, and two or three windows that work after your city's school run. A Cambridge IGCSE tutor can be proposed from that within a day. 'Needs help with science' takes a week of questions first, and three of those questions will be ones your examinations officer could have answered.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: An hour with the person who would actually teach, working on something real. Ask them inside the hour where candidates lose marks in the paper your child is weakest at. Topics and command terms in the answer mean they have taught the course; generalities about confidence mean they have not, however pleasantly it is said.

process.title: A baseline from annotated work
process.description: Before a block is agreed, a short written baseline built from marked questions rather than from a conversation. It separates missing content from lost technique, which need different plans and different amounts of money. It is also the document everything afterwards is measured against, so it is worth reading properly.

process.title: A fixed slot in Arabia Standard Time
process.description: Written in Saudi local time and held for the term, so a tutor abroad changing their clocks does not move your lesson. Set it against your worst school-run week. Where two subjects need work they go on separate evenings, never back to back after a Sunday-to-Thursday school day.

process.title: Review at the end of each block
process.description: A review against the baseline using marked work: what moved, what did not, and whether the plan or the tutor should change. If the match is wrong, we re-match early rather than extend. A review that reports effort and attitude instead of marks is not telling you anything you can act on.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the code, not the subject
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge 0620 candidate and an Edexcel 4CH1 candidate sit different papers in a different style, and their past papers do not transfer. Matching starts from the entry code your school holds, which is why we ask for it in the first message rather than the fourth.

whyPoints.title: The staffing gap named honestly
whyPoints.description: Most families here need a tutor because a school could not staff one subject with a specialist, not because the school is weak. Saying that plainly makes the brief sharper: you are filling a named hole in a timetable, and the work is narrower and cheaper than general support.

whyPoints.title: Regulators explained, not borrowed
whyPoints.description: We set out what the Ministry of Education, the Education and Training Evaluation Commission and the boards each do, and what none of them does. Nothing here claims approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from any of them, because we hold none of those relationships.

whyPoints.title: Slots that survive a clock change
whyPoints.description: Every slot is written in Arabia Standard Time, UTC+3, and the tutor converts into their own time. That removes the most common reason an arrangement with a tutor abroad quietly stops working after one term, which is a slot that drifts by an hour and then collides with a school night.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty written down
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches criteria, questions a research question and gives feedback on the student's own drafts. We do not write, redraft or supply text for coursework or a Personal Project, and the student is told that directly. Several providers in this market are deliberately vague on that line.

whyPoints.title: Evidence instead of claims
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no success percentages, no star ratings and no counts we cannot show you. Progress is reported from annotated work against a written baseline, which is slower to produce than a testimonial and considerably harder to invent.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an IGCSE coursework draft, and what may they never do?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, explain which band a draft currently sits in and why, question the argument, and set the next revision for the student to carry out themselves. A tutor may not write, rewrite, translate or supply text for assessed work, and may not provide material for a student to submit as their own. The distinction is between teaching a student to improve their work and improving it for them. Keep dated drafts showing the student's own revisions, and tell the school a tutor is involved: supervision records exist so that outside help can be legitimate and visible.

faqs.question: How is the Middle Years Programme Personal Project assessed, and where does an outside tutor fit?
faqs.answer: The Personal Project is assessed against published criteria covering the process as much as the finished product, and the process journal forms part of the evidence. A tutor's legitimate role is to teach what each criterion strand is asking for, press the student on whether their goal is specific enough to assess, and read what the student has written and explain where it sits. The decisions must be the student's own. A project where the tutor supplied the thinking tends to show up in the journal, because the reflection no longer matches the documented process.

faqs.question: Can a tutor proofread an IGCSE English coursework folder before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Not in the sense most families mean. Correcting spelling, grammar and expression in assessed writing changes the thing being marked, because language is part of what the criteria assess. What a tutor can legitimately do is teach the student to proofread: point out that a paragraph has three sentences doing the same job, that a tense shifts halfway through, or that the task asked for a specific form and the piece is in another. The student then makes the changes. If a tutor returns a cleaner version of the text, that version is no longer the student's work.

faqs.question: What happens if a school in the Kingdom suspects malpractice in IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: The school investigates under the board's malpractice procedures and reports where required, and the board decides the outcome. Consequences range from the loss of marks on a component to the loss of a grade in the subject or across the entry. The process is slow, it sits outside the family's control, and it arrives in the term when a student can least absorb it. This is the practical reason to refuse any offer to produce assessed work: a weak grade can be resat in the November series, while a malpractice finding cannot be undone by effort.

faqs.question: How does a family keep a record that an IGCSE assignment is the student's own work?
faqs.answer: Keep the drafts and keep them dated. A sequence of versions showing the student's own revisions, with a tutor's feedback visible as comments rather than as rewritten text, answers an authorship question better than any assurance can. Where a tutor is involved, tell the school at the start rather than if asked later. Ask your tutor to record what was discussed in each session on assessed work, in a line or two. None of this is onerous, and all of it exists because the student, not the household, has to be able to stand behind the submission.

faqs.question: Which topics in Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 most often need outside teaching?
faqs.answer: Four recur. Algebraic manipulation, because everything later is built on it and a student who is slow at it runs out of time rather than out of knowledge. Trigonometry and bearings, where the diagram is the whole problem and most candidates do not draw one. Transformations and vectors, which are taught late and often rushed. And probability with tree diagrams, where the arithmetic is easy and the structure is not. Underlying all four is method marks: a candidate who shows no working and reaches a wrong answer scores nothing for reasoning they actually did.

faqs.question: Why do candidates lose marks on the longer questions in IGCSE Biology 0610?
faqs.answer: Because they answer the topic instead of the verb. A question that says 'explain' wants a mechanism with causal links, and a question that says 'describe' wants the observable sequence without the reasoning. A candidate who writes everything they know about osmosis will score some of the available marks by accident and miss the rest. The second cause is precision: naming a process correctly and never saying what it does. Both are fixable in a handful of sessions with marked answers in front of the student, which is far faster than re-covering the content.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE Chemistry 0620 definitions are examined most strictly?
faqs.answer: The qualitative-analysis tests, where the reagent, the observation and the colour all have to be right and partial credit is rare. Alongside them sit the energetics and equilibrium definitions, where a candidate who writes 'the energy change' instead of the enthalpy change under the stated conditions has lost a mark on vocabulary rather than chemistry. Rates of reaction definitions and the mole relationships are similar. These are the cheapest marks in the paper to recover because they are recall rather than reasoning, and most students have never been drilled on them.

faqs.question: How is practical work examined when a school enters the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: On the Cambridge route a school chooses between a practical test and the alternative-to-practical paper, and many schools in the Kingdom enter the second. It asks a candidate to read a method they have never performed and identify the independent and controlled variables, spot sources of error, read instruments, plot results and suggest improvements. It is an examinable skill with its own technique, and it is frequently untaught because it does not belong to any topic. Candidates who have run experiments without ever being asked to analyse somebody else's method lose marks here routinely.

faqs.question: Where does weak algebra show up later in IGCSE Physics 0625?
faqs.answer: In rearranging equations under time pressure, which is where most of it goes, and then in three specific places: the lens and resistance calculations where a reciprocal has to be handled, the gradient questions where a graph has to be converted into a quantity, and anything requiring a unit conversion inside a substitution. The physics is usually understood. What fails is the manipulation, and because it fails mid-question the candidate loses the marks downstream as well. Fixing the algebra in a mathematics session frequently raises a Physics mark more than Physics teaching does.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are most often taught by a non-specialist in a Saudi school?
faqs.answer: The separate sciences first, and Chemistry most of all, because a school that recruits two science specialists rather than three has to cover the third from inside. Additional Mathematics 0606 and Further Pure Mathematics 4PM1 are often added to whoever has a free period. Computer Science 0478 is regularly taught by an ICT teacher, which is a different subject with a different paper. Second-language English is sometimes taught by a first-language specialist. None of this reflects badly on a school; it is a recruitment reality, and it is the usual reason a family here hires outside help.

faqs.question: How does the Ministry of Education license a private school offering IGCSE in the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, which is the authority for operating a school here regardless of the curriculum it teaches. School evaluation and accreditation runs separately, through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission. The board a school enters candidates with, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, is a third and unrelated relationship covering the syllabus and the examinations. A licence tells a family that a school may operate. It says nothing about whether a particular subject will be staffed by a specialist next year, which is the question that affects a student.

faqs.question: What does the Education and Training Evaluation Commission do, and what does it not do?
faqs.answer: It handles school evaluation and accreditation in the Kingdom, operating e-services for national school accreditation and for approving international accreditation bodies, and through its National Center for Assessment it runs the Qudurat and Tahsili tests. What it does not do is assess your child's IGCSE work, which belongs to the board, or approve, register or vet private tutors, which nobody in the Kingdom does. Reading an evaluation outcome as a judgement on one subject department is a common error. It is a judgement on a school's processes and provision as a whole.

faqs.question: What should a family ask a Saudi school about IGCSE subject availability before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Three precise questions. Which IGCSE subjects will actually run next year, as opposed to being listed in the prospectus. Which of those will be taught by a specialist in that subject, and which will be covered by a teacher from another department. And which, if any, are entered as self-study with supervision rather than taught. Ask in the spring rather than the autumn, because by the autumn staffing is settled and the only remaining variable is what the family arranges itself. Schools answer this honestly when the question is specific enough to answer.

faqs.question: What do families do when a Saudi school offers an IGCSE subject only as a self-study entry?
faqs.answer: They arrange the teaching themselves, and the arrangement needs to be more structured than ordinary top-up support. A self-study candidate has no scheme of work, no class deadlines and no mock timetable, so those have to be created: a term-by-term plan against the syllabus, interim deadlines, and marked work on a schedule. The school still makes the entry and holds the codes, so confirm in writing which syllabus and tier is being entered. This is the one case where a tutor is carrying the course rather than supplementing it, and it should be briefed that way.

faqs.question: How does a Saudi school's own term calendar differ from the Ministry of Education school year?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and families with children in both systems feel it. Ministry public schools run a two-semester year starting in late August and ending in late June, with an autumn break, a midyear break and an Eid Al Fitr break. International and British-curriculum schools set their own calendars and most run three terms, so two campuses in the same city can differ by a fortnight on either side of a break. Always work from your own school's published calendar rather than a general one, and agree tutoring around it before the term starts.

igcse-tutors.closingHeading: What to send us to get a named IGCSE tutor
igcse-tutors.closingBody: The board, the syllabus code, the tier if one applies, the year group, and two or three windows that genuinely work after your city's school run. From that we propose a named tutor who has taught that specification, arrange a free trial lesson with that person, and write a baseline from marked work before any block of hours is agreed. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Arabia Standard Time, Sunday to Thursday, with Friday morning blocks where a full paper under timed conditions is the right use of two hours. If no specialist is free in your subject and window, we will say so rather than send a generalist.

intro.heading: Start with the assessment, then count the weeks
paragraphs: There is a large and long-established Indian professional community in the Kingdom, so the search for an Indian IB tutor in Saudi Arabia is one of the commonest in this market. The reasons are practical: a language the family uses at home, a teaching manner the parents recognise from their own schooling, and a deep pool of subject teachers in India who work online across the Gulf. All of that is real and none of it is the thing that decides a Diploma grade.

What decides a Diploma grade is whether somebody understands how the assessment pays out. CBSE and ICSE courses are demanding and produce teachers with genuine depth, particularly in mathematics and physics. The IB asks for something adjacent but not identical: a command term answered exactly as it was asked, a mark scheme satisfied rather than impressed, and independent work judged against a criterion grid. A teacher can be excellent at the first system and new to the second.

So this page is built the way the course is built. It opens on the assessment structure itself, component by component, because that is what a plan has to serve. Then it counts the two years backwards from the May session, which is the fixed point every Saudi IB school works towards and the thing almost no tutoring page bothers to set out. Then it deals with the two calendars, the series confusion, curriculum switches and how you tell in the first month whether this is working.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on a slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address, and home visits are a service offered only in India. For this particular search that distinction is worth stating twice, because a tutor in Kochi or Chennai teaching a student in Al Khobar is exactly the arrangement most families are already imagining, and it works well when the week is agreed properly at the start.

Where a family wants a tutor from a particular background, that is recorded with the subject and the level and the match is made against all of it. What it cannot override is experience of the course. A tutor who has taken four cohorts of Chemistry HL through to the May session is a different proposition from a strong chemist who has never seen an Internal Assessment moderated, and the difference shows up in Paper 3. Both can be worth paying for, at different points in the two years and for different jobs, and the useful thing is to know which one is sitting in the lesson. Ask the question directly; a specialist will answer it in one sentence and a generalist will change the subject.

sections.heading: What a Diploma grade is actually assembled from
paragraphs: Start with the assessment, because everything else follows from it. A Diploma grade in any subject comes from written papers sat in the May session plus internally assessed work completed across the course. Six subject grades of one to seven give forty-two points, and the Theory of Knowledge essay and the Extended Essay combine in a matrix worth up to three more. That is the whole arithmetic, and a family that knows it can read a school report properly for the first time.

Inside a subject, the papers do different jobs. Paper 1 tests core content at speed. Paper 2 asks for extended responses across the whole course. Paper 3, which Higher Level candidates sit in most subjects, tests options, practical work or unseen data, and it is frequently where a Higher Level grade is settled. Internal assessment is independent work marked by the school and moderated by the board, and it is commonly a fifth to a quarter of a subject grade.

What this structure means for teaching is specific. A tutor who knows the content can lift Paper 1. Lifting Paper 2 and Paper 3 needs somebody who knows what a mark scheme pays for in an extended answer, which is a different kind of knowledge. Lifting internal assessment marks needs somebody who can read a criterion grid and say which criterion is underserved without writing a word of it. Those three skills do not arrive together, so ask which one you are buying.

sections.heading: What a CBSE or ICSE background gives a tutor, and what it does not
paragraphs: A teacher trained on an Indian board usually brings a genuine strength: depth in the subject, and fluency with hard mathematics and physics in particular. CBSE and ICSE courses are demanding, and somebody who has run Class 11 and Class 12 physics for years is not short of content. Families searching for this are often buying exactly that, and for Paper 1 and for repairing weak foundations it is good value for money.

What does not transfer automatically is the assessment culture. Indian boards reward accurate, complete answers to well-defined questions. The IB rewards a command term answered precisely: evaluate is not describe, justify is not state, and a well-written paragraph aimed at the wrong verb scores low. Internal assessment has no close equivalent in most Indian school experience, and neither does a criterion grid in which the process is marked alongside the outcome.

So the question to ask is not which board a tutor trained on. It is how many cohorts of this Diploma subject they have taught through to the May session, and what they can tell you about the mark scheme for a six-mark question in it. A teacher who has worked in both systems is often the strongest option on the table, because they can name the difference rather than discover it on your child's paper. It is also worth asking what they would do in the first three sessions, since a tutor who answers with content is planning to teach the subject again, while one who answers with a marked paper is planning to teach the examination.

sections.heading: The year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Diploma planning works in reverse, and almost nobody does it that way. The fixed point is the May session. Everything else is a distance from it measured in weeks, and the useful question at any moment is not what shall we study next but what should already be true by now. Written down like that, two years stop feeling open-ended and start showing which decisions have a window that closes.

The windows are the part worth watching. Subject levels can be changed early and not late. An Extended Essay subject is chosen well before a first draft exists. Internal assessment deadlines are set by the school and they do not move for a tutor's convenience. Mock examinations arrive early enough to be useful evidence and late enough that a family who ignored the first year has little room left. The table sets out what belongs in each window.

Counting backwards also changes what a lesson is for. Eighteen months out, a lesson closes content gaps. Twelve months out, it teaches the criteria the internal assessment is marked against. Six months out, it converts mock papers into a ranked list of weaknesses. In the final eight weeks it is timed papers and nothing else, because new content learnt at that point displaces revision of content that is already half known. The same hour buys something different depending on where it sits, which is why a plan that names the stage is worth more than one that names a number of lessons.

sections.heading: An Indian tutor's week against a Saudi school week
paragraphs: Two calendars have to be reconciled, and the mismatch is wider than the clock. Schools in the Kingdom run Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as the weekend. Much of the teaching week in India runs Monday to Saturday with Sunday off. A Sunday evening lesson for a Riyadh student lands on an India-based tutor's one free day, and a Friday lesson lands squarely on their working one. Both are arrangeable; neither should be assumed.

The clock is the easier half. Arabia Standard Time is UTC+3 and never changes, while Indian Standard Time runs two and a half hours ahead. A seven in the evening slot in Jeddah is half past nine at night in India, which an adult can sustain for a while but not indefinitely. Earlier is better at both ends: a slot between five and seven here is a civilised evening in both countries and still survives a school run.

Then there are the term calendars. Indian school years and Saudi international school years break at different points, so a tutor's own examination fortnight can arrive in the middle of your child's term. Ask at the start when their commitments fall and agree what happens to the slot in those weeks. During Ramadan the school day here shortens and study shifts later, which usually suits a tutor in India better rather than worse. The long summer break is the other point to settle: a slot held through it with a lighter schedule is easier to restart than one given up and recovered.

sections.heading: The February and March series is an arrangement for schools in India
paragraphs: This is where copied content does real damage. Cambridge runs a February and March series for schools in India, and a great deal of tutoring copy written for Indian families repeats its deadlines without checking who they apply to. A candidate in the Kingdom does not sit it. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel candidates here sit the June series as the main one, with November used for resits and for November-entry candidates.

For the IB the fixed point is the May session, which is what almost every Diploma school in Saudi Arabia works towards. Entry administration runs through the school's Diploma Programme coordinator rather than through a family, and the deadlines that actually bite are the school's internal ones for assessed components, which arrive considerably earlier than any written paper. Those are the dates that belong in a revision plan.

The practical consequence is one question for any tutor who has worked mainly with families elsewhere. Which series is your plan built around? A tutor who answers with the right one has adjusted to this market. A tutor who quotes an entry deadline borrowed from another country's timetable is working from an assumption, and that assumption moves a revision plan by months. Your school's examinations officer holds the dates that bind, and the Diploma Programme coordinator holds the internal ones. Between them those two people can confirm every deadline that matters in an email, which is worth more than any published summary, including this page.

sections.heading: Switching between an Indian school and the IB
paragraphs: Families in the Kingdom move children between an Indian-curriculum school and an international one in both directions, and the question is always what survives the switch. Mathematics and the sciences travel well: a student who has done Class 10 mathematics on an Indian board is usually ahead on algebra and arithmetic fluency. Languages and humanities travel less well, because the writing expected is different in kind rather than simply harder.

Moving into the Diploma, the work is assessment literacy. Command terms, criterion grids, and the expectation that a student argues from evidence instead of reproducing a model answer. Expect a term of discomfort and plan for it: one hour a week on how answers are marked is worth more in that term than three hours of content. Moving the other way, into an Indian board, the gap is usually speed and coverage under a single terminal examination.

Timing matters as much as subject. A switch between the end of Class 10 and the start of the Diploma is clean. A switch during the first Diploma year is manageable if assessed work begun elsewhere can be carried or restarted. A switch during the second year is hard, and honesty serves a family better than optimism: ask the receiving school what it will accept, in writing, before building a plan around it. The questions worth putting in that email are which subjects have places, which levels are running, and what happens to assessed work already started.

sections.heading: The first month, and how you tell whether it is working
paragraphs: The first session should produce a document rather than a feeling. A diagnostic hour on the subject in trouble, a real past-paper question marked against the published scheme, and a short written note naming the question types where the marks went. If a family finishes a trial lesson with nothing written down, there is nothing to judge the next three months against, and that is precisely how a year goes by unnoticed.

Through the first month the useful outputs are small and specific. A topic checklist marked unsafe, shaky or secure. A note after each session saying what was covered and what was set. A ranked list of the components costing the most marks. None of that needs a reporting department; it needs a tutor who has decided what the work is for. Ask for it in the first week rather than at the end of a term.

Then judge it on movement in the written record. The same question type stops leaking marks. The checklist shifts. Mock scores improve on the paper that was targeted rather than in general. If after a term nothing in the record has changed, the response is to change the plan or change the tutor, and asking for a different tutor after two or three sessions is a normal request rather than a complaint. A term is the right unit for that judgement, because a fortnight is too short to show anything and a year is long enough to waste.

faqs.question: Does an India-based tutor's Monday-to-Saturday working week clash with a Sunday-to-Thursday school week?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is the first thing to settle. Schools here run Sunday to Thursday, so the natural lesson evenings are Sunday through Wednesday. Much of the teaching week in India runs Monday to Saturday, which means a Sunday lesson falls on the tutor's rest day. Tutors who teach Gulf families regularly have arranged their week around this already. Ask which evenings are genuinely free for the whole term.

faqs.question: Can a tutor trained on CBSE teach Mathematics AA HL properly?
faqs.answer: Often very well, because the content overlap is substantial and Indian board mathematics is demanding. What has to be checked is Paper 3, the Higher Level extension and the Internal Assessment exploration, none of which has a close CBSE equivalent. Ask how many AA HL cohorts the tutor has taken to the May session, and what a Paper 3 question looks like. A specific answer settles it in a minute.

faqs.question: What happens to a weekly slot when an India-based tutor's own school term starts?
faqs.answer: Agree it at the beginning instead of discovering it later. A tutor who also teaches in a school has an examination fortnight, a results period and term breaks that fall on a different calendar from your child's. The honest arrangements are either a tutor who tutors full time, or a named cover week where sessions are moved rather than cancelled. Put the dates of their commitments in writing in the first week, and keep the slot itself fixed in Arabia Standard Time so nothing drifts.

faqs.question: Can a candidate in the Kingdom sit the Cambridge February and March series that schools in India use?
faqs.answer: No. That series exists for schools in India, and Saudi candidates sit the June series as their main one, with November for resits and November-entry candidates. This matters because a great deal of tutoring copy is written for Indian families and repeats Indian entry deadlines, which would move a revision plan by months in the wrong direction. If a tutor quotes you a February deadline, they are working from the wrong timetable. Your school's examinations officer holds the dates that apply here.

faqs.question: What should the first month with a new IB tutor produce in writing?
faqs.answer: Four things. A marked past-paper question with the lost marks identified by question type. A topic checklist labelled unsafe, shaky or secure. A note after each session saying what was covered and what was set. And a ranked list of the components costing the most marks, which becomes the order of the work. If none of that exists after four sessions, the plan is being carried in somebody's head.

faqs.question: How is progress reported when the tutor is in another country?
faqs.answer: In writing, because distance makes a corridor conversation impossible. The workable pattern is a short note after each session, an updated topic checklist, and a longer review each term comparing marked work against the plan. Ask what the note will contain before lessons start, because a tutor who has done this before already has a format and one who has not will improvise it.

faqs.question: What happens if the match with an Indian tutor is not working after three lessons?
faqs.answer: You say so and a different tutor is arranged. Three sessions is enough to tell whether a student is being taught or being talked at, and raising it early is normal rather than awkward. Nothing about a background preference obliges a family to persist with one person. Say what is not working, because a specific complaint produces a better second match: pace, language, too much content, too little marking, or a slot too late in the evening.

faqs.question: Our child is moving from a CBSE school in Riyadh into the Diploma — what transfers?
faqs.answer: The mathematics and science content largely transfers, and often puts the student ahead for the first term. What does not transfer is how answers are marked: command terms, criterion grids, and internally assessed work judged on process as well as result. Written humanities and English will need the most attention, because the IB asks for argument from evidence rather than a well-learnt model answer. Plan the first term around assessment literacy and the content will look after itself.

faqs.question: Does an ICSE Class 10 student need extra work before starting Diploma English A?
faqs.answer: Usually some, and it is rarely about vocabulary. ICSE English produces strong accurate writing; Diploma English A asks for close analysis of unseen texts and for oral commentary under conditions, which is a different performance. The oral components are the part most often under-practised, because an Indian school career may include very little assessed speaking. A term of unseen-text work and two or three recorded practice orals usually closes the gap before the first formal assessment arrives.

faqs.question: How do Diploma command terms differ from what an Indian board asks for?
faqs.answer: Indian board questions tend to be well defined and reward a complete, accurate answer. Diploma questions turn on a verb. Describe wants features, explain wants a mechanism, evaluate wants judgement with both sides weighed, justify wants a conclusion defended. A student who gives a strong description to an evaluate question loses most of the marks while feeling they answered well. Teaching the verbs explicitly is the highest-value hour of the first month.

faqs.question: Is a Friday-morning lesson sensible when the tutor in India is working that day?
faqs.answer: It can work, but check it twice. Friday is a weekend day in the Kingdom and a working day across much of India, so a Friday morning here falls on somebody's teaching day. Some full-time tutors keep it free deliberately and it becomes the most reliable slot of the week, with no school run competing. Others cancel it first when something shifts. Ask whether the slot is protected for the term.

faqs.question: How do lessons work during Ramadan when the tutor is outside the Kingdom?
faqs.answer: The school day here shortens and family routines move later, so the lesson usually moves later too rather than stopping. A tutor abroad is often more available at that hour because they have planned for it. Agree the pattern a few weeks ahead: the slot time, which days, and whether sessions shorten. Students who keep a reduced but regular schedule lose far less ground than those who pause entirely.

faqs.question: What should an India-based tutor know about our school's scheme of work?
faqs.answer: Enough not to run a parallel course. Send the subject outline, the order of topics for the term, the internal assessment deadlines and the last two pieces of marked work. A tutor teaching ahead of the class creates confusion, and one teaching behind it wastes the hour. The deadlines matter most: a school's internal date for a draft is the real constraint in the second year, and it is the thing a tutor working from another country's calendar is most likely to miss.

faqs.question: Counting back from the May session, when is it genuinely too late to add a second subject?
faqs.answer: Six months out, adding a second subject usually costs more than it gains, because the hours come out of the subject that was already failing. Twelve months out it is reasonable. In the final eight weeks it is rarely sensible, since that window belongs to timed papers in whichever subject matters most. The better move late on is to narrow rather than widen: pick the two papers with the most recoverable marks and work only those until the session.

indian-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Count the weeks, then book the diagnostic
indian-ib-tutor.closingBody: Send the subject, the level, the component that is costing marks and the evenings that work in Arabia Standard Time, and say whether you want a tutor based in India or simply the best match for the paper. You will get a free diagnostic lesson that marks a real question, a written note of what failed, and a plan counting weeks back from the May session. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, anywhere in the Kingdom, and a different tutor after two sessions is a normal request rather than a complaint.

intro.heading: Three documents first, then a plan
paragraphs: The Indian community in the Kingdom is large and long-settled, and families move children between Indian-curriculum schools and Cambridge or Edexcel ones constantly, so the search for an Indian IGCSE tutor in Saudi Arabia is one of the busiest in this market. The reasons are sound: a shared language at home, a teaching manner the parents recognise, and a deep pool of subject teachers in India who already work online across the Gulf at reasonable rates.

What this page adds is the part nobody sends you. Before any teaching is planned there are three documents worth having: the entry confirmation showing which tier and which component codes your child has been registered for, a past paper marked against the published mark scheme, and the most recent mock percentages read against recent grade boundaries rather than against a pass mark. Those three say where a student actually is. A report comment saying good progress says almost nothing.

The second half of the page is about the system around the qualification, because IGCSE sits in an odd position in the Kingdom. It is not the final secondary certificate, so the Ministry of Education equivalency step does not arrive at this stage; it is entry evidence for sixth form and a record of subject grades. Meanwhile the school holds the tier decision, the awarding body holds the papers and the moderation, and ETEC evaluates the school rather than the teaching of any one class.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on a slot pinned to Arabia Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a Saudi address, and home visits are a service offered only in India. For this search that is worth saying plainly, because a tutor in Hyderabad or Kochi teaching a student in Jubail is exactly the arrangement most families are picturing, and it works well once the two working weeks have been reconciled.

Where a family wants a tutor from a particular background, that preference is recorded with the board, the syllabus code and the tier. What it cannot replace is experience of the examination. A teacher who has run CBSE Class 10 mathematics for a decade knows more mathematics than the paper requires and may still not know that 0580 Extended rewards a method shown over an answer reached. Both facts can be true at once, and the second one is what costs marks on the day. The fix is not a different kind of tutor but a different kind of question at the start, and the questions worth asking are set out further down this page. None of them take longer than a minute to answer, and a teacher who has taught the course answers all of them without pausing.

sections.heading: The three documents that tell you where a student actually is
paragraphs: A school report is written to be read by a hundred families at once, so it says progress is satisfactory and a parent learns nothing. Three documents do better. The first is the entry confirmation, which lists the syllabus codes and the tier your child has been registered for. Families are often surprised by what is on it. A Core entry in a science caps the grade at C, and a child aiming at a sixth-form science course with a Core entry has a problem that no amount of teaching solves.

The second is a past paper marked against the published mark scheme, question by question, with the lost marks grouped by type. That turns an impression into a list: method marks dropped for unshown working, definitions almost right, command terms misread, time lost on the long question at the end. The third is the most recent mock percentage read against recent grade boundaries rather than against a notional pass, because a percentage without a boundary is a number with no meaning attached.

Ask for all three before paying anybody for teaching. The examinations officer holds the entry confirmation, the subject teacher holds the mock data, and a marked paper can be produced in a single diagnostic hour. Together they take about a week to assemble and they change what the first month is for. Without them, a tutor and a family spend a term discovering what the documents would have said on the first day.
