sections.heading: Working back from those documents to a term plan
paragraphs: With the three documents in front of you the plan is nearly mechanical. Rank the question types by marks lost. Identify the topics each one rests on. Order the work by recoverable marks rather than by difficulty, which usually means the dull middle of the syllabus comes before the hard final chapter. Then count the weeks to the June series and see whether the list fits. If it does not, the plan has to shrink rather than the weeks stretch.

Put the plan on one page and keep it visible. Components, topics, weeks, and the evidence that will show each item is done. The evidence matters more than the schedule: a topic is not closed because it was taught, it is closed when a question of that type is answered correctly under timing. Tutors who write plans without naming the evidence end up teaching a syllabus again rather than fixing what the papers showed.

Review it against the same three documents each term. New mock percentages, a fresh marked paper, and a check that the entry and tier have not changed. If the marks have moved on the components you targeted, carry on. If they have moved everywhere except there, something in the teaching is drifting back to content delivery. If nothing has moved at all, change the plan or the tutor, and do it at the end of a term rather than at the end of a year. A term is long enough to show something and short enough to recover from.

sections.heading: Who regulates what: the school, the board and the tutor
paragraphs: Three different bodies sit behind an IGCSE and families routinely merge them into one. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education. School evaluation and accreditation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission, ETEC, which operates e-services for national school accreditation and for the approval of international accreditation bodies. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are awarding bodies: they write the syllabuses, set and mark the papers and moderate coursework.

None of those three accredits a private tutor, and no tutor anywhere holds a licence from any of them, ourselves included. A tutor may have taught a syllabus for years, may have marked for a board in a particular series, and may hold a teaching qualification from somewhere. Those are checkable facts about a person. They are not a status conferred by a regulator, and a provider implying otherwise is describing something that does not exist.

What this means practically is that the useful questions are specific rather than official. Which board and which syllabus code has the tutor taught, and for how many cohorts? Which component have they marked, and in what role? What does the mark scheme reward in a six-mark question in this subject? A teacher who answers those three crisply has the only credentials that matter at this level, whatever letterhead is or is not involved. The same test works in reverse: a provider that answers with logos rather than with syllabus codes is selling reassurance, and reassurance has never moved a grade boundary.

sections.heading: Tier entry: the one decision with a ceiling inside it
paragraphs: Many Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered, and the tier is a school decision registered with the board. Core is graded C to G; Extended is graded A* to E. A student entered for Core cannot be awarded above a C no matter how well the papers go, and that fact closes doors two years later at sixth-form entry. Pearson Edexcel does the same thing with different words, splitting mathematics into Foundation and Higher.

Schools make the decision for defensible reasons. A student secure at Core level scores better on Core papers than one struggling at Extended, and a borderline candidate entered too high can come out with less than they were capable of. The problem is not the logic, it is the silence: the decision is often made from internal assessment data a family has never seen, and communicated as a line on a form. Ask which evidence supported it.

The window is the thing to understand. A tier can be changed while entries are still open and not afterwards, so the conversation belongs well before the deadline the examinations officer is working to. If you want a tier reviewed, bring evidence rather than an opinion: two papers at the higher tier, marked honestly against the scheme, are a stronger argument than any amount of conviction. A good school will look at that evidence and say what it shows, and a tier left at Core because nobody asked is the version worth avoiding.

sections.heading: Coursework, moderation and what a tutor may touch
paragraphs: Where an IGCSE subject carries coursework or a portfolio component, the school marks it against the published criteria and the awarding body moderates those marks, which can move a cohort's marks up or down. The work itself has to be the student's own, and schools are required to run a malpractice process where they suspect it is not. That is the whole frame, and it decides what outside help can legitimately look like.

A tutor may teach the skill the task needs, explain the criteria line by line, work through an example on a different topic, and read what the student has written and say which criterion is underserved. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a paragraph or decide the conclusion. The distinction is easy to apply once it is stated: feedback points at the criteria, and anything that points at the page in the student's own file has gone too far.

Keep the record, because it protects the student rather than the tutor. Dated drafts, written feedback kept as sent, and a short note of what each session covered give a school everything it needs if a question is raised during moderation. Tell the school that an outside tutor is reading drafts; teachers would rather know than find out. A tutor unwilling to leave written feedback behind is telling you something worth hearing early, because the whole value of the component is that the marks belong to work the student did.

sections.heading: Where an IGCSE sits in the Saudi university pathway, and where it does not
paragraphs: This is the part that confuses families arriving from another system. An IGCSE is not a school-leaving certificate in the Kingdom. It is the qualification that gets a student into a sixth form and a record of subject grades that a sixth form uses to decide which A Levels or Diploma subjects it will allow. The certificate a Saudi university eventually looks at is the one issued two years later.

That ordering matters because the Ministry of Education equivalency decision, mu'adalah, attaches to the final secondary certificate rather than to an interim one. Families who try to arrange it on IGCSE results are early by two years. Separately, ETEC runs Qudurat and Tahsili through its National Center for Assessment, Qiyas, and those are sat towards the end of school rather than at sixteen. Each university then publishes its own admission criteria by programme, and those published criteria are the only binding version.

What a family can usefully do at IGCSE stage is protect the options. Keep the science and mathematics tiers high enough to leave a science route open. Keep a second language if an overseas application is possible. Check what the intended sixth form requires before the option forms are signed rather than after the results arrive. None of that needs a decision about universities yet; it simply avoids closing a door for the sake of an easier Year 11. The cost of keeping an option open at sixteen is a term of harder work, and the cost of closing it is a route that is no longer available.

sections.heading: What an Indian-board teacher brings to IGCSE, and what has to be checked
paragraphs: The strength is real and worth paying for. CBSE and ICSE courses are demanding, particularly in mathematics and the sciences, and a teacher who has run Class 9 and Class 10 for years is fluent in content that an IGCSE paper treats as assumed. For a student with weak foundations, that fluency is the fastest route back, and it tends to cost less per hour than a UK-based specialist advertising the same subject.

What has to be checked is the examination behaviour rather than the subject. IGCSE mark schemes pay for a method shown, a definition given in the expected words, a command term answered as written, and a practical method described precisely enough to repeat. An Indian board rewards an accurate complete answer to a well-defined question, which is a different habit. A teacher who has not taught the syllabus can pass on their own habit without noticing, and a student loses marks while being taught well.

So ask the specific questions. Which syllabus code, and how many cohorts? Core or Extended, and what differs between the papers? What does the alternative-to-practical paper ask for that a textbook never drills? A teacher who has taught both systems is usually the best option on the table, because they can name the gap instead of discovering it in a mock. Those who have taught only one can still be excellent, provided somebody is watching the assessment side. Ask for a marked paper in the first fortnight and you will know which case you are in.

faqs.question: Does an Indian IGCSE tutor need to know both Cambridge and Edexcel, or just one?
faqs.answer: Just the one your child is entered for, and that is the point: they are different examinations. Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1 cover similar mathematics with different paper structures, formula provision and tiering language. A tutor who knows one well and assumes the other is similar will teach the wrong paper discipline. Send the syllabus code from the entry confirmation and ask whether they have taught that exact code. A specialist in both exists; a specialist in neither is the risk.

faqs.question: Our tutor taught CBSE Class 10 mathematics — is that enough for 0580 Extended?
faqs.answer: For content, usually more than enough. For marks, it depends on one habit. Paper 4 pays method marks for working shown on multi-step questions with no scaffolding, and students trained to produce clean final answers lose those marks routinely. Ask the tutor to mark one Paper 4 question against the published scheme in front of you. If they award and explain the method marks correctly, the content strength is the advantage it looks like.

faqs.question: Which marked work should we send a new IGCSE tutor before the first session?
faqs.answer: The most recent marked paper with the mark scheme if you have it, the last two pieces of returned classwork, and the entry confirmation showing codes and tier. Those three let a tutor plan the first hour instead of spending it asking questions. If marked work is not available, say so and ask for a diagnostic paper in the first session instead. What should not happen is a first lesson that begins with chapter one of the textbook.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects does a school in the Kingdom usually enter at Core tier without telling the family?
faqs.answer: The sciences most often, and sometimes mathematics for students who struggled in Year 9. It is rarely concealed deliberately; it appears on a form a parent never reads closely. The consequence is real, because a Core entry caps the grade at C and a sixth form asking for a B in a science will not see one. Ask the examinations officer for the entry confirmation in the autumn term of Year 10, and read the tier beside every subject.

faqs.question: Can a school change our child's IGCSE tier after the entry has gone in?
faqs.answer: While entries are still open, usually yes, and after they close, no. That makes the timing of the conversation everything. If you want a tier reviewed, go early and go with evidence: two higher-tier papers marked against the published scheme are a far stronger argument than a conviction that your child is capable of more. Ask the examinations officer for the internal deadline, because it falls earlier than families expect and no appeal exists afterwards.

faqs.question: If an India-based tutor gives feedback on coursework, what has to be recorded?
faqs.answer: Keep three things: the dated drafts in the student's own file, the feedback exactly as the tutor sent it, and a one-line note of what each session covered. That set answers any question a school asks during moderation. Tell the subject teacher that an outside tutor is reading drafts, because teachers would rather know than discover it. Nothing about outside teaching is prohibited; what is prohibited is anybody other than the student producing the work.

faqs.question: Does using an India-based tutor create any academic honesty issue a Saudi school would flag?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. Schools care about who produced the work, not about where the teaching came from. What does get flagged is a sudden change in a student's written voice, work handed in that the student cannot explain, or coursework with no draft history. All three are avoidable with a tutor who gives feedback rather than text. Keeping the drafts and the written comments turns a potential question into a one-minute conversation.

faqs.question: What does ETEC's school accreditation tell us about the IGCSE results a school gets?
faqs.answer: Less than families hope. The Education and Training Evaluation Commission handles school evaluation and accreditation, including e-services for national school accreditation and for approving international accreditation bodies, and the Ministry of Education licenses private and international schools. Both operate at the level of the institution. Neither reports which tier a Year 10 group was entered for, who teaches it, or how a particular subject performed. For that, ask the school for its own subject-level results.

faqs.question: At which point in a Saudi school career does the Ministry of Education equivalency step actually arrive?
faqs.answer: At the end, on the final secondary certificate, not on IGCSE results. An international certificate needs an equivalency decision from the Ministry before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate, and that decision attaches to the A Level or Diploma certificate issued two years after IGCSE. Families who start the process at sixteen are early. What is worth doing at sixteen is confirming what the Ministry and the intended universities ask for.

faqs.question: Our child is moving from an ICSE Class 9 into IGCSE Year 10 — what is lost?
faqs.answer: Very little content, and a certain amount of time. ICSE Class 9 covers more than enough mathematics and science for the start of an IGCSE course, so the gap is assessment style: shorter answers, strict command terms, mark schemes that reward a specific move, and practical or alternative-to-practical papers with no ICSE equivalent. Budget the first term for that rather than for catching up on topics, and check which tier the school intends to enter.

faqs.question: Is it better to finish Class 10 on an Indian board or move to IGCSE now?
faqs.answer: If the family is staying in the Kingdom and the child will go on to A Levels or the Diploma, moving before Year 10 is cleaner than moving during it. Mid-year moves cost a term to assessment style and may land the student in a tier decision made on no local evidence. If the move has to happen mid-course, ask the receiving school in writing which subjects have places, which tier they would enter, and what they will accept from the previous school.

faqs.question: What does a school in the Kingdom ask for when admitting a student from an Indian board into Year 10?
faqs.answer: Typically the last two years of reports, any standardised test results the previous school holds, and often its own placement assessment in English and mathematics. The placement paper matters more than the reports, because it is what the tier decision will rest on. A student who sits it straight off a flight, jet-lagged and unfamiliar with the question style, can be placed lower than they belong. Ask whether it can be sat a fortnight after arrival instead.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to pick up after an Indian-board Class 9?
faqs.answer: English First Language and the humanities, consistently. The content is not the problem; the writing is. Source-based history questions, directed writing in a fixed register, and extended answers judged on structure rather than completeness are all new performances. Physics and chemistry are usually comfortable except for the alternative-to-practical paper, which asks for experimental reasoning no Indian board examines in that form. Plan those two gaps deliberately and the rest tends to look after itself.

faqs.question: How do we judge after one term whether an India-based IGCSE tutor is worth continuing with?
faqs.answer: Read the same evidence you started with. Have the question types on the ranked list stopped leaking marks? Has the topic checklist moved? Did the mock percentage rise on the paper that was targeted rather than across the board? If the answer is yes to two of the three, continue. If nothing in the written record has changed in a term, change the plan or the tutor, and say which specific thing is not working so the second match is better.

indian-igcse-tutor.closingBody: Ask the examinations officer for the entry confirmation showing the syllabus codes and the tier, find the most recent marked paper, and send both with the evenings that work in Arabia Standard Time. You will get a free diagnostic lesson that marks a real question, a written note of the question types costing marks, and a one-page plan counting weeks to the June series. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, anywhere in the Kingdom, and a different tutor after two sessions is a normal request rather than a complaint.

jazan.heroEyebrow: IB AND IGCSE TUITION FOR JAZAN FAMILIES
jazan.heroSubtitle: IB and IGCSE tutors for families in Jazan teach one-to-one over live video, because in the far south-west of the Kingdom distance, not curriculum, is the thing that limits choice. This page starts where a parent here has the least information: what measurable progress in an international syllabus actually looks like, what evidence proves it, and how a term of teaching is planned backwards from that evidence. Rates, year-group timing, the series calendar and the university step all follow from it.

Lessons on Arabia Standard Time, Sunday to Thursday, after the school day
A free trial lesson before anything is paid, with a written baseline

jazan.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach Diploma Programme subjects, the Middle Years Programme and Cambridge or Edexcel IGCSE. Each profile states the syllabus, the level and which papers that tutor prepares students for, so a family in Jazan can see the teaching experience behind the match rather than a list of adjectives about enthusiasm.

intro.heading: Begin with the evidence, then build the term around it
paragraphs: Most tutoring decisions in Jazan are made without a baseline. A school report says seventy-two per cent. A teacher says the student is capable. Neither statement says what a Cambridge examiner would pay for the same script, and that is the number a family is actually buying a change in. So the first useful act is not booking lessons. It is producing one piece of comparable evidence: a timed section of a past paper, marked against the published mark scheme, with the losses sorted by question type. That takes an hour and it reframes everything that follows.

The reason this matters more here than in Riyadh or the Eastern Province is isolation. Jazan is a Red Sea province capital in the far south-west, with an economic city and a university driving recent growth, and international-curriculum provision across the province is minimal. There is no large pool of parents comparing notes about the same Diploma cohort, no neighbour whose daughter sat the same Extended-tier paper last session, and often no local teacher who has marked one. A family here is working without the informal benchmarking that families in bigger markets take for granted, which makes formal evidence the substitute.

Measurable progress has a specific meaning in these courses, and it is worth stating. It is not a higher percentage on the next school test. It is a raw mark on a comparable past paper moving upwards, a named loss pattern disappearing from the marked script, a criterion descriptor on a piece of coursework being met where it previously was not, and the student finishing the paper instead of abandoning the last question. Each of those is checkable by a parent who has never studied the syllabus, which is exactly why they are the right measures.

From that baseline the plan runs in one direction only: backwards from the series the student is entered for. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series and a November series, and schools in the Kingdom enter candidates for those; the IB's main sitting for Saudi schools is the May session. Everything else in the plan is positioned relative to those fixed points, including coursework deadlines, mock examinations and the final weeks when technique rather than content is where the remaining marks sit.

Lessons for families in Jazan are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to an address anywhere in the Kingdom, and home visits are a service we run only in India. In a province where the nearest large international-school market is several hundred kilometres up the coast, that is not a compromise: it is the only arrangement that puts a student in front of somebody who has taught their actual syllabus. The alternative most families weigh is relocation or boarding, which is a far larger decision than a weekly lesson.

jazan.programmesIntro: Four programmes account for nearly every request that reaches us from this province, and the right one for a family is often decided by which school place was actually available rather than by preference. Each entry below says what the programme assesses and what it means for a student studying it from a part of the Kingdom with very few international places.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led units rather than separate subjects, with no external examinations and a final-year exhibition the student plans and presents. The assessment a parent sees is formative and descriptive. What carries forward into later programmes is reading stamina, number fluency and the habit of writing down a line of reasoning instead of only an answer.
programmes.countryNote: Few Jazan families have a PYP place locally, so the requests that arrive are usually from households preparing a child for a move to an international school elsewhere in the Kingdom, or supporting one who has just arrived in an inquiry-led classroom from a very different one. The work is almost always written explanation in English rather than subject content.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years, eight subject groups, and every subject marked against four criteria out of eight. Criterion grades, not test percentages, are the currency. The Personal Project closes the programme and is assessed on planning, applying skills and reflecting. Some schools enter candidates for MYP eAssessment, which pairs on-screen examinations with ePortfolios for the MYP Certificate.
programmes.countryNote: The measurable thing at this stage is criterion movement, and it is the easiest kind of progress for a Jazan parent to verify because the descriptors are published. A student scoring five on knowledge and three on evaluating does not need more content; they need to be taught what the top band of that one criterion actually asks for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three Higher and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are graded together on a matrix worth up to three additional points, and the Diploma has pass conditions beyond the total. Higher Level courses carry more taught hours and, in several subjects, an extra paper.
programmes.countryNote: A Jazan student in the Diploma is usually either boarding, living with relatives nearer a school, or relocated with the family. Weekly online teaching is what keeps the subject with the thinnest local support from becoming the grade that decides the total, and in practice that is most often a Higher Level science or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by written papers, with sciences adding a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 is tiered: Core papers cap the grade range and Extended papers open the top of it. The sciences divide the same way. The tier a school enters a candidate for sets the ceiling before the paper is opened.
programmes.countryNote: IGCSE is the commonest international qualification in requests from this province, often taken by a student who moved into a British-curriculum school for the final two years of secondary school. Tier entry is the question to settle early, because a candidate placed on Core to keep a mixed class manageable cannot reach the top grades at all.

jazan.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects families in the south-west ask about most. Each entry names the components and the weighting where it is published, because a parent who knows which paper carries the most marks can see immediately whether a tutor's plan is aimed at the right thing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 are worth thirty per cent each, Paper 3 twenty, and the exploration twenty. Paper 1 is written without technology, so algebraic fluency is exposed directly. Progress here is visible as speed and accuracy on untimed manipulation first, then as structured reasoning on the Paper 3 extended problem.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: A calculator is allowed throughout and the statistical and modelling content is heavier. At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 are worth forty per cent each with the exploration at twenty. The loss pattern is interpretation rather than calculation: a regression performed correctly and never explained in context earns part of the available marks.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, fields, waves, electricity and nuclear physics, with the Higher Level extension adding whole topics rather than extra detail. The written papers carry eighty per cent between them and the scientific investigation twenty. Graph interpretation and the precise wording of definitions are the two places marks reliably disappear.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Quantitative chemistry, energetics, kinetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms, with twenty per cent from the internally assessed investigation. Multi-step calculations lose marks through dropped units and unrounded intermediate values; mechanisms lose them through missing curly arrows that the mark scheme expects to see.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Concept-led content from molecular biology to ecology, examined partly through data-based questions on experiments the student has never seen. The investigation is twenty per cent. The characteristic error is volume: writing everything recalled about a topic when the question is paying for three developed points.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics and the global economy. At Higher Level, Paper 1 is twenty per cent, Paper 2 thirty, the quantitative Paper 3 thirty and the internal assessment twenty. At Standard Level the commentaries carry thirty. Diagram accuracy and explicit real-world application decide most of the extended-response marks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is a guided analysis of an unseen text at thirty-five per cent for both levels. Higher Level adds the HL essay at twenty per cent, with the individual oral internally assessed. The examined skill is close reading at speed, which improves through weekly timed practice on unseen texts and detailed marking.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: Receptive, productive and interactive skills across five prescribed themes, with text types that have to be produced correctly. Confident speakers frequently score below their ability in writing, because register and structure are marked as well as accuracy. Less common tenses are the usual technical gap.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Physical and human geography with case studies that have to be specific to earn credit, plus internally assessed fieldwork. Students in a coastal agricultural province often have strong local material for coasts, water and food systems, and lose marks only by keeping examples general when the question asks for a named place.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Organisation, human resources, finance, marketing and operations, with a pre-released case study for one paper. Tools are usually known and evaluation is usually weak: a listed analysis instead of a judgement, or a recommendation with no stated criteria. Finance calculations are the other recurring loss.

jazan.igcseSubjectsIntro: IGCSE requests from Jazan Province concentrate on the Extended tier and on the sciences, which carry an extra practical component that a student in a small school may have had little chance to rehearse. Syllabus codes are given so a family can check that a tutor knows the actual paper structure.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics 0580
igcseSubjects.description: Core candidates sit Papers 1 and 3 for a capped grade range; Extended candidates sit Papers 2 and 4 and can reach the top. Extended Paper 4 is where most tuition time goes, because its multi-part questions give method marks only when the method is written down.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology 0610
igcseSubjects.description: From characteristics of living organisms to ecology and human influence, with a practical test or the alternative to practical. Extended candidates meet longer structured questions on unfamiliar data, where the command word suggest expects reasoning rather than a recalled fact.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry 0620
igcseSubjects.description: Multiple-choice, theory and a practical component. Moles and stoichiometry come first in almost every teaching plan, then electrolysis and organic chemistry. The alternative-to-practical paper is a separate skill: reading apparatus, identifying variables and improving a described method.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics 0625
igcseSubjects.description: Forces and motion, thermal physics, waves, electricity and atomic physics. Definitions are marked strictly, so a nearly correct definition scores nothing, and graph questions reward axis labels, units and read-offs taken from the line rather than from the data points.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language 0510
igcseSubjects.description: Reading, writing and listening, with speaking assessed separately. The writing tasks are marked on content and language together, and able readers still lose marks by missing the audience and purpose the task specifies.

igcseSubjects.name: Geography 0460 and Economics 0455
igcseSubjects.description: Both reward precise definitions and named examples, and both include data-response questions where the stimulus material has to be read properly before anything is written. Geography adds coursework or an alternative paper, depending on what the school enters.

jazan.regionsTitle: Jazan Province, and what the geography does to a school week
jazan.regionsIntro: Jazan Province runs from the Red Sea coast and the Farasan Islands inland to the highland governorates, with the provincial capital, the economic city and the university at its centre. Travel times inside the province are the reason an online slot is often the only workable arrangement, and the reason the summer break does so much of the work.

regions.name: Jazan city and the Corniche
regions.note: The provincial capital, port and administrative centre, with the widest choice of schooling in the province and the shortest journeys to it. Most requests from the province come from here, and most are for a subject the local school cannot cover in depth.

regions.name: Jazan Economic City
regions.note: The industrial development north of the city, with its own workforce and housing. Shift patterns here shape the household evening more than traffic does, so lesson slots tend to be agreed late and kept short rather than long and ambitious.

regions.name: Sabya
regions.note: One of the larger governorates north of the capital, agricultural and well connected by road. Families here often commute into Jazan city for schooling, which pushes the realistic start of an evening lesson past seven o'clock in term time.

regions.name: Abu Arish
regions.note: South-east of the capital and close enough for a daily school commute. Requests from this area lean towards IGCSE rather than the Diploma, usually for a student who joined a British-curriculum school late in secondary school.

regions.name: Samtah
regions.note: Near the southern coastal strip, further from the capital's schools. The distance is what makes a weekly online slot practical where a drive to a tutor would not be, particularly for a student carrying two subjects at once.

regions.name: Ahad Al Masarihah
regions.note: A southern governorate with its own town centre and services. Families here are typically choosing between a long daily commute and online teaching for the subjects their nearest school does not staff at the level required.

regions.name: Baish and Al Darb
regions.note: North of the capital along the coastal road, agricultural and dispersed. Internet reliability rather than distance is the practical question for an online lesson here, and a fallback plan for a dropped connection belongs in the arrangement from the start.

regions.name: Farasan Islands
regions.note: Offshore and reached by ferry from Jazan port, with a small resident population. Nothing about a daily commute to a mainland tutor is realistic, which makes a scheduled video lesson the only arrangement that survives a term.

regions.name: Fifa and the highland governorates
regions.note: Mountain communities inland, reached by steep roads that make evening travel slow. Families here plan around the drive, so sessions are usually set for later in the evening or consolidated into the weekend when a series is close.

schoolClusters.city: Jeddah, the nearest large international-school market
schoolClusters.note: Several hundred kilometres north along the Red Sea coast, Jeddah carries the nearest substantial concentration of international and IB provision, running as a long coastal spine from the historic centre up to Obhur. Jazan families who want an IB Diploma place usually look here first, by relocation, by boarding or by a weekly commute that very few households sustain. Private and international schools in the Kingdom are licensed by the Ministry of Education, and school evaluation runs through the Education and Training Evaluation Commission.

schoolClusters.city: Riyadh, where Diploma Programme choice is widest
schoolClusters.note: The capital holds the broadest range of IB World Schools in the Kingdom and therefore the widest choice of Higher Level combinations, which is why a relocating family with a DP1 student often ends up there rather than on the coast. IB World Schools are concentrated in Riyadh, Jeddah and the Eastern Province rather than spread evenly; the IB publishes its own searchable directory, and that is the place to confirm whether a school currently runs the programme you need.

jazan.schoolDisclaimer: These schools are named to describe the choices open to a Jazan family, as context only; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and programme availability should be confirmed with each school directly.
jazan.modesIntro: Three arrangements cover almost everything requested from this province, and the choice between them follows from the evidence rather than from preference. A student with content gaps needs weekly teaching; a student with a technique problem close to a series needs timed papers; a student with coursework due needs criterion feedback on their own draft.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the term
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, one slot held across the term. Work is set after each lesson and marked before the next, which is what makes progress measurable week by week rather than visible only at the next report. This is the arrangement that shifts a loss pattern, because a pattern only shifts through repeated feedback on the same kind of question.
bullets: A fixed weekly slot written in Arabia Standard Time
Marked work returned before the following lesson
A short written note to the parent naming paper, topic and progress
Paused and resumed around school holidays without losing the slot

modes.title: A summer rebuild block
modes.description: The long break is the one period when a student is working in the morning rather than after a full school day, and in a hot, humid coastal province it is also when the household is least likely to be travelling for anything else. A rebuild block uses it to repair a foundation from the year below, which is slow work that does not fit comfortably into a term-time evening.
bullets: Morning sessions, two or three a week, over several weeks
Aimed at the previous year's gaps rather than the coming year's syllabus
A written baseline at the start and the same paper repeated at the end
Best used after a disappointing result, not instead of term-time work

modes.title: Coursework criterion clinics
modes.description: Scheduled sessions around an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Personal Project, in which the tutor reads what the student has written and teaches against the published criteria. The student does the writing throughout. Nothing is drafted, rewritten or supplied for them, and the school supervisor remains the person who authenticates the work.
bullets: Research questions tested for scope before the writing starts
Feedback mapped to criterion descriptors, not line edits
Method and data-handling review for science investigations
A written record of each session the school can see

sections.heading: What measurable progress actually looks like in these courses
paragraphs: Ask most providers what progress looks like and the answer is confidence, engagement or a percentage. None of those survives contact with an examiner. In an IB or IGCSE course, progress is visible in four places and nowhere else: the raw mark on a comparable past paper, the distribution of lost marks across question types, the criterion descriptors met on a piece of assessed coursework, and whether the candidate finished the paper. A family that tracks those four needs no faith in anybody's enthusiasm.

Each of them is checkable by a parent who has never studied the subject. A marked past paper comes with a published mark scheme, and the lost marks can be sorted into categories: content not known, command term misread, method not shown, time ran out. That sort is the diagnosis. It tells a family whether they are buying teaching, technique or stamina, and those three purchases look completely different in practice. Buying weekly content teaching for a timing problem wastes a term.

The fourth measure is the one families overlook. A candidate who leaves eighteen marks unattempted at the end of a paper is not short of knowledge; they are short of pace, and pace is trained by sitting whole papers under the clock rather than by covering more syllabus. In a province where a student may be the only person in their class taking a particular Higher Level subject, nobody else will notice that pattern. The marked script will.

sections.heading: Counting the plan backwards from the series
paragraphs: Once a baseline exists, the plan is arithmetic. There is a fixed date the student sits papers, and everything else is positioned relative to it. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run a June series, which is the main one for schools in the Kingdom, and a November series used for resits and November-entry candidates. The IB's main sitting for Saudi schools is the May session. Your school's examinations officer holds the exact dates, and the Diploma Programme coordinator holds the internal deadlines, which are usually the ones that bite first.

One correction is worth making because copied-in advice gets it wrong constantly: Cambridge's February and March series is sat in India and not in the Kingdom, so a Jazan family should ignore any entry deadline quoted for it. Candidates here enter June or November. Acting on an Indian calendar has a real cost, because entries close months ahead of the papers and a missed window means either a late-entry fee or a wait for the next series.

The table below is the shape of a cycle rather than a set of dates, which is deliberate: the specific days differ by school and by board, and the school is the authoritative source for all of them. What does not change is the order, and the order is what families get wrong. Coursework is scoped long before anybody feels urgency about it, entries close before the mocks are marked, and the last eight weeks are worth far more if the syllabus was finished before them.

sections.heading: Year by year: what matters at MYP, IGCSE, DP1 and DP2
paragraphs: The same request means different things in different year groups, and buying the wrong year's support is a common and expensive mistake. In the Middle Years Programme the currency is criterion grades, so the work is teaching a student what the top band of a specific criterion asks for. At IGCSE the decisive event is tier entry, which happens quietly and sets a ceiling. In the first Diploma year the work is foundations and coursework scoping. In the second it is technique, because by then there is no time to rebuild anything large.

The hinge year is the first Diploma year, and it is the one families most often leave alone because there is no examination at the end of it. That is precisely why it is cheap to fix and expensive to ignore. A student who reaches the second year with weak algebra, an unscoped Extended Essay and no experience of a full timed paper is carrying three problems that each need a term, and they now have one term for all three. A student who finishes the first year with those three in order needs technique teaching, which is fast.

Starting late is not hopeless, but the honest version is narrower. With a single term before a series, the realistic target is marks that come from technique: reading the command term, structuring a six-mark answer, showing method so arithmetic errors cost one mark instead of four, and pacing the paper so the last question gets attempted. Content gains in that window are limited to high-yield topics the paper almost always samples. A tutor promising more than that in eight weeks is selling something nobody can deliver.

sections.heading: Weightings, and where the marks are actually earned
paragraphs: Families plan revision by subject. Examiners award marks by component. Those two facts are the source of a great deal of wasted effort, because a student can spend a month on the part of a course worth a fifth of the grade while the component worth a third goes unrehearsed. Published weightings fix this, and they are worth having on the wall at home. They also make it obvious when a tutor's plan is aimed somewhere other than where the marks live.

The internally assessed components deserve particular attention in a province with little local specialist support. A science investigation is worth twenty per cent of the final grade at both levels and is done over weeks, with published criteria, which makes it the most controllable fifth of the grade in the whole course. The mathematics exploration is the same twenty per cent. A student who treats coursework as an inconvenience is giving away the one part of the course where time, rather than talent or luck on the day, is what decides the mark.

The written papers then reward different things, and the differences are not intuitive. A non-calculator paper tests fluency; a data-response paper tests reading; an extended-response paper tests the shape of an argument. The practical consequence for a Jazan student working with limited classroom contact is that each component needs rehearsing on its own terms, and the fastest way to find out which one is weakest is to sit each of them once, timed, and mark them against the scheme.

sections.heading: Distance, not curriculum, is the constraint here
paragraphs: It is worth being direct about the geography, because it is the real difference between studying an international syllabus in Jazan and studying one in Riyadh. International-curriculum provision in this province is minimal. The nearest large market is Jeddah, several hundred kilometres north along the coast; Abha and Khamis Mushait sit inland to the north-east at altitude and share a catchment with each other rather than with the coast. For most families here, the options are a national-curriculum school locally, relocation, boarding, or an international course supported from outside the province.

That shapes which subjects cause trouble. A student in a school with one teacher per subject area is not badly taught, but they have no second opinion available, no departmental past-paper culture, and no colleague who has marked for the board. The components that suffer are the ones that need a specialist eye: the scientific investigation, the Higher Level extension topics, the quantitative paper in Economics, and unseen textual analysis. Those are exactly the components that reward an hour a week with somebody who teaches that paper regularly.

Internet reliability, not distance, is the practical planning question for an online lesson in the outlying governorates. It is worth testing the connection at the time of day the lesson will actually run, which is not the same as testing it at noon, and worth agreeing in advance what happens if a session drops: resume, reschedule, or continue by voice with the document shared. Families who settle that in the first week rarely lose a lesson to it afterwards.

sections.heading: The summer window, and why Jazan families use it
paragraphs: The long summer break does more work in this province than anywhere else we teach in the Kingdom. The climate on this part of the Red Sea coast is hot and humid for much of the year, outdoor time in the middle of the day is limited, and the break itself is long. A student who had a poor year has one period available in which they are fresh in the morning rather than depleted after a full school day, and morning work on a weak foundation is worth roughly double the same hour at nine in the evening.

Rebuilding a foundation is slow, unglamorous work: index laws, rearranging formulae, balancing equations, the grammar of a paragraph. None of it fits comfortably into a term-time evening slot alongside homework, and most of it is the reason a student is losing marks two years later. A summer block aimed at the previous year's gaps, with a written baseline at the start and the same diagnostic repeated at the end, is the cheapest intervention available in these courses and the one most often skipped.

What the summer is not good for is covering next year's syllabus ahead of the school. Students who arrive in September having been pre-taught a term's content usually disengage from the lessons that follow and end the year no further ahead. The exception is a student entering the first Diploma year from a different system, where a few weeks on the specific vocabulary of command terms, on how criteria work, and on what a timed paper feels like genuinely pays for itself in the first month.

sections.heading: The first month, and the review that decides whether to continue
paragraphs: A first month that produces no evidence has produced nothing. The free trial lesson should end with a diagnosis a parent can repeat in one sentence, and the first full session should produce a marked timed paper rather than a conversation. From those two the tutor writes a plan: the topics in teaching order, the papers to be practised, the parent's part, and the date of the review. A plan without a review date is an open-ended subscription.

Reporting should be short and concrete. The paper, the topic, the loss pattern, whether the work set arrived, and what the next fortnight targets. Four lines beat four paragraphs, and anything that could have been written about any student in the Kingdom should be sent back. Across a term the reports are a record a family can read in sequence to see whether a named weakness moved, which is the only question that matters at the review.

At the review the answer should be one of three things, given plainly. It is working, continue. It is working too slowly, and here is what changes: a different tutor, a different component, a different frequency. Or it is not working, and here is the honest reason, which might be that the student is not doing the work, or that the subject is not the real problem, or that the match is wrong. Changing tutor after a month is routine and costs almost nothing. A term spent waiting costs a term.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: Several providers in this part of the market sell something that is not tutoring, and a family should know where the line sits before they are offered the wrong side of it. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria, explain what a descriptor means in practice, read a draft the student has written and identify which criterion it fails, challenge a research question that cannot be answered within the word count, teach the statistics or the referencing conventions the student has not met, and review a method for a science investigation.

A tutor may not write, redraft or supply any part of assessed work. They do not produce the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay or the Personal Project, and they do not hand over text to be pasted in. Editing a student's draft sentence by sentence into something better is the same offence in a more respectable jacket. The candidate signs a declaration that the work is their own, the school supervisor authenticates it, and a school that suspects malpractice is required to investigate. The consequences fall on the student.

Word and page limits are worth knowing in advance, because they are applied strictly: the Extended Essay runs to four thousand words, the Theory of Knowledge essay to sixteen hundred, a science investigation to three thousand, and a mathematics exploration to roughly twelve to twenty pages. Work beyond the limit is not read past the cap, which turns a strong conclusion into no conclusion at all. Keeping a written record of each feedback session also protects the student, because it shows exactly what help was given and when.
bullets: Teaching the criteria and reviewing the student's own draft is legitimate
No part of assessed work is ever written or rewritten by a tutor

sections.heading: After school: equivalency and the Qiyas tests from a Jazan starting point
paragraphs: A family planning towards a Saudi university needs to know about a step that most pages in this market never mention. An international certificate, whether an IB Diploma, A Levels or an American high school diploma, requires an equivalency decision from the Ministry of Education before a Saudi university treats it as equivalent to the Saudi secondary certificate. The process is administrative, it takes time, and it belongs in the final-year plan rather than in the weeks after results. Some universities also limit how old a secondary certificate may be when it is submitted.

Two national tests sit alongside school grades. Qudurat, the General Aptitude Test, is administered by the Education and Training Evaluation Commission through its National Center for Assessment, Qiyas, and examines verbal and quantitative reasoning rather than syllabus content; it can be taken in Arabic or in English. Tahsili, the Achievement Test, covers the science-stream subjects: mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English. Its content follows the Saudi national curriculum.

That final detail is the one international-curriculum families most need and least often hear. A Diploma or IGCSE student has usually met most of the Tahsili material, but in a different sequence, with different framing and in a question style they have never practised. The overlap is genuine and the presentation is not, which is why strong candidates sometimes find Tahsili harder than their own examinations. Preparation is a separate piece of work from Diploma teaching and starts with past papers in the test's own format. Each university publishes its own admission criteria combining school grades with these tests, and the weightings differ by university and by programme, so read the institution's own published requirements rather than a summary of them.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the last marked work
process.description: The useful starting information is the syllabus code, the level, the series the student is entered for and a photograph of the most recent marked script. From that we can tell before any lesson whether the problem is likely to be content, technique or pace, and which tutor should take the trial.

process.title: A free trial lesson that ends in a diagnosis
process.description: The tutor works through the marked script and a question or two from a past paper, then states plainly what is going wrong. No payment is taken before that. A trial lesson spent on introductions and encouragement has not done its job, and you should say so.

process.title: A timed baseline, marked to the published scheme
process.description: The first full session produces a marked past-paper section with the lost marks sorted by cause: content not known, command term misread, method not shown, time ran out. That sorting is what decides the plan, and it is the number everything later is measured against.

process.title: A written plan, counted backwards from the series
process.description: Teaching order, papers to practise, coursework deadlines, the parent's part and a review date, all positioned relative to the June series, the November series or the May session. Your school's internal deadlines go in first, because they usually arrive before the board's.

process.title: Weekly teaching, with marked work in between
process.description: The slot runs Sunday to Thursday on Arabia Standard Time, with work set after each lesson and marked before the next. Reports name the paper, the topic and whether the identified weakness has moved, in a form a parent can read in sequence across a term.

process.title: A review with three possible answers
process.description: At the review we compare current evidence with the baseline and give one of three answers: continue, change something specific, or stop. Each comes with the reason. Changing tutor or stopping is a legitimate outcome and far cheaper than a term of hoping it improves.

whyPoints.title: A baseline before a bill
whyPoints.description: The arrangement starts with a marked timed paper and a written diagnosis, so a family knows what they are buying a change in. Where there is no local cohort to compare against, that evidence is the only reliable benchmark a Jazan parent has, and it costs an hour to produce.

whyPoints.title: Planned backwards from the series
whyPoints.description: The series the student sits is the fixed point and everything else is positioned against it: coursework scoping, entry windows, mock examinations, and the final weeks of timed papers. Your school holds the exact dates, and those go into the plan before anything else does.

whyPoints.title: The right year group's work
whyPoints.description: First-year Diploma support looks nothing like second-year support, and MYP work is about criterion descriptors rather than content. Matching the support to the year group avoids the commonest waste in this market: buying technique teaching for a student who still has a foundation gap.

whyPoints.title: Reach that does not depend on the road
whyPoints.description: Teaching is online, one-to-one and on Saudi local time, which is what makes a specialist reachable from Samtah, Farasan or a highland governorate. The tutor is chosen because they teach that paper, not because a drive to your district is feasible on a weekday evening.

whyPoints.title: Clear about coursework, in writing
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach criteria and give written feedback on work the student wrote. No Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project is produced for a candidate. The feedback record is deliberately visible, because that protects the student if a school ever asks what help was given.

faqs.question: How is a target grade set honestly for a Jazan student with no mock examination history?
faqs.answer: From a baseline rather than from ambition. A timed past-paper section marked to the published scheme gives a current raw mark; the realistic target is set from that, the time remaining and how much of the loss is technique rather than missing content. Technique losses close faster than content gaps, so two students on the same mark can have different honest targets. The target is then reviewed when the first real mock arrives, because a full paper tests pace and stamina that a single section cannot show.

faqs.question: How many Diploma points do the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge contribute together, and how are they combined?
faqs.answer: Up to three, awarded from a matrix that reads the two grades together rather than adding them separately. A strong grade in one and a weak grade in the other produces fewer points than two solid middling grades, which surprises families who assume the Extended Essay can simply carry the core. There are also conditions in the Diploma's pass requirements attached to the core, so a failing core grade matters beyond the points. Your school's Diploma coordinator can show you the current matrix and explain how it applies to your child's two grades.

faqs.question: Who decides whether a student sits Cambridge Core or Extended tier papers, and when is that fixed?
faqs.answer: The school decides, as part of its entry for the series, and in practice the decision is often made earlier than families expect when teaching groups are set. It matters because Core papers cap the grade range while Extended papers open the top of it, so a candidate placed on Core cannot reach the highest grades however well they perform. Ask explicitly, in writing, which tier your child is being prepared for and which they will be entered for. If the answer is Core and the target needs more, that conversation has to happen while there is still time to change the teaching.

faqs.question: Which papers carry the most weight in Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Papers 1 and 2 carry forty per cent each, and the exploration twenty. Both papers allow a graphic display calculator, which means the examination does not reward speed at manual arithmetic; it rewards choosing the right tool and then interpreting what it produced. Most of the lost marks in this course sit in that second half: a statistical test run correctly and never explained in the context of the data, or a model used without stating its limitations. Revision weighted towards interpretation rather than calculation usually moves the mark faster.

faqs.question: How is internally assessed coursework moderated once a school has marked it?
faqs.answer: The school marks the work against the published criteria and submits marks with a sample of the work itself. The board then reviews that sample to check the school applied the criteria at the same standard as everyone else, and adjusts the cohort's marks if it did not. The practical consequence for a family is that a generous internal mark is not a result: it can move down. The way to protect a coursework grade is to make it meet the descriptors plainly enough that no moderator has to interpret it kindly.

faqs.question: What evidence should a Jazan family ask for before agreeing to continue after one term?
faqs.answer: Three things, side by side: the baseline from week one, the most recent comparable marked paper, and the sequence of weekly notes in between. Those answer the only question that matters, which is whether the weakness identified at the start has moved. Ask for it as a comparison rather than a summary, because a summary can describe effort while the marks sit still. If the evidence is thin, that is itself the answer, and the better response is to change something specific rather than to buy another term on trust.

faqs.question: How do we diagnose a starting point for a Jazan student who has never sat a full past paper?
faqs.answer: Start with a section rather than the whole thing. A thirty to forty minute slice of a real paper, taken under time pressure and marked to the published scheme, produces a usable loss profile without the demoralising experience of a full paper a student is not ready for. Once that profile exists, a full timed paper is scheduled deliberately, usually a few weeks later, specifically to test pace and stamina. Running the full paper first tends to measure unfamiliarity with the format rather than ability in the subject.

faqs.question: What does the first month look like for a Jazan student moving from a national-curriculum school into IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Mostly translation rather than new content. The subject knowledge usually transfers better than families fear; what does not transfer is the question style, the command words and the expectation that an answer earns marks only in the form the scheme describes. The first month therefore goes on reading questions properly, writing to the mark allocation, and learning the technical English of the syllabus. A diagnostic early on also shows which topics the previous curriculum sequenced later, and those get taught first.

faqs.question: When should support start for a Jazan student about to enter the first year of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Before the first term ends, and ideally in the weeks before it starts if the student is arriving from a different system. The first Diploma year has no external examination, which is exactly why families leave it alone and why problems accumulate quietly inside it. A student who finishes that year with sound foundations, a scoped Extended Essay topic and one experience of a timed paper enters the second year needing technique teaching only, and technique is the fastest thing to improve.

faqs.question: What should a Jazan MYP student have in place before starting IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Three things that are rarely taught explicitly: algebraic fluency that does not need a calculator, the habit of writing a reasoned explanation rather than an answer, and enough technical vocabulary in English to read a question quickly. MYP criterion work builds the second of those well and the first less reliably, because criterion assessment can reward a good method described in words even when the manipulation is shaky. A term spent on manipulation before IGCSE starts removes the single commonest cause of lost marks in the two years that follow.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in the final Diploma year for a student in Jazan?
faqs.answer: No, but the honest target narrows. With one or two terms left, the reliable gains come from technique: identifying the command term, structuring answers to the mark allocation, showing method so a slip costs one mark instead of four, and pacing a paper so the final question is attempted. Content work is restricted to high-yield topics the paper almost always samples. That combination moves marks for most students. Anybody promising a transformation across all six subjects in eight weeks is describing something that does not happen.

faqs.question: What does the last eight weeks before the June series need to achieve for a Jazan candidate?
faqs.answer: Two or three timed papers a week per subject, marked properly and taught from, plus a per-paper timing plan the student has actually rehearsed. By this stage the syllabus should be finished, so the work is converting knowledge into marks: question selection, order of attempt, what to do when a question stalls, and what to do with the last ten minutes. The other job is logistical, because entries, equipment, identification and the examination timetable all need checking with the school rather than assumed.

faqs.question: How much notice does a November-series resit need from a student in Jazan?
faqs.answer: Decide within days of the results, not weeks. Entries for the November series close early, and the school's examinations officer holds that deadline, so the first call after a disappointing result is to the school rather than to a tutor. The teaching then targets the specific component that cost the grade rather than the whole course, which is the commonest mistake in resit preparation. A resit candidate who re-reads the textbook from the beginning usually arrives at the same paper with the same technique and the same mark.

faqs.question: What happens if progress stalls after two months of weekly lessons in Jazan?
faqs.answer: We name the reason rather than add hours. A stall usually has one of four causes: the work set between lessons is not being attempted, the diagnosis was wrong and the real gap is a year below, the component being practised is not the one costing the marks, or the match between student and tutor is not working. Each has a different fix and three of them cost nothing. Buying more lessons without identifying which one is in play is how a family spends a term and ends it where it started.

faqs.question: How should a Jazan student use the long summer break to rebuild a weak subject?
faqs.answer: Mornings, short sessions, and the previous year's material rather than the next year's. Two or three sessions a week across several weeks of the break, aimed squarely at foundations such as manipulation, equation balancing or paragraph structure, with a written baseline at the start and the same diagnostic repeated at the end so the gain is measurable. In a hot and humid coastal province the middle of the day is unusable anyway, which makes the break the only period when a student is genuinely fresh while they work.

jazan.closingHeading: Get the baseline first, then decide what to buy
jazan.closingBody: The next step costs an hour. Send the subject, the level, the syllabus code and a photograph of the most recent marked script, and a tutor who teaches that course will take a free trial lesson and tell you plainly what is going wrong. If you want it, the first full session produces a timed past-paper section marked to the published scheme, which is the baseline everything afterwards is measured against. Lessons for families in Jazan are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, on Arabia Standard Time, in a slot built around the Sunday to Thursday week and whichever series the student is entered for.

jeddah.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the Diploma Programme, the Middle Years Programme and Cambridge IGCSE to students at Jeddah's British, American and IB schools. Whether the match is an IB Diploma tutor in Jeddah or an IGCSE tutor in Jeddah, it is made on the exact syllabus and paper your child sits, and every tutor works to the Sunday-to-Thursday week.

intro.heading: Start with the money, because that is where every Jeddah enquiry starts
paragraphs: Almost every parent who contacts us about IB and IGCSE tutors in Jeddah opens with the same question, and it is a fair one: what does this cost? The honest answer is that the city has two separate markets and they are priced differently. A generalist who can keep a Year 8 student moving through a maths workbook is advertised from around SAR 55 an hour on tutoring platforms, and budget online providers list Cambridge IGCSE one-to-one from about SAR 35. A specialist who has taught Physics at Higher Level, marked to the published criteria and can tell you where Paper 2 quietly loses four marks is advertised at SAR 180 to 220. Those are advertised figures from vendor listings, not a market average, and not our price. They tell you something useful anyway: the number tracks scarcity, not effort.

The second thing Jeddah parents raise is the clock. Jeddah is not a compact city. It runs as a long coastal spine from the historic centre at Al Balad north through Al Shati and Al Hamra and on to Obhur, and most of the international-school traffic moves along that axis twice a day. A family living in Obhur whose child attends a campus closer to the centre is not choosing between a 4pm and a 5pm lesson. They are choosing between a 5:30pm lesson and a child who falls asleep in it. That single fact decides more about whether tuition works than the tutor's CV does, and no rival page in this market mentions it.

This is why we deliver every lesson for Jeddah families online, one-to-one, over live video. It is not a compromise on an in-home service. In-home tuition in this city prices travel into the rate, and the tutor pool shrinks to whoever is willing to drive your stretch of Prince Sultan Road at six in the evening. Online, the pool is the whole set of specialists who teach your child's syllabus, and the thirty-five minutes that would have gone on a tutor's commute goes into the lesson or back into your evening. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Kingdom; home visits are a service we offer only in India, and we say so plainly rather than letting a search phrase imply otherwise.

Jeddah's academic shape matters too. The city is the Kingdom's second international-school market, and its schools skew British and American, with a smaller set running the full IB continuum. Diploma cohorts here are smaller than Riyadh's. The practical consequence shows up in Year 12: a student who has chosen a less common Higher Level subject may be the only one in the year group sitting it, which means no study group, no peer to compare a mark scheme with, and a teacher splitting one specialism across two year groups. That is a staffing reality, not a criticism of any school, and it is the most common reason a Jeddah family looks outside the school gate.

What follows is the whole picture in order: what the market charges and why, what Jeddah's geography does to the hours available, what the extra money actually buys, which subjects this city struggles to staff, how a Sunday-to-Thursday week fits a tutor who may be in India or the United Kingdom, where group teaching is and is not worth it, what a tutor may and may not touch on assessed work, and what happens after the Diploma when a Saudi university asks for an equivalency decision. Read the tables. They are the part nobody else publishes.
